chapters.title: The Netherfield Ball
chapters.recap_uz: Uikhem balga kelmaydi. Elizabet Darsi bilan raqsga tushadi va Uikhem haqida keskin gaplashadi. Kollinz, Meri va Missis Bennet balda oilani sharmanda qilishadi; Darsi buni kuzatib turadi.

paras.en: Till Elizabeth entered the drawing-room at Netherfield, and looked in vain for Mr. Wickham among the cluster of red coats there assembled, a doubt of his being present had never occurred to her. The certainty of meeting him had not been checked by any of those recollections that might not unreasonably have alarmed her. She had dressed with more than usual care, and prepared in the highest spirits for the conquest of all that remained unsubdued of his heart, trusting that it was not more than might be won in the course of the evening. But in an instant arose the dreadful suspicion of his being purposely omitted for Mr. Darcy's pleasure in the Bingleys' invitation to the officers; and though this was not exactly the case, the absolute fact of his absence was pronounced by his friend Denny, to whom Lydia eagerly applied, and who told them that Wickham had been obliged to go to town on business the day before, and was not yet returned; adding, with a significant smile, “I do not imagine his business would have called him away just now, if he had not wanted to avoid a certain gentleman here.”
paras.uz: Elizabet Nezerfilddagi mehmonxonaga kirib, u yerda to'plangan qizil kamzullilar orasida janob Uikhemni behuda izlaguncha, uning kelmasligi mumkinligi haqida bir marta ham shubha qilmagan edi. Uni uchratishiga bo'lgan ishonchni uni asossiz bo'lmagan holda xavotirga solishi mumkin bo'lgan xotiralarning birortasi ham to'xtatmagan edi. U odatdagidan ko'proq ehtiyotkorlik bilan kiyingan va uning qalbidan hali bo'ysunmay qolgan barcha narsani zabt etishga eng yuksak kayfiyat bilan tayyorlangan edi, bu oqshom davomida qo'lga kiritib bo'lmaydigan darajada ko'p emas deb ishongan edi. Lekin bir zumda Binglilar ofitserlarni taklif qilganda janob Darsiga yoqish uchun uni ataylab chetlab o'tishgan, degan dahshatli gumon paydo bo'ldi; garchi aslida bu aynan shunday bo'lmasa ham, uning yo'qligi haqidagi mutlaq faktni Lidiya shoshilib murojaat qilgan do'sti Denni e'lon qildi: u Uikhem kecha ish bilan Londonga ketishga majbur bo'lganini va hali qaytmaganini aytdi va ma'noli jilmayib qo'shib qo'ydi: «Agar u bu yerdagi bir janobdan qochishni istamaganida, ishi uni aynan hozir chaqirib ketardi deb o'ylamayman».

paras.en: This part of his intelligence, though unheard by Lydia, was caught by Elizabeth, and, as it assured her that Darcy was not less answerable for Wickham's absence than if her first surmise had been just, every feeling of displeasure against the former was so sharpened by immediate disappointment, that she could hardly reply with tolerable civility to the polite inquiries which he directly afterwards approached to make. Attendance, forbearance, patience with Darcy, was injury to Wickham. She was resolved against any sort of conversation with him, and turned away with a degree of ill-humour which she could not wholly surmount even in speaking to Mr. Bingley, whose blind partiality provoked her.
paras.uz: Ma'lumotning bu qismini Lidiya eshitmadi, lekin Elizabet ilg'ab oldi va bu unga Darsi, agar uning birinchi taxmini to'g'ri bo'lganida qanchalik javobgar bo'lsa, Uikhemning yo'qligi uchun shunchalik javobgar ekaniga ishontirgani sababli, darhol kelgan hafsalasi pirligi birinchisiga nisbatan har qanday norozilik tuyg'usini shunchalik o'tkirlashtirdiki, u darhol keyin yonaga kelib bergan xushmuomala so'roqlariga zo'rg'a chidab bo'ladigan xushmuomalalik bilan javob bera oldi. Darsiga e'tibor, toqat, sabr Uikhemga zarar edi. U u bilan har qanday suhbatdan voz kechishga qaror qildi va hatto ko'r-ko'rona tarafkashligi uning jahlini chiqargan janob Bingli bilan gaplashganda ham butunlay yenga olmagan darajadagi g'ashlik bilan o'girildi.

paras.en: But Elizabeth was not formed for ill-humour; and though every prospect of her own was destroyed for the evening, it could not dwell long on her spirits; and having told all her griefs to Charlotte Lucas, whom she had not seen for a week, she was soon able to make a voluntary transition to the oddities of her cousin, and to point him out to her particular notice. The first two dances, however, brought a return of distress; they were dances of mortification. Mr. Collins, awkward and solemn, apologising instead of attending, and often moving wrong without being aware of it, gave her all the shame and misery which a disagreeable partner for a couple of dances can give. The moment of her release from him was ecstasy.
paras.uz: Lekin Elizabet g'ashlik uchun yaratilmagan edi; garchi oqshom uchun barcha umidlari barbod bo'lgan bo'lsa ham, bu uning kayfiyatiga uzoq ta'sir qila olmadi; bir haftadan beri ko'rmagan Sharlotta Lukasga barcha dardlarini aytib bergach, tez orada o'z ixtiyori bilan amakivachchasining g'aroyibliklariga o'tib, uni dugonasining alohida e'tiboriga ko'rsata oldi. Biroq birinchi ikki raqs qayg'uni qaytardi; ular xo'rlanish raqslari edi. Beso'naqay va salobatli, e'tibor berish o'rniga uzr so'raydigan va ko'pincha buni sezmay noto'g'ri harakat qiladigan janob Kollinz unga bir-ikki raqs uchun yoqimsiz sherik bera oladigan barcha uyat va azobni berdi. Undan qutulgan lahza zavq edi.

paras.en: She danced next with an officer, and had the refreshment of talking of Wickham, and of hearing that he was universally liked. When those dances were over, she returned to Charlotte Lucas, and was in conversation with her, when she found herself suddenly addressed by Mr. Darcy who took her so much by surprise in his application for her hand, that, without knowing what she did, she accepted him. He walked away again immediately, and she was left to fret over her own want of presence of mind; Charlotte tried to console her:
paras.uz: Keyin u bir ofitser bilan raqs tushdi va Uikhem haqida gaplashish hamda uni hamma yaxshi ko'rishini eshitish bilan yengil tortdi. O'sha raqslar tugagach, u Sharlotta Lukasning oldiga qaytdi va u bilan suhbatlashayotgan edi, to'satdan janob Darsi unga murojaat qilib, raqsga taklif qildi — bu uni shunchalik kutilmaganda qoldirdiki, nima qilayotganini bilmay, rozi bo'ldi. U darhol yana nari ketdi, Elizabet esa o'zining hozirjavobligi yetishmaganidan kuyinib qoldi; Sharlotta uni yupatishga urindi:

paras.en: “I dare say you will find him very agreeable.”
paras.uz: «Ishonamanki, uni juda yoqimli deb topasan».

paras.en: “Heaven forbid! That would be the greatest misfortune of all! To find a man agreeable whom one is determined to hate! Do not wish me such an evil.”
paras.uz: «Xudo saqlasin! Bu hammasidan katta baxtsizlik bo'lardi! Nafratlanishga qaror qilgan erkakni yoqimli deb topish! Menga bunday yomonlikni tilama».

paras.en: When the dancing recommenced, however, and Darcy approached to claim her hand, Charlotte could not help cautioning her in a whisper, not to be a simpleton, and allow her fancy for Wickham to make her appear unpleasant in the eyes of a man ten times his consequence. Elizabeth made no answer, and took her place in the set, amazed at the dignity to which she was arrived in being allowed to stand opposite to Mr. Darcy, and reading in her neighbours' looks, their equal amazement in beholding it. They stood for some time without speaking a word; and she began to imagine that their silence was to last through the two dances, and at first was resolved not to break it; till suddenly fancying that it would be the greater punishment to her partner to oblige him to talk, she made some slight observation on the dance. He replied, and was again silent. After a pause of some minutes, she addressed him a second time with:--“It is your turn to say something now, Mr. Darcy. I talked about the dance, and you ought to make some sort of remark on the size of the room, or the number of couples.”
paras.uz: Biroq raqslar qayta boshlanib, Darsi uning qo'lini so'rab kelganida, Sharlotta uni pichirlab ogohlantirmay qololmadi: ahmoqlik qilmasin va Uikhemga bo'lgan havasi uni undan o'n barobar mavqeli erkakning ko'zida yoqimsiz ko'rsatishiga yo'l qo'ymasin. Elizabet javob bermadi va safda o'z o'rnini egalladi; janob Darsining ro'parasida turishga ruxsat berilib, erishgan obro'sidan hayratlandi va qo'shnilarining qarashlarida buni ko'rib ular ham xuddi shunday hayratda ekanini o'qidi. Ular bir muddat bir og'iz ham gapirmay turishdi; u ularning sukuti ikki raqs davomida davom etadi deb o'ylay boshladi va avvaliga uni buzmaslikka qaror qildi; toki to'satdan sherigini gapirishga majbur qilish unga kattaroq jazo bo'ladi, degan fikr xayoliga kelib, raqs haqida arzimas bir gap aytdi. U javob berdi va yana jim bo'ldi. Bir necha daqiqalik sukutdan keyin u unga ikkinchi marta murojaat qildi: «Endi biror narsa aytish navbati sizda, janob Darsi. Men raqs haqida gapirdim, siz esa xonaning kattaligi yoki juftlar soni haqida biror gap aytishingiz kerak».

paras.en: He smiled, and assured her that whatever she wished him to say should be said.
paras.uz: U jilmaydi va u nima deyishini xohlasa, shu aytilishiga ishontirdi.

paras.en: “Very well. That reply will do for the present. Perhaps by and by I may observe that private balls are much pleasanter than public ones. But now we may be silent.”
paras.uz: «Juda yaxshi. Hozircha bu javob yetadi. Ehtimol, birozdan keyin xususiy ballar ommaviylaridan ancha yoqimliroq ekanini aytarman. Lekin hozir jim tursak bo'ladi».

paras.en: “Do you talk by rule, then, while you are dancing?”
paras.uz: «Demak, raqs tushayotganda qoida bo'yicha gapirasizmi?»

paras.en: “Sometimes. One must speak a little, you know. It would look odd to be entirely silent for half an hour together; and yet for the advantage of some, conversation ought to be so arranged, as that they may have the trouble of saying as little as possible.”
paras.uz: «Ba'zan. Bilasizmi, biroz gapirish kerak. Yarim soat butunlay jim turish g'alati ko'rinardi; shu bilan birga, ba'zilarning foydasi uchun suhbat shunday tashkil qilinishi kerakki, ular iloji boricha kam gapirish zahmatini chekishsin».

paras.en: “Are you consulting your own feelings in the present case, or do you imagine that you are gratifying mine?”
paras.uz: «Hozirgi holatda o'z tuyg'ularingizni hisobga olyapsizmi yoki meni mamnun qilyapman deb o'ylaysizmi?»

paras.en: “Both,” replied Elizabeth archly; “for I have always seen a great similarity in the turn of our minds. We are each of an unsocial, taciturn disposition, unwilling to speak, unless we expect to say something that will amaze the whole room, and be handed down to posterity with all the eclat of a proverb.”
paras.uz: «Ikkalasini ham, — ayyorona javob berdi Elizabet, — chunki men doim fikrlash tarzimizda katta o'xshashlik ko'rganman. Ikkalamiz ham kirishimsiz, kamgap tabiatlimiz, butun xonani hayratga soladigan va maqolning butun shon-shuhrati bilan avlodlarga o'tadigan biror gap aytishni kutmasak, gapirishni istamaymiz».

paras.en: “This is no very striking resemblance of your own character, I am sure,” said he. “How near it may be to mine, I cannot pretend to say. You think it a faithful portrait undoubtedly.”
paras.uz: «Bu sizning xarakteringizga unchalik o'xshash emas, ishonchim komil, — dedi u. — Meniki bilan qanchalik yaqinligini ayta olmayman. Siz buni shubhasiz sodiq portret deb hisoblaysiz».

paras.en: “I must not decide on my own performance.”
paras.uz: «O'z ishimga baho berishim kerak emas».

paras.en: He made no answer, and they were again silent till they had gone down the dance, when he asked her if she and her sisters did not very often walk to Meryton. She answered in the affirmative, and, unable to resist the temptation, added, “When you met us there the other day, we had just been forming a new acquaintance.”
paras.uz: U javob bermadi va ular raqs oxirigacha yana jim borishdi, keyin u undan opa-singillari bilan Meritonga tez-tez piyoda borishadimi, deb so'radi. U tasdiqlab javob berdi va vasvasaga qarshi tura olmay, qo'shib qo'ydi: «O'tgan kuni bizni u yerda uchratganingizda, biz endigina yangi tanish orttirayotgan edik».

paras.en: The effect was immediate. A deeper shade of hauteur overspread his features, but he said not a word, and Elizabeth, though blaming herself for her own weakness, could not go on. At length Darcy spoke, and in a constrained manner said, “Mr. Wickham is blessed with such happy manners as may ensure his making friends--whether he may be equally capable of retaining them, is less certain.”
paras.uz: Ta'sir darhol bo'ldi. Uning chehrasini kibrning yanada quyuqroq soyasi qopladi, lekin u bir og'iz ham gapirmadi, Elizabet esa o'z zaifligi uchun o'zini ayblasa ham, davom eta olmadi. Nihoyat Darsi gapirdi va zo'riqqan ohangda dedi: «Janob Uikhem do'st orttirishini ta'minlay oladigan shunday baxtli muomala bilan siylangan — ularni xuddi shunday saqlab qola olishi esa unchalik aniq emas».

paras.en: “He has been so unlucky as to lose your friendship,” replied Elizabeth with emphasis, “and in a manner which he is likely to suffer from all his life.”
paras.uz: «U sizning do'stligingizni yo'qotish baxtsizligiga uchragan, — urg'u bilan javob berdi Elizabet, — va shunday tarzdaki, butun umri davomida undan azob chekishi mumkin».

paras.en: Darcy made no answer, and seemed desirous of changing the subject. At that moment, Sir William Lucas appeared close to them, meaning to pass through the set to the other side of the room; but on perceiving Mr. Darcy, he stopped with a bow of superior courtesy to compliment him on his dancing and his partner.
paras.uz: Darsi javob bermadi va mavzuni o'zgartirishni istayotganga o'xshardi. Shu payt ularning yonida ser Uilyam Lukas paydo bo'ldi, u saf orqali xonaning narigi tomoniga o'tmoqchi edi; lekin janob Darsini ko'rib, uning raqsi va sherigi bilan tabriklash uchun yuksak xushmuomalalik bilan ta'zim qilib to'xtadi.

paras.en: “I have been most highly gratified indeed, my dear sir. Such very superior dancing is not often seen. It is evident that you belong to the first circles. Allow me to say, however, that your fair partner does not disgrace you, and that I must hope to have this pleasure often repeated, especially when a certain desirable event, my dear Eliza (glancing at her sister and Bingley) shall take place. What congratulations will then flow in! I appeal to Mr. Darcy:--but let me not interrupt you, sir. You will not thank me for detaining you from the bewitching converse of that young lady, whose bright eyes are also upbraiding me.”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham nihoyatda mamnun bo'ldim, aziz ser. Bunday a'lo raqsni tez-tez ko'rib bo'lmaydi. Siz birinchi doiralarga mansub ekaningiz aniq. Biroq aytishga ijozat bering, go'zal sherigingiz sizni sharmanda qilmaydi va men bu zavqning tez-tez takrorlanishiga umid qilishim kerak, ayniqsa ma'lum bir orzu qilingan voqea, azizim Eliza (opasi va Binglige qarab), sodir bo'lganda. O'shanda qanday tabriklar yog'iladi! Janob Darsiga murojaat qilaman... lekin sizni to'xtatmay, ser. Sizni bu yosh xonimning sehrli suhbatidan ushlab qolganim uchun menga rahmat aytmaysiz, uning yorqin ko'zlari ham meni koyimoqda».

paras.en: The latter part of this address was scarcely heard by Darcy; but Sir William's allusion to his friend seemed to strike him forcibly, and his eyes were directed with a very serious expression towards Bingley and Jane, who were dancing together. Recovering himself, however, shortly, he turned to his partner, and said, “Sir William's interruption has made me forget what we were talking of.”
paras.uz: Bu murojaatning oxirgi qismini Darsi deyarli eshitmadi; lekin ser Uilyamning do'stiga qilgan ishorasi unga qattiq ta'sir qilganday ko'rindi va uning ko'zlari juda jiddiy ifoda bilan birga raqs tushayotgan Bingli va Jeynga qaratildi. Biroq tez orada o'zini tutib olib, u sherigiga o'girildi va dedi: «Ser Uilyamning gapimizni bo'lishi nima haqida gaplashayotganimizni unutdirib qo'ydi».

paras.en: “I do not think we were speaking at all. Sir William could not have interrupted two people in the room who had less to say for themselves. We have tried two or three subjects already without success, and what we are to talk of next I cannot imagine.”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, umuman gaplashmayotgan edik. Ser Uilyam xonada o'zlari haqida aytadigan gapi bundan ham kam bo'lgan ikki odamning gapini bo'la olmasdi. Biz allaqachon ikki-uch mavzuni muvaffaqiyatsiz sinab ko'rdik, keyin nima haqida gaplashishimizni tasavvur ham qila olmayman».

paras.en: “What think you of books?” said he, smiling.
paras.uz: «Kitoblar haqida qanday fikrdasiz?» — dedi u jilmayib.

paras.en: “Books--oh! no. I am sure we never read the same, or not with the same feelings.”
paras.uz: «Kitoblar — oh! yo'q. Ishonchim komilki, biz hech qachon bir xil kitoblarni o'qimaymiz yoki bir xil tuyg'ular bilan o'qimaymiz».

paras.en: “I am sorry you think so; but if that be the case, there can at least be no want of subject. We may compare our different opinions.”
paras.uz: «Shunday deb o'ylaganingizdan afsusdaman; lekin agar shunday bo'lsa, hech bo'lmaganda mavzu yetishmasligi mumkin emas. Turli fikrlarimizni taqqoslashimiz mumkin».

paras.en: “No--I cannot talk of books in a ball-room; my head is always full of something else.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q — bal zalida kitoblar haqida gapira olmayman; boshim doim boshqa narsa bilan to'la bo'ladi».

paras.en: “The present always occupies you in such scenes--does it?” said he, with a look of doubt.
paras.uz: «Bunday sahnalarda sizni doim hozirgi lahza band qiladi — shundaymi?» — dedi u shubhali qarash bilan.

paras.en: “Yes, always,” she replied, without knowing what she said, for her thoughts had wandered far from the subject, as soon afterwards appeared by her suddenly exclaiming, “I remember hearing you once say, Mr. Darcy, that you hardly ever forgave, that your resentment once created was unappeasable. You are very cautious, I suppose, as to its being created.”
paras.uz: «Ha, doim», — javob berdi u, nima deyayotganini bilmay, chunki uning fikrlari mavzudan ancha uzoqqa ketib qolgan edi, bu tez orada uning to'satdan xitob qilganidan ma'lum bo'ldi: «Esimda, bir marta sizning deyarli hech qachon kechirmasligingizni, bir marta paydo bo'lgan kekingiz bosilmasligini aytganingizni eshitgan edim, janob Darsi. O'ylaymanki, uning paydo bo'lishiga juda ehtiyotkorsiz».

paras.en: “I am,” said he, with a firm voice.
paras.uz: «Shundayman», — dedi u qat'iy ovozda.

paras.en: “And never allow yourself to be blinded by prejudice?”
paras.uz: «Va hech qachon o'zingizni xurofot ko'r qilishiga yo'l qo'ymaysizmi?»

paras.en: “I hope not.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, yo'q».

paras.en: “It is particularly incumbent on those who never change their opinion, to be secure of judging properly at first.”
paras.uz: «Hech qachon fikrini o'zgartirmaydiganlar uchun boshidanoq to'g'ri hukm chiqarishga ishonch hosil qilish ayniqsa muhim».

paras.en: “May I ask to what these questions tend?”
paras.uz: «Bu savollar nimaga qaratilganini so'rasam bo'ladimi?»

paras.en: “Merely to the illustration of your character,” said she, endeavouring to shake off her gravity. “I am trying to make it out.”
paras.uz: «Faqat sizning xarakteringizni tasvirlashga, — dedi u jiddiyligini yengishga urinib. — Uni tushunishga harakat qilyapman».

paras.en: “And what is your success?”
paras.uz: «Va qanday muvaffaqiyatga erishyapsiz?»

paras.en: She shook her head. “I do not get on at all. I hear such different accounts of you as puzzle me exceedingly.”
paras.uz: U boshini chayqadi. «Umuman oldinga siljiyotganim yo'q. Siz haqingizda shunchalik turli gaplar eshitamanki, ular meni nihoyatda chalkashtiradi».

paras.en: “I can readily believe,” answered he gravely, “that reports may vary greatly with respect to me; and I could wish, Miss Bennet, that you were not to sketch my character at the present moment, as there is reason to fear that the performance would reflect no credit on either.”
paras.uz: «Ishonaman, — jiddiy javob berdi u, — men haqimdagi mish-mishlar juda farq qilishi mumkin; va xohlardimki, miss Bennet, hozirgi paytda xarakterimni chizmasangiz, chunki bu ish hech birimizga sharaf keltirmasligidan qo'rqish uchun asos bor».

paras.en: “But if I do not take your likeness now, I may never have another opportunity.”
paras.uz: «Lekin agar hozir sizning suratingizni olmasam, boshqa imkoniyatim bo'lmasligi mumkin».

paras.en: “I would by no means suspend any pleasure of yours,” he coldly replied. She said no more, and they went down the other dance and parted in silence; and on each side dissatisfied, though not to an equal degree, for in Darcy's breast there was a tolerably powerful feeling towards her, which soon procured her pardon, and directed all his anger against another.
paras.uz: «Sizning hech qanday zavqingizni to'xtatmagan bo'lardim», — sovuq javob berdi u. U boshqa gapirmadi, ular ikkinchi raqsni tushishdi va jimgina ajralishdi; ikkala tomon ham norozi edi, garchi teng darajada bo'lmasa ham, chunki Darsining ko'kragida unga nisbatan ancha kuchli tuyg'u bor edi, bu tez orada uni kechirishga va butun g'azabini boshqa birovga qaratishga olib keldi.

paras.en: They had not long separated, when Miss Bingley came towards her, and with an expression of civil disdain accosted her:
paras.uz: Ular ajralishganiga ko'p o'tmay, miss Bingli uning oldiga keldi va xushmuomala nafrat ifodasi bilan unga murojaat qildi:

paras.en: “So, Miss Eliza, I hear you are quite delighted with George Wickham! Your sister has been talking to me about him, and asking me a thousand questions; and I find that the young man quite forgot to tell you, among his other communication, that he was the son of old Wickham, the late Mr. Darcy's steward. Let me recommend you, however, as a friend, not to give implicit confidence to all his assertions; for as to Mr. Darcy's using him ill, it is perfectly false; for, on the contrary, he has always been remarkably kind to him, though George Wickham has treated Mr. Darcy in a most infamous manner.
paras.uz: «Demak, miss Eliza, eshitishimcha, siz Jorj Uikhemdan juda mamnunsiz! Opangiz men bilan u haqida gaplashib, ming bir savol berdi; va bilishimcha, yosh yigit sizga boshqa gaplari orasida o'zining marhum janob Darsining boshqaruvchisi keksa Uikhemning o'g'li ekanini aytishni butunlay unutibdi. Biroq do'st sifatida sizga uning barcha da'volariga so'zsiz ishonmaslikni maslahat beraman; chunki janob Darsi unga yomon munosabatda bo'lgani mutlaqo yolg'on; aksincha, u unga doim nihoyatda mehribon bo'lgan, Jorj Uikhem esa janob Darsiga eng sharmandali tarzda munosabatda bo'lgan.

paras.en: I do not know the particulars, but I know very well that Mr. Darcy is not in the least to blame, that he cannot bear to hear George Wickham mentioned, and that though my brother thought that he could not well avoid including him in his invitation to the officers, he was excessively glad to find that he had taken himself out of the way. His coming into the country at all is a most insolent thing, indeed, and I wonder how he could presume to do it. I pity you, Miss Eliza, for this discovery of your favourite's guilt; but really, considering his descent, one could not expect much better.”
paras.uz: Tafsilotlarini bilmayman, lekin juda yaxshi bilamanki, janob Darsi zarracha aybdor emas, u Jorj Uikhemning nomini eshitishga ham chiday olmaydi va akam ofitserlarni taklif qilganda uni qo'shmasdan ilojim yo'q deb o'ylagan bo'lsa ham, uning o'zi yo'ldan chetlashganini bilib nihoyatda xursand bo'ldi. Uning bu yerlarga kelishining o'zi haqiqatan ham juda surbetlik va qanday jur'at qilganiga hayronman. Sevimlingizning aybi ochilgani uchun sizga achinaman, miss Eliza; lekin rostini aytganda, uning kelib chiqishini hisobga olsak, bundan yaxshiroq narsani kutib bo'lmasdi».

paras.en: “His guilt and his descent appear by your account to be the same,” said Elizabeth angrily; “for I have heard you accuse him of nothing worse than of being the son of Mr. Darcy's steward, and of that, I can assure you, he informed me himself.”
paras.uz: «Sizning aytishingizcha, uning aybi va kelib chiqishi bir narsa ekan, — dedi Elizabet g'azab bilan, — chunki men sizning uni janob Darsining boshqaruvchisining o'g'li ekanidan yomonroq narsada ayblaganingizni eshitmadim, buni esa, sizni ishontirib aytamanki, u menga o'zi aytgan».

paras.en: “I beg your pardon,” replied Miss Bingley, turning away with a sneer. “Excuse my interference--it was kindly meant.”
paras.uz: «Kechirasiz, — javob berdi miss Bingli, kesatiq bilan o'girilib. — Aralashganim uchun uzr — bu yaxshi niyatda edi».

paras.en: “Insolent girl!” said Elizabeth to herself. “You are much mistaken if you expect to influence me by such a paltry attack as this. I see nothing in it but your own wilful ignorance and the malice of Mr. Darcy.” She then sought her eldest sister, who had undertaken to make inquiries on the same subject of Bingley. Jane met her with a smile of such sweet complacency, a glow of such happy expression, as sufficiently marked how well she was satisfied with the occurrences of the evening. Elizabeth instantly read her feelings, and at that moment solicitude for Wickham, resentment against his enemies, and everything else, gave way before the hope of Jane's being in the fairest way for happiness.
paras.uz: «Surbet qiz! — dedi Elizabet o'ziga o'zi. — Agar bunday arzimas hujum bilan menga ta'sir qilaman deb o'ylasang, qattiq adashasan. Men bunda sening ataylab bilmaslikingdan va janob Darsining g'arazidan boshqa hech narsani ko'rmayapman». Keyin u Binglidan xuddi shu mavzuda so'rab bilishni o'z zimmasiga olgan to'ng'ich opasini izladi. Jeyn uni shunchalik shirin mamnuniyat tabassumi, shunchalik baxtli ifoda nuri bilan kutib oldiki, bu uning oqshom voqealaridan qanchalik mamnun ekanini yetarlicha ko'rsatib turardi. Elizabet uning tuyg'ularini darhol o'qidi va o'sha lahzada Uikhem uchun tashvish, uning dushmanlariga qarshi g'azab va boshqa hamma narsa Jeyn baxtga eng to'g'ri yo'lda ekaniga bo'lgan umid oldida chekindi.

paras.en: “I want to know,” said she, with a countenance no less smiling than her sister's, “what you have learnt about Mr. Wickham. But perhaps you have been too pleasantly engaged to think of any third person; in which case you may be sure of my pardon.”
paras.uz: «Bilmoqchiman, — dedi u opasinikidan kam jilmaymagan chehra bilan, — janob Uikhem haqida nima bilib olding. Lekin ehtimol sen uchinchi bir odam haqida o'ylash uchun haddan tashqari yoqimli band bo'lgandirsan; bu holda kechirishimga ishonishing mumkin».

paras.en: “No,” replied Jane, “I have not forgotten him; but I have nothing satisfactory to tell you. Mr. Bingley does not know the whole of his history, and is quite ignorant of the circumstances which have principally offended Mr. Darcy; but he will vouch for the good conduct, the probity, and honour of his friend, and is perfectly convinced that Mr. Wickham has deserved much less attention from Mr. Darcy than he has received; and I am sorry to say by his account as well as his sister's, Mr. Wickham is by no means a respectable young man. I am afraid he has been very imprudent, and has deserved to lose Mr. Darcy's regard.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, — javob berdi Jeyn, — uni unutmadim; lekin senga aytadigan qoniqarli gapim yo'q. Janob Bingli uning butun tarixini bilmaydi va janob Darsini asosan ranjitgan holatlardan butunlay bexabar; lekin u do'stining yaxshi xulqi, halolligi va sharafiga kafolat beradi va janob Uikhem janob Darsidan olganidan ancha kam e'tiborga loyiq bo'lganiga to'liq ishonadi; afsus bilan aytishim kerakki, uning ham, singlisining ham aytishicha, janob Uikhem umuman hurmatli yosh yigit emas. Qo'rqamanki, u juda ehtiyotsiz bo'lgan va janob Darsining hurmatini yo'qotishga loyiq bo'lgan».

paras.en: “Mr. Bingley does not know Mr. Wickham himself?”
paras.uz: «Janob Binglining o'zi janob Uikhemni bilmaydimi?»

paras.en: “No; he never saw him till the other morning at Meryton.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q; o'tgan kuni ertalab Meritonda ko'rgunicha uni hech qachon ko'rmagan».

paras.en: “This account then is what he has received from Mr. Darcy. I am satisfied. But what does he say of the living?”
paras.uz: «Demak, bu u janob Darsidan eshitgan hikoya. Qanoatlandim. Lekin u lavozim haqida nima deydi?»

paras.en: “He does not exactly recollect the circumstances, though he has heard them from Mr. Darcy more than once, but he believes that it was left to him conditionally only.”
paras.uz: «U holatlarni aniq eslay olmaydi, garchi ularni janob Darsidan bir necha marta eshitgan bo'lsa ham, lekin u uni faqat shartli ravishda qoldirilgan deb hisoblaydi».

paras.en: “I have not a doubt of Mr. Bingley's sincerity,” said Elizabeth warmly; “but you must excuse my not being convinced by assurances only. Mr. Bingley's defense of his friend was a very able one, I dare say; but since he is unacquainted with several parts of the story, and has learnt the rest from that friend himself, I shall venture to still think of both gentlemen as I did before.”
paras.uz: «Janob Binglining samimiyligiga zarracha shubham yo'q, — dedi Elizabet qizg'in, — lekin faqat ishontirishlar bilan ishonmaganim uchun meni kechirishing kerak. Janob Binglining do'stini himoya qilishi juda mohirona bo'lgandir, ishonaman; lekin u hikoyaning bir necha qismidan bexabar va qolganini o'sha do'stining o'zidan bilib olgani uchun, men ikkala janob haqida ham avvalgidek o'ylashga jur'at qilaman».

paras.en: She then changed the discourse to one more gratifying to each, and on which there could be no difference of sentiment. Elizabeth listened with delight to the happy, though modest hopes which Jane entertained of Mr. Bingley's regard, and said all in her power to heighten her confidence in it. On their being joined by Mr. Bingley himself, Elizabeth withdrew to Miss Lucas; to whose inquiry after the pleasantness of her last partner she had scarcely replied, before Mr. Collins came up to them, and told her with great exultation that he had just been so fortunate as to make a most important discovery.
paras.uz: Keyin u suhbatni har ikkisi uchun yoqimliroq, tuyg'ularda hech qanday farq bo'lishi mumkin bo'lmagan mavzuga burdi. Elizabet Jeynning janob Binglining hurmati haqidagi baxtli, garchi kamtarona umidlarini zavq bilan tingladi va unga bo'lgan ishonchini oshirish uchun qo'lidan kelgan hamma narsani aytdi. Ularga janob Binglining o'zi qo'shilganda, Elizabet miss Lukasning oldiga chekindi; oxirgi sherigining qanchalik yoqimli bo'lgani haqidagi savoliga zo'rg'a javob berib ulgurmasdan, janob Kollinz ularning oldiga keldi va katta tantana bilan hozirgina juda muhim kashfiyot qilish baxtiga muyassar bo'lganini aytdi.

paras.en: “I have found out,” said he, “by a singular accident, that there is now in the room a near relation of my patroness. I happened to overhear the gentleman himself mentioning to the young lady who does the honours of the house the names of his cousin Miss de Bourgh, and of her mother Lady Catherine. How wonderfully these sort of things occur! Who would have thought of my meeting with, perhaps, a nephew of Lady Catherine de Bourgh in this assembly! I am most thankful that the discovery is made in time for me to pay my respects to him, which I am now going to do, and trust he will excuse my not having done it before. My total ignorance of the connection must plead my apology.”
paras.uz: «G'aroyib tasodif tufayli bilib oldimki, — dedi u, — hozir xonada homiyamning yaqin qarindoshi bor ekan. Janobning o'zi uy sohibasi vazifasini bajarayotgan yosh xonimga amakivachchasi miss de Burg va uning onasi ledi Ketrinning ismlarini tilga olayotganini tasodifan eshitib qoldim. Bunday narsalar qanday ajoyib tarzda yuz beradi! Bu yig'inda, ehtimol, ledi Ketrin de Burgning jiyanini uchratishimni kim o'ylabdi! Kashfiyot unga hurmatimni bildirishga ulguradigan vaqtda qilinganidan nihoyatda minnatdorman, buni hozir qilmoqchiman va ishonamanki, u buni oldinroq qilmaganim uchun kechiradi. Bu qarindoshlikdan butunlay bexabarligim uzrim bo'lishi kerak».

paras.en: “You are not going to introduce yourself to Mr. Darcy!”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsiga o'zingizni o'zingiz tanishtirmoqchi emassiz-ku!»

paras.en: “Indeed I am. I shall entreat his pardon for not having done it earlier. I believe him to be Lady Catherine's nephew. It will be in my power to assure him that her ladyship was quite well yesterday se'nnight.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, tanishtiraman. Buni oldinroq qilmaganim uchun undan kechirim so'rayman. Uni ledi Ketrinning jiyani deb ishonaman. Uni janoblari o'tgan haftaning shu kuni sog'-salomat bo'lganiga ishontira olaman».

paras.en: Elizabeth tried hard to dissuade him from such a scheme, assuring him that Mr. Darcy would consider his addressing him without introduction as an impertinent freedom, rather than a compliment to his aunt; that it was not in the least necessary there should be any notice on either side; and that if it were, it must belong to Mr. Darcy, the superior in consequence, to begin the acquaintance. Mr. Collins listened to her with the determined air of following his own inclination, and, when she ceased speaking, replied thus:
paras.uz: Elizabet uni bu rejadan qaytarishga qattiq urindi: janob Darsi tanishtirilmasdan unga murojaat qilishini xolasiga hurmat emas, balki surbetlarcha erkinlik deb hisoblashini; hech bir tomondan hech qanday e'tibor zarur emasligini; agar zarur bo'lsa ham, tanishuvni boshlash mavqei yuqoriroq janob Darsiga tegishli ekanini aytib ishontirdi. Janob Kollinz uni o'z xohishiga amal qilishga qat'iy qaror qilgan qiyofada tingladi va u gapini tugatgach, shunday javob berdi:

paras.en: “My dear Miss Elizabeth, I have the highest opinion in the world in your excellent judgement in all matters within the scope of your understanding; but permit me to say, that there must be a wide difference between the established forms of ceremony amongst the laity, and those which regulate the clergy; for, give me leave to observe that I consider the clerical office as equal in point of dignity with the highest rank in the kingdom--provided that a proper humility of behaviour is at the same time maintained. You must therefore allow me to follow the dictates of my conscience on this occasion, which leads me to perform what I look on as a point of duty.
paras.uz: «Aziz miss Elizabet, sizning tushunchangiz doirasidagi barcha masalalarda ajoyib mulohazangiz haqida dunyodagi eng yuqori fikrdaman; lekin aytishga ijozat bering, oddiy xalq orasidagi o'rnatilgan odob qoidalari bilan ruhoniylarni tartibga soluvchi qoidalar o'rtasida katta farq bo'lishi kerak; chunki ruxsat bering, men ruhoniylik lavozimini qadr-qimmat jihatidan qirollikdagi eng yuksak martaba bilan teng deb hisoblashimni aytay — faqat bir vaqtda xulqda munosib kamtarlik saqlansa. Shuning uchun bu safar menga vijdonimning amriga ergashishga ruxsat berishingiz kerak, u meni burch deb biladigan narsani bajarishga undaydi.

paras.en: Pardon me for neglecting to profit by your advice, which on every other subject shall be my constant guide, though in the case before us I consider myself more fitted by education and habitual study to decide on what is right than a young lady like yourself.” And with a low bow he left her to attack Mr. Darcy, whose reception of his advances she eagerly watched, and whose astonishment at being so addressed was very evident. Her cousin prefaced his speech with a solemn bow and though she could not hear a word of it, she felt as if hearing it all, and saw in the motion of his lips the words “apology,” “Hunsford,” and “Lady Catherine de Bourgh.” It vexed her to see him expose himself to such a man.
paras.uz: Maslahatingizdan foydalanmaganim uchun meni kechiring, u boshqa har qanday mavzuda mening doimiy yo'lboshchim bo'ladi, garchi oldimizdagi holatda nima to'g'ri ekanini hal qilishga sizdek yosh xonimdan ko'ra ta'lim va odatiy o'qishim tufayli ko'proq loyiq deb hisoblasam ham». Va past ta'zim bilan u uni tark etib, janob Darsiga hujum qilgani ketdi; Elizabet uning intilishlarini qanday qabul qilishini ishtiyoq bilan kuzatdi, bunday murojaatdan uning hayratlangani juda aniq ko'rinib turardi. Amakivachchasi nutqini salobatli ta'zim bilan boshladi va u bir og'iz ham eshitmasa ham, go'yo hammasini eshitayotgandek his qildi va uning lablari harakatida «uzr», «Xansford» va «ledi Ketrin de Burg» so'zlarini ko'rdi. Uning bunday odam oldida o'zini sharmanda qilayotganini ko'rish uning g'ashini keltirdi.

paras.en: Mr. Darcy was eyeing him with unrestrained wonder, and when at last Mr. Collins allowed him time to speak, replied with an air of distant civility. Mr. Collins, however, was not discouraged from speaking again, and Mr. Darcy's contempt seemed abundantly increasing with the length of his second speech, and at the end of it he only made him a slight bow, and moved another way. Mr. Collins then returned to Elizabeth.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi unga yashirmagan hayrat bilan qarab turardi va nihoyat janob Kollinz unga gapirishga vaqt berganida, uzoq xushmuomalalik bilan javob berdi. Biroq janob Kollinz yana gapirishdan cho'chimadi va janob Darsining nafrati uning ikkinchi nutqi cho'zilgani sari mo'l-ko'l ortib borayotganga o'xshardi, oxirida esa u unga faqat yengil ta'zim qildi va boshqa tomonga yurib ketdi. Shundan keyin janob Kollinz Elizabetning oldiga qaytdi.

paras.en: “I have no reason, I assure you,” said he, “to be dissatisfied with my reception. Mr. Darcy seemed much pleased with the attention. He answered me with the utmost civility, and even paid me the compliment of saying that he was so well convinced of Lady Catherine's discernment as to be certain she could never bestow a favour unworthily. It was really a very handsome thought. Upon the whole, I am much pleased with him.”
paras.uz: «Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, — dedi u, — qabulimdan norozi bo'lishga hech qanday sabab yo'q. Janob Darsi e'tibordan juda mamnun ko'rindi. U menga eng katta xushmuomalalik bilan javob berdi va hatto ledi Ketrinning farosatiga shunchalik ishonganini, u hech qachon noloyiq odamga iltifot ko'rsatmasligiga amin ekanini aytib, menga iltifot ham qildi. Bu haqiqatan ham juda chiroyli fikr edi. Umuman olganda, undan juda mamnunman».

paras.en: As Elizabeth had no longer any interest of her own to pursue, she turned her attention almost entirely on her sister and Mr. Bingley; and the train of agreeable reflections which her observations gave birth to, made her perhaps almost as happy as Jane. She saw her in idea settled in that very house, in all the felicity which a marriage of true affection could bestow; and she felt capable, under such circumstances, of endeavouring even to like Bingley's two sisters. Her mother's thoughts she plainly saw were bent the same way, and she determined not to venture near her, lest she might hear too much.
paras.uz: Elizabetning endi o'zining kuzatadigan qiziqishi qolmagani uchun, u e'tiborini deyarli butunlay opasi va janob Binglige qaratdi; kuzatishlari tug'dirgan yoqimli o'ylar zanjiri uni, ehtimol, deyarli Jeyn kabi baxtli qildi. U xayolida uni aynan shu uyda, haqiqiy mehrga asoslangan nikoh bera oladigan barcha baxt ichida joylashgan holda ko'rdi; va bunday sharoitda hatto Binglining ikki opa-singilini yoqtirishga harakat qilishga ham qodir ekanini his qildi. U onasining fikrlari ham xuddi shu tomonga qaratilganini aniq ko'rdi va juda ko'p narsa eshitib qolmaslik uchun uning yoniga yaqinlashmaslikka qaror qildi.

paras.en: When they sat down to supper, therefore, she considered it a most unlucky perverseness which placed them within one of each other; and deeply was she vexed to find that her mother was talking to that one person (Lady Lucas) freely, openly, and of nothing else but her expectation that Jane would soon be married to Mr. Bingley. It was an animating subject, and Mrs. Bennet seemed incapable of fatigue while enumerating the advantages of the match. His being such a charming young man, and so rich, and living but three miles from them, were the first points of self-gratulation; and then it was such a comfort to think how fond the two sisters were of Jane, and to be certain that they must desire the connection as much as she could do.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun kechki ovqatga o'tirishganda, ularni bir-birining yoniga o'tqazgan bu tasodifni eng omadsiz teskarilik deb hisobladi; va onasining o'sha bir odamga (ledi Lukasga) erkin, ochiqchasiga va Jeyn tez orada janob Binglige turmushga chiqishini kutishidan boshqa hech narsa haqida gapirmayotganini bilib, qattiq g'ashlandi. Bu jonlantiruvchi mavzu edi va missis Bennet bu nikohning afzalliklarini sanashda charchashni bilmaydiganga o'xshardi. Uning shunday maftunkor yosh yigit ekani, shunchalik boyligi va ulardan atigi uch mil narida yashashi o'zini tabriklashning birinchi nuqtalari edi; keyin ikki opa-singil Jeynni qanchalik yaxshi ko'rishini o'ylash va ular ham bu qarindoshlikni o'zi kabi xohlashlari kerakligiga ishonch hosil qilish shunchalik taskin berardi.

paras.en: It was, moreover, such a promising thing for her younger daughters, as Jane's marrying so greatly must throw them in the way of other rich men; and lastly, it was so pleasant at her time of life to be able to consign her single daughters to the care of their sister, that she might not be obliged to go into company more than she liked. It was necessary to make this circumstance a matter of pleasure, because on such occasions it is the etiquette; but no one was less likely than Mrs. Bennet to find comfort in staying home at any period of her life. She concluded with many good wishes that Lady Lucas might soon be equally fortunate, though evidently and triumphantly believing there was no chance of it.
paras.uz: Bundan tashqari, bu kichik qizlari uchun ham juda istiqbolli narsa edi, chunki Jeynning bunchalik yaxshi turmushga chiqishi ularni boshqa boy erkaklar yo'liga olib chiqishi kerak edi; va nihoyat, uning yoshida turmushga chiqmagan qizlarini opalarining qaramog'iga topshira olish shunchalik yoqimli ediki, u xohlaganidan ko'proq jamiyatga chiqishga majbur bo'lmasdi. Bu holatni zavq manbai qilib ko'rsatish kerak edi, chunki bunday hollarda odob shuni talab qiladi; lekin hayotining hech bir davrida uyda qolishdan taskin topishi ehtimoli missis Bennetdan kam bo'lgan odam yo'q edi. U ledi Lukasga ham tez orada xuddi shunday omad kulib boqishini ko'p tilaklar bilan tilab, gapini tugatdi, garchi bunday imkoniyat yo'qligiga aniq va g'olibona ishonsa ham.

paras.en: In vain did Elizabeth endeavour to check the rapidity of her mother's words, or persuade her to describe her felicity in a less audible whisper; for, to her inexpressible vexation, she could perceive that the chief of it was overheard by Mr. Darcy, who sat opposite to them. Her mother only scolded her for being nonsensical.
paras.uz: Elizabet onasining so'zlari tezligini to'xtatishga yoki uni baxtini kamroq eshitiladigan pichirlash bilan tasvirlashga ko'ndirishga behuda urindi; chunki ta'riflab bo'lmas g'ashligi bilan u gaplarning asosiy qismini ularning ro'parasida o'tirgan janob Darsi eshitayotganini sezdi. Onasi uni faqat bema'ni gaplar uchun koyidi.

paras.en: “What is Mr. Darcy to me, pray, that I should be afraid of him? I am sure we owe him no such particular civility as to be obliged to say nothing he may not like to hear.”
paras.uz: «Iltimos, janob Darsi menga kim ekanki, undan qo'rqishim kerak? Ishonchim komilki, biz unga u eshitishni yoqtirmaydigan hech narsa demaslikka majbur bo'ladigan darajada alohida xushmuomalalik qarzdor emasmiz».

paras.en: “For heaven's sake, madam, speak lower. What advantage can it be for you to offend Mr. Darcy? You will never recommend yourself to his friend by so doing!”
paras.uz: «Xudo haqqi, oyijon, pastroq gapiring. Janob Darsini ranjitishdan sizga qanday foyda bor? Bunday qilib uning do'stiga hech qachon o'zingizni yoqtira olmaysiz!»

paras.en: Nothing that she could say, however, had any influence. Her mother would talk of her views in the same intelligible tone. Elizabeth blushed and blushed again with shame and vexation. She could not help frequently glancing her eye at Mr. Darcy, though every glance convinced her of what she dreaded; for though he was not always looking at her mother, she was convinced that his attention was invariably fixed by her. The expression of his face changed gradually from indignant contempt to a composed and steady gravity.
paras.uz: Biroq uning hech qanday gapi ta'sir qilmadi. Onasi o'z rejalari haqida o'sha tushunarli ohangda gapirishda davom etdi. Elizabet uyat va g'ashlikdan qayta-qayta qizardi. U tez-tez janob Darsiga ko'z tashlamay qololmadi, garchi har bir qarash uni qo'rqqan narsasiga ishontirsa ham; chunki u har doim ham onasiga qaramasa ham, uning e'tibori o'zgarmas tarzda unga qaratilganiga amin edi. Uning yuzidagi ifoda asta-sekin g'azabli nafratdan xotirjam va barqaror jiddiylikka o'zgardi.

paras.en: At length, however, Mrs. Bennet had no more to say; and Lady Lucas, who had been long yawning at the repetition of delights which she saw no likelihood of sharing, was left to the comforts of cold ham and chicken. Elizabeth now began to revive. But not long was the interval of tranquillity; for, when supper was over, singing was talked of, and she had the mortification of seeing Mary, after very little entreaty, preparing to oblige the company. By many significant looks and silent entreaties, did she endeavour to prevent such a proof of complaisance, but in vain; Mary would not understand them; such an opportunity of exhibiting was delightful to her, and she began her song.
paras.uz: Biroq nihoyat missis Bennetning aytadigan gapi qolmadi; o'zi bo'lishish ehtimolini ko'rmagan zavqlarning takrorlanishidan uzoq vaqt esnab o'tirgan ledi Lukas sovuq vetchina va tovuq go'shti taskinlariga qoldirildi. Elizabet endi o'ziga kela boshladi. Lekin osoyishtalik oralig'i uzoq bo'lmadi; chunki kechki ovqat tugagach, qo'shiq aytish haqida gap ketdi va u Merining juda oz iltimosdan keyin davrani xursand qilishga tayyorlanayotganini ko'rib xo'rlandi. U ko'p ma'noli qarashlar va jim iltimoslar bilan bunday xushmuomalalik namoyishining oldini olishga urindi, lekin behuda; Meri ularni tushunishni istamadi; o'zini ko'rsatish uchun bunday imkoniyat unga zavq berardi va u qo'shig'ini boshladi.

paras.en: Elizabeth's eyes were fixed on her with most painful sensations, and she watched her progress through the several stanzas with an impatience which was very ill rewarded at their close; for Mary, on receiving, amongst the thanks of the table, the hint of a hope that she might be prevailed on to favour them again, after the pause of half a minute began another. Mary's powers were by no means fitted for such a display; her voice was weak, and her manner affected. Elizabeth was in agonies. She looked at Jane, to see how she bore it; but Jane was very composedly talking to Bingley. She looked at his two sisters, and saw them making signs of derision at each other, and at Darcy, who continued, however, imperturbably grave. She looked at her father to entreat his interference, lest Mary should be singing all night.
paras.uz: Elizabetning ko'zlari eng og'riqli tuyg'ular bilan unga qadaldi va u uning bir necha bandni kuylashini sabrsizlik bilan kuzatdi, bu sabrsizlik oxirida juda yomon taqdirlandi; chunki Meri stol atrofidagilarning minnatdorchiliklari orasida uni yana bir bor ularni xursand qilishga ko'ndirish mumkin degan umid ishorasini olgach, yarim daqiqalik sukutdan keyin boshqasini boshladi. Merining qobiliyatlari bunday namoyish uchun umuman mos emasdi; ovozi zaif, uslubi soxta edi. Elizabet azob chekardi. U Jeyn bunga qanday chidayotganini ko'rish uchun unga qaradi; lekin Jeyn juda xotirjam Bingli bilan gaplashayotgan edi. U uning ikki opa-singiliga qaradi va ularning bir-biriga hamda Darsiga masxara ishoralarini qilayotganini ko'rdi, biroq u bezovtalanmay jiddiyligicha qoldi. U Meri tun bo'yi qo'shiq aytmasligi uchun aralashishini iltimos qilib, otasiga qaradi.

paras.en: He took the hint, and when Mary had finished her second song, said aloud, “That will do extremely well, child. You have delighted us long enough. Let the other young ladies have time to exhibit.”
paras.uz: U ishorani tushundi va Meri ikkinchi qo'shig'ini tugatgach, baland ovozda dedi: «Bu juda yaxshi bo'ldi, bolam. Bizni yetarlicha uzoq xursand qilding. Boshqa yosh xonimlarga ham o'zlarini ko'rsatishga vaqt ber».

paras.en: Mary, though pretending not to hear, was somewhat disconcerted; and Elizabeth, sorry for her, and sorry for her father's speech, was afraid her anxiety had done no good. Others of the party were now applied to.
paras.uz: Meri eshitmaganga olsa ham, biroz xijolat bo'ldi; unga ham, otasining gapiga ham achingan Elizabet tashvishi hech qanday foyda keltirmaganidan qo'rqdi. Endi davradagi boshqalarga murojaat qilindi.

paras.en: “If I,” said Mr. Collins, “were so fortunate as to be able to sing, I should have great pleasure, I am sure, in obliging the company with an air; for I consider music as a very innocent diversion, and perfectly compatible with the profession of a clergyman. I do not mean, however, to assert that we can be justified in devoting too much of our time to music, for there are certainly other things to be attended to. The rector of a parish has much to do. In the first place, he must make such an agreement for tithes as may be beneficial to himself and not offensive to his patron. He must write his own sermons; and the time that remains will not be too much for his parish duties, and the care and improvement of his dwelling, which he cannot be excused from making as comfortable as possible.
paras.uz: «Agar men, — dedi janob Kollinz, — qo'shiq ayta olish baxtiga ega bo'lganimda, ishonchim komilki, davrani bir kuy bilan xursand qilishdan katta zavq olardim; chunki musiqani juda beg'ubor ermak va ruhoniy kasbiga to'liq mos deb hisoblayman. Biroq vaqtimizning haddan tashqari ko'p qismini musiqaga bag'ishlashimizni oqlash mumkin, demoqchi emasman, chunki e'tibor berish kerak bo'lgan boshqa narsalar ham, albatta, bor. Qavm ruhoniysining ishi ko'p. Birinchi navbatda, u ushr bo'yicha shunday kelishuv tuzishi kerakki, u o'zi uchun foydali va homiysi uchun haqoratli bo'lmasin. U o'z va'zlarini o'zi yozishi kerak; qolgan vaqt esa qavm vazifalari va turar joyiga g'amxo'rlik qilish hamda uni yaxshilash uchun ortiqcha bo'lmaydi, uni iloji boricha qulay qilishdan esa u ozod bo'la olmaydi.

paras.en: And I do not think it of light importance that he should have attentive and conciliatory manners towards everybody, especially towards those to whom he owes his preferment. I cannot acquit him of that duty; nor could I think well of the man who should omit an occasion of testifying his respect towards anybody connected with the family.” And with a bow to Mr. Darcy, he concluded his speech, which had been spoken so loud as to be heard by half the room. Many stared--many smiled; but no one looked more amused than Mr. Bennet himself, while his wife seriously commended Mr. Collins for having spoken so sensibly, and observed in a half-whisper to Lady Lucas, that he was a remarkably clever, good kind of young man.
paras.uz: Va men uning hammaga, ayniqsa martabasi uchun qarzdor bo'lganlarga nisbatan e'tiborli va murosali muomalaga ega bo'lishini yengil ahamiyatli deb hisoblamayman. Uni bu burchdan ozod qila olmayman; oila bilan bog'liq har qanday odamga hurmatini bildirish imkoniyatini qo'ldan boy beradigan odam haqida ham yaxshi o'ylay olmasdim». Va janob Darsiga ta'zim qilib, u xonaning yarmi eshitadigan darajada baland ovozda aytilgan nutqini tugatdi. Ko'pchilik tikilib qoldi — ko'pchilik jilmaydi; lekin hech kim janob Bennetning o'zidan ko'ra ko'proq zavqlangan ko'rinmadi, uning xotini esa janob Kollinzni bunchalik oqilona gapirgani uchun jiddiy maqtadi va ledi Lukasga yarim pichirlab, u nihoyatda aqlli, yaxshi yosh yigit ekanini aytdi.

paras.en: To Elizabeth it appeared that, had her family made an agreement to expose themselves as much as they could during the evening, it would have been impossible for them to play their parts with more spirit or finer success; and happy did she think it for Bingley and her sister that some of the exhibition had escaped his notice, and that his feelings were not of a sort to be much distressed by the folly which he must have witnessed. That his two sisters and Mr. Darcy, however, should have such an opportunity of ridiculing her relations, was bad enough, and she could not determine whether the silent contempt of the gentleman, or the insolent smiles of the ladies, were more intolerable.
paras.uz: Elizabetga shunday tuyuldiki, agar uning oilasi oqshom davomida o'zlarini iloji boricha sharmanda qilishga kelishib olganida ham, ular o'z rollarini bundan jo'shqinroq yoki muvaffaqiyatliroq o'ynay olmasdi; Bingli va opasi uchun namoyishning bir qismi uning e'tiboridan chetda qolgani va uning tuyg'ulari guvohi bo'lgan bema'nilikdan qattiq iztirobga tushadigan turdagi emasligi baxt edi. Biroq uning ikki opa-singili va janob Darsi uning qarindoshlarini masxara qilish uchun bunday imkoniyatga ega bo'lgani yetarlicha yomon edi va u janobning jim nafratimi yoki xonimlarning surbet tabassumlarimi, qaysi biri chidab bo'lmasroq ekanini aniqlay olmadi.

paras.en: The rest of the evening brought her little amusement. She was teased by Mr. Collins, who continued most perseveringly by her side, and though he could not prevail on her to dance with him again, put it out of her power to dance with others. In vain did she entreat him to stand up with somebody else, and offer to introduce him to any young lady in the room. He assured her, that as to dancing, he was perfectly indifferent to it; that his chief object was by delicate attentions to recommend himself to her and that he should therefore make a point of remaining close to her the whole evening. There was no arguing upon such a project. She owed her greatest relief to her friend Miss Lucas, who often joined them, and good-naturedly engaged Mr. Collins's conversation to herself.
paras.uz: Oqshomning qolgan qismi unga kam zavq berdi. Uni yonida eng qat'iyat bilan qolishda davom etgan janob Kollinz bezor qildi; u uni yana o'zi bilan raqs tushishga ko'ndira olmasa ham, uning boshqalar bilan raqs tushishiga imkon bermadi. U behuda undan boshqa birov bilan raqsga tushishni iltimos qildi va xonadagi istalgan yosh xonim bilan tanishtirishni taklif qildi. U raqsga kelsak, unga mutlaqo befarq ekanini; asosiy maqsadi nozik e'tiborlar bilan o'zini unga yoqtirish ekanini va shuning uchun butun oqshom uning yonida qolishni o'ziga qoida qilishini aytib ishontirdi. Bunday reja haqida bahslashib bo'lmasdi. U eng katta yengillikni tez-tez ularga qo'shilib, xushfe'llik bilan janob Kollinzning suhbatini o'ziga qaratgan dugonasi miss Lukasdan topdi.

paras.en: She was at least free from the offense of Mr. Darcy's further notice; though often standing within a very short distance of her, quite disengaged, he never came near enough to speak. She felt it to be the probable consequence of her allusions to Mr. Wickham, and rejoiced in it.
paras.uz: Hech bo'lmaganda u janob Darsining keyingi e'tiboridan kelib chiqadigan ranjishdan xoli edi; u ko'pincha undan juda yaqin masofada, butunlay bo'sh holda tursa ham, hech qachon gaplashish uchun yetarlicha yaqin kelmadi. U buni janob Uikhemga qilgan ishoralarining ehtimoliy oqibati deb his qildi va bundan xursand bo'ldi.

paras.en: The Longbourn party were the last of all the company to depart, and, by a manoeuvre of Mrs. Bennet, had to wait for their carriage a quarter of an hour after everybody else was gone, which gave them time to see how heartily they were wished away by some of the family. Mrs. Hurst and her sister scarcely opened their mouths, except to complain of fatigue, and were evidently impatient to have the house to themselves. They repulsed every attempt of Mrs. Bennet at conversation, and by so doing threw a languor over the whole party, which was very little relieved by the long speeches of Mr. Collins, who was complimenting Mr. Bingley and his sisters on the elegance of their entertainment, and the hospitality and politeness which had marked their behaviour to their guests. Darcy said nothing at all. Mr. Bennet, in equal silence, was enjoying the scene.
paras.uz: Longborn oilasi butun mehmonlar ichida eng oxirida ketdi va missis Bennetning hiylasi tufayli hamma ketganidan keyin kareta uchun chorak soat kutishga majbur bo'ldi, bu esa ularga oilaning ba'zi a'zolari ularning ketishini qanchalik chin dildan istashini ko'rishga vaqt berdi. Missis Xerst va uning singlisi charchoqdan shikoyat qilishdan boshqa hollarda deyarli og'iz ochishmadi va uyni o'zlariga qoldirishni sabrsizlik bilan kutayotgani aniq edi. Ular missis Bennetning har bir suhbatga urinishini rad etishdi va shunday qilib butun davraga holsizlik soldilar, buni janob Kollinzning uzun nutqlari juda kam yengillashtirdi — u janob Bingli va uning opa-singillarini ziyofatlarining nafisligi va mehmonlarga ko'rsatgan mehmondo'stligi hamda xushmuomalaligi uchun maqtayotgan edi. Darsi umuman hech narsa demadi. Janob Bennet ham xuddi shunday jimgina sahnadan zavqlanardi.

paras.en: Mr. Bingley and Jane were standing together, a little detached from the rest, and talked only to each other. Elizabeth preserved as steady a silence as either Mrs. Hurst or Miss Bingley; and even Lydia was too much fatigued to utter more than the occasional exclamation of “Lord, how tired I am!” accompanied by a violent yawn.
paras.uz: Janob Bingli va Jeyn boshqalardan biroz chetda birga turishar va faqat bir-biri bilan gaplashishardi. Elizabet missis Xerst yoki miss Bingli kabi barqaror sukut saqladi; hatto Lidiya ham shunchalik charchagan ediki, vaqti-vaqti bilan qattiq esnash bilan birga «Voy, qanchalik charchadim!» deb xitob qilishdan boshqa gap aytmadi.

paras.en: When at length they arose to take leave, Mrs. Bennet was most pressingly civil in her hope of seeing the whole family soon at Longbourn, and addressed herself especially to Mr. Bingley, to assure him how happy he would make them by eating a family dinner with them at any time, without the ceremony of a formal invitation. Bingley was all grateful pleasure, and he readily engaged for taking the earliest opportunity of waiting on her, after his return from London, whither he was obliged to go the next day for a short time.
paras.uz: Nihoyat ular xayrlashish uchun turishganda, missis Bennet butun oilani tez orada Longbornda ko'rishga umid qilishini eng qistovli xushmuomalalik bilan bildirdi va ayniqsa janob Binglige murojaat qilib, rasmiy taklifsiz istalgan vaqtda ular bilan oilaviy tushlik qilsa, ularni qanchalik baxtli qilishini aytib ishontirdi. Bingli minnatdor zavqqa to'la edi va ertasi kuni qisqa muddatga borishga majbur bo'lgan Londondan qaytgach, birinchi imkoniyatda uning huzuriga kelishga darhol va'da berdi.

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet was perfectly satisfied, and quitted the house under the delightful persuasion that, allowing for the necessary preparations of settlements, new carriages, and wedding clothes, she should undoubtedly see her daughter settled at Netherfield in the course of three or four months. Of having another daughter married to Mr. Collins, she thought with equal certainty, and with considerable, though not equal, pleasure. Elizabeth was the least dear to her of all her children; and though the man and the match were quite good enough for her, the worth of each was eclipsed by Mr. Bingley and Netherfield.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet to'liq mamnun edi va nikoh shartnomalari, yangi aravalar va to'y kiyimlari uchun zarur tayyorgarliklarni hisobga olsak ham, uch-to'rt oy ichida qizini Nezerfildda joylashgan holda albatta ko'rishiga yoqimli ishonch bilan uydan chiqdi. Yana bir qizining janob Kollinzga turmushga chiqishi haqida ham xuddi shunday ishonch bilan va teng bo'lmasa ham, ancha katta zavq bilan o'yladi. Elizabet barcha farzandlari ichida unga eng kam aziz edi; garchi erkak ham, nikoh ham uning uchun yetarlicha yaxshi bo'lsa ham, har birining qadri janob Bingli va Nezerfild oldida xira tortardi.

quiz.why_uz: U rad etishga ulgurmay rozi bo'lib qoladi.
