chapters.title: Mr. Collins Proposes
chapters.recap_uz: Kollinz Elizabetga rasmiy ravishda turmush taklif qiladi. Elizabet bir necha marta rad etadi, lekin Kollinz buni «ayollarga xos noz» deb o'ylaydi.

paras.en: The next day opened a new scene at Longbourn. Mr. Collins made his declaration in form. Having resolved to do it without loss of time, as his leave of absence extended only to the following Saturday, and having no feelings of diffidence to make it distressing to himself even at the moment, he set about it in a very orderly manner, with all the observances, which he supposed a regular part of the business. On finding Mrs. Bennet, Elizabeth, and one of the younger girls together, soon after breakfast, he addressed the mother in these words:
paras.uz: Ertasi kun Longbornda yangi sahna ochdi. Janob Kollinz rasman izhor qildi. Ta'tili faqat keyingi shanbagacha bo'lgani uchun buni vaqt yo'qotmasdan qilishga qaror qilib, hatto o'sha lahzada ham buni o'zi uchun azobli qiladigan hech qanday tortinchoqlik tuyg'usiga ega bo'lmagani holda, u bu ishga juda tartibli, ishning odatiy qismi deb hisoblagan barcha rasm-rusumlarga rioya qilib kirishdi. Nonushtadan ko'p o'tmay missis Bennet, Elizabet va kichik qizlardan birini birga topib, u onaga shu so'zlar bilan murojaat qildi:

paras.en: “May I hope, madam, for your interest with your fair daughter Elizabeth, when I solicit for the honour of a private audience with her in the course of this morning?”
paras.uz: «Xonim, bugun ertalab go'zal qizingiz Elizabet bilan yolg'iz suhbatlashish sharafini so'raganimda, sizning qo'llab-quvvatlashingizga umid qilsam bo'ladimi?»

paras.en: Before Elizabeth had time for anything but a blush of surprise, Mrs. Bennet answered instantly, “Oh dear!--yes--certainly. I am sure Lizzy will be very happy--I am sure she can have no objection. Come, Kitty, I want you up stairs.” And, gathering her work together, she was hastening away, when Elizabeth called out:
paras.uz: Elizabet hayratdan qizarishdan boshqa narsaga ulgurmasidan, missis Bennet darhol javob berdi: «Voy! — ha — albatta. Ishonchim komilki, Lizzi juda xursand bo'ladi — ishonchim komilki, uning hech qanday e'tirozi bo'lmaydi. Yur, Ketti, sen menga yuqorida kerakson». Va tikuvini yig'ishtirib, shoshib chiqib ketayotgan edi, Elizabet chaqirdi:

paras.en: “Dear madam, do not go. I beg you will not go. Mr. Collins must excuse me. He can have nothing to say to me that anybody need not hear. I am going away myself.”
paras.uz: «Aziz oyijon, ketmang. Iltimos, ketmang. Janob Kollinz meni kechirishi kerak. Uning menga boshqalar eshitmasligi kerak bo'lgan hech qanday gapi bo'lishi mumkin emas. O'zim ketaman».

paras.en: “No, no, nonsense, Lizzy. I desire you to stay where you are.” And upon Elizabeth's seeming really, with vexed and embarrassed looks, about to escape, she added: “Lizzy, I insist upon your staying and hearing Mr. Collins.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, yo'q, bema'nilik, Lizzi. Turgan joyingda qolishingni xohlayman». Va Elizabet g'ashlangan va xijolat tortgan qiyofada haqiqatan ham qochib ketmoqchi bo'lib ko'ringanida, qo'shib qo'ydi: «Lizzi, qolishingni va janob Kollinzni tinglashingni talab qilaman».

paras.en: Elizabeth would not oppose such an injunction--and a moment's consideration making her also sensible that it would be wisest to get it over as soon and as quietly as possible, she sat down again and tried to conceal, by incessant employment the feelings which were divided between distress and diversion. Mrs. Bennet and Kitty walked off, and as soon as they were gone, Mr. Collins began.
paras.uz: Elizabet bunday buyruqqa qarshi chiqmadi — bir lahzalik mulohaza unga buni iloji boricha tez va jimgina tugatish eng oqilona ekanini ham tushuntirib, u yana o'tirdi va to'xtovsiz mashg'ulot bilan tashvish va kulgi o'rtasida bo'lingan tuyg'ularini yashirishga urindi. Missis Bennet va Ketti chiqib ketishdi va ular ketishi bilan janob Kollinz boshladi.

paras.en: “Believe me, my dear Miss Elizabeth, that your modesty, so far from doing you any disservice, rather adds to your other perfections. You would have been less amiable in my eyes had there not been this little unwillingness; but allow me to assure you, that I have your respected mother's permission for this address. You can hardly doubt the purport of my discourse, however your natural delicacy may lead you to dissemble; my attentions have been too marked to be mistaken. Almost as soon as I entered the house, I singled you out as the companion of my future life. But before I am run away with by my feelings on this subject, perhaps it would be advisable for me to state my reasons for marrying--and, moreover, for coming into Hertfordshire with the design of selecting a wife, as I certainly did.”
paras.uz: «Ishoning, aziz miss Elizabet, sizning kamtarligingiz sizga hech qanday zarar keltirmaydi, aksincha, boshqa fazilatlaringizga qo'shimcha bo'ladi. Agar bu kichik istaksizlik bo'lmaganida, mening ko'zimda kamroq yoqimli bo'lardingiz; lekin ijozat bering, sizni ishontirib aytay, bu murojaat uchun hurmatli onangizning ruxsatini oldim. Tabiiy nozikligingiz sizni o'zingizni bilmaganga olishga undasa ham, nutqimning mazmuniga zo'rg'a shubha qila olasiz; e'tiborlarim xato tushunilishi uchun haddan tashqari aniq bo'lgan. Uyga kirishim bilanoq sizni kelajak hayotimning hamrohi sifatida tanlab oldim. Lekin bu mavzuda tuyg'ularim meni olib ketishidan oldin, ehtimol, uylanish sabablarimni — va bundan tashqari, xotin tanlash niyatida Xertfordshirga kelganimni, chunki albatta shunday qildim, — bayon qilishim maqsadga muvofiq bo'lar».

paras.en: The idea of Mr. Collins, with all his solemn composure, being run away with by his feelings, made Elizabeth so near laughing, that she could not use the short pause he allowed in any attempt to stop him further, and he continued:
paras.uz: Butun salobatli xotirjamligi bilan janob Kollinzni tuyg'ulari olib ketishi haqidagi fikr Elizabetni kulgidan shunchalik yaqin qildiki, u u bergan qisqa sukutdan uni to'xtatishga urinish uchun foydalana olmadi va u davom etdi:

paras.en: “My reasons for marrying are, first, that I think it a right thing for every clergyman in easy circumstances (like myself) to set the example of matrimony in his parish; secondly, that I am convinced that it will add very greatly to my happiness; and thirdly--which perhaps I ought to have mentioned earlier, that it is the particular advice and recommendation of the very noble lady whom I have the honour of calling patroness. Twice has she condescended to give me her opinion (unasked too!) on this subject; and it was but the very Saturday night before I left Hunsford--between our pools at quadrille, while Mrs. Jenkinson was arranging Miss de Bourgh's footstool, that she said, 'Mr. Collins, you must marry. A clergyman like you must marry.
paras.uz: «Uylanish sabablarim quyidagilar: birinchidan, men (o'zimdek) farovon ahvoldagi har bir ruhoniy o'z qavmida nikohga o'rnak ko'rsatishini to'g'ri ish deb bilaman; ikkinchidan, bu baxtimni juda katta oshirishiga aminman; uchinchidan esa — buni, ehtimol, oldinroq aytishim kerak edi — bu homiyam deb atash sharafiga muyassar bo'lgan o'ta oliyjanob xonimning alohida maslahati va tavsiyasidir. U ikki marta bu mavzuda menga fikrini bildirish iltifotini ko'rsatgan (so'ramasam ham!); va aynan Xansforddan ketishimdan oldingi shanba oqshomi — kadril o'yinlarimiz oralig'ida, missis Jenkinson miss de Burgning oyoq kursisini to'g'rilayotganda — u shunday degan edi: "Janob Kollinz, siz uylanishingiz kerak. Sizdek ruhoniy uylanishi kerak.

paras.en: Choose properly, choose a gentlewoman for my sake; and for your own, let her be an active, useful sort of person, not brought up high, but able to make a small income go a good way. This is my advice. Find such a woman as soon as you can, bring her to Hunsford, and I will visit her.' Allow me, by the way, to observe, my fair cousin, that I do not reckon the notice and kindness of Lady Catherine de Bourgh as among the least of the advantages in my power to offer. You will find her manners beyond anything I can describe; and your wit and vivacity, I think, must be acceptable to her, especially when tempered with the silence and respect which her rank will inevitably excite.
paras.uz: To'g'ri tanlang, men uchun nasl-nasabli ayolni tanlang; o'zingiz uchun esa u chaqqon, foydali odam bo'lsin, yuqori darajada tarbiyalanmagan, lekin kichik daromadni ko'pga yetkaza oladigan bo'lsin. Mening maslahatim shu. Bunday ayolni iloji boricha tezroq toping, uni Xansfordga olib keling, men uning oldiga boraman". Aytgancha, go'zal amakivachcham, shuni aytishga ijozat beringki, men ledi Ketrin de Burgning e'tibori va mehribonligini taklif qila oladigan afzalliklarim ichida eng kichigi deb hisoblamayman. Uning muomalasini men tasvirlay oladigan har qanday narsadan ustun deb topasiz; sizning aqlingiz va jo'shqinligingiz esa, menimcha, unga ma'qul bo'lishi kerak, ayniqsa uning martabasi muqarrar ravishda uyg'otadigan sukut va hurmat bilan yumshatilganda.

paras.en: Thus much for my general intention in favour of matrimony; it remains to be told why my views were directed towards Longbourn instead of my own neighbourhood, where I can assure you there are many amiable young women. But the fact is, that being, as I am, to inherit this estate after the death of your honoured father (who, however, may live many years longer), I could not satisfy myself without resolving to choose a wife from among his daughters, that the loss to them might be as little as possible, when the melancholy event takes place--which, however, as I have already said, may not be for several years. This has been my motive, my fair cousin, and I flatter myself it will not sink me in your esteem. And now nothing remains for me but to assure you in the most animated language of the violence of my affection.
paras.uz: Nikoh foydasidagi umumiy niyatim haqida shuncha; endi qarashlarim nega o'z mahallam o'rniga Longbornga qaratilganini aytish qoldi, sizni ishontirib aytamanki, u yerda yoqimli yosh ayollar ko'p. Lekin gap shundaki, men hurmatli otangiz vafotidan keyin (biroq u hali ko'p yillar yashashi mumkin) bu mulkni meros qilib olishim sababli, qayg'uli voqea sodir bo'lganda ularning yo'qotishi iloji boricha kam bo'lishi uchun uning qizlari orasidan xotin tanlashga qaror qilmasdan o'zimni qoniqtira olmadim — biroq, avval aytganimdek, bu bir necha yil bo'lmasligi mumkin. Bu mening sababim edi, go'zal amakivachcham, va umid qilamanki, bu sizning nazaringizda meni pastga tushirmaydi. Endi menga faqat sizni eng jo'shqin so'zlar bilan mehrimning shiddatiga ishontirish qoldi.

paras.en: To fortune I am perfectly indifferent, and shall make no demand of that nature on your father, since I am well aware that it could not be complied with; and that one thousand pounds in the four per cents, which will not be yours till after your mother's decease, is all that you may ever be entitled to. On that head, therefore, I shall be uniformly silent; and you may assure yourself that no ungenerous reproach shall ever pass my lips when we are married.”
paras.uz: Boylikka mutlaqo befarqman va otangizdan bunday talab qo'ymayman, chunki uni bajarish mumkin emasligini yaxshi bilaman; va onangiz vafotidan keyingina sizniki bo'ladigan to'rt foizli ming funt — siz hech qachon haqli bo'lishingiz mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsa. Shuning uchun bu borada doimo jim bo'laman; va ishonishingiz mumkinki, turmush qurganimizda lablarimdan hech qachon tantiqlik bilan qilingan ta'na chiqmaydi».

paras.en: It was absolutely necessary to interrupt him now.
paras.uz: Endi uning gapini bo'lish mutlaqo zarur edi.

paras.en: “You are too hasty, sir,” she cried. “You forget that I have made no answer. Let me do it without further loss of time. Accept my thanks for the compliment you are paying me. I am very sensible of the honour of your proposals, but it is impossible for me to do otherwise than to decline them.”
paras.uz: «Siz haddan tashqari shoshyapsiz, ser, — xitob qildi u. — Men hali javob bermaganimni unutyapsiz. Buni vaqt yo'qotmay qilishimga ruxsat bering. Menga ko'rsatayotgan iltifotingiz uchun minnatdorchiligimni qabul qiling. Taklifingiz sharafini juda yaxshi his qilaman, lekin uni rad etishdan boshqa ilojim yo'q».

paras.en: “I am not now to learn,” replied Mr. Collins, with a formal wave of the hand, “that it is usual with young ladies to reject the addresses of the man whom they secretly mean to accept, when he first applies for their favour; and that sometimes the refusal is repeated a second, or even a third time. I am therefore by no means discouraged by what you have just said, and shall hope to lead you to the altar ere long.”
paras.uz: «Men endi bilib olishim shart emaski, — javob berdi janob Kollinz, rasmiy qo'l silkitib, — yosh xonimlar yashirincha qabul qilmoqchi bo'lgan erkakning murojaatini u birinchi marta iltifot so'raganda rad etishlari odatiy hol; ba'zan esa rad etish ikkinchi, hatto uchinchi marta takrorlanadi. Shuning uchun hozir aytganlaringizdan umuman ruhim tushmaydi va tez orada sizni mehrob oldiga olib borishga umid qilaman».

paras.en: “Upon my word, sir,” cried Elizabeth, “your hope is a rather extraordinary one after my declaration. I do assure you that I am not one of those young ladies (if such young ladies there are) who are so daring as to risk their happiness on the chance of being asked a second time. I am perfectly serious in my refusal. You could not make me happy, and I am convinced that I am the last woman in the world who could make you so. Nay, were your friend Lady Catherine to know me, I am persuaded she would find me in every respect ill qualified for the situation.”
paras.uz: «Ochig'ini aytsam, ser, — xitob qildi Elizabet, — mening bayonotimdan keyin umidingiz ancha g'ayrioddiy. Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, men baxtini ikkinchi marta so'ralish ehtimoliga tikishga jur'at qiladigan yosh xonimlardan (agar bunday yosh xonimlar bo'lsa) emasman. Rad etishimda mutlaqo jiddiyman. Siz meni baxtli qila olmasdingiz va ishonchim komilki, men sizni baxtli qila oladigan dunyodagi eng oxirgi ayolman. Yo'q, agar do'stingiz ledi Ketrin meni bilganida, ishonamanki, u meni bu vaziyat uchun har jihatdan nomaqbul deb topgan bo'lardi».

paras.en: “Were it certain that Lady Catherine would think so,” said Mr. Collins very gravely--“but I cannot imagine that her ladyship would at all disapprove of you. And you may be certain when I have the honour of seeing her again, I shall speak in the very highest terms of your modesty, economy, and other amiable qualification.”
paras.uz: «Agar ledi Ketrin shunday o'ylashi aniq bo'lganida, — dedi janob Kollinz juda jiddiy, — lekin janoblari sizni umuman ma'qullamasligini tasavvur qila olmayman. Va ishonishingiz mumkinki, uni yana ko'rish sharafiga muyassar bo'lganimda, sizning kamtarligingiz, tejamkorligingiz va boshqa yoqimli fazilatlaringiz haqida eng yuksak so'zlar bilan gapiraman».

paras.en: “Indeed, Mr. Collins, all praise of me will be unnecessary. You must give me leave to judge for myself, and pay me the compliment of believing what I say. I wish you very happy and very rich, and by refusing your hand, do all in my power to prevent your being otherwise. In making me the offer, you must have satisfied the delicacy of your feelings with regard to my family, and may take possession of Longbourn estate whenever it falls, without any self-reproach. This matter may be considered, therefore, as finally settled.” And rising as she thus spoke, she would have quitted the room, had Mr. Collins not thus addressed her:
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham, janob Kollinz, meni maqtashning hech qanday hojati yo'q. O'zim uchun o'zim hukm chiqarishimga ruxsat berishingiz va aytganlarimga ishonish iltifotini ko'rsatishingiz kerak. Sizga katta baxt va katta boylik tilayman va qo'lingizni rad etib, aksincha bo'lishining oldini olish uchun qo'limdan kelganini qilaman. Menga taklif qilib, siz oilamga nisbatan tuyg'ularingiz nozikligini qondirgan bo'lsangiz kerak va Longborn mulki qachon sizga o'tsa, hech qanday vijdon azobisiz uni egallashingiz mumkin. Shuning uchun bu masalani butunlay hal bo'lgan deb hisoblash mumkin». Va shunday deb o'rnidan turib, agar janob Kollinz unga shunday murojaat qilmaganida, xonani tark etgan bo'lardi:

paras.en: “When I do myself the honour of speaking to you next on the subject, I shall hope to receive a more favourable answer than you have now given me; though I am far from accusing you of cruelty at present, because I know it to be the established custom of your sex to reject a man on the first application, and perhaps you have even now said as much to encourage my suit as would be consistent with the true delicacy of the female character.”
paras.uz: «Keyingi safar bu mavzuda siz bilan gaplashish sharafiga muyassar bo'lganimda, hozir bergan javobingizdan ko'ra ijobiyroq javob olishga umid qilaman; garchi hozir sizni shafqatsizlikda ayblashdan yiroq bo'lsam ham, chunki erkakni birinchi murojaatda rad etish sizning jinsingizning o'rnatilgan odati ekanini bilaman va ehtimol, siz hozir ham ayol xarakterining haqiqiy nozikligiga mos keladigan darajada sovchiligimni rag'batlantiradigan gaplarni aytgandirsiz».

paras.en: “Really, Mr. Collins,” cried Elizabeth with some warmth, “you puzzle me exceedingly. If what I have hitherto said can appear to you in the form of encouragement, I know not how to express my refusal in such a way as to convince you of its being one.”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham, janob Kollinz, — biroz qizishib xitob qildi Elizabet, — siz meni nihoyatda chalkashtiryapsiz. Agar hozirgacha aytganlarim sizga rag'bat shaklida ko'rinsa, rad etishimni sizni uning rad etish ekaniga ishontiradigan tarzda qanday ifodalashni bilmayman».

paras.en: “You must give me leave to flatter myself, my dear cousin, that your refusal of my addresses is merely words of course. My reasons for believing it are briefly these: It does not appear to me that my hand is unworthy of your acceptance, or that the establishment I can offer would be any other than highly desirable. My situation in life, my connections with the family of de Bourgh, and my relationship to your own, are circumstances highly in my favour; and you should take it into further consideration, that in spite of your manifold attractions, it is by no means certain that another offer of marriage may ever be made you. Your portion is unhappily so small that it will in all likelihood undo the effects of your loveliness and amiable qualifications. As I must therefore conclude that you are not serious in your rejection of me, I shall choose to attribute it to your wish of increasing my love by suspense, according to the usual practice of elegant females.”
paras.uz: «Ruxsat berishingiz kerak, aziz amakivachcham, murojaatlarimni rad etishingiz shunchaki odatiy so'zlar deb o'zimni ovutishimga. Bunga ishonishim sabablari qisqacha shunday: menga qo'lim sizning qabulingizga nomunosib yoki taklif qila oladigan uy-joyim juda orzu qilinadigan narsadan boshqa narsa bo'lib ko'rinmaydi. Hayotdagi mavqeim, de Burglar oilasi bilan aloqalarim va sizning oilangiz bilan qarindoshligim — juda foydamga bo'lgan holatlar; bundan tashqari, shuni ham hisobga olishingiz kerakki, ko'p jozibalaringizga qaramay, sizga yana nikoh taklifi qilinishi umuman aniq emas. Sizning sepingiz afsuski shunchalik kamki, u, ehtimol, go'zalligingiz va yoqimli fazilatlaringiz ta'sirini yo'qqa chiqaradi. Shuning uchun meni rad etishingizda jiddiy emassiz degan xulosaga kelishim kerakligi sababli, buni nafis ayollarning odatiy amaliyotiga ko'ra muhabbatimni intizorlik bilan oshirish istagingizga bog'lashni afzal ko'raman».

paras.en: “I do assure you, sir, that I have no pretensions whatever to that kind of elegance which consists in tormenting a respectable man. I would rather be paid the compliment of being believed sincere. I thank you again and again for the honour you have done me in your proposals, but to accept them is absolutely impossible. My feelings in every respect forbid it. Can I speak plainer? Do not consider me now as an elegant female, intending to plague you, but as a rational creature, speaking the truth from her heart.”
paras.uz: «Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, ser, hurmatli erkakni qiynashdan iborat bunday nafislikka hech qanday da'vom yo'q. Menga samimiy ekanimga ishonish iltifoti ko'rsatilishini afzal ko'raman. Taklifingiz bilan menga ko'rsatgan sharafingiz uchun sizga qayta-qayta rahmat aytaman, lekin uni qabul qilish mutlaqo imkonsiz. Tuyg'ularim har jihatdan buni man etadi. Bundan aniqroq gapira olamanmi? Endi meni sizni qiynashni niyat qilgan nafis ayol deb emas, balki qalbidan haqiqatni gapirayotgan oqil mavjudot deb hisoblang».

paras.en: “You are uniformly charming!” cried he, with an air of awkward gallantry; “and I am persuaded that when sanctioned by the express authority of both your excellent parents, my proposals will not fail of being acceptable.”
paras.uz: «Siz har doim maftunkorsiz! — xitob qildi u beso'naqay xushomad qiyofasida. — Va ishonamanki, ikkala ajoyib ota-onangizning aniq roziligi bilan taklifim albatta ma'qul bo'ladi».

paras.en: To such perseverance in wilful self-deception Elizabeth would make no reply, and immediately and in silence withdrew; determined, if he persisted in considering her repeated refusals as flattering encouragement, to apply to her father, whose negative might be uttered in such a manner as to be decisive, and whose behaviour at least could not be mistaken for the affectation and coquetry of an elegant female.
paras.uz: Bunday ataylab o'zini aldashdagi qat'iyatga Elizabet javob bermadi va darhol, jimgina chiqib ketdi; agar u uning qayta-qayta rad etishlarini xushomadli rag'bat deb hisoblashda davom etsa, otasiga murojaat qilishga qaror qildi — uning rad javobi hal qiluvchi tarzda aytilishi mumkin edi va hech bo'lmaganda uning xatti-harakatini nafis ayolning soxtaligi va noz-karashmasi deb xato tushunib bo'lmasdi.

quiz.q: Why does Mr. Collins not accept Elizabeth's refusal?
o: He thinks elegant women always refuse at first
quiz.why_uz: U o'zining «yaxshi kuyov» ekaniga shubha qilmaydi.

quiz.q: Why does Mr. Collins want to marry?
o: Because Lady Catherine advised him and it is right for a clergyman
quiz.why_uz: Uning sabablari ro'yxati juda kulgili va hissiz.

chapters.title: Mr. Bennet Decides
chapters.recap_uz: Missis Bennet Elizabetni Kollinzga turmushga chiqishga majburlamoqchi. Janob Bennet esa: «Agar unga turmushga chiqmasang, onang seni boshqa ko'rmaydi; chiqsang — men ko'rmayman», deydi.

paras.en: Mr. Collins was not left long to the silent contemplation of his successful love; for Mrs. Bennet, having dawdled about in the vestibule to watch for the end of the conference, no sooner saw Elizabeth open the door and with quick step pass her towards the staircase, than she entered the breakfast-room, and congratulated both him and herself in warm terms on the happy prospect of their nearer connection. Mr. Collins received and returned these felicitations with equal pleasure, and then proceeded to relate the particulars of their interview, with the result of which he trusted he had every reason to be satisfied, since the refusal which his cousin had steadfastly given him would naturally flow from her bashful modesty and the genuine delicacy of her character.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinz muvaffaqiyatli muhabbatini jimgina tafakkur qilish uchun uzoq qoldirilmadi; chunki suhbat tugashini kuzatish uchun dahlizda timirskilanib yurgan missis Bennet Elizabetning eshikni ochib, tez qadam bilan uning yonidan zinapoya tomon o'tib ketganini ko'rishi bilanoq, nonushta xonasiga kirdi va uni ham, o'zini ham ularning yaqinroq qarindosh bo'lishi baxtli istiqboli bilan qizg'in so'zlarda tabrikladi. Janob Kollinz bu tabriklarni xuddi shunday mamnuniyat bilan qabul qildi va qaytardi, keyin suhbatlarining tafsilotlarini aytib berishga kirishdi va uning natijasidan qoniqish uchun barcha asoslari bor deb ishondi, chunki amakivachchasining qat'iy rad etishi tabiiy ravishda uning uyatchan kamtarligi va xarakterining chinakam nozikligidan kelib chiqqan bo'lishi kerak edi.

paras.en: This information, however, startled Mrs. Bennet; she would have been glad to be equally satisfied that her daughter had meant to encourage him by protesting against his proposals, but she dared not believe it, and could not help saying so.
paras.uz: Biroq bu xabar missis Bennetni cho'chitib yubordi; u qizi taklifga qarshi chiqib, uni rag'batlantirmoqchi bo'lganiga xuddi shunday ishonishdan xursand bo'lardi, lekin bunga ishonishga jur'at eta olmadi va buni aytmay qololmadi.

paras.en: “But, depend upon it, Mr. Collins,” she added, “that Lizzy shall be brought to reason. I will speak to her about it directly. She is a very headstrong, foolish girl, and does not know her own interest but I will make her know it.”
paras.uz: «Lekin ishoning, janob Kollinz, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — Lizzini aqlga keltiramiz. U bilan bu haqda darhol gaplashaman. U juda o'jar, ahmoq qiz va o'z manfaatini bilmaydi, lekin men uni bildirib qo'yaman».

paras.en: “Pardon me for interrupting you, madam,” cried Mr. Collins; “but if she is really headstrong and foolish, I know not whether she would altogether be a very desirable wife to a man in my situation, who naturally looks for happiness in the marriage state. If therefore she actually persists in rejecting my suit, perhaps it were better not to force her into accepting me, because if liable to such defects of temper, she could not contribute much to my felicity.”
paras.uz: «Gapingizni bo'lganim uchun kechiring, xonim, — xitob qildi janob Kollinz, — lekin agar u haqiqatan ham o'jar va ahmoq bo'lsa, u tabiiy ravishda nikohda baxt izlaydigan mening ahvolimdagi odam uchun juda maqbul xotin bo'lishini bilmayman. Shuning uchun agar u haqiqatan ham sovchiligimni rad etishda davom etsa, ehtimol uni meni qabul qilishga majburlamaslik yaxshiroqdir, chunki agar u fe'lining bunday kamchiliklariga moyil bo'lsa, baxtimga ko'p hissa qo'sha olmasdi».

paras.en: “Sir, you quite misunderstand me,” said Mrs. Bennet, alarmed. “Lizzy is only headstrong in such matters as these. In everything else she is as good-natured a girl as ever lived. I will go directly to Mr. Bennet, and we shall very soon settle it with her, I am sure.”
paras.uz: «Ser, meni butunlay noto'g'ri tushunyapsiz, — dedi missis Bennet xavotirlanib. — Lizzi faqat shunga o'xshash masalalarda o'jar. Boshqa hamma narsada u dunyodagi eng xushfe'l qiz. Darhol janob Bennetning oldiga boraman va ishonchim komilki, u bilan juda tez hal qilamiz».

paras.en: She would not give him time to reply, but hurrying instantly to her husband, called out as she entered the library, “Oh! Mr. Bennet, you are wanted immediately; we are all in an uproar. You must come and make Lizzy marry Mr. Collins, for she vows she will not have him, and if you do not make haste he will change his mind and not have her.”
paras.uz: U unga javob berishga vaqt bermadi, darhol eriga shoshilib, kutubxonaga kirarkan, qichqirdi: «Oh! Janob Bennet, siz darhol keraksiz; hammamiz to'polondamiz. Kelib, Lizzini janob Kollinzga turmushga chiqishga majbur qilishingiz kerak, chunki u unga tegmayman deb qasam ichyapti, agar shoshilmasangiz, u fikrini o'zgartiradi va unga uylanmaydi».

paras.en: Mr. Bennet raised his eyes from his book as she entered, and fixed them on her face with a calm unconcern which was not in the least altered by her communication.
paras.uz: U kirganida janob Bennet kitobidan ko'zlarini ko'tardi va ularni uning yuziga xotirjam befarqlik bilan qadadi, bu befarqlik uning xabaridan zarracha ham o'zgarmadi.

paras.en: “I have not the pleasure of understanding you,” said he, when she had finished her speech. “Of what are you talking?”
paras.uz: «Sizni tushunish sharafiga muyassar emasman, — dedi u, u nutqini tugatgach. — Nima haqida gapiryapsiz?»

paras.en: “Of Mr. Collins and Lizzy. Lizzy declares she will not have Mr. Collins, and Mr. Collins begins to say that he will not have Lizzy.”
paras.uz: «Janob Kollinz va Lizzi haqida. Lizzi janob Kollinzga tegmasligini e'lon qilyapti, janob Kollinz esa Lizziga uylanmasligini ayta boshladi».

paras.en: “And what am I to do on the occasion? It seems an hopeless business.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, bu holatda men nima qilishim kerak? Bu umidsiz ishga o'xshaydi».

paras.en: “Speak to Lizzy about it yourself. Tell her that you insist upon her marrying him.”
paras.uz: «Lizzi bilan bu haqda o'zingiz gaplashing. Unga uning unga turmushga chiqishini talab qilayotganingizni ayting».

paras.en: “Let her be called down. She shall hear my opinion.”
paras.uz: «Uni pastga chaqirishsin. U mening fikrimni eshitadi».

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet rang the bell, and Miss Elizabeth was summoned to the library.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet qo'ng'iroq chaldi va miss Elizabet kutubxonaga chaqirildi.

paras.en: “Come here, child,” cried her father as she appeared. “I have sent for you on an affair of importance. I understand that Mr. Collins has made you an offer of marriage. Is it true?” Elizabeth replied that it was. “Very well--and this offer of marriage you have refused?”
paras.uz: «Bu yoqqa kel, bolam, — xitob qildi otasi u paydo bo'lganda. — Seni muhim ish bo'yicha chaqirtirdim. Tushunishimcha, janob Kollinz senga turmush qurishni taklif qilibdi. Rostmi?» Elizabet rost ekanini aytdi. «Juda yaxshi — va sen bu nikoh taklifini rad etdingmi?»

paras.en: “I have, sir.”
paras.uz: «Rad etdim, ser».

paras.en: “Very well. We now come to the point. Your mother insists upon your accepting it. Is it not so, Mrs. Bennet?”
paras.uz: «Juda yaxshi. Endi asosiy masalaga keldik. Onang uni qabul qilishingni talab qilyapti. Shunday emasmi, missis Bennet?»

paras.en: “Yes, or I will never see her again.”
paras.uz: «Ha, aks holda uni boshqa hech qachon ko'rmayman».

paras.en: “An unhappy alternative is before you, Elizabeth. From this day you must be a stranger to one of your parents. Your mother will never see you again if you do not marry Mr. Collins, and I will never see you again if you do.”
paras.uz: «Oldingda baxtsiz tanlov turibdi, Elizabet. Bugundan boshlab ota-onangdan biriga begona bo'lishing kerak. Agar janob Kollinzga turmushga chiqmasang, onang seni boshqa hech qachon ko'rmaydi, agar chiqsang, men seni boshqa hech qachon ko'rmayman».

paras.en: Elizabeth could not but smile at such a conclusion of such a beginning, but Mrs. Bennet, who had persuaded herself that her husband regarded the affair as she wished, was excessively disappointed.
paras.uz: Elizabet bunday boshlanishning bunday yakunidan jilmaymay qololmadi, lekin eri ishga o'zi istagandek qaraydi deb o'zini ishontirgan missis Bennetning hafsalasi qattiq pir bo'ldi.

paras.en: “What do you mean, Mr. Bennet, in talking this way? You promised me to insist upon her marrying him.”
paras.uz: «Bunday gapirib nima demoqchisiz, janob Bennet? Siz menga uning unga turmushga chiqishini talab qilishga va'da bergan edingiz».

paras.en: “My dear,” replied her husband, “I have two small favours to request. First, that you will allow me the free use of my understanding on the present occasion; and secondly, of my room. I shall be glad to have the library to myself as soon as may be.”
paras.uz: «Azizim, — javob berdi eri, — ikkita kichik iltimosim bor. Birinchidan, hozirgi holatda aqlimdan erkin foydalanishimga ruxsat berishingiz; ikkinchidan esa, xonamdan. Kutubxonani iloji boricha tezroq o'zimga qoldirishsa, xursand bo'lardim».

paras.en: Not yet, however, in spite of her disappointment in her husband, did Mrs. Bennet give up the point. She talked to Elizabeth again and again; coaxed and threatened her by turns. She endeavoured to secure Jane in her interest; but Jane, with all possible mildness, declined interfering; and Elizabeth, sometimes with real earnestness, and sometimes with playful gaiety, replied to her attacks. Though her manner varied, however, her determination never did.
paras.uz: Biroq eridan hafsalasi pir bo'lishiga qaramay, missis Bennet hali ham bu masaladan voz kechmadi. U Elizabet bilan qayta-qayta gaplashdi; navbatma-navbat erkaladi va qo'rqitdi. U Jeynni o'z tomoniga og'dirishga urindi; lekin Jeyn iloji boricha muloyimlik bilan aralashishdan bosh tortdi; Elizabet esa ba'zan chinakam jiddiylik bilan, ba'zan o'ynoqi shodlik bilan uning hujumlariga javob berdi. Biroq uning uslubi o'zgarsa ham, qat'iyati hech qachon o'zgarmadi.

paras.en: Mr. Collins, meanwhile, was meditating in solitude on what had passed. He thought too well of himself to comprehend on what motives his cousin could refuse him; and though his pride was hurt, he suffered in no other way. His regard for her was quite imaginary; and the possibility of her deserving her mother's reproach prevented his feeling any regret.
paras.uz: Bu orada janob Kollinz yolg'izlikda bo'lib o'tgan voqealar haqida mulohaza yuritardi. U o'zi haqida shunchalik yaxshi o'ylardiki, amakivachchasi uni qanday sabablarga ko'ra rad etishi mumkinligini tushuna olmadi; garchi g'ururi ranjigan bo'lsa ham, boshqa hech qanday tarzda azob chekmadi. Uning unga bo'lgan mehri butunlay xayoliy edi; uning onasining tanbehiga loyiq bo'lishi ehtimoli esa unga hech qanday afsus his qilishga yo'l qo'ymadi.

paras.en: While the family were in this confusion, Charlotte Lucas came to spend the day with them. She was met in the vestibule by Lydia, who, flying to her, cried in a half whisper, “I am glad you are come, for there is such fun here! What do you think has happened this morning? Mr. Collins has made an offer to Lizzy, and she will not have him.”
paras.uz: Oila shu sarosimada bo'lganida, Sharlotta Lukas kunni ular bilan o'tkazish uchun keldi. Uni dahlizda Lidiya kutib oldi, u uning oldiga yugurib kelib, yarim pichirlab qichqirdi: «Kelganingdan xursandman, chunki bu yerda shunday qiziq gaplar! Bugun ertalab nima bo'ldi deb o'ylaysan? Janob Kollinz Lizziga taklif qildi, u esa unga tegmaydi».

paras.en: Charlotte hardly had time to answer, before they were joined by Kitty, who came to tell the same news; and no sooner had they entered the breakfast-room, where Mrs. Bennet was alone, than she likewise began on the subject, calling on Miss Lucas for her compassion, and entreating her to persuade her friend Lizzy to comply with the wishes of all her family. “Pray do, my dear Miss Lucas,” she added in a melancholy tone, “for nobody is on my side, nobody takes part with me. I am cruelly used, nobody feels for my poor nerves.”
paras.uz: Sharlotta javob berishga zo'rg'a ulgurdi, ularga xuddi shu yangilikni aytish uchun kelgan Ketti qo'shildi; ular missis Bennet yolg'iz o'tirgan nonushta xonasiga kirishlari bilanoq, u ham xuddi shu mavzuni boshladi, miss Lukasdan hamdardlik so'radi va dugonasi Lizzini butun oilasining istaklariga ko'nishga ko'ndirishini iltimos qildi. «Iltimos, shunday qiling, aziz miss Lukas, — qo'shib qo'ydi u g'amgin ohangda, — chunki hech kim men tomonda emas, hech kim meni qo'llab-quvvatlamaydi. Menga shafqatsizlarcha munosabatda bo'lishyapti, hech kim bechora asablarimga achinmaydi».

paras.en: Charlotte's reply was spared by the entrance of Jane and Elizabeth.
paras.uz: Sharlottani javob berishdan Jeyn va Elizabetning kirib kelishi qutqardi.

paras.en: “Aye, there she comes,” continued Mrs. Bennet, “looking as unconcerned as may be, and caring no more for us than if we were at York, provided she can have her own way. But I tell you, Miss Lizzy--if you take it into your head to go on refusing every offer of marriage in this way, you will never get a husband at all--and I am sure I do not know who is to maintain you when your father is dead. I shall not be able to keep you--and so I warn you. I have done with you from this very day. I told you in the library, you know, that I should never speak to you again, and you will find me as good as my word. I have no pleasure in talking to undutiful children. Not that I have much pleasure, indeed, in talking to anybody. People who suffer as I do from nervous complaints can have no great inclination for talking. Nobody can tell what I suffer! But it is always so. Those who do not complain are never pitied.”
paras.uz: «Ha, mana u keldi, — davom etdi missis Bennet, — iloji boricha befarq qiyofada, faqat o'z bilganini qila olsa bo'ldi, bizga Yorkda bo'lganimizdagidan ortiq ahamiyat bermaydi. Lekin sizga aytaman, miss Lizzi — agar har bir nikoh taklifini shu tarzda rad etishda davom etishni boshingizga olsangiz, umuman er topa olmaysiz — va ishonchim komilki, otangiz vafot etgach, sizni kim boqishini bilmayman. Men sizni boqa olmayman — shuning uchun sizni ogohlantiraman. Bugundan boshlab siz bilan ishim tugadi. Bilasizmi, kutubxonada siz bilan boshqa hech qachon gaplashmasligimni aytgan edim va so'zimning ustidan chiqishimni ko'rasiz. Itoatsiz bolalar bilan gaplashishdan zavq olmayman. Aslida, umuman hech kim bilan gaplashishdan ko'p zavq olmayman. Men kabi asab kasalliklaridan azob chekadigan odamlarning gapirishga unchalik moyilligi bo'lmaydi. Hech kim mening qanday azob chekayotganimni ayta olmaydi! Lekin doim shunday. Shikoyat qilmaydiganlarga hech qachon achinishmaydi».

paras.en: Her daughters listened in silence to this effusion, sensible that any attempt to reason with her or soothe her would only increase the irritation. She talked on, therefore, without interruption from any of them, till they were joined by Mr. Collins, who entered the room with an air more stately than usual, and on perceiving whom, she said to the girls, “Now, I do insist upon it, that you, all of you, hold your tongues, and let me and Mr. Collins have a little conversation together.”
paras.uz: Qizlari bu to'lqinni jimgina tinglashdi, chunki u bilan mantiqan gaplashish yoki uni tinchlantirishga har qanday urinish faqat g'azabini oshirishini bilishardi. Shuning uchun u hech biri gapini bo'lmasdan gapirishda davom etdi, toki ularga xonaga odatdagidan ham salobatliroq qiyofada kirgan janob Kollinz qo'shildi; uni ko'rib, u qizlarga dedi: «Endi hammangiz tilingizni tiyishingizni va menga janob Kollinz bilan biroz gaplashishga imkon berishingizni qat'iy talab qilaman».

paras.en: Elizabeth passed quietly out of the room, Jane and Kitty followed, but Lydia stood her ground, determined to hear all she could; and Charlotte, detained first by the civility of Mr. Collins, whose inquiries after herself and all her family were very minute, and then by a little curiosity, satisfied herself with walking to the window and pretending not to hear. In a doleful voice Mrs. Bennet began the projected conversation: “Oh! Mr. Collins!”
paras.uz: Elizabet jimgina xonadan chiqib ketdi, Jeyn va Ketti uning ortidan ketishdi, lekin Lidiya iloji boricha hamma narsani eshitishga qaror qilib, joyida qoldi; Sharlotta esa avval o'zi va butun oilasi haqida juda batafsil so'ragan janob Kollinzning xushmuomalaligi, keyin esa biroz qiziqish bilan ushlanib qolib, deraza oldiga borib, eshitmaganga olish bilan kifoyalandi. Missis Bennet rejalashtirilgan suhbatni g'amgin ovozda boshladi: «Oh! Janob Kollinz!»

paras.en: “My dear madam,” replied he, “let us be for ever silent on this point. Far be it from me,” he presently continued, in a voice that marked his displeasure, “to resent the behaviour of your daughter. Resignation to inevitable evils is the duty of us all; the peculiar duty of a young man who has been so fortunate as I have been in early preferment; and I trust I am resigned. Perhaps not the less so from feeling a doubt of my positive happiness had my fair cousin honoured me with her hand; for I have often observed that resignation is never so perfect as when the blessing denied begins to lose somewhat of its value in our estimation.
paras.uz: «Aziz xonim, — javob berdi u, — bu masalada abadiy jim bo'laylik. Qizingizning xatti-harakatidan ranjish mendan yiroq, — davom etdi u tez orada noroziligini bildiruvchi ovozda. — Muqarrar yomonliklarga bo'ysunish barchamizning burchimiz; ayniqsa men kabi erta martabaga erishgan yosh yigitning alohida burchi; va ishonamanki, men bo'ysundim. Ehtimol, go'zal amakivachcham meni qo'li bilan sharaflaganida haqiqiy baxtim haqida shubha qilganim uchun bundan kam emasdir; chunki men tez-tez kuzatganmanki, rad etilgan ne'mat bizning nazarimizda qadrini biroz yo'qota boshlaganda, bo'ysunish hech qachon bunchalik mukammal bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: You will not, I hope, consider me as showing any disrespect to your family, my dear madam, by thus withdrawing my pretensions to your daughter's favour, without having paid yourself and Mr. Bennet the compliment of requesting you to interpose your authority in my behalf. My conduct may, I fear, be objectionable in having accepted my dismission from your daughter's lips instead of your own. But we are all liable to error. I have certainly meant well through the whole affair. My object has been to secure an amiable companion for myself, with due consideration for the advantage of all your family, and if my manner has been at all reprehensible, I here beg leave to apologise.”
paras.uz: Umid qilamanki, aziz xonim, sizdan va janob Bennetdan mening foydamga obro'ingizni ishlatishni iltimos qilish iltifotini ko'rsatmasdan, qizingizning iltifotiga da'volarimni shu tarzda qaytarib olishim bilan oilangizga hech qanday hurmatsizlik ko'rsatayotgan deb hisoblamaysiz. Qo'rqamanki, rad javobimni sizning lablaringizdan emas, qizingizning lablaridan qabul qilganim uchun xatti-harakatim e'tirozli bo'lishi mumkin. Lekin barchamiz xato qilishimiz mumkin. Butun ish davomida niyatim, albatta, yaxshi bo'lgan. Maqsadim butun oilangizning manfaatini munosib hisobga olgan holda o'zim uchun yoqimli hamroh topish edi va agar uslubim umuman tanbehga loyiq bo'lgan bo'lsa, shu yerda uzr so'rashga ijozat so'rayman».

quiz.q: What does Mr. Bennet say to Elizabeth?
o: Her mother will never see her again if she doesn't, and he won't if she does
quiz.why_uz: Bu — romanning eng kulgili jumlalaridan biri.

quiz.q: Whose side does Mr. Bennet take?
quiz.why_uz: U aqlli qiziga ishonadi va uni qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

chapters.title: Bingley Leaves
chapters.recap_uz: Bingleylar to'satdan Londonga ketadi. Miss Bingli Jeynga xat yozib, akasi qaytmasligini va Darsining singlisiga uylanishi mumkinligini aytadi. Jeyn xafa bo'ladi.

paras.en: The discussion of Mr. Collins's offer was now nearly at an end, and Elizabeth had only to suffer from the uncomfortable feelings necessarily attending it, and occasionally from some peevish allusions of her mother. As for the gentleman himself, his feelings were chiefly expressed, not by embarrassment or dejection, or by trying to avoid her, but by stiffness of manner and resentful silence. He scarcely ever spoke to her, and the assiduous attentions which he had been so sensible of himself were transferred for the rest of the day to Miss Lucas, whose civility in listening to him was a seasonable relief to them all, and especially to her friend.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinzning taklifi haqidagi muhokama endi deyarli tugagan edi va Elizabetga faqat u bilan muqarrar bog'liq bo'lgan noqulay tuyg'ulardan, vaqti-vaqti bilan esa onasining ba'zi jizzaki ishoralaridan azob chekish qolgan edi. Janobning o'ziga kelsak, uning tuyg'ulari asosan xijolat yoki tushkunlik bilan yoki undan qochishga urinish bilan emas, balki muomaladagi qotib qolganlik va ranjigan sukut bilan ifodalanardi. U u bilan deyarli gaplashmadi va o'zi juda yaxshi his qilgan tirishqoq e'tiborlari kunning qolgan qismida miss Lukasga o'tdi; uning uni tinglashdagi xushmuomalaligi hammaga, ayniqsa dugonasiga o'z vaqtida kelgan yengillik bo'ldi.

paras.en: The morrow produced no abatement of Mrs. Bennet's ill-humour or ill health. Mr. Collins was also in the same state of angry pride. Elizabeth had hoped that his resentment might shorten his visit, but his plan did not appear in the least affected by it. He was always to have gone on Saturday, and to Saturday he meant to stay.
paras.uz: Ertasi kun missis Bennetning yomon kayfiyatini ham, yomon sog'lig'ini ham yengillashtirmadi. Janob Kollinz ham xuddi o'sha g'azabli g'urur holatida edi. Elizabet uning ranjishi tashrifini qisqartirishiga umid qilgan edi, lekin uning rejasiga bu zarracha ta'sir qilmaganga o'xshardi. U doim shanba kuni ketishi kerak edi va shanbagacha qolmoqchi edi.

paras.en: After breakfast, the girls walked to Meryton to inquire if Mr. Wickham were returned, and to lament over his absence from the Netherfield ball. He joined them on their entering the town, and attended them to their aunt's where his regret and vexation, and the concern of everybody, was well talked over. To Elizabeth, however, he voluntarily acknowledged that the necessity of his absence had been self-imposed.
paras.uz: Nonushtadan keyin qizlar janob Uikhem qaytganmi, deb so'rash va uning Nezerfild balida yo'qligidan nolish uchun Meritonga piyoda borishdi. U shaharga kirishlari bilan ularga qo'shildi va ularni xolalarinikiga kuzatib bordi, u yerda uning afsusi va g'ashligi hamda hammaning tashvishi yaxshilab muhokama qilindi. Biroq Elizabetga u yo'qligi zarurati o'zi tomonidan qo'yilganini o'z ixtiyori bilan tan oldi.

paras.en: “I found,” said he, “as the time drew near that I had better not meet Mr. Darcy; that to be in the same room, the same party with him for so many hours together, might be more than I could bear, and that scenes might arise unpleasant to more than myself.”
paras.uz: «Vaqt yaqinlashgan sari tushundimki, — dedi u, — janob Darsi bilan uchrashmaganim ma'qul; u bilan bir xonada, bir davrada shuncha soat birga bo'lish men bardosh bera oladiganimdan ortiq bo'lishi va nafaqat men uchun yoqimsiz sahnalar yuzaga kelishi mumkin edi».

paras.en: She highly approved his forbearance, and they had leisure for a full discussion of it, and for all the commendation which they civilly bestowed on each other, as Wickham and another officer walked back with them to Longbourn, and during the walk he particularly attended to her. His accompanying them was a double advantage; she felt all the compliment it offered to herself, and it was most acceptable as an occasion of introducing him to her father and mother.
paras.uz: U uning o'zini tutishini juda ma'qulladi va ular buni to'liq muhokama qilishga, bir-birlariga xushmuomalalik bilan aytgan barcha maqtovlarga vaqt topishdi, chunki Uikhem va yana bir ofitser ular bilan Longborngacha qaytib borishdi va yo'l davomida u ayniqsa unga e'tibor berdi. Uning ularni kuzatib borishi ikki tomonlama foydali edi; u bu o'ziga ko'rsatilgan iltifotni to'liq his qildi va bu uni otasi va onasi bilan tanishtirish imkoniyati sifatida ham juda ma'qul edi.

paras.en: Soon after their return, a letter was delivered to Miss Bennet; it came from Netherfield. The envelope contained a sheet of elegant, little, hot-pressed paper, well covered with a lady's fair, flowing hand; and Elizabeth saw her sister's countenance change as she read it, and saw her dwelling intently on some particular passages. Jane recollected herself soon, and putting the letter away, tried to join with her usual cheerfulness in the general conversation; but Elizabeth felt an anxiety on the subject which drew off her attention even from Wickham; and no sooner had he and his companion taken leave, than a glance from Jane invited her to follow her up stairs. When they had gained their own room, Jane, taking out the letter, said:
paras.uz: Ular qaytganidan ko'p o'tmay, miss Bennetga xat keltirildi; u Nezerfilddan kelgan edi. Konvertda nafis, kichkina, silliqlangan qog'oz varag'i bor edi, u ayolning chiroyli, ravon husnixati bilan to'la yozilgan edi; Elizabet opasining xatni o'qiyotganda yuzi o'zgarganini va ba'zi alohida joylarga diqqat bilan to'xtalayotganini ko'rdi. Jeyn tez orada o'zini tutib oldi va xatni chetga qo'yib, odatdagi shodligi bilan umumiy suhbatga qo'shilishga urindi; lekin Elizabet bu masalada shunday tashvishni his qildiki, u uning e'tiborini hatto Uikhemdan ham chalg'itdi; u va hamrohi xayrlashishlari bilanoq, Jeynning bir qarashi uni ortidan yuqoriga chiqishga taklif qildi. O'z xonalariga yetib kelgach, Jeyn xatni chiqarib, dedi:

paras.en: “This is from Caroline Bingley; what it contains has surprised me a good deal. The whole party have left Netherfield by this time, and are on their way to town--and without any intention of coming back again. You shall hear what she says.”
paras.uz: «Bu Kerolayn Binglidan; unda yozilganlar meni ancha hayratga soldi. Butun davra hozirga kelib Nezerfildni tark etib, Londonga yo'lga chiqdi — va qaytib kelish niyati yo'q. Uning nima deganini eshitasan».

paras.en: She then read the first sentence aloud, which comprised the information of their having just resolved to follow their brother to town directly, and of their meaning to dine in Grosvenor Street, where Mr. Hurst had a house. The next was in these words: “I do not pretend to regret anything I shall leave in Hertfordshire, except your society, my dearest friend; but we will hope, at some future period, to enjoy many returns of that delightful intercourse we have known, and in the meanwhile may lessen the pain of separation by a very frequent and most unreserved correspondence. I depend on you for that.” To these highflown expressions Elizabeth listened with all the insensibility of distrust; and though the suddenness of their removal surprised her, she saw nothing in it really to lament; it was not to be supposed that their absence from Netherfield would prevent Mr. Bingley's being there; and as to the loss of their society, she was persuaded that Jane must cease to regard it, in the enjoyment of his.
paras.uz: Keyin u birinchi jumlani ovoz chiqarib o'qidi, unda ular akalari ortidan darhol Londonga borishga hozirgina qaror qilganlari va janob Xerstning uyi bo'lgan Grosvenor ko'chasida tushlik qilmoqchi ekanlari haqidagi xabar bor edi. Keyingisi shunday edi: «Xertfordshirda qoldiradigan hech narsamga afsuslanaman deb da'vo qilmayman, faqat sizning davrangizdan tashqari, eng aziz dugonam; lekin umid qilamizki, kelajakda biz bilgan o'sha yoqimli muloqotning ko'p takrorlanishidan zavqlanamiz, hozircha esa juda tez-tez va eng ochiq yozishmalar bilan ajralish og'rig'ini kamaytirishimiz mumkin. Bunda sizga ishonaman». Bu dabdabali iboralarni Elizabet ishonchsizlikning butun befarqligi bilan tingladi; garchi ularning to'satdan ketishi uni hayratga solgan bo'lsa ham, u bunda chindan ham nolish kerak bo'lgan hech narsa ko'rmadi; ularning Nezerfildda yo'qligi janob Binglining u yerda bo'lishiga to'sqinlik qiladi deb o'ylash mumkin emasdi; ularning davrasini yo'qotishga kelsak, u Jeyn uning davrasidan zavqlanib, buni qadrlashni to'xtatishi kerak, deb ishonardi.

paras.en: “It is unlucky,” said she, after a short pause, “that you should not be able to see your friends before they leave the country. But may we not hope that the period of future happiness to which Miss Bingley looks forward may arrive earlier than she is aware, and that the delightful intercourse you have known as friends will be renewed with yet greater satisfaction as sisters? Mr. Bingley will not be detained in London by them.”
paras.uz: «Afsuski, — dedi u qisqa sukutdan keyin, — dugonalaringiz bu yerlardan ketishdan oldin ularni ko'ra olmaysan. Lekin miss Bingli intizorlik bilan kutayotgan kelajakdagi baxt davri u kutganidan ertaroq kelishiga va do'st sifatida bilgan yoqimli muloqotingiz opa-singil sifatida yanada katta mamnuniyat bilan yangilanishiga umid qilsak bo'lmaydimi? Janob Binglini ular Londonda ushlab qola olmaydi».

paras.en: “Caroline decidedly says that none of the party will return into Hertfordshire this winter. I will read it to you:”
paras.uz: «Kerolayn qat'iy aytyaptiki, davradan hech kim bu qish Xertfordshirga qaytmaydi. Senga o'qib beraman:»

paras.en: “When my brother left us yesterday, he imagined that the business which took him to London might be concluded in three or four days; but as we are certain it cannot be so, and at the same time convinced that when Charles gets to town he will be in no hurry to leave it again, we have determined on following him thither, that he may not be obliged to spend his vacant hours in a comfortless hotel. Many of my acquaintances are already there for the winter; I wish that I could hear that you, my dearest friend, had any intention of making one of the crowd--but of that I despair. I sincerely hope your Christmas in Hertfordshire may abound in the gaieties which that season generally brings, and that your beaux will be so numerous as to prevent your feeling the loss of the three of whom we shall deprive you.”
paras.uz: «Akam kecha bizni tark etganida, uni Londonga olib ketgan ish uch-to'rt kunda tugashi mumkin deb o'yladi; lekin bunday bo'lmasligiga amin bo'lganimiz va shu bilan birga Charlz shaharga yetib borgach, uni yana tark etishga shoshilmasligiga ishonganimiz uchun, u bo'sh soatlarini noqulay mehmonxonada o'tkazishga majbur bo'lmasligi uchun uning ortidan u yerga borishga qaror qildik. Tanishlarimning ko'pchiligi allaqachon qishni o'tkazish uchun u yerda; sizning ham, eng aziz dugonam, olomonga qo'shilish niyatingiz borligini eshitishni istardim — lekin bundan umidimni uzganman. Chin dildan umid qilamanki, Xertfordshirdagi Rojdestvoyingiz bu fasl odatda olib keladigan quvnoqliklarga boy bo'ladi va xushtorlaringiz shunchalik ko'p bo'ladiki, biz sizni mahrum qiladigan uch kishining yo'qligini his qilmaysiz».

paras.en: “It is evident by this,” added Jane, “that he comes back no more this winter.”
paras.uz: «Bundan aniq ko'rinib turibdiki, — qo'shib qo'ydi Jeyn, — u bu qish boshqa qaytmaydi».

paras.en: “It is only evident that Miss Bingley does not mean that he should.”
paras.uz: «Faqat miss Bingli uning qaytishini istamasligi aniq ko'rinib turibdi».

paras.en: “Why will you think so? It must be his own doing. He is his own master. But you do not know all. I will read you the passage which particularly hurts me. I will have no reserves from you.”
paras.uz: «Nega bunday o'ylaysan? Bu uning o'z ishi bo'lsa kerak. U o'z-o'ziga xo'jayin. Lekin sen hammasini bilmaysan. Seni menga ayniqsa og'riq bergan joyni o'qib beraman. Sendan hech narsa yashirmayman».

paras.en: “Mr. Darcy is impatient to see his sister; and, to confess the truth, we are scarcely less eager to meet her again. I really do not think Georgiana Darcy has her equal for beauty, elegance, and accomplishments; and the affection she inspires in Louisa and myself is heightened into something still more interesting, from the hope we dare entertain of her being hereafter our sister. I do not know whether I ever before mentioned to you my feelings on this subject; but I will not leave the country without confiding them, and I trust you will not esteem them unreasonable. My brother admires her greatly already; he will have frequent opportunity now of seeing her on the most intimate footing; her relations all wish the connection as much as his own; and a sister's partiality is not misleading me, I think, when I call Charles most capable of engaging any woman's heart. With all these circumstances to favour an attachment, and nothing to prevent it, am I wrong, my dearest Jane, in indulging the hope of an event which will secure the happiness of so many?”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi singlisini ko'rishga sabrsizlanmoqda; rostini aytsam, biz ham u bilan yana uchrashishga undan kam intilmaymiz. Haqiqatan ham Jorjiana Darsiga go'zallik, nafosat va hunarlarda teng keladigan odam yo'q deb o'ylayman; u Luiza bilan menda uyg'otgan mehr uning kelajakda opa-singlimiz bo'lishi haqida jur'at qilib kutayotgan umidimiz tufayli yanada qiziqarliroq narsaga aylanadi. Bu masaladagi tuyg'ularimni sizga avval aytganmanmi, bilmayman; lekin ularni sizga ishonib aytmasdan bu yerlarni tark etmayman va umid qilamanki, ularni asossiz deb hisoblamaysiz. Akam allaqachon undan juda maftun; endi uni eng yaqin munosabatda ko'rish uchun tez-tez imkoniyati bo'ladi; uning qarindoshlari ham akamning qarindoshlari kabi bu qarindoshlikni xohlaydi; va menimcha, Charlzni har qanday ayolning qalbini zabt etishga eng qodir deb ataganimda, singillik tarafkashligi meni chalg'itmayapti. Bu barcha holatlar bog'lanishga yordam berib turganda va unga hech narsa to'sqinlik qilmayotganda, eng aziz Jeyn, shuncha odamning baxtini ta'minlaydigan voqea umidiga berilib, xato qilyapmanmi?»

paras.en: “What do you think of this sentence, my dear Lizzy?” said Jane as she finished it. “Is it not clear enough? Does it not expressly declare that Caroline neither expects nor wishes me to be her sister; that she is perfectly convinced of her brother's indifference; and that if she suspects the nature of my feelings for him, she means (most kindly!) to put me on my guard? Can there be any other opinion on the subject?”
paras.uz: «Bu jumla haqida nima deb o'ylaysan, azizim Lizzi? — dedi Jeyn uni tugatgach. — Yetarlicha aniq emasmi? Kerolayn mening opa-singlisi bo'lishimni na kutishini, na xohlashini; akasining befarqligiga to'liq ishonishini; va agar unga bo'lgan tuyg'ularimning tabiatidan shubhalansa, meni (juda mehribonlik bilan!) ogohlantirmoqchi ekanini ochiq-oydin e'lon qilmayaptimi? Bu masalada boshqa fikr bo'lishi mumkinmi?»

paras.en: “Yes, there can; for mine is totally different. Will you hear it?”
paras.uz: «Ha, bo'lishi mumkin; chunki meniki butunlay boshqacha. Eshitasanmi?»

paras.en: “Most willingly.”
paras.uz: «Jon deb».

paras.en: “You shall have it in a few words. Miss Bingley sees that her brother is in love with you, and wants him to marry Miss Darcy. She follows him to town in hope of keeping him there, and tries to persuade you that he does not care about you.”
paras.uz: «Uni bir necha so'zda aytaman. Miss Bingli akasi senga oshiq ekanini ko'ryapti va uning miss Darsiga uylanishini istaydi. U uni u yerda ushlab qolish umidida uning ortidan shaharga boryapti va seni u senga ahamiyat bermasligiga ishontirishga urinyapti».

paras.en: Jane shook her head.
paras.uz: Jeyn boshini chayqadi.

paras.en: “Indeed, Jane, you ought to believe me. No one who has ever seen you together can doubt his affection. Miss Bingley, I am sure, cannot. She is not such a simpleton. Could she have seen half as much love in Mr. Darcy for herself, she would have ordered her wedding clothes. But the case is this: We are not rich enough or grand enough for them; and she is the more anxious to get Miss Darcy for her brother, from the notion that when there has been one intermarriage, she may have less trouble in achieving a second; in which there is certainly some ingenuity, and I dare say it would succeed, if Miss de Bourgh were out of the way. But, my dearest Jane, you cannot seriously imagine that because Miss Bingley tells you her brother greatly admires Miss Darcy, he is in the smallest degree less sensible of your merit than when he took leave of you on Tuesday, or that it will be in her power to persuade him that, instead of being in love with you, he is very much in love with her friend.”
paras.uz: «Rostdan ham, Jeyn, menga ishonishing kerak. Sizlarni birga ko'rgan hech kim uning mehriga shubha qila olmaydi. Ishonchim komilki, miss Bingli ham qila olmaydi. U unchalik ahmoq emas. Agar u janob Darsida o'ziga nisbatan buning yarmicha muhabbatni ko'rganida, to'y kiyimlariga buyurtma bergan bo'lardi. Lekin gap shunda: biz ular uchun yetarlicha boy yoki yetarlicha ulug' emasmiz; u esa bir marta o'zaro nikoh bo'lgach, ikkinchisiga erishish osonroq bo'ladi degan fikr bilan miss Darsini akasiga olishga yanada intilyapti; bunda, albatta, ma'lum bir zukkolik bor va ishonamanki, agar miss de Burg yo'lda bo'lmaganida, bu muvaffaqiyatli bo'lardi. Lekin, eng aziz Jeyn, miss Bingli senga akasi miss Darsidan juda maftun ekanini aytgani uchun u seshanba kuni sen bilan xayrlashgandagidan sening fazilatlaringni zarracha kamroq his qiladi yoki uni senga oshiq bo'lish o'rniga uning dugonasiga qattiq oshiq ekaniga ishontirish uning qo'lidan keladi, deb jiddiy tasavvur qila olmaysan».

paras.en: “If we thought alike of Miss Bingley,” replied Jane, “your representation of all this might make me quite easy. But I know the foundation is unjust. Caroline is incapable of wilfully deceiving anyone; and all that I can hope in this case is that she is deceiving herself.”
paras.uz: «Agar miss Bingli haqida bir xil o'ylaganimizda, — javob berdi Jeyn, — bularning hammasini bunday tasvirlashing meni butunlay tinchlantirishi mumkin edi. Lekin asos adolatsiz ekanini bilaman. Kerolayn hech kimni ataylab aldashga qodir emas; bu holatda umid qila oladiganim shuki, u o'zini o'zi aldayapti».

paras.en: “That is right. You could not have started a more happy idea, since you will not take comfort in mine. Believe her to be deceived, by all means. You have now done your duty by her, and must fret no longer.”
paras.uz: «To'g'ri. Meniki bilan taskin topmaganing uchun bundan baxtliroq fikrni o'ylab topa olmasding. Uni aldangan deb ishon, albatta. Endi unga nisbatan burchingni bajarding va boshqa kuyinmasliging kerak».

paras.en: “But, my dear sister, can I be happy, even supposing the best, in accepting a man whose sisters and friends are all wishing him to marry elsewhere?”
paras.uz: «Lekin, azizim singlim, eng yaxshisini taxmin qilganda ham, opa-singillari va do'stlarining hammasi uning boshqa joyga uylanishini istayotgan erkakni qabul qilib, baxtli bo'la olamanmi?»

paras.en: “You must decide for yourself,” said Elizabeth; “and if, upon mature deliberation, you find that the misery of disobliging his two sisters is more than equivalent to the happiness of being his wife, I advise you by all means to refuse him.”
paras.uz: «Buni o'zing hal qilishing kerak, — dedi Elizabet, — agar yaxshilab o'ylab ko'rgach, uning ikki opa-singilining ko'nglini qoldirish azobi uning xotini bo'lish baxtidan ortiq deb topsang, senga uni albatta rad etishni maslahat beraman».

paras.en: “How can you talk so?” said Jane, faintly smiling. “You must know that though I should be exceedingly grieved at their disapprobation, I could not hesitate.”
paras.uz: «Qanday qilib bunday gapira olasan? — dedi Jeyn, zo'rg'a jilmayib. — Bilishing kerakki, ularning noroziligidan nihoyatda qayg'ursam ham, ikkilana olmasdim».

paras.en: “I did not think you would; and that being the case, I cannot consider your situation with much compassion.”
paras.uz: «Ikkilanasan deb o'ylamagandim; shunday ekan, ahvolingga unchalik achina olmayman».

paras.en: “But if he returns no more this winter, my choice will never be required. A thousand things may arise in six months!”
paras.uz: «Lekin agar u bu qish boshqa qaytmasa, mening tanlovim hech qachon kerak bo'lmaydi. Olti oyda ming bir narsa bo'lishi mumkin!»

paras.en: The idea of his returning no more Elizabeth treated with the utmost contempt. It appeared to her merely the suggestion of Caroline's interested wishes, and she could not for a moment suppose that those wishes, however openly or artfully spoken, could influence a young man so totally independent of everyone.
paras.uz: Uning boshqa qaytmasligi haqidagi fikrga Elizabet eng katta mensimaslik bilan qaradi. Bu unga shunchaki Kerolaynning manfaatparast istaklarining taklifi bo'lib ko'rindi va u bu istaklar, qanchalik ochiq yoki ayyorona aytilmasin, hammadan butunlay mustaqil bo'lgan yosh yigitga ta'sir qilishi mumkinligini bir lahzaga ham tasavvur qila olmadi.

paras.en: She represented to her sister as forcibly as possible what she felt on the subject, and had soon the pleasure of seeing its happy effect. Jane's temper was not desponding, and she was gradually led to hope, though the diffidence of affection sometimes overcame the hope, that Bingley would return to Netherfield and answer every wish of her heart.
paras.uz: U opasiga bu masalada his qilganlarini iloji boricha kuchli tarzda tushuntirdi va tez orada uning baxtli ta'sirini ko'rib xursand bo'ldi. Jeynning fe'li tushkun emasdi va u asta-sekin, garchi mehrdagi ishonchsizlik ba'zan umiddan ustun kelsa ham, Bingli Nezerfildga qaytib, qalbining har bir istagiga javob berishiga umid qila boshladi.

paras.en: They agreed that Mrs. Bennet should only hear of the departure of the family, without being alarmed on the score of the gentleman's conduct; but even this partial communication gave her a great deal of concern, and she bewailed it as exceedingly unlucky that the ladies should happen to go away just as they were all getting so intimate together. After lamenting it, however, at some length, she had the consolation that Mr. Bingley would be soon down again and soon dining at Longbourn, and the conclusion of all was the comfortable declaration, that though he had been invited only to a family dinner, she would take care to have two full courses.
paras.uz: Ular missis Bennet janobning xatti-harakati tufayli xavotirga tushmasdan, faqat oilaning ketgani haqida eshitishi kerak, deb kelishib olishdi; lekin hatto bu qisman xabar ham unga katta tashvish berdi va u xonimlar aynan hammalari shunchalik yaqinlashib qolgan paytda ketib qolganini nihoyatda omadsizlik deb nolidi. Biroq bu haqda ancha nolib bo'lgach, u janob Bingli tez orada yana kelib, tez orada Longbornda tushlik qilishi bilan o'zini ovutdi va hammasining xulosasi shunday taskinli bayonot bo'ldiki, garchi u faqat oilaviy tushlikka taklif qilingan bo'lsa ham, u ikki to'liq taom bo'lishini ta'minlaydi.
