chapters.title: The Gardiners
chapters.recap_uz: Missis Bennetning aqlli akasi janob Gardiner va xotini Rojdestvoga keladi. Ular Jeynni Londonga taklif qilishadi. Missis Gardiner Elizabetni Uikhemga ko'ngil qo'ymaslikka ogohlantiradi.

paras.en: After a week spent in professions of love and schemes of felicity, Mr. Collins was called from his amiable Charlotte by the arrival of Saturday. The pain of separation, however, might be alleviated on his side, by preparations for the reception of his bride; as he had reason to hope, that shortly after his return into Hertfordshire, the day would be fixed that was to make him the happiest of men. He took leave of his relations at Longbourn with as much solemnity as before; wished his fair cousins health and happiness again, and promised their father another letter of thanks.
paras.uz: Muhabbat izhorlari va baxt rejalari bilan o'tgan bir haftadan keyin, shanba kunining kelishi janob Kollinzni yoqimli Sharlottasidan ajratdi. Biroq uning tomonidan ajralish og'rig'ini kelinini kutib olishga tayyorgarlik yengillashtirishi mumkin edi; chunki u Xertfordshirga qaytganidan ko'p o'tmay uni eng baxtli erkakka aylantiradigan kun belgilanishiga umid qilish uchun asosga ega edi. U Longborndagi qarindoshlari bilan avvalgidek salobat bilan xayrlashdi; go'zal amakivachchalariga yana sog'lik va baxt tiladi va otalariga yana bir minnatdorchilik xatini va'da qildi.

paras.en: On the following Monday, Mrs. Bennet had the pleasure of receiving her brother and his wife, who came as usual to spend the Christmas at Longbourn. Mr. Gardiner was a sensible, gentlemanlike man, greatly superior to his sister, as well by nature as education. The Netherfield ladies would have had difficulty in believing that a man who lived by trade, and within view of his own warehouses, could have been so well-bred and agreeable. Mrs. Gardiner, who was several years younger than Mrs. Bennet and Mrs. Phillips, was an amiable, intelligent, elegant woman, and a great favourite with all her Longbourn nieces. Between the two eldest and herself especially, there subsisted a particular regard. They had frequently been staying with her in town.
paras.uz: Keyingi dushanba kuni missis Bennet odatdagidek Rojdestvoni Longbornda o'tkazish uchun kelgan ukasi va uning xotinini kutib olish zavqiga ega bo'ldi. Janob Gardiner aqlli, janoblarga xos odam edi, tabiati bilan ham, tarbiyasi bilan ham opasidan ancha ustun edi. Nezerfild xonimlari savdo bilan kun ko'radigan va o'z omborlari ko'rinib turadigan joyda yashaydigan odam bunchalik yaxshi tarbiyali va yoqimli bo'lishi mumkinligiga ishonishga qiynalgan bo'lardi. Missis Bennet va missis Fillipsdan bir necha yosh kichik bo'lgan missis Gardiner yoqimli, aqlli, nafis ayol edi va Longborndagi barcha jiyanlarining sevimlisi edi. Ayniqsa ikki kattasi bilan uning o'rtasida alohida mehr bor edi. Ular tez-tez Londonda uning uyida mehmon bo'lishgan.

paras.en: The first part of Mrs. Gardiner's business on her arrival was to distribute her presents and describe the newest fashions. When this was done she had a less active part to play. It became her turn to listen. Mrs. Bennet had many grievances to relate, and much to complain of. They had all been very ill-used since she last saw her sister. Two of her girls had been upon the point of marriage, and after all there was nothing in it.
paras.uz: Missis Gardinerning kelgach qiladigan ishining birinchi qismi sovg'alarini tarqatish va eng so'nggi modalarni tasvirlab berish edi. Bu bajarilgach, unga kamroq faol rol qoldi. Endi tinglash navbati unga keldi. Missis Bennetning aytib beradigan ko'p dardlari va shikoyat qiladigan ko'p narsalari bor edi. Kelinini oxirgi marta ko'rganidan beri ularga juda yomon munosabatda bo'lishgan. Ikki qizi turmushga chiqish arafasida bo'lgan, oxir-oqibat esa hech narsa chiqmagan.

paras.en: “I do not blame Jane,” she continued, “for Jane would have got Mr. Bingley if she could. But Lizzy! Oh, sister! It is very hard to think that she might have been Mr. Collins's wife by this time, had it not been for her own perverseness. He made her an offer in this very room, and she refused him. The consequence of it is, that Lady Lucas will have a daughter married before I have, and that the Longbourn estate is just as much entailed as ever. The Lucases are very artful people indeed, sister. They are all for what they can get. I am sorry to say it of them, but so it is. It makes me very nervous and poorly, to be thwarted so in my own family, and to have neighbours who think of themselves before anybody else. However, your coming just at this time is the greatest of comforts, and I am very glad to hear what you tell us, of long sleeves.”
paras.uz: «Jeynni ayblamayman, — davom etdi u, — chunki Jeyn qo'lidan kelsa, janob Binglini olgan bo'lardi. Lekin Lizzi! Oh, kelin! Agar o'zining o'jarligi bo'lmaganida, u hozirga kelib janob Kollinzning xotini bo'lishi mumkin edi, deb o'ylash juda og'ir. U unga aynan shu xonada taklif qildi, u esa uni rad etdi. Buning oqibati shuki, ledi Lukasning qizi menikidan oldin turmushga chiqadi, Longborn mulki esa avvalgidek meros cheklovi ostida qoladi. Lukaslar haqiqatan ham juda ayyor odamlar, kelin. Ular faqat qo'lga kiritadigan narsalarini o'ylashadi. Ular haqida buni aytishdan afsusdaman, lekin shunday. O'z oilamda bunday to'siqqa uchrash va hammadan oldin o'zlarini o'ylaydigan qo'shnilarga ega bo'lish meni juda asabiy va kasal qiladi. Biroq aynan shu paytda kelishingiz eng katta taskin va bizga uzun yenglar haqida aytganlaringizni eshitib juda xursandman».

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner, to whom the chief of this news had been given before, in the course of Jane and Elizabeth's correspondence with her, made her sister a slight answer, and, in compassion to her nieces, turned the conversation.
paras.uz: Bu yangiliklarning asosiy qismini avvalroq Jeyn va Elizabet bilan yozishmalari davomida bilgan missis Gardiner opasiga qisqa javob berdi va jiyanlariga achinib, suhbatni boshqa tomonga burdi.

paras.en: When alone with Elizabeth afterwards, she spoke more on the subject. “It seems likely to have been a desirable match for Jane,” said she. “I am sorry it went off. But these things happen so often! A young man, such as you describe Mr. Bingley, so easily falls in love with a pretty girl for a few weeks, and when accident separates them, so easily forgets her, that these sort of inconsistencies are very frequent.”
paras.uz: Keyinroq Elizabet bilan yolg'iz qolganda, u bu mavzuda ko'proq gapirdi. «Bu Jeyn uchun orzu qilinadigan nikoh bo'lganga o'xshaydi, — dedi u. — Uning barbod bo'lganidan afsusdaman. Lekin bunday narsalar juda tez-tez bo'ladi! Sen janob Binglini tasvirlaganingdek yosh yigit chiroyli qizga bir necha haftaga shunchalik oson oshiq bo'ladi va tasodif ularni ajratganda, uni shunchalik oson unutadiki, bunday nomuvofiqliklar juda tez-tez uchraydi».

paras.en: “An excellent consolation in its way,” said Elizabeth, “but it will not do for us. We do not suffer by accident. It does not often happen that the interference of friends will persuade a young man of independent fortune to think no more of a girl whom he was violently in love with only a few days before.”
paras.uz: «O'ziga yarasha ajoyib taskin, — dedi Elizabet, — lekin bizga to'g'ri kelmaydi. Biz tasodifdan azob chekmayapmiz. Do'stlarining aralashuvi mustaqil boylikka ega yosh yigitni bir necha kun oldin qattiq oshiq bo'lgan qiz haqida boshqa o'ylamaslikka ko'ndirishi tez-tez bo'lmaydi».

paras.en: “But that expression of 'violently in love' is so hackneyed, so doubtful, so indefinite, that it gives me very little idea. It is as often applied to feelings which arise from a half-hour's acquaintance, as to a real, strong attachment. Pray, how violent was Mr. Bingley's love?”
paras.uz: «Lekin bu "qattiq oshiq" iborasi shunchalik siyqa, shunchalik shubhali, shunchalik noaniqki, menga juda oz tasavvur beradi. U haqiqiy, kuchli mehrga qanchalik qo'llanilsa, yarim soatlik tanishuvdan paydo bo'ladigan tuyg'ularga ham shunchalik tez-tez qo'llaniladi. Ayt-chi, janob Binglining muhabbati qanchalik qattiq edi?»

paras.en: “I never saw a more promising inclination; he was growing quite inattentive to other people, and wholly engrossed by her. Every time they met, it was more decided and remarkable. At his own ball he offended two or three young ladies, by not asking them to dance; and I spoke to him twice myself, without receiving an answer. Could there be finer symptoms? Is not general incivility the very essence of love?”
paras.uz: «Bundan istiqbolliroq moyillikni hech qachon ko'rmaganman; u boshqa odamlarga nisbatan butunlay e'tiborsiz bo'lib qolgan va butunlay u bilan band edi. Har safar uchrashganlarida bu yanada aniqroq va ko'zga tashlanadigan bo'lardi. O'z balida u ikki-uch yosh xonimni raqsga taklif qilmay ranjitdi; men o'zim unga ikki marta gapirdim, javob olmadim. Bundan ham yaxshiroq alomatlar bo'lishi mumkinmi? Umumiy xushmuomalasizlik muhabbatning aynan mohiyati emasmi?»

paras.en: “Oh, yes!--of that kind of love which I suppose him to have felt. Poor Jane! I am sorry for her, because, with her disposition, she may not get over it immediately. It had better have happened to you, Lizzy; you would have laughed yourself out of it sooner. But do you think she would be prevailed upon to go back with us? Change of scene might be of service--and perhaps a little relief from home may be as useful as anything.”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha! — men u his qilgan deb taxmin qilgan o'sha turdagi muhabbatning. Bechora Jeyn! Unga achinaman, chunki uning fe'li bilan u buni darhol yengib o'tmasligi mumkin. Bu sening boshingga tushgani yaxshiroq bo'lardi, Lizzi; sen buni kulib, tezroq yengib o'tgan bo'larding. Lekin uni biz bilan qaytishga ko'ndirish mumkin deb o'ylaysanmi? Muhitni o'zgartirish foydali bo'lishi mumkin — ehtimol, uydan biroz dam olish har qanday narsa kabi foydali bo'lar».

paras.en: Elizabeth was exceedingly pleased with this proposal, and felt persuaded of her sister's ready acquiescence.
paras.uz: Elizabet bu taklifdan nihoyatda xursand bo'ldi va opasi darhol rozi bo'lishiga ishondi.

paras.en: “I hope,” added Mrs. Gardiner, “that no consideration with regard to this young man will influence her. We live in so different a part of town, all our connections are so different, and, as you well know, we go out so little, that it is very improbable that they should meet at all, unless he really comes to see her.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, — qo'shib qo'ydi missis Gardiner, — bu yosh yigitga oid hech qanday mulohaza unga ta'sir qilmaydi. Biz shaharning shunchalik boshqa qismida yashaymiz, barcha aloqalarimiz shunchalik boshqacha va o'zing yaxshi bilganingdek, juda kam tashqariga chiqamiz, shuning uchun agar u chindan ham uni ko'rgani kelmasa, ularning umuman uchrashishi juda ehtimoldan yiroq».

paras.en: “And that is quite impossible; for he is now in the custody of his friend, and Mr. Darcy would no more suffer him to call on Jane in such a part of London! My dear aunt, how could you think of it? Mr. Darcy may perhaps have heard of such a place as Gracechurch Street, but he would hardly think a month's ablution enough to cleanse him from its impurities, were he once to enter it; and depend upon it, Mr. Bingley never stirs without him.”
paras.uz: «Bu esa mutlaqo imkonsiz; chunki u endi do'stining qaramog'ida va janob Darsi uning Londonning bunday qismida Jeynning oldiga borishiga aslo yo'l qo'ymaydi! Aziz xolajon, qanday qilib bunday o'ylay oldingiz? Janob Darsi, ehtimol, Greyschurch ko'chasi degan joy haqida eshitgandir, lekin agar u bir marta u yerga kirsa, uning nopokliklaridan tozalanish uchun bir oylik yuvinish ham yetarli deb o'ylamaydi; va ishonavering, janob Bingli usiz bir qadam ham bosmaydi».

paras.en: “So much the better. I hope they will not meet at all. But does not Jane correspond with his sister? She will not be able to help calling.”
paras.uz: «Shunisi yaxshi. Umid qilamanki, ular umuman uchrashmaydi. Lekin Jeyn uning singlisi bilan yozishmaydimi? U uning oldiga bormasdan ilojsiz qoladi».

paras.en: “She will drop the acquaintance entirely.”
paras.uz: «U tanishlikni butunlay to'xtatadi».

paras.en: But in spite of the certainty in which Elizabeth affected to place this point, as well as the still more interesting one of Bingley's being withheld from seeing Jane, she felt a solicitude on the subject which convinced her, on examination, that she did not consider it entirely hopeless. It was possible, and sometimes she thought it probable, that his affection might be reanimated, and the influence of his friends successfully combated by the more natural influence of Jane's attractions.
paras.uz: Lekin Elizabet bu masalani, shuningdek, Binglining Jeynni ko'rishdan ushlab qolinishi kabi yanada qiziqarliroq masalani qanchalik aniq qilib ko'rsatishga urinmasin, u bu mavzuda shunday tashvish his qildiki, o'ylab ko'rganda, bu uni buni butunlay umidsiz deb hisoblamasligiga ishontirdi. Uning mehri qayta jonlanishi va do'stlarining ta'siri Jeynning jozibasining tabiiyroq ta'siri bilan muvaffaqiyatli yengilishi mumkin edi, ba'zan esa u buni ehtimol deb ham o'ylardi.

paras.en: Miss Bennet accepted her aunt's invitation with pleasure; and the Bingleys were no otherwise in her thoughts at the same time, than as she hoped by Caroline's not living in the same house with her brother, she might occasionally spend a morning with her, without any danger of seeing him.
paras.uz: Miss Bennet xolasining taklifini mamnuniyat bilan qabul qildi; o'sha paytda Binglilar uning xayolida faqat bir jihatdan bor edi: Kerolayn akasi bilan bir uyda yashamagani uchun, uni ko'rish xavfisiz vaqti-vaqti bilan u bilan bir ertalabni o'tkazishi mumkinligiga umid qilardi.

paras.en: The Gardiners stayed a week at Longbourn; and what with the Phillipses, the Lucases, and the officers, there was not a day without its engagement. Mrs. Bennet had so carefully provided for the entertainment of her brother and sister, that they did not once sit down to a family dinner. When the engagement was for home, some of the officers always made part of it--of which officers Mr. Wickham was sure to be one; and on these occasions, Mrs. Gardiner, rendered suspicious by Elizabeth's warm commendation, narrowly observed them both. Without supposing them, from what she saw, to be very seriously in love, their preference of each other was plain enough to make her a little uneasy; and she resolved to speak to Elizabeth on the subject before she left Hertfordshire, and represent to her the imprudence of encouraging such an attachment.
paras.uz: Gardinerlar Longbornda bir hafta qolishdi; Fillipslar, Lukaslar va ofitserlar bilan birorta ham kun tadbirsiz o'tmadi. Missis Bennet ukasi va kelinining ko'ngilxushligini shunchalik puxta ta'minlagan ediki, ular birorta ham oilaviy tushlikka o'tirishmadi. Tadbir uyda bo'lganda, ofitserlardan ba'zilari doim unda qatnashardi — bu ofitserlar orasida janob Uikhem albatta bo'lardi; bunday paytlarda Elizabetning qizg'in maqtovidan shubhalangan missis Gardiner ikkalasini diqqat bilan kuzatdi. Ko'rganlariga qaraganda ularni juda jiddiy oshiq deb taxmin qilmasa ham, ularning bir-birini afzal ko'rishi uni biroz bezovta qilish uchun yetarlicha aniq edi; va u Xertfordshirni tark etishdan oldin Elizabet bilan bu mavzuda gaplashib, unga bunday mehrni rag'batlantirishning ehtiyotsizligini tushuntirishga qaror qildi.

paras.en: To Mrs. Gardiner, Wickham had one means of affording pleasure, unconnected with his general powers. About ten or a dozen years ago, before her marriage, she had spent a considerable time in that very part of Derbyshire to which he belonged. They had, therefore, many acquaintances in common; and though Wickham had been little there since the death of Darcy's father, it was yet in his power to give her fresher intelligence of her former friends than she had been in the way of procuring.
paras.uz: Uikhemning missis Gardinerga zavq bag'ishlashning umumiy qobiliyatlari bilan bog'liq bo'lmagan bir vositasi bor edi. Taxminan o'n yoki o'n ikki yil oldin, turmushga chiqishdan oldin, u aynan u tegishli bo'lgan Derbishirning o'sha qismida ancha vaqt o'tkazgan edi. Shuning uchun ularning ko'plab umumiy tanishlari bor edi; garchi Uikhem Darsining otasi vafotidan beri u yerda kam bo'lgan bo'lsa ham, baribir u unga sobiq do'stlari haqida o'zi olishi mumkin bo'lganidan yangiroq ma'lumot bera olardi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner had seen Pemberley, and known the late Mr. Darcy by character perfectly well. Here consequently was an inexhaustible subject of discourse. In comparing her recollection of Pemberley with the minute description which Wickham could give, and in bestowing her tribute of praise on the character of its late possessor, she was delighting both him and herself. On being made acquainted with the present Mr. Darcy's treatment of him, she tried to remember some of that gentleman's reputed disposition when quite a lad which might agree with it, and was confident at last that she recollected having heard Mr. Fitzwilliam Darcy formerly spoken of as a very proud, ill-natured boy.
paras.uz: Missis Gardiner Pemberlini ko'rgan va marhum janob Darsini xarakteri bo'yicha juda yaxshi bilgan edi. Shuning uchun bu bitmas-tuganmas suhbat mavzusi edi. Pemberli haqidagi xotiralarini Uikhem bera oladigan batafsil tasvir bilan taqqoslab va uning marhum egasining xarakteriga maqtov aytib, u ham uni, ham o'zini xursand qilardi. Hozirgi janob Darsining unga qanday munosabatda bo'lganidan xabardor bo'lgach, u o'sha janobning bolaligida u haqida aytilgan, bunga mos kelishi mumkin bo'lgan fe'l-atvorini eslashga urindi va oxir-oqibat janob Fitsuilyam Darsi haqida ilgari juda mag'rur, yomon fe'lli bola deb gapirilganini eshitganini eslaganiga amin bo'ldi.

gloss.ex: Gardiner was a sensible, gentlemanlike man, greatly superior to his sister, as well by nature as education.
It does not often happen that the interference of friends will persuade a young man of independent fortune to think no more of a girl whom he was violently in…
It is as often applied to feelings which arise from a half-hour's acquaintance, as to a real, strong attachment.
Gardiner, to whom the chief of this news had been given before, in the course of Jane and Elizabeth's correspondence with her, made her sister a slight answer, and, in…
They had, therefore, many acquaintances in common; and though Wickham had been little there since the death of Darcy's father, it was yet in his power to give her fresher…
“An excellent consolation in its way,”
Elizabeth was exceedingly pleased with this proposal, and felt persuaded of her sister's ready acquiescence.

quiz.q: Why does Mrs. Gardiner warn Elizabeth about Wickham?
o: He has no money, so the match would be imprudent
quiz.why_uz: Ikkalasining ham puli yo'q — bunday nikoh ehtiyotsizlik bo'lardi.

quiz.q: Who are the Gardiners?
o: Mrs. Bennet's sensible brother and his wife
quiz.why_uz: Ular — Bennetlar oilasidagi eng aqlli qarindoshlar.

chapters.title: Jane in London
chapters.recap_uz: Jeyn Londonda Miss Binglini ko'rgani boradi, lekin u sovuq munosabatda bo'ladi. Jeyn nihoyat aldanganini tushunadi. Uikhem esa boy merosxo'r Miss Kingga e'tibor qila boshlaydi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner's caution to Elizabeth was punctually and kindly given on the first favourable opportunity of speaking to her alone; after honestly telling her what she thought, she thus went on:
paras.uz: Missis Gardinerning Elizabetga ogohlantirishi u bilan yolg'iz gaplashish uchun birinchi qulay imkoniyatda aniq va mehribonlik bilan berildi; nima o'ylaganini halol aytgach, u shunday davom etdi:

paras.en: “You are too sensible a girl, Lizzy, to fall in love merely because you are warned against it; and, therefore, I am not afraid of speaking openly. Seriously, I would have you be on your guard. Do not involve yourself or endeavour to involve him in an affection which the want of fortune would make so very imprudent. I have nothing to say against him; he is a most interesting young man; and if he had the fortune he ought to have, I should think you could not do better. But as it is, you must not let your fancy run away with you. You have sense, and we all expect you to use it. Your father would depend on your resolution and good conduct, I am sure. You must not disappoint your father.”
paras.uz: «Sen faqat undan ogohlantirilganing uchun oshiq bo'lib qoladigan darajada aqlsiz qiz emassan, Lizzi; shuning uchun ochiq gapirishdan qo'rqmayman. Jiddiy aytaman, ehtiyot bo'lishingni istardim. O'zingni yoki uni boylik yo'qligi juda ehtiyotsiz qiladigan mehrga aralashtirmagin. Unga qarshi aytadigan gapim yo'q; u juda qiziqarli yosh yigit; agar unda bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan boylik bo'lganida, sen bundan yaxshiroq tanlov qila olmasang kerak, deb o'ylardim. Lekin hozirgi ahvolda xayolingga erk bermasliging kerak. Senda aql bor va hammamiz undan foydalanishingni kutamiz. Ishonchim komilki, otang sening qat'iyatingga va yaxshi xulqingga tayanadi. Otangning hafsalasini pir qilmasliging kerak».

paras.en: “My dear aunt, this is being serious indeed.”
paras.uz: «Aziz xolajon, bu haqiqatan ham jiddiy gap».

paras.en: “Yes, and I hope to engage you to be serious likewise.”
paras.uz: «Ha, va umid qilamanki, seni ham jiddiy bo'lishga undayman».

paras.en: “Well, then, you need not be under any alarm. I will take care of myself, and of Mr. Wickham too. He shall not be in love with me, if I can prevent it.”
paras.uz: «Unday bo'lsa, xavotirlanishingizga hojat yo'q. O'zimga ham, janob Uikhemga ham ehtiyot bo'laman. Agar oldini ola olsam, u menga oshiq bo'lmaydi».

paras.en: “Elizabeth, you are not serious now.”
paras.uz: «Elizabet, hozir jiddiy emassan».

paras.en: “I beg your pardon, I will try again. At present I am not in love with Mr. Wickham; no, I certainly am not. But he is, beyond all comparison, the most agreeable man I ever saw--and if he becomes really attached to me--I believe it will be better that he should not. I see the imprudence of it. Oh! that abominable Mr. Darcy! My father's opinion of me does me the greatest honour, and I should be miserable to forfeit it. My father, however, is partial to Mr. Wickham.
paras.uz: «Kechirasiz, yana urinib ko'raman. Hozir men janob Uikhemga oshiq emasman; yo'q, albatta, oshiq emasman. Lekin u hech qanday taqqoslab bo'lmaydigan darajada men ko'rgan eng yoqimli erkak — va agar u menga chindan bog'lanib qolsa — menimcha, bunday bo'lmagani yaxshiroq. Buning ehtiyotsizligini ko'ryapman. Oh! O'sha jirkanch janob Darsi! Otamning men haqimdagi fikri menga eng katta sharaf, uni yo'qotsam, baxtsiz bo'lardim. Biroq otam janob Uikhemga moyil.

paras.en: In short, my dear aunt, I should be very sorry to be the means of making any of you unhappy; but since we see every day that where there is affection, young people are seldom withheld by immediate want of fortune from entering into engagements with each other, how can I promise to be wiser than so many of my fellow-creatures if I am tempted, or how am I even to know that it would be wisdom to resist? All that I can promise you, therefore, is not to be in a hurry. I will not be in a hurry to believe myself his first object. When I am in company with him, I will not be wishing. In short, I will do my best.”
paras.uz: Qisqasi, aziz xolajon, sizlardan birortangizni baxtsiz qilishga sabab bo'lsam, juda afsuslanardim; lekin har kuni ko'rib turibmizki, mehr bor joyda yoshlarni bir-biri bilan unashtirishdan darhol boylik yetishmasligi kamdan-kam to'xtatadi, shunday ekan, agar vasvasaga tushsam, shuncha ko'p hamjinslarimdan aqlliroq bo'lishga qanday va'da bera olaman yoki qarshilik ko'rsatish aql bo'lishini qayerdan bilaman? Shuning uchun sizga va'da bera oladiganim — shoshilmaslik. O'zimni uning birinchi maqsadi deb ishonishga shoshilmayman. U bilan bir davrada bo'lganimda, orzu qilmayman. Qisqasi, qo'limdan kelganini qilaman».

paras.en: “Perhaps it will be as well if you discourage his coming here so very often. At least, you should not remind your mother of inviting him.”
paras.uz: «Ehtimol, uning bu yerga bunchalik tez-tez kelishini rag'batlantirmasang yaxshi bo'lar. Hech bo'lmaganda onangga uni taklif qilishni eslatmasliging kerak».

paras.en: “As I did the other day,” said Elizabeth with a conscious smile: “very true, it will be wise in me to refrain from that. But do not imagine that he is always here so often. It is on your account that he has been so frequently invited this week. You know my mother's ideas as to the necessity of constant company for her friends. But really, and upon my honour, I will try to do what I think to be the wisest; and now I hope you are satisfied.”
paras.uz: «O'tgan kuni qilganimdek, — dedi Elizabet, o'zini bilgan holda jilmayib, — juda to'g'ri, bundan o'zimni tiysam aqlli ish qilgan bo'laman. Lekin u doim bu yerda bunchalik tez-tez bo'ladi deb o'ylamang. Bu hafta uni sizlar tufayli shunchalik ko'p taklif qilishdi. Onamning do'stlari uchun doimiy davra zarurligi haqidagi fikrlarini bilasiz. Lekin chindan ham, sharafim haqqi, eng oqilona deb bilganimni qilishga harakat qilaman; endi umid qilamanki, qoniqdingiz».

paras.en: Her aunt assured her that she was, and Elizabeth having thanked her for the kindness of her hints, they parted; a wonderful instance of advice being given on such a point, without being resented.
paras.uz: Xolasi uni qoniqqaniga ishontirdi va Elizabet uning mehribon ishoralari uchun rahmat aytgach, ular ajralishdi; bu bunday masalada maslahat berilib, undan ranjilmaganining ajoyib misoli edi.

paras.en: Mr. Collins returned into Hertfordshire soon after it had been quitted by the Gardiners and Jane; but as he took up his abode with the Lucases, his arrival was no great inconvenience to Mrs. Bennet. His marriage was now fast approaching, and she was at length so far resigned as to think it inevitable, and even repeatedly to say, in an ill-natured tone, that she “wished they might be happy.” Thursday was to be the wedding day, and on Wednesday Miss Lucas paid her farewell visit; and when she rose to take leave, Elizabeth, ashamed of her mother's ungracious and reluctant good wishes, and sincerely affected herself, accompanied her out of the room. As they went downstairs together, Charlotte said:
paras.uz: Janob Kollinz Gardinerlar va Jeyn Xertfordshirni tark etganidan ko'p o'tmay qaytib keldi; lekin u Lukaslarnikiga joylashgani uchun uning kelishi missis Bennet uchun unchalik noqulaylik tug'dirmadi. Uning nikohi endi tez yaqinlashib kelayotgan edi va u nihoyat uni muqarrar deb hisoblash darajasida taslim bo'lgan va hatto g'arazli ohangda «ular baxtli bo'lishini tilayman» deb qayta-qayta aytardi. To'y payshanba kuni bo'lishi kerak edi, chorshanba kuni esa miss Lukas xayrlashish tashrifini qildi; u xayrlashish uchun o'rnidan turganda, onasining iltifotsiz va istamay qilgan tilaklaridan uyalgan va o'zi chin dildan ta'sirlangan Elizabet uni xonadan kuzatib chiqdi. Ular birga pastga tushayotganda, Sharlotta dedi:

paras.en: “I shall depend on hearing from you very often, Eliza.”
paras.uz: «Sendan tez-tez xat olishimga ishonaman, Eliza».

paras.en: “That you certainly shall.”
paras.uz: «Albatta olasan».

paras.en: “And I have another favour to ask you. Will you come and see me?”
paras.uz: «Va sendan yana bir iltimosim bor. Meni ko'rgani kelasanmi?»

paras.en: “We shall often meet, I hope, in Hertfordshire.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, Xertfordshirda tez-tez uchrashamiz».

paras.en: “I am not likely to leave Kent for some time. Promise me, therefore, to come to Hunsford.”
paras.uz: «Ehtimol, men Kentni bir muddat tark etmayman. Shuning uchun Xansfordga kelishga va'da ber».

paras.en: Elizabeth could not refuse, though she foresaw little pleasure in the visit.
paras.uz: Elizabet rad eta olmadi, garchi tashrifdan kam zavq olishini oldindan ko'rsa ham.

paras.en: “My father and Maria are coming to me in March,” added Charlotte, “and I hope you will consent to be of the party. Indeed, Eliza, you will be as welcome as either of them.”
paras.uz: «Otam va Mariya martda menikiga kelishadi, — qo'shib qo'ydi Sharlotta, — umid qilamanki, sen ham ularga qo'shilishga rozi bo'lasan. Rostdan ham, Eliza, sen ularning har biri kabi xush kelgan bo'lasan».

paras.en: The wedding took place; the bride and bridegroom set off for Kent from the church door, and everybody had as much to say, or to hear, on the subject as usual. Elizabeth soon heard from her friend; and their correspondence was as regular and frequent as it had ever been; that it should be equally unreserved was impossible. Elizabeth could never address her without feeling that all the comfort of intimacy was over, and though determined not to slacken as a correspondent, it was for the sake of what had been, rather than what was.
paras.uz: To'y bo'lib o'tdi; kelin-kuyov cherkov eshigidan to'g'ri Kentga jo'nab ketishdi va hamma bu mavzuda odatdagidek ko'p gapirdi yoki eshitdi. Elizabet tez orada dugonasidan xat oldi; ularning yozishmalari avvalgidek muntazam va tez-tez edi; lekin avvalgidek ochiq bo'lishi imkonsiz edi. Elizabet unga yaqinlikning butun taskini tugaganini his qilmasdan hech qachon murojaat qila olmasdi va yozishmalarda sustlik qilmaslikka qaror qilgan bo'lsa ham, bu hozirgi narsa uchun emas, balki o'tmishda bo'lgan narsa uchun edi.

paras.en: Charlotte's first letters were received with a good deal of eagerness; there could not but be curiosity to know how she would speak of her new home, how she would like Lady Catherine, and how happy she would dare pronounce herself to be; though, when the letters were read, Elizabeth felt that Charlotte expressed herself on every point exactly as she might have foreseen. She wrote cheerfully, seemed surrounded with comforts, and mentioned nothing which she could not praise. The house, furniture, neighbourhood, and roads, were all to her taste, and Lady Catherine's behaviour was most friendly and obliging. It was Mr. Collins's picture of Hunsford and Rosings rationally softened; and Elizabeth perceived that she must wait for her own visit there to know the rest.
paras.uz: Sharlottaning birinchi xatlari ancha ishtiyoq bilan qabul qilindi; uning yangi uyi haqida qanday gapirishini, ledi Ketrinni qanchalik yoqtirishini va o'zini qanchalik baxtli deb e'lon qilishga jur'at etishini bilishga qiziqmaslikning iloji yo'q edi; garchi xatlar o'qilgach, Elizabet Sharlotta har bir masalada aynan u oldindan ko'rishi mumkin bo'lgandek ifodalaganini his qilgan bo'lsa ham. U quvnoq yozardi, qulayliklar bilan o'ralganga o'xshardi va maqtay olmaydigan hech narsani tilga olmasdi. Uy, mebel, mahalla va yo'llar — hammasi uning didiga mos edi, ledi Ketrinning xatti-harakati esa eng do'stona va iltifotli edi. Bu janob Kollinzning Xansford va Rozings haqidagi tasvirining oqilona yumshatilgani edi; Elizabet qolganini bilish uchun o'zining u yerga tashrifini kutishi kerakligini tushundi.

paras.en: Jane had already written a few lines to her sister to announce their safe arrival in London; and when she wrote again, Elizabeth hoped it would be in her power to say something of the Bingleys.
paras.uz: Jeyn singlisiga Londonga eson-omon yetib kelishganini e'lon qilish uchun allaqachon bir necha satr yozgan edi; u yana yozganda, Elizabet u Binglilar haqida biror narsa ayta oladi deb umid qildi.

paras.en: Her impatience for this second letter was as well rewarded as impatience generally is. Jane had been a week in town without either seeing or hearing from Caroline. She accounted for it, however, by supposing that her last letter to her friend from Longbourn had by some accident been lost.
paras.uz: Uning bu ikkinchi xatga sabrsizligi odatda sabrsizlik qanday taqdirlansa, shunday taqdirlandi. Jeyn Londonda bir hafta bo'lgan, lekin Kerolaynni na ko'rgan, na undan xabar olgan edi. Biroq u buni Longborndan dugonasiga yozgan oxirgi xati qandaydir tasodif bilan yo'qolgan deb taxmin qilib tushuntirdi.

paras.en: “My aunt,” she continued, “is going to-morrow into that part of the town, and I shall take the opportunity of calling in Grosvenor Street.”
paras.uz: «Xolam, — davom etdi u, — ertaga shaharning o'sha qismiga boradi va men bu imkoniyatdan foydalanib, Grosvenor ko'chasiga kirib o'taman».

paras.en: She wrote again when the visit was paid, and she had seen Miss Bingley. “I did not think Caroline in spirits,” were her words, “but she was very glad to see me, and reproached me for giving her no notice of my coming to London. I was right, therefore, my last letter had never reached her. I inquired after their brother, of course. He was well, but so much engaged with Mr. Darcy that they scarcely ever saw him. I found that Miss Darcy was expected to dinner. I wish I could see her. My visit was not long, as Caroline and Mrs. Hurst were going out. I dare say I shall see them soon here.”
paras.uz: U tashrif amalga oshgach va miss Binglini ko'rgach yana yozdi. «Kerolaynni kayfiyati yaxshi deb o'ylamadim, — deb yozgandi u, — lekin u meni ko'rganidan juda xursand bo'ldi va Londonga kelishim haqida unga xabar bermaganim uchun meni koyidi. Demak, men to'g'ri edim, oxirgi xatim unga hech qachon yetib bormagan. Albatta, ularning akasi haqida so'radim. U sog'-salomat, lekin janob Darsi bilan shunchalik band ekanki, ular uni deyarli ko'rishmas ekan. Miss Darsini tushlikka kutishayotganini bildim. Uni ko'ra olsam edi. Tashrifim uzoq bo'lmadi, chunki Kerolayn va missis Xerst tashqariga chiqmoqchi edi. Ishonamanki, tez orada ularni bu yerda ko'raman».

paras.en: Elizabeth shook her head over this letter. It convinced her that accident only could discover to Mr. Bingley her sister's being in town.
paras.uz: Elizabet bu xatni o'qib, boshini chayqadi. Bu uni opasining Londonda ekanini janob Binglige faqat tasodifgina ochishi mumkinligiga ishontirdi.

paras.en: Four weeks passed away, and Jane saw nothing of him. She endeavoured to persuade herself that she did not regret it; but she could no longer be blind to Miss Bingley's inattention. After waiting at home every morning for a fortnight, and inventing every evening a fresh excuse for her, the visitor did at last appear; but the shortness of her stay, and yet more, the alteration of her manner would allow Jane to deceive herself no longer. The letter which she wrote on this occasion to her sister will prove what she felt.
paras.uz: To'rt hafta o'tdi, Jeyn uni umuman ko'rmadi. U o'zini bundan afsuslanmasligiga ishontirishga urindi; lekin endi miss Binglining e'tiborsizligiga ko'z yuma olmasdi. Ikki hafta davomida har kuni ertalab uyda kutib, har oqshom uning uchun yangi bahona o'ylab topgach, nihoyat mehmon paydo bo'ldi; lekin uning qisqa qolishi, undan ham ko'ra muomalasining o'zgarishi Jeynga endi o'zini aldashga yo'l qo'ymadi. Bu munosabat bilan u singlisiga yozgan xat nimani his qilganini isbotlaydi.

paras.en: “My dearest Lizzy will, I am sure, be incapable of triumphing in her better judgement, at my expense, when I confess myself to have been entirely deceived in Miss Bingley's regard for me. But, my dear sister, though the event has proved you right, do not think me obstinate if I still assert that, considering what her behaviour was, my confidence was as natural as your suspicion. I do not at all comprehend her reason for wishing to be intimate with me; but if the same circumstances were to happen again, I am sure I should be deceived again. Caroline did not return my visit till yesterday; and not a note, not a line, did I receive in the meantime.
paras.uz: «Eng aziz Lizzim, ishonchim komilki, miss Binglining menga bo'lgan hurmatida butunlay aldanganimni tan olsam, mening hisobimga o'zining yaxshiroq mulohazasi bilan g'olibona maqtana olmaydi. Lekin, azizim singlim, voqea seni haq chiqargan bo'lsa ham, agar uning xatti-harakatini hisobga olsak, mening ishonchim sening shubhang kabi tabiiy bo'lganini hali ham ta'kidlasam, meni o'jar deb o'ylama. Uning men bilan yaqin bo'lishni istash sababini umuman tushunmayman; lekin agar xuddi shu holatlar yana takrorlansa, ishonchim komilki, yana aldanardim. Kerolayn tashrifimga faqat kecha javob qaytardi; bu orada undan birorta xat ham, birorta satr ham olmadim.

paras.en: When she did come, it was very evident that she had no pleasure in it; she made a slight, formal apology, for not calling before, said not a word of wishing to see me again, and was in every respect so altered a creature, that when she went away I was perfectly resolved to continue the acquaintance no longer. I pity, though I cannot help blaming her. She was very wrong in singling me out as she did; I can safely say that every advance to intimacy began on her side. But I pity her, because she must feel that she has been acting wrong, and because I am very sure that anxiety for her brother is the cause of it.
paras.uz: U kelganida, bundan hech qanday zavq olmagani juda aniq edi; u oldinroq kelmagani uchun qisqa, rasmiy uzr so'radi, meni yana ko'rishni istashi haqida bir og'iz ham gapirmadi va har jihatdan shunchalik o'zgargan mavjudot ediki, u ketgach, tanishlikni boshqa davom ettirmaslikka qat'iy qaror qildim. Uni ayblamay ilojim bo'lmasa ham, unga achinaman. U meni shunday ajratib ko'rsatganida juda noto'g'ri qilgan; ishonch bilan ayta olamanki, yaqinlikka har bir qadam uning tomonidan boshlangan. Lekin unga achinaman, chunki u noto'g'ri harakat qilganini his qilishi kerak va bunga akasi uchun tashvishlanishi sabab ekaniga juda aminman.

paras.en: I need not explain myself farther; and though we know this anxiety to be quite needless, yet if she feels it, it will easily account for her behaviour to me; and so deservedly dear as he is to his sister, whatever anxiety she must feel on his behalf is natural and amiable. I cannot but wonder, however, at her having any such fears now, because, if he had at all cared about me, we must have met, long ago. He knows of my being in town, I am certain, from something she said herself; and yet it would seem, by her manner of talking, as if she wanted to persuade herself that he is really partial to Miss Darcy. I cannot understand it. If I were not afraid of judging harshly, I should be almost tempted to say that there is a strong appearance of duplicity in all this.
paras.uz: Ortiq tushuntirishimga hojat yo'q; garchi bu tashvish mutlaqo keraksiz ekanini bilsak ham, agar u buni his qilsa, bu uning menga nisbatan xatti-harakatini osongina tushuntiradi; u singlisi uchun munosib ravishda shunchalik aziz bo'lgani uchun, uning nomidan his qiladigan har qanday tashvishi tabiiy va yoqimli. Biroq uning hozir bunday qo'rquvlari borligidan hayron bo'lmay ilojim yo'q, chunki agar u menga umuman ahamiyat berganida, biz allaqachon uchrashgan bo'lardik. U mening Londonda ekanimni biladi, bunga uning o'zi aytgan bir gapdan aminman; shunga qaramay, uning gapirish tarzidan u o'zini akasi chindan ham miss Darsiga moyil ekaniga ishontirmoqchidek tuyuladi. Buni tushuna olmayman. Agar qattiq hukm chiqarishdan qo'rqmaganimda, bularning hammasida ikkiyuzlamachilikning kuchli alomati bor, deyishga deyarli moyil bo'lardim.

paras.en: But I will endeavour to banish every painful thought, and think only of what will make me happy--your affection, and the invariable kindness of my dear uncle and aunt. Let me hear from you very soon. Miss Bingley said something of his never returning to Netherfield again, of giving up the house, but not with any certainty. We had better not mention it. I am extremely glad that you have such pleasant accounts from our friends at Hunsford. Pray go to see them, with Sir William and Maria. I am sure you will be very comfortable there.--Yours, etc.”
paras.uz: Lekin har qanday og'riqli fikrni haydashga va faqat meni baxtli qiladigan narsa — sening mehring va aziz tog'am hamda xolamning o'zgarmas mehribonligi haqida o'ylashga harakat qilaman. Tez orada sendan xabar olay. Miss Bingli uning Nezerfildga boshqa hech qachon qaytmasligi, uydan voz kechishi haqida nimadir dedi, lekin aniq emas. Buni tilga olmaganimiz ma'qul. Xansforddagi do'stlarimizdan shunday yoqimli xabarlar olayotganingdan nihoyatda xursandman. Iltimos, ser Uilyam va Mariya bilan ularni ko'rgani bor. Ishonchim komilki, u yerda o'zingni juda qulay his qilasan. — Seniki va hokazo».

paras.en: This letter gave Elizabeth some pain; but her spirits returned as she considered that Jane would no longer be duped, by the sister at least. All expectation from the brother was now absolutely over. She would not even wish for a renewal of his attentions. His character sunk on every review of it; and as a punishment for him, as well as a possible advantage to Jane, she seriously hoped he might really soon marry Mr. Darcy's sister, as by Wickham's account, she would make him abundantly regret what he had thrown away.
paras.uz: Bu xat Elizabetga biroz og'riq berdi; lekin Jeyn endi hech bo'lmaganda singil tomonidan aldanmasligini o'ylab, kayfiyati qaytdi. Akadan endi har qanday umid butunlay tugagan edi. U hatto uning e'tiborlari yangilanishini ham istamasdi. Uning xarakteri har safar ko'rib chiqilganda pastga tushardi; unga jazo sifatida, shuningdek Jeyn uchun mumkin bo'lgan foyda sifatida, u chin dildan uning tez orada janob Darsining singlisiga uylanishiga umid qildi, chunki Uikhemning aytishicha, u uni qo'ldan boy bergan narsasi uchun mo'l-ko'l afsuslantirgan bo'lardi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner about this time reminded Elizabeth of her promise concerning that gentleman, and required information; and Elizabeth had such to send as might rather give contentment to her aunt than to herself. His apparent partiality had subsided, his attentions were over, he was the admirer of some one else. Elizabeth was watchful enough to see it all, but she could see it and write of it without material pain. Her heart had been but slightly touched, and her vanity was satisfied with believing that she would have been his only choice, had fortune permitted it. The sudden acquisition of ten thousand pounds was the most remarkable charm of the young lady to whom he was now rendering himself agreeable; but Elizabeth, less clear-sighted perhaps in this case than in Charlotte's, did not quarrel with him for his wish of independence. Nothing, on the contrary, could be more natural; and while able to suppose that it cost him a few struggles to relinquish her, she was ready to allow it a wise and desirable measure for both, and could very sincerely wish him happy.
paras.uz: Taxminan shu paytda missis Gardiner Elizabetga o'sha janob haqidagi va'dasini eslatdi va ma'lumot so'radi; Elizabetning yuboradigan ma'lumoti o'zidan ko'ra xolasini ko'proq qoniqtirishi mumkin edi. Uning ko'rinib turgan moyilligi so'ngan, e'tiborlari tugagan, u endi boshqa birovning muxlisi edi. Elizabet bularning hammasini ko'radigan darajada hushyor edi, lekin u buni ko'rishi va bu haqda katta og'riqsiz yozishi mumkin edi. Uning qalbi faqat yengilgina tegilgan edi, shuhratparastligi esa agar boylik imkon berganida, u uning yagona tanlovi bo'lgan bo'lardi degan ishonch bilan qoniqardi. To'satdan qo'lga kiritilgan o'n ming funt u endi o'zini yoqtirishga urinayotgan yosh xonimning eng diqqatga sazovor jozibasi edi; lekin Elizabet, ehtimol, bu holatda Sharlottanikidagidan kamroq ziyrak bo'lib, uning mustaqillikka bo'lgan istagi uchun u bilan janjallashmadi. Aksincha, hech narsa bundan tabiiyroq bo'lishi mumkin emasdi; uni tark etish unga biroz ichki kurashga tushganini taxmin qila olgani holda, u buni ikkalasi uchun ham oqilona va maqbul chora deb tan olishga tayyor edi va unga juda samimiy baxt tilay olardi.

paras.en: All this was acknowledged to Mrs. Gardiner; and after relating the circumstances, she thus went on: “I am now convinced, my dear aunt, that I have never been much in love; for had I really experienced that pure and elevating passion, I should at present detest his very name, and wish him all manner of evil. But my feelings are not only cordial towards him; they are even impartial towards Miss King. I cannot find out that I hate her at all, or that I am in the least unwilling to think her a very good sort of girl. There can be no love in all this. My watchfulness has been effectual; and though I certainly should be a more interesting object to all my acquaintances were I distractedly in love with him, I cannot say that I regret my comparative insignificance. Importance may sometimes be purchased too dearly. Kitty and Lydia take his defection much more to heart than I do. They are young in the ways of the world, and not yet open to the mortifying conviction that handsome young men must have something to live on as well as the plain.”
paras.uz: Bularning hammasi missis Gardinerga tan olindi; holatlarni aytib bergach, u shunday davom etdi: «Endi ishonch hosil qildim, aziz xolajon, men hech qachon unchalik oshiq bo'lmaganman; chunki agar men chindan ham o'sha sof va yuksaltiruvchi ehtirosni boshdan kechirganimda, hozir uning nomidan ham nafratlanardim va unga har xil yomonlik tilardim. Lekin mening tuyg'ularim unga nisbatan nafaqat samimiy; ular hatto miss Kingga nisbatan ham xolis. Undan umuman nafratlanayotganimni yoki uni juda yaxshi qiz deb o'ylashni zarracha istamayotganimni topa olmayman. Bularning hammasida muhabbat bo'lishi mumkin emas. Hushyorligim samarali bo'ldi; agar unga telbalarcha oshiq bo'lganimda, albatta barcha tanishlarim uchun qiziqarliroq obyekt bo'lardim, lekin nisbatan ahamiyatsizligimdan afsuslanaman deya olmayman. Ahamiyat ba'zan haddan tashqari qimmatga sotib olinishi mumkin. Ketti va Lidiya uning ketib qolishini mendan ko'ra ko'proq yuraklariga olishyapti. Ular dunyo yo'llarida yosh va hali chiroyli yosh yigitlar ham xunuklar kabi nimadir bilan kun ko'rishi kerak degan xo'rlovchi ishonchga ochiq emas».

gloss.ex: After waiting at home every morning for a fortnight, and inventing every evening a fresh excuse for her, the visitor did at last appear; but the shortness of her stay,…
All this was acknowledged to Mrs.
The house, furniture, neighbourhood, and roads, were all to her taste, and Lady Catherine's behaviour was most friendly and obliging.
I do not at all comprehend her reason for wishing to be intimate with me; but if the same circumstances were to happen again, I am sure I should be…
When she did come, it was very evident that she had no pleasure in it; she made a slight, formal apology, for not calling before, said not a word of…
All this was acknowledged to Mrs.
She endeavoured to persuade herself that she did not regret it; but she could no longer be blind to Miss Bingley's inattention.

quiz.q: What does Jane finally realise in London?
o: Miss Bingley was never her friend
quiz.why_uz: Jeyn birinchi marta kimdir uni aldaganini tan oladi.

quiz.q: Whom does Wickham start to court?
o: Miss King, who has inherited money
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet buni xotirjam qabul qiladi — demak, uni sevmagan ekan.

chapters.title: Journey to Hunsford
chapters.recap_uz: Mart oyida Elizabet Ser Uilyam va Mariya Lukas bilan Sharlottaning Hansforddagi yangi uyiga yo'l oladi. Yo'lda Londonda Jeyn va Gardinerlar bilan to'xtaydi.

paras.en: With no greater events than these in the Longbourn family, and otherwise diversified by little beyond the walks to Meryton, sometimes dirty and sometimes cold, did January and February pass away. March was to take Elizabeth to Hunsford. She had not at first thought very seriously of going thither; but Charlotte, she soon found, was depending on the plan and she gradually learned to consider it herself with greater pleasure as well as greater certainty. Absence had increased her desire of seeing Charlotte again, and weakened her disgust of Mr. Collins. There was novelty in the scheme, and as, with such a mother and such uncompanionable sisters, home could not be faultless, a little change was not unwelcome for its own sake. The journey would moreover give her a peep at Jane; and, in short, as the time drew near, she would have been very sorry for any delay. Everything, however, went on smoothly, and was finally settled according to Charlotte's first sketch. She was to accompany Sir William and his second daughter. The improvement of spending a night in London was added in time, and the plan became perfect as plan could be.
paras.uz: Longborn oilasida bulardan katta voqealar bo'lmagan va boshqa jihatdan ba'zan loyli, ba'zan sovuq Meritonga sayrlardan boshqa narsa bilan rang-baranglashmagan holda yanvar va fevral o'tib ketdi. Mart Elizabetni Xansfordga olib borishi kerak edi. Avvaliga u u yerga borish haqida unchalik jiddiy o'ylamagan edi; lekin tez orada Sharlotta bu rejaga tayanayotganini bildi va asta-sekin o'zi ham unga kattaroq zavq va kattaroq ishonch bilan qarashni o'rgandi. Uzoqlik uning Sharlottani yana ko'rish istagini kuchaytirgan va janob Kollinzdan jirkanishini susaytirgan edi. Rejada yangilik bor edi va bunday ona hamda bunday kirishimsiz opa-singillar bilan uy beayb bo'la olmagani uchun, biroz o'zgarish o'z-o'zidan yoqimsiz emasdi. Bundan tashqari, sayohat unga Jeynni bir ko'rib olish imkonini berardi; qisqasi, vaqt yaqinlashgani sari u har qanday kechikishdan juda afsuslangan bo'lardi. Biroq hamma narsa silliq ketdi va oxir-oqibat Sharlottaning dastlabki rejasiga muvofiq hal qilindi. U ser Uilyam va uning ikkinchi qizi bilan birga borishi kerak edi. Vaqtida Londonda bir tun o'tkazish qulayligi qo'shildi va reja reja bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan darajada mukammal bo'ldi.

paras.en: The only pain was in leaving her father, who would certainly miss her, and who, when it came to the point, so little liked her going, that he told her to write to him, and almost promised to answer her letter.
paras.uz: Yagona og'riq uni albatta sog'inadigan otasini tark etishda edi; ish shunga kelganda u uning ketishini shunchalik kam yoqtirdiki, unga xat yozishni aytdi va uning xatiga javob berishga deyarli va'da berdi.

paras.en: The farewell between herself and Mr. Wickham was perfectly friendly; on his side even more. His present pursuit could not make him forget that Elizabeth had been the first to excite and to deserve his attention, the first to listen and to pity, the first to be admired; and in his manner of bidding her adieu, wishing her every enjoyment, reminding her of what she was to expect in Lady Catherine de Bourgh, and trusting their opinion of her--their opinion of everybody--would always coincide, there was a solicitude, an interest which she felt must ever attach her to him with a most sincere regard; and she parted from him convinced that, whether married or single, he must always be her model of the amiable and pleasing.
paras.uz: U bilan janob Uikhem o'rtasidagi xayrlashuv mutlaqo do'stona edi; uning tomonidan hatto bundan ham ko'proq. Hozirgi intilishi uni Elizabet uning e'tiborini birinchi bo'lib uyg'otgan va unga loyiq bo'lgan, birinchi bo'lib tinglagan va achingan, birinchi bo'lib hayratlantirgan ekanini unutishga majbur qila olmasdi; uning u bilan xayrlashish tarzida, unga har qanday zavq tilashida, ledi Ketrin de Burgdan nimani kutish kerakligini eslatishida va uning haqidagi fikrlari — hamma haqidagi fikrlari — doim mos kelishiga ishonishida shunday g'amxo'rlik, shunday qiziqish bor ediki, u bu uni doim unga eng samimiy hurmat bilan bog'lab turishini his qildi; va u turmush qurgan bo'ladimi yoki bo'ydoq, u doim uning uchun yoqimli va maftunkorlik namunasi bo'lishiga ishonch hosil qilib, u bilan ajraldi.

paras.en: Her fellow-travellers the next day were not of a kind to make her think him less agreeable. Sir William Lucas, and his daughter Maria, a good-humoured girl, but as empty-headed as himself, had nothing to say that could be worth hearing, and were listened to with about as much delight as the rattle of the chaise. Elizabeth loved absurdities, but she had known Sir William's too long. He could tell her nothing new of the wonders of his presentation and knighthood; and his civilities were worn out, like his information.
paras.uz: Ertasi kungi yo'ldoshlari uni kamroq yoqimli deb o'ylatadigan turdagi odamlar emasdi. Ser Uilyam Lukas va uning qizi Mariya — xushfe'l, lekin otasi kabi boshi bo'sh qiz — eshitishga arziydigan hech narsa aytmasdi va ularni taxminan aravaning taraqlashi kabi zavq bilan tinglashardi. Elizabet bema'nilikni yaxshi ko'rardi, lekin ser Uilyamnikini haddan tashqari uzoq vaqtdan beri bilardi. U unga saroyga tanishtirilishi va ritsarlik unvoni mo'jizalari haqida hech qanday yangi narsa ayta olmasdi; uning xushmuomalaliklari ma'lumotlari kabi eskirib qolgan edi.

paras.en: It was a journey of only twenty-four miles, and they began it so early as to be in Gracechurch Street by noon. As they drove to Mr. Gardiner's door, Jane was at a drawing-room window watching their arrival; when they entered the passage she was there to welcome them, and Elizabeth, looking earnestly in her face, was pleased to see it healthful and lovely as ever. On the stairs were a troop of little boys and girls, whose eagerness for their cousin's appearance would not allow them to wait in the drawing-room, and whose shyness, as they had not seen her for a twelvemonth, prevented their coming lower. All was joy and kindness. The day passed most pleasantly away; the morning in bustle and shopping, and the evening at one of the theatres.
paras.uz: Bu atigi yigirma to'rt millik safar edi va ular uni shunchalik erta boshlashdiki, tushga kelib Greyschurch ko'chasida edilar. Ular janob Gardinerning eshigi oldiga kelganlarida, Jeyn mehmonxona derazasidan ularning kelishini kuzatib turardi; ular dahlizga kirganlarida, u ularni kutib olish uchun u yerda edi va Elizabet uning yuziga diqqat bilan qarab, uni har doimgidek sog'lom va go'zal ko'rib xursand bo'ldi. Zinapoyada bir to'da kichkina o'g'il va qiz bolalar turardi, ularning amakivachchasining paydo bo'lishiga bo'lgan ishtiyoqi ularni mehmonxonada kutishga qo'ymagan, bir yildan beri uni ko'rmaganlari uchun uyatchanliklari esa pastroqqa tushishlariga yo'l qo'ymagan edi. Hammasi quvonch va mehribonlik edi. Kun juda yoqimli o'tdi; ertalab shovqin-suron va xaridlar bilan, kechqurun esa teatrlardan birida.

paras.en: Elizabeth then contrived to sit by her aunt. Their first object was her sister; and she was more grieved than astonished to hear, in reply to her minute inquiries, that though Jane always struggled to support her spirits, there were periods of dejection. It was reasonable, however, to hope that they would not continue long. Mrs. Gardiner gave her the particulars also of Miss Bingley's visit in Gracechurch Street, and repeated conversations occurring at different times between Jane and herself, which proved that the former had, from her heart, given up the acquaintance.
paras.uz: Shunda Elizabet xolasining yonida o'tirishni uddaladi. Ularning birinchi mavzusi opasi edi; va u batafsil so'roqlariga javoban Jeyn doim kayfiyatini saqlashga harakat qilsa ham, tushkunlik davrlari bo'lishini eshitib, hayron bo'lishdan ko'ra ko'proq qayg'urdi. Biroq ular uzoq davom etmasligiga umid qilish oqilona edi. Missis Gardiner unga miss Binglining Greyschurch ko'chasiga tashrifi tafsilotlarini ham aytib berdi va turli vaqtlarda Jeyn bilan o'zi o'rtasida bo'lib o'tgan suhbatlarni takrorladi, ular Jeyn tanishlikdan chin dildan voz kechganini isbotlardi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner then rallied her niece on Wickham's desertion, and complimented her on bearing it so well.
paras.uz: Keyin missis Gardiner jiyanini Uikhemning tashlab ketgani bilan masxaraladi va unga bunga shunchalik yaxshi bardosh bergani uchun maqtov aytdi.

paras.en: “But my dear Elizabeth,” she added, “what sort of girl is Miss King? I should be sorry to think our friend mercenary.”
paras.uz: «Lekin, azizim Elizabet, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — miss King qanday qiz? Do'stimizni pulparast deb o'ylashdan afsuslanardim».

paras.en: “Pray, my dear aunt, what is the difference in matrimonial affairs, between the mercenary and the prudent motive? Where does discretion end, and avarice begin? Last Christmas you were afraid of his marrying me, because it would be imprudent; and now, because he is trying to get a girl with only ten thousand pounds, you want to find out that he is mercenary.”
paras.uz: «Iltimos, aziz xolajon, nikoh ishlarida pulparastlik va oqilonalik sababi o'rtasida qanday farq bor? Ehtiyotkorlik qayerda tugaydi va ochko'zlik qayerda boshlanadi? O'tgan Rojdestvoda siz uning menga uylanishidan qo'rqdingiz, chunki bu ehtiyotsizlik bo'lardi; endi esa u atigi o'n ming funtli qizni olishga urinayotgani uchun uni pulparast deb topmoqchisiz».

paras.en: “If you will only tell me what sort of girl Miss King is, I shall know what to think.”
paras.uz: «Faqat menga miss King qanday qiz ekanini aytsang, nima deb o'ylashni bilaman».

paras.en: “She is a very good kind of girl, I believe. I know no harm of her.”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, u juda yaxshi qiz. U haqida yomon narsa bilmayman».

paras.en: “But he paid her not the smallest attention till her grandfather's death made her mistress of this fortune.”
paras.uz: «Lekin u bobosining o'limi uni bu boylikning egasiga aylantirmaguncha unga zarracha e'tibor bermagan».

paras.en: “No--why should he? If it were not allowable for him to gain my affections because I had no money, what occasion could there be for making love to a girl whom he did not care about, and who was equally poor?”
paras.uz: «Yo'q — nega berishi kerak edi? Agar puli yo'qligi uchun mening mehrimni qozonish unga ruxsat etilmagan bo'lsa, o'zi ahamiyat bermaydigan va xuddi shunday kambag'al qizga oshiqlik qilishga qanday sabab bo'lishi mumkin edi?»

paras.en: “But there seems an indelicacy in directing his attentions towards her so soon after this event.”
paras.uz: «Lekin bu voqeadan keyin bunchalik tez e'tiborini unga qaratishda nazokatsizlik borga o'xshaydi».

paras.en: “A man in distressed circumstances has not time for all those elegant decorums which other people may observe. If she does not object to it, why should we?”
paras.uz: «Og'ir ahvoldagi odamning boshqalar rioya qilishi mumkin bo'lgan barcha nafis odob qoidalariga vaqti yo'q. Agar u bunga e'tiroz bildirmasa, nega biz bildirishimiz kerak?»

paras.en: “Her not objecting does not justify him. It only shows her being deficient in something herself--sense or feeling.”
paras.uz: «Uning e'tiroz bildirmasligi uni oqlamaydi. Bu faqat uning o'zida nimadir — aql yoki tuyg'u yetishmasligini ko'rsatadi».

paras.en: “Well,” cried Elizabeth, “have it as you choose. He shall be mercenary, and she shall be foolish.”
paras.uz: «Mayli, — xitob qildi Elizabet, — xohlaganingizcha bo'lsin. U pulparast bo'ladi, qiz esa ahmoq».

paras.en: “No, Lizzy, that is what I do not choose. I should be sorry, you know, to think ill of a young man who has lived so long in Derbyshire.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, Lizzi, men aynan buni xohlamayman. Bilasanmi, Derbishirda shunchalik uzoq yashagan yosh yigit haqida yomon o'ylashdan afsuslanardim».

paras.en: “Oh! if that is all, I have a very poor opinion of young men who live in Derbyshire; and their intimate friends who live in Hertfordshire are not much better. I am sick of them all. Thank Heaven! I am going to-morrow where I shall find a man who has not one agreeable quality, who has neither manner nor sense to recommend him. Stupid men are the only ones worth knowing, after all.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Agar gap shunda bo'lsa, Derbishirda yashaydigan yosh yigitlar haqida juda past fikrdaman; ularning Xertfordshirda yashaydigan yaqin do'stlari ham ulardan unchalik yaxshi emas. Hammasidan bezor bo'ldim. Xudoga shukr! Ertaga birorta ham yoqimli fazilati yo'q, o'zini tavsiya qiladigan na muomalasi, na aqli bo'lgan erkakni topadigan joyga ketyapman. Oxir-oqibat, faqat ahmoq erkaklar bilan tanishishga arziydi».

paras.en: “Take care, Lizzy; that speech savours strongly of disappointment.”
paras.uz: «Ehtiyot bo'l, Lizzi; bu gapdan hafsala pirligining hidi kelib turibdi».

paras.en: Before they were separated by the conclusion of the play, she had the unexpected happiness of an invitation to accompany her uncle and aunt in a tour of pleasure which they proposed taking in the summer.
paras.uz: Spektakl tugashi ularni ajratishidan oldin, u tog'asi va xolasi yozda qilmoqchi bo'lgan sayohatga ularga hamroh bo'lish taklifini olishdek kutilmagan baxtga muyassar bo'ldi.

paras.en: “We have not determined how far it shall carry us,” said Mrs. Gardiner, “but, perhaps, to the Lakes.”
paras.uz: «Bu bizni qanchalik uzoqqa olib borishini hali hal qilmadik, — dedi missis Gardiner, — lekin, ehtimol, Ko'llar o'lkasigacha».

paras.en: No scheme could have been more agreeable to Elizabeth, and her acceptance of the invitation was most ready and grateful. “Oh, my dear, dear aunt,” she rapturously cried, “what delight! what felicity! You give me fresh life and vigour. Adieu to disappointment and spleen. What are young men to rocks and mountains? Oh! what hours of transport we shall spend! And when we do return, it shall not be like other travellers, without being able to give one accurate idea of anything. We will know where we have gone--we will recollect what we have seen. Lakes, mountains, and rivers shall not be jumbled together in our imaginations; nor when we attempt to describe any particular scene, will we begin quarreling about its relative situation. Let our first effusions be less insupportable than those of the generality of travellers.”
paras.uz: Elizabet uchun hech qanday reja bundan yoqimliroq bo'lishi mumkin emasdi va u taklifni eng tayyor va minnatdor tarzda qabul qildi. «Oh, aziz, aziz xolajon, — hayajon bilan xitob qildi u, — qanday zavq! Qanday baxt! Siz menga yangi hayot va kuch bag'ishlayapsiz. Alvido, hafsala pirligi va g'am-g'ussa. Qoyalar va tog'lar oldida yosh yigitlar nima ekan? Oh! Qanday hayajonli soatlarni o'tkazamiz! Qaytganimizda esa boshqa sayyohlar kabi biror narsa haqida birorta aniq tasavvur bera olmaydigan bo'lib qaytmaymiz. Qayerga borganimizni bilamiz — nimani ko'rganimizni eslaymiz. Ko'llar, tog'lar va daryolar xayolimizda aralashib ketmaydi; biror sahnani tasvirlashga urinayotganimizda uning joylashuvi haqida janjallasha boshlamaymiz. Birinchi hayajonli gaplarimiz ko'pchilik sayyohlarnikidan kamroq toqat qilib bo'lmaydigan bo'lsin».

gloss.ex: The journey would moreover give her a peep at Jane; and, in short, as the time drew near, she would have been very sorry for any delay.
Before they were separated by the conclusion of the play, she had the unexpected happiness of an invitation to accompany her uncle and aunt in a tour of pleasure which…
Gardiner, “but, perhaps, to the Lakes.”
Their first object was her sister; and she was more grieved than astonished to hear, in reply to her minute inquiries, that though Jane always struggled to support her spirits,…

Gardiner gave her the particulars also of Miss Bingley's visit in Gracechurch Street, and repeated conversations occurring at different times between Jane and herself, which proved that the former had,…
“Take care, Lizzy; that speech savours strongly of disappointment.”
