chapters.title: Charlotte's New Home
chapters.recap_uz: Kollinz uyini va bog'ini maqtab ko'rsatadi. Sharlotta erini iloji boricha kam ko'rish usullarini topgan. Ledi Ketrinning qizi Miss de Burg aravada o'tadi.

paras.en: Every object in the next day's journey was new and interesting to Elizabeth; and her spirits were in a state of enjoyment; for she had seen her sister looking so well as to banish all fear for her health, and the prospect of her northern tour was a constant source of delight.
paras.uz: Ertasi kungi safardagi har bir narsa Elizabet uchun yangi va qiziqarli edi; kayfiyati zavq holatida edi; chunki u opasini sog'lig'i haqidagi har qanday qo'rquvni haydaydigan darajada yaxshi ko'rgan edi, shimoliy sayohat istiqboli esa doimiy quvonch manbai edi.

paras.en: When they left the high road for the lane to Hunsford, every eye was in search of the Parsonage, and every turning expected to bring it in view. The palings of Rosings Park was their boundary on one side. Elizabeth smiled at the recollection of all that she had heard of its inhabitants.
paras.uz: Ular katta yo'ldan Xansfordga boradigan tor yo'lga burilishganda, hammaning ko'zi ruhoniy uyini izlardi va har bir burilish uni ko'rsatishi kutilardi. Bir tomonda ularning chegarasi Rozings Park panjarasi edi. Elizabet uning aholisi haqida eshitganlarining hammasini eslab jilmaydi.

paras.en: At length the Parsonage was discernible. The garden sloping to the road, the house standing in it, the green pales, and the laurel hedge, everything declared they were arriving. Mr. Collins and Charlotte appeared at the door, and the carriage stopped at the small gate which led by a short gravel walk to the house, amidst the nods and smiles of the whole party. In a moment they were all out of the chaise, rejoicing at the sight of each other. Mrs. Collins welcomed her friend with the liveliest pleasure, and Elizabeth was more and more satisfied with coming when she found herself so affectionately received. She saw instantly that her cousin's manners were not altered by his marriage; his formal civility was just what it had been, and he detained her some minutes at the gate to hear and satisfy his inquiries after all her family. They were then, with no other delay than his pointing out the neatness of the entrance, taken into the house; and as soon as they were in the parlour, he welcomed them a second time, with ostentatious formality to his humble abode, and punctually repeated all his wife's offers of refreshment.
paras.uz: Nihoyat ruhoniy uyi ko'rindi. Yo'lga qarab qiyalab tushgan bog', unda turgan uy, yashil panjara va dafna to'sig'i — hamma narsa ular yetib kelayotganini bildirardi. Janob Kollinz va Sharlotta eshikda paydo bo'lishdi va kareta butun davraning bosh irg'ashlari va tabassumlari orasida qisqa shag'alli yo'lak orqali uyga olib boradigan kichkina darvoza oldida to'xtadi. Bir lahzada hammalari aravadan tushib, bir-birini ko'rganidan xursand bo'lishdi. Missis Kollinz dugonasini eng jo'shqin zavq bilan kutib oldi va Elizabet o'zini shunchalik mehr bilan qabul qilishganini ko'rib, kelganidan tobora ko'proq mamnun bo'ldi. U darhol amakivachchasining muomalasi nikohdan keyin o'zgarmaganini ko'rdi; uning rasmiy xushmuomalaligi avvalgidek edi va u uni butun oilasi haqidagi so'roqlarini eshitish va qondirish uchun bir necha daqiqa darvoza oldida ushlab turdi. Keyin uning kirish joyining ozodaligini ko'rsatishidan boshqa hech qanday kechikishsiz ularni uyga olib kirishdi; mehmonxonaga kirishlari bilanoq u ularni ikkinchi marta, ko'z-ko'z qiluvchi rasmiyat bilan o'zining kamtarona maskaniga xush kelibsiz dedi va xotinining barcha mehmon qilish takliflarini aniq takrorladi.

paras.en: Elizabeth was prepared to see him in his glory; and she could not help in fancying that in displaying the good proportion of the room, its aspect and its furniture, he addressed himself particularly to her, as if wishing to make her feel what she had lost in refusing him. But though everything seemed neat and comfortable, she was not able to gratify him by any sigh of repentance, and rather looked with wonder at her friend that she could have so cheerful an air with such a companion. When Mr. Collins said anything of which his wife might reasonably be ashamed, which certainly was not unseldom, she involuntarily turned her eye on Charlotte. Once or twice she could discern a faint blush; but in general Charlotte wisely did not hear.
paras.uz: Elizabet uni o'z shon-shuhratida ko'rishga tayyor edi; u xonaning yaxshi o'lchamlarini, ko'rinishini va jihozlarini ko'rsatayotganda go'yo uni rad etib nimani yo'qotganini his qildirmoqchidek ayniqsa unga murojaat qilayotgandek tuyulishidan o'zini tiya olmadi. Lekin hamma narsa ozoda va qulay ko'rinsa ham, u uni hech qanday pushaymonlik xo'rsinig'i bilan xursand qila olmadi, aksincha dugonasiga bunday hamroh bilan qanday qilib bunchalik quvnoq qiyofada bo'la olishidan hayratlanib qaradi. Janob Kollinz xotini asosli ravishda uyalishi mumkin bo'lgan biror gap aytganda — bu, albatta, kamdan-kam emasdi — u beixtiyor ko'zini Sharlottaga qaratardi. Bir-ikki marta u zaif qizarishni sezdi; lekin umuman olganda Sharlotta oqilona ravishda eshitmasdi.

paras.en: After sitting long enough to admire every article of furniture in the room, from the sideboard to the fender, to give an account of their journey, and of all that had happened in London, Mr. Collins invited them to take a stroll in the garden, which was large and well laid out, and to the cultivation of which he attended himself. To work in this garden was one of his most respectable pleasures; and Elizabeth admired the command of countenance with which Charlotte talked of the healthfulness of the exercise, and owned she encouraged it as much as possible. Here, leading the way through every walk and cross walk, and scarcely allowing them an interval to utter the praises he asked for, every view was pointed out with a minuteness which left beauty entirely behind.
paras.uz: Xonadagi har bir jihozni — bufetdan kamin panjarasigacha — maqtash, safarlari va Londonda bo'lgan hamma narsa haqida hisobot berish uchun yetarlicha uzoq o'tirgach, janob Kollinz ularni katta va yaxshi rejalashtirilgan, o'zi parvarish qiladigan bog'da sayr qilishga taklif qildi. Bu bog'da ishlash uning eng hurmatli zavqlaridan biri edi; Elizabet Sharlottaning bu mashg'ulotning sog'liq uchun foydaliligi haqida gapirgandagi va uni iloji boricha rag'batlantirishini tan olgandagi yuz ifodasini boshqarishiga qoyil qoldi. Bu yerda u har bir yo'lak va kesishgan yo'lak bo'ylab boshlab borib, ular o'zi so'ragan maqtovlarni aytishiga zo'rg'a oraliq qoldirib, har bir manzarani go'zallikni butunlay ortda qoldiradigan mayda-chuydalik bilan ko'rsatdi.

paras.en: He could number the fields in every direction, and could tell how many trees there were in the most distant clump. But of all the views which his garden, or which the country or kingdom could boast, none were to be compared with the prospect of Rosings, afforded by an opening in the trees that bordered the park nearly opposite the front of his house. It was a handsome modern building, well situated on rising ground.
paras.uz: U har tomondagi dalalarni sanay olar va eng uzoqdagi daraxtzorda nechta daraxt borligini ayta olardi. Lekin uning bog'i, mamlakat yoki qirollik maqtana oladigan barcha manzaralar ichida hech biri uyining old tomoniga deyarli ro'para bo'lgan parkni o'rab turgan daraxtlar orasidagi ochiq joydan ko'rinadigan Rozings manzarasi bilan tenglasha olmasdi. U balandlikda yaxshi joylashgan chiroyli zamonaviy bino edi.

paras.en: From his garden, Mr. Collins would have led them round his two meadows; but the ladies, not having shoes to encounter the remains of a white frost, turned back; and while Sir William accompanied him, Charlotte took her sister and friend over the house, extremely well pleased, probably, to have the opportunity of showing it without her husband's help. It was rather small, but well built and convenient; and everything was fitted up and arranged with a neatness and consistency of which Elizabeth gave Charlotte all the credit. When Mr. Collins could be forgotten, there was really an air of great comfort throughout, and by Charlotte's evident enjoyment of it, Elizabeth supposed he must be often forgotten.
paras.uz: Bog'idan keyin janob Kollinz ularni ikki o'tloq atrofida aylantirmoqchi edi; lekin xonimlar oq qirov qoldiqlariga dosh beradigan oyoq kiyimlariga ega bo'lmagani uchun ortga qaytishdi; ser Uilyam unga hamroh bo'lgan paytda Sharlotta singlisi va dugonasini uyni ko'rsatish uchun olib ketdi, ehtimol, uni erining yordamisiz ko'rsatish imkoniyatidan nihoyatda mamnun bo'lgandir. Uy ancha kichik, lekin yaxshi qurilgan va qulay edi; hamma narsa shunday ozodalik va izchillik bilan jihozlangan va tartibga solingan ediki, Elizabet buning uchun Sharlottaga to'liq tahsin aytdi. Janob Kollinzni unutish mumkin bo'lganda, butun uyda haqiqatan ham katta qulaylik ruhi bor edi va Sharlottaning bundan aniq zavqlanishiga qarab, Elizabet uni tez-tez unutish kerak bo'lsa kerak, deb taxmin qildi.

paras.en: She had already learnt that Lady Catherine was still in the country. It was spoken of again while they were at dinner, when Mr. Collins joining in, observed:
paras.uz: U ledi Ketrin hali ham shu yerlarda ekanini allaqachon bilib olgan edi. Bu haqda tushlik paytida yana gap bo'ldi, shunda janob Kollinz suhbatga qo'shilib, dedi:

paras.en: “Yes, Miss Elizabeth, you will have the honour of seeing Lady Catherine de Bourgh on the ensuing Sunday at church, and I need not say you will be delighted with her. She is all affability and condescension, and I doubt not but you will be honoured with some portion of her notice when service is over. I have scarcely any hesitation in saying she will include you and my sister Maria in every invitation with which she honours us during your stay here. Her behaviour to my dear Charlotte is charming. We dine at Rosings twice every week, and are never allowed to walk home. Her ladyship's carriage is regularly ordered for us. I should say, one of her ladyship's carriages, for she has several.”
paras.uz: «Ha, miss Elizabet, kelasi yakshanba kuni cherkovda ledi Ketrin de Burgni ko'rish sharafiga muyassar bo'lasiz va undan zavqlanishingizni aytishga hojat yo'q. U butunlay xushmuomalalik va yuqoridan mehribonlik timsoli va shubham yo'qki, ibodat tugagach, sizni uning e'tiboridan biroz ulush bilan sharaflashadi. Bu yerda bo'lgan vaqtingizda u bizni sharaflaydigan har bir taklifga sizni va singlim Mariyani ham qo'shishini aytishda deyarli ikkilanmayman. Uning aziz Sharlottamga munosabati maftunkor. Biz haftada ikki marta Rozingsda tushlik qilamiz va bizga hech qachon uyga piyoda qaytishga ruxsat berilmaydi. Biz uchun muntazam ravishda janoblarining karetasi buyuriladi. Janoblarining karetalaridan biri desam to'g'riroq bo'ladi, chunki uning bir nechtasi bor».

paras.en: “Lady Catherine is a very respectable, sensible woman indeed,” added Charlotte, “and a most attentive neighbour.”
paras.uz: «Ledi Ketrin haqiqatan ham juda hurmatli, aqlli ayol, — qo'shib qo'ydi Sharlotta, — va juda e'tiborli qo'shni».

paras.en: “Very true, my dear, that is exactly what I say. She is the sort of woman whom one cannot regard with too much deference.”
paras.uz: «Juda to'g'ri, azizim, men aynan shuni aytaman. U shunday ayolki, unga haddan tashqari ko'p ehtirom bilan qarashning iloji yo'q».

paras.en: The evening was spent chiefly in talking over Hertfordshire news, and telling again what had already been written; and when it closed, Elizabeth, in the solitude of her chamber, had to meditate upon Charlotte's degree of contentment, to understand her address in guiding, and composure in bearing with, her husband, and to acknowledge that it was all done very well. She had also to anticipate how her visit would pass, the quiet tenor of their usual employments, the vexatious interruptions of Mr. Collins, and the gaieties of their intercourse with Rosings. A lively imagination soon settled it all.
paras.uz: Oqshom asosan Xertfordshir yangiliklarini muhokama qilish va allaqachon yozilgan narsalarni yana aytib berish bilan o'tdi; u tugagach, Elizabet xonasida yolg'iz qolib, Sharlottaning qanchalik qanoatli ekani haqida o'ylashi, erini boshqarishdagi mahoratini va unga chidashdagi xotirjamligini tushunishi va bularning hammasi juda yaxshi bajarilganini tan olishi kerak edi. Shuningdek, u tashrifi qanday o'tishini — ularning odatiy mashg'ulotlarining sokin oqimini, janob Kollinzning g'ashga tegadigan aralashuvlarini va Rozings bilan muloqotlarining quvnoqliklarini oldindan tasavvur qilishi kerak edi. Jo'shqin tasavvur tez orada bularning hammasini hal qildi.

paras.en: About the middle of the next day, as she was in her room getting ready for a walk, a sudden noise below seemed to speak the whole house in confusion; and, after listening a moment, she heard somebody running up stairs in a violent hurry, and calling loudly after her. She opened the door and met Maria in the landing place, who, breathless with agitation, cried out--
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni tush payti, u xonasida sayrga tayyorlanayotganda, pastdagi to'satdan shovqin butun uy sarosimaga tushganini bildirganday bo'ldi; bir lahza tinglab, kimdir juda shoshib yuqoriga yugurib chiqayotganini va uni baland ovozda chaqirayotganini eshitdi. U eshikni ochdi va zinapoya maydonchasida hayajondan nafasi tiqilgan Mariyani uchratdi, u qichqirdi:

paras.en: “Oh, my dear Eliza! pray make haste and come into the dining-room, for there is such a sight to be seen! I will not tell you what it is. Make haste, and come down this moment.”
paras.uz: «Oh, azizim Eliza! Iltimos, shoshil va ovqatxonaga kel, chunki u yerda shunday manzara bor! Nima ekanini aytmayman. Shoshil va hozir pastga tush».

paras.en: Elizabeth asked questions in vain; Maria would tell her nothing more, and down they ran into the dining-room, which fronted the lane, in quest of this wonder; It was two ladies stopping in a low phaeton at the garden gate.
paras.uz: Elizabet behuda savollar berdi; Mariya unga boshqa hech narsa aytmadi va ular bu mo'jizani izlab tor yo'lga qaragan ovqatxonaga yugurib tushishdi; bu bog' darvozasi oldida past faetonda to'xtagan ikki xonim edi.

paras.en: “And is this all?” cried Elizabeth. “I expected at least that the pigs were got into the garden, and here is nothing but Lady Catherine and her daughter.”
paras.uz: «Shu xolosmi? — xitob qildi Elizabet. — Hech bo'lmaganda cho'chqalar bog'ga kirib olgan deb kutgandim, bu yerda esa ledi Ketrin va uning qizidan boshqa hech narsa yo'q».

paras.en: “La! my dear,” said Maria, quite shocked at the mistake, “it is not Lady Catherine. The old lady is Mrs. Jenkinson, who lives with them; the other is Miss de Bourgh. Only look at her. She is quite a little creature. Who would have thought that she could be so thin and small?”
paras.uz: «Voy! azizim, — dedi Mariya, xatodan butunlay dahshatga tushib, — bu ledi Ketrin emas. Keksa xonim ular bilan yashaydigan missis Jenkinson; ikkinchisi miss de Burg. Unga bir qara. U juda kichkina mavjudot. Uning bunchalik oriq va kichkina bo'lishi mumkinligini kim o'ylabdi?»

paras.en: “She is abominably rude to keep Charlotte out of doors in all this wind. Why does she not come in?”
paras.uz: «Sharlottani shunday shamolda tashqarida ushlab turishi jirkanch darajada qo'pollik. Nega u ichkariga kirmaydi?»

paras.en: “Oh, Charlotte says she hardly ever does. It is the greatest of favours when Miss de Bourgh comes in.”
paras.uz: «Oh, Sharlotta aytishicha, u deyarli hech qachon kirmaydi. Miss de Burg ichkariga kirsa, bu eng katta iltifot».

paras.en: “I like her appearance,” said Elizabeth, struck with other ideas. “She looks sickly and cross. Yes, she will do for him very well. She will make him a very proper wife.”
paras.uz: «Uning tashqi ko'rinishi menga yoqadi, — dedi Elizabet, boshqa fikrlarga berilib. — U kasalmand va jahldor ko'rinadi. Ha, u unga juda mos keladi. U unga juda munosib xotin bo'ladi».

paras.en: Mr. Collins and Charlotte were both standing at the gate in conversation with the ladies; and Sir William, to Elizabeth's high diversion, was stationed in the doorway, in earnest contemplation of the greatness before him, and constantly bowing whenever Miss de Bourgh looked that way.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinz va Sharlotta ikkalasi ham darvoza oldida xonimlar bilan suhbatlashib turishardi; ser Uilyam esa Elizabetni juda kuldirib, eshik og'zida joylashib olib, oldidagi ulug'vorlikni jiddiy tafakkur qilar va miss de Burg u tomonga qaraganda doim ta'zim qilardi.

paras.en: At length there was nothing more to be said; the ladies drove on, and the others returned into the house. Mr. Collins no sooner saw the two girls than he began to congratulate them on their good fortune, which Charlotte explained by letting them know that the whole party was asked to dine at Rosings the next day.
paras.uz: Nihoyat aytadigan gap qolmadi; xonimlar yo'lida davom etishdi, boshqalar esa uyga qaytishdi. Janob Kollinz ikki qizni ko'rishi bilanoq ularni omadlari bilan tabriklay boshladi, buni Sharlotta butun davra ertaga Rozingsga tushlikka taklif qilinganini aytib tushuntirdi.

chapters.title: Dinner at Rosings
chapters.recap_uz: Mehmonlar Rozingsga, ledi Ketrinning saroyiga taklif qilinadi. Ledi Ketrin hamma narsaga aralashadi va Elizabetni so'roqqa tutadi; Elizabet esa undan qo'rqmay javob beradi.

paras.en: Mr. Collins's triumph, in consequence of this invitation, was complete. The power of displaying the grandeur of his patroness to his wondering visitors, and of letting them see her civility towards himself and his wife, was exactly what he had wished for; and that an opportunity of doing it should be given so soon, was such an instance of Lady Catherine's condescension, as he knew not how to admire enough.
paras.uz: Bu taklif natijasida janob Kollinzning g'alabasi to'liq bo'ldi. Hayratlangan mehmonlariga homiysining ulug'vorligini namoyish qilish va ularga uning o'ziga va xotiniga ko'rsatadigan xushmuomalaligini ko'rsatish imkoniyati aynan u orzu qilgan narsa edi; buning uchun bunchalik tez imkoniyat berilishi ledi Ketrinning shunday iltifoti ediki, u unga qanchalik qoyil qolishni bilmasdi.

paras.en: “I confess,” said he, “that I should not have been at all surprised by her ladyship's asking us on Sunday to drink tea and spend the evening at Rosings. I rather expected, from my knowledge of her affability, that it would happen. But who could have foreseen such an attention as this? Who could have imagined that we should receive an invitation to dine there (an invitation, moreover, including the whole party) so immediately after your arrival!”
paras.uz: «Tan olaman, — dedi u, — agar janoblari bizni yakshanba kuni Rozingsga choy ichib, oqshomni o'tkazishga taklif qilganida, umuman hayron bo'lmagan bo'lardim. Uning xushmuomalaligini bilganim uchun, shunday bo'lishini kutgandim ham. Lekin bunday e'tiborni kim oldindan ko'ra olardi? Sizlar kelishingiz bilanoq bizni u yerga tushlikka taklif qilishlarini (buning ustiga butun davrani qamrab olgan taklif) kim tasavvur qila olardi!»

paras.en: “I am the less surprised at what has happened,” replied Sir William, “from that knowledge of what the manners of the great really are, which my situation in life has allowed me to acquire. About the court, such instances of elegant breeding are not uncommon.”
paras.uz: «Bo'lib o'tgan voqeadan kamroq hayron bo'ldim, — javob berdi ser Uilyam, — chunki hayotdagi mavqeim menga ulug'larning muomalasi aslida qanday ekanini bilib olishga imkon bergan. Saroy atrofida bunday nafis tarbiya namunalari kam uchramaydi».

paras.en: Scarcely anything was talked of the whole day or next morning but their visit to Rosings. Mr. Collins was carefully instructing them in what they were to expect, that the sight of such rooms, so many servants, and so splendid a dinner, might not wholly overpower them.
paras.uz: Butun kun va ertasi ertalab ularning Rozingsga tashrifidan boshqa hech narsa haqida deyarli gapirilmadi. Janob Kollinz bunday xonalarni, shuncha ko'p xizmatkorlarni va bunchalik dabdabali tushlikni ko'rish ularni butunlay esankiratib qo'ymasligi uchun ularga nimani kutish kerakligini puxta o'rgatardi.

paras.en: When the ladies were separating for the toilette, he said to Elizabeth--
paras.uz: Xonimlar kiyinish uchun tarqalishayotganda, u Elizabetga dedi:

paras.en: “Do not make yourself uneasy, my dear cousin, about your apparel. Lady Catherine is far from requiring that elegance of dress in us which becomes herself and her daughter. I would advise you merely to put on whatever of your clothes is superior to the rest--there is no occasion for anything more. Lady Catherine will not think the worse of you for being simply dressed. She likes to have the distinction of rank preserved.”
paras.uz: «Kiyimingiz haqida xavotirlanmang, aziz amakivachcham. Ledi Ketrin bizdan o'ziga va qiziga yarashgan kiyim nafisligini talab qilishdan yiroq. Sizga shunchaki kiyimlaringizdan qolganlaridan yaxshirog'ini kiyishni maslahat beraman — bundan ortiq narsaga hojat yo'q. Ledi Ketrin oddiy kiyinganingiz uchun siz haqingizda yomonroq o'ylamaydi. U martaba farqi saqlanishini yaxshi ko'radi».

paras.en: While they were dressing, he came two or three times to their different doors, to recommend their being quick, as Lady Catherine very much objected to be kept waiting for her dinner. Such formidable accounts of her ladyship, and her manner of living, quite frightened Maria Lucas who had been little used to company, and she looked forward to her introduction at Rosings with as much apprehension as her father had done to his presentation at St. James's.
paras.uz: Ular kiyinayotganda, u ikki-uch marta ularning eshiklariga kelib, tezroq bo'lishni tavsiya qildi, chunki ledi Ketrin tushligini kuttirishlariga juda qarshi edi. Janoblari va uning turmush tarzi haqidagi bunday qo'rqinchli hikoyalar jamiyatga kam o'rgangan Mariya Lukasni butunlay qo'rqitib yubordi va u Rozingsda tanishtirilishini otasi Sent-Jeymsda tanishtirilishini kutgandek qo'rquv bilan kutdi.

paras.en: As the weather was fine, they had a pleasant walk of about half a mile across the park. Every park has its beauty and its prospects; and Elizabeth saw much to be pleased with, though she could not be in such raptures as Mr. Collins expected the scene to inspire, and was but slightly affected by his enumeration of the windows in front of the house, and his relation of what the glazing altogether had originally cost Sir Lewis de Bourgh.
paras.uz: Ob-havo yaxshi bo'lgani uchun ular park bo'ylab taxminan yarim millik yoqimli sayr qilishdi. Har bir parkning o'z go'zalligi va manzaralari bor; Elizabet mamnun bo'ladigan ko'p narsalarni ko'rdi, garchi janob Kollinz sahna uyg'otishini kutgan darajada hayajonga tusha olmasa ham va uning uyning old tomonidagi derazalarni sanashi hamda barcha oynalar dastlab ser Lyuis de Burgga qanchaga tushgani haqidagi hikoyasidan juda kam ta'sirlandi.

paras.en: When they ascended the steps to the hall, Maria's alarm was every moment increasing, and even Sir William did not look perfectly calm. Elizabeth's courage did not fail her. She had heard nothing of Lady Catherine that spoke her awful from any extraordinary talents or miraculous virtue, and the mere stateliness of money or rank she thought she could witness without trepidation.
paras.uz: Ular zinapoyadan zalga ko'tarilishayotganda, Mariyaning qo'rquvi har lahza ortib bordi, hatto ser Uilyam ham mutlaqo xotirjam ko'rinmasdi. Elizabetning jasorati uni tark etmadi. U ledi Ketrin haqida uni biror g'ayrioddiy iste'dod yoki mo'jizaviy fazilat tufayli qo'rqinchli qiladigan hech narsa eshitmagan edi, pul yoki martabaning shunchaki salobatini esa titramay kuzata olaman, deb o'ylardi.

paras.en: From the entrance-hall, of which Mr. Collins pointed out, with a rapturous air, the fine proportion and the finished ornaments, they followed the servants through an ante-chamber, to the room where Lady Catherine, her daughter, and Mrs. Jenkinson were sitting. Her ladyship, with great condescension, arose to receive them; and as Mrs. Collins had settled it with her husband that the office of introduction should be hers, it was performed in a proper manner, without any of those apologies and thanks which he would have thought necessary.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinz hayajonli qiyofada uning chiroyli mutanosibligi va pardozlangan bezaklarini ko'rsatgan kirish zalidan ular xizmatkorlar ortidan oldingi xona orqali ledi Ketrin, uning qizi va missis Jenkinson o'tirgan xonaga borishdi. Janoblari katta iltifot bilan ularni qabul qilish uchun o'rnidan turdi; missis Kollinz eri bilan tanishtirish vazifasi o'ziniki bo'lishini kelishib olgani uchun, u munosib tarzda, eri zarur deb hisoblagan uzr va minnatdorchiliklarning birortasisiz bajarildi.

paras.en: In spite of having been at St. James's, Sir William was so completely awed by the grandeur surrounding him, that he had but just courage enough to make a very low bow, and take his seat without saying a word; and his daughter, frightened almost out of her senses, sat on the edge of her chair, not knowing which way to look. Elizabeth found herself quite equal to the scene, and could observe the three ladies before her composedly. Lady Catherine was a tall, large woman, with strongly-marked features, which might once have been handsome. Her air was not conciliating, nor was her manner of receiving them such as to make her visitors forget their inferior rank. She was not rendered formidable by silence; but whatever she said was spoken in so authoritative a tone, as marked her self-importance, and brought Mr. Wickham immediately to Elizabeth's mind; and from the observation of the day altogether, she believed Lady Catherine to be exactly what he represented.
paras.uz: Sent-Jeymsda bo'lganiga qaramay, ser Uilyam atrofidagi ulug'vorlikdan shunchalik qattiq hayratda qoldiki, juda past ta'zim qilib, bir og'iz ham gapirmay o'tirishga zo'rg'a jur'ati yetdi; qizi esa qo'rquvdan deyarli es-hushini yo'qotib, qaysi tomonga qarashni bilmay, kursisining chetiga o'tirdi. Elizabet o'zini sahnaga butunlay munosib his qildi va oldidagi uch xonimni xotirjam kuzata oldi. Ledi Ketrin baland bo'yli, yirik ayol edi, keskin chehrasi bir paytlar chiroyli bo'lgan bo'lishi mumkin edi. Uning qiyofasi murosali emasdi, ularni qabul qilish tarzi ham mehmonlariga past martabasini unuttiradigan darajada emasdi. Sukut uni qo'rqinchli qilmasdi; lekin nima demasin, shunday hukmron ohangda aytilardiki, bu uning o'zini muhim sanashini ko'rsatardi va darhol Elizabetning xayoliga janob Uikhemni keltirdi; kun davomidagi kuzatishlaridan u ledi Ketrin aynan u tasvirlagandek ekaniga ishondi.

paras.en: When, after examining the mother, in whose countenance and deportment she soon found some resemblance of Mr. Darcy, she turned her eyes on the daughter, she could almost have joined in Maria's astonishment at her being so thin and so small. There was neither in figure nor face any likeness between the ladies. Miss de Bourgh was pale and sickly; her features, though not plain, were insignificant; and she spoke very little, except in a low voice, to Mrs. Jenkinson, in whose appearance there was nothing remarkable, and who was entirely engaged in listening to what she said, and placing a screen in the proper direction before her eyes.
paras.uz: Chehrasi va o'zini tutishida tez orada janob Darsiga biroz o'xshashlik topgan onani ko'zdan kechirgach, u ko'zlarini qizga qaratganida, Mariyaning uning bunchalik oriq va kichkina ekanidan hayratiga deyarli qo'shilishi mumkin edi. Xonimlar o'rtasida na qomatda, na yuzda hech qanday o'xshashlik yo'q edi. Miss de Burg rangpar va kasalmand edi; uning chehrasi xunuk bo'lmasa ham, ko'zga tashlanmasdi; u juda kam gapirardi, faqat past ovozda tashqi ko'rinishida hech qanday diqqatga sazovor narsa bo'lmagan va butunlay uning aytganlarini tinglash hamda ko'zlari oldidagi to'siqni to'g'ri yo'nalishga qo'yish bilan band bo'lgan missis Jenkinsonga gapirardi.

paras.en: After sitting a few minutes, they were all sent to one of the windows to admire the view, Mr. Collins attending them to point out its beauties, and Lady Catherine kindly informing them that it was much better worth looking at in the summer.
paras.uz: Bir necha daqiqa o'tirgach, hammalarini manzaraga qoyil qolish uchun derazalardan biriga yuborishdi; janob Kollinz uning go'zalliklarini ko'rsatish uchun ularga hamroh bo'ldi, ledi Ketrin esa mehribonlik bilan yozda unga qarash ancha arziydi, deb xabar berdi.

paras.en: The dinner was exceedingly handsome, and there were all the servants and all the articles of plate which Mr. Collins had promised; and, as he had likewise foretold, he took his seat at the bottom of the table, by her ladyship's desire, and looked as if he felt that life could furnish nothing greater. He carved, and ate, and praised with delighted alacrity; and every dish was commended, first by him and then by Sir William, who was now enough recovered to echo whatever his son-in-law said, in a manner which Elizabeth wondered Lady Catherine could bear. But Lady Catherine seemed gratified by their excessive admiration, and gave most gracious smiles, especially when any dish on the table proved a novelty to them. The party did not supply much conversation.
paras.uz: Tushlik nihoyatda dabdabali edi, janob Kollinz va'da qilgan barcha xizmatkorlar va barcha kumush idishlar bor edi; u xuddi oldindan aytganidek, janoblarining xohishi bilan stolning quyi uchiga o'tirdi va hayot bundan kattaroq narsa bera olmasligini his qilayotganday ko'rinardi. U go'shtni kesdi, yedi va zavqli chaqqonlik bilan maqtadi; har bir taomni avval u, keyin ser Uilyam maqtardi — u endi kuyovining har bir gapini takrorlash uchun yetarlicha o'ziga kelgan edi, shunday tarzdaki, Elizabet ledi Ketrin bunga qanday chidashiga hayron bo'ldi. Lekin ledi Ketrin ularning haddan tashqari hayratidan mamnun ko'rinardi va ayniqsa stoldagi biror taom ular uchun yangilik bo'lib chiqqanda eng marhamatli tabassumlarni hadya qilardi. Davra ko'p suhbat bera olmadi.

paras.en: Elizabeth was ready to speak whenever there was an opening, but she was seated between Charlotte and Miss de Bourgh--the former of whom was engaged in listening to Lady Catherine, and the latter said not a word to her all dinner-time. Mrs. Jenkinson was chiefly employed in watching how little Miss de Bourgh ate, pressing her to try some other dish, and fearing she was indisposed. Maria thought speaking out of the question, and the gentlemen did nothing but eat and admire.
paras.uz: Elizabet imkon bo'lganda gapirishga tayyor edi, lekin u Sharlotta va miss de Burg o'rtasida o'tirgan edi — birinchisi ledi Ketrinni tinglash bilan band edi, ikkinchisi esa butun tushlik davomida unga bir og'iz ham gapirmadi. Missis Jenkinson asosan miss de Burg qanchalik kam yeyayotganini kuzatish, uni boshqa taomni tatib ko'rishga undash va uning tobi yo'qligidan qo'rqish bilan band edi. Mariya gapirishni aqlga sig'maydigan narsa deb hisoblardi, janoblar esa yeyish va hayratlanishdan boshqa hech narsa qilmasdi.

paras.en: When the ladies returned to the drawing-room, there was little to be done but to hear Lady Catherine talk, which she did without any intermission till coffee came in, delivering her opinion on every subject in so decisive a manner, as proved that she was not used to have her judgement controverted. She inquired into Charlotte's domestic concerns familiarly and minutely, gave her a great deal of advice as to the management of them all; told her how everything ought to be regulated in so small a family as hers, and instructed her as to the care of her cows and her poultry. Elizabeth found that nothing was beneath this great lady's attention, which could furnish her with an occasion of dictating to others.
paras.uz: Xonimlar mehmonxonaga qaytgach, ledi Ketrinning gapini tinglashdan boshqa qiladigan ish kam qoldi, u esa qahva kelgunicha to'xtovsiz gapirdi, har bir mavzu bo'yicha fikrini shunchalik qat'iy bildirdiki, bu uning hukmiga e'tiroz bildirilishiga o'rganmaganini isbotlardi. U Sharlottaning uy ishlari haqida bemalol va batafsil so'radi, ularning hammasini boshqarish bo'yicha unga juda ko'p maslahat berdi; uning oilasidek kichik oilada hamma narsa qanday tartibga solinishi kerakligini aytdi va sigirlari hamda parrandalariga qanday qarash kerakligini o'rgatdi. Elizabet bu buyuk xonimga boshqalarga buyruq berish imkoniyatini bera oladigan hech narsa uning e'tiboridan past emasligini ko'rdi.

paras.en: In the intervals of her discourse with Mrs. Collins, she addressed a variety of questions to Maria and Elizabeth, but especially to the latter, of whose connections she knew the least, and who she observed to Mrs. Collins was a very genteel, pretty kind of girl. She asked her, at different times, how many sisters she had, whether they were older or younger than herself, whether any of them were likely to be married, whether they were handsome, where they had been educated, what carriage her father kept, and what had been her mother's maiden name? Elizabeth felt all the impertinence of her questions but answered them very composedly. Lady Catherine then observed,
paras.uz: Missis Kollinz bilan suhbatining oraliqlarida u Mariya va Elizabetga turli savollar berdi, lekin ayniqsa ikkinchisiga, chunki uning qarindoshlari haqida eng kam bilardi va missis Kollinzga u juda odobli, chiroyli qiz ekanini aytdi. U undan turli vaqtlarda nechta opa-singlisi borligini, ular undan katta yoki kichikligini, ulardan birortasi turmushga chiqishi ehtimoli bormi, ular chiroylimi, qayerda ta'lim olishgan, otasi qanday kareta saqlaydi va onasining qizlik familiyasi nima bo'lganini so'radi. Elizabet uning savollarining butun surbetligini his qildi, lekin ularga juda xotirjam javob berdi. Shunda ledi Ketrin dedi:

paras.en: “Your father's estate is entailed on Mr. Collins, I think. For your sake,” turning to Charlotte, “I am glad of it; but otherwise I see no occasion for entailing estates from the female line. It was not thought necessary in Sir Lewis de Bourgh's family. Do you play and sing, Miss Bennet?”
paras.uz: «Otangizning mulki janob Kollinzga meros cheklovi bilan o'tadi, menimcha. Sizning xotiringiz uchun, — Sharlottaga o'girilib, — bundan xursandman; lekin aks holda mulklarni ayollar avlodidan meros cheklovi bilan tortib olish uchun hech qanday sabab ko'rmayman. Ser Lyuis de Burgning oilasida buni zarur deb hisoblashmagan. Siz chalasizmi va kuylaysizmi, miss Bennet?»

paras.en: “A little.”
paras.uz: «Ozgina».

paras.en: “Oh! then--some time or other we shall be happy to hear you. Our instrument is a capital one, probably superior to----You shall try it some day. Do your sisters play and sing?”
paras.uz: «Oh! Unday bo'lsa — qachondir sizni eshitishdan xursand bo'lamiz. Bizning cholg'uimiz a'lo darajada, ehtimol ...dan ham ustun. Bir kun uni sinab ko'rasiz. Opa-singillaringiz chalib, kuylaydimi?»

paras.en: “One of them does.”
paras.uz: «Ulardan biri».

paras.en: “Why did not you all learn? You ought all to have learned. The Miss Webbs all play, and their father has not so good an income as yours. Do you draw?”
paras.uz: «Nega hammangiz o'rganmadingiz? Hammangiz o'rganishingiz kerak edi. Miss Vebblarning hammasi chaladi, otalarining daromadi esa sizning otangiznikidek yaxshi emas. Rasm chizasizmi?»

paras.en: “No, not at all.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, umuman».

paras.en: “What, none of you?”
paras.uz: «Nima, hech biringiz?»

paras.en: “Not one.”
paras.uz: «Birortamiz ham».

paras.en: “That is very strange. But I suppose you had no opportunity. Your mother should have taken you to town every spring for the benefit of masters.”
paras.uz: «Bu juda g'alati. Lekin, o'ylaymanki, imkoniyatingiz bo'lmagan. Onangiz sizlarni har bahorda ustozlardan foydalanish uchun Londonga olib borishi kerak edi».

paras.en: “My mother would have had no objection, but my father hates London.”
paras.uz: «Onamning e'tirozi bo'lmasdi, lekin otam Londonni yomon ko'radi».

paras.en: “Has your governess left you?”
paras.uz: «Murabbiyangiz sizlarni tark etdimi?»

paras.en: “We never had any governess.”
paras.uz: «Bizda hech qachon murabbiya bo'lmagan».

paras.en: “No governess! How was that possible? Five daughters brought up at home without a governess! I never heard of such a thing. Your mother must have been quite a slave to your education.”
paras.uz: «Murabbiya yo'q! Bu qanday mumkin edi? Besh qiz uyda murabbiyasiz tarbiyalangan! Bunday narsani hech qachon eshitmaganman. Onangiz sizlarning ta'limingizning quliga aylangan bo'lsa kerak».

paras.en: Elizabeth could hardly help smiling as she assured her that had not been the case.
paras.uz: Elizabet bunday bo'lmaganiga ishontirarkan, jilmaymaslikka zo'rg'a tutib turdi.

paras.en: “Then, who taught you? who attended to you? Without a governess, you must have been neglected.”
paras.uz: «Unda sizlarni kim o'qitgan? Sizlarga kim qaragan? Murabbiyasiz sizlar e'tiborsiz qolgan bo'lsangiz kerak».

paras.en: “Compared with some families, I believe we were; but such of us as wished to learn never wanted the means. We were always encouraged to read, and had all the masters that were necessary. Those who chose to be idle, certainly might.”
paras.uz: «Ba'zi oilalar bilan solishtirganda, menimcha, shunday bo'lgandir; lekin oramizdan o'qishni istaganlar hech qachon vositalarga muhtoj bo'lmagan. Bizni doim o'qishga rag'batlantirishgan va zarur bo'lgan barcha ustozlarimiz bo'lgan. Dangasa bo'lishni tanlaganlar, albatta, shunday bo'lishi mumkin edi».

paras.en: “Aye, no doubt; but that is what a governess will prevent, and if I had known your mother, I should have advised her most strenuously to engage one. I always say that nothing is to be done in education without steady and regular instruction, and nobody but a governess can give it. It is wonderful how many families I have been the means of supplying in that way. I am always glad to get a young person well placed out. Four nieces of Mrs. Jenkinson are most delightfully situated through my means; and it was but the other day that I recommended another young person, who was merely accidentally mentioned to me, and the family are quite delighted with her. Mrs. Collins, did I tell you of Lady Metcalf's calling yesterday to thank me? She finds Miss Pope a treasure. 'Lady Catherine,' said she, 'you have given me a treasure.' Are any of your younger sisters out, Miss Bennet?”
paras.uz: «Ha, shubhasiz; lekin murabbiya aynan buning oldini oladi va agar onangizni bilganimda, unga murabbiya yollashni qattiq maslahat bergan bo'lardim. Men doim aytaman, barqaror va muntazam ta'limsiz tarbiyada hech narsa qilib bo'lmaydi va buni murabbiyadan boshqa hech kim bera olmaydi. Shu yo'l bilan qanchadan-qancha oilalarni ta'minlashga sababchi bo'lganim ajoyib. Yosh odamni yaxshi joyga joylashtirishdan doim xursand bo'laman. Missis Jenkinsonning to'rt jiyani mening sharofatim bilan juda yoqimli joylashgan; yaqinda esa menga shunchaki tasodifan tilga olingan yana bir yosh odamni tavsiya qildim va oila undan juda xursand. Missis Kollinz, sizga ledi Metkalfning kecha menga rahmat aytish uchun kelganini aytdimmi? U miss Popni xazina deb topyapti. "Ledi Ketrin, — dedi u, — siz menga xazina berdingiz". Kichik opa-singillaringizdan birortasi jamiyatga chiqqanmi, miss Bennet?»

paras.en: “Yes, ma'am, all.”
paras.uz: «Ha, xonim, hammasi».

paras.en: “All! What, all five out at once? Very odd! And you only the second. The younger ones out before the elder ones are married! Your younger sisters must be very young?”
paras.uz: «Hammasi! Nima, beshalasi bir vaqtda jamiyatga chiqqanmi? Juda g'alati! Siz esa faqat ikkinchisisiz. Kattalari turmushga chiqmasdan kichiklari jamiyatga chiqqan! Kichik opa-singillaringiz juda yosh bo'lsa kerak?»

paras.en: “Yes, my youngest is not sixteen. Perhaps she is full young to be much in company. But really, ma'am, I think it would be very hard upon younger sisters, that they should not have their share of society and amusement, because the elder may not have the means or inclination to marry early. The last-born has as good a right to the pleasures of youth as the first. And to be kept back on such a motive! I think it would not be very likely to promote sisterly affection or delicacy of mind.”
paras.uz: «Ha, eng kichigimiz hali o'n oltiga to'lmagan. Ehtimol, u jamiyatda ko'p bo'lish uchun juda yoshdir. Lekin, rostini aytsam, xonim, kattalarining erta turmushga chiqish imkoniyati yoki istagi bo'lmagani uchun kichik opa-singillar jamiyat va ko'ngilxushlikdagi ulushidan mahrum bo'lishi ular uchun juda og'ir bo'lardi, deb o'ylayman. Oxirgi tug'ilgan ham birinchisi kabi yoshlik zavqlariga haqli. Va shunday sabab bilan ortda ushlab turilish! Menimcha, bu opa-singillik mehrini yoki ruh nozikligini rivojlantirishi ehtimoldan yiroq».

paras.en: “Upon my word,” said her ladyship, “you give your opinion very decidedly for so young a person. Pray, what is your age?”
paras.uz: «Ochig'ini aytsam, — dedi janoblari, — bunchalik yosh odam uchun fikringizni juda qat'iy bildirasiz. Iltimos, yoshingiz nechada?»

paras.en: “With three younger sisters grown up,” replied Elizabeth, smiling, “your ladyship can hardly expect me to own it.”
paras.uz: «Uch kichik opa-singlim voyaga yetgan bo'lsa, — jilmayib javob berdi Elizabet, — janoblari buni tan olishimni kutmasa kerak».

paras.en: Lady Catherine seemed quite astonished at not receiving a direct answer; and Elizabeth suspected herself to be the first creature who had ever dared to trifle with so much dignified impertinence.
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrin to'g'ridan-to'g'ri javob olmaganidan butunlay hayratlanganday ko'rindi; Elizabet esa bunday salobatli surbetlik bilan hazillashishga jur'at etgan birinchi mavjudot o'zi ekanidan gumon qildi.

paras.en: “You cannot be more than twenty, I am sure, therefore you need not conceal your age.”
paras.uz: «Ishonchim komilki, siz yigirmadan oshmagansiz, shuning uchun yoshingizni yashirishingizga hojat yo'q».

paras.en: “I am not one-and-twenty.”
paras.uz: «Men yigirma birga to'lmaganman».

paras.en: When the gentlemen had joined them, and tea was over, the card-tables were placed. Lady Catherine, Sir William, and Mr. and Mrs. Collins sat down to quadrille; and as Miss de Bourgh chose to play at cassino, the two girls had the honour of assisting Mrs. Jenkinson to make up her party. Their table was superlatively stupid. Scarcely a syllable was uttered that did not relate to the game, except when Mrs. Jenkinson expressed her fears of Miss de Bourgh's being too hot or too cold, or having too much or too little light. A great deal more passed at the other table. Lady Catherine was generally speaking--stating the mistakes of the three others, or relating some anecdote of herself. Mr. Collins was employed in agreeing to everything her ladyship said, thanking her for every fish he won, and apologising if he thought he won too many. Sir William did not say much. He was storing his memory with anecdotes and noble names.
paras.uz: Janoblar ularga qo'shilib, choy tugagach, karta stollari qo'yildi. Ledi Ketrin, ser Uilyam va janob hamda missis Kollinz kadril o'ynashga o'tirishdi; miss de Burg kassino o'ynashni tanlagani uchun ikki qiz missis Jenkinsonga uning davrasini to'ldirishga yordam berish sharafiga muyassar bo'lishdi. Ularning stoli o'ta zerikarli edi. Missis Jenkinson miss de Burgga juda issiq yoki juda sovuq bo'lishidan yoki yorug'lik juda ko'p yoki juda kam bo'lishidan qo'rquvini bildirgan paytlardan tashqari, o'yinga aloqasi bo'lmagan birorta bo'g'in ham aytilmadi. Boshqa stolda ancha ko'p narsa bo'lib o'tdi. Odatda ledi Ketrin gapirardi — qolgan uchtasining xatolarini aytardi yoki o'zi haqida biror latifa hikoya qilardi. Janob Kollinz janoblari aytgan hamma narsaga rozi bo'lish, yutgan har bir fishkasi uchun unga rahmat aytish va agar haddan tashqari ko'p yutdim deb o'ylasa, uzr so'rash bilan band edi. Ser Uilyam ko'p gapirmadi. U xotirasini latifalar va oliyjanob ismlar bilan to'ldirardi.

paras.en: When Lady Catherine and her daughter had played as long as they chose, the tables were broken up, the carriage was offered to Mrs. Collins, gratefully accepted and immediately ordered. The party then gathered round the fire to hear Lady Catherine determine what weather they were to have on the morrow. From these instructions they were summoned by the arrival of the coach; and with many speeches of thankfulness on Mr. Collins's side and as many bows on Sir William's they departed. As soon as they had driven from the door, Elizabeth was called on by her cousin to give her opinion of all that she had seen at Rosings, which, for Charlotte's sake, she made more favourable than it really was. But her commendation, though costing her some trouble, could by no means satisfy Mr. Collins, and he was very soon obliged to take her ladyship's praise into his own hands.
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrin va uning qizi xohlaganicha o'ynab bo'lgach, stollar yig'ishtirildi, missis Kollinzga kareta taklif qilindi, u minnatdorlik bilan qabul qilindi va darhol buyurildi. Keyin davra ledi Ketrinning ertaga qanday ob-havo bo'lishini belgilashini eshitish uchun kamin atrofiga to'plandi. Bu ko'rsatmalardan ularni karetaning kelishi chaqirib oldi; janob Kollinz tomonidan ko'plab minnatdorchilik nutqlari va ser Uilyam tomonidan shuncha ta'zimlar bilan ular jo'nab ketishdi. Eshikdan uzoqlashishlari bilanoq, amakivachchasi Elizabetdan Rozingsda ko'rgan hamma narsa haqida fikrini so'radi, u esa Sharlotta xotiri uchun uni aslidan ko'ra ijobiyroq qilib ko'rsatdi. Lekin uning maqtovi, garchi unga biroz qiyinchilik tug'dirgan bo'lsa ham, janob Kollinzni umuman qoniqtira olmadi va u tez orada janoblarini maqtashni o'z qo'liga olishga majbur bo'ldi.

chapters.title: Darcy Arrives
chapters.recap_uz: Ser Uilyam ketadi. Darsi va uning amakivachchasi polkovnik Fitsuilyam Rozingsga kelishadi va darhol Kollinzlarning uyiga tashrif buyurishadi.

paras.en: Sir William stayed only a week at Hunsford, but his visit was long enough to convince him of his daughter's being most comfortably settled, and of her possessing such a husband and such a neighbour as were not often met with. While Sir William was with them, Mr. Collins devoted his morning to driving him out in his gig, and showing him the country; but when he went away, the whole family returned to their usual employments, and Elizabeth was thankful to find that they did not see more of her cousin by the alteration, for the chief of the time between breakfast and dinner was now passed by him either at work in the garden or in reading and writing, and looking out of the window in his own book-room, which fronted the road. The room in which the ladies sat was backwards.
paras.uz: Ser Uilyam Xansfordda atigi bir hafta qoldi, lekin uning tashrifi qizi juda qulay joylashganiga va unda kamdan-kam uchraydigan shunday er va shunday qo'shni borligiga ishonch hosil qilish uchun yetarlicha uzoq bo'ldi. Ser Uilyam ular bilan bo'lgan paytda janob Kollinz ertalablarini uni yengil aravasida sayr qildirib, atrofni ko'rsatishga bag'ishladi; lekin u ketgach, butun oila odatiy mashg'ulotlariga qaytdi va Elizabet bu o'zgarish bilan amakivachchasini ko'proq ko'rmasliklaridan minnatdor bo'ldi, chunki nonushta bilan tushlik orasidagi vaqtning asosiy qismini u endi yo bog'da ishlab, yo yo'lga qaragan o'z kitobxonasida o'qib, yozib va derazadan qarab o'tkazardi. Xonimlar o'tiradigan xona orqa tomonda edi.

paras.en: Elizabeth had at first rather wondered that Charlotte should not prefer the dining-parlour for common use; it was a better sized room, and had a more pleasant aspect; but she soon saw that her friend had an excellent reason for what she did, for Mr. Collins would undoubtedly have been much less in his own apartment, had they sat in one equally lively; and she gave Charlotte credit for the arrangement.
paras.uz: Avvaliga Elizabet Sharlotta nega kundalik foydalanish uchun ovqatxonani afzal ko'rmasligiga ancha hayron bo'lgan edi; u kattaroq xona edi va ko'rinishi yoqimliroq edi; lekin tez orada u dugonasining qilgan ishiga ajoyib sababi borligini ko'rdi, chunki agar ular xuddi shunday jonli xonada o'tirganlarida, janob Kollinz shubhasiz o'z xonasida ancha kamroq bo'lardi; va u bu tartib uchun Sharlottaga tahsin aytdi.

paras.en: From the drawing-room they could distinguish nothing in the lane, and were indebted to Mr. Collins for the knowledge of what carriages went along, and how often especially Miss de Bourgh drove by in her phaeton, which he never failed coming to inform them of, though it happened almost every day. She not unfrequently stopped at the Parsonage, and had a few minutes' conversation with Charlotte, but was scarcely ever prevailed upon to get out.
paras.uz: Mehmonxonadan ular tor yo'lda hech narsani ajrata olmasdilar va qanday aravalar o'tganini, ayniqsa miss de Burg faetonida qanchalik tez-tez o'tganini bilishda janob Kollinzga qarzdor edilar — u bu haqda ularga xabar berishga kelishni hech qachon kanda qilmasdi, garchi bu deyarli har kuni bo'lsa ham. U ruhoniy uyi oldida tez-tez to'xtab, Sharlotta bilan bir necha daqiqa suhbatlashardi, lekin uni tushishga deyarli hech qachon ko'ndirib bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: Very few days passed in which Mr. Collins did not walk to Rosings, and not many in which his wife did not think it necessary to go likewise; and till Elizabeth recollected that there might be other family livings to be disposed of, she could not understand the sacrifice of so many hours. Now and then they were honoured with a call from her ladyship, and nothing escaped her observation that was passing in the room during these visits. She examined into their employments, looked at their work, and advised them to do it differently; found fault with the arrangement of the furniture; or detected the housemaid in negligence; and if she accepted any refreshment, seemed to do it only for the sake of finding out that Mrs. Collins's joints of meat were too large for her family.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinz Rozingsga piyoda bormagan kunlar juda kam o'tardi, xotini ham borishni zarur deb hisoblamagan kunlar esa ko'p emasdi; Elizabet oilaning boshqa ruhoniylik lavozimlari ham taqsimlanishi mumkinligini eslaguncha shuncha soatlarning qurbon qilinishini tushuna olmadi. Vaqti-vaqti bilan janoblari ularni tashrifi bilan sharaflardi va bu tashriflar davomida xonada bo'layotgan hech narsa uning nazaridan chetda qolmasdi. U ularning mashg'ulotlarini tekshirar, ishlariga qarar va boshqacha qilishni maslahat berardi; mebelning joylashuvidan ayb topardi yoki xizmatkor qizni beparvolikda fosh qilardi; agar biror yegulikni qabul qilsa, buni faqat missis Kollinzning go'sht bo'laklari uning oilasi uchun haddan tashqari katta ekanini aniqlash uchun qilganday ko'rinardi.

paras.en: Elizabeth soon perceived, that though this great lady was not in commission of the peace of the county, she was a most active magistrate in her own parish, the minutest concerns of which were carried to her by Mr. Collins; and whenever any of the cottagers were disposed to be quarrelsome, discontented, or too poor, she sallied forth into the village to settle their differences, silence their complaints, and scold them into harmony and plenty.
paras.uz: Elizabet tez orada sezdiki, bu buyuk xonim grafligining tinchlik sudyasi bo'lmasa ham, o'z qavmida eng faol hakam edi, uning eng mayda ishlarini ham janob Kollinz unga yetkazardi; va qishloq aholisidan birortasi janjalkash, norozi yoki juda kambag'al bo'lishga moyil bo'lsa, u ularning kelishmovchiliklarini hal qilish, shikoyatlarini o'chirish va ularni koyib, totuvlik va farovonlikka keltirish uchun qishloqqa yo'l olardi.

paras.en: The entertainment of dining at Rosings was repeated about twice a week; and, allowing for the loss of Sir William, and there being only one card-table in the evening, every such entertainment was the counterpart of the first. Their other engagements were few, as the style of living in the neighbourhood in general was beyond Mr. Collins's reach. This, however, was no evil to Elizabeth, and upon the whole she spent her time comfortably enough; there were half-hours of pleasant conversation with Charlotte, and the weather was so fine for the time of year that she had often great enjoyment out of doors. Her favourite walk, and where she frequently went while the others were calling on Lady Catherine, was along the open grove which edged that side of the park, where there was a nice sheltered path, which no one seemed to value but herself, and where she felt beyond the reach of Lady Catherine's curiosity.
paras.uz: Rozingsda tushlik qilish ko'ngilxushligi haftada taxminan ikki marta takrorlanardi; ser Uilyamning yo'qligini va kechqurun faqat bitta karta stoli bo'lishini hisobga olmaganda, har bir bunday ko'ngilxushlik birinchisining aynan nusxasi edi. Ularning boshqa tadbirlari kam edi, chunki mahalladagi turmush tarzi umuman janob Kollinzning imkoniyatlaridan yuqori edi. Biroq bu Elizabet uchun yomonlik emasdi va umuman olganda u vaqtini ancha qulay o'tkazardi; Sharlotta bilan yarim soatlik yoqimli suhbatlar bo'lardi, yilning bu fasli uchun ob-havo shunchalik yaxshi ediki, u ko'pincha tashqarida katta zavq olardi. Uning sevimli sayr joyi, boshqalar ledi Ketrinni ko'rgani borganda tez-tez boradigan joyi parkning o'sha tomonini o'rab turgan ochiq daraxtzor bo'ylab edi; u yerda o'zidan boshqa hech kim qadrlamaydiganga o'xshagan yoqimli, panada yo'lak bor edi va u yerda u o'zini ledi Ketrinning qiziquvchanligidan yiroqda his qilardi.

paras.en: In this quiet way, the first fortnight of her visit soon passed away. Easter was approaching, and the week preceding it was to bring an addition to the family at Rosings, which in so small a circle must be important. Elizabeth had heard soon after her arrival that Mr. Darcy was expected there in the course of a few weeks, and though there were not many of her acquaintances whom she did not prefer, his coming would furnish one comparatively new to look at in their Rosings parties, and she might be amused in seeing how hopeless Miss Bingley's designs on him were, by his behaviour to his cousin, for whom he was evidently destined by Lady Catherine, who talked of his coming with the greatest satisfaction, spoke of him in terms of the highest admiration, and seemed almost angry to find that he had already been frequently seen by Miss Lucas and herself.
paras.uz: Shu sokin tarzda tashrifining birinchi ikki haftasi tez o'tib ketdi. Pasxa yaqinlashardi va undan oldingi hafta Rozingsdagi oilaga qo'shimcha olib kelishi kerak edi, bu esa bunchalik kichik davrada muhim bo'lishi muqarrar edi. Elizabet kelganidan ko'p o'tmay janob Darsi bir necha hafta ichida u yerga kutilayotganini eshitgan edi; garchi u afzal ko'rmaydigan tanishlari ko'p bo'lmasa ham, uning kelishi Rozingsdagi yig'inlarda qarash uchun nisbatan yangi bir odamni taqdim etardi va uning ledi Ketrin uni aniq mo'ljallagan amakivachchasiga bo'lgan munosabatiga qarab, miss Binglining unga bo'lgan rejalari qanchalik umidsiz ekanini ko'rib ko'ngil ochishi mumkin edi; ledi Ketrin uning kelishi haqida eng katta mamnuniyat bilan gapirar, u haqida eng yuksak hayrat so'zlari bilan so'zlar va uni miss Lukas va Elizabet allaqachon tez-tez ko'rganini bilib, deyarli g'azablanganday ko'rinardi.

paras.en: His arrival was soon known at the Parsonage; for Mr. Collins was walking the whole morning within view of the lodges opening into Hunsford Lane, in order to have the earliest assurance of it, and after making his bow as the carriage turned into the Park, hurried home with the great intelligence. On the following morning he hastened to Rosings to pay his respects. There were two nephews of Lady Catherine to require them, for Mr. Darcy had brought with him a Colonel Fitzwilliam, the younger son of his uncle Lord ----, and, to the great surprise of all the party, when Mr. Collins returned, the gentlemen accompanied him. Charlotte had seen them from her husband's room, crossing the road, and immediately running into the other, told the girls what an honour they might expect, adding:
paras.uz: Uning kelgani tez orada ruhoniy uyida ma'lum bo'ldi; chunki janob Kollinz bundan eng birinchi bo'lib xabardor bo'lish uchun butun ertalab Xansford yo'liga ochiladigan qorovulxonalar ko'rinadigan joyda sayr qilib yurdi va kareta parkka burilganda ta'zim qilgach, katta xabar bilan uyga shoshildi. Ertasi kuni ertalab u hurmatini bildirish uchun Rozingsga shoshildi. Hurmat talab qiladigan ledi Ketrinning ikki jiyani bor edi, chunki janob Darsi o'zi bilan tog'asi lord ----ning kichik o'g'li polkovnik Fitsuilyamni olib kelgan edi; va janob Kollinz qaytganida butun davraning katta hayratiga janoblar unga hamroh bo'lishdi. Sharlotta ularni erining xonasidan yo'lni kesib o'tayotganlarida ko'rgan edi va darhol boshqa xonaga yugurib kirib, qizlarga qanday sharafni kutishlari mumkinligini aytdi va qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “I may thank you, Eliza, for this piece of civility. Mr. Darcy would never have come so soon to wait upon me.”
paras.uz: «Bu xushmuomalalik uchun senga rahmat aytsam bo'ladi, Eliza. Janob Darsi hech qachon meni ko'rgani bunchalik tez kelmasdi».

paras.en: Elizabeth had scarcely time to disclaim all right to the compliment, before their approach was announced by the door-bell, and shortly afterwards the three gentlemen entered the room. Colonel Fitzwilliam, who led the way, was about thirty, not handsome, but in person and address most truly the gentleman. Mr. Darcy looked just as he had been used to look in Hertfordshire--paid his compliments, with his usual reserve, to Mrs. Collins, and whatever might be his feelings toward her friend, met her with every appearance of composure. Elizabeth merely curtseyed to him without saying a word.
paras.uz: Elizabet bu iltifotga hech qanday haqqi yo'qligini aytishga zo'rg'a ulgurdi, eshik qo'ng'irog'i ularning kelishini e'lon qildi va ko'p o'tmay uch janob xonaga kirdi. Oldinda kelgan polkovnik Fitsuilyam o'ttiz yoshlarda, chiroyli emas, lekin qiyofasi va muomalasida chinakam janob edi. Janob Darsi Xertfordshirda odatda qanday ko'rinsa, xuddi shunday ko'rinardi — missis Kollinzga odatdagi vazminligi bilan salom berdi va dugonasiga nisbatan tuyg'ulari qanday bo'lmasin, u bilan to'liq xotirjamlik qiyofasida ko'rishdi. Elizabet unga bir og'iz ham gapirmay, faqat ta'zim qildi.

paras.en: Colonel Fitzwilliam entered into conversation directly with the readiness and ease of a well-bred man, and talked very pleasantly; but his cousin, after having addressed a slight observation on the house and garden to Mrs. Collins, sat for some time without speaking to anybody. At length, however, his civility was so far awakened as to inquire of Elizabeth after the health of her family. She answered him in the usual way, and after a moment's pause, added:
paras.uz: Polkovnik Fitsuilyam darhol yaxshi tarbiyali odamning tayyorligi va yengilligi bilan suhbatga kirishdi va juda yoqimli gapirdi; lekin uning amakivachchasi missis Kollinzga uy va bog' haqida qisqa gap aytgach, bir muddat hech kim bilan gaplashmay o'tirdi. Biroq nihoyat uning xushmuomalaligi Elizabetdan oilasining sog'lig'i haqida so'raydigan darajada uyg'ondi. U unga odatiy tarzda javob berdi va bir lahzalik sukutdan keyin qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “My eldest sister has been in town these three months. Have you never happened to see her there?”
paras.uz: «Opam uch oydan beri Londonda. U yerda tasodifan uni ko'rmadingizmi?»

paras.en: She was perfectly sensible that he never had; but she wished to see whether he would betray any consciousness of what had passed between the Bingleys and Jane, and she thought he looked a little confused as he answered that he had never been so fortunate as to meet Miss Bennet. The subject was pursued no farther, and the gentlemen soon afterwards went away.
paras.uz: U uni hech qachon ko'rmaganini juda yaxshi bilardi; lekin u Binglilar bilan Jeyn o'rtasida bo'lib o'tgan voqeadan xabardorligini biror tarzda oshkor qiladimi, yo'qmi, ko'rmoqchi edi va u miss Bennetni uchratish baxtiga hech qachon muyassar bo'lmaganini aytarkan, biroz xijolat tortganday ko'rindi, deb o'yladi. Mavzu boshqa davom ettirilmadi va janoblar ko'p o'tmay ketishdi.
