quiz.q: Who comes to Rosings with Darcy?
quiz.why_uz: Polkovnik Fitsuilyam — Darsining amakivachchasi.

quiz.q: Why, according to Charlotte, did Darcy come to the parsonage so quickly?
quiz.why_uz: Sharlotta allaqachon nimanidir sezadi.

chapters.title: At the Piano
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet Rozingsda pianino chaladi va Darsi bilan hazillashib bahslashadi. Ledi Ketrin hamma narsaga aralashib turadi.

paras.en: Colonel Fitzwilliam's manners were very much admired at the Parsonage, and the ladies all felt that he must add considerably to the pleasures of their engagements at Rosings. It was some days, however, before they received any invitation thither--for while there were visitors in the house, they could not be necessary; and it was not till Easter-day, almost a week after the gentlemen's arrival, that they were honoured by such an attention, and then they were merely asked on leaving church to come there in the evening. For the last week they had seen very little of Lady Catherine or her daughter. Colonel Fitzwilliam had called at the Parsonage more than once during the time, but Mr. Darcy they had seen only at church.
paras.uz: Polkovnik Fitsuilyamning muomalasi ruhoniy uyida juda yoqdi va xonimlarning hammasi u Rozingsdagi uchrashuvlarning zavqini ancha oshirishi kerakligini his qilishdi. Biroq u yerga taklif olishlariga bir necha kun o'tdi — chunki uyda mehmonlar bor ekan, ular kerak bo'lmasdi; va faqat Pasxa kuni, janoblar kelganidan deyarli bir hafta o'tib, ularni bunday e'tibor bilan sharaflashdi, shunda ham ularni cherkovdan chiqayotganlarida kechqurun kelishga taklif qilishdi, xolos. O'tgan hafta davomida ular ledi Ketrinni ham, uning qizini ham juda kam ko'rishgan edi. Bu vaqt ichida polkovnik Fitsuilyam ruhoniy uyiga bir necha marta kirgan edi, lekin janob Darsini faqat cherkovda ko'rishgan edi.

paras.en: The invitation was accepted of course, and at a proper hour they joined the party in Lady Catherine's drawing-room. Her ladyship received them civilly, but it was plain that their company was by no means so acceptable as when she could get nobody else; and she was, in fact, almost engrossed by her nephews, speaking to them, especially to Darcy, much more than to any other person in the room.
paras.uz: Taklif, albatta, qabul qilindi va munosib soatda ular ledi Ketrinning mehmonxonasidagi davraga qo'shilishdi. Janoblari ularni xushmuomalalik bilan qabul qildi, lekin ularning davrasi u boshqa hech kimni topa olmagan paytdagidek unchalik ma'qul emasligi aniq edi; aslida u deyarli butunlay jiyanlari bilan band edi, ular bilan, ayniqsa Darsi bilan xonadagi boshqa har qanday odamdan ko'ra ko'proq gaplashardi.

paras.en: Colonel Fitzwilliam seemed really glad to see them; anything was a welcome relief to him at Rosings; and Mrs. Collins's pretty friend had moreover caught his fancy very much. He now seated himself by her, and talked so agreeably of Kent and Hertfordshire, of travelling and staying at home, of new books and music, that Elizabeth had never been half so well entertained in that room before; and they conversed with so much spirit and flow, as to draw the attention of Lady Catherine herself, as well as of Mr. Darcy. His eyes had been soon and repeatedly turned towards them with a look of curiosity; and that her ladyship, after a while, shared the feeling, was more openly acknowledged, for she did not scruple to call out:
paras.uz: Polkovnik Fitsuilyam ularni ko'rganidan chindan ham xursand ko'rindi; Rozingsda har qanday narsa unga xush kelgan yengillik edi; bundan tashqari, missis Kollinzning chiroyli dugonasi unga juda yoqib qolgan edi. U endi uning yoniga o'tirdi va Kent va Xertfordshir haqida, sayohat qilish va uyda qolish haqida, yangi kitoblar va musiqa haqida shunchalik yoqimli gapirdiki, Elizabet bu xonada ilgari hech qachon buning yarmicha ham ko'ngil ochmagan edi; ular shunchalik jo'shqin va ravon suhbatlashishdiki, ledi Ketrinning o'zining ham, janob Darsining ham e'tiborini tortishdi. Uning ko'zlari tez orada va qayta-qayta qiziqish bilan ularga qaratildi; janoblari esa birozdan keyin bu tuyg'uni baham ko'rgani ochiqroq tan olindi, chunki u baqirib so'rashdan tortinmadi:

paras.en: “What is that you are saying, Fitzwilliam? What is it you are talking of? What are you telling Miss Bennet? Let me hear what it is.”
paras.uz: «Nima deyapsan, Fitsuilyam? Nima haqida gaplashyapsan? Miss Bennetga nima aytyapsan? Menga ham eshitishga ruxsat ber».

paras.en: “We are speaking of music, madam,” said he, when no longer able to avoid a reply.
paras.uz: «Musiqa haqida gaplashyapmiz, xonim», — dedi u, javobdan qochishning iloji qolmagach.

paras.en: “Of music! Then pray speak aloud. It is of all subjects my delight. I must have my share in the conversation if you are speaking of music. There are few people in England, I suppose, who have more true enjoyment of music than myself, or a better natural taste. If I had ever learnt, I should have been a great proficient. And so would Anne, if her health had allowed her to apply. I am confident that she would have performed delightfully. How does Georgiana get on, Darcy?”
paras.uz: «Musiqa haqida! Unda, iltimos, baland ovozda gapir. Bu men uchun barcha mavzular ichida eng yoqimlisi. Agar musiqa haqida gapirayotgan bo'lsangiz, suhbatda mening ham ulushim bo'lishi kerak. Menimcha, Angliyada musiqadan mendan ko'ra ko'proq chinakam zavq oladigan yoki tabiatan yaxshiroq didga ega odamlar kam. Agar qachondir o'rganganimda, katta mohir bo'lardim. Enn ham, agar sog'lig'i shug'ullanishga imkon berganida, shunday bo'lardi. Ishonchim komilki, u ajoyib ijro etardi. Jorjiananing ishlari qanday, Darsi?»

paras.en: Mr. Darcy spoke with affectionate praise of his sister's proficiency.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi singlisining mahorati haqida mehr bilan maqtab gapirdi.

paras.en: “I am very glad to hear such a good account of her,” said Lady Catherine; “and pray tell her from me, that she cannot expect to excel if she does not practice a good deal.”
paras.uz: «U haqida bunday yaxshi xabar eshitganimdan juda xursandman, — dedi ledi Ketrin, — iltimos, unga mendan ayt, agar ko'p mashq qilmasa, ustun bo'lishni kuta olmaydi».

paras.en: “I assure you, madam,” he replied, “that she does not need such advice. She practises very constantly.”
paras.uz: «Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, xonim, — javob berdi u, — unga bunday maslahat kerak emas. U juda muntazam mashq qiladi».

paras.en: “So much the better. It cannot be done too much; and when I next write to her, I shall charge her not to neglect it on any account. I often tell young ladies that no excellence in music is to be acquired without constant practice. I have told Miss Bennet several times, that she will never play really well unless she practises more; and though Mrs. Collins has no instrument, she is very welcome, as I have often told her, to come to Rosings every day, and play on the pianoforte in Mrs. Jenkinson's room. She would be in nobody's way, you know, in that part of the house.”
paras.uz: «Shunisi yaxshi. Buni haddan tashqari ko'p qilib bo'lmaydi; keyingi safar unga xat yozganimda, hech qanday holatda buni e'tiborsiz qoldirmaslikni buyuraman. Men yosh xonimlarga tez-tez aytaman, musiqada hech qanday mukammallikka doimiy mashqsiz erishib bo'lmaydi. Miss Bennetga bir necha marta aytganmanki, ko'proq mashq qilmasa, hech qachon chindan yaxshi chala olmaydi; garchi missis Kollinzda cholg'u bo'lmasa ham, unga tez-tez aytganimdek, u har kuni Rozingsga kelib, missis Jenkinsonning xonasidagi fortepianoda chalishi mumkin. Bilasizmi, uyning o'sha qismida u hech kimga xalaqit bermaydi».

paras.en: Mr. Darcy looked a little ashamed of his aunt's ill-breeding, and made no answer.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi xolasining tarbiyasizligidan biroz uyalganday ko'rindi va javob bermadi.

paras.en: When coffee was over, Colonel Fitzwilliam reminded Elizabeth of having promised to play to him; and she sat down directly to the instrument. He drew a chair near her. Lady Catherine listened to half a song, and then talked, as before, to her other nephew; till the latter walked away from her, and making with his usual deliberation towards the pianoforte stationed himself so as to command a full view of the fair performer's countenance. Elizabeth saw what he was doing, and at the first convenient pause, turned to him with an arch smile, and said:
paras.uz: Qahva tugagach, polkovnik Fitsuilyam Elizabetga unga chalib berishga va'da berganini eslatdi va u darhol cholg'u oldiga o'tirdi. U uning yoniga stul qo'ydi. Ledi Ketrin qo'shiqning yarmini tingladi, keyin avvalgidek boshqa jiyani bilan gaplashdi; toki u undan uzoqlashib, odatdagi shoshmasligi bilan fortepiano tomon yurib, go'zal ijrochining chehrasini to'liq ko'ra oladigan joyga turdi. Elizabet uning nima qilayotganini ko'rdi va birinchi qulay to'xtamda unga ayyorona tabassum bilan o'girilib, dedi:

paras.en: “You mean to frighten me, Mr. Darcy, by coming in all this state to hear me? I will not be alarmed though your sister does play so well. There is a stubbornness about me that never can bear to be frightened at the will of others. My courage always rises at every attempt to intimidate me.”
paras.uz: «Meni eshitish uchun bunchalik salobat bilan kelib, meni qo'rqitmoqchimisiz, janob Darsi? Singlingiz juda yaxshi chalsa ham, men cho'chimayman. Menda shunday o'jarlik borki, boshqalarning xohishi bilan qo'rqitilishga hech qachon chiday olmaydi. Meni cho'chitishga bo'lgan har bir urinishda jasoratim doim ortadi».

paras.en: “I shall not say you are mistaken,” he replied, “because you could not really believe me to entertain any design of alarming you; and I have had the pleasure of your acquaintance long enough to know that you find great enjoyment in occasionally professing opinions which in fact are not your own.”
paras.uz: «Adashyapsiz demayman, — javob berdi u, — chunki siz meni sizni qo'rqitish niyatim bor deb chindan ishona olmaysiz; men siz bilan tanishlik zavqiga yetarlicha uzoq vaqtdan beri ega bo'lib, vaqti-vaqti bilan aslida o'zingizniki bo'lmagan fikrlarni izhor qilishdan katta zavq olishingizni bilaman».

paras.en: Elizabeth laughed heartily at this picture of herself, and said to Colonel Fitzwilliam, “Your cousin will give you a very pretty notion of me, and teach you not to believe a word I say. I am particularly unlucky in meeting with a person so able to expose my real character, in a part of the world where I had hoped to pass myself off with some degree of credit. Indeed, Mr. Darcy, it is very ungenerous in you to mention all that you knew to my disadvantage in Hertfordshire--and, give me leave to say, very impolitic too--for it is provoking me to retaliate, and such things may come out as will shock your relations to hear.”
paras.uz: Elizabet o'zining bu tasviridan chin dildan kuldi va polkovnik Fitsuilyamga dedi: «Amakivachchangiz sizga men haqimda juda chiroyli tasavvur beradi va aytgan birorta so'zimga ishonmaslikni o'rgatadi. O'zimni biroz obro' bilan ko'rsatishga umid qilgan dunyoning bir qismida haqiqiy xarakterimni fosh qila oladigan odamni uchratganim ayniqsa omadsizlik. Rostdan ham, janob Darsi, Xertfordshirda men haqimda bilgan barcha salbiy narsalarni tilga olishingiz juda olijanoblikdan emas — va aytishga ruxsat bering, juda nooqilona ham — chunki bu meni qasos olishga undaydi va qarindoshlaringizni eshitib hayratga soladigan narsalar oshkor bo'lishi mumkin».

paras.en: “I am not afraid of you,” said he, smilingly.
paras.uz: «Sizdan qo'rqmayman», — dedi u jilmayib.

paras.en: “Pray let me hear what you have to accuse him of,” cried Colonel Fitzwilliam. “I should like to know how he behaves among strangers.”
paras.uz: «Iltimos, uni nimada ayblashingizni eshitay, — xitob qildi polkovnik Fitsuilyam. — Uning begonalar orasida o'zini qanday tutishini bilishni istardim».

paras.en: “You shall hear then--but prepare yourself for something very dreadful. The first time of my ever seeing him in Hertfordshire, you must know, was at a ball--and at this ball, what do you think he did? He danced only four dances, though gentlemen were scarce; and, to my certain knowledge, more than one young lady was sitting down in want of a partner. Mr. Darcy, you cannot deny the fact.”
paras.uz: «Unda eshitasiz — lekin juda dahshatli narsaga tayyorlaning. Bilishingiz kerakki, uni Xertfordshirda birinchi marta balda ko'rganman — va bu balda u nima qildi deb o'ylaysiz? Janoblar kam bo'lishiga qaramay, u atigi to'rtta raqsga tushdi; aniq bilishimcha, bir nechta yosh xonim sherik yo'qligidan o'tirib qolgan edi. Janob Darsi, bu faktni inkor eta olmaysiz».

paras.en: “I had not at that time the honour of knowing any lady in the assembly beyond my own party.”
paras.uz: «O'sha paytda yig'indagi o'z davramdan tashqari hech bir xonim bilan tanish bo'lish sharafiga ega emasdim».

paras.en: “True; and nobody can ever be introduced in a ball-room. Well, Colonel Fitzwilliam, what do I play next? My fingers wait your orders.”
paras.uz: «To'g'ri; bal zalida esa hech kimni hech qachon tanishtirib bo'lmaydi. Xo'sh, polkovnik Fitsuilyam, keyin nima chalay? Barmoqlarim buyrug'ingizni kutmoqda».

paras.en: “Perhaps,” said Darcy, “I should have judged better, had I sought an introduction; but I am ill-qualified to recommend myself to strangers.”
paras.uz: «Ehtimol, — dedi Darsi, — agar tanishtirishni so'raganimda, to'g'riroq ish qilgan bo'lardim; lekin begonalarga o'zimni yoqtirishga qobiliyatim yo'q».

paras.en: “Shall we ask your cousin the reason of this?” said Elizabeth, still addressing Colonel Fitzwilliam. “Shall we ask him why a man of sense and education, and who has lived in the world, is ill qualified to recommend himself to strangers?”
paras.uz: «Amakivachchangizdan buning sababini so'raymizmi? — dedi Elizabet, hali ham polkovnik Fitsuilyamga murojaat qilib. — Undan aqlli va o'qimishli, dunyo ko'rgan odam nega begonalarga o'zini yoqtirishga qobiliyatsiz ekanini so'raymizmi?»

paras.en: “I can answer your question,” said Fitzwilliam, “without applying to him. It is because he will not give himself the trouble.”
paras.uz: «Savolingizga undan so'ramasdan javob bera olaman, — dedi Fitsuilyam. — Chunki u o'ziga zahmat berishni istamaydi».

paras.en: “I certainly have not the talent which some people possess,” said Darcy, “of conversing easily with those I have never seen before. I cannot catch their tone of conversation, or appear interested in their concerns, as I often see done.”
paras.uz: «Menda, albatta, ba'zi odamlarda bo'lgan, ilgari hech qachon ko'rmagan odamlar bilan oson suhbatlashish iste'dodi yo'q, — dedi Darsi. — Men ularning suhbat ohangini ilg'ay olmayman yoki ko'pincha ko'rganimdek, ularning ishlariga qiziqayotgandek ko'rina olmayman».

paras.en: “My fingers,” said Elizabeth, “do not move over this instrument in the masterly manner which I see so many women's do. They have not the same force or rapidity, and do not produce the same expression. But then I have always supposed it to be my own fault--because I will not take the trouble of practising. It is not that I do not believe my fingers as capable as any other woman's of superior execution.”
paras.uz: «Mening barmoqlarim, — dedi Elizabet, — bu cholg'u ustida men ko'p ayollarnikida ko'rgan mohirona tarzda harakatlanmaydi. Ularda xuddi shunday kuch yoki tezlik yo'q va xuddi shunday ifoda yaratmaydi. Lekin men doim buni o'z aybim deb hisoblaganman — chunki mashq qilish zahmatini chekishni istamayman. Barmoqlarim boshqa har qanday ayolniki kabi yuqori ijroga qodir ekaniga ishonmasligim uchun emas».

paras.en: Darcy smiled and said, “You are perfectly right. You have employed your time much better. No one admitted to the privilege of hearing you can think anything wanting. We neither of us perform to strangers.”
paras.uz: Darsi jilmaydi va dedi: «Siz mutlaqo haqsiz. Vaqtingizni ancha yaxshiroq sarfladingiz. Sizni eshitish imtiyoziga ega bo'lgan hech kim biror narsa yetishmaydi deb o'ylay olmaydi. Ikkalamiz ham begonalar oldida ijro etmaymiz».

paras.en: Here they were interrupted by Lady Catherine, who called out to know what they were talking of. Elizabeth immediately began playing again. Lady Catherine approached, and, after listening for a few minutes, said to Darcy:
paras.uz: Shu yerda ularning gapini ledi Ketrin bo'ldi, u nima haqida gaplashayotganlarini bilish uchun baqirdi. Elizabet darhol yana chala boshladi. Ledi Ketrin yaqinlashdi va bir necha daqiqa tinglagach, Darsiga dedi:

paras.en: “Miss Bennet would not play at all amiss if she practised more, and could have the advantage of a London master. She has a very good notion of fingering, though her taste is not equal to Anne's. Anne would have been a delightful performer, had her health allowed her to learn.”
paras.uz: «Agar miss Bennet ko'proq mashq qilsa va London ustozidan foydalana olsa, umuman yomon chalmagan bo'lardi. Uning barmoq qo'yish haqida juda yaxshi tushunchasi bor, garchi didi Ennikiga teng bo'lmasa ham. Agar sog'lig'i o'rganishga imkon berganida, Enn ajoyib ijrochi bo'lardi».

paras.en: Elizabeth looked at Darcy to see how cordially he assented to his cousin's praise; but neither at that moment nor at any other could she discern any symptom of love; and from the whole of his behaviour to Miss de Bourgh she derived this comfort for Miss Bingley, that he might have been just as likely to marry her, had she been his relation.
paras.uz: Elizabet amakivachchasining maqtoviga qanchalik samimiy qo'shilishini ko'rish uchun Darsiga qaradi; lekin na o'sha lahzada, na boshqa paytda u hech qanday muhabbat alomatini sezmadi; va uning miss de Burgga nisbatan butun xatti-harakatidan u miss Bingli uchun shunday taskin chiqardi: agar u uning qarindoshi bo'lganida, u unga ham xuddi shunday ehtimol bilan uylanishi mumkin edi.

paras.en: Lady Catherine continued her remarks on Elizabeth's performance, mixing with them many instructions on execution and taste. Elizabeth received them with all the forbearance of civility, and, at the request of the gentlemen, remained at the instrument till her ladyship's carriage was ready to take them all home.
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrin Elizabetning ijrosi haqidagi mulohazalarini davom ettirdi va ularga ijro va did bo'yicha ko'plab ko'rsatmalar qo'shdi. Elizabet ularni xushmuomalalikning butun sabri bilan qabul qildi va janoblarning iltimosiga ko'ra, janoblarining karetasi ularning hammasini uyga olib ketishga tayyor bo'lgunicha cholg'u oldida qoldi.

gloss.ex: Collins has no instrument, she is very welcome, as I have often told her, to come to Rosings every day, and play on the pianoforte in Mrs.
said Lady Catherine; “and pray tell her from me, that she cannot expect to excel if she does not practice a good deal.”
“I should like to know how he behaves among strangers.”
He now seated himself by her, and talked so agreeably of Kent and Hertfordshire, of travelling and staying at home, of new books and music, that Elizabeth had never been…
“I certainly have not the talent which some people possess,”
he replied, “because you could not really believe me to entertain any design of alarming you; and I have had the pleasure of your acquaintance long enough to know that…
His eyes had been soon and repeatedly turned towards them with a look of curiosity; and that her ladyship, after a while, shared the feeling, was more openly acknowledged, for…

quiz.q: What does Darcy say about himself?
o: He finds it hard to talk to strangers
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet: «Bu mashq qilmaslik natijasi», deb javob beradi.

quiz.q: Who keeps interrupting with comments on music?
quiz.why_uz: Ledi Ketrin o'zi o'rganmagan, lekin hamma narsani biladiganday gapiradi.

chapters.title: An Unexpected Visit
chapters.recap_uz: Darsi Elizabetning oldiga yolg'iz keladi, ular noqulay suhbatlashadi. Keyin u tez-tez kelib, ko'p gapirmay o'tiradi. Sharlotta u Elizabetni sevib qolgan bo'lsa kerak, deb o'ylaydi.

paras.en: Elizabeth was sitting by herself the next morning, and writing to Jane while Mrs. Collins and Maria were gone on business into the village, when she was startled by a ring at the door, the certain signal of a visitor. As she had heard no carriage, she thought it not unlikely to be Lady Catherine, and under that apprehension was putting away her half-finished letter that she might escape all impertinent questions, when the door opened, and, to her very great surprise, Mr. Darcy, and Mr. Darcy only, entered the room.
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab missis Kollinz va Mariya ish bilan qishloqqa ketganda, Elizabet yolg'iz o'tirib, Jeynga xat yozayotgan edi, shu payt eshik qo'ng'irog'i — mehmon kelganining aniq belgisi — uni cho'chitib yubordi. U hech qanday arava ovozini eshitmagani uchun bu ledi Ketrin bo'lishi ehtimoldan yiroq emas deb o'yladi va shu xavotir bilan barcha surbet savollardan qochish uchun yarim yozilgan xatini yashirayotgan edi, eshik ochildi va uning juda katta hayratiga janob Darsi, faqat janob Darsi xonaga kirdi.

paras.en: He seemed astonished too on finding her alone, and apologised for his intrusion by letting her know that he had understood all the ladies were to be within.
paras.uz: U ham uni yolg'iz topganidan hayratlanganday ko'rindi va barcha xonimlar uyda bo'ladi deb tushunganini aytib, bezovta qilgani uchun uzr so'radi.

paras.en: They then sat down, and when her inquiries after Rosings were made, seemed in danger of sinking into total silence. It was absolutely necessary, therefore, to think of something, and in this emergence recollecting when she had seen him last in Hertfordshire, and feeling curious to know what he would say on the subject of their hasty departure, she observed:
paras.uz: Keyin ular o'tirishdi va u Rozings haqida so'ragach, butunlay sukutga cho'mish xavfi tug'ilganday bo'ldi. Shuning uchun biror narsa o'ylash mutlaqo zarur edi va bu favqulodda holatda uni oxirgi marta Xertfordshirda qachon ko'rganini eslab, ularning shoshilinch ketishi haqida u nima deyishini bilishga qiziqib, dedi:

paras.en: “How very suddenly you all quitted Netherfield last November, Mr. Darcy! It must have been a most agreeable surprise to Mr. Bingley to see you all after him so soon; for, if I recollect right, he went but the day before. He and his sisters were well, I hope, when you left London?”
paras.uz: «O'tgan noyabrda Nezerfildni qanchalik to'satdan tark etdingiz, janob Darsi! Hammangizni o'z ortidan bunchalik tez ko'rish janob Bingli uchun juda yoqimli syurpriz bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak; chunki agar to'g'ri eslasam, u bir kun oldin ketgan edi. Umid qilamanki, Londondan ketganingizda u va opa-singillari sog'-salomat edi?»

paras.en: “Perfectly so, I thank you.”
paras.uz: «Mutlaqo, rahmat».

paras.en: She found that she was to receive no other answer, and, after a short pause added:
paras.uz: U boshqa javob olmasligini tushundi va qisqa sukutdan keyin qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “I think I have understood that Mr. Bingley has not much idea of ever returning to Netherfield again?”
paras.uz: «Tushunishimcha, janob Bingli Nezerfildga qachondir yana qaytish haqida unchalik o'ylamayapti shekilli?»

paras.en: “I have never heard him say so; but it is probable that he may spend very little of his time there in the future. He has many friends, and is at a time of life when friends and engagements are continually increasing.”
paras.uz: «Undan bunday deganini hech qachon eshitmaganman; lekin ehtimol, kelajakda u yerda juda kam vaqt o'tkazar. Uning do'stlari ko'p va u do'stlar hamda majburiyatlar doimiy ravishda ko'payib boradigan yoshda».

paras.en: “If he means to be but little at Netherfield, it would be better for the neighbourhood that he should give up the place entirely, for then we might possibly get a settled family there. But, perhaps, Mr. Bingley did not take the house so much for the convenience of the neighbourhood as for his own, and we must expect him to keep it or quit it on the same principle.”
paras.uz: «Agar u Nezerfildda kam bo'lmoqchi bo'lsa, mahalla uchun u joydan butunlay voz kechgani yaxshiroq bo'lardi, chunki shunda u yerga doimiy yashaydigan oila kelishi mumkin edi. Lekin, ehtimol, janob Bingli uyni mahallaning qulayligi uchun emas, balki o'z qulayligi uchun olgandir, shuning uchun uni xuddi shu tamoyil asosida saqlashini yoki tark etishini kutishimiz kerak».

paras.en: “I should not be surprised,” said Darcy, “if he were to give it up as soon as any eligible purchase offers.”
paras.uz: «Agar u biror munosib xaridor chiqishi bilanoq undan voz kechsa, hayron bo'lmagan bo'lardim», — dedi Darsi.

paras.en: Elizabeth made no answer. She was afraid of talking longer of his friend; and, having nothing else to say, was now determined to leave the trouble of finding a subject to him.
paras.uz: Elizabet javob bermadi. U uning do'sti haqida uzoqroq gapirishdan qo'rqdi; aytadigan boshqa gapi bo'lmagani uchun endi mavzu topish zahmatini unga qoldirishga qaror qildi.

paras.en: He took the hint, and soon began with, “This seems a very comfortable house. Lady Catherine, I believe, did a great deal to it when Mr. Collins first came to Hunsford.”
paras.uz: U ishorani tushundi va tez orada gap boshladi: «Bu juda qulay uyga o'xshaydi. Menimcha, janob Kollinz Xansfordga birinchi kelganida ledi Ketrin unga ko'p narsa qilgan».

paras.en: “I believe she did--and I am sure she could not have bestowed her kindness on a more grateful object.”
paras.uz: «Shunday deb o'ylayman — va ishonchim komilki, u o'z mehribonligini bundan minnatdorroq odamga ko'rsata olmasdi».

paras.en: “Mr. Collins appears to be very fortunate in his choice of a wife.”
paras.uz: «Janob Kollinz xotin tanlashda juda omadli bo'lganga o'xshaydi».

paras.en: “Yes, indeed, his friends may well rejoice in his having met with one of the very few sensible women who would have accepted him, or have made him happy if they had. My friend has an excellent understanding--though I am not certain that I consider her marrying Mr. Collins as the wisest thing she ever did. She seems perfectly happy, however, and in a prudential light it is certainly a very good match for her.”
paras.uz: «Ha, haqiqatan ham, uning do'stlari uning uni qabul qiladigan yoki qabul qilgan taqdirda baxtli qiladigan juda kam sonli aqlli ayollardan birini uchratganidan xursand bo'lishlari mumkin. Dugonamning aqli ajoyib — garchi uning janob Kollinzga turmushga chiqishini qilgan ishlarining eng oqilonasi deb hisoblashimga amin bo'lmasam ham. Biroq u mutlaqo baxtli ko'rinadi va ehtiyotkorlik nuqtai nazaridan bu, albatta, u uchun juda yaxshi nikoh».

paras.en: “It must be very agreeable for her to be settled within so easy a distance of her own family and friends.”
paras.uz: «Uning o'z oilasi va do'stlaridan bunchalik yaqin masofada joylashgani u uchun juda yoqimli bo'lsa kerak».

paras.en: “An easy distance, do you call it? It is nearly fifty miles.”
paras.uz: «Yaqin masofa deysizmi? Deyarli ellik mil-ku».

paras.en: “And what is fifty miles of good road? Little more than half a day's journey. Yes, I call it a very easy distance.”
paras.uz: «Yaxshi yo'lda ellik mil nima ekan? Yarim kunlik yo'ldan biroz ko'proq. Ha, men buni juda yaqin masofa deyman».

paras.en: “I should never have considered the distance as one of the advantages of the match,” cried Elizabeth. “I should never have said Mrs. Collins was settled near her family.”
paras.uz: «Men masofani hech qachon nikohning afzalliklaridan biri deb hisoblamagan bo'lardim, — xitob qildi Elizabet. — Missis Kollinz oilasining yaqinida joylashgan, deb hech qachon aytmagan bo'lardim».

paras.en: “It is a proof of your own attachment to Hertfordshire. Anything beyond the very neighbourhood of Longbourn, I suppose, would appear far.”
paras.uz: «Bu sizning Xertfordshirga bog'liqligingizning isboti. O'ylaymanki, Longbornning shundoq yonidan narida bo'lgan har qanday joy sizga uzoq tuyuladi».

paras.en: As he spoke there was a sort of smile which Elizabeth fancied she understood; he must be supposing her to be thinking of Jane and Netherfield, and she blushed as she answered:
paras.uz: U gapirayotganda yuzida bir xil tabassum bor edi, Elizabet uni tushungandek bo'ldi; u uni Jeyn va Nezerfild haqida o'ylayapti deb taxmin qilayotgan bo'lsa kerak, deb o'yladi va javob berarkan qizarib ketdi:

paras.en: “I do not mean to say that a woman may not be settled too near her family. The far and the near must be relative, and depend on many varying circumstances. Where there is fortune to make the expenses of travelling unimportant, distance becomes no evil. But that is not the case here. Mr. and Mrs. Collins have a comfortable income, but not such a one as will allow of frequent journeys--and I am persuaded my friend would not call herself near her family under less than half the present distance.”
paras.uz: «Ayol oilasiga haddan tashqari yaqin joylasha olmaydi demoqchi emasman. Uzoq va yaqin nisbiy bo'lishi va ko'plab o'zgaruvchan holatlarga bog'liq bo'lishi kerak. Sayohat xarajatlarini ahamiyatsiz qiladigan boylik bor joyda masofa yomonlik bo'lmaydi. Lekin bu yerda bunday emas. Janob va missis Kollinzning daromadi qulay, lekin tez-tez safarga imkon beradigan darajada emas — va ishonchim komilki, dugonam hozirgi masofaning yarmidan kamida ham o'zini oilasiga yaqin deb atamagan bo'lardi».

paras.en: Mr. Darcy drew his chair a little towards her, and said, “You cannot have a right to such very strong local attachment. You cannot have been always at Longbourn.”
paras.uz: Janob Darsi kursisini biroz unga yaqinroq surdi va dedi: «Sizda bunchalik kuchli joyga bog'liqlikka haqqingiz bo'lishi mumkin emas. Siz doim Longbornda bo'lmagan bo'lsangiz kerak».

paras.en: Elizabeth looked surprised. The gentleman experienced some change of feeling; he drew back his chair, took a newspaper from the table, and glancing over it, said, in a colder voice:
paras.uz: Elizabet hayron ko'rindi. Janobning tuyg'ularida qandaydir o'zgarish yuz berdi; u kursisini orqaga tortdi, stoldan gazeta oldi va unga ko'z yugurtirib, sovuqroq ovozda dedi:

paras.en: “Are you pleased with Kent?”
paras.uz: «Kent sizga yoqdimi?»

paras.en: A short dialogue on the subject of the country ensued, on either side calm and concise--and soon put an end to by the entrance of Charlotte and her sister, just returned from her walk. The tete-a-tete surprised them. Mr. Darcy related the mistake which had occasioned his intruding on Miss Bennet, and after sitting a few minutes longer without saying much to anybody, went away.
paras.uz: Bu yerlar mavzusida har ikki tomondan sokin va qisqa suhbat bo'lib o'tdi — va tez orada sayrdan endigina qaytgan Sharlotta va singlisining kirib kelishi bilan tugadi. Yuzma-yuz suhbat ularni hayratga soldi. Janob Darsi miss Bennetni bezovta qilishiga sabab bo'lgan xatoni aytib berdi va hech kim bilan ko'p gaplashmay yana bir necha daqiqa o'tirgach, ketdi.

paras.en: “What can be the meaning of this?” said Charlotte, as soon as he was gone. “My dear, Eliza, he must be in love with you, or he would never have called us in this familiar way.”
paras.uz: «Bu nimani anglatishi mumkin? — dedi Sharlotta, u ketishi bilanoq. — Azizim Eliza, u senga oshiq bo'lsa kerak, aks holda bizga hech qachon bunday bemalol kelmasdi».

paras.en: But when Elizabeth told of his silence, it did not seem very likely, even to Charlotte's wishes, to be the case; and after various conjectures, they could at last only suppose his visit to proceed from the difficulty of finding anything to do, which was the more probable from the time of year. All field sports were over. Within doors there was Lady Catherine, books, and a billiard-table, but gentlemen cannot always be within doors; and in the nearness of the Parsonage, or the pleasantness of the walk to it, or of the people who lived in it, the two cousins found a temptation from this period of walking thither almost every day. They called at various times of the morning, sometimes separately, sometimes together, and now and then accompanied by their aunt.
paras.uz: Lekin Elizabet uning sukuti haqida aytib berganda, bu hatto Sharlottaning istaklari uchun ham unchalik ehtimolli ko'rinmadi; turli taxminlardan keyin ular nihoyat uning tashrifi qiladigan ish topish qiyinligidan kelib chiqqan bo'lsa kerak, deb taxmin qila olishdi, bu esa yilning shu faslini hisobga olsak, yanada ehtimolli edi. Barcha dala ovlari tugagan edi. Uy ichida ledi Ketrin, kitoblar va bilyard stoli bor edi, lekin janoblar doim uy ichida bo'la olmaydi; shu vaqtdan boshlab ikki amakivachcha ruhoniy uyining yaqinligida, unga boradigan yo'lning yoqimliligida yoki unda yashaydigan odamlarda u yerga deyarli har kuni piyoda borish uchun vasvasa topishdi. Ular ertalabning turli vaqtlarida, ba'zan alohida, ba'zan birga, vaqti-vaqti bilan esa xolalari hamrohligida kelishardi.

paras.en: It was plain to them all that Colonel Fitzwilliam came because he had pleasure in their society, a persuasion which of course recommended him still more; and Elizabeth was reminded by her own satisfaction in being with him, as well as by his evident admiration of her, of her former favourite George Wickham; and though, in comparing them, she saw there was less captivating softness in Colonel Fitzwilliam's manners, she believed he might have the best informed mind.
paras.uz: Polkovnik Fitsuilyam ularning davrasidan zavq olgani uchun kelishi hammaga aniq edi, bu ishonch esa, albatta, uni yanada yoqimliroq qilardi; Elizabetga u bilan bo'lishdan o'zining mamnunligi, shuningdek uning unga aniq hayratlanishi avvalgi sevimlisi Jorj Uikhemni eslatardi; garchi ularni taqqoslaganda, polkovnik Fitsuilyamning muomalasida kamroq maftunkor muloyimlik borligini ko'rsa ham, u eng bilimli aqlga ega bo'lishi mumkin, deb ishonardi.

paras.en: But why Mr. Darcy came so often to the Parsonage, it was more difficult to understand. It could not be for society, as he frequently sat there ten minutes together without opening his lips; and when he did speak, it seemed the effect of necessity rather than of choice--a sacrifice to propriety, not a pleasure to himself. He seldom appeared really animated. Mrs. Collins knew not what to make of him. Colonel Fitzwilliam's occasionally laughing at his stupidity, proved that he was generally different, which her own knowledge of him could not have told her; and as she would liked to have believed this change the effect of love, and the object of that love her friend Eliza, she set herself seriously to work to find it out. She watched him whenever they were at Rosings, and whenever he came to Hunsford; but without much success. He certainly looked at her friend a great deal, but the expression of that look was disputable. It was an earnest, steadfast gaze, but she often doubted whether there were much admiration in it, and sometimes it seemed nothing but absence of mind.
paras.uz: Lekin janob Darsi nega ruhoniy uyiga bunchalik tez-tez kelishini tushunish qiyinroq edi. Bu davra uchun bo'lishi mumkin emasdi, chunki u u yerda ko'pincha o'n daqiqa lab ochmasdan o'tirardi; gapirganda esa bu tanlovdan ko'ra zaruratning natijasiga o'xshardi — o'ziga zavq emas, odob uchun qurbonlik. U kamdan-kam chinakam jonli ko'rinardi. Missis Kollinz u haqida nima deb o'ylashni bilmasdi. Polkovnik Fitsuilyamning vaqti-vaqti bilan uning ahmoqligiga kulishi u odatda boshqacha ekanini isbotlardi, buni uning o'z bilimi ayta olmasdi; va u bu o'zgarishni muhabbatning natijasi, bu muhabbatning obyekti esa dugonasi Eliza deb ishonishni istagani uchun, buni aniqlashga jiddiy kirishdi. U Rozingsda bo'lganlarida ham, u Xansfordga kelganida ham uni kuzatdi; lekin katta muvaffaqiyatga erishmadi. U, albatta, dugonasiga ko'p qarardi, lekin bu qarashning ifodasi bahsli edi. Bu jiddiy, sobit nigoh edi, lekin u ko'pincha unda ko'p hayrat bormi, deb shubhalanardi, ba'zan esa bu shunchaki parishonxotirlikdan boshqa narsa emasdek tuyulardi.

paras.en: She had once or twice suggested to Elizabeth the possibility of his being partial to her, but Elizabeth always laughed at the idea; and Mrs. Collins did not think it right to press the subject, from the danger of raising expectations which might only end in disappointment; for in her opinion it admitted not of a doubt, that all her friend's dislike would vanish, if she could suppose him to be in her power.
paras.uz: U bir-ikki marta Elizabetga uning unga moyil bo'lishi mumkinligini aytgan edi, lekin Elizabet bu fikrga doim kulardi; missis Kollinz esa faqat hafsala pirligi bilan tugashi mumkin bo'lgan umidlar uyg'otish xavfi tufayli bu mavzuni qistashni to'g'ri deb hisoblamadi; chunki uning fikricha, agar dugonasi uni o'z qo'lida deb taxmin qila olsa, uning barcha yoqtirmasligi yo'qolib ketishiga hech qanday shubha yo'q edi.

paras.en: In her kind schemes for Elizabeth, she sometimes planned her marrying Colonel Fitzwilliam. He was beyond comparison the most pleasant man; he certainly admired her, and his situation in life was most eligible; but, to counterbalance these advantages, Mr. Darcy had considerable patronage in the church, and his cousin could have none at all.
paras.uz: Elizabet uchun mehribon rejalarida u ba'zan uning polkovnik Fitsuilyamga turmushga chiqishini rejalashtirardi. U taqqoslab bo'lmaydigan darajada eng yoqimli erkak edi; u, albatta, undan maftun edi va hayotdagi mavqei juda munosib edi; lekin bu afzalliklarni muvozanatlash uchun janob Darsining cherkovda katta homiylik imkoniyatlari bor edi, uning amakivachchasida esa umuman yo'q edi.

gloss.ex: They then sat down, and when her inquiries after Rosings were made, seemed in danger of sinking into total silence.
It was plain to them all that Colonel Fitzwilliam came because he had pleasure in their society, a persuasion which of course recommended him still more; and Elizabeth was reminded…
“It must be very agreeable for her to be settled within so easy a distance of her own family and friends.”
Collins did not think it right to press the subject, from the danger of raising expectations which might only end in disappointment; for in her opinion it admitted not of…
“If he means to be but little at Netherfield, it would be better for the neighbourhood that he should give up the place entirely, for then we might possibly get…
The far and the near must be relative, and depend on many varying circumstances.
As she had heard no carriage, she thought it not unlikely to be Lady Catherine, and under that apprehension was putting away her half-finished letter that she might escape all…

chapters.title: A Walk with the Colonel
chapters.recap_uz: Polkovnik Fitsuilyam Elizabetga Darsi yaqinda do'stini «noqulay nikoh»dan qutqarganini aytadi. Elizabet bu Bingley va Jeyn ekanini tushunib, Darsiga nisbatan g'azabga to'ladi.

paras.en: More than once did Elizabeth, in her ramble within the park, unexpectedly meet Mr. Darcy. She felt all the perverseness of the mischance that should bring him where no one else was brought, and, to prevent its ever happening again, took care to inform him at first that it was a favourite haunt of hers. How it could occur a second time, therefore, was very odd! Yet it did, and even a third. It seemed like wilful ill-nature, or a voluntary penance, for on these occasions it was not merely a few formal inquiries and an awkward pause and then away, but he actually thought it necessary to turn back and walk with her.
paras.uz: Elizabet park ichida sayr qilarkan, bir necha marta kutilmaganda janob Darsini uchratdi. U boshqa hech kim kelmaydigan joyga uni olib keladigan bu omadsizlikning butun teskariligini his qildi va bu boshqa hech qachon takrorlanmasligi uchun dastlab unga bu o'zining sevimli sayr joyi ekanini aytib qo'yishga harakat qildi. Shuning uchun bu ikkinchi marta qanday sodir bo'lishi mumkinligi juda g'alati edi! Shunga qaramay, bu sodir bo'ldi, hatto uchinchi marta ham. Bu ataylab qilingan g'arazlik yoki ixtiyoriy tavbaga o'xshardi, chunki bunday paytlarda gap shunchaki bir nechta rasmiy so'roq, noqulay sukut va keyin ketish bilan cheklanmasdi, balki u haqiqatan ham ortga burilib, u bilan birga yurishni zarur deb hisoblardi.

paras.en: He never said a great deal, nor did she give herself the trouble of talking or of listening much; but it struck her in the course of their third rencontre that he was asking some odd unconnected questions--about her pleasure in being at Hunsford, her love of solitary walks, and her opinion of Mr. and Mrs. Collins's happiness; and that in speaking of Rosings and her not perfectly understanding the house, he seemed to expect that whenever she came into Kent again she would be staying there too. His words seemed to imply it. Could he have Colonel Fitzwilliam in his thoughts? She supposed, if he meant anything, he must mean an allusion to what might arise in that quarter. It distressed her a little, and she was quite glad to find herself at the gate in the pales opposite the Parsonage.
paras.uz: U hech qachon ko'p gapirmasdi, u ham ko'p gapirish yoki tinglash zahmatini chekmasdi; lekin uchinchi uchrashuvlari davomida u g'alati, bir-biriga bog'lanmagan savollar berayotgani — uning Xansfordda bo'lishdan zavqlanishi, yolg'iz sayrlarni yaxshi ko'rishi va janob hamda missis Kollinzning baxti haqidagi fikri haqida — uning e'tiborini tortdi; Rozings haqida va uning uyni to'liq tushunmasligi haqida gapirganda, u go'yo u Kentga qachon yana kelsa, u yerda ham qolishini kutayotganday tuyuldi. Uning so'zlari shunga ishora qilayotganday edi. U polkovnik Fitsuilyamni o'ylayotgan bo'lishi mumkinmi? U, agar u biror narsani nazarda tutsa, o'sha tomonda yuzaga kelishi mumkin bo'lgan narsaga ishora qilayotgan bo'lsa kerak, deb taxmin qildi. Bu uni biroz bezovta qildi va u ruhoniy uyi ro'parasidagi panjaradagi darvoza oldida o'zini topganidan juda xursand bo'ldi.

paras.en: She was engaged one day as she walked, in perusing Jane's last letter, and dwelling on some passages which proved that Jane had not written in spirits, when, instead of being again surprised by Mr. Darcy, she saw on looking up that Colonel Fitzwilliam was meeting her. Putting away the letter immediately and forcing a smile, she said:
paras.uz: Bir kuni u sayr qilarkan, Jeynning oxirgi xatini o'qish va Jeyn yaxshi kayfiyatda yozmaganini isbotlaydigan ba'zi joylarga to'xtalish bilan band edi, shu payt yana janob Darsidan hayratlanish o'rniga, boshini ko'tarib, polkovnik Fitsuilyam qarshisidan kelayotganini ko'rdi. Xatni darhol yashirib, majburan jilmayib, dedi:

paras.en: “I did not know before that you ever walked this way.”
paras.uz: «Bu yo'ldan yurishingizni avval bilmagan ekanman».

paras.en: “I have been making the tour of the park,” he replied, “as I generally do every year, and intend to close it with a call at the Parsonage. Are you going much farther?”
paras.uz: «Odatda har yili qilganimdek, park bo'ylab aylanib chiqdim, — javob berdi u, — va uni ruhoniy uyiga kirib tugatmoqchiman. Siz ancha uzoqqa boryapsizmi?»

paras.en: “No, I should have turned in a moment.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, bir lahzadan keyin ortga burilmoqchi edim».

paras.en: And accordingly she did turn, and they walked towards the Parsonage together.
paras.uz: Va shunga ko'ra u ortga burildi va ular birga ruhoniy uyi tomon yurishdi.

paras.en: “Do you certainly leave Kent on Saturday?” said she.
paras.uz: «Kentni aniq shanba kuni tark etasizlarmi?» — dedi u.

paras.en: “Yes--if Darcy does not put it off again. But I am at his disposal. He arranges the business just as he pleases.”
paras.uz: «Ha — agar Darsi uni yana keyinga surmasa. Lekin men uning ixtiyoridaman. U ishni o'zi xohlaganidek tashkil qiladi».

paras.en: “And if not able to please himself in the arrangement, he has at least pleasure in the great power of choice. I do not know anybody who seems more to enjoy the power of doing what he likes than Mr. Darcy.”
paras.uz: «Va agar tartibda o'zini qoniqtira olmasa ham, hech bo'lmaganda tanlashning katta kuchidan zavq oladi. Xohlaganini qila olish kuchidan janob Darsidan ko'ra ko'proq zavqlanadiganga o'xshagan birorta odamni bilmayman».

paras.en: “He likes to have his own way very well,” replied Colonel Fitzwilliam. “But so we all do. It is only that he has better means of having it than many others, because he is rich, and many others are poor. I speak feelingly. A younger son, you know, must be inured to self-denial and dependence.”
paras.uz: «U o'z bilganini qilishni juda yaxshi ko'radi, — javob berdi polkovnik Fitsuilyam. — Lekin hammamiz ham shunday. Faqat uning bunga erishish uchun ko'pchilikdan yaxshiroq vositalari bor, chunki u boy, ko'pchilik esa kambag'al. His qilib gapiryapman. Bilasizmi, kichik o'g'il o'zini cheklashga va qaramlikka o'rganishi kerak».

paras.en: “In my opinion, the younger son of an earl can know very little of either. Now seriously, what have you ever known of self-denial and dependence? When have you been prevented by want of money from going wherever you chose, or procuring anything you had a fancy for?”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, grafning kichik o'g'li ikkalasi haqida ham juda kam bilishi mumkin. Endi jiddiy aytsangiz, siz o'zini cheklash va qaramlik haqida nimani bilgansiz? Qachon pul yetishmasligi sizni xohlagan joyingizga borishdan yoki ko'nglingiz tusagan narsani sotib olishdan to'xtatgan?»

paras.en: “These are home questions--and perhaps I cannot say that I have experienced many hardships of that nature. But in matters of greater weight, I may suffer from want of money. Younger sons cannot marry where they like.”
paras.uz: «Bu shaxsiy savollar — va ehtimol, bunday turdagi ko'p qiyinchiliklarni boshdan kechirganman deya olmayman. Lekin muhimroq masalalarda pul yetishmasligidan azob chekishim mumkin. Kichik o'g'illar xohlagan joyiga uylana olmaydi».

paras.en: “Unless where they like women of fortune, which I think they very often do.”
paras.uz: «Agar ular boy ayollarni xohlamasa, — menimcha, ular buni juda tez-tez qilishadi».

paras.en: “Our habits of expense make us too dependent, and there are not many in my rank of life who can afford to marry without some attention to money.”
paras.uz: «Xarajat qilish odatlarimiz bizni haddan tashqari qaram qiladi va mening martabamdagi ko'pchilik pulga biroz e'tibor bermasdan uylanishga qodir emas».

paras.en: “Is this,” thought Elizabeth, “meant for me?” and she coloured at the idea; but, recovering herself, said in a lively tone, “And pray, what is the usual price of an earl's younger son? Unless the elder brother is very sickly, I suppose you would not ask above fifty thousand pounds.”
paras.uz: «Bu menga qaratilganmi?» — deb o'yladi Elizabet va bu fikrdan qizarib ketdi; lekin o'zini tutib olib, jonli ohangda dedi: «Ayting-chi, grafning kichik o'g'lining odatiy narxi qancha? Agar katta akasi juda kasalmand bo'lmasa, menimcha, siz ellik ming funtdan ortiq so'ramaysiz».

paras.en: He answered her in the same style, and the subject dropped. To interrupt a silence which might make him fancy her affected with what had passed, she soon afterwards said:
paras.uz: U unga xuddi shu uslubda javob berdi va mavzu to'xtadi. Uni bo'lib o'tgan gap unga ta'sir qilgan deb o'ylatishi mumkin bo'lgan sukutni buzish uchun, u ko'p o'tmay dedi:

paras.en: “I imagine your cousin brought you down with him chiefly for the sake of having someone at his disposal. I wonder he does not marry, to secure a lasting convenience of that kind. But, perhaps, his sister does as well for the present, and, as she is under his sole care, he may do what he likes with her.”
paras.uz: «Tasavvur qilamanki, amakivachchangiz sizni o'zi bilan asosan ixtiyorida biror kishi bo'lishi uchun olib kelgan. Hayronmanki, bunday doimiy qulaylikni ta'minlash uchun u uylanmaydi. Lekin, ehtimol, hozircha singlisi ham shunday xizmat qiladi va u faqat uning qaramog'ida bo'lgani uchun, u bilan xohlaganini qila oladi».

paras.en: “No,” said Colonel Fitzwilliam, “that is an advantage which he must divide with me. I am joined with him in the guardianship of Miss Darcy.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, — dedi polkovnik Fitsuilyam, — bu u men bilan bo'lishishi kerak bo'lgan afzallik. Men u bilan birga miss Darsining vasiyiman».

paras.en: “Are you indeed? And pray what sort of guardians do you make? Does your charge give you much trouble? Young ladies of her age are sometimes a little difficult to manage, and if she has the true Darcy spirit, she may like to have her own way.”
paras.uz: «Rostdanmi? Ayting-chi, qanday vasiylarsiz? Qaramog'ingizdagi qiz sizga ko'p tashvish beradimi? Uning yoshidagi yosh xonimlarni boshqarish ba'zan biroz qiyin bo'ladi va agar unda haqiqiy Darsilar ruhi bo'lsa, u o'z bilganini qilishni yaxshi ko'rishi mumkin».

paras.en: As she spoke she observed him looking at her earnestly; and the manner in which he immediately asked her why she supposed Miss Darcy likely to give them any uneasiness, convinced her that she had somehow or other got pretty near the truth. She directly replied:
paras.uz: U gapirayotganda uning unga diqqat bilan qarayotganini sezdi; va uning darhol nega miss Darsi ularga biror tashvish berishi mumkin deb taxmin qilganini so'rash tarzi uni qandaydir tarzda haqiqatga ancha yaqinlashganiga ishontirdi. U darhol javob berdi:

paras.en: “You need not be frightened. I never heard any harm of her; and I dare say she is one of the most tractable creatures in the world. She is a very great favourite with some ladies of my acquaintance, Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley. I think I have heard you say that you know them.”
paras.uz: «Qo'rqishingizga hojat yo'q. U haqida hech qachon yomon gap eshitmaganman; ishonamanki, u dunyodagi eng itoatkor mavjudotlardan biri. U mening tanishlarimdan ba'zi xonimlar — missis Xerst va miss Binglining katta sevimlisi. Ularni bilishingizni aytganingizni eshitgandek bo'lgandim».

paras.en: “I know them a little. Their brother is a pleasant gentlemanlike man--he is a great friend of Darcy's.”
paras.uz: «Ularni ozgina bilaman. Ularning akasi yoqimli, janoblarga xos odam — u Darsining katta do'sti».

paras.en: “Oh! yes,” said Elizabeth drily; “Mr. Darcy is uncommonly kind to Mr. Bingley, and takes a prodigious deal of care of him.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Ha, — dedi Elizabet quruq ohangda, — janob Darsi janob Binglige g'ayrioddiy mehribon va unga juda katta g'amxo'rlik qiladi».

paras.en: “Care of him! Yes, I really believe Darcy does take care of him in those points where he most wants care. From something that he told me in our journey hither, I have reason to think Bingley very much indebted to him. But I ought to beg his pardon, for I have no right to suppose that Bingley was the person meant. It was all conjecture.”
paras.uz: «Unga g'amxo'rlik! Ha, haqiqatan ham ishonamanki, Darsi unga eng ko'p g'amxo'rlik kerak bo'lgan masalalarda g'amxo'rlik qiladi. Bu yerga kelayotganimizda u menga aytgan bir gapdan Bingli unga juda qarzdor deb o'ylash uchun asosim bor. Lekin undan kechirim so'rashim kerak, chunki gap Bingli haqida bo'lgan deb taxmin qilishga haqqim yo'q. Hammasi taxmin edi».

paras.en: “What is it you mean?”
paras.uz: «Nima demoqchisiz?»

paras.en: “It is a circumstance which Darcy could not wish to be generally known, because if it were to get round to the lady's family, it would be an unpleasant thing.”
paras.uz: «Bu Darsi hammaga ma'lum bo'lishini istamaydigan holat, chunki agar u xonimning oilasiga yetib borsa, yoqimsiz narsa bo'lardi».

paras.en: “You may depend upon my not mentioning it.”
paras.uz: «Uni tilga olmasligimga ishonishingiz mumkin».

paras.en: “And remember that I have not much reason for supposing it to be Bingley. What he told me was merely this: that he congratulated himself on having lately saved a friend from the inconveniences of a most imprudent marriage, but without mentioning names or any other particulars, and I only suspected it to be Bingley from believing him the kind of young man to get into a scrape of that sort, and from knowing them to have been together the whole of last summer.”
paras.uz: «Va unutmangki, buni Bingli deb taxmin qilishim uchun ko'p asosim yo'q. U menga faqat shuni aytdi: u yaqinda bir do'stini juda ehtiyotsiz nikoh noqulayliklaridan qutqarganidan o'zini tabriklagan, lekin ismlar yoki boshqa tafsilotlarni aytmagan; men esa uni shunday ko'ngilsizlikka tushib qoladigan yosh yigit deb bilganim va ular butun o'tgan yoz birga bo'lganini bilganim uchungina buni Bingli deb gumon qildim».

paras.en: “Did Mr. Darcy give you reasons for this interference?”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi sizga bu aralashuvning sabablarini aytdimi?»

paras.en: “I understood that there were some very strong objections against the lady.”
paras.uz: «Tushunishimcha, xonimga qarshi juda kuchli e'tirozlar bo'lgan».

paras.en: “And what arts did he use to separate them?”
paras.uz: «Va ularni ajratish uchun qanday hiylalar ishlatgan?»

paras.en: “He did not talk to me of his own arts,” said Fitzwilliam, smiling. “He only told me what I have now told you.”
paras.uz: «U menga o'z hiylalari haqida gapirmadi, — dedi Fitsuilyam jilmayib. — U menga faqat hozir sizga aytganimni aytdi».

paras.en: Elizabeth made no answer, and walked on, her heart swelling with indignation. After watching her a little, Fitzwilliam asked her why she was so thoughtful.
paras.uz: Elizabet javob bermadi va yurishda davom etdi, qalbi g'azabdan to'lib-toshardi. Uni biroz kuzatgach, Fitsuilyam undan nega bunchalik o'yga botganini so'radi.

paras.en: “I am thinking of what you have been telling me,” said she. “Your cousin's conduct does not suit my feelings. Why was he to be the judge?”
paras.uz: «Siz aytib bergan narsa haqida o'ylayapman, — dedi u. — Amakivachchangizning xatti-harakati mening tuyg'ularimga mos kelmaydi. Nega u hakam bo'lishi kerak edi?»

paras.en: “You are rather disposed to call his interference officious?”
paras.uz: «Siz uning aralashuvini ortiqcha deb atashga moyilsizmi?»

paras.en: “I do not see what right Mr. Darcy had to decide on the propriety of his friend's inclination, or why, upon his own judgement alone, he was to determine and direct in what manner his friend was to be happy. But,” she continued, recollecting herself, “as we know none of the particulars, it is not fair to condemn him. It is not to be supposed that there was much affection in the case.”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi do'stining moyilligi o'rinli ekanini hal qilishga qanday haqqi borligini yoki nega faqat o'z hukmiga asoslanib, do'sti qanday tarzda baxtli bo'lishini belgilashi va yo'naltirishi kerakligini tushunmayman. Lekin, — davom etdi u o'zini tutib olib, — hech qanday tafsilotni bilmaganimiz uchun uni qoralash adolatdan emas. Bu holatda ko'p mehr bo'lgan deb taxmin qilib bo'lmaydi».

paras.en: “That is not an unnatural surmise,” said Fitzwilliam, “but it is a lessening of the honour of my cousin's triumph very sadly.”
paras.uz: «Bu g'ayritabiiy taxmin emas, — dedi Fitsuilyam, — lekin bu amakivachchamning g'alabasi sharafini juda achinarli darajada kamaytiradi».

paras.en: This was spoken jestingly; but it appeared to her so just a picture of Mr. Darcy, that she would not trust herself with an answer, and therefore, abruptly changing the conversation talked on indifferent matters until they reached the Parsonage. There, shut into her own room, as soon as their visitor left them, she could think without interruption of all that she had heard. It was not to be supposed that any other people could be meant than those with whom she was connected. There could not exist in the world two men over whom Mr. Darcy could have such boundless influence. That he had been concerned in the measures taken to separate Bingley and Jane she had never doubted; but she had always attributed to Miss Bingley the principal design and arrangement of them. If his own vanity, however, did not mislead him, he was the cause, his pride and caprice were the cause, of all that Jane had suffered, and still continued to suffer. He had ruined for a while every hope of happiness for the most affectionate, generous heart in the world; and no one could say how lasting an evil he might have inflicted.
paras.uz: Bu hazil bilan aytildi; lekin bu unga janob Darsining shunchalik adolatli tasviri bo'lib tuyuldiki, u o'ziga javob berishga ishonmadi va shuning uchun suhbatni keskin o'zgartirib, ruhoniy uyiga yetib borgunlaricha befarq mavzularda gaplashdi. U yerda mehmon ketishi bilanoq o'z xonasiga qamalib, eshitganlarining hammasini halaqitsiz o'ylay oldi. U bog'langan odamlardan boshqa odamlar nazarda tutilgan bo'lishi mumkin deb taxmin qilib bo'lmasdi. Dunyoda janob Darsi bunchalik cheksiz ta'sir o'tkaza oladigan ikki erkak bo'lishi mumkin emasdi. U Bingli va Jeynni ajratish uchun ko'rilgan choralarda ishtirok etganiga hech qachon shubha qilmagan edi; lekin u doim ularning asosiy rejasi va tashkil etilishini miss Binglige bog'lagan edi. Biroq agar o'zining shuhratparastligi uni chalg'itmagan bo'lsa, Jeyn chekkan va hali ham chekayotgan barcha azoblarga u sababchi edi, uning g'ururi va injiqligi sababchi edi. U dunyodagi eng mehribon, eng olijanob qalbning baxtga bo'lgan har qanday umidini bir muddatga barbod qilgan edi; va u yetkazgan yomonlik qanchalik uzoq davom etishini hech kim ayta olmasdi.

paras.en: “There were some very strong objections against the lady,” were Colonel Fitzwilliam's words; and those strong objections probably were, her having one uncle who was a country attorney, and another who was in business in London.
paras.uz: «Xonimga qarshi juda kuchli e'tirozlar bo'lgan» — polkovnik Fitsuilyamning so'zlari shunday edi; bu kuchli e'tirozlar esa, ehtimol, uning bir tog'asi qishloq advokati, boshqasi esa Londonda savdo bilan shug'ullanishi edi.

paras.en: “To Jane herself,” she exclaimed, “there could be no possibility of objection; all loveliness and goodness as she is!--her understanding excellent, her mind improved, and her manners captivating. Neither could anything be urged against my father, who, though with some peculiarities, has abilities Mr. Darcy himself need not disdain, and respectability which he will probably never reach.” When she thought of her mother, her confidence gave way a little; but she would not allow that any objections there had material weight with Mr. Darcy, whose pride, she was convinced, would receive a deeper wound from the want of importance in his friend's connections, than from their want of sense; and she was quite decided, at last, that he had been partly governed by this worst kind of pride, and partly by the wish of retaining Mr. Bingley for his sister.
paras.uz: «Jeynning o'ziga, — xitob qildi u, — hech qanday e'tiroz bo'lishi mumkin emas edi; u butunlay go'zallik va yaxshilik timsoli-ku! — aqli ajoyib, fikri rivojlangan, muomalasi maftunkor. Otamga qarshi ham hech narsa aytib bo'lmasdi, u ba'zi g'aroyibliklari bo'lsa ham, janob Darsining o'zi ham mensimasligi kerak bo'lgan qobiliyatlarga va u, ehtimol, hech qachon erisha olmaydigan hurmatga ega». Onasi haqida o'ylaganda, ishonchi biroz susaydi; lekin u u yerdagi har qanday e'tiroz janob Darsi uchun jiddiy ahamiyatga ega bo'lganini tan olmadi, uning g'ururi, u ishonganidek, do'stining qarindoshlarida aql yetishmasligidan ko'ra ahamiyat yetishmasligidan chuqurroq yaralanardi; va oxir-oqibat u qisman g'ururning eng yomon turi, qisman janob Binglini singlisi uchun saqlab qolish istagi bilan boshqarilgan, degan qat'iy xulosaga keldi.

paras.en: The agitation and tears which the subject occasioned, brought on a headache; and it grew so much worse towards the evening, that, added to her unwillingness to see Mr. Darcy, it determined her not to attend her cousins to Rosings, where they were engaged to drink tea. Mrs. Collins, seeing that she was really unwell, did not press her to go and as much as possible prevented her husband from pressing her; but Mr. Collins could not conceal his apprehension of Lady Catherine's being rather displeased by her staying at home.
paras.uz: Bu mavzu sabab bo'lgan hayajon va ko'z yoshlari bosh og'rig'ini keltirib chiqardi; u kechga yaqin shunchalik kuchaydiki, janob Darsini ko'rishni istamasligi bilan qo'shilib, uni amakivachchalariga hamroh bo'lib, ular choyga taklif qilingan Rozingsga bormaslikka qaror qildirdi. Missis Kollinz uning chindan ham tobi yo'qligini ko'rib, uni borishga majburlamadi va iloji boricha erining ham majburlashiga yo'l qo'ymadi; lekin janob Kollinz ledi Ketrin uning uyda qolganidan ancha norozi bo'lishidan qo'rquvini yashira olmadi.
