In town I believe he chiefly lived, but his studying the law was a mere pretence, and being now free from all restraint, his life was a life of idleness…
That I was desirous of believing her indifferent is certain--but I will venture to say that my investigation and decisions are not usually influenced by my hopes or fears.
You must, therefore, pardon the freedom with which I demand your attention; your feelings, I know, will bestow it unwillingly, but I demand it of your justice.
About a year ago, she was taken from school, and an establishment formed for her in London; and last summer she went with the lady who presided over it, to…
His circumstances, he assured me, and I had no difficulty in believing it, were exceedingly bad.
After this period every appearance of acquaintance was dropped.

quiz.q: What did Wickham try to do to Georgiana Darcy?
o: Elope with her for her fortune
quiz.why_uz: Bu sir Darsi Elizabetga ishongani uchun ochiladi.

quiz.q: Why did Darcy separate Bingley from Jane?
o: He believed Jane did not really love Bingley
quiz.why_uz: Jeyn tuyg'ularini yashirgani uchun Darsi xato qilgan.

chapters.title: Till This Moment
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet xatni qayta-qayta o'qiydi va Uikhem haqidagi faktlarni eslab, Darsi haq ekanini tushunadi. «Shu lahzagacha men o'zimni bilmagan ekanman», deydi u.

paras.en: If Elizabeth, when Mr. Darcy gave her the letter, did not expect it to contain a renewal of his offers, she had formed no expectation at all of its contents. But such as they were, it may well be supposed how eagerly she went through them, and what a contrariety of emotion they excited. Her feelings as she read were scarcely to be defined. With amazement did she first understand that he believed any apology to be in his power; and steadfastly was she persuaded, that he could have no explanation to give, which a just sense of shame would not conceal. With a strong prejudice against everything he might say, she began his account of what had happened at Netherfield.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi unga xatni berganida, Elizabet unda takliflarining yangilanishini kutmagan bo'lsa ham, uning mazmuni haqida umuman hech qanday taxmin qilmagan edi. Lekin ular qanday bo'lmasin, u ularni qanchalik ishtiyoq bilan o'qib chiqqanini va ular qanday qarama-qarshi tuyg'ular uyg'otganini tasavvur qilish mumkin. O'qiyotganda uning tuyg'ularini zo'rg'a ta'riflash mumkin edi. U avvaliga hayrat bilan uning biror uzr qo'lidan keladi deb ishonganini tushundi; va u adolatli uyat hissi yashirmaydigan hech qanday tushuntirishi bo'lishi mumkin emasligiga qat'iy ishondi. U aytishi mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsaga nisbatan kuchli xurofot bilan u Nezerfildda bo'lib o'tgan voqealar haqidagi bayonini o'qishni boshladi.

paras.en: She read with an eagerness which hardly left her power of comprehension, and from impatience of knowing what the next sentence might bring, was incapable of attending to the sense of the one before her eyes. His belief of her sister's insensibility she instantly resolved to be false; and his account of the real, the worst objections to the match, made her too angry to have any wish of doing him justice. He expressed no regret for what he had done which satisfied her; his style was not penitent, but haughty. It was all pride and insolence.
paras.uz: U shunday ishtiyoq bilan o'qidiki, bu unga tushunish qobiliyatini deyarli qoldirmadi va keyingi jumla nima olib kelishini bilishga sabrsizlikdan ko'z oldidagi jumlaning ma'nosiga e'tibor bera olmadi. Uning opasi befarq ekaniga ishonishini u darhol yolg'on deb hal qildi; nikohga qarshi haqiqiy, eng yomon e'tirozlar haqidagi bayoni esa uni unga adolat qilish istagi bo'lmaydigan darajada g'azablantirdi. U qilgan ishi uchun uni qoniqtiradigan hech qanday afsus bildirmagan edi; uning uslubi tavba qiluvchi emas, mag'rur edi. Bularning hammasi g'urur va surbetlik edi.

paras.en: But when this subject was succeeded by his account of Mr. Wickham--when she read with somewhat clearer attention a relation of events which, if true, must overthrow every cherished opinion of his worth, and which bore so alarming an affinity to his own history of himself--her feelings were yet more acutely painful and more difficult of definition. Astonishment, apprehension, and even horror, oppressed her. She wished to discredit it entirely, repeatedly exclaiming, “This must be false! This cannot be! This must be the grossest falsehood!”--and when she had gone through the whole letter, though scarcely knowing anything of the last page or two, put it hastily away, protesting that she would not regard it, that she would never look in it again.
paras.uz: Lekin bu mavzudan keyin janob Uikhem haqidagi bayoni kelganda — agar rost bo'lsa, uning qadri haqidagi har bir aziz fikrni ag'darib tashlashi kerak bo'lgan va uning o'zi haqidagi hikoyasiga shunchalik xavotirli o'xshashligi bo'lgan voqealar bayonini biroz aniqroq e'tibor bilan o'qiganida — uning tuyg'ulari yanada o'tkirroq og'riqli va ta'riflash qiyinroq bo'ldi. Hayrat, xavotir va hatto dahshat uni ezdi. U bunga butunlay ishonmaslikni istadi va qayta-qayta xitob qildi: «Bu yolg'on bo'lishi kerak! Bunday bo'lishi mumkin emas! Bu eng qo'pol yolg'on bo'lishi kerak!» — va butun xatni o'qib chiqqach, oxirgi bir-ikki sahifadan deyarli hech narsani bilmasa ham, uni shoshilib yashirdi va unga ahamiyat bermasligini, unga boshqa hech qachon qaramasligini ta'kidladi.

paras.en: In this perturbed state of mind, with thoughts that could rest on nothing, she walked on; but it would not do; in half a minute the letter was unfolded again, and collecting herself as well as she could, she again began the mortifying perusal of all that related to Wickham, and commanded herself so far as to examine the meaning of every sentence. The account of his connection with the Pemberley family was exactly what he had related himself; and the kindness of the late Mr. Darcy, though she had not before known its extent, agreed equally well with his own words. So far each recital confirmed the other; but when she came to the will, the difference was great.
paras.uz: Fikrlari hech narsada to'xtay olmaydigan bunday bezovta ruhiy holatda u yurishda davom etdi; lekin bu foyda bermadi; yarim daqiqadan keyin xat yana ochildi va iloji boricha o'zini yig'ib, u yana Uikhemga oid hamma narsani xo'rlovchi tarzda o'qishni boshladi va har bir jumlaning ma'nosini tekshirish darajasida o'zini qo'lga oldi. Uning Pemberli oilasi bilan aloqasi haqidagi bayon aynan u o'zi aytib bergandek edi; marhum janob Darsining mehribonligi esa, garchi u avval uning ko'lamini bilmagan bo'lsa ham, uning o'z so'zlariga xuddi shunday mos kelardi. Shu paytgacha har bir hikoya ikkinchisini tasdiqlardi; lekin vasiyatnomaga kelganda farq katta edi.

paras.en: What Wickham had said of the living was fresh in her memory, and as she recalled his very words, it was impossible not to feel that there was gross duplicity on one side or the other; and, for a few moments, she flattered herself that her wishes did not err. But when she read and re-read with the closest attention, the particulars immediately following of Wickham's resigning all pretensions to the living, of his receiving in lieu so considerable a sum as three thousand pounds, again was she forced to hesitate. She put down the letter, weighed every circumstance with what she meant to be impartiality--deliberated on the probability of each statement--but with little success. On both sides it was only assertion.
paras.uz: Uikhemning lavozim haqida aytganlari uning xotirasida yangi edi va uning aynan so'zlarini eslarkan, u yoki bu tomonda qo'pol ikkiyuzlamachilik borligini his qilmaslik imkonsiz edi; va bir necha lahza u istaklari adashmayotgani bilan o'zini ovutdi. Lekin u darhol keyin keladigan Uikhemning lavozimga bo'lgan barcha da'volaridan voz kechgani, evaziga uch ming funtdek katta summa olgani haqidagi tafsilotlarni eng diqqatli e'tibor bilan qayta-qayta o'qiganida, yana ikkilanishga majbur bo'ldi. U xatni qo'ydi, har bir holatni xolislik deb niyat qilgan narsa bilan tortdi — har bir bayonotning ehtimolligi haqida mulohaza yuritdi — lekin kam muvaffaqiyat bilan. Ikkala tomonda ham faqat da'vo edi.

paras.en: Again she read on; but every line proved more clearly that the affair, which she had believed it impossible that any contrivance could so represent as to render Mr. Darcy's conduct in it less than infamous, was capable of a turn which must make him entirely blameless throughout the whole.
paras.uz: Yana u o'qishda davom etdi; lekin har bir satr u janob Darsining undagi xatti-harakatini sharmandalikdan kam qilib ko'rsatadigan hech qanday hiyla bo'lishi mumkin emas deb ishongan ishning uni butun davomida butunlay aybsiz qiladigan tusga kirishi mumkinligini tobora aniqroq isbotlardi.

paras.en: The extravagance and general profligacy which he scrupled not to lay at Mr. Wickham's charge, exceedingly shocked her; the more so, as she could bring no proof of its injustice. She had never heard of him before his entrance into the ----shire Militia, in which he had engaged at the persuasion of the young man who, on meeting him accidentally in town, had there renewed a slight acquaintance. Of his former way of life nothing had been known in Hertfordshire but what he told himself. As to his real character, had information been in her power, she had never felt a wish of inquiring. His countenance, voice, and manner had established him at once in the possession of every virtue.
paras.uz: U janob Uikhemga yuklashdan tortinmagan isrofgarchilik va umumiy buzuqlik uni nihoyatda hayratga soldi; ayniqsa u uning adolatsizligiga hech qanday dalil keltira olmagani uchun. U u haqida u ----shir militsiyasiga kirguncha hech narsa eshitmagan edi, u unga Londonda tasodifan uchratib, u yerda yengil tanishlikni yangilagan yosh yigitning ko'ndirishi bilan kirgan edi. Uning avvalgi turmush tarzi haqida Xertfordshirda u o'zi aytganidan boshqa hech narsa ma'lum emasdi. Uning haqiqiy xarakteriga kelsak, agar ma'lumot olish imkoni bo'lganida ham, u hech qachon so'rashni istamagan edi. Uning chehrasi, ovozi va muomalasi uni darhol barcha fazilatlarning egasi qilib qo'ygan edi.

paras.en: She tried to recollect some instance of goodness, some distinguished trait of integrity or benevolence, that might rescue him from the attacks of Mr. Darcy; or at least, by the predominance of virtue, atone for those casual errors under which she would endeavour to class what Mr. Darcy had described as the idleness and vice of many years' continuance. But no such recollection befriended her. She could see him instantly before her, in every charm of air and address; but she could remember no more substantial good than the general approbation of the neighbourhood, and the regard which his social powers had gained him in the mess. After pausing on this point a considerable while, she once more continued to read.
paras.uz: U uni janob Darsining hujumlaridan qutqarishi mumkin bo'lgan biror yaxshilik namunasini, halollik yoki ezgulikning biror ajralib turuvchi xususiyatini eslashga urindi; yoki hech bo'lmaganda fazilatning ustunligi bilan janob Darsi ko'p yillik bekorchilik va illat deb tasvirlagan narsani tasnif qilishga harakat qilishi mumkin bo'lgan tasodifiy xatolarni yuvishi mumkin bo'lgan narsani. Lekin bunday xotira unga yordam bermadi. U uni darhol ko'z oldida qiyofasi va muomalasining butun jozibasi bilan ko'ra olardi; lekin mahallaning umumiy ma'qullashi va ijtimoiy qobiliyatlari unga ofitserlar davrasida qozongan hurmatdan ortiq jiddiy yaxshilikni eslay olmadi. Bu nuqtada ancha vaqt to'xtagach, u yana o'qishda davom etdi.

paras.en: But, alas! the story which followed, of his designs on Miss Darcy, received some confirmation from what had passed between Colonel Fitzwilliam and herself only the morning before; and at last she was referred for the truth of every particular to Colonel Fitzwilliam himself--from whom she had previously received the information of his near concern in all his cousin's affairs, and whose character she had no reason to question. At one time she had almost resolved on applying to him, but the idea was checked by the awkwardness of the application, and at length wholly banished by the conviction that Mr. Darcy would never have hazarded such a proposal, if he had not been well assured of his cousin's corroboration.
paras.uz: Lekin, afsus! Keyin kelgan uning miss Darsiga nisbatan rejalari haqidagi hikoya faqat kecha ertalab polkovnik Fitsuilyam bilan o'zi o'rtasida bo'lib o'tgan suhbatdan ma'lum tasdiq oldi; va nihoyat har bir tafsilotning haqiqatligi uchun uni polkovnik Fitsuilyamning o'ziga yo'llashgan edi — undan u avvalroq amakivachchasining barcha ishlariga yaqindan aloqadorligi haqida ma'lumot olgan edi va uning xarakteriga shubha qilish uchun hech qanday asosi yo'q edi. Bir paytda u unga murojaat qilishga deyarli qaror qilgan edi, lekin bu fikrni murojaatning noqulayligi to'xtatdi va nihoyat janob Darsi, agar amakivachchasining tasdig'iga yaxshi ishonmaganida, bunday taklifni hech qachon xavf ostiga qo'ymagan bo'lardi, degan ishonch uni butunlay haydab yubordi.

paras.en: She perfectly remembered everything that had passed in conversation between Wickham and herself, in their first evening at Mr. Phillips's. Many of his expressions were still fresh in her memory. She was now struck with the impropriety of such communications to a stranger, and wondered it had escaped her before. She saw the indelicacy of putting himself forward as he had done, and the inconsistency of his professions with his conduct. She remembered that he had boasted of having no fear of seeing Mr. Darcy--that Mr. Darcy might leave the country, but that he should stand his ground; yet he had avoided the Netherfield ball the very next week. She remembered also that, till the Netherfield family had quitted the country, he had told his story to no one but herself; but that after their removal it had been everywhere discussed; that he had then no reserves, no scruples in sinking Mr. Darcy's character, though he had assured her that respect for the father would always prevent his exposing the son.
paras.uz: U janob Fillipsnikidagi birinchi oqshomlarida Uikhem bilan o'zi o'rtasida bo'lib o'tgan suhbatning hammasini mukammal eslardi. Uning ko'plab iboralari hali ham xotirasida yangi edi. Endi u begonaga bunday gaplarni aytishning nomunosibligidan hayratga tushdi va bu avval qanday qilib uning e'tiboridan chetda qolganiga hayron bo'ldi. U o'zini shunday oldinga surishining nazokatsizligini va da'volarining xatti-harakatiga nomuvofiqligini ko'rdi. U janob Darsini ko'rishdan qo'rqmasligi bilan maqtanganini — janob Darsi bu yerlarni tark etishi mumkin, lekin o'zi joyida turishini aytganini esladi; shunga qaramay, aynan keyingi haftada u Nezerfild balidan qochgan edi. U shuningdek Nezerfild oilasi bu yerlarni tark etgunicha u o'z hikoyasini o'zidan boshqa hech kimga aytmaganini; lekin ular ketgach, u hamma joyda muhokama qilinganini; o'shanda janob Darsining obro'sini to'kishda hech qanday tortinish, hech qanday ikkilanish qilmaganini esladi, garchi unga otaga bo'lgan hurmat doim o'g'lini fosh qilishdan to'xtatishini aytib ishontirgan bo'lsa ham.

paras.en: How differently did everything now appear in which he was concerned! His attentions to Miss King were now the consequence of views solely and hatefully mercenary; and the mediocrity of her fortune proved no longer the moderation of his wishes, but his eagerness to grasp at anything. His behaviour to herself could now have had no tolerable motive; he had either been deceived with regard to her fortune, or had been gratifying his vanity by encouraging the preference which she believed she had most incautiously shown.
paras.uz: U bilan bog'liq hamma narsa endi qanchalik boshqacha ko'rinardi! Uning miss Kingga e'tiborlari endi faqat va jirkanch darajada pulparast maqsadlarning natijasi edi; uning boyligining o'rtachaligi endi istaklarining mo''tadilligini emas, balki har qanday narsaga yopishishga ishtiyoqini isbotlardi. Uning o'ziga nisbatan xatti-harakatining endi hech qanday maqbul sababi bo'lishi mumkin emasdi; u yo uning boyligi haqida aldangan, yo u juda ehtiyotsizlik bilan ko'rsatgan deb ishongan afzallikni rag'batlantirib, shuhratparastligini qondirgan edi.

paras.en: Every lingering struggle in his favour grew fainter and fainter; and in farther justification of Mr. Darcy, she could not but allow that Mr. Bingley, when questioned by Jane, had long ago asserted his blamelessness in the affair; that proud and repulsive as were his manners, she had never, in the whole course of their acquaintance--an acquaintance which had latterly brought them much together, and given her a sort of intimacy with his ways--seen anything that betrayed him to be unprincipled or unjust--anything that spoke him of irreligious or immoral habits; that among his own connections he was esteemed and valued--that even Wickham had allowed him merit as a brother, and that she had often heard him speak so affectionately of his sister as to prove him capable of some amiable feeling; that had his actions been what Mr. Wickham represented them, so gross a violation of everything right could hardly have been concealed from the world; and that friendship between a person capable of it, and such an amiable man as Mr. Bingley, was incomprehensible.
paras.uz: Uning foydasiga bo'lgan har bir qolgan kurash tobora zaiflashib bordi; va janob Darsini yanada oqlash uchun u tan olmay qololmadi: Jeyn so'raganida, janob Bingli uzoq vaqt oldin uning bu ishda aybsizligini ta'kidlagan edi; uning muomalasi qanchalik mag'rur va itaruvchi bo'lmasin, u butun tanishliklari davomida — so'nggi paytlarda ularni ko'p birga bo'lishga olib kelgan va unga uning odatlari bilan o'ziga xos yaqinlik bergan tanishlik davomida — uni tamoyilsiz yoki adolatsiz ekanini oshkor qiladigan hech narsani — uning dinsiz yoki axloqsiz odatlari haqida gapiradigan hech narsani ko'rmagan edi; o'z qarindoshlari orasida uni hurmat qilishar va qadrlashardi — hatto Uikhem ham uning aka sifatidagi fazilatini tan olgan edi va u ko'pincha uning singlisi haqida shunchalik mehr bilan gapirganini eshitgan ediki, bu uning biror yoqimli tuyg'uga qodir ekanini isbotlardi; agar uning harakatlari janob Uikhem tasvirlagandek bo'lganida, hamma to'g'ri narsalarning bunchalik qo'pol buzilishini dunyodan zo'rg'a yashirish mumkin edi; va bunga qodir odam bilan janob Binglidek yoqimli odam o'rtasidagi do'stlik tushunib bo'lmas edi.

paras.en: She grew absolutely ashamed of herself. Of neither Darcy nor Wickham could she think without feeling she had been blind, partial, prejudiced, absurd.
paras.uz: U o'zidan butunlay uyalib ketdi. Darsi haqida ham, Uikhem haqida ham u ko'r, tarafkash, xurofotli, bema'ni bo'lganini his qilmasdan o'ylay olmasdi.

paras.en: “How despicably I have acted!” she cried; “I, who have prided myself on my discernment! I, who have valued myself on my abilities! who have often disdained the generous candour of my sister, and gratified my vanity in useless or blameable mistrust! How humiliating is this discovery! Yet, how just a humiliation! Had I been in love, I could not have been more wretchedly blind! But vanity, not love, has been my folly. Pleased with the preference of one, and offended by the neglect of the other, on the very beginning of our acquaintance, I have courted prepossession and ignorance, and driven reason away, where either were concerned. Till this moment I never knew myself.”
paras.uz: «Qanchalik jirkanch harakat qildim! — xitob qildi u. — Men, farosatim bilan faxrlanib yurgan men! Qobiliyatlarim bilan o'zimni qadrlagan men! Opamning olijanob xolisligini tez-tez mensimagan va shuhratparastligimni befoyda yoki ayblanishga loyiq ishonchsizlik bilan qondirgan men! Bu kashfiyot qanchalik kamsituvchi! Shunga qaramay, qanchalik adolatli kamsitish! Agar oshiq bo'lganimda, bundan ham ayanchliroq ko'r bo'la olmasdim! Lekin mening ahmoqligim muhabbat emas, shuhratparastlik bo'ldi. Tanishuvimizning aynan boshida birining afzal ko'rishidan mamnun bo'lib, ikkinchisining e'tiborsizligidan ranjib, ikkalasiga tegishli joyda xurofot va jaholatni qo'llab, aqlni haydab yubordim. Shu lahzagacha o'zimni hech qachon bilmagan ekanman».

paras.en: From herself to Jane--from Jane to Bingley, her thoughts were in a line which soon brought to her recollection that Mr. Darcy's explanation there had appeared very insufficient, and she read it again. Widely different was the effect of a second perusal. How could she deny that credit to his assertions in one instance, which she had been obliged to give in the other? He declared himself to be totally unsuspicious of her sister's attachment; and she could not help remembering what Charlotte's opinion had always been. Neither could she deny the justice of his description of Jane. She felt that Jane's feelings, though fervent, were little displayed, and that there was a constant complacency in her air and manner not often united with great sensibility.
paras.uz: O'zidan Jeynga — Jeyndan Binglige, uning fikrlari shunday chiziqda edi ki, tez orada janob Darsining u yerdagi tushuntirishi juda yetarsiz ko'ringanini esladi va uni yana o'qidi. Ikkinchi o'qishning ta'siri butunlay boshqacha edi. Bir holatda berishga majbur bo'lgan ishonchni boshqa holatda uning da'volariga qanday qilib rad eta olardi? U opasining mehridan butunlay shubhalanmaganini e'lon qilgan edi; va u Sharlottaning fikri doim qanday bo'lganini eslamay qololmadi. Uning Jeyn tasvirining adolatliligini ham inkor eta olmasdi. U Jeynning tuyg'ulari qizg'in bo'lsa ham, kam namoyon bo'lishini va uning qiyofasi hamda muomalasida katta ta'sirchanlik bilan kamdan-kam qo'shiladigan doimiy mamnuniyat borligini his qildi.

paras.en: When she came to that part of the letter in which her family were mentioned in terms of such mortifying, yet merited reproach, her sense of shame was severe. The justice of the charge struck her too forcibly for denial, and the circumstances to which he particularly alluded as having passed at the Netherfield ball, and as confirming all his first disapprobation, could not have made a stronger impression on his mind than on hers.
paras.uz: U xatning oilasi shunday xo'rlovchi, lekin munosib tanbeh so'zlari bilan tilga olingan qismiga kelganda, uyat hissi qattiq edi. Ayblovning adolatliligi unga inkor etish uchun haddan tashqari kuchli ta'sir qildi va u ayniqsa Nezerfild balida bo'lib o'tgan va uning dastlabki noroziligini tasdiqlagan deb ishora qilgan holatlar uning ongida uning ongidagidan kuchliroq taassurot qoldira olmasdi.

paras.en: The compliment to herself and her sister was not unfelt. It soothed, but it could not console her for the contempt which had thus been self-attracted by the rest of her family; and as she considered that Jane's disappointment had in fact been the work of her nearest relations, and reflected how materially the credit of both must be hurt by such impropriety of conduct, she felt depressed beyond anything she had ever known before.
paras.uz: O'ziga va opasiga qilingan iltifot sezilmay qolmadi. U yengillik berdi, lekin oilasining qolgan a'zolari shu tarzda o'zlariga tortgan nafrat uchun uni yupata olmadi; va Jeynning hafsalasi pir bo'lishi aslida eng yaqin qarindoshlarining ishi ekanini o'ylab, bunday nomunosib xatti-harakat ikkalasining obro'siga qanchalik jiddiy zarar yetkazishi kerakligini mulohaza qilib, u ilgari hech qachon bilmagan darajada tushkunlikka tushdi.

paras.en: After wandering along the lane for two hours, giving way to every variety of thought--re-considering events, determining probabilities, and reconciling herself, as well as she could, to a change so sudden and so important, fatigue, and a recollection of her long absence, made her at length return home; and she entered the house with the wish of appearing cheerful as usual, and the resolution of repressing such reflections as must make her unfit for conversation.
paras.uz: Ikki soat davomida tor yo'l bo'ylab kezib, har xil fikrlarga berilib — voqealarni qayta ko'rib chiqib, ehtimolliklarni aniqlab va iloji boricha bunchalik to'satdan va bunchalik muhim o'zgarish bilan murosaga kelib, charchoq va uzoq yo'qligini eslash uni nihoyat uyga qaytishga majbur qildi; va u odatdagidek quvnoq ko'rinish istagi va uni suhbatga yaroqsiz qiladigan bunday mulohazalarni bostirish qarori bilan uyga kirdi.

paras.en: She was immediately told that the two gentlemen from Rosings had each called during her absence; Mr. Darcy, only for a few minutes, to take leave--but that Colonel Fitzwilliam had been sitting with them at least an hour, hoping for her return, and almost resolving to walk after her till she could be found. Elizabeth could but just affect concern in missing him; she really rejoiced at it. Colonel Fitzwilliam was no longer an object; she could think only of her letter.
paras.uz: Unga darhol Rozingsdan ikki janob uning yo'qligida alohida-alohida kelib ketganini aytishdi; janob Darsi xayrlashish uchun atigi bir necha daqiqaga kelgan — lekin polkovnik Fitsuilyam uning qaytishiga umid qilib, ular bilan kamida bir soat o'tirgan va u topilgunicha uning ortidan piyoda borishga deyarli qaror qilgan edi. Elizabet uni ko'rmay qolganidan zo'rg'a afsuslanganday ko'rina oldi; aslida u bundan xursand edi. Polkovnik Fitsuilyam endi qiziqish obyekti emasdi; u faqat xati haqida o'ylay olardi.

quiz.q: What does Elizabeth realise?

quiz.why_uz: Bu — romanning asosiy burilish nuqtasi.

quiz.q: Which part of the letter hurts her most?
quiz.why_uz: U oilasining xatti-harakati haqidagi gaplar to'g'ri ekanini tan oladi.

chapters.title: Leaving Rosings
chapters.recap_uz: Darsi va polkovnik ketishadi. Elizabet xatni yodlab oladi va oilasining kamchiliklari, ayniqsa Lidiya va Ketti haqida qayg'uradi.

paras.en: The two gentlemen left Rosings the next morning, and Mr. Collins having been in waiting near the lodges, to make them his parting obeisance, was able to bring home the pleasing intelligence, of their appearing in very good health, and in as tolerable spirits as could be expected, after the melancholy scene so lately gone through at Rosings. To Rosings he then hastened, to console Lady Catherine and her daughter; and on his return brought back, with great satisfaction, a message from her ladyship, importing that she felt herself so dull as to make her very desirous of having them all to dine with her.
paras.uz: Ikki janob ertasi kuni ertalab Rozingsni tark etishdi va ularga xayrlashish ta'zimini qilish uchun qorovulxonalar yonida kutib turgan janob Kollinz ular juda sog'lom va Rozingsda yaqinda bo'lib o'tgan qayg'uli sahnadan keyin kutish mumkin bo'lgan darajada yaxshi kayfiyatda ko'rinishgani haqidagi yoqimli xabarni uyga olib kela oldi. Keyin u ledi Ketrin va uning qizini yupatish uchun Rozingsga shoshildi; qaytib kelib esa katta mamnuniyat bilan janoblaridan xabar olib keldi: u o'zini shunchalik zerikkan his qilyaptiki, hammalarini o'zi bilan tushlik qilishlarini juda istayapti.

paras.en: Elizabeth could not see Lady Catherine without recollecting that, had she chosen it, she might by this time have been presented to her as her future niece; nor could she think, without a smile, of what her ladyship's indignation would have been. “What would she have said? how would she have behaved?” were questions with which she amused herself.
paras.uz: Elizabet ledi Ketrinni ko'rib, agar xohlaganida hozirga kelib unga kelajakdagi jiyani sifatida tanishtirilgan bo'lishi mumkinligini eslamay qololmadi; janoblarining g'azabi qanday bo'lishini ham jilmaymasdan o'ylay olmadi. «U nima degan bo'lardi? O'zini qanday tutgan bo'lardi?» — u o'zini shu savollar bilan ovutardi.

paras.en: Their first subject was the diminution of the Rosings party. “I assure you, I feel it exceedingly,” said Lady Catherine; “I believe no one feels the loss of friends so much as I do. But I am particularly attached to these young men, and know them to be so much attached to me! They were excessively sorry to go! But so they always are. The dear Colonel rallied his spirits tolerably till just at last; but Darcy seemed to feel it most acutely, more, I think, than last year. His attachment to Rosings certainly increases.”
paras.uz: Ularning birinchi mavzusi Rozings davrasining kamayishi edi. «Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, buni nihoyatda his qilyapman, — dedi ledi Ketrin. — Menimcha, hech kim do'stlarni yo'qotishni men kabi his qilmaydi. Lekin bu yosh yigitlarga ayniqsa bog'langanman va ular ham menga juda bog'langanini bilaman! Ular ketishdan nihoyatda afsuslanishdi! Lekin ular doim shunday. Aziz polkovnik oxirigacha kayfiyatini ancha yaxshi saqladi; lekin Darsi buni eng o'tkir his qilganday ko'rindi, menimcha, o'tgan yildagidan ham ko'proq. Uning Rozingsga bog'liqligi, albatta, ortib bormoqda».

paras.en: Mr. Collins had a compliment, and an allusion to throw in here, which were kindly smiled on by the mother and daughter.
paras.uz: Bu yerda janob Kollinzning qistirib o'tadigan iltifoti va ishorasi bor edi, ona va qiz bunga mehribonlik bilan jilmayishdi.

paras.en: Lady Catherine observed, after dinner, that Miss Bennet seemed out of spirits, and immediately accounting for it by herself, by supposing that she did not like to go home again so soon, she added:
paras.uz: Tushlikdan keyin ledi Ketrin miss Bennetning kayfiyati yo'qdek ko'rinayotganini aytdi va darhol buni o'zi uchun uyga bunchalik tez qaytishni istamayotgani bilan tushuntirib, qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “But if that is the case, you must write to your mother and beg that you may stay a little longer. Mrs. Collins will be very glad of your company, I am sure.”
paras.uz: «Lekin agar shunday bo'lsa, onangizga xat yozib, biroz uzoqroq qolishga ruxsat so'rashingiz kerak. Ishonchim komilki, missis Kollinz sizning davrangizdan juda xursand bo'ladi».

paras.en: “I am much obliged to your ladyship for your kind invitation,” replied Elizabeth, “but it is not in my power to accept it. I must be in town next Saturday.”
paras.uz: «Janoblarining mehribon taklifi uchun juda minnatdorman, — javob berdi Elizabet, — lekin uni qabul qilish qo'limdan kelmaydi. Kelasi shanba kuni Londonda bo'lishim kerak».

paras.en: “Why, at that rate, you will have been here only six weeks. I expected you to stay two months. I told Mrs. Collins so before you came. There can be no occasion for your going so soon. Mrs. Bennet could certainly spare you for another fortnight.”
paras.uz: «Axir, bu hisobda siz bu yerda atigi olti hafta bo'lgan bo'lasiz. Men sizni ikki oy qoladi deb kutgandim. Siz kelishingizdan oldin missis Kollinzga shunday degan edim. Bunchalik tez ketishingizga hech qanday sabab bo'lishi mumkin emas. Missis Bennet albatta sizsiz yana ikki hafta tura oladi».

paras.en: “But my father cannot. He wrote last week to hurry my return.”
paras.uz: «Lekin otam tura olmaydi. U o'tgan hafta qaytishimni tezlashtirish uchun xat yozdi».

paras.en: “Oh! your father of course may spare you, if your mother can. Daughters are never of so much consequence to a father. And if you will stay another month complete, it will be in my power to take one of you as far as London, for I am going there early in June, for a week; and as Dawson does not object to the barouche-box, there will be very good room for one of you--and indeed, if the weather should happen to be cool, I should not object to taking you both, as you are neither of you large.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Agar onangiz tura olsa, otangiz, albatta, sizsiz tura oladi. Qizlar ota uchun hech qachon bunchalik muhim bo'lmaydi. Agar yana to'liq bir oy qolsangiz, biringizni Londongacha olib borish qo'limdan keladi, chunki men iyun boshida bir haftaga u yerga boraman; Douson barusha qutisiga e'tiroz bildirmagani uchun, biringiz uchun juda yaxshi joy bo'ladi — haqiqatan ham, agar ob-havo salqin bo'lsa, ikkalangizni ham olishga qarshi emasman, chunki hech biringiz katta emassiz».

paras.en: “You are all kindness, madam; but I believe we must abide by our original plan.”
paras.uz: «Siz mehribonlikning o'zisiz, xonim; lekin menimcha, biz dastlabki rejamizga amal qilishimiz kerak».

paras.en: Lady Catherine seemed resigned. “Mrs. Collins, you must send a servant with them. You know I always speak my mind, and I cannot bear the idea of two young women travelling post by themselves. It is highly improper. You must contrive to send somebody. I have the greatest dislike in the world to that sort of thing. Young women should always be properly guarded and attended, according to their situation in life. When my niece Georgiana went to Ramsgate last summer, I made a point of her having two men-servants go with her. Miss Darcy, the daughter of Mr. Darcy, of Pemberley, and Lady Anne, could not have appeared with propriety in a different manner. I am excessively attentive to all those things. You must send John with the young ladies, Mrs. Collins. I am glad it occurred to me to mention it; for it would really be discreditable to you to let them go alone.”
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrin taslim bo'lganday ko'rindi. «Missis Kollinz, ular bilan xizmatkor yuborishingiz kerak. Bilasiz, men doim fikrimni ochiq aytaman va ikki yosh ayolning yolg'iz o'zi pochta aravasida sayohat qilishi fikriga chiday olmayman. Bu juda nomunosib. Kimnidir yuborishning yo'lini topishingiz kerak. Bunday narsani dunyoda eng yomon ko'raman. Yosh ayollarni doim hayotdagi mavqeiga ko'ra munosib qo'riqlash va kuzatib borish kerak. Jiyanim Jorjiana o'tgan yozda Ramsgeytga borganida, u bilan ikki erkak xizmatkor borishini qat'iy talab qildim. Pemberlilik janob Darsi va ledi Ennning qizi miss Darsi boshqacha tarzda munosib ko'rina olmasdi. Men bunday narsalarning hammasiga nihoyatda e'tiborliman. Yosh xonimlar bilan Jonni yuborishingiz kerak, missis Kollinz. Buni aytish xayolimga kelganidan xursandman; chunki ularni yolg'iz yuborish siz uchun haqiqatan ham sharmandalik bo'lardi».

paras.en: “My uncle is to send a servant for us.”
paras.uz: «Tog'am biz uchun xizmatkor yuboradi».

paras.en: “Oh! Your uncle! He keeps a man-servant, does he? I am very glad you have somebody who thinks of these things. Where shall you change horses? Oh! Bromley, of course. If you mention my name at the Bell, you will be attended to.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Tog'angiz! Uning erkak xizmatkori bormi? Bunday narsalar haqida o'ylaydigan odamingiz borligidan juda xursandman. Otlarni qayerda almashtirasiz? Oh! Albatta, Bromlida. Agar "Qo'ng'iroq" mehmonxonasida mening nomimni tilga olsangiz, sizga xizmat ko'rsatishadi».

paras.en: Lady Catherine had many other questions to ask respecting their journey, and as she did not answer them all herself, attention was necessary, which Elizabeth believed to be lucky for her; or, with a mind so occupied, she might have forgotten where she was. Reflection must be reserved for solitary hours; whenever she was alone, she gave way to it as the greatest relief; and not a day went by without a solitary walk, in which she might indulge in all the delight of unpleasant recollections.
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrinning ularning safari haqida so'raydigan boshqa ko'p savollari bor edi va u ularning hammasiga o'zi javob bermagani uchun e'tibor zarur edi, Elizabet buni o'zi uchun omad deb hisobladi; aks holda, fikri bunchalik band bo'lgani uchun, qayerda ekanini unutib qo'yishi mumkin edi. Mulohazani yolg'iz soatlarga qoldirish kerak edi; har safar yolg'iz qolganda, u unga eng katta yengillik sifatida berilardi; va yoqimsiz xotiralarning butun zavqiga berilishi mumkin bo'lgan yolg'iz sayrsiz birorta ham kun o'tmasdi.

paras.en: Mr. Darcy's letter she was in a fair way of soon knowing by heart. She studied every sentence; and her feelings towards its writer were at times widely different. When she remembered the style of his address, she was still full of indignation; but when she considered how unjustly she had condemned and upbraided him, her anger was turned against herself; and his disappointed feelings became the object of compassion. His attachment excited gratitude, his general character respect; but she could not approve him; nor could she for a moment repent her refusal, or feel the slightest inclination ever to see him again. In her own past behaviour, there was a constant source of vexation and regret; and in the unhappy defects of her family, a subject of yet heavier chagrin. They were hopeless of remedy.
paras.uz: Janob Darsining xatini u tez orada yoddan bilish yo'lida edi. U har bir jumlani o'rgandi; muallifiga nisbatan tuyg'ulari ba'zan butunlay farq qilardi. Uning murojaat uslubini eslaganda, u hali ham g'azabga to'la edi; lekin uni qanchalik adolatsiz qoralagani va koyiganini o'ylaganda, g'azabi o'ziga qarshi burilar, uning hafsalasi pir bo'lgan tuyg'ulari esa achinish obyektiga aylanardi. Uning mehri minnatdorlik, umumiy xarakteri hurmat uyg'otardi; lekin u uni ma'qullay olmasdi; rad etganidan bir lahzaga ham pushaymon bo'la olmasdi yoki uni yana ko'rishga zarracha moyillik his qila olmasdi. O'zining o'tgan xatti-harakatida doimiy g'ashlik va afsus manbai, oilasining baxtsiz kamchiliklarida esa yanada og'irroq g'am mavzusi bor edi. Ularni tuzatishdan umid yo'q edi.

paras.en: Her father, contented with laughing at them, would never exert himself to restrain the wild giddiness of his youngest daughters; and her mother, with manners so far from right herself, was entirely insensible of the evil. Elizabeth had frequently united with Jane in an endeavour to check the imprudence of Catherine and Lydia; but while they were supported by their mother's indulgence, what chance could there be of improvement? Catherine, weak-spirited, irritable, and completely under Lydia's guidance, had been always affronted by their advice; and Lydia, self-willed and careless, would scarcely give them a hearing. They were ignorant, idle, and vain. While there was an officer in Meryton, they would flirt with him; and while Meryton was within a walk of Longbourn, they would be going there forever.
paras.uz: Ularga kulish bilan qanoatlanadigan otasi hech qachon kichik qizlarining yovvoyi yengiltakligini jilovlash uchun harakat qilmasdi; muomalasi o'zi to'g'rilikdan shunchalik yiroq bo'lgan onasi esa yomonlikni butunlay sezmasdi. Elizabet ko'pincha Ketrin va Lidiyaning ehtiyotsizligini to'xtatishga urinishda Jeyn bilan birlashgan edi; lekin ular onalarining erkalatishi bilan qo'llab-quvvatlanar ekan, yaxshilanishga qanday imkoniyat bo'lishi mumkin edi? Zaif irodali, jizzaki va butunlay Lidiyaning ta'siri ostidagi Ketrin ularning maslahatidan doim ranjirdi; o'jar va beparvo Lidiya esa ularni deyarli tinglamasdi. Ular johil, dangasa va manman edi. Meritonda ofitser bor ekan, ular u bilan noz-karashma qilishardi; Meriton Longborndan piyoda boriladigan masofada ekan, ular u yerga abadiy borib turishardi.

paras.en: Anxiety on Jane's behalf was another prevailing concern; and Mr. Darcy's explanation, by restoring Bingley to all her former good opinion, heightened the sense of what Jane had lost. His affection was proved to have been sincere, and his conduct cleared of all blame, unless any could attach to the implicitness of his confidence in his friend. How grievous then was the thought that, of a situation so desirable in every respect, so replete with advantage, so promising for happiness, Jane had been deprived, by the folly and indecorum of her own family!
paras.uz: Jeyn uchun tashvish yana bir ustun tashvish edi; janob Darsining tushuntirishi Binglini uning avvalgi barcha yaxshi fikriga qaytarib, Jeyn nimani yo'qotgani hissini kuchaytirdi. Uning mehri samimiy bo'lgani isbotlandi va xatti-harakati, agar do'stiga bo'lgan so'zsiz ishonchiga biror ayb tegishi mumkin bo'lmasa, barcha ayblardan tozalandi. Demak, har jihatdan shunchalik orzu qilinadigan, shunchalik afzalliklarga to'la, baxt uchun shunchalik istiqbolli vaziyatdan Jeyn o'z oilasining ahmoqligi va odobsizligi tufayli mahrum bo'lgani haqidagi fikr qanchalik og'ir edi!

paras.en: When to these recollections was added the development of Wickham's character, it may be easily believed that the happy spirits which had seldom been depressed before, were now so much affected as to make it almost impossible for her to appear tolerably cheerful.
paras.uz: Bu xotiralarga Uikhem xarakterining ochilishi qo'shilganda, ilgari kamdan-kam tushkunlikka tushgan baxtli kayfiyati endi shunchalik ta'sirlanganini osongina ishonish mumkinki, unga ozgina bo'lsa ham quvnoq ko'rinish deyarli imkonsiz edi.

paras.en: Their engagements at Rosings were as frequent during the last week of her stay as they had been at first. The very last evening was spent there; and her ladyship again inquired minutely into the particulars of their journey, gave them directions as to the best method of packing, and was so urgent on the necessity of placing gowns in the only right way, that Maria thought herself obliged, on her return, to undo all the work of the morning, and pack her trunk afresh.
paras.uz: Uning qolishining so'nggi haftasida Rozingsdagi uchrashuvlar dastlabki paytdagidek tez-tez edi. Eng oxirgi oqshom u yerda o'tkazildi; janoblari yana safarlarining tafsilotlarini batafsil so'radi, ularga yuklarni joylashning eng yaxshi usuli bo'yicha ko'rsatmalar berdi va ko'ylaklarni yagona to'g'ri usulda joylash zarurligini shunchalik qistadiki, Mariya qaytgach, ertalabki barcha ishni buzib, sandig'ini qaytadan joylashga majbur deb hisobladi.

paras.en: When they parted, Lady Catherine, with great condescension, wished them a good journey, and invited them to come to Hunsford again next year; and Miss de Bourgh exerted herself so far as to curtsey and hold out her hand to both.
paras.uz: Ular ajralishganda, ledi Ketrin katta iltifot bilan ularga oq yo'l tiladi va kelasi yil yana Xansfordga kelishga taklif qildi; miss de Burg esa ikkalasiga ta'zim qilib, qo'l uzatish darajasida harakat qildi.

gloss.ex: How grievous then was the thought that, of a situation so desirable in every respect, so replete with advantage, so promising for happiness, Jane had been deprived, by the folly…
They were ignorant, idle, and vain.
When she remembered the style of his address, she was still full of indignation; but when she considered how unjustly she had condemned and upbraided him, her anger was turned…
When they parted, Lady Catherine, with great condescension, wished them a good journey, and invited them to come to Hunsford again next year; and Miss de Bourgh exerted herself so…
Collins having been in waiting near the lodges, to make them his parting obeisance, was able to bring home the pleasing intelligence, of their appearing in very good health, and…
“I assure you, I feel it exceedingly,”
They were excessively sorry to go!

chapters.title: Return Home
chapters.recap_uz: Kollinz Elizabetni kuzatib qo'yadi va o'z baxtini maqtaydi. Elizabet Londonda Jeynni olib, uyga qaytishga tayyorlanadi.

paras.en: On Saturday morning Elizabeth and Mr. Collins met for breakfast a few minutes before the others appeared; and he took the opportunity of paying the parting civilities which he deemed indispensably necessary.
paras.uz: Shanba kuni ertalab Elizabet va janob Kollinz boshqalar paydo bo'lishidan bir necha daqiqa oldin nonushtada uchrashishdi; u bu imkoniyatdan foydalanib, mutlaqo zarur deb hisoblagan xayrlashish xushmuomalaliklarini ado etdi.

paras.en: “I know not, Miss Elizabeth,” said he, “whether Mrs. Collins has yet expressed her sense of your kindness in coming to us; but I am very certain you will not leave the house without receiving her thanks for it. The favour of your company has been much felt, I assure you. We know how little there is to tempt anyone to our humble abode. Our plain manner of living, our small rooms and few domestics, and the little we see of the world, must make Hunsford extremely dull to a young lady like yourself; but I hope you will believe us grateful for the condescension, and that we have done everything in our power to prevent your spending your time unpleasantly.”
paras.uz: «Bilmayman, miss Elizabet, — dedi u, — missis Kollinz bizga kelgan mehribonligingiz uchun minnatdorligini allaqachon bildirdimi, yo'qmi; lekin ishonchim komilki, siz undan bu uchun rahmat olmasdan uydan ketmaysiz. Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, davrangizning iltifoti juda his qilindi. Kamtarona maskanimizga hech kimni jalb qiladigan narsa qanchalik kamligini bilamiz. Oddiy turmush tarzimiz, kichik xonalarimiz va oz sonli xizmatkorlarimiz, dunyodan kam ko'rishimiz Xansfordni sizdek yosh xonim uchun nihoyatda zerikarli qilsa kerak; lekin umid qilamanki, iltifotingiz uchun minnatdor ekanimizga va vaqtingizni yoqimsiz o'tkazmasligingiz uchun qo'limizdan kelgan hamma narsani qilganimizga ishonasiz».

paras.en: Elizabeth was eager with her thanks and assurances of happiness. She had spent six weeks with great enjoyment; and the pleasure of being with Charlotte, and the kind attentions she had received, must make her feel the obliged. Mr. Collins was gratified, and with a more smiling solemnity replied:
paras.uz: Elizabet minnatdorchilik va baxtli bo'lganiga ishontirishda shoshildi. U olti haftani katta zavq bilan o'tkazgan edi; Sharlotta bilan bo'lish zavqi va unga ko'rsatilgan mehribon e'tiborlar uni minnatdor his qildirishi kerak edi. Janob Kollinz mamnun bo'ldi va ko'proq jilmayuvchi salobat bilan javob berdi:

paras.en: “It gives me great pleasure to hear that you have passed your time not disagreeably. We have certainly done our best; and most fortunately having it in our power to introduce you to very superior society, and, from our connection with Rosings, the frequent means of varying the humble home scene, I think we may flatter ourselves that your Hunsford visit cannot have been entirely irksome. Our situation with regard to Lady Catherine's family is indeed the sort of extraordinary advantage and blessing which few can boast. You see on what a footing we are. You see how continually we are engaged there. In truth I must acknowledge that, with all the disadvantages of this humble parsonage, I should not think anyone abiding in it an object of compassion, while they are sharers of our intimacy at Rosings.”
paras.uz: «Vaqtingizni yoqimsiz o'tkazmaganingizni eshitish menga katta zavq beradi. Biz, albatta, qo'limizdan kelganini qildik; sizni juda yuqori jamiyat bilan tanishtirish va Rozings bilan aloqamiz tufayli kamtarona uy manzarasini tez-tez o'zgartirish imkoniyatiga ega bo'lganimiz eng katta omad bo'lib, o'ylaymanki, Xansforddagi tashrifingiz butunlay zerikarli bo'lmagan, deb o'zimizni ovutishimiz mumkin. Ledi Ketrinning oilasiga nisbatan mavqeimiz haqiqatan ham kam odam maqtana oladigan g'ayrioddiy afzallik va ne'matdir. Qanday munosabatda ekanimizni ko'rib turibsiz. U yerga qanchalik doimiy taklif qilinishimizni ko'rib turibsiz. Rostini aytsam, tan olishim kerakki, bu kamtarona ruhoniy uyining barcha noqulayliklariga qaramay, Rozingsdagi yaqinligimizga sherik ekan, unda yashovchi har qanday odamni achinishga loyiq deb hisoblamayman».

paras.en: Words were insufficient for the elevation of his feelings; and he was obliged to walk about the room, while Elizabeth tried to unite civility and truth in a few short sentences.
paras.uz: So'zlar uning tuyg'ularining yuksakligi uchun yetarli emasdi; u xona bo'ylab yurishga majbur bo'ldi, Elizabet esa bir necha qisqa jumlada xushmuomalalik va haqiqatni birlashtirishga urindi.

paras.en: “You may, in fact, carry a very favourable report of us into Hertfordshire, my dear cousin. I flatter myself at least that you will be able to do so. Lady Catherine's great attentions to Mrs. Collins you have been a daily witness of; and altogether I trust it does not appear that your friend has drawn an unfortunate--but on this point it will be as well to be silent. Only let me assure you, my dear Miss Elizabeth, that I can from my heart most cordially wish you equal felicity in marriage. My dear Charlotte and I have but one mind and one way of thinking. There is in everything a most remarkable resemblance of character and ideas between us. We seem to have been designed for each other.”
paras.uz: «Aslida, aziz amakivachcham, Xertfordshirga biz haqimizda juda ijobiy xabar olib borishingiz mumkin. Hech bo'lmaganda shunday qila olishingiz bilan o'zimni ovutaman. Ledi Ketrinning missis Kollinzga ko'rsatgan katta e'tiborlariga siz har kuni guvoh bo'ldingiz; umuman olganda ishonamanki, dugonangiz omadsiz... lekin bu masalada jim turganim ma'qul. Faqat sizni ishontirishga ruxsat bering, aziz miss Elizabet, men chin dildan sizga nikohda xuddi shunday baxt tilay olaman. Aziz Sharlottam va menda faqat bitta fikr va bitta fikrlash tarzi bor. Hamma narsada bizning xarakterimiz va g'oyalarimiz o'rtasida eng ajoyib o'xshashlik bor. Biz bir-birimiz uchun yaratilganga o'xshaymiz».

paras.en: Elizabeth could safely say that it was a great happiness where that was the case, and with equal sincerity could add, that she firmly believed and rejoiced in his domestic comforts. She was not sorry, however, to have the recital of them interrupted by the lady from whom they sprang. Poor Charlotte! it was melancholy to leave her to such society! But she had chosen it with her eyes open; and though evidently regretting that her visitors were to go, she did not seem to ask for compassion. Her home and her housekeeping, her parish and her poultry, and all their dependent concerns, had not yet lost their charms.
paras.uz: Elizabet ishonch bilan bunday bo'lgan joyda bu katta baxt ekanini ayta olardi va xuddi shunday samimiyat bilan uning oilaviy qulayliklariga qat'iy ishonishini va ulardan xursand ekanini qo'shib qo'yishi mumkin edi. Biroq ular haqidagi hikoyani ularning manbai bo'lgan xonim bo'lganidan afsuslanmadi. Bechora Sharlotta! Uni bunday davrada qoldirish qayg'uli edi! Lekin u buni ko'zlari ochiq holda tanlagan edi; mehmonlari ketayotganidan afsuslanayotgani aniq bo'lsa ham, u hamdardlik so'rayotganga o'xshamasdi. Uning uyi va uy xo'jaligi, qavmi va parrandalari va ularga bog'liq barcha ishlar hali jozibasini yo'qotmagan edi.

paras.en: At length the chaise arrived, the trunks were fastened on, the parcels placed within, and it was pronounced to be ready. After an affectionate parting between the friends, Elizabeth was attended to the carriage by Mr. Collins, and as they walked down the garden he was commissioning her with his best respects to all her family, not forgetting his thanks for the kindness he had received at Longbourn in the winter, and his compliments to Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner, though unknown. He then handed her in, Maria followed, and the door was on the point of being closed, when he suddenly reminded them, with some consternation, that they had hitherto forgotten to leave any message for the ladies at Rosings.
paras.uz: Nihoyat arava keldi, sandiqlar bog'landi, tugunlar ichkariga joylashtirildi va u tayyor deb e'lon qilindi. Dugonalar o'rtasidagi mehrli xayrlashuvdan keyin janob Kollinz Elizabetni aravagacha kuzatib bordi va ular bog' bo'ylab yurisharkan, u unga butun oilasiga eng yaxshi hurmatlarini, qishda Longbornda ko'rgan mehribonligi uchun minnatdorchiligini unutmasdan, notanish bo'lsa ham janob va missis Gardinerga salomlarini topshirdi. Keyin u unga aravaga chiqishga yordam berdi, Mariya ortidan chiqdi va eshik yopilay deb turganda, u to'satdan biroz sarosima bilan ular hozirgacha Rozingsdagi xonimlarga hech qanday salom qoldirishni unutganlarini eslatdi.

paras.en: “But,” he added, “you will of course wish to have your humble respects delivered to them, with your grateful thanks for their kindness to you while you have been here.”
paras.uz: «Lekin, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — siz, albatta, bu yerda bo'lganingizda sizga ko'rsatgan mehribonliklari uchun minnatdorchiligingiz bilan birga kamtarona hurmatlaringiz ularga yetkazilishini istaysiz».

paras.en: Elizabeth made no objection; the door was then allowed to be shut, and the carriage drove off.
paras.uz: Elizabet e'tiroz bildirmadi; keyin eshik yopilishiga ruxsat berildi va arava jo'nab ketdi.

paras.en: “Good gracious!” cried Maria, after a few minutes' silence, “it seems but a day or two since we first came! and yet how many things have happened!”
paras.uz: «Yo xudo! — xitob qildi Mariya bir necha daqiqalik sukutdan keyin. — Birinchi kelganimizga bir-ikki kun bo'lganga o'xshaydi! Shunga qaramay qanchadan-qancha narsalar bo'lib o'tdi!»

paras.en: “A great many indeed,” said her companion with a sigh.
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham juda ko'p», — dedi hamrohi xo'rsinib.

paras.en: “We have dined nine times at Rosings, besides drinking tea there twice! How much I shall have to tell!”
paras.uz: «Rozingsda to'qqiz marta tushlik qildik, ikki marta choy ichganimizdan tashqari! Qanchalik ko'p narsa aytib beraman!»

paras.en: Elizabeth added privately, “And how much I shall have to conceal!”
paras.uz: Elizabet ichida qo'shib qo'ydi: «Men esa qanchalik ko'p narsani yashirishim kerak!»

paras.en: Their journey was performed without much conversation, or any alarm; and within four hours of their leaving Hunsford they reached Mr. Gardiner's house, where they were to remain a few days.
paras.uz: Ularning safari ko'p suhbatsiz va hech qanday xavotirsiz o'tdi; Xansfordni tark etganlaridan to'rt soat ichida ular bir necha kun qolishlari kerak bo'lgan janob Gardinerning uyiga yetib kelishdi.

paras.en: Jane looked well, and Elizabeth had little opportunity of studying her spirits, amidst the various engagements which the kindness of her aunt had reserved for them. But Jane was to go home with her, and at Longbourn there would be leisure enough for observation.
paras.uz: Jeyn yaxshi ko'rinardi va Elizabetning xolasining mehribonligi ular uchun tayyorlab qo'ygan turli tadbirlar orasida uning kayfiyatini o'rganish uchun imkoniyati kam edi. Lekin Jeyn u bilan uyga borishi kerak edi va Longbornda kuzatish uchun yetarlicha bo'sh vaqt bo'ladi.

paras.en: It was not without an effort, meanwhile, that she could wait even for Longbourn, before she told her sister of Mr. Darcy's proposals. To know that she had the power of revealing what would so exceedingly astonish Jane, and must, at the same time, so highly gratify whatever of her own vanity she had not yet been able to reason away, was such a temptation to openness as nothing could have conquered but the state of indecision in which she remained as to the extent of what she should communicate; and her fear, if she once entered on the subject, of being hurried into repeating something of Bingley which might only grieve her sister further.
paras.uz: Bu orada, opasiga janob Darsining taklifi haqida aytib berishdan oldin hatto Longborngacha kutish ham uning uchun osonlikcha bo'lmadi. Jeynni nihoyatda hayratga soladigan va shu bilan birga o'zining hali aql bilan yengib ulgurmagan shuhratparastligini juda qondirishi kerak bo'lgan narsani ochib berish qo'lidan kelishini bilish ochiqlikka shunday vasvasa ediki, uni faqat nimani aytishi kerakligi ko'lami haqidagi qarorsizlik holati va agar bir marta mavzuga kirsa, Bingli haqida opasini yanada qayg'uga solishi mumkin bo'lgan biror narsani takrorlashga shoshib qolish qo'rquvi yengishi mumkin edi.

gloss.ex: Only let me assure you, my dear Miss Elizabeth, that I can from my heart most cordially wish you equal felicity in marriage.
Collins met for breakfast a few minutes before the others appeared; and he took the opportunity of paying the parting civilities which he deemed indispensably necessary.
Elizabeth could safely say that it was a great happiness where that was the case, and with equal sincerity could add, that she firmly believed and rejoiced in his domestic…
Our plain manner of living, our small rooms and few domestics, and the little we see of the world, must make Hunsford extremely dull to a young lady like yourself;…
Their journey was performed without much conversation, or any alarm; and within four hours of their leaving Hunsford they reached Mr.

chapters.title: Lydia's News
chapters.recap_uz: Lidiya va Ketti opalarini kutib olishadi. Polk Braytonga ketmoqda, Lidiya ham borishni orzu qiladi. Uikhem Miss Kingga uylanmabdi.

paras.en: It was the second week in May, in which the three young ladies set out together from Gracechurch Street for the town of ----, in Hertfordshire; and, as they drew near the appointed inn where Mr. Bennet's carriage was to meet them, they quickly perceived, in token of the coachman's punctuality, both Kitty and Lydia looking out of a dining-room up stairs. These two girls had been above an hour in the place, happily employed in visiting an opposite milliner, watching the sentinel on guard, and dressing a salad and cucumber.
paras.uz: May oyining ikkinchi haftasi edi, uch yosh xonim birga Greyschurch ko'chasidan Xertfordshirdagi ---- shahriga yo'lga chiqishdi; janob Bennetning aravasi ularni kutib olishi kerak bo'lgan belgilangan mehmonxonaga yaqinlashganlarida, ular aravakashning aniqligidan nishon sifatida Ketti va Lidiyaning yuqori qavatdagi ovqatxonadan qarab turganini darhol ko'rishdi. Bu ikki qiz u yerda bir soatdan ortiq bo'lgan va ro'paradagi shlyapa do'koniga kirish, qorovul askarni kuzatish va bodring bilan salat tayyorlash bilan baxtli band bo'lgan edi.

paras.en: After welcoming their sisters, they triumphantly displayed a table set out with such cold meat as an inn larder usually affords, exclaiming, “Is not this nice? Is not this an agreeable surprise?”
paras.uz: Opalarini kutib olgach, ular mehmonxona omborxonasi odatda taqdim etadigan sovuq go'sht bilan tuzalgan stolni g'olibona ko'rsatib, xitob qilishdi: «Yaxshi emasmi? Yoqimli syurpriz emasmi?»

paras.en: “And we mean to treat you all,” added Lydia, “but you must lend us the money, for we have just spent ours at the shop out there.” Then, showing her purchases--“Look here, I have bought this bonnet. I do not think it is very pretty; but I thought I might as well buy it as not. I shall pull it to pieces as soon as I get home, and see if I can make it up any better.”
paras.uz: «Biz hammangizni mehmon qilmoqchimiz, — qo'shib qo'ydi Lidiya, — lekin bizga pul qarz berishingiz kerak, chunki o'zimiznikini hozirgina anavi do'konda sarfladik». Keyin xaridlarini ko'rsatib: «Mana qarang, men bu shlyapani sotib oldim. Unchalik chiroyli deb o'ylamayman; lekin sotib olmaganimdan ko'ra olganim ma'qul deb o'yladim. Uyga borishim bilanoq uni titib tashlayman va yaxshiroq qilib tikib chiqa olamanmi, ko'raman».

paras.en: And when her sisters abused it as ugly, she added, with perfect unconcern, “Oh! but there were two or three much uglier in the shop; and when I have bought some prettier-coloured satin to trim it with fresh, I think it will be very tolerable. Besides, it will not much signify what one wears this summer, after the ----shire have left Meryton, and they are going in a fortnight.”
paras.uz: Opalari uni xunuk deb haqorat qilganida, u mutlaqo befarq qo'shib qo'ydi: «Oh! Lekin do'konda bundan ancha xunukroq ikki-uchtasi bor edi; uni yangidan bezash uchun chiroyliroq rangli atlas sotib olganimda, menimcha, juda chidasa bo'ladigan bo'ladi. Bundan tashqari, ----shir polki Meritonni tark etgandan keyin bu yoz nima kiyishning unchalik ahamiyati bo'lmaydi, ular esa ikki haftadan keyin ketishyapti».

paras.en: “Are they indeed!” cried Elizabeth, with the greatest satisfaction.
paras.uz: «Rostdanmi!» — eng katta mamnuniyat bilan xitob qildi Elizabet.

paras.en: “They are going to be encamped near Brighton; and I do so want papa to take us all there for the summer! It would be such a delicious scheme; and I dare say would hardly cost anything at all. Mamma would like to go too of all things! Only think what a miserable summer else we shall have!”
paras.uz: «Ular Brayton yaqinida lager qurishmoqchi; dadamning yozga hammamizni u yerga olib borishini juda xohlayman! Bu shunday mazali reja bo'lardi; va ishonamanki, deyarli hech narsaga tushmasdi. Oyim ham hammadan ko'ra borishni xohlaydi! O'ylab ko'ring-chi, aks holda qanday ayanchli yozimiz bo'ladi!»

paras.en: “Yes,” thought Elizabeth, “that would be a delightful scheme indeed, and completely do for us at once. Good Heaven! Brighton, and a whole campful of soldiers, to us, who have been overset already by one poor regiment of militia, and the monthly balls of Meryton!”
paras.uz: «Ha, — deb o'yladi Elizabet, — bu haqiqatan ham ajoyib reja bo'lardi va bizni birdaniga butunlay tugatardi. Yo xudo! Brayton va askarlarga to'la butun lager — bitta bechora militsiya polki va Meritonning oylik ballari bilan allaqachon ostin-ustun bo'lgan bizga!»

paras.en: “Now I have got some news for you,” said Lydia, as they sat down at table. “What do you think? It is excellent news--capital news--and about a certain person we all like!”
paras.uz: «Endi sizlarga yangiligim bor, — dedi Lidiya, ular stolga o'tirishganda. — Nima deb o'ylaysizlar? Bu ajoyib yangilik — zo'r yangilik — va hammamiz yoqtiradigan bir odam haqida!»

paras.en: Jane and Elizabeth looked at each other, and the waiter was told he need not stay. Lydia laughed, and said:
paras.uz: Jeyn va Elizabet bir-biriga qarashdi va ofitsiantga qolishi shart emasligini aytishdi. Lidiya kulib dedi:

paras.en: “Aye, that is just like your formality and discretion. You thought the waiter must not hear, as if he cared! I dare say he often hears worse things said than I am going to say. But he is an ugly fellow! I am glad he is gone. I never saw such a long chin in my life. Well, but now for my news; it is about dear Wickham; too good for the waiter, is it not? There is no danger of Wickham's marrying Mary King. There's for you! She is gone down to her uncle at Liverpool: gone to stay. Wickham is safe.”
paras.uz: «Ha, bu aynan sizlarning rasmiyatchiligingiz va ehtiyotkorligingizga o'xshaydi. Ofitsiant eshitmasligi kerak deb o'yladinglar, go'yo unga farqi bordek! Ishonamanki, u men aytmoqchi bo'lganimdan ham yomonroq gaplarni tez-tez eshitadi. Lekin u xunuk yigit! Ketganidan xursandman. Umrimda bunday uzun iyakni ko'rmaganman. Xo'sh, endi yangiligimga kelsak; bu aziz Uikhem haqida; ofitsiant uchun haddan tashqari yaxshi, shunday emasmi? Uikhemning Meri Kingga uylanish xavfi yo'q. Mana sizlarga! U Liverpuldagi tog'asinikiga ketdi: butunlay qolish uchun ketdi. Uikhem xavfsiz».

paras.en: “And Mary King is safe!” added Elizabeth; “safe from a connection imprudent as to fortune.”
paras.uz: «Meri King ham xavfsiz! — qo'shib qo'ydi Elizabet. — Boylik jihatidan ehtiyotsiz qarindoshlikdan xavfsiz».

paras.en: “She is a great fool for going away, if she liked him.”
paras.uz: «Agar uni yoqtirgan bo'lsa, ketib qolib katta ahmoqlik qildi».

paras.en: “But I hope there is no strong attachment on either side,” said Jane.
paras.uz: «Lekin umid qilamanki, hech bir tomonda kuchli mehr yo'q», — dedi Jeyn.

paras.en: “I am sure there is not on his. I will answer for it, he never cared three straws about her--who could about such a nasty little freckled thing?”
paras.uz: «Uning tomonida yo'qligiga aminman. Kafolat beraman, u unga hech qachon zarracha ham ahamiyat bermagan — bunday sepkilli, jirkanch kichkina narsaga kim ahamiyat bera olardi?»

paras.en: Elizabeth was shocked to think that, however incapable of such coarseness of expression herself, the coarseness of the sentiment was little other than her own breast had harboured and fancied liberal!
paras.uz: Elizabet o'zi bunday qo'pol ifodaga qanchalik qodir bo'lmasin, tuyg'uning qo'polligi uning o'z ko'kragida saqlagan va keng fikrlilik deb tasavvur qilgan narsadan unchalik farq qilmasligini o'ylab, dahshatga tushdi!

paras.en: As soon as all had ate, and the elder ones paid, the carriage was ordered; and after some contrivance, the whole party, with all their boxes, work-bags, and parcels, and the unwelcome addition of Kitty's and Lydia's purchases, were seated in it.
paras.uz: Hamma ovqatlanib bo'lib, kattalar haq to'lagach, arava buyurildi; ozgina hiyla-nayrangdan keyin butun davra barcha qutilari, tikuv xaltalari va tugunlari, shuningdek Ketti va Lidiyaning xaridlaridan iborat yoqimsiz qo'shimcha bilan unga joylashdi.

paras.en: “How nicely we are all crammed in,” cried Lydia. “I am glad I bought my bonnet, if it is only for the fun of having another bandbox! Well, now let us be quite comfortable and snug, and talk and laugh all the way home. And in the first place, let us hear what has happened to you all since you went away. Have you seen any pleasant men? Have you had any flirting? I was in great hopes that one of you would have got a husband before you came back. Jane will be quite an old maid soon, I declare. She is almost three-and-twenty! Lord, how ashamed I should be of not being married before three-and-twenty! My aunt Phillips wants you so to get husbands, you can't think.
paras.uz: «Hammamiz qanday chiroyli tiqilib o'tirdik! — xitob qildi Lidiya. — Shlyapani sotib olganimdan xursandman, hatto yana bir shlyapa qutisi bo'lishining qiziqligi uchun bo'lsa ham! Xo'sh, endi butunlay qulay va shinam o'tirib, uygacha gaplashib, kulib boraylik. Birinchi navbatda, ketganingizdan beri boshingizdan nimalar o'tganini eshitaylik. Birorta yoqimli erkak ko'rdinglarmi? Noz-karashma qildinglarmi? Qaytishingizdan oldin biringiz er topib olasiz deb juda umid qilgandim. Rostini aytsam, Jeyn tez orada butunlay qari qiz bo'ladi. U deyarli yigirma uchda! Yo xudo, yigirma uchdan oldin turmushga chiqmaganim uchun qanchalik uyalgan bo'lardim! Fillips xolam sizlarning er topishingizni shunchalik xohlaydiki, tasavvur ham qila olmaysizlar.

paras.en: She says Lizzy had better have taken Mr. Collins; but I do not think there would have been any fun in it. Lord! how I should like to be married before any of you; and then I would chaperon you about to all the balls. Dear me! we had such a good piece of fun the other day at Colonel Forster's. Kitty and me were to spend the day there, and Mrs. Forster promised to have a little dance in the evening; (by the bye, Mrs. Forster and me are such friends!) and so she asked the two Harringtons to come, but Harriet was ill, and so Pen was forced to come by herself; and then, what do you think we did? We dressed up Chamberlayne in woman's clothes on purpose to pass for a lady, only think what fun!
paras.uz: U Lizzi janob Kollinzni olgani yaxshiroq bo'lardi deydi; lekin menimcha, bunda hech qanday qiziqarli narsa bo'lmasdi. Yo xudo! Hammangizdan oldin turmushga chiqishni qanchalik istardim; keyin sizlarni barcha ballarga kuzatib yurardim. Voy! O'tgan kuni polkovnik Forsternikida shunday qiziqarli bo'ldi. Ketti bilan men kunni u yerda o'tkazishimiz kerak edi va missis Forster kechqurun kichik raqs kechasi qilishga va'da berdi; (aytgancha, missis Forster bilan juda do'stmiz!) shuning uchun u ikki Xarringtonni kelishga taklif qildi, lekin Harriyet kasal edi, shuning uchun Pen yolg'iz kelishga majbur bo'ldi; keyin nima qildik deb o'ylaysizlar? Chemberleynni ataylab xonimga o'xshatish uchun ayollar kiyimida kiyintirdik, o'ylab ko'ring-chi, qanday qiziq!

paras.en: Not a soul knew of it, but Colonel and Mrs. Forster, and Kitty and me, except my aunt, for we were forced to borrow one of her gowns; and you cannot imagine how well he looked! When Denny, and Wickham, and Pratt, and two or three more of the men came in, they did not know him in the least. Lord! how I laughed! and so did Mrs. Forster. I thought I should have died. And that made the men suspect something, and then they soon found out what was the matter.”
paras.uz: Polkovnik va missis Forster, Ketti va mendan boshqa hech kim bilmasdi, xolamdan tashqari, chunki uning ko'ylaklaridan birini qarz olishga majbur bo'ldik; va u qanchalik yaxshi ko'rinishini tasavvur ham qila olmaysizlar! Denni, Uikhem, Pratt va yana ikki-uch yigit kirganda, ular uni umuman tanishmadi. Yo xudo! Qanchalik kuldim! Missis Forster ham. O'lib qolaman deb o'yladim. Bu esa yigitlarni nimadandir shubhalantirdi va keyin ular tez orada nima gapligini bilib olishdi».

paras.en: With such kinds of histories of their parties and good jokes, did Lydia, assisted by Kitty's hints and additions, endeavour to amuse her companions all the way to Longbourn. Elizabeth listened as little as she could, but there was no escaping the frequent mention of Wickham's name.
paras.uz: Lidiya Kettining ishoralari va qo'shimchalari yordamida o'zlarining kechalari va yaxshi hazillari haqidagi shunday hikoyalar bilan Longborngacha butun yo'l davomida hamrohlarini xursand qilishga urindi. Elizabet iloji boricha kam tingladi, lekin Uikhem nomining tez-tez tilga olinishidan qochib bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: Their reception at home was most kind. Mrs. Bennet rejoiced to see Jane in undiminished beauty; and more than once during dinner did Mr. Bennet say voluntarily to Elizabeth:
paras.uz: Uyda ularni juda mehribonlik bilan kutib olishdi. Missis Bennet Jeynni kamaymagan go'zalligi bilan ko'rib xursand bo'ldi; tushlik paytida esa janob Bennet bir necha marta o'z ixtiyori bilan Elizabetga dedi:

paras.en: “I am glad you are come back, Lizzy.”
paras.uz: «Qaytib kelganingdan xursandman, Lizzi».

paras.en: Their party in the dining-room was large, for almost all the Lucases came to meet Maria and hear the news; and various were the subjects that occupied them: Lady Lucas was inquiring of Maria, after the welfare and poultry of her eldest daughter; Mrs. Bennet was doubly engaged, on one hand collecting an account of the present fashions from Jane, who sat some way below her, and, on the other, retailing them all to the younger Lucases; and Lydia, in a voice rather louder than any other person's, was enumerating the various pleasures of the morning to anybody who would hear her.
paras.uz: Ovqatxonadagi davra katta edi, chunki Mariyani kutib olish va yangiliklarni eshitish uchun deyarli barcha Lukaslar kelgan edi; ularni turli mavzular band qildi: ledi Lukas Mariyadan to'ng'ich qizining farovonligi va parrandalari haqida so'rardi; missis Bennet ikki tomonlama band edi, bir tomondan undan biroz pastroqda o'tirgan Jeyndan hozirgi modalar haqida ma'lumot to'plar, boshqa tomondan ularning hammasini kichik Lukaslarga yetkazardi; Lidiya esa boshqa har kimnikidan ancha balandroq ovozda ertalabgi turli zavqlarni uni eshitadigan har kimga sanab berardi.

paras.en: “Oh! Mary,” said she, “I wish you had gone with us, for we had such fun! As we went along, Kitty and I drew up the blinds, and pretended there was nobody in the coach; and I should have gone so all the way, if Kitty had not been sick; and when we got to the George, I do think we behaved very handsomely, for we treated the other three with the nicest cold luncheon in the world, and if you would have gone, we would have treated you too. And then when we came away it was such fun! I thought we never should have got into the coach. I was ready to die of laughter. And then we were so merry all the way home! we talked and laughed so loud, that anybody might have heard us ten miles off!”
paras.uz: «Oh! Meri, — dedi u, — biz bilan borganingda edi, chunki shunday qiziqarli bo'ldi! Yo'lda Ketti bilan pardalarni tushirib, aravada hech kim yo'qdek ko'rsatdik; agar Ketti ko'ngli aynimaganida, butun yo'l shunday ketgan bo'lardim; "Jorj" mehmonxonasiga yetib kelganimizda, menimcha, juda olijanob harakat qildik, chunki qolgan uchtasini dunyodagi eng zo'r sovuq tushlik bilan mehmon qildik, agar sen borganingda, seni ham mehmon qilgan bo'lardik. Keyin ketayotganimizda shunday qiziq bo'ldi! Aravaga hech qachon sig'maymiz deb o'yladim. Kulgidan o'lishga tayyor edim. Keyin uygacha shunchalik quvnoq bo'ldik! Shunchalik baland gaplashib, kuldikki, har kim o'n mil naridan ham bizni eshitishi mumkin edi!»

paras.en: To this Mary very gravely replied, “Far be it from me, my dear sister, to depreciate such pleasures! They would doubtless be congenial with the generality of female minds. But I confess they would have no charms for me--I should infinitely prefer a book.”
paras.uz: Bunga Meri juda jiddiy javob berdi: «Bunday zavqlarni kamsitish mendan yiroq, aziz singlim! Ular, shubhasiz, ko'pchilik ayol aqllariga mos keladi. Lekin tan olaman, ular men uchun hech qanday jozibaga ega bo'lmasdi — men cheksiz darajada kitobni afzal ko'rardim».

paras.en: But of this answer Lydia heard not a word. She seldom listened to anybody for more than half a minute, and never attended to Mary at all.
paras.uz: Lekin bu javobdan Lidiya bir og'iz ham eshitmadi. U kamdan-kam hollarda kimnidir yarim daqiqadan ortiq tinglardi, Meriga esa umuman e'tibor bermasdi.

paras.en: In the afternoon Lydia was urgent with the rest of the girls to walk to Meryton, and to see how everybody went on; but Elizabeth steadily opposed the scheme. It should not be said that the Miss Bennets could not be at home half a day before they were in pursuit of the officers. There was another reason too for her opposition. She dreaded seeing Mr. Wickham again, and was resolved to avoid it as long as possible. The comfort to her of the regiment's approaching removal was indeed beyond expression. In a fortnight they were to go--and once gone, she hoped there could be nothing more to plague her on his account.
paras.uz: Tushdan keyin Lidiya qolgan qizlarni Meritonga piyoda borib, hammaning ahvolini ko'rishga qistadi; lekin Elizabet bu rejaga qat'iy qarshi chiqdi. Miss Bennetlar ofitserlarni quvishdan oldin uyda yarim kun ham o'tira olmaydi, deyilmasligi kerak edi. Uning qarshiligining yana bir sababi bor edi. U janob Uikhemni yana ko'rishdan qo'rqardi va iloji boricha uzoqroq bundan qochishga qaror qilgan edi. Polkning yaqinlashib kelayotgan ketishi unga bergan taskin haqiqatan ham ta'riflab bo'lmas edi. Ikki haftadan keyin ular ketishlari kerak edi — va bir marta ketgach, u uning tufayli uni boshqa hech narsa qiynamasligiga umid qilardi.

paras.en: She had not been many hours at home before she found that the Brighton scheme, of which Lydia had given them a hint at the inn, was under frequent discussion between her parents. Elizabeth saw directly that her father had not the smallest intention of yielding; but his answers were at the same time so vague and equivocal, that her mother, though often disheartened, had never yet despaired of succeeding at last.
paras.uz: U uyda ko'p soat bo'lmasdanoq, Lidiya mehmonxonada ishora qilgan Brayton rejasi ota-onasi o'rtasida tez-tez muhokama qilinayotganini bildi. Elizabet darhol otasining zarracha ham ko'nish niyati yo'qligini ko'rdi; lekin uning javoblari shu bilan birga shunchalik noaniq va ikki ma'noli ediki, onasi tez-tez ruhi tushsa ham, oxir-oqibat muvaffaqiyatga erishishdan hali hech qachon umidini uzmagan edi.

gloss.ex: Brighton, and a whole campful of soldiers, to us, who have been overset already by one poor regiment of militia, and the monthly balls of Meryton!”
Then, showing her purchases--“Look here, I have bought this bonnet.
“But I hope there is no strong attachment on either side,”
Is not this an agreeable surprise?”
added Elizabeth; “safe from a connection imprudent as to fortune.”
Bennet's carriage was to meet them, they quickly perceived, in token of the coachman's punctuality, both Kitty and Lydia looking out of a dining-room up stairs.
Elizabeth was shocked to think that, however incapable of such coarseness of expression herself, the coarseness of the sentiment was little other than her own breast had harboured and fancied…

quiz.why_uz: Lidiya ham Braytonga borishni juda istaydi.
