chapters.title: Elizabeth Tells Jane
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet Jeynga Darsining taklifi va Uikhem haqidagi haqiqatni aytadi, lekin Bingley haqida gapirmaydi. Opa-singil Uikhemni fosh qilmaslikka qaror qilishadi.

paras.en: Elizabeth's impatience to acquaint Jane with what had happened could no longer be overcome; and at length, resolving to suppress every particular in which her sister was concerned, and preparing her to be surprised, she related to her the next morning the chief of the scene between Mr. Darcy and herself.
paras.uz: Elizabetning bo'lib o'tgan voqeani Jeynga aytishga bo'lgan sabrsizligini endi yengib bo'lmasdi; nihoyat opasiga tegishli har bir tafsilotni yashirishga qaror qilib va uni hayratga tayyorlab, u ertasi kuni ertalab unga janob Darsi bilan o'zi o'rtasidagi sahnaning asosiy qismini aytib berdi.

paras.en: Miss Bennet's astonishment was soon lessened by the strong sisterly partiality which made any admiration of Elizabeth appear perfectly natural; and all surprise was shortly lost in other feelings. She was sorry that Mr. Darcy should have delivered his sentiments in a manner so little suited to recommend them; but still more was she grieved for the unhappiness which her sister's refusal must have given him.
paras.uz: Miss Bennetning hayrati tez orada Elizabetga bo'lgan har qanday hayratni mutlaqo tabiiy ko'rsatadigan kuchli opalik tarafkashligi tufayli kamaydi; va har qanday hayron qolish tez orada boshqa tuyg'ular ichida yo'qoldi. U janob Darsi o'z tuyg'ularini ularni tavsiya qilishga bunchalik kam mos keladigan tarzda izhor qilganidan afsuslandi; lekin undan ham ko'proq singlisining rad etishi unga keltirgan baxtsizlik uchun qayg'urdi.

paras.en: “His being so sure of succeeding was wrong,” said she, “and certainly ought not to have appeared; but consider how much it must increase his disappointment!”
paras.uz: «Uning muvaffaqiyatga bunchalik ishonchi noto'g'ri edi, — dedi u, — va, albatta, ko'rinmasligi kerak edi; lekin o'ylab ko'r, bu uning hafsalasi pir bo'lishini qanchalik oshirgan bo'lsa kerak!»

paras.en: “Indeed,” replied Elizabeth, “I am heartily sorry for him; but he has other feelings, which will probably soon drive away his regard for me. You do not blame me, however, for refusing him?”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham, — javob berdi Elizabet, — men unga chin dildan achinaman; lekin unda boshqa tuyg'ular ham bor, ular, ehtimol, tez orada menga bo'lgan mehrini haydab yuboradi. Biroq meni uni rad etganim uchun ayblamaysanmi?»

paras.en: “Blame you! Oh, no.”
paras.uz: «Seni ayblaymanmi! Oh, yo'q».

paras.en: “But you blame me for having spoken so warmly of Wickham?”
paras.uz: «Lekin Uikhem haqida bunchalik qizg'in gapirganim uchun meni ayblaysanmi?»

paras.en: “No--I do not know that you were wrong in saying what you did.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q — aytgan gaplaringda noto'g'ri bo'lganingni bilmayman».

paras.en: “But you will know it, when I tell you what happened the very next day.”
paras.uz: «Lekin ertasi kuni nima bo'lganini aytib berganimda, bilib olasan».

paras.en: She then spoke of the letter, repeating the whole of its contents as far as they concerned George Wickham. What a stroke was this for poor Jane! who would willingly have gone through the world without believing that so much wickedness existed in the whole race of mankind, as was here collected in one individual. Nor was Darcy's vindication, though grateful to her feelings, capable of consoling her for such discovery. Most earnestly did she labour to prove the probability of error, and seek to clear the one without involving the other.
paras.uz: Keyin u xat haqida gapirdi va uning Jorj Uikhemga tegishli bo'lgan barcha mazmunini takrorladi. Bu bechora Jeyn uchun qanday zarba edi! U butun insoniyatda bu yerda bir shaxsda to'plangan shuncha yovuzlik borligiga ishonmasdan dunyodan o'tishni mamnuniyat bilan xohlagan bo'lardi. Darsining oqlanishi ham, garchi uning tuyg'ulariga yoqimli bo'lsa ham, uni bunday kashfiyot uchun yupata olmadi. U eng jiddiy tarzda xato ehtimolini isbotlashga va birini ikkinchisini aralashtirmasdan oqlashga urindi.

paras.en: “This will not do,” said Elizabeth; “you never will be able to make both of them good for anything. Take your choice, but you must be satisfied with only one. There is but such a quantity of merit between them; just enough to make one good sort of man; and of late it has been shifting about pretty much. For my part, I am inclined to believe it all Darcy's; but you shall do as you choose.”
paras.uz: «Bu foyda bermaydi, — dedi Elizabet, — sen hech qachon ikkalasini ham biror narsaga yaroqli qila olmaysan. Tanlovingni qil, lekin faqat bittasi bilan qanoatlanishing kerak. Ular o'rtasida faqat shuncha fazilat bor; bir yaxshi odamni yaratish uchun yetarli; so'nggi paytlarda esa u ancha u yoqdan-bu yoqqa ko'chib yurdi. Men o'zim uning hammasi Darsiniki ekaniga ishonishga moyilman; lekin sen xohlaganingcha qil».

paras.en: It was some time, however, before a smile could be extorted from Jane.
paras.uz: Biroq Jeyndan tabassum chiqarib olish uchun biroz vaqt kerak bo'ldi.

paras.en: “I do not know when I have been more shocked,” said she. “Wickham so very bad! It is almost past belief. And poor Mr. Darcy! Dear Lizzy, only consider what he must have suffered. Such a disappointment! and with the knowledge of your ill opinion, too! and having to relate such a thing of his sister! It is really too distressing. I am sure you must feel it so.”
paras.uz: «Qachon bundan ko'proq hayratga tushganimni bilmayman, — dedi u. — Uikhem bunchalik yomon! Bunga ishonish deyarli imkonsiz. Bechora janob Darsi! Aziz Lizzi, o'ylab ko'r-chi, u qanchalik azob chekkan bo'lsa kerak. Shunday hafsala pirligi! Buning ustiga sening yomon fikringni bilgan holda! Va singlisi haqida shunday narsani aytib berishga majbur bo'lib! Bu haqiqatan ham juda og'ir. Ishonchim komilki, sen ham buni shunday his qilasan».

paras.en: “Oh! no, my regret and compassion are all done away by seeing you so full of both. I know you will do him such ample justice, that I am growing every moment more unconcerned and indifferent. Your profusion makes me saving; and if you lament over him much longer, my heart will be as light as a feather.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Yo'q, seni ikkalasiga to'la ko'rib, mening afsusim va hamdardligim butunlay yo'qoldi. Bilaman, sen unga shunchalik mo'l adolat ko'rsatasanki, men har lahza befarqroq va loqaydroq bo'lib boryapman. Sening saxiyliging meni tejamkor qiladi; agar u uchun yana uzoqroq nolisang, qalbim patdek yengil bo'ladi».

paras.en: “Poor Wickham! there is such an expression of goodness in his countenance! such an openness and gentleness in his manner!”
paras.uz: «Bechora Uikhem! Uning chehrasida shunday yaxshilik ifodasi bor! Muomalasida shunday ochiqlik va muloyimlik!»

paras.en: “There certainly was some great mismanagement in the education of those two young men. One has got all the goodness, and the other all the appearance of it.”
paras.uz: «Bu ikki yosh yigitning tarbiyasida, albatta, qandaydir katta xato bo'lgan. Biriga butun yaxshilik, ikkinchisiga esa uning butun ko'rinishi tushgan».

paras.en: “I never thought Mr. Darcy so deficient in the appearance of it as you used to do.”
paras.uz: «Men janob Darsini sen o'ylaganingdek yaxshilik ko'rinishidan bunchalik mahrum deb hech qachon o'ylamaganman».

paras.en: “And yet I meant to be uncommonly clever in taking so decided a dislike to him, without any reason. It is such a spur to one's genius, such an opening for wit, to have a dislike of that kind. One may be continually abusive without saying anything just; but one cannot always be laughing at a man without now and then stumbling on something witty.”
paras.uz: «Shunga qaramay, men unga hech qanday sababsiz bunchalik qat'iy yoqtirmaslik bildirib, g'ayrioddiy aqlli bo'lmoqchi edim. Bunday yoqtirmaslik iste'dod uchun shunday turtki, zukkolik uchun shunday imkoniyat. Hech qanday adolatli gap aytmasdan doimiy haqorat qilish mumkin; lekin erkak ustidan doim kulib, vaqti-vaqti bilan biror zukko narsaga duch kelmaslik mumkin emas».

paras.en: “Lizzy, when you first read that letter, I am sure you could not treat the matter as you do now.”
paras.uz: «Lizzi, o'sha xatni birinchi o'qiganingda, ishonchim komilki, bu masalaga hozirgidek qaray olmagansan».

paras.en: “Indeed, I could not. I was uncomfortable enough, I may say unhappy. And with no one to speak to about what I felt, no Jane to comfort me and say that I had not been so very weak and vain and nonsensical as I knew I had! Oh! how I wanted you!”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham, qaray olmadim. Juda noqulay edim, baxtsiz edim desam ham bo'ladi. Buning ustiga his qilganlarim haqida gaplashadigan hech kim yo'q edi, meni yupatib, o'zim bilganimdek unchalik zaif, shuhratparast va bema'ni bo'lmaganimni aytadigan Jeyn yo'q edi! Oh! Seni qanchalik sog'indim!»

paras.en: “How unfortunate that you should have used such very strong expressions in speaking of Wickham to Mr. Darcy, for now they do appear wholly undeserved.”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsiga Uikhem haqida gapirganda bunchalik kuchli iboralar ishlatganing qanchalik omadsizlik, chunki endi ular butunlay noloyiq ko'rinadi».

paras.en: “Certainly. But the misfortune of speaking with bitterness is a most natural consequence of the prejudices I had been encouraging. There is one point on which I want your advice. I want to be told whether I ought, or ought not, to make our acquaintances in general understand Wickham's character.”
paras.uz: «Albatta. Lekin achchiq gapirish baxtsizligi men rag'batlantirib kelgan xurofotlarning eng tabiiy oqibati. Bir masalada maslahatingni xohlayman. Tanishlarimizga umuman Uikhemning xarakterini tushuntirishim kerakmi yoki yo'qmi, shuni aytishingni xohlayman».

paras.en: Miss Bennet paused a little, and then replied, “Surely there can be no occasion for exposing him so dreadfully. What is your opinion?”
paras.uz: Miss Bennet biroz to'xtab, keyin javob berdi: «Albatta, uni bunchalik dahshatli fosh qilishga hech qanday sabab bo'lishi mumkin emas. Sening fikring qanday?»

paras.en: “That it ought not to be attempted. Mr. Darcy has not authorised me to make his communication public. On the contrary, every particular relative to his sister was meant to be kept as much as possible to myself; and if I endeavour to undeceive people as to the rest of his conduct, who will believe me? The general prejudice against Mr. Darcy is so violent, that it would be the death of half the good people in Meryton to attempt to place him in an amiable light. I am not equal to it. Wickham will soon be gone; and therefore it will not signify to anyone here what he really is. Some time hence it will be all found out, and then we may laugh at their stupidity in not knowing it before. At present I will say nothing about it.”
paras.uz: «Bunga urinmaslik kerak. Janob Darsi menga uning xabarini ommaga oshkor qilishga ruxsat bermagan. Aksincha, singlisiga oid har bir tafsilot iloji boricha faqat menda qolishi mo'ljallangan edi; agar men odamlarni uning qolgan xatti-harakati haqida aldanishdan qutqarishga urinsam, menga kim ishonadi? Janob Darsiga qarshi umumiy xurofot shunchalik kuchliki, uni yoqimli tarzda ko'rsatishga urinish Meritondagi yaxshi odamlarning yarmining o'limiga sabab bo'lardi. Men bunga qodir emasman. Uikhem tez orada ketadi; shuning uchun uning aslida kim ekanligi bu yerdagi hech kim uchun ahamiyatga ega bo'lmaydi. Birozdan keyin hammasi oshkor bo'ladi, shunda biz ularning buni avval bilmaganlik ahmoqligiga kulishimiz mumkin. Hozircha bu haqda hech narsa demayman».

paras.en: “You are quite right. To have his errors made public might ruin him for ever. He is now, perhaps, sorry for what he has done, and anxious to re-establish a character. We must not make him desperate.”
paras.uz: «Sen mutlaqo haqsan. Uning xatolarini ommaga oshkor qilish uni abadiy barbod qilishi mumkin. Ehtimol, u hozir qilgan ishidan afsuslanayotgandir va obro'sini qayta tiklashga intilayotgandir. Biz uni umidsizlikka solmasligimiz kerak».

paras.en: The tumult of Elizabeth's mind was allayed by this conversation. She had got rid of two of the secrets which had weighed on her for a fortnight, and was certain of a willing listener in Jane, whenever she might wish to talk again of either. But there was still something lurking behind, of which prudence forbade the disclosure. She dared not relate the other half of Mr. Darcy's letter, nor explain to her sister how sincerely she had been valued by her friend. Here was knowledge in which no one could partake; and she was sensible that nothing less than a perfect understanding between the parties could justify her in throwing off this last encumbrance of mystery. “And then,” said she, “if that very improbable event should ever take place, I shall merely be able to tell what Bingley may tell in a much more agreeable manner himself. The liberty of communication cannot be mine till it has lost all its value!”
paras.uz: Bu suhbat Elizabetning qalbidagi to'polonni tinchitdi. U ikki hafta davomida uni ezib kelgan ikki sirdan qutulgan edi va qachon ulardan biri haqida yana gaplashishni istasa, Jeynda tayyor tinglovchi borligiga amin edi. Lekin hali ham orqada yashiringan bir narsa bor edi, uni oshkor qilishni oqilonalik man etardi. U janob Darsi xatining ikkinchi yarmini aytib berishga yoki opasiga uni uning do'sti qanchalik samimiy qadrlaganini tushuntirishga jur'at eta olmadi. Bu hech kim baham ko'ra olmaydigan bilim edi; va u tomonlar o'rtasidagi to'liq kelishuvdan kam bo'lmagan narsa uni sirning bu oxirgi yukidan qutulishga oqlay olishini his qildi. «Shunda, — dedi u, — agar o'sha juda ehtimoldan yiroq voqea qachondir sodir bo'lsa, men faqat Binglining o'zi ancha yoqimliroq tarzda ayta oladigan narsani aytib bera olaman. Xabar berish erkinligi barcha qadrini yo'qotmaguncha meniki bo'la olmaydi!»

paras.en: She was now, on being settled at home, at leisure to observe the real state of her sister's spirits. Jane was not happy. She still cherished a very tender affection for Bingley. Having never even fancied herself in love before, her regard had all the warmth of first attachment, and, from her age and disposition, greater steadiness than most first attachments often boast; and so fervently did she value his remembrance, and prefer him to every other man, that all her good sense, and all her attention to the feelings of her friends, were requisite to check the indulgence of those regrets which must have been injurious to her own health and their tranquillity.
paras.uz: Endi uyda joylashgach, u opasining kayfiyatining haqiqiy holatini kuzatishga vaqt topdi. Jeyn baxtli emasdi. U hali ham Binglige juda nozik mehr saqlardi. Ilgari hech qachon o'zini oshiq deb tasavvur ham qilmagani uchun, uning mehri birinchi muhabbatning butun iliqligiga va yoshi hamda fe'li tufayli ko'pchilik birinchi muhabbatlar maqtana oladiganidan kattaroq barqarorlikka ega edi; u uning xotirasini shunchalik qizg'in qadrlardi va uni boshqa har qanday erkakdan shunchalik afzal ko'rardiki, o'z sog'lig'iga va do'stlarining osoyishtaligiga zarar yetkazishi muqarrar bo'lgan afsuslarga berilishni to'xtatish uchun uning butun sog'lom aqli va do'stlarining tuyg'ulariga bo'lgan butun e'tibori kerak edi.

paras.en: “Well, Lizzy,” said Mrs. Bennet one day, “what is your opinion now of this sad business of Jane's? For my part, I am determined never to speak of it again to anybody. I told my sister Phillips so the other day. But I cannot find out that Jane saw anything of him in London. Well, he is a very undeserving young man--and I do not suppose there's the least chance in the world of her ever getting him now. There is no talk of his coming to Netherfield again in the summer; and I have inquired of everybody, too, who is likely to know.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, Lizzi, — dedi bir kuni missis Bennet, — Jeynning bu qayg'uli ishi haqida endi qanday fikrdasan? Men o'zim bu haqda boshqa hech kimga hech qachon gapirmaslikka qaror qildim. O'tgan kuni opam Fillipsga shunday dedim. Lekin Jeyn Londonda uni ko'rganini bila olmayapman. Xo'sh, u juda noloyiq yosh yigit — va endi uning uni olishiga dunyoda zarracha imkoniyat borligiga ishonmayman. Uning yozda yana Nezerfildga kelishi haqida hech gap yo'q; buni bilishi mumkin bo'lgan hammadan so'radim ham».

paras.en: “I do not believe he will ever live at Netherfield any more.”
paras.uz: «U Nezerfildda boshqa hech qachon yashaydi deb o'ylamayman».

paras.en: “Oh well! it is just as he chooses. Nobody wants him to come. Though I shall always say he used my daughter extremely ill; and if I was her, I would not have put up with it. Well, my comfort is, I am sure Jane will die of a broken heart; and then he will be sorry for what he has done.”
paras.uz: «Mayli! Bu uning xohishi. Hech kim uning kelishini istamaydi. Garchi men doim u qizimga nihoyatda yomon munosabatda bo'lgan deyman; agar men uning o'rnida bo'lganimda, bunga chidamagan bo'lardim. Xo'sh, mening taskinim shuki, ishonchim komilki, Jeyn singan yurakdan o'ladi; shunda u qilgan ishidan afsuslanadi».

paras.en: But as Elizabeth could not receive comfort from any such expectation, she made no answer.
paras.uz: Lekin Elizabet bunday kutishdan hech qanday taskin ola olmagani uchun javob bermadi.

paras.en: “Well, Lizzy,” continued her mother, soon afterwards, “and so the Collinses live very comfortable, do they? Well, well, I only hope it will last. And what sort of table do they keep? Charlotte is an excellent manager, I dare say. If she is half as sharp as her mother, she is saving enough. There is nothing extravagant in their housekeeping, I dare say.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, Lizzi, — davom etdi onasi ko'p o'tmay, — demak, Kollinzlar juda qulay yashashadi, shundaymi? Mayli, mayli, faqat bu davom etishiga umid qilaman. Ular qanday dasturxon tutishadi? Ishonamanki, Sharlotta ajoyib bekadir. Agar u onasining yarmicha ziyrak bo'lsa, yetarlicha tejamkor. Ishonamanki, ularning uy xo'jaligida hech qanday isrofgarchilik yo'q».

paras.en: “No, nothing at all.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, umuman yo'q».

paras.en: “A great deal of good management, depend upon it. Yes, yes, they will take care not to outrun their income. They will never be distressed for money. Well, much good may it do them! And so, I suppose, they often talk of having Longbourn when your father is dead. They look upon it as quite their own, I dare say, whenever that happens.”
paras.uz: «Juda yaxshi tejamkorlik, ishonavering. Ha, ha, ular daromadidan oshib ketmaslikka ehtiyot bo'lishadi. Ular hech qachon pulga muhtoj bo'lmaydi. Mayli, ko'p foydasi tegsin! Demak, menimcha, ular otang vafot etgach, Longbornga ega bo'lish haqida tez-tez gaplashishadi. Ishonamanki, bu qachon sodir bo'lmasin, uni butunlay o'zlariniki deb hisoblashadi».

paras.en: “It was a subject which they could not mention before me.”
paras.uz: «Bu ular mening oldimda tilga ola olmaydigan mavzu edi».

paras.en: “No; it would have been strange if they had; but I make no doubt they often talk of it between themselves. Well, if they can be easy with an estate that is not lawfully their own, so much the better. I should be ashamed of having one that was only entailed on me.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q; agar tilga olishganida g'alati bo'lardi; lekin shubham yo'qki, ular bu haqda o'zaro tez-tez gaplashishadi. Mayli, agar ular qonuniy ravishda o'zlariniki bo'lmagan mulk bilan xotirjam bo'la olsalar, shunisi yaxshi. Men faqat meros cheklovi bilan menga o'tgan mulkka ega bo'lishdan uyalgan bo'lardim».

said she, “and certainly ought not to have appeared; but consider how much it must increase his disappointment!”

quiz.q: What do Jane and Elizabeth decide about Wickham?
o: To report him to the police
quiz.why_uz: Bu qaror keyin Lidiya voqeasida og'ir oqibatga olib keladi.

quiz.q: What does Elizabeth NOT tell Jane?
o: About Bingley's role and Darcy's part in it
quiz.why_uz: U opasini yana xafa qilishni istamaydi.

chapters.title: Lydia Goes to Brighton
chapters.recap_uz: Lidiyani polkovnik Forsterning xotini Braytonga taklif qiladi. Elizabet otasini uni qo'yib yubormaslikka ko'ndirmoqchi bo'ladi, lekin janob Bennet tinchlik uchun rozi bo'ladi.

paras.en: The first week of their return was soon gone. The second began. It was the last of the regiment's stay in Meryton, and all the young ladies in the neighbourhood were drooping apace. The dejection was almost universal. The elder Miss Bennets alone were still able to eat, drink, and sleep, and pursue the usual course of their employments. Very frequently were they reproached for this insensibility by Kitty and Lydia, whose own misery was extreme, and who could not comprehend such hard-heartedness in any of the family.
paras.uz: Qaytganlarining birinchi haftasi tez o'tib ketdi. Ikkinchisi boshlandi. Bu polkning Meritonda turishining oxirgi haftasi edi va mahalladagi barcha yosh xonimlar tez so'lib borardi. Tushkunlik deyarli umumiy edi. Faqat katta miss Bennetlar hali ham yeb-icha, uxlay va odatiy mashg'ulotlarini davom ettira olardi. Ketti va Lidiya ularni bu befarqlik uchun juda tez-tez koyishardi, ularning o'z iztiroblari haddan oshgan edi va oiladagi har kimda bunday bag'ritoshlikni tushuna olmasdilar.

paras.en: “Good Heaven! what is to become of us? What are we to do?” would they often exclaim in the bitterness of woe. “How can you be smiling so, Lizzy?”
paras.uz: «Yo xudo! Bizga nima bo'ladi? Nima qilamiz?» — deb ular ko'pincha qayg'u achchiqligida xitob qilishardi. — «Qanday qilib bunchalik jilmaya olasan, Lizzi?»

paras.en: Their affectionate mother shared all their grief; she remembered what she had herself endured on a similar occasion, five-and-twenty years ago.
paras.uz: Ularning mehribon onasi butun qayg'ularini baham ko'rardi; u yigirma besh yil oldin shunga o'xshash holatda o'zi nimalarni boshdan kechirganini eslardi.

paras.en: “I am sure,” said she, “I cried for two days together when Colonel Miller's regiment went away. I thought I should have broken my heart.”
paras.uz: «Ishonchim komilki, — dedi u, — polkovnik Millerning polki ketganda ikki kun to'xtovsiz yig'laganman. Yuragim yorilib ketadi deb o'ylagandim».

paras.en: “I am sure I shall break mine,” said Lydia.
paras.uz: «Meniki albatta yoriladi», — dedi Lidiya.

paras.en: “If one could but go to Brighton!” observed Mrs. Bennet.
paras.uz: «Qaniydi Braytonga borish mumkin bo'lsa!» — dedi missis Bennet.

paras.en: “Oh, yes!--if one could but go to Brighton! But papa is so disagreeable.”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha! — qaniydi Braytonga borish mumkin bo'lsa! Lekin dadam juda yoqimsiz».

paras.en: “A little sea-bathing would set me up forever.”
paras.uz: «Ozgina dengizda cho'milish meni butunlay oyoqqa turg'izardi».

paras.en: “And my aunt Phillips is sure it would do me a great deal of good,” added Kitty.
paras.uz: «Fillips xolam esa bu menga juda foydali bo'lishiga ishonadi», — qo'shib qo'ydi Ketti.

paras.en: Such were the kind of lamentations resounding perpetually through Longbourn House. Elizabeth tried to be diverted by them; but all sense of pleasure was lost in shame. She felt anew the justice of Mr. Darcy's objections; and never had she been so much disposed to pardon his interference in the views of his friend.
paras.uz: Longborn uyida to'xtovsiz shunday nolalar yangrardi. Elizabet ulardan ko'ngil ochishga urindi; lekin har qanday zavq hissi uyat ichida yo'qoldi. U janob Darsining e'tirozlari adolatli ekanini yana his qildi va uning do'stining rejalariga aralashuvini kechirishga hech qachon bunchalik moyil bo'lmagan edi.

paras.en: But the gloom of Lydia's prospect was shortly cleared away; for she received an invitation from Mrs. Forster, the wife of the colonel of the regiment, to accompany her to Brighton. This invaluable friend was a very young woman, and very lately married. A resemblance in good humour and good spirits had recommended her and Lydia to each other, and out of their three months' acquaintance they had been intimate two.
paras.uz: Lekin Lidiyaning istiqbolidagi g'amginlik tez orada tarqaldi; chunki u polk polkovnigining xotini missis Forsterdan Braytonga unga hamroh bo'lish taklifini oldi. Bu bebaho do'st juda yosh va yaqinda turmushga chiqqan ayol edi. Xushfe'llik va quvnoqlikdagi o'xshashlik uni va Lidiyani bir-biriga yoqtirgan edi va uch oylik tanishliklarining ikki oyi davomida ular yaqin do'st edilar.

paras.en: The rapture of Lydia on this occasion, her adoration of Mrs. Forster, the delight of Mrs. Bennet, and the mortification of Kitty, are scarcely to be described. Wholly inattentive to her sister's feelings, Lydia flew about the house in restless ecstasy, calling for everyone's congratulations, and laughing and talking with more violence than ever; whilst the luckless Kitty continued in the parlour repined at her fate in terms as unreasonable as her accent was peevish.
paras.uz: Bu munosabat bilan Lidiyaning hayajoni, uning missis Forsterga sig'inishi, missis Bennetning zavqi va Kettining xo'rlanishini zo'rg'a ta'riflash mumkin. Singlisining tuyg'ulariga butunlay e'tiborsiz Lidiya tinimsiz zavq ichida uy bo'ylab uchib yurar, hammadan tabrik talab qilar, har qachongidan ham shiddatliroq kulib gapirardi; omadsiz Ketti esa mehmonxonada qolib, taqdiridan ohangi qanchalik jizzaki bo'lsa, shunchalik asossiz so'zlar bilan nolirdi.

paras.en: “I cannot see why Mrs. Forster should not ask me as well as Lydia,” said she, “Though I am not her particular friend. I have just as much right to be asked as she has, and more too, for I am two years older.”
paras.uz: «Nega missis Forster meni ham Lidiya kabi taklif qilmasligini tushunmayman, — dedi u, — garchi men uning alohida dugonasi bo'lmasam ham. Menda ham taklif qilinishga u kabi haqqim bor, hatto ko'proq, chunki men undan ikki yosh kattaman».

paras.en: In vain did Elizabeth attempt to make her reasonable, and Jane to make her resigned. As for Elizabeth herself, this invitation was so far from exciting in her the same feelings as in her mother and Lydia, that she considered it as the death warrant of all possibility of common sense for the latter; and detestable as such a step must make her were it known, she could not help secretly advising her father not to let her go. She represented to him all the improprieties of Lydia's general behaviour, the little advantage she could derive from the friendship of such a woman as Mrs. Forster, and the probability of her being yet more imprudent with such a companion at Brighton, where the temptations must be greater than at home. He heard her attentively, and then said:
paras.uz: Elizabet uni aqlga keltirishga, Jeyn esa uni taslim bo'lishga ko'ndirishga behuda urinishdi. Elizabetning o'ziga kelsak, bu taklif unda onasi va Lidiyadagi kabi tuyg'ular uyg'otishdan shunchalik yiroq ediki, u buni Lidiya uchun sog'lom aqlning har qanday imkoniyatiga o'lim hukmi deb hisobladi; va agar ma'lum bo'lsa, bunday qadam uni qanchalik jirkanch qilishi kerak bo'lsa ham, u yashirincha otasiga uni qo'yib yubormaslikni maslahat bermay qololmadi. U unga Lidiyaning umumiy xatti-harakatidagi barcha nomunosibliklarni, missis Forsterdek ayolning do'stligidan u oladigan kam foydani va bunday hamroh bilan Braytonda, vasvasalar uydagidan kattaroq bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan joyda, uning yanada ehtiyotsizroq bo'lishi ehtimolini tushuntirdi. U uni diqqat bilan tingladi, keyin dedi:

paras.en: “Lydia will never be easy until she has exposed herself in some public place or other, and we can never expect her to do it with so little expense or inconvenience to her family as under the present circumstances.”
paras.uz: «Lidiya biror jamoat joyida o'zini sharmanda qilmaguncha hech qachon tinchimaydi va biz undan buni hozirgi sharoitdagidek oilasiga bunchalik kam xarajat va noqulaylik bilan qilishini hech qachon kuta olmaymiz».

paras.en: “If you were aware,” said Elizabeth, “of the very great disadvantage to us all which must arise from the public notice of Lydia's unguarded and imprudent manner--nay, which has already arisen from it, I am sure you would judge differently in the affair.”
paras.uz: «Agar siz, — dedi Elizabet, — Lidiyaning ehtiyotsiz va beparvo muomalasining ommaga ma'lum bo'lishidan hammamiz uchun kelib chiqishi kerak bo'lgan — yo'q, allaqachon kelib chiqqan — juda katta zarar haqida bilganingizda, ishonchim komilki, bu ishda boshqacha hukm chiqargan bo'lardingiz».

paras.en: “Already arisen?” repeated Mr. Bennet. “What, has she frightened away some of your lovers? Poor little Lizzy! But do not be cast down. Such squeamish youths as cannot bear to be connected with a little absurdity are not worth a regret. Come, let me see the list of pitiful fellows who have been kept aloof by Lydia's folly.”
paras.uz: «Allaqachon kelib chiqqanmi? — takrorladi janob Bennet. — Nima, u oshiqlaringdan ba'zilarini qo'rqitib yubordimi? Bechora kichkina Lizzi! Lekin ruhing tushmasin. Ozgina bema'nilik bilan bog'liq bo'lishga chiday olmaydigan bunday injiq yigitlar afsuslanishga arzimaydi. Qani, Lidiyaning ahmoqligi tufayli uzoqda turgan ayanchli yigitlar ro'yxatini ko'ray».

paras.en: “Indeed you are mistaken. I have no such injuries to resent. It is not of particular, but of general evils, which I am now complaining. Our importance, our respectability in the world must be affected by the wild volatility, the assurance and disdain of all restraint which mark Lydia's character. Excuse me, for I must speak plainly. If you, my dear father, will not take the trouble of checking her exuberant spirits, and of teaching her that her present pursuits are not to be the business of her life, she will soon be beyond the reach of amendment.
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham adashyapsiz. Menda ranjiydigan bunday zararlar yo'q. Men hozir xususiy emas, umumiy yomonliklardan shikoyat qilyapman. Bizning ahamiyatimiz, dunyodagi obro'yimiz Lidiyaning xarakterini belgilovchi yovvoyi yengiltaklik, surbetlik va har qanday cheklovni mensimaslik tufayli zarar ko'rishi muqarrar. Kechiring, chunki ochiq gapirishim kerak. Agar siz, aziz otajon, uning haddan oshgan jo'shqinligini jilovlash va unga hozirgi mashg'ulotlari hayotining ishi bo'lmasligi kerakligini o'rgatish zahmatini chekmasangiz, u tez orada tuzatish imkoniyatidan tashqarida bo'ladi.

paras.en: Her character will be fixed, and she will, at sixteen, be the most determined flirt that ever made herself or her family ridiculous; a flirt, too, in the worst and meanest degree of flirtation; without any attraction beyond youth and a tolerable person; and, from the ignorance and emptiness of her mind, wholly unable to ward off any portion of that universal contempt which her rage for admiration will excite. In this danger Kitty also is comprehended. She will follow wherever Lydia leads. Vain, ignorant, idle, and absolutely uncontrolled! Oh! my dear father, can you suppose it possible that they will not be censured and despised wherever they are known, and that their sisters will not be often involved in the disgrace?”
paras.uz: Uning xarakteri qotib qoladi va u o'n olti yoshida o'zini yoki oilasini kulgi qilgan eng qat'iy noz-karashmachi bo'ladi; buning ustiga noz-karashmaning eng yomon va eng past darajasidagi noz-karashmachi; yoshlik va chidasa bo'ladigan qiyofadan boshqa hech qanday jozibasiz; va aqlining johilligi hamda bo'shligi tufayli uning hayratga bo'lgan telba intilishi uyg'otadigan umumiy nafratning hech bir qismini qaytara olmaydigan. Bu xavfga Ketti ham kiradi. U Lidiya qayerga boshlasa, o'sha yerga ergashadi. Manman, johil, dangasa va mutlaqo nazoratsiz! Oh! Aziz otajon, ular qayerda tanilmasin, qoralanmasligi va nafratlanilmasligi, opa-singillari esa tez-tez sharmandalikka aralashtirilmasligi mumkin deb o'ylay olasizmi?»

paras.en: Mr. Bennet saw that her whole heart was in the subject, and affectionately taking her hand said in reply:
paras.uz: Janob Bennet uning butun qalbi bu mavzuda ekanini ko'rdi va mehr bilan uning qo'lini ushlab, javob berdi:

paras.en: “Do not make yourself uneasy, my love. Wherever you and Jane are known you must be respected and valued; and you will not appear to less advantage for having a couple of--or I may say, three--very silly sisters. We shall have no peace at Longbourn if Lydia does not go to Brighton. Let her go, then. Colonel Forster is a sensible man, and will keep her out of any real mischief; and she is luckily too poor to be an object of prey to anybody. At Brighton she will be of less importance even as a common flirt than she has been here. The officers will find women better worth their notice. Let us hope, therefore, that her being there may teach her her own insignificance. At any rate, she cannot grow many degrees worse, without authorising us to lock her up for the rest of her life.”
paras.uz: «Xavotirlanma, azizim. Sen va Jeyn qayerda tanilsangiz ham, sizlarni hurmat qilishlari va qadrlashlari muqarrar; bir juft — yoki aytishim mumkin, uchta — juda ahmoq opa-singilga ega bo'lganingiz uchun kamroq afzal ko'rinmaysizlar. Agar Lidiya Braytonga bormasa, Longbornda tinchligimiz bo'lmaydi. Shunday ekan, borsin. Polkovnik Forster aqlli odam va uni har qanday haqiqiy ko'ngilsizlikdan saqlaydi; u esa baxtiga hech kimga o'lja bo'lish uchun haddan tashqari kambag'al. Braytonda u hatto oddiy noz-karashmachi sifatida ham bu yerdagidan kamroq ahamiyatga ega bo'ladi. Ofitserlar e'tiborlariga ko'proq arziydigan ayollarni topishadi. Shuning uchun umid qilaylikki, u yerda bo'lishi unga o'zining ahamiyatsizligini o'rgatadi. Har holda, u bizga uni umrining oxirigacha qamab qo'yishga ruxsat beradigan darajada ko'p yomonlashmaydi».

paras.en: With this answer Elizabeth was forced to be content; but her own opinion continued the same, and she left him disappointed and sorry. It was not in her nature, however, to increase her vexations by dwelling on them. She was confident of having performed her duty, and to fret over unavoidable evils, or augment them by anxiety, was no part of her disposition.
paras.uz: Elizabet bu javob bilan qanoatlanishga majbur bo'ldi; lekin uning fikri o'zgarmadi va u undan hafsalasi pir bo'lgan va afsuslangan holda chiqib ketdi. Biroq ularga to'xtalib g'ashliklarini oshirish uning tabiatida yo'q edi. U burchini bajarganiga ishonardi, muqarrar yomonliklar ustida kuyinish yoki tashvish bilan ularni ko'paytirish esa uning fe'lida yo'q edi.

paras.en: Had Lydia and her mother known the substance of her conference with her father, their indignation would hardly have found expression in their united volubility. In Lydia's imagination, a visit to Brighton comprised every possibility of earthly happiness. She saw, with the creative eye of fancy, the streets of that gay bathing-place covered with officers. She saw herself the object of attention, to tens and to scores of them at present unknown. She saw all the glories of the camp--its tents stretched forth in beauteous uniformity of lines, crowded with the young and the gay, and dazzling with scarlet; and, to complete the view, she saw herself seated beneath a tent, tenderly flirting with at least six officers at once.
paras.uz: Agar Lidiya va onasi uning otasi bilan suhbatining mazmunini bilganlarida, ularning g'azabi birgalikdagi vaysaqiligida ham zo'rg'a ifoda topgan bo'lardi. Lidiyaning tasavvurida Braytonga tashrif yerdagi baxtning barcha imkoniyatlarini o'z ichiga olardi. U xayolning ijodkor ko'zi bilan o'sha quvnoq cho'milish joyining ko'chalarini ofitserlar bilan qoplangan holda ko'rardi. U o'zini hozircha noma'lum o'nlab va yuzlab ofitserlarning e'tibor markazida ko'rardi. U lagerning butun shon-shuhratini — go'zal bir xil qatorlar bo'ylab cho'zilgan, yosh va quvnoqlar bilan to'la, qirmizi rang bilan ko'zni qamashtiruvchi chodirlarini ko'rardi; manzarani to'ldirish uchun esa o'zini chodir ostida o'tirib, kamida oltita ofitser bilan bir vaqtda nozik noz-karashma qilayotganini ko'rardi.

paras.en: Had she known her sister sought to tear her from such prospects and such realities as these, what would have been her sensations? They could have been understood only by her mother, who might have felt nearly the same. Lydia's going to Brighton was all that consoled her for her melancholy conviction of her husband's never intending to go there himself.
paras.uz: Agar u opasi uni bunday istiqbollar va bunday haqiqatlardan ajratishga urinayotganini bilganida, qanday his qilgan bo'lardi? Ularni faqat deyarli xuddi shunday his qilishi mumkin bo'lgan onasi tushunishi mumkin edi. Lidiyaning Braytonga borishi uning erining hech qachon u yerga o'zi borishni niyat qilmasligi haqidagi qayg'uli ishonchi uchun yagona taskin edi.

paras.en: But they were entirely ignorant of what had passed; and their raptures continued, with little intermission, to the very day of Lydia's leaving home.
paras.uz: Lekin ular bo'lib o'tgan voqeadan butunlay bexabar edilar; va ularning hayajonlari Lidiyaning uydan ketish kunigacha deyarli to'xtovsiz davom etdi.

paras.en: Elizabeth was now to see Mr. Wickham for the last time. Having been frequently in company with him since her return, agitation was pretty well over; the agitations of former partiality entirely so. She had even learnt to detect, in the very gentleness which had first delighted her, an affectation and a sameness to disgust and weary. In his present behaviour to herself, moreover, she had a fresh source of displeasure, for the inclination he soon testified of renewing those intentions which had marked the early part of their acquaintance could only serve, after what had since passed, to provoke her. She lost all concern for him in finding herself thus selected as the object of such idle and frivolous gallantry; and while she steadily repressed it, could not but feel the reproof contained in his believing, that however long, and for whatever cause, his attentions had been withdrawn, her vanity would be gratified, and her preference secured at any time by their renewal.
paras.uz: Endi Elizabet janob Uikhemni oxirgi marta ko'rishi kerak edi. Qaytganidan beri u bilan tez-tez bir davrada bo'lgani uchun hayajon ancha o'tib ketgan edi; avvalgi moyillikning hayajonlari esa butunlay o'tgan edi. U hatto avval uni zavqlantirgan aynan o'sha muloyimlikda jirkantiradigan va charchatadigan soxtalik va bir xillikni payqashni o'rgangan edi. Bundan tashqari, uning hozirgi o'ziga nisbatan xatti-harakatida u yangi norozilik manbaini topdi, chunki u tez orada tanishliklarining dastlabki qismini belgilagan o'sha niyatlarni yangilashga moyilligini ko'rsatdi, bu esa o'shandan beri bo'lib o'tgan voqealardan keyin faqat uning g'ashini keltirishi mumkin edi. U o'zini bunday bekorchi va yengiltak xushomadning obyekti sifatida tanlanganini ko'rib, unga bo'lgan barcha qiziqishini yo'qotdi; va uni qat'iy ravishda bostirarkan, uning e'tiborlari qanchalik uzoq va qanday sabab bilan to'xtatilgan bo'lmasin, ularni yangilash bilan uning shuhratparastligi istalgan paytda qondiriladi va afzal ko'rishi ta'minlanadi, deb ishonishida mujassam bo'lgan haqoratni his qilmay qololmadi.

paras.en: On the very last day of the regiment's remaining at Meryton, he dined, with other of the officers, at Longbourn; and so little was Elizabeth disposed to part from him in good humour, that on his making some inquiry as to the manner in which her time had passed at Hunsford, she mentioned Colonel Fitzwilliam's and Mr. Darcy's having both spent three weeks at Rosings, and asked him, if he was acquainted with the former.
paras.uz: Polkning Meritonda qolishining eng oxirgi kuni u boshqa ofitserlar bilan Longbornda tushlik qildi; Elizabet u bilan yaxshi kayfiyatda ajralishga shunchalik kam moyil ediki, u Xansfordda vaqtini qanday o'tkazgani haqida so'raganida, u polkovnik Fitsuilyam va janob Darsining ikkalasi ham Rozingsda uch hafta o'tkazganini aytdi va undan birinchisi bilan tanishmi, deb so'radi.

paras.en: He looked surprised, displeased, alarmed; but with a moment's recollection and a returning smile, replied, that he had formerly seen him often; and, after observing that he was a very gentlemanlike man, asked her how she had liked him. Her answer was warmly in his favour. With an air of indifference he soon afterwards added:
paras.uz: U hayron, norozi, xavotirli ko'rindi; lekin bir lahzada o'zini tutib olib, yana jilmayib, avvallari uni tez-tez ko'rganini aytdi; va uning juda janoblarga xos odam ekanini aytgach, undan uni qanchalik yoqtirganini so'radi. Uning javobi qizg'in uning foydasiga edi. Befarqlik qiyofasida u ko'p o'tmay qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “How long did you say he was at Rosings?”
paras.uz: «U Rozingsda qancha bo'ldi dedingiz?»

paras.en: “Nearly three weeks.”
paras.uz: «Deyarli uch hafta».

paras.en: “And you saw him frequently?”
paras.uz: «Va siz uni tez-tez ko'rdingizmi?»

paras.en: “Yes, almost every day.”
paras.uz: «Ha, deyarli har kuni».

paras.en: “His manners are very different from his cousin's.”
paras.uz: «Uning muomalasi amakivachchasinikidan juda farq qiladi».

paras.en: “Yes, very different. But I think Mr. Darcy improves upon acquaintance.”
paras.uz: «Ha, juda farq qiladi. Lekin menimcha, janob Darsi yaqindan tanishganda yaxshilanadi».

paras.en: “Indeed!” cried Mr. Wickham with a look which did not escape her. “And pray, may I ask?--” But checking himself, he added, in a gayer tone, “Is it in address that he improves? Has he deigned to add aught of civility to his ordinary style?--for I dare not hope,” he continued in a lower and more serious tone, “that he is improved in essentials.”
paras.uz: «Rostdanmi! — xitob qildi janob Uikhem, uning nazaridan chetda qolmagan qarash bilan. — Iltimos, so'rasam bo'ladimi?..» Lekin o'zini tiyib, quvnoqroq ohangda qo'shib qo'ydi: «U muomalada yaxshilanadimi? U odatiy uslubiga biror xushmuomalalik qo'shishni o'ziga ep ko'rdimi? — chunki umid qilishga jur'at etmayman, — davom etdi u pastroq va jiddiyroq ohangda, — u mohiyatan yaxshilangan bo'lsa».

paras.en: “Oh, no!” said Elizabeth. “In essentials, I believe, he is very much what he ever was.”
paras.uz: «Oh, yo'q! — dedi Elizabet. — Mohiyatan, menimcha, u har doimgidek».

paras.en: While she spoke, Wickham looked as if scarcely knowing whether to rejoice over her words, or to distrust their meaning. There was a something in her countenance which made him listen with an apprehensive and anxious attention, while she added:
paras.uz: U gapirayotganda, Uikhem uning so'zlaridan xursand bo'lishni yoki ularning ma'nosiga ishonmaslikni zo'rg'a bilayotganday ko'rindi. Uning chehrasida shunday bir narsa bor ediki, u uni xavotirli va tashvishli e'tibor bilan tinglashga majbur qildi, u esa qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “When I said that he improved on acquaintance, I did not mean that his mind or his manners were in a state of improvement, but that, from knowing him better, his disposition was better understood.”
paras.uz: «Uni yaqindan tanishganda yaxshilanadi deganimda, uning aqli yoki muomalasi yaxshilanish holatida ekanini emas, balki uni yaxshiroq bilganim sababli fe'li yaxshiroq tushunilganini nazarda tutdim».

paras.en: Wickham's alarm now appeared in a heightened complexion and agitated look; for a few minutes he was silent, till, shaking off his embarrassment, he turned to her again, and said in the gentlest of accents:
paras.uz: Endi Uikhemning xavotiri yuzining qizarishi va hayajonli qarashida ko'rindi; u bir necha daqiqa jim turdi, keyin xijolatini yengib, yana unga o'girildi va eng muloyim ohangda dedi:

paras.en: “You, who so well know my feeling towards Mr. Darcy, will readily comprehend how sincerely I must rejoice that he is wise enough to assume even the appearance of what is right. His pride, in that direction, may be of service, if not to himself, to many others, for it must only deter him from such foul misconduct as I have suffered by. I only fear that the sort of cautiousness to which you, I imagine, have been alluding, is merely adopted on his visits to his aunt, of whose good opinion and judgement he stands much in awe. His fear of her has always operated, I know, when they were together; and a good deal is to be imputed to his wish of forwarding the match with Miss de Bourgh, which I am certain he has very much at heart.”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsiga nisbatan tuyg'ularimni juda yaxshi biladigan siz, uning hatto to'g'ri narsaning ko'rinishini qabul qilish uchun yetarlicha aqlli ekanidan qanchalik samimiy xursand bo'lishim kerakligini osongina tushunasiz. Uning g'ururi bu yo'nalishda o'zi uchun bo'lmasa ham, ko'pchilik uchun foydali bo'lishi mumkin, chunki u uni faqat men azob chekkan bunday jirkanch nojo'ya xatti-harakatdan to'xtatishi kerak. Faqat qo'rqamanki, siz, menimcha, ishora qilgan ehtiyotkorlikning bu turi faqat u yaxshi fikri va mulohazasidan juda hayiqadigan xolasiga tashriflari paytida qabul qilinadi. Bilaman, ular birga bo'lganda uning undan qo'rquvi doim ta'sir qilgan; va ko'p narsani uning miss de Burg bilan nikohni tezlashtirish istagiga bog'lash kerak, ishonchim komilki, bu uning yuragiga juda yaqin».

paras.en: Elizabeth could not repress a smile at this, but she answered only by a slight inclination of the head. She saw that he wanted to engage her on the old subject of his grievances, and she was in no humour to indulge him. The rest of the evening passed with the appearance, on his side, of usual cheerfulness, but with no further attempt to distinguish Elizabeth; and they parted at last with mutual civility, and possibly a mutual desire of never meeting again.
paras.uz: Elizabet bunga jilmayishini bosa olmadi, lekin faqat boshini biroz egish bilan javob berdi. U uning o'z dardlari haqidagi eski mavzuga uni jalb qilmoqchi ekanini ko'rdi va unga yon berish kayfiyatida emasdi. Oqshomning qolgan qismi uning tomonidan odatiy quvnoqlik qiyofasida o'tdi, lekin Elizabetni ajratib ko'rsatishga boshqa urinish bo'lmadi; va ular nihoyat o'zaro xushmuomalalik bilan va, ehtimol, boshqa hech qachon uchrashmaslik haqidagi o'zaro istak bilan ajralishdi.

paras.en: When the party broke up, Lydia returned with Mrs. Forster to Meryton, from whence they were to set out early the next morning. The separation between her and her family was rather noisy than pathetic. Kitty was the only one who shed tears; but she did weep from vexation and envy. Mrs. Bennet was diffuse in her good wishes for the felicity of her daughter, and impressive in her injunctions that she should not miss the opportunity of enjoying herself as much as possible--advice which there was every reason to believe would be well attended to; and in the clamorous happiness of Lydia herself in bidding farewell, the more gentle adieus of her sisters were uttered without being heard.
paras.uz: Davra tarqalgach, Lidiya missis Forster bilan Meritonga qaytdi, u yerdan ular ertasi kuni erta tongda yo'lga chiqishlari kerak edi. Uning oilasi bilan xayrlashuvi ta'sirli bo'lishdan ko'ra shovqinliroq bo'ldi. Ko'z yoshi to'kkan yagona odam Ketti edi; lekin u g'ashlik va hasaddan yig'ladi. Missis Bennet qizining baxti uchun yaxshi tilaklarida ko'p so'zli va iloji boricha ko'proq ko'ngil ochish imkoniyatini qo'ldan boy bermaslik haqidagi ko'rsatmalarida ta'sirli edi — bu maslahatga yaxshi amal qilinishiga ishonish uchun barcha asoslar bor edi; va Lidiyaning o'zining xayrlashuvdagi shovqinli baxtida opalarining muloyimroq xayrlashuvlari eshitilmay qoldi.

quiz.q: Why does Mr. Bennet let Lydia go?
quiz.why_uz: Bu — otaning mas'uliyatsizligi namunasi.

quiz.q: What does Elizabeth hint to Wickham?
o: That she knows the truth about him and Darcy
quiz.why_uz: Uikhem buni sezib, xavotirga tushadi.

chapters.title: To Derbyshire
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabetning otasi va onasining nikohi baxtsiz ekani ko'rsatiladi. Gardinerlar bilan Derbishirga sayohat boshlanadi. Darsining Pemberli mulki yonidan o'tishadi.

paras.en: Had Elizabeth's opinion been all drawn from her own family, she could not have formed a very pleasing opinion of conjugal felicity or domestic comfort. Her father, captivated by youth and beauty, and that appearance of good humour which youth and beauty generally give, had married a woman whose weak understanding and illiberal mind had very early in their marriage put an end to all real affection for her. Respect, esteem, and confidence had vanished for ever; and all his views of domestic happiness were overthrown. But Mr. Bennet was not of a disposition to seek comfort for the disappointment which his own imprudence had brought on, in any of those pleasures which too often console the unfortunate for their folly or their vice. He was fond of the country and of books; and from these tastes had arisen his principal enjoyments. To his wife he was very little otherwise indebted, than as her ignorance and folly had contributed to his amusement. This is not the sort of happiness which a man would in general wish to owe to his wife; but where other powers of entertainment are wanting, the true philosopher will derive benefit from such as are given.
paras.uz: Agar Elizabetning fikri butunlay o'z oilasidan olinganida, u nikoh baxti yoki oilaviy qulaylik haqida unchalik yoqimli fikr shakllantira olmasdi. Uning otasi yoshlik va go'zallik hamda yoshlik va go'zallik odatda beradigan xushfe'llik ko'rinishiga mahliyo bo'lib, zaif aqli va tor fikri nikohlarining juda erta davridayoq unga bo'lgan har qanday haqiqiy mehrga barham bergan ayolga uylangan edi. Hurmat, qadrlash va ishonch abadiy yo'qolgan edi; va uning oilaviy baxt haqidagi barcha qarashlari ag'darilgan edi. Lekin janob Bennet o'z ehtiyotsizligi keltirgan hafsala pirligi uchun baxtsizlarni ko'pincha ahmoqligi yoki illati uchun yupatadigan zavqlarning birortasidan taskin izlaydigan fe'lda emasdi. U qishloqni va kitoblarni yaxshi ko'rardi; uning asosiy zavqlari shu didlardan kelib chiqqan edi. Xotiniga u uning johilligi va ahmoqligi ko'ngil ochishiga hissa qo'shganidan boshqa jihatdan juda kam qarzdor edi. Bu erkak odatda xotiniga qarzdor bo'lishni istaydigan baxt turi emas; lekin boshqa ko'ngilxushlik vositalari yetishmagan joyda, haqiqiy faylasuf berilganlaridan foyda oladi.

paras.en: Elizabeth, however, had never been blind to the impropriety of her father's behaviour as a husband. She had always seen it with pain; but respecting his abilities, and grateful for his affectionate treatment of herself, she endeavoured to forget what she could not overlook, and to banish from her thoughts that continual breach of conjugal obligation and decorum which, in exposing his wife to the contempt of her own children, was so highly reprehensible. But she had never felt so strongly as now the disadvantages which must attend the children of so unsuitable a marriage, nor ever been so fully aware of the evils arising from so ill-judged a direction of talents; talents, which, rightly used, might at least have preserved the respectability of his daughters, even if incapable of enlarging the mind of his wife.
paras.uz: Biroq Elizabet otasining er sifatidagi xatti-harakatining nomunosibligiga hech qachon ko'r bo'lmagan edi. U buni doim og'riq bilan ko'rardi; lekin uning qobiliyatlarini hurmat qilib va o'ziga mehribon munosabati uchun minnatdor bo'lib, u e'tiborsiz qoldira olmaydigan narsani unutishga va xotinini o'z bolalarining nafratiga duchor qilishda juda ayblanishga loyiq bo'lgan nikoh majburiyati va odobining doimiy buzilishini fikrlaridan haydashga urinardi. Lekin u hech qachon hozirgidek bunchalik nomunosib nikohning farzandlariga muqarrar ravishda hamroh bo'ladigan noqulayliklarni kuchli his qilmagan, qobiliyatlarning bunchalik noto'g'ri yo'naltirilishidan kelib chiqadigan yomonliklarni ham bunchalik to'liq anglamagan edi; to'g'ri ishlatilganda, xotinining aqlini kengaytirishga qodir bo'lmasa ham, hech bo'lmaganda qizlarining obro'sini saqlab qolishi mumkin bo'lgan qobiliyatlar.

paras.en: When Elizabeth had rejoiced over Wickham's departure she found little other cause for satisfaction in the loss of the regiment. Their parties abroad were less varied than before, and at home she had a mother and sister whose constant repinings at the dullness of everything around them threw a real gloom over their domestic circle; and, though Kitty might in time regain her natural degree of sense, since the disturbers of her brain were removed, her other sister, from whose disposition greater evil might be apprehended, was likely to be hardened in all her folly and assurance by a situation of such double danger as a watering-place and a camp. Upon the whole, therefore, she found, what has been sometimes found before, that an event to which she had been looking with impatient desire did not, in taking place, bring all the satisfaction she had promised herself.
paras.uz: Elizabet Uikhemning ketganidan xursand bo'lgach, polkning yo'qolishida mamnuniyat uchun boshqa sabab kam topdi. Ularning tashqaridagi yig'inlari avvalgidan kamroq rang-barang edi, uyda esa atrofdagi hamma narsaning zerikarliligidan doimiy nolishlari oila davrasiga chinakam g'amginlik solgan onasi va singlisi bor edi; garchi Ketti miyasini bezovta qiluvchilar olib ketilgani uchun vaqt o'tib o'zining tabiiy aql darajasini qayta tiklashi mumkin bo'lsa ham, fe'lidan kattaroq yomonlik kutilishi mumkin bo'lgan boshqa singlisi kurort va lager kabi ikki tomonlama xavfli vaziyatda barcha ahmoqligi va surbetligida qotib qolishi ehtimoli bor edi. Shuning uchun umuman olganda u ilgari ham ba'zan aniqlangan narsani aniqladi: u sabrsiz istak bilan kutgan voqea sodir bo'lganda, o'ziga va'da qilgan barcha mamnuniyatni keltirmadi.

paras.en: It was consequently necessary to name some other period for the commencement of actual felicity--to have some other point on which her wishes and hopes might be fixed, and by again enjoying the pleasure of anticipation, console herself for the present, and prepare for another disappointment. Her tour to the Lakes was now the object of her happiest thoughts; it was her best consolation for all the uncomfortable hours which the discontentedness of her mother and Kitty made inevitable; and could she have included Jane in the scheme, every part of it would have been perfect.
paras.uz: Natijada haqiqiy baxtning boshlanishi uchun boshqa bir davrni belgilash zarur edi — istaklari va umidlari qadalishi mumkin bo'lgan boshqa nuqtaga ega bo'lish va yana intizorlik zavqidan bahramand bo'lib, hozirgi uchun o'zini yupatish va yana bir hafsala pirligiga tayyorlanish. Ko'llar o'lkasiga sayohati endi uning eng baxtli o'ylarining obyekti edi; bu onasi va Kettining noroziligi muqarrar qilgan barcha noqulay soatlar uchun uning eng yaxshi taskini edi; agar u rejaga Jeynni ham qo'sha olganida, uning har bir qismi mukammal bo'lardi.

paras.en: “But it is fortunate,” thought she, “that I have something to wish for. Were the whole arrangement complete, my disappointment would be certain. But here, by carrying with me one ceaseless source of regret in my sister's absence, I may reasonably hope to have all my expectations of pleasure realised. A scheme of which every part promises delight can never be successful; and general disappointment is only warded off by the defence of some little peculiar vexation.”
paras.uz: «Lekin baxtimga, — deb o'yladi u, — menda orzu qiladigan narsa bor. Agar butun tartib to'liq bo'lganida, hafsalam pir bo'lishi aniq bo'lardi. Lekin bu yerda opamning yo'qligida o'zim bilan bitmas-tuganmas afsus manbaini olib borib, zavq haqidagi barcha kutishlarim amalga oshishiga asosli umid qilishim mumkin. Har bir qismi zavq va'da qiladigan reja hech qachon muvaffaqiyatli bo'la olmaydi; umumiy hafsala pirligining oldini faqat biror kichik o'ziga xos g'ashlik himoyasi oladi».

paras.en: When Lydia went away she promised to write very often and very minutely to her mother and Kitty; but her letters were always long expected, and always very short. Those to her mother contained little else than that they were just returned from the library, where such and such officers had attended them, and where she had seen such beautiful ornaments as made her quite wild; that she had a new gown, or a new parasol, which she would have described more fully, but was obliged to leave off in a violent hurry, as Mrs. Forster called her, and they were going off to the camp; and from her correspondence with her sister, there was still less to be learnt--for her letters to Kitty, though rather longer, were much too full of lines under the words to be made public.
paras.uz: Lidiya ketayotganda onasi va Kettiga juda tez-tez va juda batafsil yozishga va'da berdi; lekin uning xatlari doim uzoq kutilardi va doim juda qisqa bo'lardi. Onasiga yozganlarida ular kutubxonadan hozirgina qaytganlari, u yerda falon-falon ofitserlar ularga hamroh bo'lgani va u yerda uni butunlay aqldan ozdirgan shunday chiroyli bezaklarni ko'rgani; uning yangi ko'ylagi yoki yangi soyaboni borligi, uni batafsilroq tasvirlagan bo'lardi, lekin missis Forster uni chaqirgani va ular lagerga ketayotgani uchun juda shoshib to'xtatishga majbur bo'lganidan boshqa narsa kam bo'lardi; singlisi bilan yozishmalaridan esa bundan ham kam narsa bilib olish mumkin edi — chunki uning Kettiga yozgan xatlari biroz uzunroq bo'lsa ham, ommaga oshkor qilish uchun so'zlar ostidagi chiziqlarga haddan tashqari to'la edi.

paras.en: After the first fortnight or three weeks of her absence, health, good humour, and cheerfulness began to reappear at Longbourn. Everything wore a happier aspect. The families who had been in town for the winter came back again, and summer finery and summer engagements arose. Mrs. Bennet was restored to her usual querulous serenity; and, by the middle of June, Kitty was so much recovered as to be able to enter Meryton without tears; an event of such happy promise as to make Elizabeth hope that by the following Christmas she might be so tolerably reasonable as not to mention an officer above once a day, unless, by some cruel and malicious arrangement at the War Office, another regiment should be quartered in Meryton.
paras.uz: Uning ketganining dastlabki ikki-uch haftasidan keyin Longbornda sog'lik, xushfe'llik va quvnoqlik qayta paydo bo'la boshladi. Hamma narsa baxtliroq qiyofaga kirdi. Qishni Londonda o'tkazgan oilalar qaytib kelishdi va yozgi bezaklar hamda yozgi tadbirlar paydo bo'ldi. Missis Bennet o'zining odatiy noliydigan osoyishtaligiga qaytdi; iyun o'rtasiga kelib Ketti Meritonga ko'z yoshisiz kira oladigan darajada tuzaldi; bu shunday baxtli istiqbolli voqea ediki, Elizabetga kelasi Rojdestvoga kelib u kuniga bir martadan ortiq ofitserni tilga olmaydigan darajada ancha oqil bo'lishi mumkinligiga umid qildirdi, agar Harbiy vazirlikdagi qandaydir shafqatsiz va g'arazli tartib bilan Meritonga boshqa polk joylashtirilmasa.

paras.en: The time fixed for the beginning of their northern tour was now fast approaching, and a fortnight only was wanting of it, when a letter arrived from Mrs. Gardiner, which at once delayed its commencement and curtailed its extent. Mr. Gardiner would be prevented by business from setting out till a fortnight later in July, and must be in London again within a month, and as that left too short a period for them to go so far, and see so much as they had proposed, or at least to see it with the leisure and comfort they had built on, they were obliged to give up the Lakes, and substitute a more contracted tour, and, according to the present plan, were to go no farther northwards than Derbyshire. In that county there was enough to be seen to occupy the chief of their three weeks; and to Mrs. Gardiner it had a peculiarly strong attraction. The town where she had formerly passed some years of her life, and where they were now to spend a few days, was probably as great an object of her curiosity as all the celebrated beauties of Matlock, Chatsworth, Dovedale, or the Peak.
paras.uz: Shimoliy sayohatlarining boshlanishi uchun belgilangan vaqt endi tez yaqinlashib kelayotgan edi va unga atigi ikki hafta qolgan edi, shu payt missis Gardinerdan xat keldi, u bir vaqtning o'zida uning boshlanishini kechiktirdi va ko'lamini qisqartirdi. Janob Gardinerni ishlari iyulda ikki hafta kechroqqacha yo'lga chiqishdan to'sib qo'yadi va u bir oy ichida yana Londonda bo'lishi kerak; bu esa ularning rejalashtirganidek uzoqqa borib, ko'p narsani ko'rishi uchun yoki hech bo'lmaganda mo'ljallagan bo'sh vaqt va qulaylik bilan ko'rishi uchun haddan tashqari qisqa muddat qoldirgani sababli, ular Ko'llar o'lkasidan voz kechib, uning o'rniga qisqaroq sayohat qilishga majbur bo'lishdi va hozirgi rejaga ko'ra Derbishirdan shimolroqqa bormasliklari kerak edi. U graflikda uch haftalarining asosiy qismini band qilish uchun yetarlicha ko'radigan narsa bor edi; missis Gardiner uchun esa unda alohida kuchli jozibasi bor edi. U ilgari hayotining bir necha yilini o'tkazgan va endi ular bir necha kun o'tkazishi kerak bo'lgan shahar, ehtimol, uning qiziqishining Metlok, Chatsuort, Douvdeyl yoki Pikning barcha mashhur go'zalliklari kabi katta obyekti edi.

paras.en: Elizabeth was excessively disappointed; she had set her heart on seeing the Lakes, and still thought there might have been time enough. But it was her business to be satisfied--and certainly her temper to be happy; and all was soon right again.
paras.uz: Elizabetning hafsalasi qattiq pir bo'ldi; u Ko'llar o'lkasini ko'rishga ko'ngil qo'ygan edi va hali ham yetarlicha vaqt bo'lishi mumkin edi, deb o'ylardi. Lekin qanoatlanish uning ishi edi — va baxtli bo'lish, albatta, uning fe'lida edi; tez orada hammasi yana joyiga tushdi.

paras.en: With the mention of Derbyshire there were many ideas connected. It was impossible for her to see the word without thinking of Pemberley and its owner. “But surely,” said she, “I may enter his county with impunity, and rob it of a few petrified spars without his perceiving me.”
paras.uz: Derbishirning tilga olinishi bilan ko'plab fikrlar bog'liq edi. U bu so'zni Pemberli va uning egasi haqida o'ylamasdan ko'ra olmasdi. «Lekin, albatta, — dedi u, — men uning grafligiga jazosiz kira olaman va u meni sezmasdan bir nechta toshga aylangan kristallni olib keta olaman».

paras.en: The period of expectation was now doubled. Four weeks were to pass away before her uncle and aunt's arrival. But they did pass away, and Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner, with their four children, did at length appear at Longbourn. The children, two girls of six and eight years old, and two younger boys, were to be left under the particular care of their cousin Jane, who was the general favourite, and whose steady sense and sweetness of temper exactly adapted her for attending to them in every way--teaching them, playing with them, and loving them.
paras.uz: Kutish davri endi ikki baravar uzaydi. Tog'asi va xolasi kelguncha to'rt hafta o'tishi kerak edi. Lekin ular o'tdi va janob hamda missis Gardiner to'rt farzandi bilan nihoyat Longbornda paydo bo'lishdi. Bolalar — olti va sakkiz yoshli ikki qiz va ikki kichikroq o'g'il — hammaning sevimlisi bo'lgan amakivachchasi Jeynning alohida qaramog'ida qoldirilishi kerak edi; uning barqaror aqli va shirin fe'li uni ularga har jihatdan qarashga — ularni o'qitish, ular bilan o'ynash va ularni sevishga aynan mos qilardi.

paras.en: The Gardiners stayed only one night at Longbourn, and set off the next morning with Elizabeth in pursuit of novelty and amusement. One enjoyment was certain--that of suitableness of companions; a suitableness which comprehended health and temper to bear inconveniences--cheerfulness to enhance every pleasure--and affection and intelligence, which might supply it among themselves if there were disappointments abroad.
paras.uz: Gardinerlar Longbornda faqat bir kecha qolishdi va ertasi kuni ertalab Elizabet bilan yangilik va ko'ngilxushlik izlab yo'lga chiqishdi. Bir zavq aniq edi — hamrohlarning mosligi; bu moslik noqulayliklarga bardosh beradigan sog'lik va fe'lni — har bir zavqni oshiradigan quvnoqlikni — va agar tashqarida hafsala pirliklari bo'lsa, uni o'zaro to'ldirishi mumkin bo'lgan mehr va aqlni o'z ichiga olardi.

paras.en: It is not the object of this work to give a description of Derbyshire, nor of any of the remarkable places through which their route thither lay; Oxford, Blenheim, Warwick, Kenilworth, Birmingham, etc. are sufficiently known. A small part of Derbyshire is all the present concern. To the little town of Lambton, the scene of Mrs. Gardiner's former residence, and where she had lately learned some acquaintance still remained, they bent their steps, after having seen all the principal wonders of the country; and within five miles of Lambton, Elizabeth found from her aunt that Pemberley was situated. It was not in their direct road, nor more than a mile or two out of it. In talking over their route the evening before, Mrs. Gardiner expressed an inclination to see the place again. Mr. Gardiner declared his willingness, and Elizabeth was applied to for her approbation.
paras.uz: Bu asarning maqsadi Derbishirni yoki u yerga boradigan yo'ldagi diqqatga sazovor joylarning birortasini tasvirlash emas; Oksford, Blenxeym, Uorik, Kenilvort, Birmingem va boshqalar yetarlicha ma'lum. Hozirgi qiziqish faqat Derbishirning kichik bir qismi. Ular mamlakatning barcha asosiy mo'jizalarini ko'rgach, missis Gardinerning avvalgi yashash joyi bo'lgan va u yaqinda ba'zi tanishlari hali ham qolganini bilib olgan kichik Lembton shahriga yo'l olishdi; Elizabet xolasidan Pemberli Lembtondan besh mil ichida joylashganini bildi. U ularning to'g'ri yo'lida emasdi, lekin undan bir-ikki mildan ortiq chetda ham emasdi. Oldingi kecha yo'nalishlarini muhokama qilayotganda missis Gardiner joyni yana ko'rish istagini bildirdi. Janob Gardiner roziligini aytdi va Elizabetdan ma'qullashini so'rashdi.

paras.en: “My love, should not you like to see a place of which you have heard so much?” said her aunt; “a place, too, with which so many of your acquaintances are connected. Wickham passed all his youth there, you know.”
paras.uz: «Azizim, shunchalik ko'p eshitgan joyingni ko'rishni istamaysanmi? — dedi xolasi. — Buning ustiga ko'plab tanishlaring bog'liq bo'lgan joy. Bilasanmi, Uikhem butun yoshligini u yerda o'tkazgan».

paras.en: Elizabeth was distressed. She felt that she had no business at Pemberley, and was obliged to assume a disinclination for seeing it. She must own that she was tired of seeing great houses; after going over so many, she really had no pleasure in fine carpets or satin curtains.
paras.uz: Elizabet xijolatga tushdi. U Pemberlida hech qanday ishi yo'qligini his qildi va uni ko'rishni istamagandek ko'rinishga majbur bo'ldi. U katta uylarni ko'rishdan charchaganini tan olishi kerak edi; shunchalik ko'pini aylanib chiqqach, u haqiqatan ham chiroyli gilamlar yoki atlas pardalardan zavq olmasdi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner abused her stupidity. “If it were merely a fine house richly furnished,” said she, “I should not care about it myself; but the grounds are delightful. They have some of the finest woods in the country.”
paras.uz: Missis Gardiner uning ahmoqligini koyidi. «Agar u shunchaki boy jihozlangan chiroyli uy bo'lganida, — dedi u, — men o'zim ham unga ahamiyat bermagan bo'lardim; lekin atrofi ajoyib. U yerda mamlakatdagi eng chiroyli o'rmonlardan ba'zilari bor».

paras.en: Elizabeth said no more--but her mind could not acquiesce. The possibility of meeting Mr. Darcy, while viewing the place, instantly occurred. It would be dreadful! She blushed at the very idea, and thought it would be better to speak openly to her aunt than to run such a risk. But against this there were objections; and she finally resolved that it could be the last resource, if her private inquiries to the absence of the family were unfavourably answered.
paras.uz: Elizabet boshqa gapirmadi — lekin uning qalbi rozi bo'la olmadi. Joyni ko'zdan kechirayotganda janob Darsini uchratish ehtimoli darhol xayoliga keldi. Bu dahshatli bo'lardi! U bu fikrdanoq qizarib ketdi va bunday xavf tug'dirgandan ko'ra xolasi bilan ochiq gaplashgani ma'qul, deb o'yladi. Lekin bunga qarshi e'tirozlar bor edi; va u nihoyat, agar oilaning yo'qligi haqidagi yashirin so'rovlariga noqulay javob berilsa, bu oxirgi chora bo'lishi mumkin, deb qaror qildi.

paras.en: Accordingly, when she retired at night, she asked the chambermaid whether Pemberley were not a very fine place? what was the name of its proprietor? and, with no little alarm, whether the family were down for the summer? A most welcome negative followed the last question--and her alarms now being removed, she was at leisure to feel a great deal of curiosity to see the house herself; and when the subject was revived the next morning, and she was again applied to, could readily answer, and with a proper air of indifference, that she had not really any dislike to the scheme. To Pemberley, therefore, they were to go.
paras.uz: Shunga ko'ra, kechqurun dam olish uchun ketganida, u xizmatkor qizdan Pemberli juda chiroyli joy emasmi? Uning egasining ismi nima? va zarracha bo'lmagan xavotir bilan oila yozni o'tkazish uchun u yerga kelganmi, deb so'radi. Oxirgi savolga eng xush kelgan inkor javob keldi — va endi xavotirlari yo'qolgach, u uyni o'zi ko'rishga katta qiziqish his qilishga vaqt topdi; ertasi kuni ertalab mavzu qayta ko'tarilib, undan yana so'ralganida, u darhol va munosib befarqlik qiyofasida rejaga hech qanday qarshiligi yo'qligini ayta oldi. Shunday qilib, ular Pemberliga borishlari kerak edi.

quiz.q: Why is Elizabeth afraid to visit Pemberley?
quiz.why_uz: U Darsi uyda yo'qligini bilgach rozi bo'ladi.

quiz.q: What does this chapter say about Mr. and Mrs. Bennet's marriage?
o: It is based on attraction, not respect, and is unhappy
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet otasining kamchiliklarini aniq ko'radi.

chapters.title: Pemberley
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet Pemberlini ko'radi va hayratda qoladi. Uy bekasi Darsini eng mehribon xo'jayin va aka deb maqtaydi. To'satdan Darsi qaytib keladi va Elizabet bilan juda xushmuomala gaplashadi.

paras.en: Elizabeth, as they drove along, watched for the first appearance of Pemberley Woods with some perturbation; and when at length they turned in at the lodge, her spirits were in a high flutter.
paras.uz: Yo'lda ketisharkan, Elizabet Pemberli o'rmonlarining birinchi ko'rinishini biroz hayajon bilan kutdi; nihoyat ular qorovulxona yonidan ichkariga burilishganda, uning yuragi qattiq dukillardi.

paras.en: The park was very large, and contained great variety of ground. They entered it in one of its lowest points, and drove for some time through a beautiful wood stretching over a wide extent.
paras.uz: Park juda katta bo'lib, xilma-xil yer relyefiga ega edi. Ular unga eng past nuqtalaridan biridan kirishdi va keng maydonga cho'zilgan go'zal o'rmon orqali bir muddat yurishdi.

paras.en: Elizabeth's mind was too full for conversation, but she saw and admired every remarkable spot and point of view. They gradually ascended for half-a-mile, and then found themselves at the top of a considerable eminence, where the wood ceased, and the eye was instantly caught by Pemberley House, situated on the opposite side of a valley, into which the road with some abruptness wound. It was a large, handsome stone building, standing well on rising ground, and backed by a ridge of high woody hills; and in front, a stream of some natural importance was swelled into greater, but without any artificial appearance. Its banks were neither formal nor falsely adorned. Elizabeth was delighted. She had never seen a place for which nature had done more, or where natural beauty had been so little counteracted by an awkward taste. They were all of them warm in their admiration; and at that moment she felt that to be mistress of Pemberley might be something!
paras.uz: Elizabetning fikrlari suhbat uchun haddan tashqari band edi, lekin u har bir diqqatga sazovor joyni va manzarani ko'rib, unga qoyil qoldi. Ular yarim mil asta-sekin ko'tarilishdi va keyin o'rmon tugagan ancha baland tepalikning cho'qqisida o'zlarini topishdi, shu yerda ko'z darhol yo'l biroz keskin burilib tushadigan vodiyning narigi tomonida joylashgan Pemberli uyiga qadaldi. Bu baland joyda yaxshi joylashgan, orqasida baland o'rmonli tepaliklar tizmasi bo'lgan katta, chiroyli tosh bino edi; oldida esa ancha tabiiy ahamiyatga ega bo'lgan soy kattaroq bo'lib kengaytirilgan, lekin hech qanday sun'iy ko'rinishsiz edi. Uning qirg'oqlari na rasmiy, na soxta bezatilgan edi. Elizabet zavqlandi. U tabiat bundan ko'proq ish qilgan yoki tabiiy go'zallikka beso'naqay did bunchalik kam to'sqinlik qilgan joyni hech qachon ko'rmagan edi. Ularning hammasi qizg'in hayratda edi; va o'sha lahzada u Pemberlining bekasi bo'lish nimadir bo'lishi mumkinligini his qildi!

paras.en: They descended the hill, crossed the bridge, and drove to the door; and, while examining the nearer aspect of the house, all her apprehension of meeting its owner returned. She dreaded lest the chambermaid had been mistaken. On applying to see the place, they were admitted into the hall; and Elizabeth, as they waited for the housekeeper, had leisure to wonder at her being where she was.
paras.uz: Ular tepalikdan tushishdi, ko'prikni kesib o'tishdi va eshik oldiga kelishdi; uyning yaqinroq ko'rinishini ko'zdan kechirarkan, uning egasini uchratish haqidagi barcha xavotirlari qaytib keldi. U xizmatkor qiz adashgan bo'lishidan qo'rqdi. Joyni ko'rishni so'rashganda, ularni zalga kiritishdi va Elizabet uy bekasini kutarkan, qayerda ekaniga hayron bo'lishga vaqt topdi.

paras.en: The housekeeper came; a respectable-looking elderly woman, much less fine, and more civil, than she had any notion of finding her. They followed her into the dining-parlour. It was a large, well proportioned room, handsomely fitted up. Elizabeth, after slightly surveying it, went to a window to enjoy its prospect. The hill, crowned with wood, which they had descended, receiving increased abruptness from the distance, was a beautiful object. Every disposition of the ground was good; and she looked on the whole scene, the river, the trees scattered on its banks and the winding of the valley, as far as she could trace it, with delight. As they passed into other rooms these objects were taking different positions; but from every window there were beauties to be seen. The rooms were lofty and handsome, and their furniture suitable to the fortune of its proprietor; but Elizabeth saw, with admiration of his taste, that it was neither gaudy nor uselessly fine; with less of splendour, and more real elegance, than the furniture of Rosings.
paras.uz: Uy bekasi keldi; u kutganidan ancha kamroq dabdabali va xushmuomalaroq, hurmatli ko'rinishli keksa ayol. Ular uning ortidan ovqatxonaga kirishdi. Bu katta, yaxshi mutanosib, chiroyli jihozlangan xona edi. Elizabet uni yuzaki ko'zdan kechirgach, manzaradan zavqlanish uchun derazalardan biriga bordi. Ular tushib kelgan, cho'qqisi o'rmon bilan qoplangan tepalik masofadan yanada keskinroq ko'rinib, go'zal manzara edi. Yerning har bir joylashuvi yaxshi edi; u butun sahnaga — daryoga, uning qirg'oqlarida sochilgan daraxtlarga va ko'z yetguncha vodiyning burilishlariga zavq bilan qaradi. Ular boshqa xonalarga o'tganlarida bu narsalar turli holatlarni egallardi; lekin har bir derazadan ko'rish mumkin bo'lgan go'zalliklar bor edi. Xonalar baland va chiroyli, mebellari esa egasining boyligiga mos edi; lekin Elizabet uning didiga qoyil qolib ko'rdiki, u na ko'zni qamashtiruvchi, na befoyda dabdabali edi; Rozings mebelidan kamroq hashamatli va ko'proq haqiqiy nafis edi.

paras.en: “And of this place,” thought she, “I might have been mistress! With these rooms I might now have been familiarly acquainted! Instead of viewing them as a stranger, I might have rejoiced in them as my own, and welcomed to them as visitors my uncle and aunt. But no,”--recollecting herself--“that could never be; my uncle and aunt would have been lost to me; I should not have been allowed to invite them.”
paras.uz: «Va bu joyning, — deb o'yladi u, — bekasi bo'lishim mumkin edi! Bu xonalar bilan hozir yaqindan tanish bo'lishim mumkin edi! Ularni begona sifatida ko'zdan kechirish o'rniga, o'zimniki deb ulardan xursand bo'lishim va tog'am bilan xolamni ularga mehmon sifatida kutib olishim mumkin edi. Lekin yo'q, — o'zini tutib olib, — bu hech qachon bo'lmasdi; tog'am va xolamdan ayrilgan bo'lardim; ularni taklif qilishimga ruxsat berilmasdi».

paras.en: This was a lucky recollection--it saved her from something very like regret.
paras.uz: Bu omadli xotira edi — u uni afsusga juda o'xshash narsadan qutqardi.

paras.en: She longed to inquire of the housekeeper whether her master was really absent, but had not the courage for it. At length however, the question was asked by her uncle; and she turned away with alarm, while Mrs. Reynolds replied that he was, adding, “But we expect him to-morrow, with a large party of friends.” How rejoiced was Elizabeth that their own journey had not by any circumstance been delayed a day!
paras.uz: U uy bekasidan xo'jayini chindan ham yo'qmi, deb so'rashni juda istadi, lekin bunga jur'ati yetmadi. Biroq nihoyat bu savolni tog'asi berdi; missis Reynolds yo'qligini aytib, «Lekin biz uni ertaga katta do'stlar davrasi bilan kutyapmiz» deb qo'shganda, u xavotir bilan o'girildi. Elizabet o'z sayohatlari biror holat tufayli bir kunga kechikmaganidan qanchalik xursand bo'ldi!

paras.en: Her aunt now called her to look at a picture. She approached and saw the likeness of Mr. Wickham, suspended, amongst several other miniatures, over the mantelpiece. Her aunt asked her, smilingly, how she liked it. The housekeeper came forward, and told them it was a picture of a young gentleman, the son of her late master's steward, who had been brought up by him at his own expense. “He is now gone into the army,” she added; “but I am afraid he has turned out very wild.”
paras.uz: Endi xolasi uni bir suratga qarashga chaqirdi. U yaqinlashdi va kamin tokchasi ustida boshqa bir nechta miniatyuralar orasida osilgan janob Uikhemning suratini ko'rdi. Xolasi undan jilmayib, bu unga qanchalik yoqishini so'radi. Uy bekasi oldinga chiqib, bu marhum xo'jayinining boshqaruvchisining o'g'li, xo'jayini o'z hisobidan tarbiyalagan yosh janobning surati ekanini aytdi. «U endi armiyaga ketgan, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — lekin qo'rqamanki, u juda yovvoyi bo'lib chiqqan».

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner looked at her niece with a smile, but Elizabeth could not return it.
paras.uz: Missis Gardiner jiyaniga jilmayib qaradi, lekin Elizabet unga javob qaytara olmadi.

paras.en: “And that,” said Mrs. Reynolds, pointing to another of the miniatures, “is my master--and very like him. It was drawn at the same time as the other--about eight years ago.”
paras.uz: «Bu esa, — dedi missis Reynolds, boshqa miniatyuraga ishora qilib, — mening xo'jayinim — va unga juda o'xshaydi. U boshqasi bilan bir vaqtda — taxminan sakkiz yil oldin chizilgan».

paras.en: “I have heard much of your master's fine person,” said Mrs. Gardiner, looking at the picture; “it is a handsome face. But, Lizzy, you can tell us whether it is like or not.”
paras.uz: «Xo'jayiningizning chiroyli qiyofasi haqida ko'p eshitganman, — dedi missis Gardiner suratga qarab. — Bu chiroyli yuz. Lekin, Lizzi, sen bizga o'xshaydimi, yo'qmi, ayta olasan».

paras.en: Mrs. Reynolds respect for Elizabeth seemed to increase on this intimation of her knowing her master.
paras.uz: Uning xo'jayinini bilishiga bo'lgan bu ishoradan missis Reynoldsning Elizabetga hurmati ortganday ko'rindi.

paras.en: “Does that young lady know Mr. Darcy?”
paras.uz: «Bu yosh xonim janob Darsini taniydimi?»

paras.en: Elizabeth coloured, and said: “A little.”
paras.uz: Elizabet qizardi va dedi: «Ozgina».

paras.en: “And do not you think him a very handsome gentleman, ma'am?”
paras.uz: «Uni juda chiroyli janob deb o'ylamaysizmi, xonim?»

paras.en: “Yes, very handsome.”
paras.uz: «Ha, juda chiroyli».
