paras.en: “I am sure I know none so handsome; but in the gallery up stairs you will see a finer, larger picture of him than this. This room was my late master's favourite room, and these miniatures are just as they used to be then. He was very fond of them.”
paras.uz: «Ishonchim komilki, men bunchalik chiroylisini bilmayman; lekin yuqoridagi galereyada uning bundan ham chiroyliroq, kattaroq suratini ko'rasiz. Bu xona marhum xo'jayinimning sevimli xonasi edi va bu miniatyuralar o'shanda qanday bo'lsa, xuddi shunday turibdi. U ularni juda yaxshi ko'rardi».

paras.en: This accounted to Elizabeth for Mr. Wickham's being among them.
paras.uz: Bu Elizabetga janob Uikhemning nega ular orasida ekanini tushuntirdi.

paras.en: Mrs. Reynolds then directed their attention to one of Miss Darcy, drawn when she was only eight years old.
paras.uz: Keyin missis Reynolds ularning e'tiborini miss Darsining atigi sakkiz yoshligida chizilgan suratiga qaratdi.

paras.en: “And is Miss Darcy as handsome as her brother?” said Mrs. Gardiner.
paras.uz: «Miss Darsi ham akasi kabi chiroylimi?» — dedi missis Gardiner.

paras.en: “Oh! yes--the handsomest young lady that ever was seen; and so accomplished!--She plays and sings all day long. In the next room is a new instrument just come down for her--a present from my master; she comes here to-morrow with him.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Ha — hech qachon ko'rilgan eng chiroyli yosh xonim; va shunchalik ko'p hunar egasi! U kun bo'yi chaladi va kuylaydi. Keyingi xonada uning uchun hozirgina keltirilgan yangi cholg'u bor — xo'jayinimning sovg'asi; u ertaga u bilan bu yerga keladi».

paras.en: Mr. Gardiner, whose manners were very easy and pleasant, encouraged her communicativeness by his questions and remarks; Mrs. Reynolds, either by pride or attachment, had evidently great pleasure in talking of her master and his sister.
paras.uz: Muomalasi juda yengil va yoqimli bo'lgan janob Gardiner savollari va mulohazalari bilan uning ochiqko'ngilligini rag'batlantirdi; missis Reynolds g'urur yoki bog'liqlik tufayli xo'jayini va uning singlisi haqida gapirishdan katta zavq olayotgani aniq edi.

paras.en: “Is your master much at Pemberley in the course of the year?”
paras.uz: «Xo'jayiningiz yil davomida Pemberlida ko'p bo'ladimi?»

paras.en: “Not so much as I could wish, sir; but I dare say he may spend half his time here; and Miss Darcy is always down for the summer months.”
paras.uz: «Men istagancha emas, ser; lekin ishonamanki, u vaqtining yarmini shu yerda o'tkazar; miss Darsi esa yoz oylarida doim shu yerda bo'ladi».

paras.en: “Except,” thought Elizabeth, “when she goes to Ramsgate.”
paras.uz: «Ramsgeytga borgan paytlardan tashqari», — deb o'yladi Elizabet.

paras.en: “If your master would marry, you might see more of him.”
paras.uz: «Agar xo'jayiningiz uylansa, uni ko'proq ko'rardingiz».

paras.en: “Yes, sir; but I do not know when that will be. I do not know who is good enough for him.”
paras.uz: «Ha, ser; lekin bu qachon bo'lishini bilmayman. Uning uchun kim yetarlicha yaxshi ekanini bilmayman».

paras.en: Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner smiled. Elizabeth could not help saying, “It is very much to his credit, I am sure, that you should think so.”
paras.uz: Janob va missis Gardiner jilmayishdi. Elizabet aytmay qololmadi: «Ishonchim komilki, sizning shunday o'ylashingiz uning uchun katta sharaf».

paras.en: “I say no more than the truth, and everybody will say that knows him,” replied the other. Elizabeth thought this was going pretty far; and she listened with increasing astonishment as the housekeeper added, “I have never known a cross word from him in my life, and I have known him ever since he was four years old.”
paras.uz: «Men haqiqatdan ortiq hech narsa demayapman, uni bilgan har kim shuni aytadi», — javob berdi u. Elizabet bu ancha uzoqqa ketayotgan deb o'yladi; va uy bekasi qo'shib qo'yganda, u ortib borayotgan hayrat bilan tingladi: «Umrimda undan bir og'iz ham qo'pol so'z eshitmaganman, men esa uni to'rt yoshidan beri bilaman».

paras.en: This was praise, of all others most extraordinary, most opposite to her ideas. That he was not a good-tempered man had been her firmest opinion. Her keenest attention was awakened; she longed to hear more, and was grateful to her uncle for saying:
paras.uz: Bu boshqalarning hammasidan eng g'ayrioddiy, uning fikrlariga eng zid maqtov edi. Uning xushfe'l odam emasligi uning eng qat'iy fikri edi. Uning eng o'tkir e'tibori uyg'ondi; u ko'proq eshitishni juda istadi va tog'asi shunday deganidan minnatdor bo'ldi:

paras.en: “There are very few people of whom so much can be said. You are lucky in having such a master.”
paras.uz: «Bu haqda shuncha narsa aytish mumkin bo'lgan odamlar juda kam. Bunday xo'jayiningiz borligi bilan omadlisiz».

paras.en: “Yes, sir, I know I am. If I were to go through the world, I could not meet with a better. But I have always observed, that they who are good-natured when children, are good-natured when they grow up; and he was always the sweetest-tempered, most generous-hearted boy in the world.”
paras.uz: «Ha, ser, bilaman. Agar butun dunyoni kezib chiqsam ham, bundan yaxshisini uchrata olmasdim. Lekin men doim kuzatganmanki, bolaligida xushfe'l bo'lganlar katta bo'lganda ham xushfe'l bo'ladi; u esa doim dunyodagi eng shirin fe'lli, eng olijanob qalbli bola edi».

paras.en: Elizabeth almost stared at her. “Can this be Mr. Darcy?” thought she.
paras.uz: Elizabet unga deyarli tikilib qoldi. «Bu janob Darsi bo'lishi mumkinmi?» — deb o'yladi u.

paras.en: “His father was an excellent man,” said Mrs. Gardiner.
paras.uz: «Uning otasi ajoyib odam edi», — dedi missis Gardiner.

paras.en: “Yes, ma'am, that he was indeed; and his son will be just like him--just as affable to the poor.”
paras.uz: «Ha, xonim, haqiqatan ham shunday edi; o'g'li ham aynan unga o'xshaydi — kambag'allarga xuddi shunday mehribon».

paras.en: Elizabeth listened, wondered, doubted, and was impatient for more. Mrs. Reynolds could interest her on no other point. She related the subjects of the pictures, the dimensions of the rooms, and the price of the furniture, in vain. Mr. Gardiner, highly amused by the kind of family prejudice to which he attributed her excessive commendation of her master, soon led again to the subject; and she dwelt with energy on his many merits as they proceeded together up the great staircase.
paras.uz: Elizabet tingladi, hayron bo'ldi, shubhalandi va ko'proq eshitishga sabrsizlandi. Missis Reynolds uni boshqa hech qanday masalada qiziqtira olmasdi. U suratlarning mavzularini, xonalarning o'lchamlarini va mebelning narxini behuda aytib berdi. Uning xo'jayinini haddan tashqari maqtashini oilaviy tarafkashlikning bir turiga bog'lagan va bundan juda zavqlangan janob Gardiner tez orada yana mavzuga qaytdi; va ular katta zinapoyadan birga ko'tarilisharkan, u uning ko'plab fazilatlari haqida g'ayrat bilan to'xtaldi.

paras.en: “He is the best landlord, and the best master,” said she, “that ever lived; not like the wild young men nowadays, who think of nothing but themselves. There is not one of his tenants or servants but will give him a good name. Some people call him proud; but I am sure I never saw anything of it. To my fancy, it is only because he does not rattle away like other young men.”
paras.uz: «U hech qachon yashagan eng yaxshi yer egasi va eng yaxshi xo'jayin, — dedi u. — Hozirgi o'zidan boshqa hech narsani o'ylamaydigan yovvoyi yosh yigitlarga o'xshamaydi. Uning ijarachilari yoki xizmatkorlaridan biror kishi yo'qki, u haqida yaxshi gap aytmasa. Ba'zi odamlar uni mag'rur deyishadi; lekin ishonchim komilki, men bunday narsani hech qachon ko'rmaganman. Menimcha, bu faqat u boshqa yosh yigitlar kabi vaysamaydi».

paras.en: “In what an amiable light does this place him!” thought Elizabeth.
paras.uz: «Bu uni qanday yoqimli tarzda ko'rsatadi!» — deb o'yladi Elizabet.

paras.en: “This fine account of him,” whispered her aunt as they walked, “is not quite consistent with his behaviour to our poor friend.”
paras.uz: «Uning haqidagi bu chiroyli ta'rif, — pichirladi xolasi ular yurisharkan, — bechora do'stimizga nisbatan xatti-harakatiga unchalik mos kelmaydi».

paras.en: “Perhaps we might be deceived.”
paras.uz: «Ehtimol, biz aldangandirmiz».

paras.en: “That is not very likely; our authority was too good.”
paras.uz: «Bu unchalik ehtimoldan emas; manbamiz juda ishonchli edi».

paras.en: On reaching the spacious lobby above they were shown into a very pretty sitting-room, lately fitted up with greater elegance and lightness than the apartments below; and were informed that it was but just done to give pleasure to Miss Darcy, who had taken a liking to the room when last at Pemberley.
paras.uz: Yuqoridagi keng dahlizga yetib kelgach, ularni pastdagi xonalardan ko'ra ko'proq nafislik va yengillik bilan yaqinda jihozlangan juda chiroyli o'tirish xonasiga olib kirishdi va bu Pemberlida oxirgi marta bo'lganida xonani yoqtirib qolgan miss Darsini xursand qilish uchun yaqindagina qilinganini aytishdi.

paras.en: “He is certainly a good brother,” said Elizabeth, as she walked towards one of the windows.
paras.uz: «U, albatta, yaxshi aka», — dedi Elizabet derazalardan biri tomon yurarkan.

paras.en: Mrs. Reynolds anticipated Miss Darcy's delight, when she should enter the room. “And this is always the way with him,” she added. “Whatever can give his sister any pleasure is sure to be done in a moment. There is nothing he would not do for her.”
paras.uz: Missis Reynolds miss Darsi xonaga kirganda qanchalik xursand bo'lishini oldindan tasavvur qildi. «U bilan doim shunday, — qo'shib qo'ydi u. — Singlisiga biror zavq bera oladigan har qanday narsa bir lahzada albatta bajariladi. U uning uchun qilmaydigan hech narsa yo'q».

paras.en: The picture-gallery, and two or three of the principal bedrooms, were all that remained to be shown. In the former were many good paintings; but Elizabeth knew nothing of the art; and from such as had been already visible below, she had willingly turned to look at some drawings of Miss Darcy's, in crayons, whose subjects were usually more interesting, and also more intelligible.
paras.uz: Ko'rsatish uchun faqat suratlar galereyasi va ikki-uch asosiy yotoqxona qolgan edi. Birinchisida ko'plab yaxshi rasmlar bor edi; lekin Elizabet san'atdan hech narsa bilmasdi; va pastda allaqachon ko'ringanlaridan u mamnuniyat bilan miss Darsining pastel bilan chizilgan ba'zi rasmlariga qarashga o'girildi, ularning mavzulari odatda qiziqarliroq va tushunarliroq edi.

paras.en: In the gallery there were many family portraits, but they could have little to fix the attention of a stranger. Elizabeth walked in quest of the only face whose features would be known to her. At last it arrested her--and she beheld a striking resemblance to Mr. Darcy, with such a smile over the face as she remembered to have sometimes seen when he looked at her. She stood several minutes before the picture, in earnest contemplation, and returned to it again before they quitted the gallery. Mrs. Reynolds informed them that it had been taken in his father's lifetime.
paras.uz: Galereyada ko'plab oilaviy portretlar bor edi, lekin ularda begonaning e'tiborini tortadigan narsa kam bo'lishi mumkin edi. Elizabet o'ziga tanish bo'ladigan yagona yuzni izlab yurdi. Nihoyat u uni to'xtatdi — va u janob Darsiga hayratlanarli o'xshashlikni ko'rdi, yuzida u ba'zan unga qaraganida ko'rganini eslaydigan shunday tabassum bor edi. U surat oldida bir necha daqiqa jiddiy tafakkur bilan turdi va galereyadan chiqishdan oldin yana unga qaytdi. Missis Reynolds u otasining hayotligida chizilganini aytdi.

paras.en: There was certainly at this moment, in Elizabeth's mind, a more gentle sensation towards the original than she had ever felt at the height of their acquaintance. The commendation bestowed on him by Mrs. Reynolds was of no trifling nature. What praise is more valuable than the praise of an intelligent servant? As a brother, a landlord, a master, she considered how many people's happiness were in his guardianship!--how much of pleasure or pain was it in his power to bestow!--how much of good or evil must be done by him! Every idea that had been brought forward by the housekeeper was favourable to his character, and as she stood before the canvas on which he was represented, and fixed his eyes upon herself, she thought of his regard with a deeper sentiment of gratitude than it had ever raised before; she remembered its warmth, and softened its impropriety of expression.
paras.uz: Shu lahzada Elizabetning ongida, albatta, tanishliklarining eng yuqori cho'qqisida ham his qilmagan, asl nusxaga nisbatan muloyimroq tuyg'u bor edi. Missis Reynolds unga aytgan maqtov arzimas emasdi. Aqlli xizmatkorning maqtovidan qimmatliroq qanday maqtov bor? Aka, yer egasi, xo'jayin sifatida — u qanchadan-qancha odamlarning baxti uning qaramog'ida ekanini o'yladi! — qanchalik zavq yoki og'riq berish uning qo'lida! — u tomonidan qanchalik yaxshilik yoki yomonlik qilinishi kerak! Uy bekasi ilgari surgan har bir fikr uning xarakteri foydasiga edi va u tasvirlangan va ko'zlarini unga qadab turgan kanvas oldida turarkan, u uning mehri haqida ilgari hech qachon uyg'otmagan chuqurroq minnatdorlik tuyg'usi bilan o'yladi; u uning iliqligini esladi va ifodasining nomunosibligini yumshatdi.

paras.en: When all of the house that was open to general inspection had been seen, they returned downstairs, and, taking leave of the housekeeper, were consigned over to the gardener, who met them at the hall-door.
paras.uz: Uyning umumiy ko'rish uchun ochiq bo'lgan hamma qismini ko'rib bo'lgach, ular pastga qaytishdi va uy bekasi bilan xayrlashib, zal eshigida ularni kutib olgan bog'bonga topshirildi.

paras.en: As they walked across the hall towards the river, Elizabeth turned back to look again; her uncle and aunt stopped also, and while the former was conjecturing as to the date of the building, the owner of it himself suddenly came forward from the road, which led behind it to the stables.
paras.uz: Ular zal orqali daryo tomon yurishayotganda, Elizabet yana qarash uchun ortga o'girildi; tog'asi va xolasi ham to'xtashdi va tog'asi binoning qurilgan sanasini taxmin qilayotganda, uning egasining o'zi to'satdan orqa tomondagi otxonaga olib boradigan yo'ldan chiqib keldi.

paras.en: They were within twenty yards of each other, and so abrupt was his appearance, that it was impossible to avoid his sight. Their eyes instantly met, and the cheeks of both were overspread with the deepest blush. He absolutely started, and for a moment seemed immovable from surprise; but shortly recovering himself, advanced towards the party, and spoke to Elizabeth, if not in terms of perfect composure, at least of perfect civility.
paras.uz: Ular bir-biridan yigirma yard masofada edilar va uning paydo bo'lishi shunchalik to'satdan bo'ldiki, uning nazaridan qochib bo'lmasdi. Ularning ko'zlari darhol uchrashdi va ikkalasining yonoqlari eng chuqur qizillik bilan qoplandi. U mutlaqo seskanib ketdi va bir lahza hayratdan qimirlay olmaganday ko'rindi; lekin tez orada o'zini tutib olib, davra tomon yurdi va Elizabetga to'liq xotirjamlik bilan bo'lmasa ham, hech bo'lmaganda to'liq xushmuomalalik bilan gapirdi.

paras.en: She had instinctively turned away; but stopping on his approach, received his compliments with an embarrassment impossible to be overcome. Had his first appearance, or his resemblance to the picture they had just been examining, been insufficient to assure the other two that they now saw Mr. Darcy, the gardener's expression of surprise, on beholding his master, must immediately have told it. They stood a little aloof while he was talking to their niece, who, astonished and confused, scarcely dared lift her eyes to his face, and knew not what answer she returned to his civil inquiries after her family.
paras.uz: U beixtiyor o'girilib ketgan edi; lekin u yaqinlashganda to'xtab, uning salomlarini yengib bo'lmas xijolat bilan qabul qildi. Agar uning birinchi paydo bo'lishi yoki ular hozirgina ko'zdan kechirgan suratga o'xshashligi qolgan ikkisini endi janob Darsini ko'rayotganlariga ishontirish uchun yetarli bo'lmaganida, bog'bonning xo'jayinini ko'rgandagi hayrat ifodasi buni darhol aytgan bo'lardi. U ularning jiyani bilan gaplashayotganda ular biroz chetda turishdi; hayratlangan va sarosimaga tushgan jiyan esa ko'zlarini uning yuziga ko'tarishga zo'rg'a jur'at etar va uning oilasi haqidagi xushmuomala so'roqlariga qanday javob berganini bilmasdi.

paras.en: Amazed at the alteration of his manner since they last parted, every sentence that he uttered was increasing her embarrassment; and every idea of the impropriety of her being found there recurring to her mind, the few minutes in which they continued were some of the most uncomfortable in her life. Nor did he seem much more at ease; when he spoke, his accent had none of its usual sedateness; and he repeated his inquiries as to the time of her having left Longbourn, and of her having stayed in Derbyshire, so often, and in so hurried a way, as plainly spoke the distraction of his thoughts.
paras.uz: Ular oxirgi marta ajralgandan beri uning muomalasi o'zgarganidan hayratlanib, u aytgan har bir jumla uning xijolatini oshirardi; va uning u yerda topilishining nomunosibligi haqidagi har bir fikr xayoliga qaytib kelarkan, ular davom etgan bir necha daqiqa uning hayotidagi eng noqulay daqiqalardan biri bo'ldi. U ham unchalik xotirjam ko'rinmasdi; u gapirganda, ohangida odatdagi salobatdan asar ham yo'q edi va u uning Longborndan qachon ketgani va Derbishirda qancha qolgani haqidagi so'roqlarini shunchalik tez-tez va shunchalik shoshilib takrorladiki, bu uning fikrlari parishonligini aniq ko'rsatardi.

paras.en: At length every idea seemed to fail him; and, after standing a few moments without saying a word, he suddenly recollected himself, and took leave.
paras.uz: Nihoyat har qanday fikr uni tark etganday tuyuldi; va bir necha lahza bir og'iz ham gapirmay turgach, u to'satdan o'zini tutib oldi va xayrlashdi.

paras.en: The others then joined her, and expressed admiration of his figure; but Elizabeth heard not a word, and wholly engrossed by her own feelings, followed them in silence. She was overpowered by shame and vexation. Her coming there was the most unfortunate, the most ill-judged thing in the world! How strange it must appear to him! In what a disgraceful light might it not strike so vain a man! It might seem as if she had purposely thrown herself in his way again! Oh! why did she come? Or, why did he thus come a day before he was expected? Had they been only ten minutes sooner, they should have been beyond the reach of his discrimination; for it was plain that he was that moment arrived--that moment alighted from his horse or his carriage. She blushed again and again over the perverseness of the meeting.
paras.uz: Keyin boshqalar unga qo'shilishdi va uning qomatiga hayratlarini bildirishdi; lekin Elizabet bir og'iz ham eshitmadi va butunlay o'z tuyg'ulari bilan band bo'lib, ularning ortidan jimgina ergashdi. Uni uyat va g'ashlik bosib ketdi. Uning bu yerga kelishi dunyodagi eng omadsiz, eng noto'g'ri o'ylangan ish edi! Bu unga qanchalik g'alati ko'rinishi kerak! Bunchalik shuhratparast odamga bu qanchalik sharmandali tarzda tuyulishi mumkin! Go'yo u ataylab yana uning yo'liga o'zini tashlaganday ko'rinishi mumkin! Oh! Nega u keldi? Yoki nega u kutilganidan bir kun oldin keldi? Agar ular atigi o'n daqiqa oldinroq bo'lganida, uning nazaridan tashqarida bo'lardilar; chunki u aynan o'sha lahzada kelgani — aynan o'sha lahzada otidan yoki aravasidan tushgani aniq edi. U uchrashuvning teskariligidan qayta-qayta qizardi.

paras.en: And his behaviour, so strikingly altered--what could it mean? That he should even speak to her was amazing!--but to speak with such civility, to inquire after her family! Never in her life had she seen his manners so little dignified, never had he spoken with such gentleness as on this unexpected meeting. What a contrast did it offer to his last address in Rosings Park, when he put his letter into her hand! She knew not what to think, or how to account for it.
paras.uz: Va uning shunchalik hayratlanarli o'zgargan xatti-harakati — bu nimani anglatishi mumkin? Uning u bilan hatto gaplashishi hayratlanarli edi! — lekin bunday xushmuomalalik bilan gaplashishi, uning oilasi haqida so'rashi! U hayotida uning muomalasini hech qachon bunchalik kam salobatli ko'rmagan, u hech qachon bu kutilmagan uchrashuvdagidek muloyimlik bilan gapirmagan edi. Bu uning Rozings parkida xatini qo'liga topshirgandagi oxirgi murojaati bilan qanday qarama-qarshilik edi! U nima deb o'ylashni yoki buni qanday tushuntirishni bilmasdi.

paras.en: They had now entered a beautiful walk by the side of the water, and every step was bringing forward a nobler fall of ground, or a finer reach of the woods to which they were approaching; but it was some time before Elizabeth was sensible of any of it; and, though she answered mechanically to the repeated appeals of her uncle and aunt, and seemed to direct her eyes to such objects as they pointed out, she distinguished no part of the scene. Her thoughts were all fixed on that one spot of Pemberley House, whichever it might be, where Mr. Darcy then was. She longed to know what at the moment was passing in his mind--in what manner he thought of her, and whether, in defiance of everything, she was still dear to him. Perhaps he had been civil only because he felt himself at ease; yet there had been that in his voice which was not like ease. Whether he had felt more of pain or of pleasure in seeing her she could not tell, but he certainly had not seen her with composure.
paras.uz: Endi ular suv bo'yidagi go'zal yo'lakka kirishgan edi va har bir qadam yanada ulug'vorroq yer pasayishini yoki ular yaqinlashayotgan o'rmonlarning yanada chiroyliroq kengligini oldinga chiqarardi; lekin Elizabet ularning birortasini sezishi uchun ancha vaqt kerak bo'ldi; garchi u tog'asi va xolasining qayta-qayta murojaatlariga mexanik ravishda javob bersa va ular ko'rsatgan narsalarga ko'zlarini qaratayotganday ko'rinsa ham, sahnaning hech bir qismini ajrata olmadi. Uning fikrlari butunlay Pemberli uyining o'sha paytda janob Darsi bo'lgan, qaysi bo'lmasin, o'sha bir nuqtasiga qadalgan edi. U o'sha lahzada uning ongida nima o'tayotganini — u u haqida qanday o'ylayotganini va hamma narsaga qaramay u hali ham unga azizmi, yo'qmi, bilishni juda istardi. Ehtimol, u faqat o'zini xotirjam his qilgani uchun xushmuomala bo'lgandir; lekin uning ovozida xotirjamlikka o'xshamaydigan narsa bor edi. U uni ko'rganda ko'proq og'riq yoki ko'proq zavq his qildimi, u ayta olmasdi, lekin u uni xotirjam ko'rmagani aniq edi.

paras.en: At length, however, the remarks of her companions on her absence of mind aroused her, and she felt the necessity of appearing more like herself.
paras.uz: Biroq nihoyat hamrohlarining uning parishonxotirligi haqidagi mulohazalari uni hushyor tortdi va u o'ziga ko'proq o'xshab ko'rinish zarurligini his qildi.

paras.en: They entered the woods, and bidding adieu to the river for a while, ascended some of the higher grounds; when, in spots where the opening of the trees gave the eye power to wander, were many charming views of the valley, the opposite hills, with the long range of woods overspreading many, and occasionally part of the stream. Mr. Gardiner expressed a wish of going round the whole park, but feared it might be beyond a walk. With a triumphant smile they were told that it was ten miles round. It settled the matter; and they pursued the accustomed circuit; which brought them again, after some time, in a descent among hanging woods, to the edge of the water, and one of its narrowest parts.
paras.uz: Ular o'rmonga kirishdi va bir muddat daryo bilan xayrlashib, balandroq joylarga ko'tarilishdi; daraxtlar orasidagi ochiq joylar ko'zga kezishga imkon bergan nuqtalarda vodiyning, ro'paradagi tepaliklarning — ularning ko'pchiligini qoplagan uzun o'rmon qatorlari bilan — va vaqti-vaqti bilan soyning bir qismining ko'plab maftunkor manzaralari ochilardi. Janob Gardiner butun parkni aylanib chiqish istagini bildirdi, lekin bu piyoda yurish uchun haddan tashqari uzoq bo'lishidan qo'rqdi. Ularga g'olibona tabassum bilan uning atrofi o'n mil ekanini aytishdi. Bu masalani hal qildi; va ular odatiy aylanma yo'ldan borishdi, u ularni biroz vaqtdan keyin osilib turgan o'rmonlar orasidan pastga tushib, yana suv bo'yiga, uning eng tor joylaridan biriga olib keldi.

paras.en: They crossed it by a simple bridge, in character with the general air of the scene; it was a spot less adorned than any they had yet visited; and the valley, here contracted into a glen, allowed room only for the stream, and a narrow walk amidst the rough coppice-wood which bordered it. Elizabeth longed to explore its windings; but when they had crossed the bridge, and perceived their distance from the house, Mrs. Gardiner, who was not a great walker, could go no farther, and thought only of returning to the carriage as quickly as possible.
paras.uz: Ular uni sahnaning umumiy ruhiga mos oddiy ko'prik orqali kesib o'tishdi; bu ular hozirgacha tashrif buyurgan har qanday joydan kamroq bezatilgan joy edi; bu yerda tor darachaga aylangan vodiy faqat soy va uni o'rab turgan qo'pol butazor orasidagi tor yo'lak uchun joy qoldirardi. Elizabet uning burilishlarini o'rganishni juda istadi; lekin ular ko'prikni kesib o'tib, uydan qanchalik uzoqda ekanlarini sezganlarida, unchalik yaxshi piyoda yuruvchi bo'lmagan missis Gardiner boshqa yura olmadi va faqat iloji boricha tezroq aravaga qaytishni o'yladi.

paras.en: Her niece was, therefore, obliged to submit, and they took their way towards the house on the opposite side of the river, in the nearest direction; but their progress was slow, for Mr. Gardiner, though seldom able to indulge the taste, was very fond of fishing, and was so much engaged in watching the occasional appearance of some trout in the water, and talking to the man about them, that he advanced but little. Whilst wandering on in this slow manner, they were again surprised, and Elizabeth's astonishment was quite equal to what it had been at first, by the sight of Mr. Darcy approaching them, and at no great distance. The walk being here less sheltered than on the other side, allowed them to see him before they met.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun jiyani bo'ysunishga majbur bo'ldi va ular daryoning narigi tomonidagi eng yaqin yo'nalishda uy tomon yo'l olishdi; lekin ularning harakati sekin edi, chunki janob Gardiner bu didini kamdan-kam qondira olsa ham, baliq ovini juda yaxshi ko'rardi va suvda vaqti-vaqti bilan paydo bo'ladigan gulmohilarni kuzatish va ular haqida odam bilan gaplashish bilan shunchalik band ediki, juda kam oldinga siljidi. Ular shu sekin tarzda kezib yurisharkan, yana hayratda qolishdi va Elizabetning hayrati birinchi marta qanchalik bo'lsa, shunchalik edi — ular janob Darsining unchalik uzoq bo'lmagan masofada ular tomon kelayotganini ko'rishdi. Bu yerdagi yo'lak narigi tomondagidan kamroq panada bo'lgani uchun ularga uchrashishdan oldin uni ko'rish imkonini berdi.

paras.en: Elizabeth, however astonished, was at least more prepared for an interview than before, and resolved to appear and to speak with calmness, if he really intended to meet them. For a few moments, indeed, she felt that he would probably strike into some other path. The idea lasted while a turning in the walk concealed him from their view; the turning past, he was immediately before them. With a glance, she saw that he had lost none of his recent civility; and, to imitate his politeness, she began, as they met, to admire the beauty of the place; but she had not got beyond the words “delightful,” and “charming,” when some unlucky recollections obtruded, and she fancied that praise of Pemberley from her might be mischievously construed. Her colour changed, and she said no more.
paras.uz: Elizabet qanchalik hayratlangan bo'lmasin, hech bo'lmaganda uchrashuvga avvalgidan ko'ra ko'proq tayyor edi va agar u chindan ham ular bilan uchrashmoqchi bo'lsa, xotirjam ko'rinishga va gapirishga qaror qildi. Bir necha lahza u haqiqatan ham u, ehtimol, boshqa yo'lakka burilib ketadi, deb his qildi. Bu fikr yo'lakdagi burilish uni ularning nazaridan yashirgan paytgacha davom etdi; burilish o'tgach, u darhol ularning oldida edi. Bir qarashda u uning yaqindagi xushmuomalaligidan hech narsani yo'qotmaganini ko'rdi; va uning odobiga taqlid qilish uchun, ular uchrashganda joyning go'zalligiga qoyil qola boshladi; lekin u «ajoyib» va «maftunkor» so'zlaridan nariga o'tmasdanoq, ba'zi omadsiz xotiralar bostirib keldi va u uning Pemberlini maqtashi g'arazli talqin qilinishi mumkin, deb tasavvur qildi. Uning rangi o'zgardi va u boshqa gapirmadi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner was standing a little behind; and on her pausing, he asked her if she would do him the honour of introducing him to her friends. This was a stroke of civility for which she was quite unprepared; and she could hardly suppress a smile at his being now seeking the acquaintance of some of those very people against whom his pride had revolted in his offer to herself. “What will be his surprise,” thought she, “when he knows who they are? He takes them now for people of fashion.”
paras.uz: Missis Gardiner biroz orqada turgan edi; u to'xtaganda, u undan uni do'stlari bilan tanishtirish sharafini ko'rsatadimi, deb so'radi. Bu u umuman tayyor bo'lmagan xushmuomalalik zarbasi edi; va u uning g'ururi o'ziga qilgan taklifida isyon qilgan aynan o'sha odamlarning ba'zilari bilan endi tanishishni izlayotganidan jilmayishini zo'rg'a bosdi. «Ular kim ekanini bilganda, qanchalik hayron bo'larkin? — deb o'yladi u. — U hozir ularni yuqori jamiyat odamlari deb hisoblayapti».

paras.en: The introduction, however, was immediately made; and as she named their relationship to herself, she stole a sly look at him, to see how he bore it, and was not without the expectation of his decamping as fast as he could from such disgraceful companions. That he was surprised by the connection was evident; he sustained it, however, with fortitude, and so far from going away, turned back with them, and entered into conversation with Mr. Gardiner. Elizabeth could not but be pleased, could not but triumph. It was consoling that he should know she had some relations for whom there was no need to blush. She listened most attentively to all that passed between them, and gloried in every expression, every sentence of her uncle, which marked his intelligence, his taste, or his good manners.
paras.uz: Biroq tanishtirish darhol amalga oshirildi; va ularning o'ziga qarindoshligini aytarkan, u qanday chidashini ko'rish uchun unga yashirincha ayyorona qaradi va uning bunday sharmandali hamrohlardan iloji boricha tez qochib ketishini kutmasdan emasdi. Uning bu qarindoshlikdan hayratlangani aniq edi; biroq u bunga matonat bilan chidadi va ketishdan yiroq, ular bilan ortga burilib, janob Gardiner bilan suhbatga kirishdi. Elizabet mamnun bo'lmay qololmadi, g'alaba qozonmay qololmadi. Uning uyalishga hojat bo'lmagan qarindoshlari borligini bilishi taskin edi. U ular o'rtasida bo'lib o'tgan hamma narsani eng diqqat bilan tingladi va tog'asining aqli, didi yoki yaxshi muomalasini ko'rsatadigan har bir iborasi, har bir jumlasi bilan faxrlandi.

paras.en: The conversation soon turned upon fishing; and she heard Mr. Darcy invite him, with the greatest civility, to fish there as often as he chose while he continued in the neighbourhood, offering at the same time to supply him with fishing tackle, and pointing out those parts of the stream where there was usually most sport. Mrs. Gardiner, who was walking arm-in-arm with Elizabeth, gave her a look expressive of wonder. Elizabeth said nothing, but it gratified her exceedingly; the compliment must be all for herself. Her astonishment, however, was extreme, and continually was she repeating, “Why is he so altered? From what can it proceed? It cannot be for me--it cannot be for my sake that his manners are thus softened. My reproofs at Hunsford could not work such a change as this. It is impossible that he should still love me.”
paras.uz: Suhbat tez orada baliq oviga burildi; va u janob Darsining uni eng katta xushmuomalalik bilan mahallada qolgan vaqtda xohlagancha bu yerda baliq ovlashga taklif qilganini, shu bilan birga unga baliq ovlash anjomlarini berishni taklif qilganini va soyning odatda eng ko'p ov bo'ladigan joylarini ko'rsatganini eshitdi. Elizabet bilan qo'ltiqlashib ketayotgan missis Gardiner unga hayratni ifodalovchi qarash bilan qaradi. Elizabet hech narsa demadi, lekin bu uni nihoyatda mamnun qildi; iltifot butunlay o'zi uchun bo'lishi kerak edi. Biroq uning hayrati cheksiz edi va u to'xtovsiz takrorlardi: «Nega u bunchalik o'zgardi? Bu nimadan kelib chiqishi mumkin? Bu men uchun bo'lishi mumkin emas — uning muomalasi men tufayli bunchalik yumshagan bo'lishi mumkin emas. Xansforddagi tanbehlarim bunday o'zgarishni qila olmasdi. Uning hali ham meni sevishi imkonsiz».

paras.en: After walking some time in this way, the two ladies in front, the two gentlemen behind, on resuming their places, after descending to the brink of the river for the better inspection of some curious water-plant, there chanced to be a little alteration. It originated in Mrs. Gardiner, who, fatigued by the exercise of the morning, found Elizabeth's arm inadequate to her support, and consequently preferred her husband's. Mr. Darcy took her place by her niece, and they walked on together. After a short silence, the lady first spoke.
paras.uz: Bir muddat shu tarzda — oldinda ikki xonim, orqada ikki janob — yurgach, qandaydir g'aroyib suv o'simligini yaxshiroq ko'rish uchun daryo qirg'og'iga tushib, yana joylarini egallaganda, tasodifan biroz o'zgarish yuz berdi. U ertalabgi harakatdan charchagan va Elizabetning qo'lini tayanch uchun yetarsiz deb topib, shuning uchun erining qo'lini afzal ko'rgan missis Gardinerdan kelib chiqdi. Janob Darsi uning jiyanining yonida uning o'rnini egalladi va ular birga yurishdi. Qisqa sukutdan keyin birinchi bo'lib xonim gapirdi.

paras.en: She wished him to know that she had been assured of his absence before she came to the place, and accordingly began by observing, that his arrival had been very unexpected--“for your housekeeper,” she added, “informed us that you would certainly not be here till to-morrow; and indeed, before we left Bakewell, we understood that you were not immediately expected in the country.” He acknowledged the truth of it all, and said that business with his steward had occasioned his coming forward a few hours before the rest of the party with whom he had been travelling. “They will join me early to-morrow,” he continued, “and among them are some who will claim an acquaintance with you--Mr. Bingley and his sisters.”
paras.uz: U unga bu joyga kelishdan oldin uning yo'qligiga ishontirilganini bilishini istadi va shunga ko'ra uning kelishi juda kutilmagan bo'lganini aytishdan boshladi — «chunki uy bekangiz, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — sizning ertaga qadar bu yerda albatta bo'lmasligingizni aytdi; haqiqatan ham, Beykvelldan chiqishimizdan oldin sizni bu yerlarga darhol kutilmayotganingizni tushungan edik». U bularning hammasi to'g'ri ekanini tan oldi va boshqaruvchisi bilan bo'lgan ish uni birga sayohat qilayotgan davradan bir necha soat oldinroq kelishga majbur qilganini aytdi. «Ular ertaga erta menga qo'shilishadi, — davom etdi u, — ular orasida siz bilan tanish ekanini da'vo qiladiganlar bor — janob Bingli va uning opa-singillari».

paras.en: Elizabeth answered only by a slight bow. Her thoughts were instantly driven back to the time when Mr. Bingley's name had been the last mentioned between them; and, if she might judge by his complexion, his mind was not very differently engaged.
paras.uz: Elizabet faqat yengil ta'zim bilan javob berdi. Uning fikrlari darhol janob Binglining nomi ular o'rtasida oxirgi marta tilga olingan vaqtga qaytdi; va agar yuzining rangiga qarab hukm qilish mumkin bo'lsa, uning ongi ham bundan unchalik farqli narsa bilan band emasdi.

paras.en: “There is also one other person in the party,” he continued after a pause, “who more particularly wishes to be known to you. Will you allow me, or do I ask too much, to introduce my sister to your acquaintance during your stay at Lambton?”
paras.uz: «Davrada yana bir kishi bor, — davom etdi u bir oz sukutdan keyin, — u siz bilan tanishishni ayniqsa istaydi. Lembtonda bo'lgan vaqtingizda singlimni siz bilan tanishtirishimga ruxsat berasizmi yoki ko'p narsa so'rayapmanmi?»

paras.en: The surprise of such an application was great indeed; it was too great for her to know in what manner she acceded to it. She immediately felt that whatever desire Miss Darcy might have of being acquainted with her must be the work of her brother, and, without looking farther, it was satisfactory; it was gratifying to know that his resentment had not made him think really ill of her.
paras.uz: Bunday iltimosning hayrati haqiqatan ham katta edi; u qanday tarzda rozi bo'lganini bilmaslik darajada katta edi. U darhol miss Darsining u bilan tanishishga bo'lgan har qanday istagi akasining ishi bo'lishi kerakligini his qildi va bundan uzoqqa qaramasdan, bu qoniqarli edi; uning g'azabi uni u haqida chindan ham yomon o'ylashga majbur qilmaganini bilish yoqimli edi.

paras.en: They now walked on in silence, each of them deep in thought. Elizabeth was not comfortable; that was impossible; but she was flattered and pleased. His wish of introducing his sister to her was a compliment of the highest kind. They soon outstripped the others, and when they had reached the carriage, Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner were half a quarter of a mile behind.
paras.uz: Endi ular har biri chuqur o'yga botgan holda jimgina yurishdi. Elizabet o'zini qulay his qilmasdi; bu imkonsiz edi; lekin u xushomaddan mamnun va xursand edi. Uning singlisini u bilan tanishtirish istagi eng yuksak darajadagi iltifot edi. Ular tez orada boshqalardan o'zib ketishdi va aravaga yetib kelganlarida, janob va missis Gardiner chorak milning yarmicha orqada edi.

paras.en: He then asked her to walk into the house--but she declared herself not tired, and they stood together on the lawn. At such a time much might have been said, and silence was very awkward. She wanted to talk, but there seemed to be an embargo on every subject. At last she recollected that she had been travelling, and they talked of Matlock and Dove Dale with great perseverance. Yet time and her aunt moved slowly--and her patience and her ideas were nearly worn out before the tete-a-tete was over. On Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner's coming up they were all pressed to go into the house and take some refreshment; but this was declined, and they parted on each side with utmost politeness. Mr. Darcy handed the ladies into the carriage; and when it drove off, Elizabeth saw him walking slowly towards the house.
paras.uz: Keyin u uni uyga kirishga taklif qildi — lekin u charchamaganini aytdi va ular maysazorda birga turishdi. Bunday paytda ko'p narsa aytilishi mumkin edi va sukut juda noqulay edi. U gapirishni istardi, lekin har bir mavzuga taqiq qo'yilganday tuyulardi. Nihoyat u sayohat qilganini esladi va ular Metlok va Douv Deyl haqida katta qat'iyat bilan gaplashishdi. Shunga qaramay, vaqt ham, xolasi ham sekin harakatlanardi — va yuzma-yuz suhbat tugaguncha uning sabri ham, fikrlari ham deyarli tugab qoldi. Janob va missis Gardiner yetib kelgach, hammalarini uyga kirib, biror narsa yeyishga qistashdi; lekin bu rad etildi va ular har ikki tomondan eng katta odob bilan ajralishdi. Janob Darsi xonimlarga aravaga chiqishga yordam berdi; arava jo'nab ketganda, Elizabet uning uy tomon sekin yurib ketayotganini ko'rdi.

paras.en: The observations of her uncle and aunt now began; and each of them pronounced him to be infinitely superior to anything they had expected. “He is perfectly well behaved, polite, and unassuming,” said her uncle.
paras.uz: Endi tog'asi va xolasining mulohazalari boshlandi; ularning har biri uni o'zlari kutgan har qanday narsadan cheksiz darajada ustun deb e'lon qildi. «U mutlaqo yaxshi tarbiyali, xushmuomala va kamtar», — dedi tog'asi.

paras.en: “There is something a little stately in him, to be sure,” replied her aunt, “but it is confined to his air, and is not unbecoming. I can now say with the housekeeper, that though some people may call him proud, I have seen nothing of it.”
paras.uz: «Unda, albatta, biroz salobat bor, — javob berdi xolasi, — lekin bu faqat qiyofasida va unga yarashmaydigan emas. Endi uy bekasi bilan birga ayta olamanki, garchi ba'zi odamlar uni mag'rur deyishsa ham, men bunday narsani ko'rmadim».

paras.en: “I was never more surprised than by his behaviour to us. It was more than civil; it was really attentive; and there was no necessity for such attention. His acquaintance with Elizabeth was very trifling.”
paras.uz: «Uning bizga nisbatan xatti-harakatidan hech qachon bunchalik hayron bo'lmaganman. Bu xushmuomalalikdan ham ortiq edi; bu chinakam e'tibor edi; bunday e'tiborga hech qanday zarurat yo'q edi. Uning Elizabet bilan tanishligi juda arzimas edi».

paras.en: “To be sure, Lizzy,” said her aunt, “he is not so handsome as Wickham; or, rather, he has not Wickham's countenance, for his features are perfectly good. But how came you to tell me that he was so disagreeable?”
paras.uz: «Albatta, Lizzi, — dedi xolasi, — u Uikhem kabi chiroyli emas; aniqrog'i, unda Uikhemning chehrasi yo'q, chunki uning yuz chiziqlari mutlaqo yaxshi. Lekin qanday qilib menga uni bunchalik yoqimsiz deb aytding?»

paras.en: Elizabeth excused herself as well as she could; said that she had liked him better when they had met in Kent than before, and that she had never seen him so pleasant as this morning.
paras.uz: Elizabet iloji boricha o'zini oqladi; u Kentda uchrashganlarida uni avvalgidan ko'ra ko'proq yoqtirganini va uni bugun ertalabgidek yoqimli hech qachon ko'rmaganini aytdi.

paras.en: “But perhaps he may be a little whimsical in his civilities,” replied her uncle. “Your great men often are; and therefore I shall not take him at his word, as he might change his mind another day, and warn me off his grounds.”
paras.uz: «Lekin ehtimol, u xushmuomalaliklarida biroz injiqdir, — javob berdi tog'asi. — Ulug' odamlaringiz ko'pincha shunday bo'ladi; shuning uchun men uning so'ziga ishonib qolmayman, chunki u boshqa kun fikrini o'zgartirib, meni o'z yerlaridan haydab yuborishi mumkin».

paras.en: Elizabeth felt that they had entirely misunderstood his character, but said nothing.
paras.uz: Elizabet ular uning xarakterini butunlay noto'g'ri tushunganini his qildi, lekin hech narsa demadi.

paras.en: “From what we have seen of him,” continued Mrs. Gardiner, “I really should not have thought that he could have behaved in so cruel a way by anybody as he has done by poor Wickham. He has not an ill-natured look. On the contrary, there is something pleasing about his mouth when he speaks. And there is something of dignity in his countenance that would not give one an unfavourable idea of his heart. But, to be sure, the good lady who showed us his house did give him a most flaming character! I could hardly help laughing aloud sometimes. But he is a liberal master, I suppose, and that in the eye of a servant comprehends every virtue.”
paras.uz: «U haqida ko'rganlarimizdan, — davom etdi missis Gardiner, — men haqiqatan ham u bechora Uikhemga qilganidek har kimga nisbatan bunchalik shafqatsiz harakat qila oladi deb o'ylamagan bo'lardim. Uning qiyofasi yomon fe'lli emas. Aksincha, u gapirganda og'zida qandaydir yoqimli narsa bor. Uning chehrasida esa qalbi haqida noxush tasavvur bermaydigan qandaydir salobat bor. Lekin, albatta, bizga uning uyini ko'rsatgan yaxshi xonim unga eng olovli ta'rif berdi! Ba'zan baland ovozda kulmaslikka zo'rg'a tutib turdim. Lekin u saxiy xo'jayin bo'lsa kerak, bu esa xizmatkor nazarida barcha fazilatlarni o'z ichiga oladi».

paras.en: Elizabeth here felt herself called on to say something in vindication of his behaviour to Wickham; and therefore gave them to understand, in as guarded a manner as she could, that by what she had heard from his relations in Kent, his actions were capable of a very different construction; and that his character was by no means so faulty, nor Wickham's so amiable, as they had been considered in Hertfordshire. In confirmation of this, she related the particulars of all the pecuniary transactions in which they had been connected, without actually naming her authority, but stating it to be such as might be relied on.
paras.uz: Shu yerda Elizabet uning Uikhemga nisbatan xatti-harakatini oqlash uchun biror narsa aytishga chaqirilganini his qildi; shuning uchun iloji boricha ehtiyotkorlik bilan ularga Kentdagi qarindoshlaridan eshitganlariga ko'ra uning harakatlarini butunlay boshqacha talqin qilish mumkinligini va uning xarakteri Xertfordshirda hisoblanganidek unchalik aybli emas, Uikhemniki esa unchalik yoqimli emasligini tushuntirdi. Buni tasdiqlash uchun u ular bog'liq bo'lgan barcha pul ishlarining tafsilotlarini aytib berdi, manbasini aniq nomlamasdan, lekin unga ishonish mumkinligini aytib.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner was surprised and concerned; but as they were now approaching the scene of her former pleasures, every idea gave way to the charm of recollection; and she was too much engaged in pointing out to her husband all the interesting spots in its environs to think of anything else. Fatigued as she had been by the morning's walk they had no sooner dined than she set off again in quest of her former acquaintance, and the evening was spent in the satisfactions of a intercourse renewed after many years' discontinuance.
paras.uz: Missis Gardiner hayron va tashvishda qoldi; lekin ular endi uning avvalgi zavqlari sahnasiga yaqinlashayotgani uchun, har qanday fikr xotira jozibasi oldida chekindi; u eriga uning atrofidagi barcha qiziqarli joylarni ko'rsatish bilan shunchalik band ediki, boshqa hech narsa haqida o'ylay olmadi. Ertalabgi sayrdan qanchalik charchagan bo'lmasin, ular tushlik qilishlari bilanoq u yana avvalgi tanishlarini izlab yo'lga chiqdi va oqshom ko'p yillik uzilishdan keyin qayta tiklangan muloqotning mamnuniyatlari bilan o'tdi.

paras.en: The occurrences of the day were too full of interest to leave Elizabeth much attention for any of these new friends; and she could do nothing but think, and think with wonder, of Mr. Darcy's civility, and, above all, of his wishing her to be acquainted with his sister.
paras.uz: Kun voqealari Elizabetga bu yangi do'stlarning birortasiga ko'p e'tibor qoldirmaslik uchun haddan tashqari qiziqarli edi; u faqat janob Darsining xushmuomalaligi va, eng muhimi, uning singlisi bilan tanishishini xohlashi haqida o'ylashdan, hayrat bilan o'ylashdan boshqa hech narsa qila olmadi.

gloss.ex: On applying to see the place, they were admitted into the hall; and Elizabeth, as they waited for the housekeeper, had leisure to wonder at her being where she was.
But I have always observed, that they who are good-natured when children, are good-natured when they grow up; and he was always the sweetest-tempered, most generous-hearted boy in the world.”
She had never seen a place for which nature had done more, or where natural beauty had been so little counteracted by an awkward taste.
Elizabeth thought this was going pretty far; and she listened with increasing astonishment as the housekeeper added, “I have never known a cross word from him in my life, and…
He absolutely started, and for a moment seemed immovable from surprise; but shortly recovering himself, advanced towards the party, and spoke to Elizabeth, if not in terms of perfect composure,…
Darcy invite him, with the greatest civility, to fish there as often as he chose while he continued in the neighbourhood, offering at the same time to supply him with…
There was certainly at this moment, in Elizabeth's mind, a more gentle sensation towards the original than she had ever felt at the height of their acquaintance.

quiz.q: What does the housekeeper say about Darcy?
o: He is the best master and brother
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet Darsini yangi ko'z bilan ko'ra boshlaydi.

quiz.q: How does Darcy behave when he meets Elizabeth and the Gardiners?
quiz.why_uz: U Elizabetning so'zlarini yodda tutib, o'zini o'zgartirgan.

chapters.title: Georgiana
chapters.recap_uz: Darsi singlisi Jorjianani Elizabet bilan tanishtirishga olib keladi. Jorjiana mag'rur emas, faqat uyatchan ekan. Bingley ham keladi va Jeyn haqida so'raydi.

paras.en: Elizabeth had settled it that Mr. Darcy would bring his sister to visit her the very day after her reaching Pemberley; and was consequently resolved not to be out of sight of the inn the whole of that morning. But her conclusion was false; for on the very morning after their arrival at Lambton, these visitors came. They had been walking about the place with some of their new friends, and were just returning to the inn to dress themselves for dining with the same family, when the sound of a carriage drew them to a window, and they saw a gentleman and a lady in a curricle driving up the street. Elizabeth immediately recognizing the livery, guessed what it meant, and imparted no small degree of her surprise to her relations by acquainting them with the honour which she expected.
paras.uz: Elizabet janob Darsi singlisini Pemberliga yetib kelgandan keyingi kuniyoq uni ko'rgani olib keladi, deb hal qilgan edi; shuning uchun o'sha kuni butun ertalab mehmonxonadan ko'zdan uzoqlashmaslikka qaror qildi. Lekin uning xulosasi noto'g'ri edi; chunki bu mehmonlar ular Lembtonga kelgan kunning ertasi ertalabiyoq kelishdi. Ular yangi do'stlaridan ba'zilari bilan atrofni aylanib yurishgan va o'sha oila bilan tushlik qilish uchun kiyinish maqsadida mehmonxonaga endigina qaytayotgan edilar, shu payt arava ovozi ularni deraza oldiga tortdi va ular ko'chada yengil ikki g'ildirakli aravada kelayotgan bir janob va bir xonimni ko'rishdi. Elizabet darhol xizmatkorlar libosini tanib, bu nimani anglatishini taxmin qildi va qarindoshlariga o'zi kutayotgan sharaf haqida xabar berib, ularga hayratining katta qismini yuqtirdi.

paras.en: Her uncle and aunt were all amazement; and the embarrassment of her manner as she spoke, joined to the circumstance itself, and many of the circumstances of the preceding day, opened to them a new idea on the business. Nothing had ever suggested it before, but they felt that there was no other way of accounting for such attentions from such a quarter than by supposing a partiality for their niece. While these newly-born notions were passing in their heads, the perturbation of Elizabeth's feelings was at every moment increasing. She was quite amazed at her own discomposure; but amongst other causes of disquiet, she dreaded lest the partiality of the brother should have said too much in her favour; and, more than commonly anxious to please, she naturally suspected that every power of pleasing would fail her.
paras.uz: Tog'asi va xolasi butunlay hayratda qolishdi; u gapirayotgandagi muomalasidagi xijolat, voqeaning o'zi va oldingi kunning ko'plab holatlari bilan birga, ularga bu ish haqida yangi fikrni ochib berdi. Ilgari hech narsa buni taklif qilmagan edi, lekin ular bunday joydan bunday e'tiborlarni jiyanlariga nisbatan moyillik borligini taxmin qilishdan boshqa yo'l bilan tushuntirib bo'lmasligini his qilishdi. Bu yangi tug'ilgan tushunchalar ularning boshlarida aylanayotganda, Elizabetning tuyg'ularidagi hayajon har lahza ortib bordi. U o'zining bezovtaligidan butunlay hayratda edi; lekin boshqa bezovtalik sabablari qatorida u akaning tarafkashligi uning foydasiga haddan tashqari ko'p gapirgan bo'lishidan qo'rqardi; va odatdagidan ko'ra ko'proq yoqishni istagani uchun, tabiiy ravishda yoqish qobiliyatining hammasi uni tark etadi, deb gumon qildi.

paras.en: She retreated from the window, fearful of being seen; and as she walked up and down the room, endeavouring to compose herself, saw such looks of inquiring surprise in her uncle and aunt as made everything worse.
paras.uz: U ko'rinib qolishdan qo'rqib, deraza oldidan chekindi; va o'zini bosishga urinib, xona bo'ylab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurarkan, tog'asi va xolasining shunday so'roqli hayrat qarashlarini ko'rdiki, bu hamma narsani yanada yomonlashtirdi.

paras.en: Miss Darcy and her brother appeared, and this formidable introduction took place. With astonishment did Elizabeth see that her new acquaintance was at least as much embarrassed as herself. Since her being at Lambton, she had heard that Miss Darcy was exceedingly proud; but the observation of a very few minutes convinced her that she was only exceedingly shy. She found it difficult to obtain even a word from her beyond a monosyllable.
paras.uz: Miss Darsi va uning akasi paydo bo'lishdi va bu qo'rqinchli tanishuv bo'lib o'tdi. Elizabet hayrat bilan yangi tanishining hech bo'lmaganda o'zi kabi xijolatda ekanini ko'rdi. Lembtonga kelganidan beri u miss Darsi nihoyatda mag'rur ekanini eshitgan edi; lekin bir necha daqiqalik kuzatish uni u shunchaki nihoyatda uyatchan ekaniga ishontirdi. Undan bir bo'g'inli so'zdan ortiq hatto bir og'iz so'z olish ham qiyin edi.

paras.en: Miss Darcy was tall, and on a larger scale than Elizabeth; and, though little more than sixteen, her figure was formed, and her appearance womanly and graceful. She was less handsome than her brother; but there was sense and good humour in her face, and her manners were perfectly unassuming and gentle. Elizabeth, who had expected to find in her as acute and unembarrassed an observer as ever Mr. Darcy had been, was much relieved by discerning such different feelings.
paras.uz: Miss Darsi baland bo'yli va Elizabetdan yirikroq edi; garchi o'n oltidan sal oshgan bo'lsa ham, qomati shakllangan, qiyofasi ayollarga xos va nafis edi. U akasidan kamroq chiroyli edi; lekin yuzida aql va xushfe'llik bor edi, muomalasi esa mutlaqo kamtar va muloyim edi. Undan janob Darsi kabi o'tkir va xijolatsiz kuzatuvchini topishni kutgan Elizabet bunchalik boshqacha tuyg'ularni ko'rib, ancha yengil tortdi.

paras.en: They had not long been together before Mr. Darcy told her that Bingley was also coming to wait on her; and she had barely time to express her satisfaction, and prepare for such a visitor, when Bingley's quick step was heard on the stairs, and in a moment he entered the room. All Elizabeth's anger against him had been long done away; but had she still felt any, it could hardly have stood its ground against the unaffected cordiality with which he expressed himself on seeing her again. He inquired in a friendly, though general way, after her family, and looked and spoke with the same good-humoured ease that he had ever done.
paras.uz: Ular birga ko'p bo'lmasdan, janob Darsi unga Bingli ham uni ko'rgani kelayotganini aytdi; u mamnuniyatini bildirishga va bunday mehmonga tayyorlanishga zo'rg'a ulgurdi, zinapoyada Binglining tez qadamlari eshitildi va bir lahzada u xonaga kirdi. Elizabetning unga nisbatan butun g'azabi allaqachon yo'qolgan edi; lekin agar hali ham biroz his qilganida ham, bu uni yana ko'rganda bildirgan samimiy iliqlik oldida zo'rg'a turardi. U do'stona, lekin umumiy tarzda uning oilasi haqida so'radi va har doimgidek xushfe'l yengillik bilan qaradi va gapirdi.

paras.en: To Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner he was scarcely a less interesting personage than to herself. They had long wished to see him. The whole party before them, indeed, excited a lively attention. The suspicions which had just arisen of Mr. Darcy and their niece directed their observation towards each with an earnest though guarded inquiry; and they soon drew from those inquiries the full conviction that one of them at least knew what it was to love. Of the lady's sensations they remained a little in doubt; but that the gentleman was overflowing with admiration was evident enough.
paras.uz: Janob va missis Gardiner uchun u o'zi uchun bo'lganidan kam qiziqarli shaxs emasdi. Ular uni ko'rishni uzoq vaqtdan beri xohlashardi. Haqiqatan ham, oldilaridagi butun davra jonli e'tibor uyg'otdi. Janob Darsi va jiyanlari haqida hozirgina paydo bo'lgan shubhalar ularning kuzatuvini har biriga jiddiy, lekin ehtiyotkor so'roq bilan yo'naltirdi; va ular tez orada bu so'roqlardan ulardan hech bo'lmaganda biri sevish nima ekanini bilishiga to'liq ishonch hosil qilishdi. Xonimning tuyg'ulari haqida ular biroz shubhada qolishdi; lekin janob hayratga to'lib-toshayotgani yetarlicha aniq edi.

paras.en: Elizabeth, on her side, had much to do. She wanted to ascertain the feelings of each of her visitors; she wanted to compose her own, and to make herself agreeable to all; and in the latter object, where she feared most to fail, she was most sure of success, for those to whom she endeavoured to give pleasure were prepossessed in her favour. Bingley was ready, Georgiana was eager, and Darcy determined, to be pleased.
paras.uz: Elizabetning o'z tomonidan qiladigan ishi ko'p edi. U har bir mehmonining tuyg'ularini aniqlamoqchi edi; o'z tuyg'ularini bosmoqchi va hammaga yoqmoqchi edi; va eng ko'p muvaffaqiyatsizlikdan qo'rqqan oxirgi maqsadda u muvaffaqiyatga eng ko'p amin edi, chunki u zavq berishga uringan kishilar allaqachon uning foydasiga moyil edi. Bingli mamnun bo'lishga tayyor, Jorjiana ishtiyoqmand, Darsi esa qat'iy edi.

paras.en: In seeing Bingley, her thoughts naturally flew to her sister; and, oh! how ardently did she long to know whether any of his were directed in a like manner. Sometimes she could fancy that he talked less than on former occasions, and once or twice pleased herself with the notion that, as he looked at her, he was trying to trace a resemblance. But, though this might be imaginary, she could not be deceived as to his behaviour to Miss Darcy, who had been set up as a rival to Jane. No look appeared on either side that spoke particular regard. Nothing occurred between them that could justify the hopes of his sister.
paras.uz: Binglini ko'rib, uning fikrlari tabiiy ravishda opasiga uchdi; va, oh! U uning fikrlaridan birortasi ham xuddi shunday yo'naltirilganmi, yo'qmi, bilishni qanchalik qizg'in istardi. Ba'zan u avvalgi paytlardagidan kamroq gapirayotgandek tuyulardi va bir-ikki marta u unga qaraganda o'xshashlikni topishga urinayotgandir, degan fikr bilan o'zini xursand qildi. Lekin bu xayoliy bo'lishi mumkin bo'lsa ham, u Jeynga raqib qilib ko'rsatilgan miss Darsiga nisbatan uning xatti-harakati haqida aldanishi mumkin emasdi. Hech bir tomondan alohida mehrni bildiruvchi biror qarash ko'rinmadi. Ular o'rtasida uning singlisining umidlarini oqlaydigan hech narsa bo'lmadi.

paras.en: On this point she was soon satisfied; and two or three little circumstances occurred ere they parted, which, in her anxious interpretation, denoted a recollection of Jane not untinctured by tenderness, and a wish of saying more that might lead to the mention of her, had he dared. He observed to her, at a moment when the others were talking together, and in a tone which had something of real regret, that it “was a very long time since he had had the pleasure of seeing her;” and, before she could reply, he added, “It is above eight months. We have not met since the 26th of November, when we were all dancing together at Netherfield.”
paras.uz: Bu masalada u tez orada qanoat hosil qildi; va ular ajralishidan oldin ikki-uch kichik holat yuz berdi, ular uning xavotirli talqinida Jeynni muloyimliksiz bo'lmagan holda eslashni va agar jur'at etganida, uni tilga olishga olib kelishi mumkin bo'lgan ko'proq narsa aytish istagini bildirardi. U boshqalar o'zaro gaplashayotgan bir lahzada, haqiqiy afsusga o'xshash ohangda unga «uni ko'rish zavqiga muyassar bo'lmaganiga juda uzoq vaqt bo'ldi» dedi; va u javob berishga ulgurmasdanoq qo'shib qo'ydi: «Sakkiz oydan oshdi. Biz Nezerfildda hammamiz birga raqs tushgan 26-noyabrdan beri uchrashmadik».

paras.en: Elizabeth was pleased to find his memory so exact; and he afterwards took occasion to ask her, when unattended to by any of the rest, whether all her sisters were at Longbourn. There was not much in the question, nor in the preceding remark; but there was a look and a manner which gave them meaning.
paras.uz: Elizabet uning xotirasi bunchalik aniq ekanini ko'rib xursand bo'ldi; keyinroq u boshqalarning hech biri e'tibor bermagan paytda undan barcha opa-singillari Longborndami, deb so'rash imkoniyatini topdi. Savolda ham, oldingi gapda ham ko'p narsa yo'q edi; lekin ularga ma'no beradigan qarash va ohang bor edi.

paras.en: It was not often that she could turn her eyes on Mr. Darcy himself; but, whenever she did catch a glimpse, she saw an expression of general complaisance, and in all that he said she heard an accent so removed from hauteur or disdain of his companions, as convinced her that the improvement of manners which she had yesterday witnessed however temporary its existence might prove, had at least outlived one day.
paras.uz: U janob Darsining o'ziga tez-tez ko'z qarata olmasdi; lekin har safar bir qarab qolganda, umumiy xushmuomalalik ifodasini ko'rdi va uning aytgan hamma narsasida hamrohlariga nisbatan kibr yoki mensimaslikdan shunchalik yiroq ohangni eshitdiki, bu uni kecha guvoh bo'lgan muomaladagi yaxshilanish qanchalik vaqtinchalik bo'lib chiqmasin, hech bo'lmaganda bir kundan ortiq yashaganiga ishontirdi.

paras.en: When she saw him thus seeking the acquaintance and courting the good opinion of people with whom any intercourse a few months ago would have been a disgrace--when she saw him thus civil, not only to herself, but to the very relations whom he had openly disdained, and recollected their last lively scene in Hunsford Parsonage--the difference, the change was so great, and struck so forcibly on her mind, that she could hardly restrain her astonishment from being visible.
paras.uz: U uni bir necha oy oldin har qanday muloqot sharmandalik bo'lgan odamlarning tanishligini izlayotgan va yaxshi fikrini qozonishga urinayotgan holda ko'rganda — uni nafaqat o'ziga, balki ochiqchasiga mensimagan aynan o'sha qarindoshlarga nisbatan shunday xushmuomala ko'rganda va Xansford ruhoniy uyidagi oxirgi jonli sahnalarini eslaganda — farq, o'zgarish shunchalik katta edi va uning ongiga shunchalik kuchli ta'sir qildiki, u hayratini ko'rinib qolishdan zo'rg'a tiya oldi.

paras.en: Never, even in the company of his dear friends at Netherfield, or his dignified relations at Rosings, had she seen him so desirous to please, so free from self-consequence or unbending reserve, as now, when no importance could result from the success of his endeavours, and when even the acquaintance of those to whom his attentions were addressed would draw down the ridicule and censure of the ladies both of Netherfield and Rosings.
paras.uz: U hech qachon, hatto Nezerfilddagi aziz do'stlari yoki Rozingsdagi salobatli qarindoshlari davrasida ham, uni hozirgidek yoqishga bunchalik intilgan, o'zini muhim sanash yoki egilmas vazminlikdan bunchalik xoli holda ko'rmagan edi — hozir uning sa'y-harakatlari muvaffaqiyatidan hech qanday ahamiyat kelib chiqmasa ham va hatto uning e'tiborlari qaratilgan kishilar bilan tanishligi Nezerfild va Rozingsdagi xonimlarning masxarasi va tanbehini tortsa ham.

paras.en: Their visitors stayed with them above half-an-hour; and when they arose to depart, Mr. Darcy called on his sister to join him in expressing their wish of seeing Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner, and Miss Bennet, to dinner at Pemberley, before they left the country. Miss Darcy, though with a diffidence which marked her little in the habit of giving invitations, readily obeyed. Mrs. Gardiner looked at her niece, desirous of knowing how she, whom the invitation most concerned, felt disposed as to its acceptance, but Elizabeth had turned away her head. Presuming however, that this studied avoidance spoke rather a momentary embarrassment than any dislike of the proposal, and seeing in her husband, who was fond of society, a perfect willingness to accept it, she ventured to engage for her attendance, and the day after the next was fixed on.
paras.uz: Mehmonlar ular bilan yarim soatdan ortiq qolishdi; ketish uchun turishganda, janob Darsi singlisini janob va missis Gardiner hamda miss Bennetni bu yerlarni tark etishlaridan oldin Pemberliga tushlikka ko'rish istaklarini bildirishda unga qo'shilishga chaqirdi. Miss Darsi taklif qilishga unchalik odatlanmaganini ko'rsatadigan tortinchoqlik bilan bo'lsa ham, darhol itoat qildi. Missis Gardiner taklif eng ko'p tegishli bo'lgan jiyani uni qabul qilishga qanday moyil ekanini bilishni istab, unga qaradi, lekin Elizabet boshini o'girgan edi. Biroq bu ataylab qochish taklifga biror yoqtirmaslikdan ko'ra lahzalik xijolatni bildiradi deb taxmin qilib va jamiyatni yaxshi ko'radigan erida uni qabul qilishga to'liq tayyorlikni ko'rib, u uning kelishiga va'da berishga jur'at qildi va indinga belgilandi.

paras.en: Bingley expressed great pleasure in the certainty of seeing Elizabeth again, having still a great deal to say to her, and many inquiries to make after all their Hertfordshire friends. Elizabeth, construing all this into a wish of hearing her speak of her sister, was pleased, and on this account, as well as some others, found herself, when their visitors left them, capable of considering the last half-hour with some satisfaction, though while it was passing, the enjoyment of it had been little. Eager to be alone, and fearful of inquiries or hints from her uncle and aunt, she stayed with them only long enough to hear their favourable opinion of Bingley, and then hurried away to dress.
paras.uz: Bingli Elizabetni yana ko'rishiga amin bo'lganidan katta mamnuniyat bildirdi, chunki unga hali aytadigan ko'p gaplari va Xertfordshirdagi barcha do'stlari haqida so'raydigan ko'p savollari bor edi. Elizabet bularning hammasini uning opasi haqida gapirishini eshitish istagi deb talqin qilib, xursand bo'ldi va shu sababli, shuningdek boshqa ba'zi sabablarga ko'ra, mehmonlar ketgach, o'tgan yarim soatni biroz mamnuniyat bilan o'ylay olishini his qildi, garchi u o'tayotganda undan oz zavq olgan bo'lsa ham. Yolg'iz qolishga intilib va tog'asi hamda xolasining so'roqlari yoki ishoralaridan qo'rqib, u ular bilan faqat ularning Bingli haqidagi ijobiy fikrlarini eshitish uchun yetarlicha qoldi, keyin kiyinish uchun shoshilib ketdi.

paras.en: But she had no reason to fear Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner's curiosity; it was not their wish to force her communication. It was evident that she was much better acquainted with Mr. Darcy than they had before any idea of; it was evident that he was very much in love with her. They saw much to interest, but nothing to justify inquiry.
paras.uz: Lekin janob va missis Gardinerning qiziqishidan qo'rqish uchun uning sababi yo'q edi; ular uni gapirishga majburlashni istamasdilar. U janob Darsi bilan ular avval tasavvur qilganidan ancha yaxshiroq tanish ekani aniq edi; u unga juda oshiq ekani aniq edi. Ular qiziqtiradigan ko'p narsani ko'rdilar, lekin so'roqni oqlaydigan hech narsani ko'rmadilar.

paras.en: Of Mr. Darcy it was now a matter of anxiety to think well; and, as far as their acquaintance reached, there was no fault to find. They could not be untouched by his politeness; and had they drawn his character from their own feelings and his servant's report, without any reference to any other account, the circle in Hertfordshire to which he was known would not have recognized it for Mr. Darcy. There was now an interest, however, in believing the housekeeper; and they soon became sensible that the authority of a servant who had known him since he was four years old, and whose own manners indicated respectability, was not to be hastily rejected. Neither had anything occurred in the intelligence of their Lambton friends that could materially lessen its weight. They had nothing to accuse him of but pride; pride he probably had, and if not, it would certainly be imputed by the inhabitants of a small market-town where the family did not visit. It was acknowledged, however, that he was a liberal man, and did much good among the poor.
paras.uz: Endi janob Darsi haqida yaxshi o'ylash tashvishli masala edi; va tanishliklari qanchalik yetsa, ayb topadigan hech narsa yo'q edi. Ular uning xushmuomalaligidan ta'sirlanmay qola olmasdilar; agar ular uning xarakterini boshqa hech qanday hikoyaga murojaat qilmasdan o'z tuyg'ulari va xizmatkorining hisobotidan chiqarganlarida, uni taniydigan Xertfordshir davrasi uni janob Darsi deb tanimagan bo'lardi. Biroq endi uy bekasiga ishonishga qiziqish bor edi; va ular tez orada uni to'rt yoshidan beri bilgan va o'z muomalasi hurmatlilikni ko'rsatadigan xizmatkorning guvohligini shoshilib rad etib bo'lmasligini tushunishdi. Lembtondagi do'stlarining ma'lumotlarida ham uning salmog'ini jiddiy kamaytira oladigan hech narsa bo'lmagan edi. Ular uni g'ururdan boshqa narsada ayblay olmasdilar; g'urur unda, ehtimol, bor edi, agar bo'lmasa ham, oila bormaydigan kichik bozor shaharchasi aholisi uni albatta unga yuklagan bo'lardi. Biroq uning saxiy odam ekani va kambag'allar orasida ko'p yaxshilik qilishi tan olinardi.

paras.en: With respect to Wickham, the travellers soon found that he was not held there in much estimation; for though the chief of his concerns with the son of his patron were imperfectly understood, it was yet a well-known fact that, on his quitting Derbyshire, he had left many debts behind him, which Mr. Darcy afterwards discharged.
paras.uz: Uikhemga kelsak, sayohatchilar tez orada u yerda uni unchalik qadrlamasliklarini bilib olishdi; chunki uning homiysining o'g'li bilan asosiy munosabatlari to'liq tushunilmagan bo'lsa ham, u Derbishirni tark etganda ortida ko'p qarzlar qoldirgani, ularni keyinroq janob Darsi to'lagani hammaga ma'lum fakt edi.

paras.en: As for Elizabeth, her thoughts were at Pemberley this evening more than the last; and the evening, though as it passed it seemed long, was not long enough to determine her feelings towards one in that mansion; and she lay awake two whole hours endeavouring to make them out. She certainly did not hate him. No; hatred had vanished long ago, and she had almost as long been ashamed of ever feeling a dislike against him, that could be so called. The respect created by the conviction of his valuable qualities, though at first unwillingly admitted, had for some time ceased to be repugnant to her feeling; and it was now heightened into somewhat of a friendlier nature, by the testimony so highly in his favour, and bringing forward his disposition in so amiable a light, which yesterday had produced.
paras.uz: Elizabetga kelsak, uning fikrlari bu oqshom avvalgisidan ko'ra ko'proq Pemberlida edi; oqshom o'tayotganda uzoq tuyulsa ham, o'sha saroydagi bir kishiga nisbatan tuyg'ularini aniqlash uchun yetarlicha uzoq emasdi; va u ularni tushunishga urinib, butun ikki soat uyg'oq yotdi. U undan, albatta, nafratlanmasdi. Yo'q; nafrat allaqachon yo'qolgan edi va u deyarli shuncha vaqtdan beri unga nisbatan shunday deb atash mumkin bo'lgan yoqtirmaslik his qilganidan uyalardi. Uning qimmatli fazilatlariga bo'lgan ishonchdan tug'ilgan hurmat, avvaliga istamay tan olingan bo'lsa ham, bir muncha vaqtdan beri uning tuyg'ulariga yot bo'lmay qolgan edi; endi esa kecha paydo bo'lgan, uning foydasiga shunchalik yuqori va uning fe'lini shunchalik yoqimli tarzda ko'rsatgan guvohlik tufayli biroz do'stonaroq tabiatga ko'tarilgan edi.

paras.en: But above all, above respect and esteem, there was a motive within her of goodwill which could not be overlooked. It was gratitude; gratitude, not merely for having once loved her, but for loving her still well enough to forgive all the petulance and acrimony of her manner in rejecting him, and all the unjust accusations accompanying her rejection. He who, she had been persuaded, would avoid her as his greatest enemy, seemed, on this accidental meeting, most eager to preserve the acquaintance, and without any indelicate display of regard, or any peculiarity of manner, where their two selves only were concerned, was soliciting the good opinion of her friends, and bent on making her known to his sister.
paras.uz: Lekin hammadan ustun, hurmat va qadrlashdan ustun, uning ichida e'tiborsiz qoldirib bo'lmaydigan xayrixohlik sababi bor edi. Bu minnatdorlik edi; nafaqat uni bir paytlar sevgani uchun, balki uni rad etishdagi barcha injiqlik va achchiqlikni, rad etishga hamroh bo'lgan barcha adolatsiz ayblovlarni kechiradigan darajada hali ham uni sevgani uchun minnatdorlik. U o'zining eng katta dushmani sifatida undan qochadi deb ishongan odam bu tasodifiy uchrashuvda tanishlikni saqlashga eng ko'p intilganday ko'rindi va faqat ikkalasiga tegishli bo'lgan joyda hech qanday nozikliksiz mehr namoyishi yoki muomaladagi biror o'ziga xoslik ko'rsatmasdan, uning do'stlarining yaxshi fikrini so'rayotgan va uni singlisi bilan tanishtirishga qat'iy ahd qilgan edi.

paras.en: Such a change in a man of so much pride exciting not only astonishment but gratitude--for to love, ardent love, it must be attributed; and as such its impression on her was of a sort to be encouraged, as by no means unpleasing, though it could not be exactly defined. She respected, she esteemed, she was grateful to him, she felt a real interest in his welfare; and she only wanted to know how far she wished that welfare to depend upon herself, and how far it would be for the happiness of both that she should employ the power, which her fancy told her she still possessed, of bringing on her the renewal of his addresses.
paras.uz: Bunchalik mag'rur odamdagi bunday o'zgarish nafaqat hayrat, balki minnatdorlik ham uyg'otardi — chunki buni muhabbatga, qizg'in muhabbatga bog'lash kerak edi; va shunday bo'lgani uchun uning unga ta'siri aniq ta'riflab bo'lmasa ham, umuman yoqimsiz bo'lmagani uchun rag'batlantiriladigan turdagi edi. U uni hurmat qilardi, qadrlardi, unga minnatdor edi, uning farovonligiga chinakam qiziqish his qilardi; va u faqat bu farovonlik o'ziga qanchalik bog'liq bo'lishini istashini va xayoli hali ham ega ekanini aytayotgan uning murojaatlarini yangilashga olib kelish kuchidan foydalanishi ikkalasining baxti uchun qanchalik bo'lishini bilishni istardi.

paras.en: It had been settled in the evening between the aunt and the niece, that such a striking civility as Miss Darcy's in coming to see them on the very day of her arrival at Pemberley, for she had reached it only to a late breakfast, ought to be imitated, though it could not be equalled, by some exertion of politeness on their side; and, consequently, that it would be highly expedient to wait on her at Pemberley the following morning. They were, therefore, to go. Elizabeth was pleased; though when she asked herself the reason, she had very little to say in reply.
paras.uz: Kechqurun xola va jiyan o'rtasida kelishib olindiki, miss Darsining Pemberliga kelgan kunining o'zida — chunki u u yerga faqat kech nonushtaga yetib kelgan edi — ularni ko'rgani kelishidek bunday hayratlanarli xushmuomalalikka, unga tenglashib bo'lmasa ham, ular tomonidan biror xushmuomalalik harakati bilan taqlid qilish kerak; va shuning uchun ertasi kuni ertalab uni Pemberlida ziyorat qilish juda maqsadga muvofiq bo'ladi. Shunday qilib, ular borishlari kerak edi. Elizabet xursand edi; garchi o'zidan buning sababini so'raganda, javob berish uchun juda kam gapi bo'lsa ham.

paras.en: Mr. Gardiner left them soon after breakfast. The fishing scheme had been renewed the day before, and a positive engagement made of his meeting some of the gentlemen at Pemberley before noon.
paras.uz: Janob Gardiner nonushtadan ko'p o'tmay ularni tark etdi. Baliq ovi rejasi kecha yangilangan edi va uning tushgacha Pemberlida ba'zi janoblar bilan uchrashishi haqida aniq kelishuv qilingan edi.

gloss.ex: Since her being at Lambton, she had heard that Miss Darcy was exceedingly proud; but the observation of a very few minutes convinced her that she was only exceedingly shy.
Bingley was ready, Georgiana was eager, and Darcy determined, to be pleased.
It was gratitude; gratitude, not merely for having once loved her, but for loving her still well enough to forgive all the petulance and acrimony of her manner in rejecting…
Nothing had ever suggested it before, but they felt that there was no other way of accounting for such attentions from such a quarter than by supposing a partiality for…
No look appeared on either side that spoke particular regard.
Her uncle and aunt were all amazement; and the embarrassment of her manner as she spoke, joined to the circumstance itself, and many of the circumstances of the preceding day,…
With astonishment did Elizabeth see that her new acquaintance was at least as much embarrassed as herself.

quiz.q: What is Georgiana really like?
quiz.why_uz: Uikhem uni mag'rur deb yolg'on gapirgan edi.

quiz.q: What does Elizabeth begin to feel for Darcy?
quiz.why_uz: Uning tuyg'ulari o'zgarib bormoqda.

chapters.title: Miss Bingley's Jealousy
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet Pemberlida Jorjianani ko'rgani boradi. Miss Bingli rashk bilan Uikhem haqida gap ochadi, lekin Jorjiana xijolat bo'ladi. Darsi Elizabetni eng chiroyli ayollardan biri deb tan oladi.

paras.en: Convinced as Elizabeth now was that Miss Bingley's dislike of her had originated in jealousy, she could not help feeling how unwelcome her appearance at Pemberley must be to her, and was curious to know with how much civility on that lady's side the acquaintance would now be renewed.
paras.uz: Elizabet endi miss Binglining uni yoqtirmasligi hasaddan kelib chiqqaniga ishonch hosil qilgani uchun, uning Pemberlida paydo bo'lishi unga qanchalik yoqimsiz bo'lishi kerakligini his qilmay qololmadi va tanishlik endi o'sha xonim tomonidan qanchalik xushmuomalalik bilan yangilanishini bilishga qiziqdi.

paras.en: On reaching the house, they were shown through the hall into the saloon, whose northern aspect rendered it delightful for summer. Its windows opening to the ground, admitted a most refreshing view of the high woody hills behind the house, and of the beautiful oaks and Spanish chestnuts which were scattered over the intermediate lawn.
paras.uz: Uyga yetib kelgach, ularni zal orqali shimolga qaragani uchun yozda juda yoqimli bo'lgan mehmonxonaga olib kirishdi. Uning yerga qadar ochiladigan derazalari uyning orqasidagi baland o'rmonli tepaliklarning va oradagi maysazorga sochilgan chiroyli eman va kashtan daraxtlarining eng tetiklantiruvchi manzarasini ochardi.

paras.en: In this house they were received by Miss Darcy, who was sitting there with Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley, and the lady with whom she lived in London. Georgiana's reception of them was very civil, but attended with all the embarrassment which, though proceeding from shyness and the fear of doing wrong, would easily give to those who felt themselves inferior the belief of her being proud and reserved. Mrs. Gardiner and her niece, however, did her justice, and pitied her.
paras.uz: Bu uyda ularni missis Xerst va miss Bingli hamda Londonda u bilan yashaydigan xonim bilan o'tirgan miss Darsi qabul qildi. Jorjiananing ularni qabul qilishi juda xushmuomala edi, lekin uyatchanlik va xato qilish qo'rquvidan kelib chiqsa ham, o'zlarini past his qiladiganlarga uning mag'rur va vazmin ekani haqida osongina ishonch beradigan butun xijolat bilan birga edi. Biroq missis Gardiner va uning jiyani unga adolat ko'rsatishdi va unga achinishdi.

paras.en: By Mrs. Hurst and Miss Bingley they were noticed only by a curtsey; and, on their being seated, a pause, awkward as such pauses must always be, succeeded for a few moments. It was first broken by Mrs. Annesley, a genteel, agreeable-looking woman, whose endeavour to introduce some kind of discourse proved her to be more truly well-bred than either of the others; and between her and Mrs. Gardiner, with occasional help from Elizabeth, the conversation was carried on.
