Miss Darcy looked as if she wished for courage enough to join in it; and sometimes did venture a short sentence when there was least danger of its being heard.
paras.uz: Missis Xerst va miss Bingli ularga faqat ta'zim bilan e'tibor berishdi; ular o'tirgach, bir necha lahza bunday sukutlar doim bo'lganidek noqulay sukut cho'kdi. Uni birinchi bo'lib odobli, yoqimli ko'rinishli ayol missis Ennsli buzdi, uning qandaydir suhbat boshlashga urinishi uni qolgan ikkalasidan ko'ra chinakam yaxshiroq tarbiyalangan ekanini isbotladi; va suhbat u bilan missis Gardiner o'rtasida, vaqti-vaqti bilan Elizabetning yordami bilan davom etdi. Miss Darsi unga qo'shilish uchun yetarlicha jasoratga ega bo'lishni istayotganday ko'rinardi; va ba'zan eshitilish xavfi eng kam bo'lgan paytda qisqa jumla aytishga jur'at etardi.

paras.en: Elizabeth soon saw that she was herself closely watched by Miss Bingley, and that she could not speak a word, especially to Miss Darcy, without calling her attention. This observation would not have prevented her from trying to talk to the latter, had they not been seated at an inconvenient distance; but she was not sorry to be spared the necessity of saying much. Her own thoughts were employing her. She expected every moment that some of the gentlemen would enter the room. She wished, she feared that the master of the house might be amongst them; and whether she wished or feared it most, she could scarcely determine. After sitting in this manner a quarter of an hour without hearing Miss Bingley's voice, Elizabeth was roused by receiving from her a cold inquiry after the health of her family. She answered with equal indifference and brevity, and the other said no more.
paras.uz: Elizabet tez orada miss Bingli uni diqqat bilan kuzatayotganini va ayniqsa miss Darsiga bir og'iz ham gapirsa, uning e'tiborini tortishini ko'rdi. Agar ular noqulay masofada o'tirmaganlarida, bu kuzatuv uni ikkinchisi bilan gaplashishga urinishdan to'xtatmagan bo'lardi; lekin u ko'p gapirish zaruratidan qutulganidan afsuslanmadi. Uni o'z fikrlari band qilardi. U har lahza janoblardan ba'zilari xonaga kirishini kutardi. U uy egasi ular orasida bo'lishini istardi, bundan qo'rqardi ham; va ko'proq istaydimi yoki ko'proq qo'rqadimi, buni zo'rg'a aniqlay olardi. Miss Binglining ovozini eshitmay chorak soat shu tarzda o'tirgach, Elizabetni undan oilasining sog'lig'i haqida sovuq so'roq olish hushyor tortdi. U xuddi shunday befarqlik va qisqalik bilan javob berdi va ikkinchisi boshqa gapirmadi.

paras.en: The next variation which their visit afforded was produced by the entrance of servants with cold meat, cake, and a variety of all the finest fruits in season; but this did not take place till after many a significant look and smile from Mrs. Annesley to Miss Darcy had been given, to remind her of her post. There was now employment for the whole party--for though they could not all talk, they could all eat; and the beautiful pyramids of grapes, nectarines, and peaches soon collected them round the table.
paras.uz: Ularning tashrifidagi keyingi o'zgarish xizmatkorlarning sovuq go'sht, pirog va mavsumdagi eng zo'r mevalarning xilma-xili bilan kirib kelishidan kelib chiqdi; lekin bu missis Ennslining miss Darsiga uning vazifasini eslatish uchun ko'p ma'noli qarash va tabassumlaridan keyingina sodir bo'ldi. Endi butun davra uchun mashg'ulot bor edi — chunki ularning hammasi gapira olmasa ham, hammasi yeya olardi; uzum, nektarin va shaftolining chiroyli piramidalari tez orada ularni stol atrofiga to'pladi.

paras.en: While thus engaged, Elizabeth had a fair opportunity of deciding whether she most feared or wished for the appearance of Mr. Darcy, by the feelings which prevailed on his entering the room; and then, though but a moment before she had believed her wishes to predominate, she began to regret that he came.
paras.uz: Shunday band bo'lgan paytda Elizabet janob Darsi xonaga kirganida ustun kelgan tuyg'ulariga qarab, uning paydo bo'lishidan ko'proq qo'rqadimi yoki ko'proq istaydimi, buni aniqlash uchun yaxshi imkoniyatga ega bo'ldi; shunda, bir lahza oldin istaklari ustun deb ishongan bo'lsa ham, uning kelganidan afsuslana boshladi.

paras.en: He had been some time with Mr. Gardiner, who, with two or three other gentlemen from the house, was engaged by the river, and had left him only on learning that the ladies of the family intended a visit to Georgiana that morning. No sooner did he appear than Elizabeth wisely resolved to be perfectly easy and unembarrassed; a resolution the more necessary to be made, but perhaps not the more easily kept, because she saw that the suspicions of the whole party were awakened against them, and that there was scarcely an eye which did not watch his behaviour when he first came into the room.
paras.uz: U bir muddat uydan ikki-uch boshqa janob bilan daryo bo'yida band bo'lgan janob Gardiner bilan birga bo'lgan va oila xonimlari o'sha ertalab Jorjianani ziyorat qilmoqchi ekanini bilgandagina uni tark etgan edi. U paydo bo'lishi bilanoq Elizabet oqilona ravishda mutlaqo xotirjam va xijolatsiz bo'lishga qaror qildi; bu qaror ancha zarur, lekin, ehtimol, saqlash osonroq bo'lmagan qaror edi, chunki u butun davraning ularga qarshi shubhalari uyg'onganini va u xonaga birinchi kirganda uning xatti-harakatini kuzatmagan ko'z deyarli yo'qligini ko'rdi.

paras.en: In no countenance was attentive curiosity so strongly marked as in Miss Bingley's, in spite of the smiles which overspread her face whenever she spoke to one of its objects; for jealousy had not yet made her desperate, and her attentions to Mr. Darcy were by no means over. Miss Darcy, on her brother's entrance, exerted herself much more to talk, and Elizabeth saw that he was anxious for his sister and herself to get acquainted, and forwarded as much as possible, every attempt at conversation on either side. Miss Bingley saw all this likewise; and, in the imprudence of anger, took the first opportunity of saying, with sneering civility:
paras.uz: Hech kimning chehrasida diqqatli qiziqish miss Binglinikidagidek kuchli namoyon bo'lmagan edi, garchi u qiziqish obyektlaridan biriga gapirganda yuzini tabassum qoplasa ham; chunki hasad uni hali umidsizlikka solmagan edi va uning janob Darsiga e'tiborlari aslo tugamagan edi. Miss Darsi akasi kirganda gapirish uchun ancha ko'proq harakat qildi va Elizabet uning singlisi bilan o'zi tanishishlarini istayotganini va har ikki tomondan suhbatga bo'lgan har bir urinishni iloji boricha qo'llab-quvvatlayotganini ko'rdi. Miss Bingli ham bularning hammasini ko'rdi; va g'azabning ehtiyotsizligida birinchi imkoniyatdan foydalanib, kesatiqli xushmuomalalik bilan dedi:

paras.en: “Pray, Miss Eliza, are not the ----shire Militia removed from Meryton? They must be a great loss to your family.”
paras.uz: «Iltimos, miss Eliza, ----shir militsiyasi Meritondan ketmadimi? Bu oilangiz uchun katta yo'qotish bo'lsa kerak».

paras.en: In Darcy's presence she dared not mention Wickham's name; but Elizabeth instantly comprehended that he was uppermost in her thoughts; and the various recollections connected with him gave her a moment's distress; but exerting herself vigorously to repel the ill-natured attack, she presently answered the question in a tolerably detached tone. While she spoke, an involuntary glance showed her Darcy, with a heightened complexion, earnestly looking at her, and his sister overcome with confusion, and unable to lift up her eyes.
paras.uz: Darsining huzurida u Uikhemning nomini tilga olishga jur'at etmadi; lekin Elizabet darhol u uning fikrlarida birinchi o'rinda ekanini tushundi; u bilan bog'liq turli xotiralar unga bir lahza tashvish berdi; lekin bu g'arazli hujumni qaytarish uchun qattiq kuch sarflab, u tez orada savolga ancha befarq ohangda javob berdi. U gapirayotganda, beixtiyor bir qarash unga yuzi qizargan holda unga diqqat bilan qarab turgan Darsini va sarosimadan ko'zlarini ko'tara olmayotgan uning singlisini ko'rsatdi.

paras.en: Had Miss Bingley known what pain she was then giving her beloved friend, she undoubtedly would have refrained from the hint; but she had merely intended to discompose Elizabeth by bringing forward the idea of a man to whom she believed her partial, to make her betray a sensibility which might injure her in Darcy's opinion, and, perhaps, to remind the latter of all the follies and absurdities by which some part of her family were connected with that corps. Not a syllable had ever reached her of Miss Darcy's meditated elopement. To no creature had it been revealed, where secrecy was possible, except to Elizabeth; and from all Bingley's connections her brother was particularly anxious to conceal it, from the very wish which Elizabeth had long ago attributed to him, of their becoming hereafter her own.
paras.uz: Agar miss Bingli o'shanda sevimli dugonasiga qanday og'riq berayotganini bilganida, shubhasiz, bu ishoradan o'zini tiygan bo'lardi; lekin u faqat Elizabetni u moyil deb ishongan erkak haqidagi fikrni ilgari surib, xijolatga solmoqchi, uni Darsining fikrida unga zarar yetkazishi mumkin bo'lgan ta'sirchanlikni oshkor qilishga majbur qilmoqchi va, ehtimol, ikkinchisiga uning oilasining bir qismi o'sha polk bilan bog'liq bo'lgan barcha ahmoqliklar va bema'niliklarni eslatmoqchi edi. Miss Darsining rejalashtirilgan qochishi haqida unga hech qachon bir bo'g'in ham yetib bormagan edi. Sir saqlash mumkin bo'lgan joyda u Elizabetdan boshqa hech bir mavjudotga oshkor qilinmagan edi; akasi esa uni ayniqsa Binglining barcha qarindoshlaridan yashirishga intilardi, aynan Elizabet uzoq vaqt oldin unga bog'lagan, ular kelajakda o'z qarindoshlariga aylanishi istagi tufayli.

paras.en: He had certainly formed such a plan, and without meaning that it should affect his endeavour to separate him from Miss Bennet, it is probable that it might add something to his lively concern for the welfare of his friend.
paras.uz: U, albatta, bunday reja tuzgan edi va uni do'stini miss Bennetdan ajratishga urinishiga ta'sir qilishini niyat qilmagan bo'lsa ham, ehtimol, bu do'stining farovonligi uchun uning jonli tashvishiga biroz qo'shgan bo'lishi mumkin edi.

paras.en: Elizabeth's collected behaviour, however, soon quieted his emotion; and as Miss Bingley, vexed and disappointed, dared not approach nearer to Wickham, Georgiana also recovered in time, though not enough to be able to speak any more. Her brother, whose eye she feared to meet, scarcely recollected her interest in the affair, and the very circumstance which had been designed to turn his thoughts from Elizabeth seemed to have fixed them on her more and more cheerfully.
paras.uz: Biroq Elizabetning vazmin xatti-harakati tez orada uning hayajonini bosdi; g'ashlangan va hafsalasi pir bo'lgan miss Bingli Uikhemga yaqinroq yaqinlashishga jur'at etmagani uchun, Jorjiana ham vaqt o'tib o'ziga keldi, garchi boshqa gapira oladigan darajada bo'lmasa ham. U ko'zi bilan uchrashishdan qo'rqqan akasi bu ishdagi uning ishtirokini deyarli eslamadi va uning fikrlarini Elizabetdan chalg'itish uchun mo'ljallangan aynan o'sha holat ularni unga tobora quvnoqroq qadagandek tuyuldi.

paras.en: Their visit did not continue long after the question and answer above mentioned; and while Mr. Darcy was attending them to their carriage Miss Bingley was venting her feelings in criticisms on Elizabeth's person, behaviour, and dress. But Georgiana would not join her. Her brother's recommendation was enough to ensure her favour; his judgement could not err. And he had spoken in such terms of Elizabeth as to leave Georgiana without the power of finding her otherwise than lovely and amiable. When Darcy returned to the saloon, Miss Bingley could not help repeating to him some part of what she had been saying to his sister.
paras.uz: Yuqorida aytilgan savol-javobdan keyin ularning tashrifi uzoq davom etmadi; janob Darsi ularni aravagacha kuzatib borayotganda, miss Bingli Elizabetning qiyofasi, xatti-harakati va kiyimini tanqid qilib, tuyg'ularini to'kib solardi. Lekin Jorjiana unga qo'shilmadi. Akasining tavsiyasi uning iltifotini ta'minlash uchun yetarli edi; uning mulohazasi xato qila olmasdi. U esa Elizabet haqida shunday so'zlar bilan gapirgan ediki, Jorjianani uni go'zal va yoqimli deb topishdan boshqa ilojsiz qoldirdi. Darsi mehmonxonaga qaytganda, miss Bingli singlisiga aytganlarining bir qismini unga takrorlamay qololmadi.

paras.en: “How very ill Miss Eliza Bennet looks this morning, Mr. Darcy,” she cried; “I never in my life saw anyone so much altered as she is since the winter. She is grown so brown and coarse! Louisa and I were agreeing that we should not have known her again.”
paras.uz: «Miss Eliza Bennet bugun ertalab qanchalik yomon ko'rinadi, janob Darsi, — xitob qildi u. — Umrimda hech kimni qishdan beri u kabi bunchalik o'zgarganini ko'rmaganman. U shunchalik qorayib, dag'allashib ketibdiki! Luiza bilan uni qayta tanimagan bo'lardik, deb kelishdik».

paras.en: However little Mr. Darcy might have liked such an address, he contented himself with coolly replying that he perceived no other alteration than her being rather tanned, no miraculous consequence of travelling in the summer.
paras.uz: Janob Darsiga bunday murojaat qanchalik yoqmagan bo'lmasin, u sovuqqonlik bilan u faqat biroz qorayganidan boshqa o'zgarish sezmaganini, bu esa yozda sayohat qilishning mo'jizaviy oqibati emasligini aytish bilan cheklandi.

paras.en: “For my own part,” she rejoined, “I must confess that I never could see any beauty in her. Her face is too thin; her complexion has no brilliancy; and her features are not at all handsome. Her nose wants character--there is nothing marked in its lines. Her teeth are tolerable, but not out of the common way; and as for her eyes, which have sometimes been called so fine, I could never see anything extraordinary in them. They have a sharp, shrewish look, which I do not like at all; and in her air altogether there is a self-sufficiency without fashion, which is intolerable.”
paras.uz: «Men o'zim, — davom etdi u, — tan olishim kerakki, unda hech qachon hech qanday go'zallik ko'rmaganman. Yuzi haddan tashqari ingichka; rangida jilo yo'q; yuz chiziqlari umuman chiroyli emas. Burnida xarakter yetishmaydi — uning chiziqlarida hech qanday aniqlik yo'q. Tishlari chidasa bo'ladi, lekin oddiydan ortiq emas; ba'zan juda chiroyli deb atalgan ko'zlariga kelsak, ularda hech qachon g'ayrioddiy narsa ko'ra olmaganman. Ularda men umuman yoqtirmaydigan o'tkir, jahldor qarash bor; uning butun qiyofasida esa nafosatsiz o'zini yetarli deb hisoblash bor, bu chidab bo'lmas».

paras.en: Persuaded as Miss Bingley was that Darcy admired Elizabeth, this was not the best method of recommending herself; but angry people are not always wise; and in seeing him at last look somewhat nettled, she had all the success she expected. He was resolutely silent, however, and, from a determination of making him speak, she continued:
paras.uz: Miss Bingli Darsi Elizabetga maftun ekaniga qanchalik ishonmasin, bu o'zini yoqtirishning eng yaxshi usuli emasdi; lekin g'azablangan odamlar har doim ham aqlli bo'lavermaydi; va nihoyat uning biroz achchiqlanganini ko'rib, u kutgan barcha muvaffaqiyatga erishdi. Biroq u qat'iy jim turdi va uni gapirtirishga qaror qilib, u davom etdi:

paras.en: “I remember, when we first knew her in Hertfordshire, how amazed we all were to find that she was a reputed beauty; and I particularly recollect your saying one night, after they had been dining at Netherfield, 'She a beauty!--I should as soon call her mother a wit.' But afterwards she seemed to improve on you, and I believe you thought her rather pretty at one time.”
paras.uz: «Esimda, uni Xertfordshirda birinchi bilganimizda, uning go'zal deb hisoblanishini bilib hammamiz qanchalik hayron bo'lgan edik; ayniqsa bir kechasi, ular Nezerfildda tushlik qilganlaridan keyin sizning "U go'zalmi! — Unda onasini aqlli deyishim ham mumkin" deganingizni eslayman. Lekin keyinroq u sizga yoqa boshlaganga o'xshadi va ishonamanki, bir paytlar siz uni ancha chiroyli deb o'ylagansiz».

paras.en: “Yes,” replied Darcy, who could contain himself no longer, “but that was only when I first saw her, for it is many months since I have considered her as one of the handsomest women of my acquaintance.”
paras.uz: «Ha, — javob berdi o'zini boshqa tuta olmagan Darsi, — lekin bu faqat uni birinchi ko'rganimda edi, chunki ko'p oylardan beri uni tanishlarim ichidagi eng go'zal ayollardan biri deb hisoblayman».

paras.en: He then went away, and Miss Bingley was left to all the satisfaction of having forced him to say what gave no one any pain but herself.
paras.uz: Keyin u ketdi va miss Bingli uni o'zidan boshqa hech kimga og'riq bermagan narsani aytishga majbur qilganining butun mamnuniyatiga qoldirildi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner and Elizabeth talked of all that had occurred during their visit, as they returned, except what had particularly interested them both. The look and behaviour of everybody they had seen were discussed, except of the person who had mostly engaged their attention. They talked of his sister, his friends, his house, his fruit--of everything but himself; yet Elizabeth was longing to know what Mrs. Gardiner thought of him, and Mrs. Gardiner would have been highly gratified by her niece's beginning the subject.
paras.uz: Qaytishayotganda missis Gardiner va Elizabet tashrif davomida bo'lib o'tgan hamma narsa haqida gaplashishdi, faqat ikkalasini ham ayniqsa qiziqtirgan narsadan tashqari. Ular ko'rgan har kimning qiyofasi va xatti-harakati muhokama qilindi, faqat ularning e'tiborini eng ko'p band qilgan shaxsnikidan tashqari. Ular uning singlisi, do'stlari, uyi, mevalari haqida — o'zidan boshqa hamma narsa haqida gaplashishdi; shunga qaramay Elizabet missis Gardiner u haqida nima deb o'ylashini bilishni juda istardi, missis Gardiner esa agar jiyani mavzuni boshlasa, juda mamnun bo'lardi.

gloss.ex: Convinced as Elizabeth now was that Miss Bingley's dislike of her had originated in jealousy, she could not help feeling how unwelcome her appearance at Pemberley must be to her,…
Her face is too thin; her complexion has no brilliancy; and her features are not at all handsome.
Convinced as Elizabeth now was that Miss Bingley's dislike of her had originated in jealousy, she could not help feeling how unwelcome her appearance at Pemberley must be to her,…
She answered with equal indifference and brevity, and the other said no more.
Gardiner, with occasional help from Elizabeth, the conversation was carried on.
In no countenance was attentive curiosity so strongly marked as in Miss Bingley's, in spite of the smiles which overspread her face whenever she spoke to one of its objects;…
Had Miss Bingley known what pain she was then giving her beloved friend, she undoubtedly would have refrained from the hint; but she had merely intended to discompose Elizabeth by…

quiz.q: How does Miss Bingley try to hurt Elizabeth?
o: By mentioning the militia and Wickham
quiz.why_uz: Lekin bu Jorjianani og'ir ahvolga soladi.

quiz.q: What does Darcy say about Elizabeth at the end?
o: She is one of the handsomest women he knows
quiz.why_uz: Miss Binglining hiylasi teskari natija beradi.

chapters.title: Lydia Has Eloped
chapters.recap_uz: Jeyndan ikki xat keladi: Lidiya Uikhem bilan qochib ketgan va ular turmush qurmagan bo'lishi mumkin. Elizabet buni Darsiga aytadi va oilasi butunlay sharmanda bo'ldi, deb o'ylaydi.

paras.en: Elizabeth had been a good deal disappointed in not finding a letter from Jane on their first arrival at Lambton; and this disappointment had been renewed on each of the mornings that had now been spent there; but on the third her repining was over, and her sister justified, by the receipt of two letters from her at once, on one of which was marked that it had been missent elsewhere. Elizabeth was not surprised at it, as Jane had written the direction remarkably ill.
paras.uz: Elizabet Lembtonga birinchi kelganlarida Jeyndan xat topmaganidan ancha hafsalasi pir bo'lgan edi; bu hafsala pirligi u yerda o'tkazilgan har ertalab yangilanib turdi; lekin uchinchi kuni uning nolishi tugadi va opasi oqlandi, chunki undan birdaniga ikki xat oldi, ulardan birida u boshqa joyga noto'g'ri yuborilgani belgilangan edi. Elizabet bundan hayron bo'lmadi, chunki Jeyn manzilni juda yomon yozgan edi.

paras.en: They had just been preparing to walk as the letters came in; and her uncle and aunt, leaving her to enjoy them in quiet, set off by themselves. The one missent must first be attended to; it had been written five days ago. The beginning contained an account of all their little parties and engagements, with such news as the country afforded; but the latter half, which was dated a day later, and written in evident agitation, gave more important intelligence. It was to this effect:
paras.uz: Xatlar kelganda ular endigina sayrga tayyorlanayotgan edilar; tog'asi va xolasi uni ulardan bemalol zavqlanish uchun qoldirib, o'zlari yo'lga chiqishdi. Avval noto'g'ri yuborilganiga e'tibor berish kerak edi; u besh kun oldin yozilgan edi. Uning boshida ularning barcha kichik yig'inlari va tadbirlari, qishloq bera oladigan yangiliklar haqida hikoya qilingan edi; lekin bir kun keyingi sana qo'yilgan va aniq hayajonda yozilgan ikkinchi yarmi muhimroq xabar berardi. U shunday edi:

paras.en: “Since writing the above, dearest Lizzy, something has occurred of a most unexpected and serious nature; but I am afraid of alarming you--be assured that we are all well. What I have to say relates to poor Lydia. An express came at twelve last night, just as we were all gone to bed, from Colonel Forster, to inform us that she was gone off to Scotland with one of his officers; to own the truth, with Wickham! Imagine our surprise. To Kitty, however, it does not seem so wholly unexpected. I am very, very sorry. So imprudent a match on both sides! But I am willing to hope the best, and that his character has been misunderstood. Thoughtless and indiscreet I can easily believe him, but this step (and let us rejoice over it) marks nothing bad at heart.
paras.uz: «Yuqoridagilarni yozgandan beri, eng aziz Lizzi, juda kutilmagan va jiddiy narsa yuz berdi; lekin seni qo'rqitishdan cho'chiyman — ishonaver, hammamiz sog'-salomatmiz. Aytadiganim bechora Lidiyaga tegishli. Kecha soat o'n ikkida, hammamiz endigina uxlashga yotganimizda, polkovnik Forsterdan shoshilinch xabarchi keldi va u uning ofitserlaridan biri bilan Shotlandiyaga qochib ketganini xabar qildi; rostini aytsam, Uikhem bilan! Hayratimizni tasavvur qil. Biroq Ketti uchun bu butunlay kutilmagan emasga o'xshaydi. Juda, juda afsusdaman. Har ikki tomondan shunchalik ehtiyotsiz nikoh! Lekin men eng yaxshisiga umid qilishga tayyorman va uning xarakteri noto'g'ri tushunilgan bo'lsa kerak. Uni beparvo va mulohazasiz ekaniga osongina ishonaman, lekin bu qadam (va bundan xursand bo'laylik) qalbida hech qanday yomonlik borligini ko'rsatmaydi.

paras.en: His choice is disinterested at least, for he must know my father can give her nothing. Our poor mother is sadly grieved. My father bears it better. How thankful am I that we never let them know what has been said against him; we must forget it ourselves. They were off Saturday night about twelve, as is conjectured, but were not missed till yesterday morning at eight. The express was sent off directly. My dear Lizzy, they must have passed within ten miles of us. Colonel Forster gives us reason to expect him here soon. Lydia left a few lines for his wife, informing her of their intention. I must conclude, for I cannot be long from my poor mother. I am afraid you will not be able to make it out, but I hardly know what I have written.”
paras.uz: Uning tanlovi hech bo'lmaganda beg'araz, chunki u otamning unga hech narsa bera olmasligini bilishi kerak. Bechora onamiz qattiq qayg'uda. Otam bunga yaxshiroq chidayapti. Ularga u haqida aytilgan gaplarni hech qachon bildirmaganimizdan qanchalik minnatdorman; o'zimiz ham uni unutishimiz kerak. Taxmin qilinishicha, ular shanba kechasi soat o'n ikkilarda jo'nab ketishgan, lekin kecha ertalab soat sakkizgacha ularning yo'qligi sezilmagan. Shoshilinch xabarchi darhol yuborilgan. Azizim Lizzi, ular bizdan o'n mil yaqinidan o'tgan bo'lsa kerak. Polkovnik Forster uni tez orada bu yerda kutishimiz uchun asos beradi. Lidiya uning xotiniga niyatlari haqida xabar beruvchi bir necha satr qoldirgan. Tugatishim kerak, chunki bechora onamdan uzoq ayrila olmayman. Qo'rqamanki, buni tushuna olmaysan, lekin nima yozganimni o'zim ham zo'rg'a bilaman».

paras.en: Without allowing herself time for consideration, and scarcely knowing what she felt, Elizabeth on finishing this letter instantly seized the other, and opening it with the utmost impatience, read as follows: it had been written a day later than the conclusion of the first.
paras.uz: O'ylashga vaqt bermasdan va nima his qilayotganini zo'rg'a bilgan holda, Elizabet bu xatni tugatgach, darhol ikkinchisini oldi va eng katta sabrsizlik bilan ochib, quyidagilarni o'qidi: u birinchisining oxiridan bir kun keyin yozilgan edi.

paras.en: “By this time, my dearest sister, you have received my hurried letter; I wish this may be more intelligible, but though not confined for time, my head is so bewildered that I cannot answer for being coherent. Dearest Lizzy, I hardly know what I would write, but I have bad news for you, and it cannot be delayed. Imprudent as the marriage between Mr. Wickham and our poor Lydia would be, we are now anxious to be assured it has taken place, for there is but too much reason to fear they are not gone to Scotland. Colonel Forster came yesterday, having left Brighton the day before, not many hours after the express.
paras.uz: «Hozirga kelib, eng aziz singlim, shoshilinch xatimni olgan bo'lsang kerak; bu tushunarliroq bo'lishini istardim, lekin vaqtim cheklanmagan bo'lsa ham, boshim shunchalik aylanib qolganki, izchil bo'lishimga kafolat bera olmayman. Eng aziz Lizzi, nima yozishni zo'rg'a bilaman, lekin senga yomon xabarim bor va uni kechiktirib bo'lmaydi. Janob Uikhem va bechora Lidiyamiz o'rtasidagi nikoh qanchalik ehtiyotsiz bo'lmasin, endi uning bo'lib o'tganiga ishonch hosil qilishni juda istaymiz, chunki ular Shotlandiyaga ketmagan bo'lishidan qo'rqish uchun haddan tashqari ko'p asos bor. Polkovnik Forster kecha keldi, u Braytonni bir kun oldin, shoshilinch xabarchidan ko'p soat o'tmay tark etgan.

paras.en: Though Lydia's short letter to Mrs. F. gave them to understand that they were going to Gretna Green, something was dropped by Denny expressing his belief that W. never intended to go there, or to marry Lydia at all, which was repeated to Colonel F., who, instantly taking the alarm, set off from B. intending to trace their route. He did trace them easily to Clapham, but no further; for on entering that place, they removed into a hackney coach, and dismissed the chaise that brought them from Epsom. All that is known after this is, that they were seen to continue the London road. I know not what to think.
paras.uz: Lidiyaning missis F.ga yozgan qisqa xati ularga Gretna Gringa ketayotganlarini tushuntirgan bo'lsa ham, Denni U. u yerga borishni yoki umuman Lidiyaga uylanishni hech qachon niyat qilmaganiga ishonishini bildiruvchi nimadir deb qo'ygan, bu polkovnik F.ga takrorlangan, u darhol xavotirga tushib, ularning yo'lini kuzatish niyatida B.dan yo'lga chiqqan. U ularni Klepemgacha oson kuzatgan, lekin undan nariga emas; chunki o'sha joyga kirgach, ular yollanma karetaga o'tishgan va ularni Epsomdan olib kelgan aravani qo'yib yuborishgan. Bundan keyin ma'lum bo'lgan narsa shuki, ularni London yo'lida davom etayotganlarini ko'rishgan. Nima deb o'ylashni bilmayman.

paras.en: After making every possible inquiry on that side London, Colonel F. came on into Hertfordshire, anxiously renewing them at all the turnpikes, and at the inns in Barnet and Hatfield, but without any success--no such people had been seen to pass through. With the kindest concern he came on to Longbourn, and broke his apprehensions to us in a manner most creditable to his heart. I am sincerely grieved for him and Mrs. F., but no one can throw any blame on them. Our distress, my dear Lizzy, is very great. My father and mother believe the worst, but I cannot think so ill of him.
paras.uz: Londonning o'sha tomonida mumkin bo'lgan barcha so'roqlarni qilgach, polkovnik F. Xertfordshirga keldi, barcha pullik yo'l postlarida, Barnet va Xetfilddagi mehmonxonalarda xavotir bilan ularni yangiladi, lekin hech qanday muvaffaqiyatsiz — bunday odamlar o'tganini hech kim ko'rmagan. Eng mehribon tashvish bilan u Longbornga keldi va xavotirlarini bizga qalbiga sharaf keltiradigan tarzda aytdi. Unga va missis F.ga chin dildan achinaman, lekin hech kim ularni ayblay olmaydi. Bizning iztirobimiz, azizim Lizzi, juda katta. Otam va onam eng yomonga ishonishadi, lekin men u haqida bunchalik yomon o'ylay olmayman.

paras.en: Many circumstances might make it more eligible for them to be married privately in town than to pursue their first plan; and even if he could form such a design against a young woman of Lydia's connections, which is not likely, can I suppose her so lost to everything? Impossible! I grieve to find, however, that Colonel F. is not disposed to depend upon their marriage; he shook his head when I expressed my hopes, and said he feared W. was not a man to be trusted. My poor mother is really ill, and keeps her room. Could she exert herself, it would be better; but this is not to be expected. And as to my father, I never in my life saw him so affected. Poor Kitty has anger for having concealed their attachment; but as it was a matter of confidence, one cannot wonder.
paras.uz: Ko'p holatlar ular uchun dastlabki rejalarini amalga oshirishdan ko'ra Londonda yashirincha turmush qurishni maqbulroq qilishi mumkin; va agar u Lidiyaning qarindoshlariga ega yosh ayolga qarshi bunday niyat qila olsa ham — bu ehtimoldan yiroq — uni hamma narsadan shunchalik mahrum deb o'ylay olamanmi? Imkonsiz! Biroq polkovnik F. ularning nikohiga ishonishga moyil emasligini bilib qayg'uraman; men umidlarimni bildirganimda u boshini chayqadi va U. ishonib bo'ladigan odam emasligidan qo'rqishini aytdi. Bechora onam haqiqatan ham kasal va xonasidan chiqmayapti. Agar u o'zini tutib olsa, yaxshiroq bo'lardi; lekin buni kutib bo'lmaydi. Otamga kelsak, umrimda uni hech qachon bunchalik ta'sirlangan holda ko'rmaganman. Bechora Ketti ularning munosabatini yashirgani uchun g'azabga uchradi; lekin bu ishonch masalasi bo'lgani uchun hayron bo'lib bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: I am truly glad, dearest Lizzy, that you have been spared something of these distressing scenes; but now, as the first shock is over, shall I own that I long for your return? I am not so selfish, however, as to press for it, if inconvenient. Adieu! I take up my pen again to do what I have just told you I would not; but circumstances are such that I cannot help earnestly begging you all to come here as soon as possible. I know my dear uncle and aunt so well, that I am not afraid of requesting it, though I have still something more to ask of the former. My father is going to London with Colonel Forster instantly, to try to discover her.
paras.uz: Chin dildan xursandman, eng aziz Lizzi, sen bu iztirobli sahnalarning biroz qismidan xalos bo'lding; lekin endi, birinchi zarba o'tgach, qaytishingni orziqib kutayotganimni tan olaymi? Biroq agar noqulay bo'lsa, buni qistash uchun unchalik xudbin emasman. Xayr! Qalamni yana qo'lga olib, hozirgina qilmasligimni aytgan narsani qilyapman; lekin vaziyat shundayki, hammangizni iloji boricha tezroq bu yerga kelishingizni astoydil iltimos qilmasdan ilojim yo'q. Aziz tog'am va xolamni shunchalik yaxshi bilamanki, buni so'rashdan qo'rqmayman, garchi birinchisidan yana bir narsa so'rashim kerak bo'lsa ham. Otam uni topishga urinish uchun polkovnik Forster bilan darhol Londonga ketyapti.

paras.en: What he means to do I am sure I know not; but his excessive distress will not allow him to pursue any measure in the best and safest way, and Colonel Forster is obliged to be at Brighton again to-morrow evening. In such an exigence, my uncle's advice and assistance would be everything in the world; he will immediately comprehend what I must feel, and I rely upon his goodness.”
paras.uz: U nima qilmoqchi ekanini, ishonchim komilki, bilmayman; lekin uning haddan tashqari iztirobi unga har qanday chorani eng yaxshi va eng xavfsiz tarzda amalga oshirishga imkon bermaydi, polkovnik Forster esa ertaga kechqurun yana Braytonda bo'lishi kerak. Bunday favqulodda holatda tog'amning maslahati va yordami dunyodagi hamma narsa bo'lardi; u darhol nimani his qilayotganimni tushunadi va men uning yaxshiligiga tayanaman».

paras.en: “Oh! where, where is my uncle?” cried Elizabeth, darting from her seat as she finished the letter, in eagerness to follow him, without losing a moment of the time so precious; but as she reached the door it was opened by a servant, and Mr. Darcy appeared. Her pale face and impetuous manner made him start, and before he could recover himself to speak, she, in whose mind every idea was superseded by Lydia's situation, hastily exclaimed, “I beg your pardon, but I must leave you. I must find Mr. Gardiner this moment, on business that cannot be delayed; I have not an instant to lose.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Qayerda, tog'am qayerda?» — xitob qildi Elizabet, xatni tugatarkan o'rnidan otilib turib, shunchalik qimmatli vaqtning bir lahzasini ham yo'qotmasdan uning ortidan borish ishtiyoqida; lekin u eshikka yetganda, uni xizmatkor ochdi va janob Darsi paydo bo'ldi. Uning rangpar yuzi va shiddatli harakati uni seskantirib yubordi va u gapirish uchun o'ziga kelishidan oldin, ongida har bir fikrni Lidiyaning ahvoli siqib chiqargan Elizabet shoshilib xitob qildi: «Kechirasiz, lekin sizni tark etishim kerak. Janob Gardinerni hozir, kechiktirib bo'lmaydigan ish bo'yicha topishim kerak; bir lahza ham yo'qotadigan vaqtim yo'q».

paras.en: “Good God! what is the matter?” cried he, with more feeling than politeness; then recollecting himself, “I will not detain you a minute; but let me, or let the servant go after Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner. You are not well enough; you cannot go yourself.”
paras.uz: «Yo xudo! Nima bo'ldi?» — xitob qildi u, xushmuomalalikdan ko'ra ko'proq tuyg'u bilan; keyin o'zini tutib olib: «Sizni bir daqiqa ham ushlab qolmayman; lekin menga yoki xizmatkorga janob va missis Gardinerning ortidan borishga ruxsat bering. Sizning ahvolingiz yaxshi emas; o'zingiz bora olmaysiz».

paras.en: Elizabeth hesitated, but her knees trembled under her and she felt how little would be gained by her attempting to pursue them. Calling back the servant, therefore, she commissioned him, though in so breathless an accent as made her almost unintelligible, to fetch his master and mistress home instantly.
paras.uz: Elizabet ikkilandi, lekin tizzalari titrardi va ularning ortidan borishga urinishidan qanchalik oz foyda bo'lishini his qildi. Shuning uchun xizmatkorni qaytarib chaqirib, uni deyarli tushunarsiz qiladigan darajada nafasi tiqilgan ohangda bo'lsa ham, xo'jayini va xonimini darhol uyga chaqirib kelishni topshirdi.

paras.en: On his quitting the room she sat down, unable to support herself, and looking so miserably ill, that it was impossible for Darcy to leave her, or to refrain from saying, in a tone of gentleness and commiseration, “Let me call your maid. Is there nothing you could take to give you present relief? A glass of wine; shall I get you one? You are very ill.”
paras.uz: U xonadan chiqqach, Elizabet o'zini tutib tura olmay o'tirdi va shunchalik ayanchli darajada kasal ko'rinardiki, Darsi uni tashlab keta olmasdi yoki muloyimlik va hamdardlik ohangida aytmasdan tura olmasdi: «Xizmatkor qizingizni chaqiray. Hozir yengillik beradigan biror narsa ichishingiz mumkin emasmi? Bir qadah vino; olib kelaymi? Ahvolingiz juda yomon».

paras.en: “No, I thank you,” she replied, endeavouring to recover herself. “There is nothing the matter with me. I am quite well; I am only distressed by some dreadful news which I have just received from Longbourn.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, rahmat, — javob berdi u, o'ziga kelishga urinib. — Menga hech narsa bo'lmagan. Men mutlaqo sog'man; faqat Longborndan hozirgina olgan dahshatli xabardan qayg'urayapman».

paras.en: She burst into tears as she alluded to it, and for a few minutes could not speak another word. Darcy, in wretched suspense, could only say something indistinctly of his concern, and observe her in compassionate silence. At length she spoke again. “I have just had a letter from Jane, with such dreadful news. It cannot be concealed from anyone. My younger sister has left all her friends--has eloped; has thrown herself into the power of--of Mr. Wickham. They are gone off together from Brighton. You know him too well to doubt the rest. She has no money, no connections, nothing that can tempt him to--she is lost for ever.”
paras.uz: U bunga ishora qilarkan, yig'lab yubordi va bir necha daqiqa boshqa bir og'iz ham gapira olmadi. Ayanchli intizorlikdagi Darsi faqat tashvishi haqida noaniq nimadir aytishi va uni hamdardlik bilan jim kuzatishi mumkin edi. Nihoyat u yana gapirdi. «Hozirgina Jeyndan shunday dahshatli xabar bilan xat oldim. Uni hech kimdan yashirib bo'lmaydi. Kichik singlim barcha do'stlarini tashlab ketdi — qochib ketdi; o'zini... janob Uikhemning qo'liga tashladi. Ular Braytondan birga ketishgan. Siz uni qolganiga shubha qilmaslik uchun haddan tashqari yaxshi bilasiz. Uning na puli, na aloqalari, uni... vasvasaga soladigan hech narsasi yo'q — u abadiy halok bo'ldi».

paras.en: Darcy was fixed in astonishment. “When I consider,” she added in a yet more agitated voice, “that I might have prevented it! I, who knew what he was. Had I but explained some part of it only--some part of what I learnt, to my own family! Had his character been known, this could not have happened. But it is all--all too late now.”
paras.uz: Darsi hayratdan qotib qoldi. «O'ylasam, — qo'shib qo'ydi u yanada hayajonliroq ovozda, — men buning oldini olishim mumkin edi! Men, uning kimligini bilgan men! Agar uning faqat bir qismini — bilib olganlarimning bir qismini o'z oilamga tushuntirganimda edi! Agar uning xarakteri ma'lum bo'lganida, bu sodir bo'lmasdi. Lekin endi hammasi — hammasi juda kech».

paras.en: “I am grieved indeed,” cried Darcy; “grieved--shocked. But is it certain--absolutely certain?”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham qayg'uryapman, — xitob qildi Darsi, — qayg'urayapman — hayratdaman. Lekin bu aniqmi — mutlaqo aniqmi?»

paras.en: “Oh, yes! They left Brighton together on Sunday night, and were traced almost to London, but not beyond; they are certainly not gone to Scotland.”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha! Ular yakshanba kechasi Braytondan birga ketishgan va deyarli Londongacha kuzatilgan, lekin undan nariga emas; ular Shotlandiyaga ketmaganligi aniq».

paras.en: “And what has been done, what has been attempted, to recover her?”
paras.uz: «Uni qaytarish uchun nima qilindi, nimaga urinildi?»

paras.en: “My father is gone to London, and Jane has written to beg my uncle's immediate assistance; and we shall be off, I hope, in half-an-hour. But nothing can be done--I know very well that nothing can be done. How is such a man to be worked on? How are they even to be discovered? I have not the smallest hope. It is every way horrible!”
paras.uz: «Otam Londonga ketdi, Jeyn esa tog'amdan darhol yordam so'rab xat yozdi; umid qilamanki, biz yarim soatda yo'lga chiqamiz. Lekin hech narsa qilib bo'lmaydi — hech narsa qilib bo'lmasligini juda yaxshi bilaman. Bunday odamga qanday ta'sir qilish mumkin? Ularni qanday topish mumkin? Zarracha ham umidim yo'q. Har tomondan dahshatli!»

paras.en: Darcy shook his head in silent acquiescence.
paras.uz: Darsi jim rozilik bilan boshini chayqadi.

paras.en: “When my eyes were opened to his real character--Oh! had I known what I ought, what I dared to do! But I knew not--I was afraid of doing too much. Wretched, wretched mistake!”
paras.uz: «Ko'zlarim uning haqiqiy xarakteriga ochilganda — Oh! Nima qilishim kerakligini, nima qilishga jur'at etishim kerakligini bilganimda edi! Lekin bilmadim — haddan tashqari ko'p narsa qilishdan qo'rqdim. Ayanchli, ayanchli xato!»

paras.en: Darcy made no answer. He seemed scarcely to hear her, and was walking up and down the room in earnest meditation, his brow contracted, his air gloomy. Elizabeth soon observed, and instantly understood it. Her power was sinking; everything must sink under such a proof of family weakness, such an assurance of the deepest disgrace. She could neither wonder nor condemn, but the belief of his self-conquest brought nothing consolatory to her bosom, afforded no palliation of her distress. It was, on the contrary, exactly calculated to make her understand her own wishes; and never had she so honestly felt that she could have loved him, as now, when all love must be vain.
paras.uz: Darsi javob bermadi. U uni zo'rg'a eshitayotganday ko'rinardi va jiddiy o'yga botib, qoshlarini chimirib, g'amgin qiyofada xona bo'ylab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurardi. Elizabet tez orada buni sezdi va darhol tushundi. Uning ta'siri so'nib borardi; oilaviy zaiflikning bunday isboti, eng chuqur sharmandalikning bunday kafolati oldida hamma narsa so'nishi muqarrar edi. U na hayron bo'la olardi, na qoralay olardi, lekin uning o'zini yengganiga ishonish uning ko'ksiga hech qanday taskin keltirmadi, iztirobini yengillashtirmadi. Aksincha, bu aynan unga o'z istaklarini tushunishga yordam berish uchun mo'ljallangan edi; va u hech qachon hozirgidek, har qanday muhabbat befoyda bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan paytdagidek, uni sevishi mumkin edi deb bunchalik halol his qilmagan edi.

paras.en: But self, though it would intrude, could not engross her. Lydia--the humiliation, the misery she was bringing on them all, soon swallowed up every private care; and covering her face with her handkerchief, Elizabeth was soon lost to everything else; and, after a pause of several minutes, was only recalled to a sense of her situation by the voice of her companion, who, in a manner which, though it spoke compassion, spoke likewise restraint, said, “I am afraid you have been long desiring my absence, nor have I anything to plead in excuse of my stay, but real, though unavailing concern. Would to Heaven that anything could be either said or done on my part that might offer consolation to such distress! But I will not torment you with vain wishes, which may seem purposely to ask for your thanks. This unfortunate affair will, I fear, prevent my sister's having the pleasure of seeing you at Pemberley to-day.”
paras.uz: Lekin o'z-o'zi, garchi bostirib kirsa ham, uni butunlay egallay olmadi. Lidiya — u hammaga keltirayotgan xo'rlik, baxtsizlik tez orada har qanday shaxsiy tashvishni yutib yubordi; va yuzini ro'molchasi bilan berkitib, Elizabet tez orada boshqa hamma narsadan uzilib qoldi; bir necha daqiqalik sukutdan keyin uni faqat hamrohining ovozi ahvolini his qilishga qaytardi, u hamdardlikni bildirsa ham, vazminlikni ham bildiradigan tarzda dedi: «Qo'rqamanki, siz uzoq vaqtdan beri ketishimni istab turibsiz va qolishimni oqlash uchun haqiqiy, lekin befoyda tashvishdan boshqa hech narsam yo'q. Qaniydi, men tomonimdan bunday iztirobga taskin bera oladigan biror narsa aytilsa yoki qilinsa! Lekin sizni ataylab minnatdorchiligingizni so'rayotgandek tuyulishi mumkin bo'lgan behuda istaklar bilan qiynamayman. Qo'rqamanki, bu baxtsiz voqea singlimni bugun sizni Pemberlida ko'rish zavqidan mahrum qiladi».

paras.en: “Oh, yes. Be so kind as to apologise for us to Miss Darcy. Say that urgent business calls us home immediately. Conceal the unhappy truth as long as it is possible, I know it cannot be long.”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha. Mehribonlik qilib, miss Darsidan biz uchun uzr so'rang. Shoshilinch ish bizni darhol uyga chaqirayotganini ayting. Baxtsiz haqiqatni iloji boricha uzoqroq yashiring, bilaman, bu uzoq davom eta olmaydi».

paras.en: He readily assured her of his secrecy; again expressed his sorrow for her distress, wished it a happier conclusion than there was at present reason to hope, and leaving his compliments for her relations, with only one serious, parting look, went away.
paras.uz: U darhol uni sir saqlashiga ishontirdi; yana uning iztirobidan qayg'usini bildirdi, unga hozir umid qilish uchun asos bo'lganidan baxtliroq yakun tiladi va qarindoshlariga salomlarini qoldirib, faqat bitta jiddiy, xayrlashuv nigohi bilan chiqib ketdi.

paras.en: As he quitted the room, Elizabeth felt how improbable it was that they should ever see each other again on such terms of cordiality as had marked their several meetings in Derbyshire; and as she threw a retrospective glance over the whole of their acquaintance, so full of contradictions and varieties, sighed at the perverseness of those feelings which would now have promoted its continuance, and would formerly have rejoiced in its termination.
paras.uz: U xonadan chiqarkan, Elizabet ular Derbishirdagi bir necha uchrashuvlarini belgilagan bunday samimiyat bilan endi hech qachon bir-birini ko'rishlari qanchalik ehtimoldan yiroq ekanini his qildi; va qarama-qarshiliklar va xilma-xilliklarga to'la butun tanishliklariga ortga nazar tashlab, endi uning davom etishiga yordam beradigan, ilgari esa uning tugashidan xursand bo'ladigan tuyg'ularning teskariligidan xo'rsindi.

paras.en: If gratitude and esteem are good foundations of affection, Elizabeth's change of sentiment will be neither improbable nor faulty. But if otherwise--if regard springing from such sources is unreasonable or unnatural, in comparison of what is so often described as arising on a first interview with its object, and even before two words have been exchanged, nothing can be said in her defence, except that she had given somewhat of a trial to the latter method in her partiality for Wickham, and that its ill success might, perhaps, authorise her to seek the other less interesting mode of attachment. Be that as it may, she saw him go with regret; and in this early example of what Lydia's infamy must produce, found additional anguish as she reflected on that wretched business. Never, since reading Jane's second letter, had she entertained a hope of Wickham's meaning to marry her.
paras.uz: Agar minnatdorlik va hurmat mehrning yaxshi asoslari bo'lsa, Elizabetning tuyg'ulari o'zgarishi na ehtimoldan yiroq, na aybli bo'ladi. Lekin agar aksincha bo'lsa — agar bunday manbalardan kelib chiqadigan mehr uning obyekti bilan birinchi uchrashuvda, hatto ikki so'z almashilmasdan oldin paydo bo'ladi deb ko'pincha tasvirlanadigan narsa bilan solishtirganda asossiz yoki g'ayritabiiy bo'lsa, uning himoyasi uchun hech narsa aytib bo'lmaydi, faqat u Uikhemga moyilligida keyingi usulni biroz sinab ko'rganini va uning muvaffaqiyatsizligi, ehtimol, unga boshqa, kamroq qiziqarli mehr usulini izlashga ruxsat berishi mumkinligini aytish mumkin. Qanday bo'lmasin, u uning ketishini afsus bilan ko'rdi; va Lidiyaning sharmandaligi keltirib chiqarishi kerak bo'lgan narsaning bu erta misolida o'sha ayanchli ish haqida o'ylarkan, qo'shimcha azob topdi. Jeynning ikkinchi xatini o'qiganidan beri u Uikhemning unga uylanish niyati borligiga hech qachon umid qilmagan edi.

paras.en: No one but Jane, she thought, could flatter herself with such an expectation. Surprise was the least of her feelings on this development. While the contents of the first letter remained in her mind, she was all surprise--all astonishment that Wickham should marry a girl whom it was impossible he could marry for money; and how Lydia could ever have attached him had appeared incomprehensible. But now it was all too natural. For such an attachment as this she might have sufficient charms; and though she did not suppose Lydia to be deliberately engaging in an elopement without the intention of marriage, she had no difficulty in believing that neither her virtue nor her understanding would preserve her from falling an easy prey.
paras.uz: Uning o'ylashicha, Jeyndan boshqa hech kim o'zini bunday kutish bilan ovuta olmasdi. Bu voqealar rivojida hayrat uning tuyg'ularining eng kichigi edi. Birinchi xatning mazmuni xayolida turganda, u butunlay hayrat — Uikhem pul uchun uylanishi mumkin bo'lmagan qizga uylanishidan butunlay hayratda edi; Lidiya qanday qilib uni o'ziga bog'lab olgani tushunib bo'lmas tuyulgan edi. Lekin endi hammasi haddan tashqari tabiiy edi. Bunday bog'lanish uchun unda yetarlicha jozibalar bo'lishi mumkin edi; garchi u Lidiyani nikoh niyatisiz qochishga ataylab rozi bo'lgan deb taxmin qilmasa ham, uning na fazilati, na aqli uni oson o'ljaga aylanishdan saqlamasligiga ishonishda hech qanday qiyinchilik sezmadi.

paras.en: She had never perceived, while the regiment was in Hertfordshire, that Lydia had any partiality for him; but she was convinced that Lydia wanted only encouragement to attach herself to anybody. Sometimes one officer, sometimes another, had been her favourite, as their attentions raised them in her opinion. Her affections had continually been fluctuating but never without an object. The mischief of neglect and mistaken indulgence towards such a girl--oh! how acutely did she now feel it!
paras.uz: Polk Xertfordshirda bo'lganida u Lidiyaning unga biror moyilligi borligini hech qachon sezmagan edi; lekin Lidiyaga har kimga bog'lanib qolishi uchun faqat rag'bat kerak ekaniga ishonardi. Ba'zan bir ofitser, ba'zan boshqasi, ularning e'tiborlari ularni uning nazarida ko'targani sari, uning sevimlisi bo'lgan edi. Uning mehri doimo o'zgarib turardi, lekin hech qachon obyektsiz emasdi. Bunday qizga nisbatan e'tiborsizlik va noto'g'ri erkalatishning zarari — oh! U buni endi qanchalik o'tkir his qilardi!

paras.en: She was wild to be at home--to hear, to see, to be upon the spot to share with Jane in the cares that must now fall wholly upon her, in a family so deranged, a father absent, a mother incapable of exertion, and requiring constant attendance; and though almost persuaded that nothing could be done for Lydia, her uncle's interference seemed of the utmost importance, and till he entered the room her impatience was severe. Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner had hurried back in alarm, supposing by the servant's account that their niece was taken suddenly ill; but satisfying them instantly on that head, she eagerly communicated the cause of their summons, reading the two letters aloud, and dwelling on the postscript of the last with trembling energy.--Though Lydia had never been a favourite with them, Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner could not but be deeply afflicted.
paras.uz: U uyda bo'lishga — eshitishga, ko'rishga, joyida bo'lib, endi butunlay Jeynning zimmasiga tushishi kerak bo'lgan tashvishlarni u bilan baham ko'rishga telbalarcha intilardi — shunchalik tartibsiz oilada, otasi yo'q, onasi harakat qilishga qodir emas va doimiy qarovni talab qiladi; Lidiya uchun hech narsa qilib bo'lmasligiga deyarli ishonsa ham, tog'asining aralashuvi juda muhim ko'rinardi va u xonaga kirguncha uning sabrsizligi qattiq edi. Janob va missis Gardiner xizmatkorning gapidan jiyanlari to'satdan kasal bo'lib qolgan deb taxmin qilib, xavotir ichida shoshib qaytishgan edi; lekin bu borada ularni darhol tinchlantirib, u ularni chaqirish sababini ishtiyoq bilan aytdi, ikki xatni ovoz chiqarib o'qib, oxirgisining qo'shimchasiga titroq g'ayrat bilan to'xtaldi. Lidiya hech qachon ularning sevimlisi bo'lmagan bo'lsa ham, janob va missis Gardiner chuqur qayg'urmay qola olmasdilar.

paras.en: Not Lydia only, but all were concerned in it; and after the first exclamations of surprise and horror, Mr. Gardiner promised every assistance in his power. Elizabeth, though expecting no less, thanked him with tears of gratitude; and all three being actuated by one spirit, everything relating to their journey was speedily settled. They were to be off as soon as possible. “But what is to be done about Pemberley?” cried Mrs. Gardiner. “John told us Mr. Darcy was here when you sent for us; was it so?”
paras.uz: Bu nafaqat Lidiyaga, balki hammaga tegishli edi; hayrat va dahshatning birinchi xitoblaridan keyin janob Gardiner qo'lidan kelgan har qanday yordamni va'da qildi. Elizabet bundan kamini kutmagan bo'lsa ham, unga minnatdorlik ko'z yoshlari bilan rahmat aytdi; uchalasi bir ruh bilan harakat qilgani uchun safarga oid hamma narsa tezda hal qilindi. Ular iloji boricha tezroq jo'nab ketishlari kerak edi. «Lekin Pemberli bilan nima qilamiz? — xitob qildi missis Gardiner. — Jon bizga sen bizni chaqirtirganingda janob Darsi shu yerda ekanini aytdi; shunday bo'ldimi?»

paras.en: “Yes; and I told him we should not be able to keep our engagement. That is all settled.”
paras.uz: «Ha; men unga kelishuvimizni bajara olmasligimizni aytdim. Hammasi hal bo'ldi».

paras.en: “What is all settled?” repeated the other, as she ran into her room to prepare. “And are they upon such terms as for her to disclose the real truth? Oh, that I knew how it was!”
paras.uz: «Nima hammasi hal bo'ldi? — takrorladi xolasi, tayyorlanish uchun xonasiga yugurib kirarkan. — Ular haqiqatni ochib aytadigan darajadagi munosabatdami? Oh, qanday ekanini bilsam edi!»

paras.en: But wishes were vain, or at least could only serve to amuse her in the hurry and confusion of the following hour. Had Elizabeth been at leisure to be idle, she would have remained certain that all employment was impossible to one so wretched as herself; but she had her share of business as well as her aunt, and amongst the rest there were notes to be written to all their friends at Lambton, with false excuses for their sudden departure. An hour, however, saw the whole completed; and Mr. Gardiner meanwhile having settled his account at the inn, nothing remained to be done but to go; and Elizabeth, after all the misery of the morning, found herself, in a shorter space of time than she could have supposed, seated in the carriage, and on the road to Longbourn.
paras.uz: Lekin istaklar behuda edi yoki hech bo'lmaganda keyingi soatdagi shoshqaloqlik va sarosimada uni faqat ovutishi mumkin edi. Agar Elizabetning bekor o'tirishga vaqti bo'lganida, u o'zidek baxtsiz odam uchun har qanday mashg'ulot imkonsiz ekaniga amin bo'lib qolardi; lekin uning ham xolasi kabi o'z ulushi bor edi va boshqalar qatori Lembtondagi barcha do'stlariga to'satdan ketishlari uchun soxta bahonalar bilan xatlar yozish kerak edi. Biroq bir soat ichida hammasi tugadi; bu orada janob Gardiner mehmonxonadagi hisobni to'lab qo'ygani uchun, ketishdan boshqa ish qolmadi; va Elizabet ertalabgi butun azobdan keyin o'zi taxmin qilganidan qisqaroq vaqt ichida aravada o'tirgan va Longborn yo'lida ekanini ko'rdi.

quiz.why_uz: O'sha davrda bu butun oilani sharmanda qilardi.

quiz.q: Why does Elizabeth think she has lost Darcy now?
