chapters.title: Return to Longbourn
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet va Gardinerlar uyga shoshilishadi. Uikhemning qarzlari va yolg'onlari fosh bo'ladi. Missis Bennet asab xurujida, janob Bennet Londonda Lidiyani izlamoqda. Lidiyaning beparvo xati o'qiladi.

paras.en: “I have been thinking it over again, Elizabeth,” said her uncle, as they drove from the town; “and really, upon serious consideration, I am much more inclined than I was to judge as your eldest sister does on the matter. It appears to me so very unlikely that any young man should form such a design against a girl who is by no means unprotected or friendless, and who was actually staying in his colonel's family, that I am strongly inclined to hope the best. Could he expect that her friends would not step forward? Could he expect to be noticed again by the regiment, after such an affront to Colonel Forster? His temptation is not adequate to the risk!”
paras.uz: «Men buni qayta o'ylab ko'rdim, Elizabet, — dedi tog'asi, ular shahardan chiqib ketishayotganda, — va haqiqatan ham jiddiy mulohaza qilib, bu masalada to'ng'ich opang kabi hukm chiqarishga avvalgidan ancha ko'proq moyilman. Menga hech qanday yosh yigit umuman himoyasiz yoki do'stsiz bo'lmagan va aslida o'z polkovnigining oilasida yashayotgan qizga qarshi bunday niyat qilishi juda ehtimoldan yiroq tuyuladi, shuning uchun eng yaxshisiga umid qilishga qattiq moyilman. U qizning do'stlari oldinga chiqmaydi deb kuta olarmidi? Polkovnik Forsterni bunday haqorat qilgandan keyin polkda yana e'tibor topishni kuta olarmidi? Uning vasvasasi xavfga arzimaydi!»

paras.en: “Do you really think so?” cried Elizabeth, brightening up for a moment.
paras.uz: «Rostdan shunday deb o'ylaysizmi?» — xitob qildi Elizabet, bir lahza yuzi yorishib.

paras.en: “Upon my word,” said Mrs. Gardiner, “I begin to be of your uncle's opinion. It is really too great a violation of decency, honour, and interest, for him to be guilty of. I cannot think so very ill of Wickham. Can you yourself, Lizzy, so wholly give him up, as to believe him capable of it?”
paras.uz: «Ochig'ini aytsam, — dedi missis Gardiner, — men ham tog'angning fikriga qo'shila boshladim. Bu uning aybdor bo'lishi uchun odob, sharaf va manfaatning haddan tashqari katta buzilishi. Uikhem haqida bunchalik yomon o'ylay olmayman. Sen o'zing, Lizzi, uni bunga qodir deb ishonadigan darajada undan butunlay voz kecha olasanmi?»

paras.en: “Not, perhaps, of neglecting his own interest; but of every other neglect I can believe him capable. If, indeed, it should be so! But I dare not hope it. Why should they not go on to Scotland if that had been the case?”
paras.uz: «Ehtimol, o'z manfaatini e'tiborsiz qoldirishga emas; lekin boshqa har qanday e'tiborsizlikka uni qodir deb ishona olaman. Qaniydi, haqiqatan ham shunday bo'lsa! Lekin bunga umid qilishga jur'at etmayman. Agar shunday bo'lganida, nega ular Shotlandiyaga ketmasdi?»

paras.en: “In the first place,” replied Mr. Gardiner, “there is no absolute proof that they are not gone to Scotland.”
paras.uz: «Birinchidan, — javob berdi janob Gardiner, — ularning Shotlandiyaga ketmagani haqida mutlaq dalil yo'q».

paras.en: “Oh! but their removing from the chaise into a hackney coach is such a presumption! And, besides, no traces of them were to be found on the Barnet road.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Lekin ularning aravadan yollanma karetaga o'tishlari juda katta asos! Bundan tashqari, Barnet yo'lida ularning hech qanday izi topilmagan».

paras.en: “Well, then--supposing them to be in London. They may be there, though for the purpose of concealment, for no more exceptional purpose. It is not likely that money should be very abundant on either side; and it might strike them that they could be more economically, though less expeditiously, married in London than in Scotland.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, unday bo'lsa — ular Londonda deb faraz qilaylik. Ular u yerda yashirinish maqsadida bo'lishi mumkin, bundan ortiq g'ayrioddiy maqsadsiz. Har ikki tomonda ham pul juda ko'p bo'lishi ehtimoldan yiroq; va ularga Londonda Shotlandiyadagidan ko'ra tejamliroq, garchi tezroq bo'lmasa ham, turmush qurish mumkinligi xayoliga kelishi mumkin».

paras.en: “But why all this secrecy? Why any fear of detection? Why must their marriage be private? Oh, no, no--this is not likely. His most particular friend, you see by Jane's account, was persuaded of his never intending to marry her. Wickham will never marry a woman without some money. He cannot afford it. And what claims has Lydia--what attraction has she beyond youth, health, and good humour that could make him, for her sake, forego every chance of benefiting himself by marrying well? As to what restraint the apprehensions of disgrace in the corps might throw on a dishonourable elopement with her, I am not able to judge; for I know nothing of the effects that such a step might produce. But as to your other objection, I am afraid it will hardly hold good. Lydia has no brothers to step forward; and he might imagine, from my father's behaviour, from his indolence and the little attention he has ever seemed to give to what was going forward in his family, that he would do as little, and think as little about it, as any father could do, in such a matter.”
paras.uz: «Lekin nega bunchalik sir saqlash? Nega fosh bo'lishdan qo'rqish? Nega ularning nikohi yashirin bo'lishi kerak? Oh, yo'q, yo'q — bu ehtimoldan yiroq. Jeynning aytishicha, uning eng yaqin do'sti uning unga hech qachon uylanish niyati bo'lmaganiga ishongan. Uikhem hech qachon biroz pulsiz ayolga uylanmaydi. Bunga qurbi yetmaydi. Lidiyaning qanday da'vosi bor — yoshlik, sog'lik va xushfe'llikdan tashqari uni qiz uchun yaxshi uylanib, o'ziga foyda ko'rishning har qanday imkoniyatidan voz kechishga majbur qiladigan qanday jozibasi bor? Polkda sharmandalikdan qo'rqish u bilan sharafsiz qochishga qanday cheklov qo'yishi mumkinligi haqida hukm chiqara olmayman; chunki bunday qadam qanday ta'sir ko'rsatishi mumkinligini bilmayman. Lekin sizning boshqa e'tirozingizga kelsak, qo'rqamanki, u o'rinli bo'lmaydi. Lidiyaning oldinga chiqadigan akalari yo'q; u esa otamning xatti-harakatidan, dangasaligidan va oilasida nima bo'layotganiga hech qachon kam e'tibor berganidan, u bunday ishda har qanday ota qila oladigan darajada kam narsa qiladi va kam o'ylaydi, deb tasavvur qilishi mumkin».

paras.en: “But can you think that Lydia is so lost to everything but love of him as to consent to live with him on any terms other than marriage?”
paras.uz: «Lekin Lidiya uni sevishdan boshqa hamma narsadan shunchalik mahrum bo'lib, u bilan nikohdan boshqa har qanday shartlarda yashashga rozi bo'ladi deb o'ylay olasanmi?»

paras.en: “It does seem, and it is most shocking indeed,” replied Elizabeth, with tears in her eyes, “that a sister's sense of decency and virtue in such a point should admit of doubt. But, really, I know not what to say. Perhaps I am not doing her justice. But she is very young; she has never been taught to think on serious subjects; and for the last half-year, nay, for a twelvemonth--she has been given up to nothing but amusement and vanity. She has been allowed to dispose of her time in the most idle and frivolous manner, and to adopt any opinions that came in her way. Since the ----shire were first quartered in Meryton, nothing but love, flirtation, and officers have been in her head. She has been doing everything in her power by thinking and talking on the subject, to give greater--what shall I call it? susceptibility to her feelings; which are naturally lively enough. And we all know that Wickham has every charm of person and address that can captivate a woman.”
paras.uz: «Bu shunday tuyuladi va haqiqatan ham eng dahshatlisi, — javob berdi Elizabet, ko'zlarida yosh bilan, — bunday masalada singlining odob va fazilat hissi shubha ostida bo'lishi. Lekin, rostdan ham, nima deyishni bilmayman. Ehtimol, unga adolat qilmayotgandirman. Lekin u juda yosh; unga hech qachon jiddiy mavzularda o'ylashni o'rgatishmagan; so'nggi yarim yil, yo'q, butun bir yil davomida u faqat ko'ngilxushlik va shuhratparastlikka berilib kelgan. Unga vaqtini eng bekorchi va yengiltak tarzda o'tkazishga va yo'lida uchragan har qanday fikrni qabul qilishga ruxsat berilgan. ----shir polki Meritonga birinchi joylashgandan beri uning boshida muhabbat, noz-karashma va ofitserlardan boshqa hech narsa yo'q. U bu mavzuda o'ylash va gapirish bilan tabiatan yetarlicha jo'shqin bo'lgan tuyg'ulariga kattaroq — nima deb ataylik? — ta'sirchanlik berish uchun qo'lidan kelgan hamma narsani qilgan. Hammamiz bilamizki, Uikhemda ayolni maftun qila oladigan qiyofa va muomalaning barcha jozibalari bor».

paras.en: “But you see that Jane,” said her aunt, “does not think so very ill of Wickham as to believe him capable of the attempt.”
paras.uz: «Lekin ko'rib turibsanki, Jeyn, — dedi xolasi, — Uikhem haqida uni bunday urinishga qodir deb ishonadigan darajada yomon o'ylamaydi».

paras.en: “Of whom does Jane ever think ill? And who is there, whatever might be their former conduct, that she would think capable of such an attempt, till it were proved against them? But Jane knows, as well as I do, what Wickham really is. We both know that he has been profligate in every sense of the word; that he has neither integrity nor honour; that he is as false and deceitful as he is insinuating.”
paras.uz: «Jeyn qachon kim haqida yomon o'ylaydi? Avvalgi xatti-harakati qanday bo'lmasin, kim borki, u ularga qarshi isbotlanmaguncha bunday urinishga qodir deb o'ylasa? Lekin Jeyn ham men kabi Uikhemning aslida kim ekanini biladi. Ikkalamiz ham bilamizki, u so'zning har qanday ma'nosida buzuq bo'lgan; unda na halollik, na sharaf bor; u qanchalik yoqimtoy bo'lsa, shunchalik yolg'onchi va makkor».

paras.en: “And do you really know all this?” cried Mrs. Gardiner, whose curiosity as to the mode of her intelligence was all alive.
paras.uz: «Va sen haqiqatan ham bularning hammasini bilasanmi?» — xitob qildi missis Gardiner, uning ma'lumot olish usuliga qiziqishi butunlay jonlanib.

paras.en: “I do indeed,” replied Elizabeth, colouring. “I told you, the other day, of his infamous behaviour to Mr. Darcy; and you yourself, when last at Longbourn, heard in what manner he spoke of the man who had behaved with such forbearance and liberality towards him. And there are other circumstances which I am not at liberty--which it is not worth while to relate; but his lies about the whole Pemberley family are endless. From what he said of Miss Darcy I was thoroughly prepared to see a proud, reserved, disagreeable girl. Yet he knew to the contrary himself. He must know that she was as amiable and unpretending as we have found her.”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham bilaman, — javob berdi Elizabet qizarib. — O'tgan kuni sizga uning janob Darsiga nisbatan sharmandali xatti-harakati haqida aytdim; siz o'zingiz Longbornda oxirgi marta bo'lganingizda, u o'ziga nisbatan shunchalik sabr va saxiylik bilan munosabatda bo'lgan odam haqida qanday gapirganini eshitgansiz. Yana boshqa holatlar ham bor, ularni aytishga haqqim yo'q — aytib o'tirishga arzimaydi; lekin uning butun Pemberli oilasi haqidagi yolg'onlari cheksiz. U miss Darsi haqida aytganlaridan men mag'rur, vazmin, yoqimsiz qizni ko'rishga to'liq tayyor edim. Shunga qaramay, u o'zi aksincha ekanini bilardi. U uning biz topgandek yoqimli va kamtar ekanini bilishi kerak».

paras.en: “But does Lydia know nothing of this? can she be ignorant of what you and Jane seem so well to understand?”
paras.uz: «Lekin Lidiya bu haqda hech narsa bilmaydimi? U sen va Jeyn shunchalik yaxshi tushunayotgan narsadan bexabar bo'lishi mumkinmi?»

paras.en: “Oh, yes!--that, that is the worst of all. Till I was in Kent, and saw so much both of Mr. Darcy and his relation Colonel Fitzwilliam, I was ignorant of the truth myself. And when I returned home, the ----shire was to leave Meryton in a week or fortnight's time. As that was the case, neither Jane, to whom I related the whole, nor I, thought it necessary to make our knowledge public; for of what use could it apparently be to any one, that the good opinion which all the neighbourhood had of him should then be overthrown? And even when it was settled that Lydia should go with Mrs. Forster, the necessity of opening her eyes to his character never occurred to me. That she could be in any danger from the deception never entered my head. That such a consequence as this could ensue, you may easily believe, was far enough from my thoughts.”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha! — mana shu, mana shu hammasidan yomoni. Kentda bo'lib, janob Darsini ham, uning qarindoshi polkovnik Fitsuilyamni ham ko'p ko'rgunimcha, men o'zim haqiqatdan bexabar edim. Uyga qaytganimda esa ----shir polki bir-ikki hafta ichida Meritonni tark etishi kerak edi. Shunday bo'lgani uchun, hammasini aytib bergan Jeyn ham, men ham bilganlarimizni oshkor qilishni zarur deb hisoblamadik; chunki butun mahallaning u haqidagi yaxshi fikrini o'shanda ag'darib tashlashdan kimga qanday foyda bo'lishi mumkin edi? Hatto Lidiya missis Forster bilan borishi hal bo'lganda ham, uning ko'zlarini uning xarakteriga ochish zarurligi xayolimga kelmadi. Uning bu aldov tufayli biror xavfga duch kelishi mumkinligi xayolimga ham kirmadi. Bunday oqibat kelib chiqishi mumkinligi, osongina ishonishingiz mumkin, fikrlarimdan juda yiroq edi».

paras.en: “When they all removed to Brighton, therefore, you had no reason, I suppose, to believe them fond of each other?”
paras.uz: «Demak, ular hammasi Braytonga ko'chib ketganda, ularni bir-birini yaxshi ko'radi deb ishonishing uchun sababing yo'q edi, shekilli?»

paras.en: “Not the slightest. I can remember no symptom of affection on either side; and had anything of the kind been perceptible, you must be aware that ours is not a family on which it could be thrown away. When first he entered the corps, she was ready enough to admire him; but so we all were. Every girl in or near Meryton was out of her senses about him for the first two months; but he never distinguished her by any particular attention; and, consequently, after a moderate period of extravagant and wild admiration, her fancy for him gave way, and others of the regiment, who treated her with more distinction, again became her favourites.”
paras.uz: «Zarracha ham. Hech bir tomonda mehrning birorta alomatini eslay olmayman; agar shunga o'xshash biror narsa sezilganida, bilishingiz kerakki, bizniki bunday narsa e'tiborsiz qoladigan oila emas. U polkka birinchi kirganda, u unga qoyil qolishga yetarlicha tayyor edi; lekin hammamiz ham shunday edik. Meritondagi yoki uning yaqinidagi har bir qiz birinchi ikki oy u tufayli esini yo'qotgan edi; lekin u uni hech qachon alohida e'tibor bilan ajratib ko'rsatmagan; shuning uchun mo''tadil muddatli haddan oshgan va yovvoyi hayratdan keyin uning unga havasi so'ndi va polkning unga ko'proq e'tibor ko'rsatgan boshqalari yana uning sevimlilariga aylandi».

paras.en: It may be easily believed, that however little of novelty could be added to their fears, hopes, and conjectures, on this interesting subject, by its repeated discussion, no other could detain them from it long, during the whole of the journey. From Elizabeth's thoughts it was never absent. Fixed there by the keenest of all anguish, self-reproach, she could find no interval of ease or forgetfulness.
paras.uz: Osongina ishonish mumkinki, bu qiziqarli mavzuni qayta-qayta muhokama qilish ularning qo'rquvlari, umidlari va taxminlariga qanchalik kam yangilik qo'shmasin, butun safar davomida boshqa hech qanday mavzu ularni undan uzoq ushlab tura olmadi. U Elizabetning fikrlaridan hech qachon chiqmadi. Barcha azoblarning eng o'tkiri — o'zini ayblash bilan u yerga qadalgan holda, u hech qanday yengillik yoki unutish oralig'ini topa olmadi.

paras.en: They travelled as expeditiously as possible, and, sleeping one night on the road, reached Longbourn by dinner time the next day. It was a comfort to Elizabeth to consider that Jane could not have been wearied by long expectations.
paras.uz: Ular iloji boricha tez sayohat qilishdi va yo'lda bir kecha uxlab, ertasi kuni tushlik vaqtiga Longbornga yetib kelishdi. Jeyn uzoq kutishdan charchamagan bo'lishi mumkinligini o'ylash Elizabetga taskin berdi.

paras.en: The little Gardiners, attracted by the sight of a chaise, were standing on the steps of the house as they entered the paddock; and, when the carriage drove up to the door, the joyful surprise that lighted up their faces, and displayed itself over their whole bodies, in a variety of capers and frisks, was the first pleasing earnest of their welcome.
paras.uz: Aravani ko'rib, jalb qilingan kichkina Gardinerlar ular hovliga kirganda uyning zinapoyasida turishardi; arava eshik oldiga kelganda, ularning yuzlarini yoritgan va butun tanalarida turli sakrash va o'ynoqlashlar bilan namoyon bo'lgan quvonchli hayrat ularni kutib olishning birinchi yoqimli belgisi edi.

paras.en: Elizabeth jumped out; and, after giving each of them a hasty kiss, hurried into the vestibule, where Jane, who came running down from her mother's apartment, immediately met her.
paras.uz: Elizabet sakrab tushdi; va har biriga shoshilib bo'sa qilgach, dahlizga shoshildi, u yerda onasining xonasidan yugurib tushgan Jeyn darhol uni kutib oldi.

paras.en: Elizabeth, as she affectionately embraced her, whilst tears filled the eyes of both, lost not a moment in asking whether anything had been heard of the fugitives.
paras.uz: Elizabet uni mehr bilan quchoqlarkan, ikkalasining ham ko'zlari yoshga to'lgan holda, qochoqlar haqida biror xabar eshitilganmi, deb so'rashda bir lahza ham vaqt yo'qotmadi.

paras.en: “Not yet,” replied Jane. “But now that my dear uncle is come, I hope everything will be well.”
paras.uz: «Hali yo'q, — javob berdi Jeyn. — Lekin endi aziz tog'am kelgach, umid qilamanki, hammasi yaxshi bo'ladi».

paras.en: “Is my father in town?”
paras.uz: «Otam Londondami?»

paras.en: “Yes, he went on Tuesday, as I wrote you word.”
paras.uz: «Ha, senga yozganimdek, u seshanba kuni ketdi».

paras.en: “And have you heard from him often?”
paras.uz: «Undan tez-tez xabar oldinglarmi?»

paras.en: “We have heard only twice. He wrote me a few lines on Wednesday to say that he had arrived in safety, and to give me his directions, which I particularly begged him to do. He merely added that he should not write again till he had something of importance to mention.”
paras.uz: «Faqat ikki marta xabar oldik. U chorshanba kuni menga eson-omon yetib kelganini aytish va ko'rsatmalarini berish uchun bir necha satr yozdi, buni undan ayniqsa iltimos qilgan edim. U faqat biror muhim narsa aytadigan bo'lmaguncha yana yozmasligini qo'shib qo'ydi».

paras.en: “And my mother--how is she? How are you all?”
paras.uz: «Onam-chi — u qanday? Hammangiz qandaysizlar?»

paras.en: “My mother is tolerably well, I trust; though her spirits are greatly shaken. She is up stairs and will have great satisfaction in seeing you all. She does not yet leave her dressing-room. Mary and Kitty, thank Heaven, are quite well.”
paras.uz: «Onam, umid qilamanki, ancha yaxshi; garchi kayfiyati juda chayqalgan bo'lsa ham. U yuqorida va hammangizni ko'rishdan juda mamnun bo'ladi. U hali kiyinish xonasidan chiqmayapti. Meri va Ketti, Xudoga shukr, mutlaqo sog'».

paras.en: “But you--how are you?” cried Elizabeth. “You look pale. How much you must have gone through!”
paras.uz: «Lekin sen-chi — sen qandaysan? — xitob qildi Elizabet. — Rangpar ko'rinasan. Qanchalik ko'p narsani boshdan kechirgan bo'lsang kerak!»

paras.en: Her sister, however, assured her of her being perfectly well; and their conversation, which had been passing while Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner were engaged with their children, was now put an end to by the approach of the whole party. Jane ran to her uncle and aunt, and welcomed and thanked them both, with alternate smiles and tears.
paras.uz: Biroq opasi uni mutlaqo sog'ligiga ishontirdi; janob va missis Gardiner bolalari bilan band bo'lgan paytda bo'lib o'tayotgan ularning suhbati endi butun davraning yaqinlashishi bilan tugadi. Jeyn tog'asi va xolasining oldiga yugurdi va navbatma-navbat tabassum va ko'z yoshlari bilan ikkalasini kutib oldi va rahmat aytdi.

paras.en: When they were all in the drawing-room, the questions which Elizabeth had already asked were of course repeated by the others, and they soon found that Jane had no intelligence to give. The sanguine hope of good, however, which the benevolence of her heart suggested had not yet deserted her; she still expected that it would all end well, and that every morning would bring some letter, either from Lydia or her father, to explain their proceedings, and, perhaps, announce their marriage.
paras.uz: Hammalari mehmonxonada bo'lganlarida, Elizabet allaqachon bergan savollar, albatta, boshqalar tomonidan takrorlandi va ular tez orada Jeynning beradigan hech qanday ma'lumoti yo'qligini bilishdi. Biroq qalbining ezguligi taklif qilgan yaxshilikka bo'lgan qizg'in umid uni hali tark etmagan edi; u hali ham hammasi yaxshi tugashini va har ertalab Lidiya yoki otasidan ularning harakatlarini tushuntiradigan va, ehtimol, ularning nikohini e'lon qiladigan biror xat kelishini kutardi.

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet, to whose apartment they all repaired, after a few minutes' conversation together, received them exactly as might be expected; with tears and lamentations of regret, invectives against the villainous conduct of Wickham, and complaints of her own sufferings and ill-usage; blaming everybody but the person to whose ill-judging indulgence the errors of her daughter must principally be owing.
paras.uz: Bir necha daqiqa birga suhbatlashgandan keyin hammalari uning xonasiga borishgan missis Bennet ularni aynan kutilganidek qabul qildi; ko'z yoshlari va afsus nolalari, Uikhemning pastkash xatti-harakatiga qarshi la'natlar va o'z azoblari hamda o'ziga yomon munosabatdan shikoyatlar bilan; qizining xatolari asosan noto'g'ri erkalatishiga bog'liq bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan shaxsdan boshqa hammani ayblab.

paras.en: “If I had been able,” said she, “to carry my point in going to Brighton, with all my family, this would not have happened; but poor dear Lydia had nobody to take care of her. Why did the Forsters ever let her go out of their sight? I am sure there was some great neglect or other on their side, for she is not the kind of girl to do such a thing if she had been well looked after. I always thought they were very unfit to have the charge of her; but I was overruled, as I always am. Poor dear child! And now here's Mr. Bennet gone away, and I know he will fight Wickham, wherever he meets him and then he will be killed, and what is to become of us all? The Collinses will turn us out before he is cold in his grave, and if you are not kind to us, brother, I do not know what we shall do.”
paras.uz: «Agar men, — dedi u, — butun oilam bilan Braytonga borish fikrimni o'tkaza olganimda, bu sodir bo'lmasdi; lekin bechora aziz Lidiyaga qaraydigan hech kim yo'q edi. Nega Forsterlar uni ko'zdan qochirishdi? Ishonchim komilki, ular tomonidan qandaydir katta beparvolik bo'lgan, chunki agar unga yaxshi qarashganida, u bunday ishni qiladigan qiz emas. Men doim ular unga qarash uchun juda nomunosib deb o'ylardim; lekin har doimgidek mening fikrimni inobatga olishmadi. Bechora aziz bolam! Endi janob Bennet ketdi va bilaman, u Uikhemni qayerda uchratsa, u bilan duelga chiqadi, keyin o'ldiriladi, shunda hammamizga nima bo'ladi? Kollinzlar u qabrida sovib ulgurmasidan bizni haydab chiqarishadi va agar sen bizga mehribon bo'lmasang, uka, nima qilishimizni bilmayman».

paras.en: They all exclaimed against such terrific ideas; and Mr. Gardiner, after general assurances of his affection for her and all her family, told her that he meant to be in London the very next day, and would assist Mr. Bennet in every endeavour for recovering Lydia.
paras.uz: Hammalari bunday dahshatli fikrlarga qarshi xitob qilishdi; janob Gardiner unga va butun oilasiga mehri haqida umumiy ishontirishlardan keyin ertasi kuniyoq Londonda bo'lmoqchi ekanini va Lidiyani qaytarishga qaratilgan har bir urinishda janob Bennetga yordam berishini aytdi.

paras.en: “Do not give way to useless alarm,” added he; “though it is right to be prepared for the worst, there is no occasion to look on it as certain. It is not quite a week since they left Brighton. In a few days more we may gain some news of them; and till we know that they are not married, and have no design of marrying, do not let us give the matter over as lost. As soon as I get to town I shall go to my brother, and make him come home with me to Gracechurch Street; and then we may consult together as to what is to be done.”
paras.uz: «Befoyda xavotirga berilmang, — qo'shib qo'ydi u. — Eng yomoniga tayyor bo'lish to'g'ri bo'lsa ham, unga aniq deb qarashga hech qanday sabab yo'q. Ular Braytondan ketganiga hali bir hafta ham bo'lmadi. Yana bir necha kunda ular haqida biror xabar olishimiz mumkin; ular turmush qurmagani va turmush qurish niyati yo'qligini bilmagunimizcha, ishni yo'qotilgan deb hisoblamaylik. Londonga yetib borishim bilan pochchamning oldiga boraman va uni men bilan Greyschurch ko'chasiga kelishga majbur qilaman; keyin nima qilish kerakligi haqida birga maslahatlashamiz».

paras.en: “Oh! my dear brother,” replied Mrs. Bennet, “that is exactly what I could most wish for. And now do, when you get to town, find them out, wherever they may be; and if they are not married already, make them marry. And as for wedding clothes, do not let them wait for that, but tell Lydia she shall have as much money as she chooses to buy them, after they are married. And, above all, keep Mr. Bennet from fighting. Tell him what a dreadful state I am in, that I am frighted out of my wits--and have such tremblings, such flutterings, all over me--such spasms in my side and pains in my head, and such beatings at heart, that I can get no rest by night nor by day. And tell my dear Lydia not to give any directions about her clothes till she has seen me, for she does not know which are the best warehouses. Oh, brother, how kind you are! I know you will contrive it all.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Aziz ukam, — javob berdi missis Bennet, — men aynan shuni eng ko'p xohlardim. Endi Londonga yetib borganingda, ular qayerda bo'lmasin, ularni top; agar ular hali turmush qurmagan bo'lsa, ularni turmush qurishga majbur qil. To'y kiyimlariga kelsak, buning uchun kutishmasin, lekin Lidiyaga ayt, turmush qurganlaridan keyin ularni sotib olish uchun xohlagancha pul oladi. Eng muhimi, janob Bennetni duel qilishdan saqla. Unga qanday dahshatli ahvolda ekanimni ayt, qo'rquvdan esimni yo'qotganimni — butun vujudimda shunday titroqlar, shunday titrashlar borligini — biqinimda shunday tutqanoqlar va boshimda og'riqlar, yuragimda shunday urishlar borki, na kechasi, na kunduzi tinchim yo'q. Aziz Lidiyamga esa meni ko'rmaguncha kiyimlari haqida hech qanday ko'rsatma bermasligini ayt, chunki u qaysi do'konlar eng yaxshi ekanini bilmaydi. Oh, uka, qanchalik mehribonsan! Bilaman, hammasini uddalaysan».

paras.en: But Mr. Gardiner, though he assured her again of his earnest endeavours in the cause, could not avoid recommending moderation to her, as well in her hopes as her fear; and after talking with her in this manner till dinner was on the table, they all left her to vent all her feelings on the housekeeper, who attended in the absence of her daughters.
paras.uz: Lekin janob Gardiner bu ishdagi jiddiy sa'y-harakatlariga uni yana ishontirsa ham, unga umidlarida ham, qo'rquvlarida ham mo''tadillikni tavsiya qilmay qololmadi; tushlik dasturxonga tortilgunicha u bilan shu tarzda gaplashgach, hammalari uni qizlari yo'qligida unga qarab turgan uy bekasiga barcha tuyg'ularini to'kib solish uchun qoldirishdi.

paras.en: Though her brother and sister were persuaded that there was no real occasion for such a seclusion from the family, they did not attempt to oppose it, for they knew that she had not prudence enough to hold her tongue before the servants, while they waited at table, and judged it better that one only of the household, and the one whom they could most trust should comprehend all her fears and solicitude on the subject.
paras.uz: Garchi ukasi va kelini uning oiladan bunday ajralib turishiga hech qanday haqiqiy sabab yo'qligiga ishonsalar ham, ular bunga qarshi chiqishga urinmadilar, chunki u xizmatkorlar stolda xizmat qilayotganda tilini tiyadigan darajada ehtiyotkor emasligini bilishardi va bu masaladagi uning barcha qo'rquvlari va tashvishlarini uy ahlidan faqat bittasi, ular eng ko'p ishonadigan bittasi tushunishi yaxshiroq deb hisoblashdi.

paras.en: In the dining-room they were soon joined by Mary and Kitty, who had been too busily engaged in their separate apartments to make their appearance before. One came from her books, and the other from her toilette. The faces of both, however, were tolerably calm; and no change was visible in either, except that the loss of her favourite sister, or the anger which she had herself incurred in this business, had given more of fretfulness than usual to the accents of Kitty. As for Mary, she was mistress enough of herself to whisper to Elizabeth, with a countenance of grave reflection, soon after they were seated at table:
paras.uz: Ovqatxonada ularga tez orada avval paydo bo'lish uchun o'z xonalarida haddan tashqari band bo'lgan Meri va Ketti qo'shilishdi. Biri kitoblaridan, ikkinchisi kiyinish stolidan keldi. Biroq ikkalasining yuzlari ancha xotirjam edi; va hech birida hech qanday o'zgarish ko'rinmadi, faqat sevimli singlisining yo'qolishi yoki bu ishda o'zi duchor bo'lgan g'azab Kettining ohangiga odatdagidan ko'proq jizzakilik bergan edi. Meriga kelsak, u stolga o'tirishlaridan ko'p o'tmay jiddiy mulohaza qiyofasida Elizabetga pichirlash uchun o'ziga yetarlicha hokim edi:

paras.en: “This is a most unfortunate affair, and will probably be much talked of. But we must stem the tide of malice, and pour into the wounded bosoms of each other the balm of sisterly consolation.”
paras.uz: «Bu eng omadsiz ish va, ehtimol, u haqida ko'p gapirishadi. Lekin biz g'araz oqimini to'xtatishimiz va bir-birimizning yaralangan ko'ksimizga opa-singillik taskinining malhamini quyishimiz kerak».

paras.en: Then, perceiving in Elizabeth no inclination of replying, she added, “Unhappy as the event must be for Lydia, we may draw from it this useful lesson: that loss of virtue in a female is irretrievable; that one false step involves her in endless ruin; that her reputation is no less brittle than it is beautiful; and that she cannot be too much guarded in her behaviour towards the undeserving of the other sex.”
paras.uz: Keyin Elizabetda javob berishga hech qanday moyillik ko'rmay, qo'shib qo'ydi: «Voqea Lidiya uchun qanchalik baxtsiz bo'lmasin, biz undan shunday foydali saboq olishimiz mumkin: ayolda fazilatning yo'qolishi qaytarib bo'lmas; bitta noto'g'ri qadam uni cheksiz halokatga soladi; uning obro'si go'zal bo'lgani kabi mo'rt hamdir; va u qarama-qarshi jinsning noloyiqlariga nisbatan xatti-harakatida haddan tashqari ehtiyotkor bo'lishi mumkin emas».

paras.en: Elizabeth lifted up her eyes in amazement, but was too much oppressed to make any reply. Mary, however, continued to console herself with such kind of moral extractions from the evil before them.
paras.uz: Elizabet hayrat bilan ko'zlarini ko'tardi, lekin javob berish uchun haddan tashqari ezilgan edi. Biroq Meri oldilaridagi yomonlikdan shunday axloqiy xulosalar chiqarib, o'zini yupatishda davom etdi.

paras.en: In the afternoon, the two elder Miss Bennets were able to be for half-an-hour by themselves; and Elizabeth instantly availed herself of the opportunity of making any inquiries, which Jane was equally eager to satisfy. After joining in general lamentations over the dreadful sequel of this event, which Elizabeth considered as all but certain, and Miss Bennet could not assert to be wholly impossible, the former continued the subject, by saying, “But tell me all and everything about it which I have not already heard. Give me further particulars. What did Colonel Forster say? Had they no apprehension of anything before the elopement took place? They must have seen them together for ever.”
paras.uz: Tushdan keyin ikki katta miss Bennet yarim soat yolg'iz qola olishdi; Elizabet darhol har qanday so'roq qilish imkoniyatidan foydalandi, Jeyn esa ularni qondirishga xuddi shunday intilardi. Elizabet deyarli aniq deb hisoblagan, miss Bennet esa butunlay imkonsiz deb ta'kidlay olmagan bu voqeaning dahshatli oqibati ustidan umumiy nolishlarga qo'shilgach, birinchisi mavzuni davom ettirib, dedi: «Lekin bu haqda men hali eshitmagan hamma narsani, har bir narsani aytib ber. Ko'proq tafsilot ber. Polkovnik Forster nima dedi? Qochish sodir bo'lishidan oldin ular hech narsadan xavotirlanishmaganmi? Ular ularni doim birga ko'rgan bo'lishsa kerak».

paras.en: “Colonel Forster did own that he had often suspected some partiality, especially on Lydia's side, but nothing to give him any alarm. I am so grieved for him! His behaviour was attentive and kind to the utmost. He was coming to us, in order to assure us of his concern, before he had any idea of their not being gone to Scotland: when that apprehension first got abroad, it hastened his journey.”
paras.uz: «Polkovnik Forster ko'pincha, ayniqsa Lidiya tomonidan qandaydir moyillikdan shubhalanganini tan oldi, lekin unga xavotir beradigan hech narsa bo'lmagan. Unga shunchalik achinaman! Uning xatti-harakati nihoyatda e'tiborli va mehribon edi. U ular Shotlandiyaga ketmagani haqida hech qanday tasavvurga ega bo'lmasdanoq, bizni tashvishiga ishontirish uchun bizga kelayotgan edi: o'sha xavotir birinchi tarqalganda, bu uning safarini tezlashtirdi».

paras.en: “And was Denny convinced that Wickham would not marry? Did he know of their intending to go off? Had Colonel Forster seen Denny himself?”
paras.uz: «Denni Uikhem uylanmasligiga ishonganmi? U ularning qochish niyatidan xabardor bo'lganmi? Polkovnik Forster Dennini o'zi ko'rganmi?»

paras.en: “Yes; but, when questioned by him, Denny denied knowing anything of their plans, and would not give his real opinion about it. He did not repeat his persuasion of their not marrying--and from that, I am inclined to hope, he might have been misunderstood before.”
paras.uz: «Ha; lekin u so'roq qilganda, Denni ularning rejalari haqida hech narsa bilishini inkor etdi va bu haqda haqiqiy fikrini aytmadi. U ularning turmush qurmasligi haqidagi ishonchini takrorlamadi — va bundan, umid qilishga moyilman, uni avval noto'g'ri tushungan bo'lishlari mumkin».

paras.en: “And till Colonel Forster came himself, not one of you entertained a doubt, I suppose, of their being really married?”
paras.uz: «Polkovnik Forsterning o'zi kelguncha, hech biringiz ularning haqiqatan ham turmush qurganiga shubha qilmagansizlar, shekilli?»

paras.en: “How was it possible that such an idea should enter our brains? I felt a little uneasy--a little fearful of my sister's happiness with him in marriage, because I knew that his conduct had not been always quite right. My father and mother knew nothing of that; they only felt how imprudent a match it must be. Kitty then owned, with a very natural triumph on knowing more than the rest of us, that in Lydia's last letter she had prepared her for such a step. She had known, it seems, of their being in love with each other, many weeks.”
paras.uz: «Bunday fikr qanday qilib miyamizga kelishi mumkin edi? Men biroz bezovta edim — singlimning u bilan nikohda baxtli bo'lishidan biroz qo'rqardim, chunki uning xatti-harakati doim ham to'g'ri bo'lmaganini bilardim. Otam va onam bu haqda hech narsa bilishmasdi; ular faqat bu qanchalik ehtiyotsiz nikoh bo'lishi kerakligini his qilishdi. Shunda Ketti qolganlarimizdan ko'proq bilganidan juda tabiiy g'alaba bilan Lidiya oxirgi xatida uni bunday qadamga tayyorlaganini tan oldi. U, shekilli, ularning bir-biriga oshiq ekanini ko'p haftalardan beri bilgan».

paras.en: “But not before they went to Brighton?”
paras.uz: «Lekin ular Braytonga ketishidan oldin emasmi?»

paras.en: “No, I believe not.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, menimcha, emas».

paras.en: “And did Colonel Forster appear to think well of Wickham himself? Does he know his real character?”
paras.uz: «Polkovnik Forster Uikhemning o'zi haqida yaxshi o'ylaganga o'xshardimi? U uning haqiqiy xarakterini biladimi?»

paras.en: “I must confess that he did not speak so well of Wickham as he formerly did. He believed him to be imprudent and extravagant. And since this sad affair has taken place, it is said that he left Meryton greatly in debt; but I hope this may be false.”
paras.uz: «Tan olishim kerakki, u Uikhem haqida avvalgidek yaxshi gapirmadi. U uni ehtiyotsiz va isrofgar deb hisobladi. Bu qayg'uli voqea sodir bo'lganidan beri aytishlaricha, u Meritonni katta qarz bilan tark etgan; lekin umid qilamanki, bu yolg'ondir».

paras.en: “Oh, Jane, had we been less secret, had we told what we knew of him, this could not have happened!”
paras.uz: «Oh, Jeyn, agar biz kamroq sir saqlaganimizda, u haqida bilganlarimizni aytganimizda, bu sodir bo'lmasdi!»

paras.en: “Perhaps it would have been better,” replied her sister. “But to expose the former faults of any person without knowing what their present feelings were, seemed unjustifiable. We acted with the best intentions.”
paras.uz: «Ehtimol, yaxshiroq bo'lardi, — javob berdi opasi. — Lekin har qanday odamning hozirgi tuyg'ulari qanday ekanini bilmasdan avvalgi xatolarini fosh qilish oqlab bo'lmaydigan tuyuldi. Biz eng yaxshi niyatlar bilan harakat qildik».

paras.en: “Could Colonel Forster repeat the particulars of Lydia's note to his wife?”
paras.uz: «Polkovnik Forster Lidiyaning xotiniga yozgan xatining tafsilotlarini takrorlay oldimi?»

paras.en: “He brought it with him for us to see.”
paras.uz: «U bizga ko'rsatish uchun uni o'zi bilan olib keldi».

paras.en: Jane then took it from her pocket-book, and gave it to Elizabeth. These were the contents:
paras.uz: Keyin Jeyn uni yon daftaridan olib, Elizabetga berdi. Uning mazmuni shunday edi:

paras.en: “MY DEAR HARRIET,
paras.uz: «AZIZ HARRIYET,

paras.en: “You will laugh when you know where I am gone, and I cannot help laughing myself at your surprise to-morrow morning, as soon as I am missed. I am going to Gretna Green, and if you cannot guess with who, I shall think you a simpleton, for there is but one man in the world I love, and he is an angel. I should never be happy without him, so think it no harm to be off. You need not send them word at Longbourn of my going, if you do not like it, for it will make the surprise the greater, when I write to them and sign my name 'Lydia Wickham.' What a good joke it will be! I can hardly write for laughing. Pray make my excuses to Pratt for not keeping my engagement, and dancing with him to-night.
paras.uz: Qayerga ketganimni bilsang, kulasan, ertaga ertalab yo'qligim sezilishi bilanoq hayratingdan o'zim ham kulmay qololmayman. Men Gretna Gringa ketyapman va agar kim bilan ekanini taxmin qila olmasang, seni ahmoq deb o'ylayman, chunki dunyoda men sevadigan faqat bitta erkak bor va u farishta. Usiz hech qachon baxtli bo'lmasdim, shuning uchun ketishimni yomon deb o'ylama. Agar xohlamasang, Longbornga ketganim haqida xabar yuborishing shart emas, chunki men ularga xat yozib, "Lidiya Uikhem" deb imzo chekkanimda hayrat yanada katta bo'ladi. Qanday zo'r hazil bo'ladi! Kulgidan zo'rg'a yozyapman. Iltimos, Prattdan va'damni bajarmay, bugun kechqurun u bilan raqsga tushmaganim uchun uzr so'rab qo'y.

paras.en: Tell him I hope he will excuse me when he knows all; and tell him I will dance with him at the next ball we meet, with great pleasure. I shall send for my clothes when I get to Longbourn; but I wish you would tell Sally to mend a great slit in my worked muslin gown before they are packed up. Good-bye. Give my love to Colonel Forster. I hope you will drink to our good journey.
paras.uz: Unga ayt, umid qilamanki, hammasini bilganda meni kechiradi; va ayt, keyingi uchrashadigan balimizda u bilan katta mamnuniyat bilan raqsga tushaman. Longbornga yetib borganimda kiyimlarim uchun odam yuboraman; lekin Sallyga ular joylanishidan oldin naqshli muslin ko'ylagimdagi katta yirtiqni tikib qo'yishni aytsang edi. Xayr. Polkovnik Forsterga salomimni yetkaz. Umid qilamanki, oq yo'limiz uchun qadah ko'tarasan.

paras.en: “Your affectionate friend,
paras.uz: Mehribon dugonang,

paras.en: “LYDIA BENNET.”
paras.uz: LIDIYA BENNET».

paras.en: “Oh! thoughtless, thoughtless Lydia!” cried Elizabeth when she had finished it. “What a letter is this, to be written at such a moment! But at least it shows that she was serious on the subject of their journey. Whatever he might afterwards persuade her to, it was not on her side a scheme of infamy. My poor father! how he must have felt it!”
paras.uz: «Oh! Beparvo, beparvo Lidiya! — xitob qildi Elizabet, uni o'qib bo'lgach. — Bunday paytda yozilgan qanday xat bu! Lekin hech bo'lmaganda bu uning safarlari masalasida jiddiy bo'lganini ko'rsatadi. Keyin u uni nimaga ko'ndirgan bo'lmasin, bu uning tomonidan sharmandali reja emasdi. Bechora otam! U buni qanchalik his qilgan bo'lsa kerak!»

paras.en: “I never saw anyone so shocked. He could not speak a word for full ten minutes. My mother was taken ill immediately, and the whole house in such confusion!”
paras.uz: «Hech kimni bunchalik hayratga tushganini ko'rmaganman. U o'n daqiqa davomida bir og'iz ham gapira olmadi. Onam darhol kasal bo'lib qoldi, butun uy esa shunday sarosimada edi!»

paras.en: “Oh! Jane,” cried Elizabeth, “was there a servant belonging to it who did not know the whole story before the end of the day?”
paras.uz: «Oh! Jeyn, — xitob qildi Elizabet, — kun oxirigacha butun voqeani bilmagan birorta xizmatkor qoldimi?»

paras.en: “I do not know. I hope there was. But to be guarded at such a time is very difficult. My mother was in hysterics, and though I endeavoured to give her every assistance in my power, I am afraid I did not do so much as I might have done! But the horror of what might possibly happen almost took from me my faculties.”
paras.uz: «Bilmayman. Umid qilamanki, qolgan. Lekin bunday paytda ehtiyotkor bo'lish juda qiyin. Onamda isteriya tutdi va men unga qo'limdan kelgan har qanday yordamni berishga urinsam ham, qo'rqamanki, qila oladiganimchalik ko'p narsa qilmadim! Lekin nima bo'lishi mumkinligi dahshati qobiliyatlarimni deyarli tortib oldi».

paras.en: “Your attendance upon her has been too much for you. You do not look well. Oh that I had been with you! you have had every care and anxiety upon yourself alone.”
paras.uz: «Unga qarash sen uchun haddan tashqari og'ir bo'ldi. Yaxshi ko'rinmayapsan. Oh, sen bilan bo'lganimda edi! Barcha tashvish va xavotirni yolg'iz o'zing ko'tarding».

paras.en: “Mary and Kitty have been very kind, and would have shared in every fatigue, I am sure; but I did not think it right for either of them. Kitty is slight and delicate; and Mary studies so much, that her hours of repose should not be broken in on. My aunt Phillips came to Longbourn on Tuesday, after my father went away; and was so good as to stay till Thursday with me. She was of great use and comfort to us all. And Lady Lucas has been very kind; she walked here on Wednesday morning to condole with us, and offered her services, or any of her daughters', if they should be of use to us.”
paras.uz: «Meri va Ketti juda mehribon bo'lishdi va ishonchim komilki, har qanday charchoqni baham ko'rgan bo'lardi; lekin men buni ularning hech biri uchun to'g'ri deb hisoblamadim. Ketti nozik va zaif; Meri esa shunchalik ko'p o'qiydiki, uning dam olish soatlarini buzmaslik kerak. Fillips xolam seshanba kuni, otam ketgandan keyin Longbornga keldi va payshanbagacha men bilan qolish yaxshiligini qildi. U hammamizga katta yordam va taskin bo'ldi. Ledi Lukas ham juda mehribon bo'ldi; u chorshanba kuni ertalab bizga hamdardlik bildirish uchun piyoda keldi va agar bizga foydali bo'lsa, o'z xizmatlarini yoki qizlaridan birortasining xizmatini taklif qildi».

paras.en: “She had better have stayed at home,” cried Elizabeth; “perhaps she meant well, but, under such a misfortune as this, one cannot see too little of one's neighbours. Assistance is impossible; condolence insufferable. Let them triumph over us at a distance, and be satisfied.”
paras.uz: «U uyda qolgani yaxshiroq bo'lardi, — xitob qildi Elizabet. — Ehtimol, u yaxshi niyatda bo'lgandir, lekin bunday baxtsizlikda qo'shnilarni iloji boricha kam ko'rgan ma'qul. Yordam berish imkonsiz; hamdardlik chidab bo'lmas. Ular bizdan uzoqda g'alaba qozonishsin va qanoatlanishsin».

paras.en: She then proceeded to inquire into the measures which her father had intended to pursue, while in town, for the recovery of his daughter.
paras.uz: Keyin u otasi Londonda qizini qaytarish uchun qanday choralar ko'rmoqchi bo'lganini so'rashga o'tdi.

paras.en: “He meant I believe,” replied Jane, “to go to Epsom, the place where they last changed horses, see the postilions and try if anything could be made out from them. His principal object must be to discover the number of the hackney coach which took them from Clapham. It had come with a fare from London; and as he thought that the circumstance of a gentleman and lady's removing from one carriage into another might be remarked he meant to make inquiries at Clapham. If he could anyhow discover at what house the coachman had before set down his fare, he determined to make inquiries there, and hoped it might not be impossible to find out the stand and number of the coach. I do not know of any other designs that he had formed; but he was in such a hurry to be gone, and his spirits so greatly discomposed, that I had difficulty in finding out even so much as this.”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, u, — javob berdi Jeyn, — ular oxirgi marta otlarni almashtirgan joy Epsomga borib, aravakashlarni ko'rmoqchi va ulardan biror narsa bilib olish mumkinmi, sinab ko'rmoqchi edi. Uning asosiy maqsadi ularni Klepemdan olib ketgan yollanma karetaning raqamini aniqlash bo'lishi kerak. U Londondan yo'lovchi bilan kelgan edi; va u bir janob va bir xonimning bir aravadan boshqasiga o'tishi holati e'tiborga tushgan bo'lishi mumkin deb o'ylagani uchun, Klepemda so'roq qilmoqchi edi. Agar u qandaydir yo'l bilan aravakash avvalgi yo'lovchisini qaysi uyga tushirganini aniqlay olsa, u yerda so'roq qilishga qaror qildi va karetaning to'xtash joyi va raqamini aniqlash imkonsiz bo'lmasligiga umid qildi. Uning boshqa rejalarini bilmayman; lekin u ketishga shunchalik shoshilardi va kayfiyati shunchalik buzilgan ediki, hatto shuncha narsani bilib olishda ham qiynaldim».

gloss.ex: My mother was in hysterics, and though I endeavoured to give her every assistance in my power, I am afraid I did not do so much as I might have…
thoughtless, thoughtless Lydia!”
As that was the case, neither Jane, to whom I related the whole, nor I, thought it necessary to make our knowledge public; for of what use could it apparently…
And there are other circumstances which I am not at liberty--which it is not worth while to relate; but his lies about the whole Pemberley family are endless.
From what he said of Miss Darcy I was thoroughly prepared to see a proud, reserved, disagreeable girl.
Had they no apprehension of anything before the elopement took place?
When they were all in the drawing-room, the questions which Elizabeth had already asked were of course repeated by the others, and they soon found that Jane had no intelligence…

quiz.q: What is revealed about Wickham in Meryton?
quiz.why_uz: Endi hamma uning haqiqiy qiyofasini ko'radi.

quiz.q: What is Lydia's attitude in her letter?
quiz.why_uz: U oilasiga qanday zarar yetkazganini tushunmaydi.

chapters.title: No News
chapters.recap_uz: Janob Bennet Londondan qaytadi — Lidiya topilmagan. Kollinz «tasalli» xati yuboradi: Lidiyaning o'lgani yaxshiroq bo'lardi, deydi. Janob Bennet o'z aybini tan oladi.

paras.en: The whole party were in hopes of a letter from Mr. Bennet the next morning, but the post came in without bringing a single line from him. His family knew him to be, on all common occasions, a most negligent and dilatory correspondent; but at such a time they had hoped for exertion. They were forced to conclude that he had no pleasing intelligence to send; but even of that they would have been glad to be certain. Mr. Gardiner had waited only for the letters before he set off.
paras.uz: Butun davra ertasi kuni ertalab janob Bennetdan xat kutgan edi, lekin pochta undan birorta satr ham keltirmadi. Oilasi uni barcha oddiy hollarda eng beparvo va sust xat yozuvchi deb bilardi; lekin bunday paytda ular undan harakat kutishgan edi. Ular uning yuboradigan yoqimli xabari yo'q, degan xulosaga kelishga majbur bo'lishdi; lekin hatto bunga ham amin bo'lishdan xursand bo'lardilar. Janob Gardiner yo'lga chiqishdan oldin faqat xatlarni kutgan edi.

paras.en: When he was gone, they were certain at least of receiving constant information of what was going on, and their uncle promised, at parting, to prevail on Mr. Bennet to return to Longbourn, as soon as he could, to the great consolation of his sister, who considered it as the only security for her husband's not being killed in a duel.
paras.uz: U ketgach, ular hech bo'lmaganda nima bo'layotgani haqida doimiy ma'lumot olishlariga amin edilar; tog'alari xayrlashayotganda janob Bennetni iloji boricha tezroq Longbornga qaytishga ko'ndirishga va'da berdi, bu esa buni erining duelda o'ldirilmasligining yagona kafolati deb hisoblagan opasiga katta taskin bo'ldi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner and the children were to remain in Hertfordshire a few days longer, as the former thought her presence might be serviceable to her nieces. She shared in their attendance on Mrs. Bennet, and was a great comfort to them in their hours of freedom. Their other aunt also visited them frequently, and always, as she said, with the design of cheering and heartening them up--though, as she never came without reporting some fresh instance of Wickham's extravagance or irregularity, she seldom went away without leaving them more dispirited than she found them.
paras.uz: Missis Gardiner va bolalar Xertfordshirda yana bir necha kun qolishlari kerak edi, chunki u o'zining bo'lishi jiyanlariga foydali bo'lishi mumkin deb o'yladi. U ular bilan birga missis Bennetga qarardi va bo'sh soatlarida ularga katta taskin edi. Ularning boshqa xolasi ham ularnikiga tez-tez kelib turardi va, o'zining aytishicha, doim ularni quvontirish va ruhlantirish niyatida — garchi u Uikhemning isrofgarchiligi yoki tartibsizligi haqida biror yangi misol keltirmasdan hech qachon kelmagani uchun, ularni topganidan ko'ra ruhiyatini tushirmasdan kamdan-kam ketardi.

paras.en: All Meryton seemed striving to blacken the man who, but three months before, had been almost an angel of light. He was declared to be in debt to every tradesman in the place, and his intrigues, all honoured with the title of seduction, had been extended into every tradesman's family. Everybody declared that he was the wickedest young man in the world; and everybody began to find out that they had always distrusted the appearance of his goodness. Elizabeth, though she did not credit above half of what was said, believed enough to make her former assurance of her sister's ruin more certain; and even Jane, who believed still less of it, became almost hopeless, more especially as the time was now come when, if they had gone to Scotland, which she had never before entirely despaired of, they must in all probability have gained some news of them.
paras.uz: Butun Meriton atigi uch oy oldin deyarli nur farishtasi bo'lgan odamni qoralashga intilayotganga o'xshardi. U shahardagi har bir savdogarga qarzdor deb e'lon qilindi va uning hammasi yo'ldan urish nomi bilan sharaflangan ishqiy sarguzashtlari har bir savdogarning oilasiga yoyilgan edi. Hamma uni dunyodagi eng yovuz yosh yigit deb e'lon qildi; va hamma uning yaxshilik ko'rinishiga doim ishonmaganini kashf qila boshladi. Elizabet aytilganlarning yarmidan ko'piga ishonmasa ham, opasining halokati haqidagi avvalgi ishonchini yanada aniqroq qiladigan darajada ishondi; hatto bundan ham kamroq ishongan Jeyn ham deyarli umidini uzdi, ayniqsa endi, agar ular Shotlandiyaga ketgan bo'lsa — u bundan avval hech qachon butunlay umidini uzmagan edi — ehtimol, ular haqida biror xabar olishlari kerak bo'lgan vaqt kelgan edi.

paras.en: Mr. Gardiner left Longbourn on Sunday; on Tuesday his wife received a letter from him; it told them that, on his arrival, he had immediately found out his brother, and persuaded him to come to Gracechurch Street; that Mr. Bennet had been to Epsom and Clapham, before his arrival, but without gaining any satisfactory information; and that he was now determined to inquire at all the principal hotels in town, as Mr. Bennet thought it possible they might have gone to one of them, on their first coming to London, before they procured lodgings. Mr. Gardiner himself did not expect any success from this measure, but as his brother was eager in it, he meant to assist him in pursuing it. He added that Mr. Bennet seemed wholly disinclined at present to leave London and promised to write again very soon. There was also a postscript to this effect:
paras.uz: Janob Gardiner yakshanba kuni Longbornni tark etdi; seshanba kuni xotini undan xat oldi; unda u yetib kelishi bilan darhol pochchasini topgani va uni Greyschurch ko'chasiga kelishga ko'ndirgani; janob Bennet u kelishidan oldin Epsom va Klepemga borgani, lekin qoniqarli ma'lumot olmagani; va endi u shahardagi barcha asosiy mehmonxonalarda so'roq qilishga qaror qilgani aytilgan edi, chunki janob Bennet ular Londonga birinchi kelganlarida, turar joy topishdan oldin ulardan biriga borgan bo'lishi mumkin deb o'yladi. Janob Gardinerning o'zi bu choradan hech qanday muvaffaqiyat kutmasdi, lekin pochchasi bunga intilgani uchun, unga yordam bermoqchi edi. U janob Bennet hozircha Londonni tark etishni umuman istamayotganga o'xshashini qo'shib qo'ydi va tez orada yana yozishga va'da berdi. Shuningdek, quyidagi mazmundagi qo'shimcha ham bor edi:

paras.en: “I have written to Colonel Forster to desire him to find out, if possible, from some of the young man's intimates in the regiment, whether Wickham has any relations or connections who would be likely to know in what part of town he has now concealed himself. If there were anyone that one could apply to with a probability of gaining such a clue as that, it might be of essential consequence. At present we have nothing to guide us. Colonel Forster will, I dare say, do everything in his power to satisfy us on this head. But, on second thoughts, perhaps, Lizzy could tell us what relations he has now living, better than any other person.”
paras.uz: «Polkovnik Forsterga xat yozib, iloji bo'lsa, yosh yigitning polkdagi yaqin do'stlaridan ba'zilaridan Uikhemning u hozir shaharning qaysi qismida yashiringanini bilishi mumkin bo'lgan biror qarindoshi yoki tanishi bormi, aniqlashni so'radim. Agar bunday iz topish ehtimoli bilan murojaat qilish mumkin bo'lgan biror kishi bo'lsa, bu juda muhim bo'lishi mumkin. Hozircha bizni yo'naltiradigan hech narsa yo'q. Ishonamanki, polkovnik Forster bu borada bizni qoniqtirish uchun qo'lidan kelgan hamma narsani qiladi. Lekin qayta o'ylab ko'rsam, ehtimol, uning hozir qanday tirik qarindoshlari borligini Lizzi boshqa har kimdan yaxshiroq aytib bera olar».

paras.en: Elizabeth was at no loss to understand from whence this deference to her authority proceeded; but it was not in her power to give any information of so satisfactory a nature as the compliment deserved. She had never heard of his having had any relations, except a father and mother, both of whom had been dead many years. It was possible, however, that some of his companions in the ----shire might be able to give more information; and though she was not very sanguine in expecting it, the application was a something to look forward to.
paras.uz: Elizabet uning fikriga bo'lgan bu hurmat qayerdan kelib chiqqanini tushunishda qiynalmadi; lekin iltifotga loyiq qoniqarli ma'lumot berish uning qo'lidan kelmasdi. U uning ota-onasidan boshqa qarindoshlari bo'lgani haqida hech qachon eshitmagan edi, ikkalasi ham ko'p yillar oldin vafot etgan edi. Biroq ----shir polkidagi ba'zi hamrohlari ko'proq ma'lumot berishi mumkin edi; garchi u buni unchalik umid bilan kutmasa ham, murojaat kutish uchun biror narsa edi.

paras.en: Every day at Longbourn was now a day of anxiety; but the most anxious part of each was when the post was expected. The arrival of letters was the grand object of every morning's impatience. Through letters, whatever of good or bad was to be told would be communicated, and every succeeding day was expected to bring some news of importance.
paras.uz: Longborndagi har kun endi tashvish kuni edi; lekin har birining eng tashvishli qismi pochta kutilgan payt edi. Xatlarning kelishi har ertalabgi sabrsizlikning asosiy obyekti edi. Xatlar orqali aytilishi kerak bo'lgan yaxshi yoki yomon har qanday narsa yetkazilardi va har bir keyingi kun qandaydir muhim yangilik olib kelishi kutilardi.

paras.en: But before they heard again from Mr. Gardiner, a letter arrived for their father, from a different quarter, from Mr. Collins; which, as Jane had received directions to open all that came for him in his absence, she accordingly read; and Elizabeth, who knew what curiosities his letters always were, looked over her, and read it likewise. It was as follows:
paras.uz: Lekin ular janob Gardinerdan yana xabar olishlaridan oldin, otalariga boshqa tomondan, janob Kollinzdan xat keldi; Jeyn uning yo'qligida unga kelgan hamma narsani ochishga ko'rsatma olgani uchun, uni o'qidi; uning xatlari doim qanday g'aroyib bo'lishini bilgan Elizabet uning yelkasi osha qarab, uni ham o'qidi. U shunday edi:

paras.en: “MY DEAR SIR,
paras.uz: «AZIZ SER,

paras.en: “I feel myself called upon, by our relationship, and my situation in life, to condole with you on the grievous affliction you are now suffering under, of which we were yesterday informed by a letter from Hertfordshire. Be assured, my dear sir, that Mrs. Collins and myself sincerely sympathise with you and all your respectable family, in your present distress, which must be of the bitterest kind, because proceeding from a cause which no time can remove. No arguments shall be wanting on my part that can alleviate so severe a misfortune--or that may comfort you, under a circumstance that must be of all others the most afflicting to a parent's mind. The death of your daughter would have been a blessing in comparison of this.
paras.uz: Qarindoshligimiz va hayotdagi mavqeim tufayli hozir boshingizga tushgan og'ir musibat munosabati bilan sizga hamdardlik bildirishga o'zimni majbur his qilaman, bu haqda kecha Xertfordshirdan kelgan xat orqali xabar topdik. Ishoning, aziz ser, missis Kollinz va men sizning va butun hurmatli oilangizning hozirgi iztirobiga chin dildan hamdardmiz, u eng achchiq turdagi bo'lishi kerak, chunki uni hech qanday vaqt yo'qota olmaydigan sababdan kelib chiqadi. Men tomonimdan bunchalik og'ir baxtsizlikni yengillashtira oladigan yoki ota-ona qalbi uchun boshqa hamma narsadan ko'ra eng azobli bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan vaziyatda sizni yupata oladigan dalillar yetishmaydi. Qizingizning o'limi bunga nisbatan ne'mat bo'lardi.

paras.en: And it is the more to be lamented, because there is reason to suppose as my dear Charlotte informs me, that this licentiousness of behaviour in your daughter has proceeded from a faulty degree of indulgence; though, at the same time, for the consolation of yourself and Mrs. Bennet, I am inclined to think that her own disposition must be naturally bad, or she could not be guilty of such an enormity, at so early an age. Howsoever that may be, you are grievously to be pitied; in which opinion I am not only joined by Mrs. Collins, but likewise by Lady Catherine and her daughter, to whom I have related the affair.
paras.uz: Bu yanada achinarli, chunki aziz Sharlottam menga aytganidek, qizingizning xatti-harakatidagi bu buzuqlik haddan tashqari erkalatishdan kelib chiqqan deb taxmin qilish uchun asos bor; garchi shu bilan birga, sizning va missis Bennetning taskini uchun men uning o'z fe'li tabiatan yomon bo'lishi kerak, aks holda u bunchalik erta yoshda bunday dahshatli ishda aybdor bo'la olmasdi, deb o'ylashga moyilman. Qanday bo'lmasin, siz achinarli darajada ayanchli holdasiz; bu fikrda menga nafaqat missis Kollinz, balki men ishni aytib bergan ledi Ketrin va uning qizi ham qo'shiladi.

paras.en: They agree with me in apprehending that this false step in one daughter will be injurious to the fortunes of all the others; for who, as Lady Catherine herself condescendingly says, will connect themselves with such a family? And this consideration leads me moreover to reflect, with augmented satisfaction, on a certain event of last November; for had it been otherwise, I must have been involved in all your sorrow and disgrace. Let me then advise you, dear sir, to console yourself as much as possible, to throw off your unworthy child from your affection for ever, and leave her to reap the fruits of her own heinous offense.
paras.uz: Ular men bilan bir qizdagi bu noto'g'ri qadam qolganlarining hammasining taqdiriga zarar yetkazishidan qo'rqishda hamfikr; chunki ledi Ketrinning o'zi iltifot bilan aytganidek, kim bunday oila bilan qarindosh bo'ladi? Bu mulohaza meni bundan tashqari o'tgan noyabrdagi ma'lum bir voqea haqida ortib borayotgan mamnuniyat bilan o'ylashga undaydi; chunki agar boshqacha bo'lganida, men ham butun qayg'u va sharmandaligingizga aralashib qolgan bo'lardim. Shunday ekan, aziz ser, sizga iloji boricha o'zingizni yupatishni, noloyiq farzandingizni mehringizdan abadiy uloqtirib tashlashni va uni o'zining jirkanch gunohining mevalarini terishga qoldirishni maslahat beraman.

paras.en: “I am, dear sir, etc., etc.”
paras.uz: Men, aziz ser, va hokazo, va hokazo».

paras.en: Mr. Gardiner did not write again till he had received an answer from Colonel Forster; and then he had nothing of a pleasant nature to send. It was not known that Wickham had a single relationship with whom he kept up any connection, and it was certain that he had no near one living. His former acquaintances had been numerous; but since he had been in the militia, it did not appear that he was on terms of particular friendship with any of them. There was no one, therefore, who could be pointed out as likely to give any news of him. And in the wretched state of his own finances, there was a very powerful motive for secrecy, in addition to his fear of discovery by Lydia's relations, for it had just transpired that he had left gaming debts behind him to a very considerable amount.
paras.uz: Janob Gardiner polkovnik Forsterdan javob olmaguncha yana yozmadi; shunda ham yuboradigan yoqimli narsasi yo'q edi. Uikhemning aloqa saqlaydigan birorta ham qarindoshi borligi ma'lum emasdi va uning yaqin tirik qarindoshi yo'qligi aniq edi. Uning avvalgi tanishlari ko'p bo'lgan; lekin militsiyaga kirganidan beri ulardan birortasi bilan alohida do'stona munosabatda bo'lmaganga o'xshardi. Shuning uchun u haqida biror xabar berishi mumkin deb ko'rsatiladigan hech kim yo'q edi. O'z moliyaviy ahvolining ayanchli holatida esa Lidiyaning qarindoshlari tomonidan fosh bo'lish qo'rquvidan tashqari sir saqlash uchun juda kuchli sabab bor edi, chunki u ortida juda katta miqdorda qimor qarzlari qoldirgani hozirgina ma'lum bo'lgan edi.

paras.en: Colonel Forster believed that more than a thousand pounds would be necessary to clear his expenses at Brighton. He owed a good deal in town, but his debts of honour were still more formidable. Mr. Gardiner did not attempt to conceal these particulars from the Longbourn family. Jane heard them with horror. “A gamester!” she cried. “This is wholly unexpected. I had not an idea of it.”
paras.uz: Polkovnik Forsterning fikricha, uning Braytondagi xarajatlarini qoplash uchun ming funtdan ortiq kerak bo'lardi. U Londonda ancha qarzdor edi, lekin uning sharaf qarzlari bundan ham dahshatliroq edi. Janob Gardiner bu tafsilotlarni Longborn oilasidan yashirishga urinmadi. Jeyn ularni dahshat bilan eshitdi. «Qimorboz! — xitob qildi u. — Bu butunlay kutilmagan. Bu haqda hech qanday tasavvurim yo'q edi».

paras.en: Mr. Gardiner added in his letter, that they might expect to see their father at home on the following day, which was Saturday. Rendered spiritless by the ill-success of all their endeavours, he had yielded to his brother-in-law's entreaty that he would return to his family, and leave it to him to do whatever occasion might suggest to be advisable for continuing their pursuit. When Mrs. Bennet was told of this, she did not express so much satisfaction as her children expected, considering what her anxiety for his life had been before.
paras.uz: Janob Gardiner xatida ular otalarini ertasi kuni, ya'ni shanba kuni uyda kutishlari mumkinligini qo'shib qo'ydi. Barcha sa'y-harakatlarining muvaffaqiyatsizligidan ruhi tushgan holda, u qaynag'asining oilasiga qaytish va qidiruvni davom ettirish uchun vaziyat maqsadga muvofiq deb ko'rsatadigan har qanday narsani qilishni unga qoldirish haqidagi iltimosiga ko'ngan edi. Missis Bennetga bu aytilganda, u avval uning hayoti uchun qanchalik tashvishlanganini hisobga olsak, farzandlari kutgancha mamnuniyat bildirmadi.

paras.en: “What, is he coming home, and without poor Lydia?” she cried. “Sure he will not leave London before he has found them. Who is to fight Wickham, and make him marry her, if he comes away?”
paras.uz: «Nima, u uyga kelyaptimi, bechora Lidiyasizmi? — xitob qildi u. — Albatta, u ularni topmaguncha Londonni tark etmaydi. Agar u ketib qolsa, Uikhem bilan kim duelga chiqib, uni unga uylanishga majbur qiladi?»

paras.en: As Mrs. Gardiner began to wish to be at home, it was settled that she and the children should go to London, at the same time that Mr. Bennet came from it. The coach, therefore, took them the first stage of their journey, and brought its master back to Longbourn.
paras.uz: Missis Gardiner uyda bo'lishni xohlay boshlagani uchun, u va bolalar janob Bennet Londondan kelgan vaqtda Londonga borishlari kelishildi. Shunday qilib, arava ularni safarlarining birinchi bosqichiga olib borib, o'z egasini Longbornga qaytarib olib keldi.

paras.en: Mrs. Gardiner went away in all the perplexity about Elizabeth and her Derbyshire friend that had attended her from that part of the world. His name had never been voluntarily mentioned before them by her niece; and the kind of half-expectation which Mrs. Gardiner had formed, of their being followed by a letter from him, had ended in nothing. Elizabeth had received none since her return that could come from Pemberley.
paras.uz: Missis Gardiner dunyoning o'sha qismidan beri unga hamroh bo'lgan Elizabet va uning Derbishirdagi do'sti haqidagi butun hayronlik bilan ketdi. Jiyani ularning oldida uning nomini hech qachon o'z ixtiyori bilan tilga olmagan edi; va missis Gardiner ularning ortidan undan xat keladi degan yarim kutishi hech narsa bilan tugamadi. Elizabet qaytganidan beri Pemberlidan kelishi mumkin bo'lgan hech qanday xat olmagan edi.

paras.en: The present unhappy state of the family rendered any other excuse for the lowness of her spirits unnecessary; nothing, therefore, could be fairly conjectured from that, though Elizabeth, who was by this time tolerably well acquainted with her own feelings, was perfectly aware that, had she known nothing of Darcy, she could have borne the dread of Lydia's infamy somewhat better. It would have spared her, she thought, one sleepless night out of two.
paras.uz: Oilaning hozirgi baxtsiz ahvoli uning ruhiy tushkunligi uchun boshqa har qanday bahonani keraksiz qilardi; shuning uchun bundan hech narsani adolatli taxmin qilib bo'lmasdi, garchi bu vaqtga kelib o'z tuyg'ulari bilan ancha yaxshi tanish bo'lgan Elizabet agar Darsi haqida hech narsa bilmaganida, Lidiyaning sharmandaligidan qo'rquvga biroz yaxshiroq chidagan bo'lishini mutlaqo yaxshi bilardi. Bu, uning o'ylashicha, uni ikki tundan bir uyqusiz tundan qutqargan bo'lardi.

paras.en: When Mr. Bennet arrived, he had all the appearance of his usual philosophic composure. He said as little as he had ever been in the habit of saying; made no mention of the business that had taken him away, and it was some time before his daughters had courage to speak of it.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet kelganda, unda odatdagi falsafiy xotirjamligining butun ko'rinishi bor edi. U har doimgidek kam gapirdi; uni olib ketgan ish haqida hech narsa demadi va qizlari bu haqda gapirishga jur'at topishlari uchun ancha vaqt o'tdi.

paras.en: It was not till the afternoon, when he had joined them at tea, that Elizabeth ventured to introduce the subject; and then, on her briefly expressing her sorrow for what he must have endured, he replied, “Say nothing of that. Who should suffer but myself? It has been my own doing, and I ought to feel it.”
paras.uz: Faqat tushdan keyin, u ularga choyda qo'shilganda, Elizabet mavzuni boshlashga jur'at etdi; va u qisqacha u chekkan azoblar uchun qayg'usini bildirganda, u javob berdi: «Bu haqda hech narsa dema. Mendan boshqa kim azob chekishi kerak? Bu mening o'z ishim va men buni his qilishim kerak».

paras.en: “You must not be too severe upon yourself,” replied Elizabeth.
paras.uz: «O'zingizga haddan tashqari qattiqqo'l bo'lmasligingiz kerak», — javob berdi Elizabet.

paras.en: “You may well warn me against such an evil. Human nature is so prone to fall into it! No, Lizzy, let me once in my life feel how much I have been to blame. I am not afraid of being overpowered by the impression. It will pass away soon enough.”
paras.uz: «Meni bunday yomonlikdan ogohlantirishing o'rinli. Inson tabiati bunga tushishga juda moyil! Yo'q, Lizzi, umrimda bir marta qanchalik aybdor ekanimni his qilishimga ruxsat ber. Taassurot meni ezib qo'yishidan qo'rqmayman. U yetarlicha tez o'tib ketadi».

paras.en: “Do you suppose them to be in London?”
paras.uz: «Ularni Londonda deb o'ylaysizmi?»

paras.en: “Yes; where else can they be so well concealed?”
paras.uz: «Ha; ular yana qayerda bunchalik yaxshi yashirina oladi?»

paras.en: “And Lydia used to want to go to London,” added Kitty.
paras.uz: «Lidiya esa Londonga borishni juda xohlardi», — qo'shib qo'ydi Ketti.

paras.en: “She is happy then,” said her father drily; “and her residence there will probably be of some duration.”
paras.uz: «Demak, u baxtli, — dedi otasi quruq ohangda, — va uning u yerda yashashi, ehtimol, ancha davom etadi».

paras.en: Then after a short silence he continued:
paras.uz: Keyin qisqa sukutdan so'ng davom etdi:

paras.en: “Lizzy, I bear you no ill-will for being justified in your advice to me last May, which, considering the event, shows some greatness of mind.”
paras.uz: «Lizzi, o'tgan may oyida menga bergan maslahatingda haq chiqqaning uchun senga hech qanday g'araz saqlamayman, bu voqeani hisobga olsak, qandaydir qalb kengligini ko'rsatadi».

paras.en: They were interrupted by Miss Bennet, who came to fetch her mother's tea.
paras.uz: Ularning gapini onasining choyini olib ketish uchun kelgan miss Bennet bo'ldi.

paras.en: “This is a parade,” he cried, “which does one good; it gives such an elegance to misfortune! Another day I will do the same; I will sit in my library, in my nightcap and powdering gown, and give as much trouble as I can; or, perhaps, I may defer it till Kitty runs away.”
paras.uz: «Bu shunday namoyishki, — xitob qildi u, — odamga yaxshilik qiladi; baxtsizlikka shunday nafislik beradi! Boshqa kun men ham shunday qilaman; kutubxonamda tungi qalpoq va xalatda o'tirib, iloji boricha ko'proq tashvish beraman; yoki, ehtimol, Ketti qochib ketguncha buni keyinga qoldiraman».

paras.en: “I am not going to run away, papa,” said Kitty fretfully. “If I should ever go to Brighton, I would behave better than Lydia.”
paras.uz: «Men qochib ketmayman, dada, — dedi Ketti jizzakilik bilan. — Agar qachondir Braytonga borsam, Lidiyadan yaxshiroq o'zimni tutardim».

paras.en: “You go to Brighton. I would not trust you so near it as Eastbourne for fifty pounds! No, Kitty, I have at last learnt to be cautious, and you will feel the effects of it. No officer is ever to enter into my house again, nor even to pass through the village. Balls will be absolutely prohibited, unless you stand up with one of your sisters. And you are never to stir out of doors till you can prove that you have spent ten minutes of every day in a rational manner.”
paras.uz: «Sen Braytonga borasanmi! Seni ellik funtga ham Istbornchalik yaqin joyga ishonmayman! Yo'q, Ketti, men nihoyat ehtiyotkor bo'lishni o'rgandim va buning ta'sirini his qilasan. Hech bir ofitser endi uyimga kirmaydi, hatto qishloq orqali ham o'tmaydi. Agar opa-singillaringdan biri bilan raqsga tushmasang, ballar mutlaqo taqiqlanadi. Va har kuni o'n daqiqani oqilona tarzda o'tkazganingni isbotlay olmaguncha uydan bir qadam ham chiqmaysan».

paras.en: Kitty, who took all these threats in a serious light, began to cry.
paras.uz: Bu tahdidlarning hammasini jiddiy qabul qilgan Ketti yig'lay boshladi.

paras.en: “Well, well,” said he, “do not make yourself unhappy. If you are a good girl for the next ten years, I will take you to a review at the end of them.”
paras.uz: «Mayli, mayli, — dedi u, — o'zingni baxtsiz qilma. Agar keyingi o'n yil davomida yaxshi qiz bo'lsang, ularning oxirida seni harbiy ko'rikka olib boraman».
