chapters.title: Lydia Will Be Married
chapters.recap_uz: Janob Gardinerdan xat keladi: Lidiya va Uikhem topilgan va nikohlanishadi, Uikhemning qarzlari to'lanadi. Hamma buni janob Gardiner qilgan deb o'ylaydi. Missis Bennet quvonchdan o'zini yo'qotadi.

paras.en: Two days after Mr. Bennet's return, as Jane and Elizabeth were walking together in the shrubbery behind the house, they saw the housekeeper coming towards them, and, concluding that she came to call them to their mother, went forward to meet her; but, instead of the expected summons, when they approached her, she said to Miss Bennet, “I beg your pardon, madam, for interrupting you, but I was in hopes you might have got some good news from town, so I took the liberty of coming to ask.”
paras.uz: Janob Bennet qaytganidan ikki kun keyin, Jeyn va Elizabet uyning orqasidagi butazorda birga sayr qilishayotganda, ular uy bekasi o'zlari tomon kelayotganini ko'rishdi va u ularni onalari huzuriga chaqirgani kelyapti deb xulosa qilib, uni kutib olish uchun oldinga yurishdi; lekin kutilgan chaqiriq o'rniga, ular yaqinlashganda, u miss Bennetga dedi: «Gapingizni bo'lganim uchun kechirasiz, xonim, lekin siz Londondan biror yaxshi xabar olgandirsiz deb umid qildim, shuning uchun so'rash uchun kelishga jur'at qildim».

paras.en: “What do you mean, Hill? We have heard nothing from town.”
paras.uz: «Nima demoqchisiz, Hill? Biz Londondan hech narsa eshitmadik».

paras.en: “Dear madam,” cried Mrs. Hill, in great astonishment, “don't you know there is an express come for master from Mr. Gardiner? He has been here this half-hour, and master has had a letter.”
paras.uz: «Aziz xonim, — xitob qildi missis Hill katta hayrat bilan, — xo'jayinga janob Gardinerdan shoshilinch xabarchi kelganini bilmaysizmi? U yarim soatdan beri shu yerda, xo'jayin esa xat oldi».

paras.en: Away ran the girls, too eager to get in to have time for speech. They ran through the vestibule into the breakfast-room; from thence to the library; their father was in neither; and they were on the point of seeking him up stairs with their mother, when they were met by the butler, who said:
paras.uz: Qizlar yugurib ketishdi, ichkariga kirishga shunchalik intilardilarki, gapirishga vaqt yo'q edi. Ular dahliz orqali nonushta xonasiga, u yerdan kutubxonaga yugurishdi; otalari ularning hech birida yo'q edi; ular uni yuqorida onalari bilan izlamoqchi bo'lib turganlarida, ularni sarkor kutib oldi va dedi:

paras.en: “If you are looking for my master, ma'am, he is walking towards the little copse.”
paras.uz: «Agar xo'jayinimni izlayotgan bo'lsangiz, xonim, u kichik daraxtzor tomon sayr qilib ketyapti».

paras.en: Upon this information, they instantly passed through the hall once more, and ran across the lawn after their father, who was deliberately pursuing his way towards a small wood on one side of the paddock.
paras.uz: Bu xabarni olib, ular darhol yana zal orqali o'tishdi va hovlining bir tomonidagi kichik o'rmon tomon shoshilmay yo'l olgan otalari ortidan maysazor bo'ylab yugurishdi.

paras.en: Jane, who was not so light nor so much in the habit of running as Elizabeth, soon lagged behind, while her sister, panting for breath, came up with him, and eagerly cried out:
paras.uz: Elizabet kabi yengil bo'lmagan va yugurishga unchalik odatlanmagan Jeyn tez orada ortda qoldi, singlisi esa nafasi tiqilib unga yetib oldi va ishtiyoq bilan qichqirdi:

paras.en: “Oh, papa, what news--what news? Have you heard from my uncle?”
paras.uz: «Oh, dada, qanday xabar — qanday xabar? Tog'amdan xabar oldingizmi?»

paras.en: “Yes I have had a letter from him by express.”
paras.uz: «Ha, undan shoshilinch xabarchi orqali xat oldim».

paras.en: “Well, and what news does it bring--good or bad?”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, u qanday xabar keltirdi — yaxshimi yoki yomonmi?»

paras.en: “What is there of good to be expected?” said he, taking the letter from his pocket. “But perhaps you would like to read it.”
paras.uz: «Qanday yaxshilik kutish mumkin? — dedi u, xatni cho'ntagidan olib. — Lekin, ehtimol, uni o'qishni istarsan».

paras.en: Elizabeth impatiently caught it from his hand. Jane now came up.
paras.uz: Elizabet sabrsizlik bilan uni uning qo'lidan oldi. Endi Jeyn ham yetib keldi.

paras.en: “Read it aloud,” said their father, “for I hardly know myself what it is about.”
paras.uz: «Ovoz chiqarib o'qi, — dedi otalari, — chunki o'zim ham u nima haqida ekanini zo'rg'a bilaman».

paras.en: “Gracechurch Street, Monday, August 2.
paras.uz: «Greyschurch ko'chasi, dushanba, 2-avgust.

paras.en: “MY DEAR BROTHER,
paras.uz: AZIZ POCHCHA,

paras.en: “At last I am able to send you some tidings of my niece, and such as, upon the whole, I hope it will give you satisfaction. Soon after you left me on Saturday, I was fortunate enough to find out in what part of London they were. The particulars I reserve till we meet; it is enough to know they are discovered. I have seen them both--”
paras.uz: Nihoyat sizga jiyanim haqida biror xabar yubora olaman, umuman olganda, umid qilamanki, u sizga qoniqish beradi. Siz shanba kuni meni tark etganingizdan ko'p o'tmay, ular Londonning qaysi qismida ekanini topish omadiga muyassar bo'ldim. Tafsilotlarni uchrashguncha saqlab qo'yaman; ular topilganini bilish yetarli. Men ikkalasini ham ko'rdim...»

paras.en: “Then it is as I always hoped,” cried Jane; “they are married!”
paras.uz: «Demak, men doim umid qilganimdek, — xitob qildi Jeyn, — ular turmush qurgan!»

paras.en: Elizabeth read on:
paras.uz: Elizabet o'qishda davom etdi:

paras.en: “I have seen them both. They are not married, nor can I find there was any intention of being so; but if you are willing to perform the engagements which I have ventured to make on your side, I hope it will not be long before they are. All that is required of you is, to assure to your daughter, by settlement, her equal share of the five thousand pounds secured among your children after the decease of yourself and my sister; and, moreover, to enter into an engagement of allowing her, during your life, one hundred pounds per annum. These are conditions which, considering everything, I had no hesitation in complying with, as far as I thought myself privileged, for you. I shall send this by express, that no time may be lost in bringing me your answer.
paras.uz: «Men ikkalasini ham ko'rdim. Ular turmush qurmagan va bunday niyat bo'lganini ham topa olmadim; lekin agar siz men sizning nomingizdan qilishga jur'at etgan majburiyatlarni bajarishga tayyor bo'lsangiz, umid qilamanki, ularning turmush qurishiga ko'p vaqt qolmaydi. Sizdan talab qilinadigan narsa — nikoh shartnomasi orqali qizingizga siz va opam vafot etgandan keyin farzandlaringiz o'rtasida taqsimlanadigan besh ming funtdan teng ulushini kafolatlash; va bundan tashqari, umringiz davomida unga yiliga yuz funt berish majburiyatini olish. Bular men hamma narsani hisobga olib, o'zimni haqli deb hisoblagan darajada siz uchun rozi bo'lishga ikkilanmagan shartlardir. Javobingizni olishda vaqt yo'qotilmasligi uchun buni shoshilinch xabarchi orqali yuboraman.

paras.en: You will easily comprehend, from these particulars, that Mr. Wickham's circumstances are not so hopeless as they are generally believed to be. The world has been deceived in that respect; and I am happy to say there will be some little money, even when all his debts are discharged, to settle on my niece, in addition to her own fortune. If, as I conclude will be the case, you send me full powers to act in your name throughout the whole of this business, I will immediately give directions to Haggerston for preparing a proper settlement. There will not be the smallest occasion for your coming to town again; therefore stay quiet at Longbourn, and depend on my diligence and care. Send back your answer as fast as you can, and be careful to write explicitly.
paras.uz: Bu tafsilotlardan siz janob Uikhemning ahvoli umuman ishonilganidek unchalik umidsiz emasligini osongina tushunasiz. Dunyo bu borada aldangan; va aytishdan xursandmanki, hatto uning barcha qarzlari to'langanda ham jiyanimga uning o'z boyligiga qo'shimcha ravishda biroz pul qoladi. Agar men xulosa qilganimdek, siz menga bu butun ishda sizning nomingizdan harakat qilish uchun to'liq vakolat yuborsangiz, Haggerstonga munosib nikoh shartnomasini tayyorlash uchun darhol ko'rsatma beraman. Sizning yana Londonga kelishingizga zarracha ham hojat bo'lmaydi; shuning uchun Longbornda tinchgina qoling va mening tirishqoqligim va g'amxo'rligimga tayaning. Javobingizni iloji boricha tez yuboring va aniq yozishga ehtiyot bo'ling.

paras.en: We have judged it best that my niece should be married from this house, of which I hope you will approve. She comes to us to-day. I shall write again as soon as anything more is determined on. Yours, etc.,
paras.uz: Jiyanim shu uydan turmushga chiqishini eng yaxshisi deb hisobladik, umid qilamanki, siz buni ma'qullaysiz. U bugun bizga keladi. Yana biror narsa hal bo'lishi bilanoq yana yozaman. Sizniki va hokazo,

paras.en: “EDW. GARDINER.”
paras.uz: EDV. GARDINER».

paras.en: “Is it possible?” cried Elizabeth, when she had finished. “Can it be possible that he will marry her?”
paras.uz: «Bu mumkinmi? — xitob qildi Elizabet, tugatgach. — U unga uylanishi mumkinmi?»

paras.en: “Wickham is not so undeserving, then, as we thought him,” said her sister. “My dear father, I congratulate you.”
paras.uz: «Demak, Uikhem biz o'ylaganimizdek noloyiq emas ekan, — dedi opasi. — Aziz otajon, sizni tabriklayman».

paras.en: “And have you answered the letter?” cried Elizabeth.
paras.uz: «Xatga javob berdingizmi?» — xitob qildi Elizabet.

paras.en: “No; but it must be done soon.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q; lekin buni tez orada qilish kerak».

paras.en: Most earnestly did she then entreat him to lose no more time before he wrote.
paras.uz: Shunda u eng jiddiy tarzda undan yozishdan oldin boshqa vaqt yo'qotmaslikni iltimos qildi.

paras.en: “Oh! my dear father,” she cried, “come back and write immediately. Consider how important every moment is in such a case.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Aziz otajon, — xitob qildi u, — qayting va darhol yozing. Bunday holatda har bir lahza qanchalik muhim ekanini o'ylang».

paras.en: “Let me write for you,” said Jane, “if you dislike the trouble yourself.”
paras.uz: «Agar o'zingiz bu zahmatni yoqtirmasangiz, men siz uchun yozay», — dedi Jeyn.

paras.en: “I dislike it very much,” he replied; “but it must be done.”
paras.uz: «Uni juda yoqtirmayman, — javob berdi u, — lekin buni qilish kerak».

paras.en: And so saying, he turned back with them, and walked towards the house.
paras.uz: Va shunday deb, u ular bilan ortga burildi va uy tomon yurdi.

paras.en: “And may I ask--” said Elizabeth; “but the terms, I suppose, must be complied with.”
paras.uz: «So'rasam bo'ladimi... — dedi Elizabet. — Lekin, menimcha, shartlarga rozi bo'lish kerak».

paras.en: “Complied with! I am only ashamed of his asking so little.”
paras.uz: «Rozi bo'lish! Men faqat uning bunchalik kam so'raganidan uyalaman».

paras.en: “And they must marry! Yet he is such a man!”
paras.uz: «Va ular turmush qurishi kerak! Shunga qaramay, u shunday odam!»

paras.en: “Yes, yes, they must marry. There is nothing else to be done. But there are two things that I want very much to know; one is, how much money your uncle has laid down to bring it about; and the other, how am I ever to pay him.”
paras.uz: «Ha, ha, ular turmush qurishi kerak. Boshqa qiladigan ish yo'q. Lekin men juda bilishni istagan ikki narsa bor; biri, tog'ang buni amalga oshirish uchun qancha pul sarflagani; ikkinchisi esa, men unga qachondir buni qanday to'lashim».

paras.en: “Money! My uncle!” cried Jane, “what do you mean, sir?”
paras.uz: «Pul! Tog'am! — xitob qildi Jeyn. — Nima demoqchisiz, ser?»

paras.en: “I mean, that no man in his senses would marry Lydia on so slight a temptation as one hundred a year during my life, and fifty after I am gone.”
paras.uz: «Demoqchimanki, hech bir aqli joyida odam mening umrim davomida yiliga yuz funt va men ketganimdan keyin ellik funt kabi arzimas vasvasa uchun Lidiyaga uylanmaydi».

paras.en: “That is very true,” said Elizabeth; “though it had not occurred to me before. His debts to be discharged, and something still to remain! Oh! it must be my uncle's doings! Generous, good man, I am afraid he has distressed himself. A small sum could not do all this.”
paras.uz: «Bu juda to'g'ri, — dedi Elizabet, — garchi bu avval xayolimga kelmagan bo'lsa ham. Uning qarzlari to'lanadi va yana biroz qoladi! Oh! Bu tog'amning ishi bo'lsa kerak! Saxiy, yaxshi odam, qo'rqamanki, u o'zini qiyin ahvolga solgan. Kichik summa bularning hammasini qila olmasdi».

paras.en: “No,” said her father; “Wickham's a fool if he takes her with a farthing less than ten thousand pounds. I should be sorry to think so ill of him, in the very beginning of our relationship.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, — dedi otasi, — agar Uikhem uni o'n ming funtdan bir chaqa kam bilan olsa, u ahmoq. Qarindoshligimizning aynan boshida u haqida bunchalik yomon o'ylashdan afsuslanardim».

paras.en: “Ten thousand pounds! Heaven forbid! How is half such a sum to be repaid?”
paras.uz: «O'n ming funt! Xudo saqlasin! Bunday summaning yarmini qanday qaytarish mumkin?»

paras.en: Mr. Bennet made no answer, and each of them, deep in thought, continued silent till they reached the house. Their father then went on to the library to write, and the girls walked into the breakfast-room.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet javob bermadi va ularning har biri chuqur o'yga botib, uyga yetib kelgunlaricha jim borishdi. Keyin otalari yozish uchun kutubxonaga ketdi, qizlar esa nonushta xonasiga kirishdi.

paras.en: “And they are really to be married!” cried Elizabeth, as soon as they were by themselves. “How strange this is! And for this we are to be thankful. That they should marry, small as is their chance of happiness, and wretched as is his character, we are forced to rejoice. Oh, Lydia!”
paras.uz: «Va ular haqiqatan ham turmush qurishadi! — xitob qildi Elizabet, ular yolg'iz qolishlari bilanoq. — Bu qanchalik g'alati! Va buning uchun minnatdor bo'lishimiz kerak. Ularning turmush qurishidan, baxt imkoniyati qanchalik kichik bo'lmasin va uning xarakteri qanchalik ayanchli bo'lmasin, xursand bo'lishga majburmiz. Oh, Lidiya!»

paras.en: “I comfort myself with thinking,” replied Jane, “that he certainly would not marry Lydia if he had not a real regard for her. Though our kind uncle has done something towards clearing him, I cannot believe that ten thousand pounds, or anything like it, has been advanced. He has children of his own, and may have more. How could he spare half ten thousand pounds?”
paras.uz: «Men o'zimni shunday o'y bilan yupataman, — javob berdi Jeyn, — agar u Lidiyaga chinakam mehr qo'ymaganida, albatta unga uylanmasdi. Mehribon tog'amiz uni qarzdan tozalash uchun biror narsa qilgan bo'lsa ham, o'n ming funt yoki shunga o'xshash biror summa berilganiga ishona olmayman. Uning o'z farzandlari bor va yana bo'lishi mumkin. U o'n ming funtning yarmini ham qanday ajrata olardi?»

paras.en: “If he were ever able to learn what Wickham's debts have been,” said Elizabeth, “and how much is settled on his side on our sister, we shall exactly know what Mr. Gardiner has done for them, because Wickham has not sixpence of his own. The kindness of my uncle and aunt can never be requited. Their taking her home, and affording her their personal protection and countenance, is such a sacrifice to her advantage as years of gratitude cannot enough acknowledge. By this time she is actually with them! If such goodness does not make her miserable now, she will never deserve to be happy! What a meeting for her, when she first sees my aunt!”
paras.uz: «Agar u qachondir Uikhemning qarzlari qancha bo'lganini va uning tomonidan singlimizga qancha ajratilganini bilib olsa, — dedi Elizabet, — janob Gardiner ular uchun aynan nima qilganini bilamiz, chunki Uikhemning o'zining olti pensi ham yo'q. Tog'am va xolamning mehribonligini hech qachon qaytarib bo'lmaydi. Ularning uni uylariga olishlari va unga shaxsiy himoya va qo'llab-quvvatlash berishlari uning foydasiga shunday qurbonlikki, uni yillar davomidagi minnatdorlik ham yetarlicha tan ola olmaydi. Hozirga kelib u haqiqatan ham ular bilan birga! Agar bunday yaxshilik uni hozir baxtsiz qilmasa, u hech qachon baxtli bo'lishga loyiq bo'lmaydi! Xolamni birinchi ko'rganida u uchun qanday uchrashuv!»

paras.en: “We must endeavour to forget all that has passed on either side,” said Jane: “I hope and trust they will yet be happy. His consenting to marry her is a proof, I will believe, that he is come to a right way of thinking. Their mutual affection will steady them; and I flatter myself they will settle so quietly, and live in so rational a manner, as may in time make their past imprudence forgotten.”
paras.uz: «Har ikki tomonda bo'lib o'tgan hamma narsani unutishga harakat qilishimiz kerak, — dedi Jeyn. — Umid qilaman va ishonamanki, ular hali baxtli bo'lishadi. Uning unga uylanishga rozi bo'lishi, ishonaman, u to'g'ri fikrlash yo'liga kelganining isboti. Ularning o'zaro mehri ularni barqaror qiladi; va o'zimni shunday umid bilan ovutamanki, ular shunchalik tinch joylashib, shunchalik oqilona yashashadiki, vaqt o'tib o'tmishdagi ehtiyotsizliklari unutiladi».

paras.en: “Their conduct has been such,” replied Elizabeth, “as neither you, nor I, nor anybody can ever forget. It is useless to talk of it.”
paras.uz: «Ularning xatti-harakati shunday bo'ldiki, — javob berdi Elizabet, — uni na sen, na men, na hech kim hech qachon unuta olmaydi. Bu haqda gapirish befoyda».

paras.en: It now occurred to the girls that their mother was in all likelihood perfectly ignorant of what had happened. They went to the library, therefore, and asked their father whether he would not wish them to make it known to her. He was writing and, without raising his head, coolly replied:
paras.uz: Endi qizlarning xayoliga onalari, ehtimol, bo'lib o'tgan voqeadan butunlay bexabar ekani keldi. Shuning uchun ular kutubxonaga borib, otalaridan unga xabar berishlarini istamaydimi, deb so'rashdi. U yozayotgan edi va boshini ko'tarmasdan sovuqqonlik bilan javob berdi:

paras.en: “Just as you please.”
paras.uz: «Xohlaganingizcha».

paras.en: “May we take my uncle's letter to read to her?”
paras.uz: «Tog'amning xatini unga o'qib berish uchun olsak bo'ladimi?»

paras.en: “Take whatever you like, and get away.”
paras.uz: «Xohlaganingizni olib, ketinglar».

paras.en: Elizabeth took the letter from his writing-table, and they went up stairs together. Mary and Kitty were both with Mrs. Bennet: one communication would, therefore, do for all. After a slight preparation for good news, the letter was read aloud. Mrs. Bennet could hardly contain herself. As soon as Jane had read Mr. Gardiner's hope of Lydia's being soon married, her joy burst forth, and every following sentence added to its exuberance. She was now in an irritation as violent from delight, as she had ever been fidgety from alarm and vexation. To know that her daughter would be married was enough. She was disturbed by no fear for her felicity, nor humbled by any remembrance of her misconduct.
paras.uz: Elizabet xatni uning yozuv stolidan oldi va ular birga yuqoriga chiqishdi. Meri va Ketti ikkalasi ham missis Bennet bilan edi: shuning uchun bitta xabar hammaga yetadi. Yaxshi xabarga biroz tayyorlagach, xat ovoz chiqarib o'qildi. Missis Bennet o'zini zo'rg'a tuta oldi. Jeyn janob Gardinerning Lidiya tez orada turmushga chiqishiga bo'lgan umidini o'qishi bilanoq, uning quvonchi otilib chiqdi va har bir keyingi jumla uning to'lib-toshishiga qo'shildi. U endi qachonlardir xavotir va g'ashlikdan qanchalik bezovta bo'lgan bo'lsa, zavqdan xuddi shunday shiddatli hayajonda edi. Qizining turmushga chiqishini bilish yetarli edi. Uni uning baxti uchun hech qanday qo'rquv bezovta qilmasdi, uning nojo'ya xatti-harakatining hech qanday xotirasi kamsitmasdi.

paras.en: “My dear, dear Lydia!” she cried. “This is delightful indeed! She will be married! I shall see her again! She will be married at sixteen! My good, kind brother! I knew how it would be. I knew he would manage everything! How I long to see her! and to see dear Wickham too! But the clothes, the wedding clothes! I will write to my sister Gardiner about them directly. Lizzy, my dear, run down to your father, and ask him how much he will give her. Stay, stay, I will go myself. Ring the bell, Kitty, for Hill. I will put on my things in a moment. My dear, dear Lydia! How merry we shall be together when we meet!”
paras.uz: «Aziz, aziz Lidiyam! — xitob qildi u. — Bu haqiqatan ham ajoyib! U turmushga chiqadi! Uni yana ko'raman! U o'n olti yoshida turmushga chiqadi! Yaxshi, mehribon ukam! Qanday bo'lishini bilgandim. Uning hamma narsani uddalashini bilgandim! Uni ko'rishni qanchalik orziqib kutyapman! Aziz Uikhemni ham ko'rishni! Lekin kiyimlar, to'y kiyimlari! Ular haqida darhol kelinim Gardinerga yozaman. Lizzi, azizim, otangning oldiga yugur va undan unga qancha berishini so'ra. To'xta, to'xta, o'zim boraman. Qo'ng'iroqni chal, Ketti, Hillni chaqir. Bir lahzada kiyinib olaman. Aziz, aziz Lidiyam! Uchrashganimizda birga qanchalik quvnoq bo'lamiz!»

paras.en: Her eldest daughter endeavoured to give some relief to the violence of these transports, by leading her thoughts to the obligations which Mr. Gardiner's behaviour laid them all under.
paras.uz: To'ng'ich qizi uning fikrlarini janob Gardinerning xatti-harakati hammalarini qanday majburiyatlar ostiga qo'yganiga yo'naltirib, bu hayajonlarning shiddatini biroz yumshatishga urindi.

paras.en: “For we must attribute this happy conclusion,” she added, “in a great measure to his kindness. We are persuaded that he has pledged himself to assist Mr. Wickham with money.”
paras.uz: «Chunki bu baxtli yakunni, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — katta darajada uning mehribonligiga bog'lashimiz kerak. Biz u janob Uikhemga pul bilan yordam berishni o'z zimmasiga olganiga ishonamiz».

paras.en: “Well,” cried her mother, “it is all very right; who should do it but her own uncle? If he had not had a family of his own, I and my children must have had all his money, you know; and it is the first time we have ever had anything from him, except a few presents. Well! I am so happy! In a short time I shall have a daughter married. Mrs. Wickham! How well it sounds! And she was only sixteen last June. My dear Jane, I am in such a flutter, that I am sure I can't write; so I will dictate, and you write for me. We will settle with your father about the money afterwards; but the things should be ordered immediately.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, — xitob qildi onasi, — bularning hammasi juda to'g'ri; uning o'z tog'asidan boshqa kim buni qilishi kerak? Agar uning o'z oilasi bo'lmaganida, bilasizlar, men va farzandlarim uning butun puliga ega bo'lishimiz kerak edi; bu esa bir nechta sovg'adan tashqari undan biror narsa olganimizning birinchi marta. Xo'sh! Men shunchalik baxtliman! Tez orada qizimni erga beraman. Missis Uikhem! Qanday yaxshi eshitiladi! U esa o'tgan iyunda endigina o'n oltiga to'lgan edi. Aziz Jeyn, shunchalik hayajondamanki, yoza olmasligimga aminman; shuning uchun men aytib turaman, sen esa men uchun yoz. Pul haqida keyinroq otang bilan hal qilamiz; lekin narsalarga darhol buyurtma berish kerak».

paras.en: She was then proceeding to all the particulars of calico, muslin, and cambric, and would shortly have dictated some very plentiful orders, had not Jane, though with some difficulty, persuaded her to wait till her father was at leisure to be consulted. One day's delay, she observed, would be of small importance; and her mother was too happy to be quite so obstinate as usual. Other schemes, too, came into her head.
paras.uz: Keyin u chit, muslin va batistning barcha tafsilotlariga o'tdi va tez orada juda mo'l buyurtmalarni aytib yozdirgan bo'lardi, agar Jeyn biroz qiyinchilik bilan bo'lsa ham, uni otasi bilan maslahatlashish uchun bo'sh bo'lgunicha kutishga ko'ndirmaganida. Bir kunlik kechikish, dedi u, unchalik ahamiyatga ega bo'lmaydi; onasi esa odatdagidek o'jar bo'lish uchun haddan tashqari baxtli edi. Uning boshiga boshqa rejalar ham keldi.

paras.en: “I will go to Meryton,” said she, “as soon as I am dressed, and tell the good, good news to my sister Philips. And as I come back, I can call on Lady Lucas and Mrs. Long. Kitty, run down and order the carriage. An airing would do me a great deal of good, I am sure. Girls, can I do anything for you in Meryton? Oh! Here comes Hill! My dear Hill, have you heard the good news? Miss Lydia is going to be married; and you shall all have a bowl of punch to make merry at her wedding.”
paras.uz: «Meritonga boraman, — dedi u, — kiyinishim bilanoq, va yaxshi, yaxshi xabarni opam Fillipsga aytaman. Qaytayotganimda esa ledi Lukas va missis Longnikiga kirishim mumkin. Ketti, pastga yugurib, arava buyur. Toza havo menga juda foydali bo'lishiga aminman. Qizlar, Meritonda sizlar uchun biror narsa qila olamanmi? Oh! Mana Hill keldi! Aziz Hill, yaxshi xabarni eshitdingizmi? Miss Lidiya turmushga chiqmoqchi; va uning to'yida quvnoq bo'lish uchun hammangizga bir kosa punsh beriladi».

paras.en: Mrs. Hill began instantly to express her joy. Elizabeth received her congratulations amongst the rest, and then, sick of this folly, took refuge in her own room, that she might think with freedom.
paras.uz: Missis Hill darhol quvonchini bildira boshladi. Elizabet boshqalar qatori uning tabriklarini qabul qildi va keyin bu ahmoqlikdan bezor bo'lib, erkin o'ylash uchun o'z xonasiga panoh izladi.

paras.en: Poor Lydia's situation must, at best, be bad enough; but that it was no worse, she had need to be thankful. She felt it so; and though, in looking forward, neither rational happiness nor worldly prosperity could be justly expected for her sister, in looking back to what they had feared, only two hours ago, she felt all the advantages of what they had gained.
paras.uz: Bechora Lidiyaning ahvoli eng yaxshi holatda ham yetarlicha yomon bo'lishi kerak edi; lekin undan yomonroq emasligi uchun shukr qilishi kerak edi. U buni shunday his qildi; garchi kelajakka qaraganda singlisi uchun na oqilona baxt, na dunyoviy farovonlikni adolatli kutib bo'lmasa ham, atigi ikki soat oldin nimadan qo'rqqanlariga ortga nazar tashlab, ular erishgan narsaning barcha afzalliklarini his qildi.

chapters.title: Regret
chapters.recap_uz: Janob Bennet pul yig'ib qo'ymaganiga afsuslanadi. Elizabet endi Darsi bilan baxtli bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan nikohni yo'qotdim deb o'ylaydi va u ular uchun eng mos er bo'lardi, deb tushunadi.

paras.en: Mr. Bennet had very often wished before this period of his life that, instead of spending his whole income, he had laid by an annual sum for the better provision of his children, and of his wife, if she survived him. He now wished it more than ever. Had he done his duty in that respect, Lydia need not have been indebted to her uncle for whatever of honour or credit could now be purchased for her. The satisfaction of prevailing on one of the most worthless young men in Great Britain to be her husband might then have rested in its proper place.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet hayotining bu davridan oldin ham juda tez-tez butun daromadini sarflash o'rniga farzandlarini va, agar undan keyin tirik qolsa, xotinini yaxshiroq ta'minlash uchun har yili ma'lum summani chetga qo'yganida edi, deb orzu qilgan edi. Endi u buni har qachongidan ham ko'proq istadi. Agar u bu borada o'z burchini bajarganida, Lidiya endi uning uchun sotib olinishi mumkin bo'lgan har qanday sharaf yoki obro' uchun tog'asiga qarzdor bo'lishi shart bo'lmasdi. Buyuk Britaniyadagi eng arzimas yosh yigitlardan birini uning eri bo'lishga ko'ndirish mamnuniyati shunda o'z munosib joyida bo'lishi mumkin edi.

paras.en: He was seriously concerned that a cause of so little advantage to anyone should be forwarded at the sole expense of his brother-in-law, and he was determined, if possible, to find out the extent of his assistance, and to discharge the obligation as soon as he could.
paras.uz: U hech kimga bunchalik kam foyda keltiradigan ishning faqat qaynag'asining hisobidan amalga oshirilishidan jiddiy tashvishlanardi va iloji bo'lsa, uning yordami ko'lamini aniqlashga va majburiyatni iloji boricha tezroq to'lashga qaror qildi.

paras.en: When first Mr. Bennet had married, economy was held to be perfectly useless, for, of course, they were to have a son. The son was to join in cutting off the entail, as soon as he should be of age, and the widow and younger children would by that means be provided for. Five daughters successively entered the world, but yet the son was to come; and Mrs. Bennet, for many years after Lydia's birth, had been certain that he would. This event had at last been despaired of, but it was then too late to be saving. Mrs. Bennet had no turn for economy, and her husband's love of independence had alone prevented their exceeding their income.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet birinchi uylanganda tejamkorlik mutlaqo befoyda hisoblanardi, chunki, albatta, ularning o'g'li bo'lishi kerak edi. O'g'il voyaga yetishi bilanoq meros chekloviini bekor qilishga qo'shilishi kerak edi, shu yo'l bilan beva va kichik farzandlar ta'minlanardi. Besh qiz ketma-ket dunyoga keldi, lekin o'g'il hali kelishi kerak edi; missis Bennet Lidiya tug'ilgandan keyin ko'p yillar davomida u albatta tug'ilishiga amin edi. Bu voqeadan nihoyat umid uzildi, lekin o'shanda tejash uchun juda kech edi. Missis Bennetda tejamkorlikka moyillik yo'q edi, faqat erining mustaqillikni yaxshi ko'rishi ularni daromadlaridan oshib ketishdan saqlab qolgan edi.

paras.en: Five thousand pounds was settled by marriage articles on Mrs. Bennet and the children. But in what proportions it should be divided amongst the latter depended on the will of the parents. This was one point, with regard to Lydia, at least, which was now to be settled, and Mr. Bennet could have no hesitation in acceding to the proposal before him. In terms of grateful acknowledgment for the kindness of his brother, though expressed most concisely, he then delivered on paper his perfect approbation of all that was done, and his willingness to fulfil the engagements that had been made for him. He had never before supposed that, could Wickham be prevailed on to marry his daughter, it would be done with so little inconvenience to himself as by the present arrangement. He would scarcely be ten pounds a year the loser by the hundred that was to be paid them; for, what with her board and pocket allowance, and the continual presents in money which passed to her through her mother's hands, Lydia's expenses had been very little within that sum.
paras.uz: Nikoh shartnomasi bo'yicha missis Bennet va farzandlarga besh ming funt ajratilgan edi. Lekin uning farzandlar o'rtasida qanday nisbatda taqsimlanishi ota-onaning xohishiga bog'liq edi. Bu hech bo'lmaganda Lidiyaga nisbatan endi hal qilinishi kerak bo'lgan bir masala edi va janob Bennet oldidagi taklifga rozi bo'lishda hech qanday ikkilanmasdi. Qaynag'asining mehribonligi uchun minnatdorlik so'zlari bilan, garchi juda qisqa ifodalangan bo'lsa ham, u qilingan hamma narsani to'liq ma'qullashini va uning nomidan olingan majburiyatlarni bajarishga tayyorligini qog'ozga tushirdi. U ilgari hech qachon, agar Uikhemni qiziga uylanishga ko'ndirish mumkin bo'lsa, bu hozirgi kelishuvdagidek o'zi uchun bunchalik kam noqulaylik bilan amalga oshadi, deb taxmin qilmagan edi. Ularga to'lanadigan yuz funt bilan u yiliga o'n funt ham zarar ko'rmasdi; chunki uning ovqati va cho'ntak puli, onasining qo'li orqali unga o'tadigan doimiy pul sovg'alari bilan Lidiyaning xarajatlari bu summadan unchalik kam emas edi.

paras.en: That it would be done with such trifling exertion on his side, too, was another very welcome surprise; for his wish at present was to have as little trouble in the business as possible. When the first transports of rage which had produced his activity in seeking her were over, he naturally returned to all his former indolence. His letter was soon dispatched; for, though dilatory in undertaking business, he was quick in its execution. He begged to know further particulars of what he was indebted to his brother, but was too angry with Lydia to send any message to her.
paras.uz: Bu uning tomonidan bunchalik arzimas harakat bilan amalga oshishi ham juda xush kelgan yana bir syurpriz edi; chunki hozir uning istagi bu ishda iloji boricha kam tashvish chekish edi. Uni qizini qidirishda faollikka undagan g'azabning dastlabki hayajonlari o'tgach, u tabiiy ravishda avvalgi butun dangasaligiga qaytdi. Uning xati tez jo'natildi; chunki u ishni boshlashda sust bo'lsa ham, uni bajarishda tez edi. U qaynag'asiga nimadan qarzdor ekani haqida qo'shimcha tafsilotlarni bilishni so'radi, lekin Lidiyaga biror xabar yuborish uchun undan haddan tashqari g'azablangan edi.

paras.en: The good news spread quickly through the house, and with proportionate speed through the neighbourhood. It was borne in the latter with decent philosophy. To be sure, it would have been more for the advantage of conversation had Miss Lydia Bennet come upon the town; or, as the happiest alternative, been secluded from the world, in some distant farmhouse. But there was much to be talked of in marrying her; and the good-natured wishes for her well-doing which had proceeded before from all the spiteful old ladies in Meryton lost but a little of their spirit in this change of circumstances, because with such an husband her misery was considered certain.
paras.uz: Yaxshi xabar uy bo'ylab tez tarqaldi, mahalla bo'ylab ham shunga mutanosib tezlikda. U yerda unga munosib falsafa bilan qarashdi. Albatta, agar miss Lidiya Bennet ko'chada qolganida yoki eng baxtli muqobil sifatida qandaydir uzoq ferma uyida dunyodan ajratilganida, suhbat uchun ancha foydaliroq bo'lardi. Lekin uning turmushga chiqishida ham gaplashadigan ko'p narsa bor edi; Meritondagi barcha g'arazli keksa xonimlardan avval kelgan uning omadi uchun xushfe'l tilaklar vaziyatning bu o'zgarishida o'z ruhini juda oz yo'qotdi, chunki bunday er bilan uning baxtsizligi aniq deb hisoblanardi.

paras.en: It was a fortnight since Mrs. Bennet had been downstairs; but on this happy day she again took her seat at the head of her table, and in spirits oppressively high. No sentiment of shame gave a damp to her triumph. The marriage of a daughter, which had been the first object of her wishes since Jane was sixteen, was now on the point of accomplishment, and her thoughts and her words ran wholly on those attendants of elegant nuptials, fine muslins, new carriages, and servants. She was busily searching through the neighbourhood for a proper situation for her daughter, and, without knowing or considering what their income might be, rejected many as deficient in size and importance.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet pastga tushmaganiga ikki hafta bo'lgan edi; lekin bu baxtli kunda u yana dasturxonning bosh tomoniga o'tirdi va kayfiyati ezuvchi darajada baland edi. Hech qanday uyat tuyg'usi uning g'alabasini so'ndirmadi. Jeyn o'n olti yoshga to'lgandan beri istaklarining birinchi obyekti bo'lgan qizining turmushga chiqishi endi amalga oshish arafasida edi va uning fikrlari va so'zlari butunlay nafis to'ylarning hamrohlari — nafis muslinlar, yangi aravalar va xizmatkorlar haqida edi. U mahalla bo'ylab qizi uchun munosib joy qidirish bilan band edi va ularning daromadi qancha bo'lishi mumkinligini bilmasdan yoki hisobga olmasdan, ko'plarini o'lchami va ahamiyati yetarsiz deb rad etdi.

paras.en: “Haye Park might do,” said she, “if the Gouldings could quit it--or the great house at Stoke, if the drawing-room were larger; but Ashworth is too far off! I could not bear to have her ten miles from me; and as for Pulvis Lodge, the attics are dreadful.”
paras.uz: «Xey Park bo'lishi mumkin, — dedi u, — agar Gouldinglar uni bo'shatsa — yoki Stokdagi katta uy, agar mehmonxonasi kattaroq bo'lsa; lekin Eshvort juda uzoq! Uning mendan o'n mil uzoqda bo'lishiga chiday olmasdim; Pulvis Lojga kelsak, uning cherdaklari dahshatli».

paras.en: Her husband allowed her to talk on without interruption while the servants remained. But when they had withdrawn, he said to her: “Mrs. Bennet, before you take any or all of these houses for your son and daughter, let us come to a right understanding. Into one house in this neighbourhood they shall never have admittance. I will not encourage the impudence of either, by receiving them at Longbourn.”
paras.uz: Xizmatkorlar qolgan vaqtda eri unga gapini bo'lmasdan gapirishga ruxsat berdi. Lekin ular chiqib ketgach, u unga dedi: «Missis Bennet, o'g'lingiz va qizingiz uchun bu uylarning birortasini yoki hammasini olishdan oldin, keling, to'g'ri tushunib olaylik. Bu mahalladagi bir uyga ularni hech qachon kiritishmaydi. Ularni Longbornda qabul qilib, hech birining surbetligini rag'batlantirmayman».

paras.en: A long dispute followed this declaration; but Mr. Bennet was firm. It soon led to another; and Mrs. Bennet found, with amazement and horror, that her husband would not advance a guinea to buy clothes for his daughter. He protested that she should receive from him no mark of affection whatever on the occasion. Mrs. Bennet could hardly comprehend it. That his anger could be carried to such a point of inconceivable resentment as to refuse his daughter a privilege without which her marriage would scarcely seem valid, exceeded all she could believe possible. She was more alive to the disgrace which her want of new clothes must reflect on her daughter's nuptials, than to any sense of shame at her eloping and living with Wickham a fortnight before they took place.
paras.uz: Bu bayonotdan keyin uzoq bahs boshlandi; lekin janob Bennet qat'iy edi. U tez orada boshqasiga olib keldi; va missis Bennet hayrat va dahshat bilan eri qiziga kiyim sotib olish uchun bir gineya ham bermasligini bildi. U bu munosabat bilan qizi undan hech qanday mehr belgisini olmasligini ta'kidladi. Missis Bennet buni zo'rg'a tushuna oldi. Uning g'azabi qiziga usiz nikohi zo'rg'a haqiqiy ko'rinadigan imtiyozni rad etadigan darajada aqlga sig'mas ranjishga yetishi u mumkin deb ishona oladigan hamma narsadan oshib ketardi. U yangi kiyimlar yo'qligi qizining to'yiga keltirishi kerak bo'lgan sharmandalikni uning qochib ketishi va to'ydan ikki hafta oldin Uikhem bilan yashaganidan uyalish hissidan ko'ra ko'proq his qilardi.

paras.en: Elizabeth was now most heartily sorry that she had, from the distress of the moment, been led to make Mr. Darcy acquainted with their fears for her sister; for since her marriage would so shortly give the proper termination to the elopement, they might hope to conceal its unfavourable beginning from all those who were not immediately on the spot.
paras.uz: Elizabet endi lahzaning iztirobidan janob Darsini singlisi uchun qo'rquvlaridan xabardor qilganidan chin dildan afsuslandi; chunki uning nikohi tez orada qochishga munosib yakun berishi sababli, ular uning noxush boshlanishini voqea joyida bevosita bo'lmagan barcha odamlardan yashirishga umid qilishlari mumkin edi.

paras.en: She had no fear of its spreading farther through his means. There were few people on whose secrecy she would have more confidently depended; but, at the same time, there was no one whose knowledge of a sister's frailty would have mortified her so much--not, however, from any fear of disadvantage from it individually to herself, for, at any rate, there seemed a gulf impassable between them. Had Lydia's marriage been concluded on the most honourable terms, it was not to be supposed that Mr. Darcy would connect himself with a family where, to every other objection, would now be added an alliance and relationship of the nearest kind with a man whom he so justly scorned.
paras.uz: U bu uning orqali yanada uzoqqa tarqalishidan qo'rqmasdi. U sir saqlashiga bundan ham ishonch bilan tayanadigan odamlar kam edi; lekin shu bilan birga, singlisining zaifligi haqida bilishi uni bunchalik xo'rlaydigan boshqa hech kim yo'q edi — biroq bu o'zi uchun shaxsan biror zarar qo'rquvidan emas, chunki har holda ular o'rtasida o'tib bo'lmas jarlik bordek tuyulardi. Agar Lidiyaning nikohi eng sharafli shartlarda tuzilganida ham, janob Darsi har bir boshqa e'tirozga endi o'zi shunchalik adolatli nafratlanadigan odam bilan eng yaqin turdagi ittifoq va qarindoshlik qo'shiladigan oila bilan bog'lanadi, deb taxmin qilib bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: From such a connection she could not wonder that he would shrink. The wish of procuring her regard, which she had assured herself of his feeling in Derbyshire, could not in rational expectation survive such a blow as this. She was humbled, she was grieved; she repented, though she hardly knew of what. She became jealous of his esteem, when she could no longer hope to be benefited by it. She wanted to hear of him, when there seemed the least chance of gaining intelligence. She was convinced that she could have been happy with him, when it was no longer likely they should meet.
paras.uz: Bunday qarindoshlikdan uning chekinishiga u hayron bo'la olmasdi. U Derbishirda uning his qilishiga ishonch hosil qilgan uning mehrini qozonish istagi oqilona kutishga ko'ra bunday zarbadan omon qola olmasdi. U kamsitilgan, qayg'urgan edi; nimadan ekanini zo'rg'a bilsa ham, pushaymon edi. U endi undan foyda ko'rishga umid qila olmaganda, uning hurmatini qizg'ana boshladi. U ma'lumot olish imkoniyati eng kam bo'lganda u haqida eshitishni istadi. U ular endi uchrashishi ehtimoldan yiroq bo'lganda, u bilan baxtli bo'lishi mumkin edi, degan ishonchga keldi.

paras.en: What a triumph for him, as she often thought, could he know that the proposals which she had proudly spurned only four months ago, would now have been most gladly and gratefully received! He was as generous, she doubted not, as the most generous of his sex; but while he was mortal, there must be a triumph.
paras.uz: U ko'pincha o'ylaganidek, agar u faqat to'rt oy oldin o'zi g'urur bilan rad etgan takliflar endi eng mamnuniyat va minnatdorlik bilan qabul qilinishini bilganida, bu u uchun qanday g'alaba bo'lardi! U, shubhasiz, o'z jinsining eng olijanobi kabi olijanob edi; lekin u inson ekan, g'alaba bo'lishi muqarrar edi.

paras.en: She began now to comprehend that he was exactly the man who, in disposition and talents, would most suit her. His understanding and temper, though unlike her own, would have answered all her wishes. It was an union that must have been to the advantage of both; by her ease and liveliness, his mind might have been softened, his manners improved; and from his judgement, information, and knowledge of the world, she must have received benefit of greater importance.
paras.uz: U endi tushuna boshladi: u fe'li va iste'dodlari bo'yicha unga eng mos keladigan aynan o'sha erkak edi. Uning aqli va fe'li, o'zinikiga o'xshamasa ham, uning barcha istaklariga javob bergan bo'lardi. Bu ikkalasi uchun ham foydali bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan ittifoq edi; uning yengilligi va jo'shqinligi bilan uning aqli yumshashi, muomalasi yaxshilanishi mumkin edi; uning mulohazasi, bilimi va dunyoni bilishidan esa u ancha muhimroq foyda olishi kerak edi.

paras.en: But no such happy marriage could now teach the admiring multitude what connubial felicity really was. An union of a different tendency, and precluding the possibility of the other, was soon to be formed in their family.
paras.uz: Lekin endi hech qanday bunday baxtli nikoh hayratlanuvchi olomonga nikoh baxti aslida nima ekanini o'rgata olmasdi. Boshqacha yo'nalishdagi va ikkinchisining imkoniyatini istisno qiladigan ittifoq tez orada ularning oilasida tuzilishi kerak edi.

paras.en: How Wickham and Lydia were to be supported in tolerable independence, she could not imagine. But how little of permanent happiness could belong to a couple who were only brought together because their passions were stronger than their virtue, she could easily conjecture.
paras.uz: Uikhem va Lidiya qanday qilib chidasa bo'ladigan mustaqillikda ta'minlanishini u tasavvur qila olmasdi. Lekin faqat ehtiroslari fazilatidan kuchliroq bo'lgani uchun birga bo'lgan juftlikka doimiy baxtning qanchalik oz qismi tegishli bo'lishi mumkinligini u osongina taxmin qila olardi.

paras.en: Mr. Gardiner soon wrote again to his brother. To Mr. Bennet's acknowledgments he briefly replied, with assurance of his eagerness to promote the welfare of any of his family; and concluded with entreaties that the subject might never be mentioned to him again. The principal purport of his letter was to inform them that Mr. Wickham had resolved on quitting the militia.
paras.uz: Janob Gardiner tez orada pochchasiga yana yozdi. Janob Bennetning minnatdorchiliklariga u qisqacha, uning oilasining har qanday a'zosining farovonligiga hissa qo'shishga intilishiga ishontirish bilan javob berdi va bu mavzu unga boshqa hech qachon tilga olinmasligi haqidagi iltimoslar bilan tugatdi. Uning xatining asosiy maqsadi ularga janob Uikhem militsiyani tark etishga qaror qilganini xabar qilish edi.

paras.en: “It was greatly my wish that he should do so,” he added, “as soon as his marriage was fixed on. And I think you will agree with me, in considering the removal from that corps as highly advisable, both on his account and my niece's. It is Mr. Wickham's intention to go into the regulars; and among his former friends, there are still some who are able and willing to assist him in the army. He has the promise of an ensigncy in General ----'s regiment, now quartered in the North. It is an advantage to have it so far from this part of the kingdom. He promises fairly; and I hope among different people, where they may each have a character to preserve, they will both be more prudent.
paras.uz: «Uning nikohi belgilanishi bilanoq shunday qilishini juda istagan edim, — qo'shib qo'ydi u. — Va menimcha, siz ham men bilan birga o'sha polkdan ketishni uning uchun ham, jiyanim uchun ham juda maqsadga muvofiq deb hisoblaysiz. Janob Uikhem doimiy armiyaga o'tish niyatida; uning avvalgi do'stlari orasida hali ham armiyada unga yordam berishga qodir va tayyor bo'lganlar bor. Unga hozir Shimolda joylashgan general ----ning polkida praporshchik lavozimi va'da qilingan. Uning qirollikning bu qismidan shunchalik uzoqda bo'lishi afzallik. U yaxshi va'dalar beryapti; umid qilamanki, har biri saqlashi kerak bo'lgan obro'ga ega bo'lgan boshqa odamlar orasida ikkalasi ham ehtiyotkorroq bo'ladi.

paras.en: I have written to Colonel Forster, to inform him of our present arrangements, and to request that he will satisfy the various creditors of Mr. Wickham in and near Brighton, with assurances of speedy payment, for which I have pledged myself. And will you give yourself the trouble of carrying similar assurances to his creditors in Meryton, of whom I shall subjoin a list according to his information? He has given in all his debts; I hope at least he has not deceived us. Haggerston has our directions, and all will be completed in a week. They will then join his regiment, unless they are first invited to Longbourn; and I understand from Mrs. Gardiner, that my niece is very desirous of seeing you all before she leaves the South. She is well, and begs to be dutifully remembered to you and her mother.--Yours, etc.,
paras.uz: Men polkovnik Forsterga xat yozib, unga hozirgi kelishuvlarimiz haqida xabar berdim va undan Brayton va uning atrofidagi janob Uikhemning turli kreditorlarini men kafolat bergan tez to'lov haqidagi ishontirishlar bilan qoniqtirishni so'radim. Siz ham Meritondagi kreditorlariga shunga o'xshash ishontirishlarni yetkazish zahmatini chekasizmi? Ularning ro'yxatini uning ma'lumotiga ko'ra ilova qilaman. U barcha qarzlarini aytdi; umid qilamanki, hech bo'lmaganda bizni aldamadi. Haggerston bizning ko'rsatmalarimizni oldi va hammasi bir haftada tugaydi. Keyin ular, agar avval Longbornga taklif qilinmasa, uning polkiga qo'shilishadi; missis Gardinerdan bilishimcha, jiyanim Janubni tark etishdan oldin hammangizni ko'rishni juda istaydi. U sog'-salomat va sizga va onasiga hurmat bilan salom yo'llaydi. — Sizniki va hokazo,

paras.en: “E. GARDINER.”
paras.uz: E. GARDINER».

paras.en: Mr. Bennet and his daughters saw all the advantages of Wickham's removal from the ----shire as clearly as Mr. Gardiner could do. But Mrs. Bennet was not so well pleased with it. Lydia's being settled in the North, just when she had expected most pleasure and pride in her company, for she had by no means given up her plan of their residing in Hertfordshire, was a severe disappointment; and, besides, it was such a pity that Lydia should be taken from a regiment where she was acquainted with everybody, and had so many favourites.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet va uning qizlari Uikhemning ----shir polkidan ketishining barcha afzalliklarini janob Gardiner kabi aniq ko'rishdi. Lekin missis Bennet bundan unchalik mamnun emasdi. Lidiyaning Shimolda joylashishi, aynan u uning davrasidan eng ko'p zavq va g'urur kutgan paytda — chunki u ularning Xertfordshirda yashash rejasidan umuman voz kechmagan edi — og'ir hafsala pirligi edi; bundan tashqari, Lidiyani hammani taniydigan va shunchalik ko'p sevimlilari bo'lgan polkdan olib ketish shunday achinarli edi.

paras.en: “She is so fond of Mrs. Forster,” said she, “it will be quite shocking to send her away! And there are several of the young men, too, that she likes very much. The officers may not be so pleasant in General ----'s regiment.”
paras.uz: «U missis Forsterni shunchalik yaxshi ko'radiki, — dedi u, — uni uzoqqa jo'natish juda dahshatli bo'ladi! Uning juda yoqtiradigan bir nechta yosh yigitlari ham bor. General ----ning polkidagi ofitserlar unchalik yoqimli bo'lmasligi mumkin».

paras.en: His daughter's request, for such it might be considered, of being admitted into her family again before she set off for the North, received at first an absolute negative. But Jane and Elizabeth, who agreed in wishing, for the sake of their sister's feelings and consequence, that she should be noticed on her marriage by her parents, urged him so earnestly yet so rationally and so mildly, to receive her and her husband at Longbourn, as soon as they were married, that he was prevailed on to think as they thought, and act as they wished. And their mother had the satisfaction of knowing that she would be able to show her married daughter in the neighbourhood before she was banished to the North. When Mr. Bennet wrote again to his brother, therefore, he sent his permission for them to come; and it was settled, that as soon as the ceremony was over, they should proceed to Longbourn. Elizabeth was surprised, however, that Wickham should consent to such a scheme, and had she consulted only her own inclination, any meeting with him would have been the last object of her wishes.
paras.uz: Qizining Shimolga jo'nashidan oldin oilasiga yana qabul qilinishi haqidagi iltimosi — buni shunday deb hisoblash mumkin edi — avvaliga mutlaq rad javobini oldi. Lekin singillarining tuyg'ulari va obro'si uchun uning nikohda ota-onasi tomonidan e'tirof etilishini istashda hamfikr bo'lgan Jeyn va Elizabet uni turmush qurishlari bilanoq uni va uning erini Longbornda qabul qilishga shunchalik jiddiy, shu bilan birga shunchalik oqilona va muloyim undashdiki, u ular kabi o'ylashga va ular istagandek harakat qilishga ko'ndirildi. Onalari esa turmushga chiqqan qizini Shimolga surgun qilinishidan oldin mahallada ko'rsata olishini bilib mamnun bo'ldi. Shuning uchun janob Bennet qaynag'asiga yana yozganda, ularning kelishiga ruxsat yubordi; va marosim tugashi bilanoq ular Longbornga borishlari kelishildi. Biroq Elizabet Uikhemning bunday rejaga rozi bo'lishidan hayron bo'ldi va agar u faqat o'z moyilligi bilan maslahatlashganida, u bilan har qanday uchrashuv uning istaklarining eng oxirgi obyekti bo'lardi.

said she, “if the Gouldings could quit it--or the great house at Stoke, if the drawing-room were larger; but Ashworth is too far off!

quiz.q: What does Elizabeth now understand about Darcy?
o: He was the man who would most suit her
quiz.why_uz: Endi esa, uning fikricha, kech.

quiz.q: What does Mr. Bennet regret?
o: Not saving money for his family
quiz.why_uz: Uning beparvoligi oilaga qimmatga tushdi.

chapters.title: Lydia's Visit
chapters.recap_uz: Lidiya va Uikhem Longbournga kelishadi — umuman uyalmay. Lidiya beixtiyor to'yda Darsi ham bo'lganini aytib yuboradi. Elizabet xolasiga xat yozib, sababini so'raydi.

paras.en: Their sister's wedding day arrived; and Jane and Elizabeth felt for her probably more than she felt for herself. The carriage was sent to meet them at ----, and they were to return in it by dinner-time. Their arrival was dreaded by the elder Miss Bennets, and Jane more especially, who gave Lydia the feelings which would have attended herself, had she been the culprit, and was wretched in the thought of what her sister must endure.
paras.uz: Singillarining to'y kuni keldi; Jeyn va Elizabet uning uchun, ehtimol, uning o'zi o'zi uchun his qilganidan ko'proq his qilishdi. Arava ularni ----da kutib olish uchun yuborildi va ular tushlik vaqtiga u bilan qaytishlari kerak edi. Ularning kelishidan katta miss Bennetlar, ayniqsa Jeyn qo'rqardi, u Lidiyaga agar o'zi aybdor bo'lganida o'zini qamrab olgan bo'ladigan tuyg'ularni berib, singlisi nimalarga chidashi kerakligini o'ylab, baxtsiz edi.

paras.en: They came. The family were assembled in the breakfast room to receive them. Smiles decked the face of Mrs. Bennet as the carriage drove up to the door; her husband looked impenetrably grave; her daughters, alarmed, anxious, uneasy.
paras.uz: Ular kelishdi. Oila ularni qabul qilish uchun nonushta xonasiga yig'ildi. Arava eshik oldiga kelganda missis Bennetning yuzini tabassumlar bezadi; eri tushunib bo'lmas darajada jiddiy ko'rinardi; qizlari esa xavotirli, tashvishli, bezovta.

paras.en: Lydia's voice was heard in the vestibule; the door was thrown open, and she ran into the room. Her mother stepped forwards, embraced her, and welcomed her with rapture; gave her hand, with an affectionate smile, to Wickham, who followed his lady; and wished them both joy with an alacrity which shewed no doubt of their happiness.
paras.uz: Dahlizda Lidiyaning ovozi eshitildi; eshik lang ochildi va u xonaga yugurib kirdi. Onasi oldinga chiqib, uni quchoqladi va hayajon bilan kutib oldi; xonimining ortidan kirgan Uikhemga mehrli tabassum bilan qo'lini uzatdi; va ikkalasiga ularning baxtiga hech qanday shubha qilmaydigan tayyorlik bilan baxt tiladi.

paras.en: Their reception from Mr. Bennet, to whom they then turned, was not quite so cordial. His countenance rather gained in austerity; and he scarcely opened his lips. The easy assurance of the young couple, indeed, was enough to provoke him. Elizabeth was disgusted, and even Miss Bennet was shocked. Lydia was Lydia still; untamed, unabashed, wild, noisy, and fearless. She turned from sister to sister, demanding their congratulations; and when at length they all sat down, looked eagerly round the room, took notice of some little alteration in it, and observed, with a laugh, that it was a great while since she had been there.
paras.uz: Keyin ular o'girilgan janob Bennet ularni unchalik samimiy qabul qilmadi. Uning chehrasi yanada qattiqroq tus oldi; u deyarli lab ochmadi. Haqiqatan ham, yosh juftlikning beparvo surbetligi uning g'ashini keltirish uchun yetarli edi. Elizabet jirkandi, hatto miss Bennet ham dahshatga tushdi. Lidiya hali ham Lidiya edi; bo'ysunmas, uyalmas, yovvoyi, shovqinli va qo'rqmas. U opadan opaga o'tib, ulardan tabrik talab qildi; nihoyat hammalari o'tirgach, xonaga ishtiyoq bilan nazar tashladi, undagi biror kichik o'zgarishni sezdi va kulib, u yerda bo'lmaganiga ancha bo'lganini aytdi.

paras.en: Wickham was not at all more distressed than herself, but his manners were always so pleasing, that had his character and his marriage been exactly what they ought, his smiles and his easy address, while he claimed their relationship, would have delighted them all. Elizabeth had not before believed him quite equal to such assurance; but she sat down, resolving within herself to draw no limits in future to the impudence of an impudent man. She blushed, and Jane blushed; but the cheeks of the two who caused their confusion suffered no variation of colour.
paras.uz: Uikhem undan umuman ko'proq xijolatda emasdi, lekin uning muomalasi doim shunchalik yoqimli ediki, agar uning xarakteri va nikohi aynan bo'lishi kerak bo'lgandek bo'lganida, ularning qarindoshligini da'vo qilayotgandagi tabassumlari va beparvo muomalasi hammani xursand qilgan bo'lardi. Elizabet ilgari uni bunday surbetlikka qodir deb ishonmagan edi; lekin u o'tirdi va ichida kelajakda surbet odamning surbetligiga hech qanday chegara qo'ymaslikka qaror qildi. U qizardi, Jeyn ham qizardi; lekin ularning xijolatiga sabab bo'lgan ikkalasining yonoqlarida hech qanday rang o'zgarishi bo'lmadi.

paras.en: There was no want of discourse. The bride and her mother could neither of them talk fast enough; and Wickham, who happened to sit near Elizabeth, began inquiring after his acquaintance in that neighbourhood, with a good humoured ease which she felt very unable to equal in her replies. They seemed each of them to have the happiest memories in the world. Nothing of the past was recollected with pain; and Lydia led voluntarily to subjects which her sisters would not have alluded to for the world.
paras.uz: Suhbatdan kamchilik yo'q edi. Kelin ham, onasi ham yetarlicha tez gapira olmasdi; tasodifan Elizabetning yonida o'tirgan Uikhem u mahalladagi tanishlari haqida shunday xushfe'l yengillik bilan so'ray boshladiki, u javoblarida unga tenglasha olmasligini his qildi. Ularning har biri dunyodagi eng baxtli xotiralarga ega bo'lganday ko'rinardi. O'tmishdan hech narsa og'riq bilan eslanmadi; Lidiya esa o'z ixtiyori bilan opalari dunyo bersa ham ishora qilmagan bo'ladigan mavzularga o'tdi.

paras.en: “Only think of its being three months,” she cried, “since I went away; it seems but a fortnight I declare; and yet there have been things enough happened in the time. Good gracious! when I went away, I am sure I had no more idea of being married till I came back again! though I thought it would be very good fun if I was.”
paras.uz: «O'ylab ko'ringlar-a, ketganimga uch oy bo'ldi, — xitob qildi u. — Rostini aytsam, atigi ikki hafta bo'lganga o'xshaydi; shunga qaramay bu vaqt ichida qanchadan-qancha narsalar bo'ldi. Voy! Ketganimda, qaytib kelgunimcha turmushga chiqishim haqida hech qanday tasavvurim yo'q edi! Garchi agar chiqsam, juda qiziq bo'ladi deb o'ylagan bo'lsam ham».

paras.en: Her father lifted up his eyes. Jane was distressed. Elizabeth looked expressively at Lydia; but she, who never heard nor saw anything of which she chose to be insensible, gaily continued, “Oh! mamma, do the people hereabouts know I am married to-day? I was afraid they might not; and we overtook William Goulding in his curricle, so I was determined he should know it, and so I let down the side-glass next to him, and took off my glove, and let my hand just rest upon the window frame, so that he might see the ring, and then I bowed and smiled like anything.”
paras.uz: Otasi ko'zlarini ko'tardi. Jeyn xijolat bo'ldi. Elizabet Lidiyaga ma'noli qaradi; lekin o'zi sezmaslikni tanlagan hech narsani hech qachon eshitmaydigan va ko'rmaydigan Lidiya quvnoq davom etdi: «Oh! Oyijon, bu yerdagi odamlar bugun turmushga chiqqanimni bilishadimi? Bilmasliklaridan qo'rqdim; biz yengil aravasida ketayotgan Uilyam Gouldingni quvib o'tdik, shuning uchun u buni bilishi kerak deb qaror qildim, uning tomonidagi yon oynani tushirdim, qo'lqopimni yechdim va qo'limni deraza romiga shunchaki qo'ydim, u uzukni ko'rishi uchun, keyin bor kuchim bilan ta'zim qilib, jilmaydim».

paras.en: Elizabeth could bear it no longer. She got up, and ran out of the room; and returned no more, till she heard them passing through the hall to the dining parlour. She then joined them soon enough to see Lydia, with anxious parade, walk up to her mother's right hand, and hear her say to her eldest sister, “Ah! Jane, I take your place now, and you must go lower, because I am a married woman.”
paras.uz: Elizabet boshqa chiday olmadi. U o'rnidan turib, xonadan yugurib chiqdi; va ularning zal orqali ovqatxonaga o'tayotganini eshitmaguncha qaytmadi. Keyin u ularga Lidiyaning tashvishli namoyish bilan onasining o'ng qo'li tomonga borganini ko'rish va uning to'ng'ich opasiga «Ah! Jeyn, endi men sening o'rningni egallayman, sen pastroqqa o'tishing kerak, chunki men turmush qurgan ayolman» deganini eshitish uchun yetarlicha tez qo'shildi.

paras.en: It was not to be supposed that time would give Lydia that embarrassment from which she had been so wholly free at first. Her ease and good spirits increased. She longed to see Mrs. Phillips, the Lucases, and all their other neighbours, and to hear herself called “Mrs. Wickham” by each of them; and in the mean time, she went after dinner to show her ring, and boast of being married, to Mrs. Hill and the two housemaids.
paras.uz: Vaqt Lidiyaga u boshidanoq butunlay xoli bo'lgan xijolatni beradi deb taxmin qilib bo'lmasdi. Uning yengilligi va yaxshi kayfiyati ortdi. U missis Fillipsni, Lukaslarni va boshqa barcha qo'shnilarini ko'rishni va ularning har biridan o'zini «missis Uikhem» deb chaqirishlarini eshitishni juda istardi; bu orada tushlikdan keyin u missis Hill va ikki xizmatkor qizga uzugini ko'rsatish va turmush qurgani bilan maqtanish uchun bordi.

paras.en: “Well, mamma,” said she, when they were all returned to the breakfast room, “and what do you think of my husband? Is not he a charming man? I am sure my sisters must all envy me. I only hope they may have half my good luck. They must all go to Brighton. That is the place to get husbands. What a pity it is, mamma, we did not all go.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, oyijon, — dedi u, hammalari nonushta xonasiga qaytgach, — erim haqida qanday fikrdasiz? U maftunkor erkak emasmi? Ishonchim komilki, opalarim hammasi menga hasad qilishsa kerak. Faqat umid qilamanki, ular mening omadimning yarmiga ega bo'lishadi. Ular hammasi Braytonga borishlari kerak. Er topish uchun joy shu. Qanday afsus, oyijon, biz hammamiz bormadik».

paras.en: “Very true; and if I had my will, we should. But my dear Lydia, I don't at all like your going such a way off. Must it be so?”
paras.uz: «Juda to'g'ri; agar mening xohishim bo'lganida, borgan bo'lardik. Lekin, aziz Lidiyam, bunchalik uzoqqa ketishing menga umuman yoqmaydi. Shunday bo'lishi shartmi?»

paras.en: “Oh, lord! yes;--there is nothing in that. I shall like it of all things. You and papa, and my sisters, must come down and see us. We shall be at Newcastle all the winter, and I dare say there will be some balls, and I will take care to get good partners for them all.”
paras.uz: «Oh, Xudoyim! Ha; — bunda hech narsa yo'q. Menga hammadan ham yoqadi. Siz, dadam va opalarim bizni ko'rgani kelishingiz kerak. Biz butun qish Nyukaslda bo'lamiz, ishonamanki, u yerda ba'zi ballar bo'ladi, men hammasiga yaxshi sheriklar topib berishga g'amxo'rlik qilaman».

paras.en: “I should like it beyond anything!” said her mother.
paras.uz: «Bu menga hamma narsadan ham yoqardi!» — dedi onasi.

paras.en: “And then when you go away, you may leave one or two of my sisters behind you; and I dare say I shall get husbands for them before the winter is over.”
paras.uz: «Keyin ketayotganingizda, opalarimdan bir-ikkitasini qoldirib ketishingiz mumkin; ishonamanki, qish tugashidan oldin ularga er topib beraman».

paras.en: “I thank you for my share of the favour,” said Elizabeth; “but I do not particularly like your way of getting husbands.”
paras.uz: «Iltifotning menga tegishli ulushi uchun rahmat, — dedi Elizabet, — lekin sening er topish usuling menga unchalik yoqmaydi».

paras.en: Their visitors were not to remain above ten days with them. Mr. Wickham had received his commission before he left London, and he was to join his regiment at the end of a fortnight.
paras.uz: Mehmonlar ular bilan o'n kundan ortiq qolmasliklari kerak edi. Janob Uikhem Londondan ketishdan oldin lavozimini olgan edi va u ikki hafta oxirida polkiga qo'shilishi kerak edi.

paras.en: No one but Mrs. Bennet regretted that their stay would be so short; and she made the most of the time by visiting about with her daughter, and having very frequent parties at home. These parties were acceptable to all; to avoid a family circle was even more desirable to such as did think, than such as did not.
paras.uz: Missis Bennetdan boshqa hech kim ularning qolishi bunchalik qisqa ekanidan afsuslanmadi; u esa vaqtdan qizi bilan mehmonga borish va uyda juda tez-tez yig'inlar o'tkazish orqali eng ko'p foydalandi. Bu yig'inlar hammaga ma'qul edi; oila davrasidan qochish o'ylamaydiganlardan ko'ra o'ylaydiganlar uchun yanada maqbulroq edi.

paras.en: Wickham's affection for Lydia was just what Elizabeth had expected to find it; not equal to Lydia's for him. She had scarcely needed her present observation to be satisfied, from the reason of things, that their elopement had been brought on by the strength of her love, rather than by his; and she would have wondered why, without violently caring for her, he chose to elope with her at all, had she not felt certain that his flight was rendered necessary by distress of circumstances; and if that were the case, he was not the young man to resist an opportunity of having a companion.
paras.uz: Uikhemning Lidiyaga mehri aynan Elizabet kutgandek edi; Lidiyaning unga mehriga teng emasdi. Narsalarning mantig'idan ularning qochishi uning muhabbatidan ko'ra Lidiyaning muhabbatining kuchi tufayli sodir bo'lganiga ishonch hosil qilish uchun unga hozirgi kuzatuvi zo'rg'a kerak edi; va agar u uning qochishi ahvolining og'irligi tufayli zarur bo'lganiga amin bo'lmaganida, u unga qattiq ahamiyat bermasdan nega u bilan umuman qochishni tanlaganiga hayron bo'lgan bo'lardi; agar shunday bo'lsa, u hamrohga ega bo'lish imkoniyatiga qarshi tura oladigan yosh yigit emasdi.

paras.en: Lydia was exceedingly fond of him. He was her dear Wickham on every occasion; no one was to be put in competition with him. He did every thing best in the world; and she was sure he would kill more birds on the first of September, than any body else in the country.
paras.uz: Lidiya uni nihoyatda yaxshi ko'rardi. U har bir holatda uning aziz Uikhemi edi; hech kim u bilan raqobatlashmasligi kerak edi. U dunyodagi hamma narsani eng yaxshi qilardi; va u 1-sentabrda u mamlakatdagi boshqa har kimdan ko'proq qush otishiga amin edi.

paras.en: One morning, soon after their arrival, as she was sitting with her two elder sisters, she said to Elizabeth:
paras.uz: Ular kelganidan ko'p o'tmay bir kuni ertalab, u ikki katta opasi bilan o'tirganda, Elizabetga dedi:

paras.en: “Lizzy, I never gave you an account of my wedding, I believe. You were not by, when I told mamma and the others all about it. Are not you curious to hear how it was managed?”
paras.uz: «Lizzi, menimcha, senga to'yim haqida hech qachon aytib bermadim. Men oyimga va boshqalarga hammasini aytib berganimda sen yonimizda yo'q eding. Bu qanday tashkil qilinganini eshitishga qiziqmaysanmi?»

paras.en: “No really,” replied Elizabeth; “I think there cannot be too little said on the subject.”
paras.uz: «Rostdan ham yo'q, — javob berdi Elizabet. — Menimcha, bu mavzuda qanchalik kam gapirilsa, shunchalik yaxshi».

paras.en: “La! You are so strange! But I must tell you how it went off. We were married, you know, at St. Clement's, because Wickham's lodgings were in that parish. And it was settled that we should all be there by eleven o'clock. My uncle and aunt and I were to go together; and the others were to meet us at the church. Well, Monday morning came, and I was in such a fuss! I was so afraid, you know, that something would happen to put it off, and then I should have gone quite distracted. And there was my aunt, all the time I was dressing, preaching and talking away just as if she was reading a sermon. However, I did not hear above one word in ten, for I was thinking, you may suppose, of my dear Wickham. I longed to know whether he would be married in his blue coat.”
paras.uz: «Voy! Sen shunchalik g'alatisan! Lekin senga qanday o'tganini aytib berishim kerak. Bilasanmi, biz Sent-Klement cherkovida nikohlandik, chunki Uikhemning turar joyi o'sha qavmda edi. Hammamiz soat o'n birgacha u yerda bo'lishimiz kelishilgan edi. Tog'am, xolam va men birga borishimiz kerak edi; boshqalar esa bizni cherkovda kutib olishlari kerak edi. Xo'sh, dushanba ertalab keldi, men shunday bezovta edim! Bilasanmi, uni keyinga qoldiradigan biror narsa bo'lishidan shunchalik qo'rqardimki, shunda butunlay aqldan ozgan bo'lardim. Men kiyinayotgan butun vaqt davomida xolam xuddi va'z o'qiyotgandek nasihat qilib, gapirib turdi. Biroq men o'nta so'zdan birini ham eshitmadim, chunki, taxmin qilishing mumkin, aziz Uikhemim haqida o'ylardim. U ko'k kamzulida nikohlanarmikin, bilishni juda istardim.

paras.en: “Well, and so we breakfasted at ten as usual; I thought it would never be over; for, by the bye, you are to understand, that my uncle and aunt were horrid unpleasant all the time I was with them. If you'll believe me, I did not once put my foot out of doors, though I was there a fortnight. Not one party, or scheme, or anything. To be sure London was rather thin, but, however, the Little Theatre was open. Well, and so just as the carriage came to the door, my uncle was called away upon business to that horrid man Mr. Stone. And then, you know, when once they get together, there is no end of it. Well, I was so frightened I did not know what to do, for my uncle was to give me away; and if we were beyond the hour, we could not be married all day. But, luckily, he came back again in ten minutes' time, and then we all set out. However, I recollected afterwards that if he had been prevented going, the wedding need not be put off, for Mr. Darcy might have done as well.”
paras.uz: Xo'sh, shunday qilib odatdagidek soat o'nda nonushta qildik; u hech qachon tugamaydi deb o'yladim; chunki, aytgancha, tushunishing kerakki, men ular bilan bo'lgan butun vaqt davomida tog'am va xolam dahshatli darajada yoqimsiz edi. Ishonasanmi, men u yerda ikki hafta bo'lsam ham, bir marta ham tashqariga qadam qo'ymadim. Birorta ham yig'in, reja yoki biror narsa yo'q. Albatta, London ancha bo'sh edi, lekin baribir Kichik teatr ochiq edi. Xo'sh, aynan arava eshik oldiga kelganda, tog'amni ish bilan o'sha dahshatli odam janob Stounning oldiga chaqirib ketishdi. Bilasanmi, ular bir marta yig'ilsa, oxiri yo'q. Xo'sh, men shunchalik qo'rqdimki, nima qilishni bilmadim, chunki tog'am meni nikohga topshirishi kerak edi; agar soatdan kech qolsak, butun kun nikohlana olmasdik. Lekin baxtimizga u o'n daqiqada qaytib keldi va keyin hammamiz yo'lga chiqdik. Biroq keyinroq esladimki, agar u bora olmaganida ham, to'yni keyinga qoldirish shart emasdi, chunki janob Darsi ham xuddi shunday qila olardi».

paras.en: “Mr. Darcy!” repeated Elizabeth, in utter amazement.
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi!» — takrorladi Elizabet butunlay hayratda.

paras.en: “Oh, yes!--he was to come there with Wickham, you know. But gracious me! I quite forgot! I ought not to have said a word about it. I promised them so faithfully! What will Wickham say? It was to be such a secret!”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha! — bilasanmi, u Uikhem bilan u yerga kelishi kerak edi. Lekin voy-dod! Butunlay unutibman! Bu haqda bir og'iz ham aytmasligim kerak edi. Ularga shunchalik sodiqlik bilan va'da bergan edim! Uikhem nima deydi? Bu shunday sir bo'lishi kerak edi!»

paras.en: “If it was to be secret,” said Jane, “say not another word on the subject. You may depend upon my seeking no further.”
paras.uz: «Agar bu sir bo'lishi kerak bo'lsa, — dedi Jeyn, — bu mavzuda boshqa bir og'iz ham gapirma. Men boshqa so'ramasligimga ishonishing mumkin».

paras.en: “Oh! certainly,” said Elizabeth, though burning with curiosity; “we will ask you no questions.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Albatta, — dedi Elizabet, garchi qiziqishdan yonib turgan bo'lsa ham, — sendan hech narsa so'ramaymiz».

paras.en: “Thank you,” said Lydia, “for if you did, I should certainly tell you all, and then Wickham would be angry.”
paras.uz: «Rahmat, — dedi Lidiya, — chunki agar so'rasangiz, albatta hammasini aytib berardim, keyin Uikhem g'azablanardi».

paras.en: On such encouragement to ask, Elizabeth was forced to put it out of her power, by running away.
paras.uz: So'rash uchun bunday rag'batga duch kelib, Elizabet yugurib ketish orqali buni qo'lidan kelmaydigan qilishga majbur bo'ldi.

paras.en: But to live in ignorance on such a point was impossible; or at least it was impossible not to try for information. Mr. Darcy had been at her sister's wedding. It was exactly a scene, and exactly among people, where he had apparently least to do, and least temptation to go. Conjectures as to the meaning of it, rapid and wild, hurried into her brain; but she was satisfied with none. Those that best pleased her, as placing his conduct in the noblest light, seemed most improbable. She could not bear such suspense; and hastily seizing a sheet of paper, wrote a short letter to her aunt, to request an explanation of what Lydia had dropt, if it were compatible with the secrecy which had been intended.
paras.uz: Lekin bunday masalada bexabar yashash imkonsiz edi; yoki hech bo'lmaganda ma'lumot olishga urinmaslik imkonsiz edi. Janob Darsi singlisining to'yida bo'lgan. Bu aynan u aftidan eng kam ishi bo'lgan va borish uchun eng kam vasvasaga ega bo'lgan sahna va aynan shunday odamlar orasida edi. Buning ma'nosi haqidagi tez va yovvoyi taxminlar uning miyasiga yopirildi; lekin u hech biridan qanoatlanmadi. Uning xatti-harakatini eng oliyjanob tarzda ko'rsatgani uchun unga eng ko'p yoqqanlari eng ehtimoldan yiroq tuyulardi. U bunday intizorlikka chiday olmadi; va shoshilib bir varaq qog'oz olib, xolasiga qisqa xat yozdi, agar bu ko'zlangan sir saqlash bilan mos kelsa, Lidiya og'zidan chiqarib yuborgan narsani tushuntirishni so'radi.

paras.en: “You may readily comprehend,” she added, “what my curiosity must be to know how a person unconnected with any of us, and (comparatively speaking) a stranger to our family, should have been amongst you at such a time. Pray write instantly, and let me understand it--unless it is, for very cogent reasons, to remain in the secrecy which Lydia seems to think necessary; and then I must endeavour to be satisfied with ignorance.”
paras.uz: «Osongina tushunishingiz mumkin, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — hech birimiz bilan bog'liq bo'lmagan va (nisbatan aytganda) oilamizga begona bo'lgan odamning bunday paytda sizlar orasida qanday bo'lganini bilishga qiziqishim qanchalik bo'lishi kerak. Iltimos, darhol yozing va menga tushuntiring — agar u juda jiddiy sabablarga ko'ra Lidiya zarur deb hisoblaganga o'xshagan sir saqlashda qolishi kerak bo'lmasa; u holda men bexabarlik bilan qanoatlanishga harakat qilishim kerak».

paras.en: “Not that I shall, though,” she added to herself, as she finished the letter; “and my dear aunt, if you do not tell me in an honourable manner, I shall certainly be reduced to tricks and stratagems to find it out.”
paras.uz: «Garchi qanoatlanmasam ham, — qo'shib qo'ydi u o'ziga, xatni tugatarkan. — Aziz xolajon, agar menga sharafli tarzda aytmasangiz, buni bilish uchun albatta hiyla va nayranglarga murojaat qilishga majbur bo'laman».

paras.en: Jane's delicate sense of honour would not allow her to speak to Elizabeth privately of what Lydia had let fall; Elizabeth was glad of it;--till it appeared whether her inquiries would receive any satisfaction, she had rather be without a confidante.
paras.uz: Jeynning nozik sharaf hissi unga Elizabet bilan Lidiya og'zidan chiqarib yuborgan narsa haqida yolg'iz gaplashishga yo'l qo'ymadi; Elizabet bundan xursand edi; — uning so'roqlari biror qoniqish oladimi, yo'qmi, ma'lum bo'lmaguncha, u sirdoshsiz bo'lishni afzal ko'rardi.

quiz.why_uz: Bu Elizabetni juda qiziqtiradi.

chapters.title: Mrs. Gardiner's Letter
chapters.recap_uz: Xola xatida haqiqatni yozadi: Darsi Lidiyani topgan, Uikhemning qarzlarini to'lagan va nikohni tashkil qilgan — lekin buni sir saqlashni so'ragan. Elizabet Darsidan cheksiz minnatdor.

paras.en: Elizabeth had the satisfaction of receiving an answer to her letter as soon as she possibly could. She was no sooner in possession of it than, hurrying into the little copse, where she was least likely to be interrupted, she sat down on one of the benches and prepared to be happy; for the length of the letter convinced her that it did not contain a denial.
paras.uz: Elizabet xatiga iloji boricha tez javob olish mamnuniyatiga ega bo'ldi. U uni qo'liga olishi bilanoq, eng kam bezovta qilinishi mumkin bo'lgan kichik daraxtzorga shoshilib, o'rindiqlardan biriga o'tirdi va baxtli bo'lishga tayyorlandi; chunki xatning uzunligi uni unda rad javob yo'qligiga ishontirdi.

paras.en: “Gracechurch street, Sept. 6.
paras.uz: «Greyschurch ko'chasi, 6-sentabr.

paras.en: “MY DEAR NIECE,
paras.uz: AZIZ JIYANIM,

paras.en: “I have just received your letter, and shall devote this whole morning to answering it, as I foresee that a little writing will not comprise what I have to tell you. I must confess myself surprised by your application; I did not expect it from you. Don't think me angry, however, for I only mean to let you know that I had not imagined such inquiries to be necessary on your side. If you do not choose to understand me, forgive my impertinence. Your uncle is as much surprised as I am--and nothing but the belief of your being a party concerned would have allowed him to act as he has done. But if you are really innocent and ignorant, I must be more explicit.
paras.uz: Hozirgina xatingni oldim va butun ertalabni unga javob berishga bag'ishlayman, chunki oldindan ko'ryapmanki, ozgina yozish senga aytadiganlarimni qamrab olmaydi. Tan olishim kerakki, murojaating meni hayratga soldi; buni sendan kutmagan edim. Biroq meni g'azablangan deb o'ylama, chunki men faqat sen tomondan bunday so'roqlar zarur deb tasavvur qilmaganimni bildirmoqchiman. Agar meni tushunishni istamasang, surbetligimni kechir. Tog'ang ham men kabi hayratda — va faqat sening ham ishtirokchi ekaningga ishonchgina unga qilganidek harakat qilishga imkon bergan bo'lardi. Lekin agar sen chindan ham beayb va bexabar bo'lsang, aniqroq gapirishim kerak.

paras.en: “On the very day of my coming home from Longbourn, your uncle had a most unexpected visitor. Mr. Darcy called, and was shut up with him several hours. It was all over before I arrived; so my curiosity was not so dreadfully racked as yours seems to have been. He came to tell Mr. Gardiner that he had found out where your sister and Mr. Wickham were, and that he had seen and talked with them both; Wickham repeatedly, Lydia once. From what I can collect, he left Derbyshire only one day after ourselves, and came to town with the resolution of hunting for them. The motive professed was his conviction of its being owing to himself that Wickham's worthlessness had not been so well known as to make it impossible for any young woman of character to love or confide in him.
paras.uz: Men Longborndan uyga qaytgan kunning o'zida tog'angga eng kutilmagan mehmon keldi. Janob Darsi kelib, u bilan bir necha soat yopilib o'tirdi. Men yetib kelgunimcha hammasi tugagan edi; shuning uchun mening qiziqishim seniki kabi dahshatli qiynalmadi. U janob Gardinerga singling va janob Uikhem qayerda ekanini topganini va ikkalasini ham ko'rib, ular bilan gaplashganini aytish uchun kelgan edi; Uikhem bilan bir necha marta, Lidiya bilan bir marta. To'plashimga ko'ra, u Derbishirni bizdan atigi bir kun keyin tark etgan va ularni qidirish qarori bilan Londonga kelgan.
