Bildirgan sababi shu ediki, Uikhemning arzimasligi hech bir obro'li yosh ayol uni sevishi yoki unga ishonishi imkonsiz bo'ladigan darajada yaxshi ma'lum bo'lmagani o'zining aybi deb ishongan.

paras.en: He generously imputed the whole to his mistaken pride, and confessed that he had before thought it beneath him to lay his private actions open to the world. His character was to speak for itself. He called it, therefore, his duty to step forward, and endeavour to remedy an evil which had been brought on by himself. If he had another motive, I am sure it would never disgrace him. He had been some days in town, before he was able to discover them; but he had something to direct his search, which was more than we had; and the consciousness of this was another reason for his resolving to follow us.
paras.uz: U saxiylik bilan hammasini o'zining noto'g'ri g'ururiga bog'ladi va avval o'z shaxsiy ishlarini dunyoga ochib berishni o'ziga ep ko'rmaganini tan oldi. Uning xarakteri o'zi uchun gapirishi kerak edi. Shuning uchun u o'zi keltirib chiqargan yomonlikni tuzatish uchun oldinga chiqib, harakat qilishni o'z burchi deb atadi. Agar uning boshqa sababi bo'lgan bo'lsa, ishonchim komilki, bu uni hech qachon sharmanda qilmasdi. U ularni topa olishidan oldin bir necha kun Londonda bo'ldi; lekin uning qidiruvini yo'naltiradigan biror narsasi bor edi, bu bizda bo'lganidan ko'proq edi; buni bilishi esa uning bizning ortimizdan borishga qaror qilishining yana bir sababi edi.

paras.en: “There is a lady, it seems, a Mrs. Younge, who was some time ago governess to Miss Darcy, and was dismissed from her charge on some cause of disapprobation, though he did not say what. She then took a large house in Edward-street, and has since maintained herself by letting lodgings. This Mrs. Younge was, he knew, intimately acquainted with Wickham; and he went to her for intelligence of him as soon as he got to town. But it was two or three days before he could get from her what he wanted. She would not betray her trust, I suppose, without bribery and corruption, for she really did know where her friend was to be found. Wickham indeed had gone to her on their first arrival in London, and had she been able to receive them into her house, they would have taken up their abode with her.
paras.uz: Aftidan, missis Yang ismli bir xonim bor ekan, u bir muncha vaqt oldin miss Darsining murabbiyasi bo'lgan va qandaydir norozilik sababi bilan vazifasidan bo'shatilgan, garchi u nima ekanini aytmagan bo'lsa ham. Keyin u Edvard ko'chasida katta uy olgan va o'shandan beri xonalarni ijaraga berib, kun ko'radi. U bu missis Yang Uikhem bilan yaqindan tanish ekanini bilardi; va Londonga yetib kelishi bilanoq u haqida ma'lumot olish uchun uning oldiga bordi. Lekin undan istaganini olishi uchun ikki-uch kun kerak bo'ldi. Menimcha, u pora va buzuqliksiz o'ziga bildirilgan ishonchga xiyonat qilmasdi, chunki u haqiqatan ham do'sti qayerda ekanini bilardi. Haqiqatan ham Uikhem Londonga birinchi kelganlarida uning oldiga borgan va agar u ularni uyiga qabul qila olganida, ular u bilan yashashgan bo'lardi.

paras.en: At length, however, our kind friend procured the wished-for direction. They were in ---- street. He saw Wickham, and afterwards insisted on seeing Lydia. His first object with her, he acknowledged, had been to persuade her to quit her present disgraceful situation, and return to her friends as soon as they could be prevailed on to receive her, offering his assistance, as far as it would go. But he found Lydia absolutely resolved on remaining where she was. She cared for none of her friends; she wanted no help of his; she would not hear of leaving Wickham. She was sure they should be married some time or other, and it did not much signify when. Since such were her feelings, it only remained, he thought, to secure and expedite a marriage, which, in his very first conversation with Wickham, he easily learnt had never been his design.
paras.uz: Biroq nihoyat mehribon do'stimiz kerakli manzilni qo'lga kiritdi. Ular ---- ko'chasida edi. U Uikhemni ko'rdi, keyin Lidiyani ko'rishni talab qildi. U tan oldiki, uning u bilan birinchi maqsadi uni hozirgi sharmandali ahvolini tark etishga va do'stlarini uni qabul qilishga ko'ndirish mumkin bo'lishi bilanoq ularga qaytishga ko'ndirish bo'lgan, qo'lidan kelgancha yordamini taklif qilgan. Lekin u Lidiyani turgan joyida qolishga mutlaqo qaror qilgan holda topdi. U hech bir do'stiga ahamiyat bermasdi; uning yordamini istamasdi; Uikhemni tashlab ketish haqida eshitishni ham istamasdi. U qachondir turmush qurishlariga amin edi va qachonligi unchalik muhim emasdi. Uning tuyg'ulari shunday bo'lgani uchun, uning o'ylashicha, faqat nikohni ta'minlash va tezlashtirish qolgan edi, Uikhem bilan birinchi suhbatidayoq u bu hech qachon uning niyati bo'lmaganini osongina bilib oldi.

paras.en: He confessed himself obliged to leave the regiment, on account of some debts of honour, which were very pressing; and scrupled not to lay all the ill-consequences of Lydia's flight on her own folly alone. He meant to resign his commission immediately; and as to his future situation, he could conjecture very little about it. He must go somewhere, but he did not know where, and he knew he should have nothing to live on.
paras.uz: U juda shoshilinch bo'lgan ba'zi sharaf qarzlari tufayli polkni tark etishga majbur ekanini tan oldi va Lidiyaning qochishining barcha yomon oqibatlarini faqat uning o'z ahmoqligiga yuklashdan tortinmadi. U darhol lavozimidan iste'foga chiqmoqchi edi; kelajakdagi ahvoliga kelsak, bu haqda juda kam taxmin qila olardi. U qayergadir borishi kerak edi, lekin qayerga ekanini bilmasdi va kun ko'rish uchun hech narsasi bo'lmasligini bilardi.

paras.en: “Mr. Darcy asked him why he had not married your sister at once. Though Mr. Bennet was not imagined to be very rich, he would have been able to do something for him, and his situation must have been benefited by marriage. But he found, in reply to this question, that Wickham still cherished the hope of more effectually making his fortune by marriage in some other country. Under such circumstances, however, he was not likely to be proof against the temptation of immediate relief.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi undan nega singlingga darhol uylanmaganini so'radi. Janob Bennet juda boy deb tasavvur qilinmasa ham, u uning uchun biror narsa qila olardi va uning ahvoli nikoh orqali yaxshilangan bo'lardi. Lekin bu savolga javoban u Uikhem hali ham boshqa mamlakatda nikoh orqali boyligini samaraliroq qilish umidini saqlashini bildi. Biroq bunday sharoitda u darhol yengillik vasvasasiga qarshi tura olishi ehtimoldan yiroq edi.

paras.en: “They met several times, for there was much to be discussed. Wickham of course wanted more than he could get; but at length was reduced to be reasonable.
paras.uz: Ular bir necha marta uchrashishdi, chunki muhokama qilinadigan ko'p narsa bor edi. Uikhem, albatta, ola oladiganidan ko'proq narsani xohlardi; lekin nihoyat oqilona bo'lishga majbur bo'ldi.

paras.en: “Every thing being settled between them, Mr. Darcy's next step was to make your uncle acquainted with it, and he first called in Gracechurch street the evening before I came home. But Mr. Gardiner could not be seen, and Mr. Darcy found, on further inquiry, that your father was still with him, but would quit town the next morning. He did not judge your father to be a person whom he could so properly consult as your uncle, and therefore readily postponed seeing him till after the departure of the former. He did not leave his name, and till the next day it was only known that a gentleman had called on business.
paras.uz: Ular o'rtasida hamma narsa hal bo'lgach, janob Darsining keyingi qadami tog'angni bundan xabardor qilish edi va u birinchi marta men uyga qaytishimdan oldingi kechqurun Greyschurch ko'chasiga keldi. Lekin janob Gardinerni ko'rib bo'lmadi va janob Darsi qo'shimcha so'roq qilib, otang hali ham u bilan ekanini, lekin ertasi kuni ertalab Londonni tark etishini bildi. U otangni tog'ang kabi munosib maslahatlashadigan odam deb hisoblamadi va shuning uchun birinchisi ketguncha u bilan uchrashishni tayyorlik bilan keyinga qoldirdi. U ismini qoldirmadi va ertasi kungacha faqat bir janob ish bilan kelgani ma'lum edi.

paras.en: “On Saturday he came again. Your father was gone, your uncle at home, and, as I said before, they had a great deal of talk together.
paras.uz: Shanba kuni u yana keldi. Otang ketgan, tog'ang uyda edi va avval aytganimdek, ular birga ko'p gaplashishdi.

paras.en: “They met again on Sunday, and then I saw him too. It was not all settled before Monday: as soon as it was, the express was sent off to Longbourn. But our visitor was very obstinate. I fancy, Lizzy, that obstinacy is the real defect of his character, after all. He has been accused of many faults at different times, but this is the true one. Nothing was to be done that he did not do himself; though I am sure (and I do not speak it to be thanked, therefore say nothing about it), your uncle would most readily have settled the whole.
paras.uz: Ular yakshanba kuni yana uchrashishdi, o'shanda men ham uni ko'rdim. Hammasi dushanbagacha hal bo'lmadi: hal bo'lishi bilanoq Longbornga shoshilinch xabarchi yuborildi. Lekin mehmonimiz juda o'jar edi. Menimcha, Lizzi, oxir-oqibat o'jarlik uning xarakterining haqiqiy kamchiligi. Uni turli vaqtlarda ko'p ayblarda ayblashgan, lekin haqiqiysi shu. O'zi qilmagan hech narsa qilinmasligi kerak edi; garchi ishonchim komilki (va buni minnatdorchilik olish uchun aytmayapman, shuning uchun bu haqda hech narsa dema), tog'ang hammasini eng tayyorlik bilan hal qilgan bo'lardi.

paras.en: “They battled it together for a long time, which was more than either the gentleman or lady concerned in it deserved. But at last your uncle was forced to yield, and instead of being allowed to be of use to his niece, was forced to put up with only having the probable credit of it, which went sorely against the grain; and I really believe your letter this morning gave him great pleasure, because it required an explanation that would rob him of his borrowed feathers, and give the praise where it was due. But, Lizzy, this must go no farther than yourself, or Jane at most.
paras.uz: Ular uzoq vaqt bu haqda bahslashishdi, bu esa unda ishtirok etgan janob ham, xonim ham loyiq bo'lganidan ko'proq edi. Lekin nihoyat tog'ang yon berishga majbur bo'ldi va jiyaniga foydali bo'lishga ruxsat berilish o'rniga, faqat buning ehtimoliy sharafiga ega bo'lish bilan qanoatlanishga majbur bo'ldi, bu esa uning ko'ngliga qattiq tegdi; va chin dildan ishonamanki, bugun ertalabgi xating unga katta zavq berdi, chunki u uning qarzga olingan patlarini tortib oladigan va maqtovni loyiq bo'lgan joyga beradigan tushuntirishni talab qildi. Lekin, Lizzi, bu sendan, ko'pi bilan Jeyndan nariga o'tmasligi kerak.

paras.en: “You know pretty well, I suppose, what has been done for the young people. His debts are to be paid, amounting, I believe, to considerably more than a thousand pounds, another thousand in addition to her own settled upon her, and his commission purchased. The reason why all this was to be done by him alone, was such as I have given above. It was owing to him, to his reserve and want of proper consideration, that Wickham's character had been so misunderstood, and consequently that he had been received and noticed as he was. Perhaps there was some truth in this; though I doubt whether his reserve, or anybody's reserve, can be answerable for the event. But in spite of all this fine talking, my dear Lizzy, you may rest perfectly assured that your uncle would never have yielded, if we had not given him credit for another interest in the affair.
paras.uz: O'ylaymanki, yoshlar uchun nima qilinganini ancha yaxshi bilasan. Uning qarzlari to'lanadi, ishonamanki, ular ming funtdan ancha ko'p, uning o'z sepiga qo'shimcha ravishda yana ming funt unga ajratiladi va uning lavozimi sotib olinadi. Bularning hammasi nega faqat u tomonidan qilinishi kerak bo'lganining sababi yuqorida aytganimdek. Uikhemning xarakteri bunchalik noto'g'ri tushunilgani va natijada u qanday qabul qilingan va e'tibor topgan bo'lsa, shunday bo'lgani uning, uning vazminligi va munosib e'tibor yetishmasligi tufayli edi. Ehtimol, bunda biroz haqiqat bordir; garchi uning vazminligi yoki biror kishining vazminligi voqea uchun javobgar bo'lishi mumkinligiga shubha qilsam ham. Lekin bu barcha chiroyli gaplarga qaramay, aziz Lizzi, mutlaqo ishonishing mumkinki, agar biz uni bu ishda boshqa qiziqishi bor deb hisoblamaganimizda, tog'ang hech qachon yon bermagan bo'lardi.

paras.en: “When all this was resolved on, he returned again to his friends, who were still staying at Pemberley; but it was agreed that he should be in London once more when the wedding took place, and all money matters were then to receive the last finish.
paras.uz: Bularning hammasi hal qilingach, u hali ham Pemberlida qolayotgan do'stlarining oldiga yana qaytdi; lekin to'y bo'lganda u yana bir marta Londonda bo'lishi va shunda barcha pul masalalari oxirgi yakunini olishi kelishildi.

paras.en: “I believe I have now told you every thing. It is a relation which you tell me is to give you great surprise; I hope at least it will not afford you any displeasure. Lydia came to us; and Wickham had constant admission to the house. He was exactly what he had been, when I knew him in Hertfordshire; but I would not tell you how little I was satisfied with her behaviour while she staid with us, if I had not perceived, by Jane's letter last Wednesday, that her conduct on coming home was exactly of a piece with it, and therefore what I now tell you can give you no fresh pain. I talked to her repeatedly in the most serious manner, representing to her all the wickedness of what she had done, and all the unhappiness she had brought on her family. If she heard me, it was by good luck, for I am sure she did not listen. I was sometimes quite provoked, but then I recollected my dear Elizabeth and Jane, and for their sakes had patience with her.
paras.uz: Menimcha, endi senga hamma narsani aytdim. Bu sen aytganingdek seni katta hayratga soladigan hikoya; umid qilamanki, hech bo'lmaganda senga norozilik keltirmaydi. Lidiya bizga keldi; Uikhem esa uyga doimiy kirib turardi. U men uni Xertfordshirda bilganimdek aynan o'sha edi; lekin agar Jeynning o'tgan chorshanba kungi xatidan uning uyga kelgandagi xatti-harakati aynan shunga o'xshash ekanini sezmaganimda, u biz bilan qolgan vaqtida uning xatti-harakatidan qanchalik kam qoniqqanimni senga aytmagan bo'lardim, shuning uchun hozir aytayotganlarim senga yangi og'riq bera olmaydi. Men u bilan qayta-qayta eng jiddiy tarzda gaplashdim, unga qilgan ishining butun yovuzligini va oilasiga keltirgan butun baxtsizlikni tushuntirdim. Agar u meni eshitgan bo'lsa, bu omad tufayli edi, chunki ishonchim komilki, u tinglamadi. Ba'zan juda g'ashim keldi, lekin keyin aziz Elizabetim va Jeynni eslab, ular uchun unga sabr qildim.

paras.en: “Mr. Darcy was punctual in his return, and as Lydia informed you, attended the wedding. He dined with us the next day, and was to leave town again on Wednesday or Thursday. Will you be very angry with me, my dear Lizzy, if I take this opportunity of saying (what I was never bold enough to say before) how much I like him. His behaviour to us has, in every respect, been as pleasing as when we were in Derbyshire. His understanding and opinions all please me; he wants nothing but a little more liveliness, and that, if he marry prudently, his wife may teach him. I thought him very sly;--he hardly ever mentioned your name. But slyness seems the fashion.
paras.uz: Janob Darsi aniq qaytib keldi va Lidiya senga aytganidek, to'yda qatnashdi. U ertasi kuni biz bilan tushlik qildi va chorshanba yoki payshanba kuni yana Londondan ketishi kerak edi. Agar bu imkoniyatdan foydalanib (ilgari hech qachon aytishga jur'atim yetmagan narsani) uni qanchalik yoqtirishimni aytsam, mendan juda g'azablanasanmi, aziz Lizzi? Uning bizga nisbatan xatti-harakati har jihatdan Derbishirda bo'lganimizdagidek yoqimli bo'ldi. Uning aqli va fikrlari hammasi menga yoqadi; unga faqat biroz ko'proq jo'shqinlik yetishmaydi, buni esa agar u oqilona uylansa, xotini unga o'rgatishi mumkin. Men uni juda ayyor deb o'yladim; — u sening ismingni deyarli hech qachon tilga olmadi. Lekin ayyorlik moda bo'lganga o'xshaydi.

paras.en: “Pray forgive me if I have been very presuming, or at least do not punish me so far as to exclude me from P. I shall never be quite happy till I have been all round the park. A low phaeton, with a nice little pair of ponies, would be the very thing.
paras.uz: Agar juda haddan oshgan bo'lsam, meni kechir yoki hech bo'lmaganda meni P.dan chetlatish darajasida jazolama. Men butun parkni aylanib chiqmagunimcha hech qachon to'liq baxtli bo'lmayman. Bir juft chiroyli kichkina poni qo'shilgan past faeton aynan kerakli narsa bo'lardi.

paras.en: “But I must write no more. The children have been wanting me this half hour.
paras.uz: Lekin boshqa yozmasligim kerak. Bolalar yarim soatdan beri meni chaqirishyapti.

paras.en: “Yours, very sincerely,
paras.uz: Juda samimiy seniki,

paras.en: “M. GARDINER.”
paras.uz: M. GARDINER».

paras.en: The contents of this letter threw Elizabeth into a flutter of spirits, in which it was difficult to determine whether pleasure or pain bore the greatest share. The vague and unsettled suspicions which uncertainty had produced of what Mr. Darcy might have been doing to forward her sister's match, which she had feared to encourage as an exertion of goodness too great to be probable, and at the same time dreaded to be just, from the pain of obligation, were proved beyond their greatest extent to be true!
paras.uz: Bu xatning mazmuni Elizabetni shunday ruhiy hayajonga soldiki, unda zavqmi yoki og'riqmi, qaysi biri katta ulushga ega ekanini aniqlash qiyin edi. Noaniqlik tug'dirgan, janob Darsi singlisining nikohini tezlashtirish uchun nima qilgan bo'lishi mumkinligi haqidagi noaniq va beqaror shubhalar — u ularni ehtimoldan yiroq bo'lgan haddan tashqari katta yaxshilik harakati sifatida rag'batlantirishdan qo'rqqan va shu bilan birga majburiyat og'rig'i tufayli adolatli bo'lishidan qo'rqqan edi — eng katta ko'lamidan ham ortiq darajada haqiqat ekani isbotlandi!

paras.en: He had followed them purposely to town, he had taken on himself all the trouble and mortification attendant on such a research; in which supplication had been necessary to a woman whom he must abominate and despise, and where he was reduced to meet, frequently meet, reason with, persuade, and finally bribe, the man whom he always most wished to avoid, and whose very name it was punishment to him to pronounce. He had done all this for a girl whom he could neither regard nor esteem. Her heart did whisper that he had done it for her. But it was a hope shortly checked by other considerations, and she soon felt that even her vanity was insufficient, when required to depend on his affection for her--for a woman who had already refused him--as able to overcome a sentiment so natural as abhorrence against relationship with Wickham. Brother-in-law of Wickham!
paras.uz: U ularning ortidan ataylab Londonga borgan, bunday qidiruvga hamroh bo'lgan barcha tashvish va xo'rlanishni o'z zimmasiga olgan edi; bunda u jirkanishi va nafratlanishi kerak bo'lgan ayoldan iltimos qilishi zarur bo'lgan va u doim eng ko'p qochishni istagan, nomini tilga olishning o'zi unga jazo bo'lgan erkak bilan uchrashishga, tez-tez uchrashishga, u bilan mantiqan gaplashishga, uni ko'ndirishga va oxir-oqibat unga pora berishga majbur bo'lgan edi. U bularning hammasini na hurmat qila oladigan, na qadrlay oladigan qiz uchun qilgan edi. Uning qalbi u buni o'zi uchun qilganini pichirlardi. Lekin bu tez orada boshqa mulohazalar bilan to'xtatilgan umid edi va u tez orada hatto shuhratparastligi ham uning o'ziga — uni allaqachon rad etgan ayolga — bo'lgan mehri Uikhem bilan qarindosh bo'lishdan nafratlanishdek tabiiy tuyg'uni yengishga qodir ekaniga tayanishi talab qilinganda yetarli emasligini his qildi. Uikhemning bajasi!

paras.en: Every kind of pride must revolt from the connection. He had, to be sure, done much. She was ashamed to think how much. But he had given a reason for his interference, which asked no extraordinary stretch of belief. It was reasonable that he should feel he had been wrong; he had liberality, and he had the means of exercising it; and though she would not place herself as his principal inducement, she could, perhaps, believe that remaining partiality for her might assist his endeavours in a cause where her peace of mind must be materially concerned. It was painful, exceedingly painful, to know that they were under obligations to a person who could never receive a return. They owed the restoration of Lydia, her character, every thing, to him.
paras.uz: Har qanday g'urur bunday qarindoshlikdan isyon qilishi kerak edi. U, albatta, ko'p narsa qilgan edi. U qanchalik ko'p ekanini o'ylashdan uyaldi. Lekin u aralashuvi uchun g'ayrioddiy ishonch talab qilmaydigan sabab ko'rsatgan edi. Uning o'zini noto'g'ri bo'lgan deb his qilishi oqilona edi; unda saxiylik bor edi va uni amalga oshirish vositalari bor edi; garchi u o'zini uning asosiy sababi deb hisoblamasa ham, ehtimol, unga nisbatan qolgan moyillik uning ruhiy osoyishtaligi jiddiy bog'liq bo'lgan ishda uning sa'y-harakatlariga yordam bergan bo'lishi mumkinligiga ishona olardi. Hech qachon qaytarib bo'lmaydigan odamga majburiyat ostida ekanliklarini bilish og'riqli, nihoyatda og'riqli edi. Ular Lidiyaning qaytarilishi, uning obro'si, hamma narsa uchun unga qarzdor edilar.

paras.en: Oh! how heartily did she grieve over every ungracious sensation she had ever encouraged, every saucy speech she had ever directed towards him. For herself she was humbled; but she was proud of him. Proud that in a cause of compassion and honour, he had been able to get the better of himself. She read over her aunt's commendation of him again and again. It was hardly enough; but it pleased her. She was even sensible of some pleasure, though mixed with regret, on finding how steadfastly both she and her uncle had been persuaded that affection and confidence subsisted between Mr. Darcy and herself.
paras.uz: Oh! U unga nisbatan qachondir rag'batlantirgan har bir iltifotsiz tuyg'u, qachondir unga qaratgan har bir surbet so'z uchun qanchalik chin dildan qayg'urdi. O'zi uchun u kamsitilgan edi; lekin u bilan faxrlanardi. U hamdardlik va sharaf ishida o'zini yenga olgani bilan faxrlanardi. U xolasining uni maqtashini qayta-qayta o'qidi. Bu zo'rg'a yetarli edi; lekin bu unga yoqdi. U hatto o'zi ham, tog'asi ham janob Darsi bilan o'zi o'rtasida mehr va ishonch borligiga qanchalik qat'iy ishonganini bilib, afsus bilan aralash bo'lsa ham, biroz zavq his qildi.

paras.en: She was roused from her seat, and her reflections, by some one's approach; and before she could strike into another path, she was overtaken by Wickham.
paras.uz: Uni o'rindig'idan va mulohazalaridan kimningdir yaqinlashishi hushyor tortdi; va u boshqa yo'lakka burilishga ulgurmasdan, Uikhem unga yetib oldi.

paras.en: “I am afraid I interrupt your solitary ramble, my dear sister?” said he, as he joined her.
paras.uz: «Qo'rqamanki, yolg'iz sayringizni buzdim, aziz singlim?» — dedi u, unga qo'shilarkan.

paras.en: “You certainly do,” she replied with a smile; “but it does not follow that the interruption must be unwelcome.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, buzdingiz, — javob berdi u jilmayib, — lekin bundan halal berish yoqimsiz bo'lishi kerak degan xulosa kelib chiqmaydi».

paras.en: “I should be sorry indeed, if it were. We were always good friends; and now we are better.”
paras.uz: «Agar shunday bo'lganida, haqiqatan ham afsuslanardim. Biz doim yaxshi do'st edik; endi esa bundan ham yaxshiroqmiz».

paras.en: “True. Are the others coming out?”
paras.uz: «To'g'ri. Boshqalar ham chiqishyaptimi?»

paras.en: “I do not know. Mrs. Bennet and Lydia are going in the carriage to Meryton. And so, my dear sister, I find, from our uncle and aunt, that you have actually seen Pemberley.”
paras.uz: «Bilmayman. Missis Bennet va Lidiya aravada Meritonga ketishyapti. Xo'sh, aziz singlim, tog'amiz va xolamizdan bilishimcha, siz haqiqatan ham Pemberlini ko'ribsiz».

paras.en: She replied in the affirmative.
paras.uz: U tasdiqlab javob berdi.

paras.en: “I almost envy you the pleasure, and yet I believe it would be too much for me, or else I could take it in my way to Newcastle. And you saw the old housekeeper, I suppose? Poor Reynolds, she was always very fond of me. But of course she did not mention my name to you.”
paras.uz: «Bu zavq uchun sizga deyarli hasad qilaman, lekin menimcha, bu men uchun haddan tashqari og'ir bo'lardi, aks holda Nyukaslga ketayotib yo'lda kirib o'tishim mumkin edi. Keksa uy bekasini ham ko'rgan bo'lsangiz kerak? Bechora Reynolds, u meni doim juda yaxshi ko'rardi. Lekin, albatta, u sizga mening nomimni tilga olmagan».

paras.en: “Yes, she did.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, tilga oldi».

paras.en: “And what did she say?”
paras.uz: «Nima dedi?»

paras.en: “That you were gone into the army, and she was afraid had--not turned out well. At such a distance as that, you know, things are strangely misrepresented.”
paras.uz: «Siz armiyaga ketganingizni va qo'rqadiki, siz... yaxshi chiqmagansiz. Bilasizmi, bunchalik uzoq masofada narsalar g'alati tarzda noto'g'ri tasvirlanadi».

paras.en: “Certainly,” he replied, biting his lips. Elizabeth hoped she had silenced him; but he soon afterwards said:
paras.uz: «Albatta», — javob berdi u, labini tishlab. Elizabet uni jim qildirdim deb umid qildi; lekin u ko'p o'tmay dedi:

paras.en: “I was surprised to see Darcy in town last month. We passed each other several times. I wonder what he can be doing there.”
paras.uz: «O'tgan oy Darsini Londonda ko'rib hayron bo'ldim. Biz bir necha marta bir-birimiz yonidan o'tdik. Qiziq, u yerda nima qilayotgan ekan».

paras.en: “Perhaps preparing for his marriage with Miss de Bourgh,” said Elizabeth. “It must be something particular, to take him there at this time of year.”
paras.uz: «Ehtimol, miss de Burg bilan nikohiga tayyorlanayotgandir, — dedi Elizabet. — Uni yilning bu faslida u yerga olib borgan narsa qandaydir alohida narsa bo'lsa kerak».

paras.en: “Undoubtedly. Did you see him while you were at Lambton? I thought I understood from the Gardiners that you had.”
paras.uz: «Shubhasiz. Lembtonda bo'lganingizda uni ko'rdingizmi? Gardinerlardan shunday tushungandek bo'ldim».

paras.en: “Yes; he introduced us to his sister.”
paras.uz: «Ha; u bizni singlisi bilan tanishtirdi».

paras.en: “And do you like her?”
paras.uz: «U sizga yoqdimi?»

paras.en: “Very much.”
paras.uz: «Juda».

paras.en: “I have heard, indeed, that she is uncommonly improved within this year or two. When I last saw her, she was not very promising. I am very glad you liked her. I hope she will turn out well.”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham eshitdimki, u so'nggi bir-ikki yil ichida g'ayrioddiy darajada yaxshilangan. Uni oxirgi marta ko'rganimda, unchalik istiqbolli emasdi. Uni yoqtirganingizdan juda xursandman. Umid qilamanki, u yaxshi chiqadi».

paras.en: “I dare say she will; she has got over the most trying age.”
paras.uz: «Ishonamanki, chiqadi; u eng qiyin yoshdan o'tib oldi».

paras.en: “Did you go by the village of Kympton?”
paras.uz: «Kimpton qishlog'i orqali o'tdingizmi?»

paras.en: “I do not recollect that we did.”
paras.uz: «O'tganimizni eslay olmayman».

paras.en: “I mention it, because it is the living which I ought to have had. A most delightful place!--Excellent Parsonage House! It would have suited me in every respect.”
paras.uz: «Buni aytayotganimning sababi, bu men olishim kerak bo'lgan ruhoniylik lavozimi. Eng ajoyib joy! — A'lo ruhoniy uyi! U menga har jihatdan mos kelgan bo'lardi».

paras.en: “How should you have liked making sermons?”
paras.uz: «Va'z yozish sizga qanchalik yoqqan bo'lardi?»

paras.en: “Exceedingly well. I should have considered it as part of my duty, and the exertion would soon have been nothing. One ought not to repine;--but, to be sure, it would have been such a thing for me! The quiet, the retirement of such a life would have answered all my ideas of happiness! But it was not to be. Did you ever hear Darcy mention the circumstance, when you were in Kent?”
paras.uz: «Nihoyatda yaxshi. Men buni burchimning bir qismi deb hisoblagan bo'lardim va bu harakat tez orada hech narsa bo'lmay qolardi. Nolimaslik kerak; — lekin, albatta, bu men uchun shunday narsa bo'lardi! Bunday hayotning osoyishtaligi, xilvatligi baxt haqidagi barcha tasavvurlarimga javob bergan bo'lardi! Lekin bunday bo'lmasligi kerak ekan. Kentda bo'lganingizda Darsining bu holatni tilga olganini hech eshitganmisiz?»

paras.en: “I have heard from authority, which I thought as good, that it was left you conditionally only, and at the will of the present patron.”
paras.uz: «Men xuddi shunday ishonchli deb hisoblagan manbadan eshitdimki, u sizga faqat shartli ravishda va hozirgi homiyning xohishiga ko'ra qoldirilgan ekan».

paras.en: “You have. Yes, there was something in that; I told you so from the first, you may remember.”
paras.uz: «Eshitgansiz. Ha, bunda nimadir bor edi; esingizda bo'lsa, buni sizga boshidanoq aytgan edim».

paras.en: “I did hear, too, that there was a time, when sermon-making was not so palatable to you as it seems to be at present; that you actually declared your resolution of never taking orders, and that the business had been compromised accordingly.”
paras.uz: «Shuningdek eshitdimki, bir paytlar va'z yozish sizga hozirgidek unchalik yoqimli bo'lmagan ekan; siz haqiqatan ham hech qachon ruhoniylikni qabul qilmaslik qaroringizni e'lon qilgansiz va ish shunga ko'ra kelishuv bilan hal qilingan».

paras.en: “You did! and it was not wholly without foundation. You may remember what I told you on that point, when first we talked of it.”
paras.uz: «Eshitgansiz! Bu ham butunlay asossiz emasdi. Esingizda bo'lsa, bu haqda birinchi gaplashganimizda nima deganimni».

paras.en: They were now almost at the door of the house, for she had walked fast to get rid of him; and unwilling, for her sister's sake, to provoke him, she only said in reply, with a good-humoured smile:
paras.uz: Endi ular deyarli uyning eshigi oldida edi, chunki u undan qutulish uchun tez yurgan edi; va singlisi xotiri uchun uni g'azablantirishni istamay, faqat xushfe'l tabassum bilan javob berdi:

paras.en: “Come, Mr. Wickham, we are brother and sister, you know. Do not let us quarrel about the past. In future, I hope we shall be always of one mind.”
paras.uz: «Qo'ying, janob Uikhem, bilasizmi, biz endi qarindoshmiz. O'tmish haqida janjallashmaylik. Kelajakda, umid qilamanki, doim hamfikr bo'lamiz».

paras.en: She held out her hand; he kissed it with affectionate gallantry, though he hardly knew how to look, and they entered the house.
paras.uz: U qo'lini uzatdi; u qanday qarashni zo'rg'a bilsa ham, uni mehrli xushomad bilan o'pdi va ular uyga kirishdi.

gloss.ex: She would not betray her trust, I suppose, without bribery and corruption, for she really did know where her friend was to be found.
For herself she was humbled; but she was proud of him.
The motive professed was his conviction of its being owing to himself that Wickham's worthlessness had not been so well known as to make it impossible for any young woman…
He had followed them purposely to town, he had taken on himself all the trouble and mortification attendant on such a research; in which supplication had been necessary to a…
Under such circumstances, however, he was not likely to be proof against the temptation of immediate relief.
If you do not choose to understand me, forgive my impertinence.
His first object with her, he acknowledged, had been to persuade her to quit her present disgraceful situation, and return to her friends as soon as they could be prevailed…

quiz.q: Who really arranged Lydia's marriage?
quiz.why_uz: Darsi buni Elizabet uchun qilgan.

quiz.q: Why did Darcy feel responsible?
o: He had not exposed Wickham's character earlier
quiz.why_uz: U o'z g'ururi tufayli Uikhemni fosh qilmaganini ayb deb biladi.

chapters.title: Bingley Returns
chapters.recap_uz: Uikhem va Lidiya ketishadi. Bingley Netherfieldga qaytadi va Darsi bilan Longbournga keladi. Darsi jim va o'ychan; Bingley yana Jeynga mehr ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: Mr. Wickham was so perfectly satisfied with this conversation that he never again distressed himself, or provoked his dear sister Elizabeth, by introducing the subject of it; and she was pleased to find that she had said enough to keep him quiet.
paras.uz: Janob Uikhem bu suhbatdan shunchalik to'liq qoniqdiki, boshqa hech qachon uning mavzusini qo'zg'ab, o'zini qiynamadi yoki aziz singlisi Elizabetning g'ashini keltirmadi; Elizabet esa uni jim tutish uchun yetarlicha gapirganini bilib xursand bo'ldi.

paras.en: The day of his and Lydia's departure soon came, and Mrs. Bennet was forced to submit to a separation, which, as her husband by no means entered into her scheme of their all going to Newcastle, was likely to continue at least a twelvemonth.
paras.uz: Uning va Lidiyaning ketish kuni tez keldi va missis Bennet ajralishga bo'ysunishga majbur bo'ldi, eri hammalari Nyukaslga borish rejasiga umuman qo'shilmagani uchun, bu ajralish kamida bir yil davom etishi ehtimoli bor edi.

paras.en: “Oh! my dear Lydia,” she cried, “when shall we meet again?”
paras.uz: «Oh! Aziz Lidiyam, — xitob qildi u, — qachon yana uchrashamiz?»

paras.en: “Oh, lord! I don't know. Not these two or three years, perhaps.”
paras.uz: «Oh, Xudoyim! Bilmayman. Ehtimol, ikki-uch yilgacha emas».

paras.en: “Write to me very often, my dear.”
paras.uz: «Menga juda tez-tez xat yoz, azizim».

paras.en: “As often as I can. But you know married women have never much time for writing. My sisters may write to me. They will have nothing else to do.”
paras.uz: «Iloji boricha tez-tez. Lekin bilasizmi, turmush qurgan ayollarning xat yozishga hech qachon ko'p vaqti bo'lmaydi. Opalarim menga yozishlari mumkin. Ularning boshqa qiladigan ishi bo'lmaydi».

paras.en: Mr. Wickham's adieus were much more affectionate than his wife's. He smiled, looked handsome, and said many pretty things.
paras.uz: Janob Uikhemning xayrlashuvi xotininikidan ancha mehrliroq edi. U jilmaydi, chiroyli ko'rindi va ko'p yoqimli gaplar aytdi.

paras.en: “He is as fine a fellow,” said Mr. Bennet, as soon as they were out of the house, “as ever I saw. He simpers, and smirks, and makes love to us all. I am prodigiously proud of him. I defy even Sir William Lucas himself to produce a more valuable son-in-law.”
paras.uz: «U men ko'rgan eng zo'r yigit, — dedi janob Bennet, ular uydan chiqishlari bilanoq. — U tirjayadi, iljayadi va hammamizga xushomad qiladi. Undan nihoyatda faxrlanaman. Hatto ser Uilyam Lukasning o'zini ham bundan qimmatliroq kuyov ko'rsatishga chaqiraman».

paras.en: The loss of her daughter made Mrs. Bennet very dull for several days.
paras.uz: Qizidan ayrilish missis Bennetni bir necha kun davomida juda zeriktirdi.

paras.en: “I often think,” said she, “that there is nothing so bad as parting with one's friends. One seems so forlorn without them.”
paras.uz: «Ko'pincha o'ylayman, — dedi u, — do'stlar bilan ajralishdan yomonroq narsa yo'q. Ularsiz odam shunchalik tashlandiq ko'rinadi».

paras.en: “This is the consequence, you see, Madam, of marrying a daughter,” said Elizabeth. “It must make you better satisfied that your other four are single.”
paras.uz: «Ko'ryapsizmi, xonim, bu qizni erga berishning oqibati, — dedi Elizabet. — Bu sizni qolgan to'rttangiz turmushga chiqmaganidan ko'proq qoniqtirishi kerak».

paras.en: “It is no such thing. Lydia does not leave me because she is married, but only because her husband's regiment happens to be so far off. If that had been nearer, she would not have gone so soon.”
paras.uz: «Bunday emas. Lidiya meni turmushga chiqqani uchun emas, balki faqat erining polki tasodifan shunchalik uzoqda bo'lgani uchun tark etyapti. Agar u yaqinroq bo'lganida, u bunchalik tez ketmasdi».

paras.en: But the spiritless condition which this event threw her into was shortly relieved, and her mind opened again to the agitation of hope, by an article of news which then began to be in circulation. The housekeeper at Netherfield had received orders to prepare for the arrival of her master, who was coming down in a day or two, to shoot there for several weeks. Mrs. Bennet was quite in the fidgets. She looked at Jane, and smiled and shook her head by turns.
paras.uz: Lekin bu voqea uni solgan ruhsiz holat tez orada o'sha paytda tarqala boshlagan yangilik tufayli yengillashdi va uning ongi yana umid hayajoniga ochildi. Nezerfilddagi uy bekasi bir-ikki kunda kelib, u yerda bir necha hafta ov qiladigan xo'jayinining kelishiga tayyorlanish haqida buyruq olgan edi. Missis Bennet butunlay bezovta bo'ldi. U Jeynga qaradi va navbatma-navbat jilmaydi va boshini chayqadi.

paras.en: “Well, well, and so Mr. Bingley is coming down, sister,” (for Mrs. Phillips first brought her the news). “Well, so much the better. Not that I care about it, though. He is nothing to us, you know, and I am sure I never want to see him again. But, however, he is very welcome to come to Netherfield, if he likes it. And who knows what may happen? But that is nothing to us. You know, sister, we agreed long ago never to mention a word about it. And so, is it quite certain he is coming?”
paras.uz: «Mayli, mayli, demak janob Bingli kelyapti, opa, — (chunki bu xabarni unga birinchi bo'lib missis Fillips keltirgan edi). — Mayli, shunisi yaxshi. Garchi bunga ahamiyat bermasam ham. Bilasizmi, u biz uchun hech kim emas va ishonchim komilki, uni boshqa hech qachon ko'rishni istamayman. Lekin baribir, agar xohlasa, Nezerfildga kelishiga xush kelibdi. Kim biladi, nima bo'lishi mumkin? Lekin bu bizga tegishli emas. Bilasizmi, opa, biz ancha oldin bu haqda bir og'iz ham gapirmaslikka kelishganmiz. Demak, uning kelishi butunlay aniqmi?»

paras.en: “You may depend on it,” replied the other, “for Mrs. Nicholls was in Meryton last night; I saw her passing by, and went out myself on purpose to know the truth of it; and she told me that it was certain true. He comes down on Thursday at the latest, very likely on Wednesday. She was going to the butcher's, she told me, on purpose to order in some meat on Wednesday, and she has got three couple of ducks just fit to be killed.”
paras.uz: «Ishonishingiz mumkin, — javob berdi ikkinchisi, — chunki missis Nikolls kecha kechqurun Meritonda edi; uning o'tib ketayotganini ko'rdim va haqiqatni bilish uchun ataylab o'zim chiqdim; u menga bu aniq rost ekanini aytdi. U eng kechi bilan payshanba kuni keladi, ehtimol chorshanba kuni. Uning aytishicha, u chorshanbaga biroz go'sht buyurtma berish uchun ataylab qassobnikiga ketayotgan edi va uning so'yishga tayyor uch juft o'rdagi bor».

paras.en: Miss Bennet had not been able to hear of his coming without changing colour. It was many months since she had mentioned his name to Elizabeth; but now, as soon as they were alone together, she said:
paras.uz: Miss Bennet uning kelishi haqida rangi o'zgarmasdan eshita olmadi. U Elizabetga uning nomini tilga olmaganiga ko'p oylar bo'lgan edi; lekin endi, ular yolg'iz qolishlari bilanoq, u dedi:

paras.en: “I saw you look at me to-day, Lizzy, when my aunt told us of the present report; and I know I appeared distressed. But don't imagine it was from any silly cause. I was only confused for the moment, because I felt that I should be looked at. I do assure you that the news does not affect me either with pleasure or pain. I am glad of one thing, that he comes alone; because we shall see the less of him. Not that I am afraid of myself, but I dread other people's remarks.”
paras.uz: «Bugun xolam bizga hozirgi mish-mish haqida aytganda, menga qaraganingni ko'rdim, Lizzi; bilaman, men xijolatda ko'rindim. Lekin buni biror ahmoqona sababdan deb o'ylama. Men faqat bir lahza sarosimaga tushdim, chunki menga qarashlarini his qildim. Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, bu xabar menga na zavq, na og'riq bilan ta'sir qiladi. Bir narsadan xursandman, u yolg'iz kelyapti; chunki biz uni kamroq ko'ramiz. O'zimdan qo'rqqanim uchun emas, lekin boshqa odamlarning gaplaridan qo'rqaman».

paras.en: Elizabeth did not know what to make of it. Had she not seen him in Derbyshire, she might have supposed him capable of coming there with no other view than what was acknowledged; but she still thought him partial to Jane, and she wavered as to the greater probability of his coming there with his friend's permission, or being bold enough to come without it.
paras.uz: Elizabet bu haqda nima deb o'ylashni bilmadi. Agar uni Derbishirda ko'rmaganida, uni tan olingandan boshqa hech qanday maqsadsiz u yerga kelishga qodir deb taxmin qilishi mumkin edi; lekin u hali ham uni Jeynga moyil deb o'ylardi va uning u yerga do'stining ruxsati bilan kelishi yoki usiz kelishga yetarlicha jasur bo'lishi qaysi biri ehtimolroq ekani haqida ikkilanardi.

paras.en: “Yet it is hard,” she sometimes thought, “that this poor man cannot come to a house which he has legally hired, without raising all this speculation! I will leave him to himself.”
paras.uz: «Shunga qaramay, bu og'ir, — deb o'ylardi u ba'zan, — bu bechora odam qonuniy ijaraga olgan uyga bularning hammasini taxmin qilishga sabab bo'lmasdan kela olmasligi! Uni o'z holiga qo'yaman».

paras.en: In spite of what her sister declared, and really believed to be her feelings in the expectation of his arrival, Elizabeth could easily perceive that her spirits were affected by it. They were more disturbed, more unequal, than she had often seen them.
paras.uz: Opasi uning kelishini kutishdagi tuyg'ulari deb e'lon qilgan va chindan ishongan narsaga qaramay, Elizabet uning kayfiyatiga bu ta'sir qilganini osongina sezdi. Ular u tez-tez ko'rganidan ko'ra bezovtaroq, notekisroq edi.

paras.en: The subject which had been so warmly canvassed between their parents, about a twelvemonth ago, was now brought forward again.
paras.uz: Taxminan bir yil oldin ota-onalari o'rtasida shunchalik qizg'in muhokama qilingan mavzu endi yana ko'tarildi.

paras.en: “As soon as ever Mr. Bingley comes, my dear,” said Mrs. Bennet, “you will wait on him of course.”
paras.uz: «Janob Bingli kelishi bilanoq, azizim, — dedi missis Bennet, — siz, albatta, uning huzuriga borasiz».

paras.en: “No, no. You forced me into visiting him last year, and promised, if I went to see him, he should marry one of my daughters. But it ended in nothing, and I will not be sent on a fool's errand again.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, yo'q. O'tgan yili meni uning oldiga borishga majbur qildingiz va agar uni ko'rgani borsam, u qizlarimdan biriga uylanishini va'da qildingiz. Lekin bu hech narsa bilan tugadi va men yana ahmoqona topshiriqqa jo'natilmayman».

paras.en: His wife represented to him how absolutely necessary such an attention would be from all the neighbouring gentlemen, on his returning to Netherfield.
paras.uz: Xotini unga janob Bingli Nezerfildga qaytganda qo'shni janoblarning barchasidan bunday e'tibor qanchalik mutlaqo zarur ekanini tushuntirdi.

paras.en: “'Tis an etiquette I despise,” said he. “If he wants our society, let him seek it. He knows where we live. I will not spend my hours in running after my neighbours every time they go away and come back again.”
paras.uz: «Bu men nafratlanadigan odob qoidasi, — dedi u. — Agar u bizning davramizni istasa, o'zi izlasin. U qayerda yashashimizni biladi. Qo'shnilarim har safar ketib, qaytib kelganda ularning ortidan yugurib, soatlarimni sarflamayman».

paras.en: “Well, all I know is, that it will be abominably rude if you do not wait on him. But, however, that shan't prevent my asking him to dine here, I am determined. We must have Mrs. Long and the Gouldings soon. That will make thirteen with ourselves, so there will be just room at table for him.”
paras.uz: «Mayli, mening bilganim shuki, agar uning huzuriga bormasangiz, bu jirkanch darajada qo'pollik bo'ladi. Lekin baribir bu meni uni bu yerga tushlikka taklif qilishimdan to'xtata olmaydi, qaror qildim. Biz tez orada missis Long va Gouldinglarni taklif qilishimiz kerak. Bu biz bilan o'n uch kishi bo'ladi, shuning uchun stolda unga aynan joy qoladi».

paras.en: Consoled by this resolution, she was the better able to bear her husband's incivility; though it was very mortifying to know that her neighbours might all see Mr. Bingley, in consequence of it, before they did. As the day of his arrival drew near,--
paras.uz: Bu qarordan taskin topib, u erining xushmuomalasizligiga yaxshiroq chiday oldi; garchi buning natijasida qo'shnilarining hammasi janob Binglini ulardan oldin ko'rishi mumkinligini bilish juda xo'rlovchi bo'lsa ham. Uning kelish kuni yaqinlashgani sari...

paras.en: “I begin to be sorry that he comes at all,” said Jane to her sister. “It would be nothing; I could see him with perfect indifference, but I can hardly bear to hear it thus perpetually talked of. My mother means well; but she does not know, no one can know, how much I suffer from what she says. Happy shall I be, when his stay at Netherfield is over!”
paras.uz: «Uning umuman kelayotganidan afsuslana boshladim, — dedi Jeyn singlisiga. — Bu hech narsa bo'lmasdi; uni mutlaq befarqlik bilan ko'ra olardim, lekin bu haqda doimo shunday gapirilishini eshitishga zo'rg'a chiday olaman. Onam yaxshi niyatda; lekin u bilmaydi, hech kim bilmaydi, uning gaplaridan qanchalik azob chekishimni. Uning Nezerfilddagi qolishi tugaganda qanchalik baxtli bo'laman!»

paras.en: “I wish I could say anything to comfort you,” replied Elizabeth; “but it is wholly out of my power. You must feel it; and the usual satisfaction of preaching patience to a sufferer is denied me, because you have always so much.”
paras.uz: «Seni yupatadigan biror narsa ayta olsam edi, — javob berdi Elizabet, — lekin bu butunlay qo'limdan kelmaydi. Sen buni his qilishing kerak; azob chekayotganga sabr haqida va'z o'qishning odatiy mamnuniyati esa menga nasib etmagan, chunki senda doim sabr shunchalik ko'p».

paras.en: Mr. Bingley arrived. Mrs. Bennet, through the assistance of servants, contrived to have the earliest tidings of it, that the period of anxiety and fretfulness on her side might be as long as it could. She counted the days that must intervene before their invitation could be sent; hopeless of seeing him before. But on the third morning after his arrival in Hertfordshire, she saw him, from her dressing-room window, enter the paddock and ride towards the house.
paras.uz: Janob Bingli keldi. Missis Bennet xizmatkorlar yordamida bu haqda eng birinchi xabar olishni uddaladi, toki o'z tomonidagi tashvish va bezovtalik davri iloji boricha uzoq bo'lsin. U taklifnomalari yuborilishi mumkin bo'lgunga qadar o'tishi kerak bo'lgan kunlarni sanadi; undan oldin uni ko'rishdan umidini uzgan edi. Lekin u Xertfordshirga kelganining uchinchi kuni ertalab u kiyinish xonasining derazasidan uning hovliga kirib, uy tomon otda kelayotganini ko'rdi.

paras.en: Her daughters were eagerly called to partake of her joy. Jane resolutely kept her place at the table; but Elizabeth, to satisfy her mother, went to the window--she looked,--she saw Mr. Darcy with him, and sat down again by her sister.
paras.uz: Qizlari uning quvonchiga sherik bo'lish uchun ishtiyoq bilan chaqirildi. Jeyn qat'iyat bilan stoldagi joyida qoldi; lekin Elizabet onasini qoniqtirish uchun deraza oldiga bordi — u qaradi — u bilan birga janob Darsini ko'rdi va yana opasining yoniga o'tirdi.

paras.en: “There is a gentleman with him, mamma,” said Kitty; “who can it be?”
paras.uz: «U bilan birga bir janob bor, oyijon, — dedi Ketti. — Kim bo'lishi mumkin?»

paras.en: “Some acquaintance or other, my dear, I suppose; I am sure I do not know.”
paras.uz: «Qandaydir tanishi bo'lsa kerak, azizim; ishonchim komilki, bilmayman».

paras.en: “La!” replied Kitty, “it looks just like that man that used to be with him before. Mr. what's-his-name. That tall, proud man.”
paras.uz: «Voy! — javob berdi Ketti. — U avval u bilan birga yuradigan o'sha odamga juda o'xshaydi. Janob falonchi. O'sha baland bo'yli, mag'rur odam».

paras.en: “Good gracious! Mr. Darcy!--and so it does, I vow. Well, any friend of Mr. Bingley's will always be welcome here, to be sure; but else I must say that I hate the very sight of him.”
paras.uz: «Yo xudo! Janob Darsi! — qasamki, aynan shunday. Mayli, janob Binglining har qanday do'sti bu yerda doim xush kelgan bo'ladi, albatta; lekin aks holda aytishim kerakki, uning ko'rinishining o'zidan nafratlanaman».

paras.en: Jane looked at Elizabeth with surprise and concern. She knew but little of their meeting in Derbyshire, and therefore felt for the awkwardness which must attend her sister, in seeing him almost for the first time after receiving his explanatory letter. Both sisters were uncomfortable enough. Each felt for the other, and of course for themselves; and their mother talked on, of her dislike of Mr. Darcy, and her resolution to be civil to him only as Mr. Bingley's friend, without being heard by either of them. But Elizabeth had sources of uneasiness which could not be suspected by Jane, to whom she had never yet had courage to shew Mrs. Gardiner's letter, or to relate her own change of sentiment towards him.
paras.uz: Jeyn Elizabetga hayrat va tashvish bilan qaradi. U ularning Derbishirdagi uchrashuvi haqida juda kam bilardi va shuning uchun uning tushuntiruvchi xatini olgandan keyin uni deyarli birinchi marta ko'rishda singlisiga hamroh bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan noqulaylikni his qildi. Ikkala opa-singil ham yetarlicha noqulay edi. Har biri boshqasi uchun, albatta, o'zi uchun ham his qilardi; onalari esa janob Darsini yoqtirmasligi va unga faqat janob Binglining do'sti sifatida xushmuomala bo'lish qarori haqida ularning hech biri eshitmagan holda gapirishda davom etdi. Lekin Elizabetda Jeyn gumon qila olmaydigan bezovtalik manbalari bor edi, u unga hali hech qachon missis Gardinerning xatini ko'rsatishga yoki unga nisbatan o'z tuyg'ularining o'zgarishini aytib berishga jur'at etmagan edi.

paras.en: To Jane, he could be only a man whose proposals she had refused, and whose merit she had undervalued; but to her own more extensive information, he was the person to whom the whole family were indebted for the first of benefits, and whom she regarded herself with an interest, if not quite so tender, at least as reasonable and just as what Jane felt for Bingley. Her astonishment at his coming--at his coming to Netherfield, to Longbourn, and voluntarily seeking her again, was almost equal to what she had known on first witnessing his altered behaviour in Derbyshire.
paras.uz: Jeyn uchun u faqat singlisi taklifini rad etgan va fazilatini kam baholagan erkak bo'lishi mumkin edi; lekin uning o'zining kengroq ma'lumotiga ko'ra, u butun oila birinchi darajali yaxshilik uchun qarzdor bo'lgan va unga o'zi Jeynning Binglige bo'lgan tuyg'usidek unchalik nozik bo'lmasa ham, hech bo'lmaganda xuddi shunday oqilona va adolatli qiziqish bilan qaraydigan shaxs edi. Uning kelishidan — Nezerfildga, Longbornga kelishidan va o'z ixtiyori bilan uni yana izlashidan hayrati Derbishirda uning o'zgargan xatti-harakatiga birinchi guvoh bo'lgandagi hayratiga deyarli teng edi.

paras.en: The colour which had been driven from her face, returned for half a minute with an additional glow, and a smile of delight added lustre to her eyes, as she thought for that space of time that his affection and wishes must still be unshaken. But she would not be secure.
paras.uz: Yuzidan qochgan rang yarim daqiqaga qo'shimcha porlash bilan qaytdi va o'sha vaqt davomida uning mehri va istaklari hali ham chayqalmagan bo'lishi kerak, deb o'ylarkan, zavq tabassumi ko'zlariga jilo qo'shdi. Lekin u ishonchga berilmadi.

paras.en: “Let me first see how he behaves,” said she; “it will then be early enough for expectation.”
paras.uz: «Avval uning o'zini qanday tutishini ko'ray, — dedi u, — shunda kutish uchun yetarlicha vaqt bo'ladi».

paras.en: She sat intently at work, striving to be composed, and without daring to lift up her eyes, till anxious curiosity carried them to the face of her sister as the servant was approaching the door. Jane looked a little paler than usual, but more sedate than Elizabeth had expected. On the gentlemen's appearing, her colour increased; yet she received them with tolerable ease, and with a propriety of behaviour equally free from any symptom of resentment or any unnecessary complaisance.
paras.uz: U xotirjam bo'lishga intilib, ko'zlarini ko'tarishga jur'at etmasdan, tikuviga diqqat bilan berilib o'tirdi, toki xizmatkor eshikka yaqinlashayotganda tashvishli qiziqish ularni opasining yuziga olib bordi. Jeyn odatdagidan biroz rangparroq ko'rinardi, lekin Elizabet kutganidan ko'ra vazminroq edi. Janoblar paydo bo'lganda, uning rangi qizardi; shunga qaramay u ularni ancha yengillik bilan va har qanday ranjish alomatidan ham, har qanday keraksiz xushomaddan ham bir xil xoli bo'lgan munosib xatti-harakat bilan qabul qildi.

paras.en: Elizabeth said as little to either as civility would allow, and sat down again to her work, with an eagerness which it did not often command. She had ventured only one glance at Darcy. He looked serious, as usual; and, she thought, more as he had been used to look in Hertfordshire, than as she had seen him at Pemberley. But, perhaps he could not in her mother's presence be what he was before her uncle and aunt. It was a painful, but not an improbable, conjecture.
paras.uz: Elizabet ularning har biriga xushmuomalalik ruxsat bergan darajada kam gapirdi va kamdan-kam bo'ladigan ishtiyoq bilan yana tikuviga o'tirdi. U Darsiga faqat bir marta qarashga jur'at etdi. U odatdagidek jiddiy ko'rinardi; va, uning o'ylashicha, u Pemberlida ko'rganidan ko'ra ko'proq Xertfordshirda odatda qanday ko'rinsa, shunday edi. Lekin, ehtimol, u onasining huzurida tog'asi va xolasining oldidagidek bo'la olmasdi. Bu og'riqli, lekin ehtimoldan yiroq bo'lmagan taxmin edi.

paras.en: Bingley, she had likewise seen for an instant, and in that short period saw him looking both pleased and embarrassed. He was received by Mrs. Bennet with a degree of civility which made her two daughters ashamed, especially when contrasted with the cold and ceremonious politeness of her curtsey and address to his friend.
paras.uz: Binglini ham bir lahza ko'rgan edi va o'sha qisqa vaqt ichida uni ham mamnun, ham xijolatda ko'rdi. Missis Bennet uni shunday darajadagi xushmuomalalik bilan qabul qildiki, bu uning ikki qizini uyaltirdi, ayniqsa uning do'stiga qilgan ta'zimi va murojaatining sovuq va rasmiy odobi bilan solishtirganda.

paras.en: Elizabeth, particularly, who knew that her mother owed to the latter the preservation of her favourite daughter from irremediable infamy, was hurt and distressed to a most painful degree by a distinction so ill applied.
paras.uz: Ayniqsa onasi sevimli qizini tuzatib bo'lmas sharmandalikdan saqlab qolgani uchun ikkinchisiga qarzdor ekanini bilgan Elizabet bunchalik noto'g'ri qo'llanilgan farqdan eng og'riqli darajada ranjidi va qayg'urdi.

paras.en: Darcy, after inquiring of her how Mr. and Mrs. Gardiner did, a question which she could not answer without confusion, said scarcely anything. He was not seated by her; perhaps that was the reason of his silence; but it had not been so in Derbyshire. There he had talked to her friends, when he could not to herself. But now several minutes elapsed without bringing the sound of his voice; and when occasionally, unable to resist the impulse of curiosity, she raised her eyes to his face, she as often found him looking at Jane as at herself, and frequently on no object but the ground. More thoughtfulness and less anxiety to please, than when they last met, were plainly expressed. She was disappointed, and angry with herself for being so.
paras.uz: Darsi undan janob va missis Gardinerning ahvolini so'ragach — bu savolga u sarosimasiz javob bera olmadi — deyarli hech narsa demadi. U uning yonida o'tirmagan edi; ehtimol, uning sukutining sababi shudir; lekin Derbishirda bunday emasdi. U yerda u o'zi bilan gaplasha olmaganda uning do'stlari bilan gaplashardi. Lekin endi bir necha daqiqa uning ovozi eshitilmay o'tdi; va vaqti-vaqti bilan qiziqish turtkisiga qarshi tura olmay, ko'zlarini uning yuziga ko'targanda, uni Jeynga ham o'ziga qaraganchalik tez-tez qarayotganini va ko'pincha yerdan boshqa hech narsaga qaramayotganini topardi. Ular oxirgi marta uchrashgandagidan ko'ra ko'proq o'ychanlik va yoqishga kamroq intilish aniq ifodalanardi. Uning hafsalasi pir bo'ldi va bunday bo'lgani uchun o'zidan g'azablandi.

paras.en: “Could I expect it to be otherwise!” said she. “Yet why did he come?”
paras.uz: «Boshqacha bo'lishini kuta olarmidim! — dedi u. — Shunga qaramay nega u keldi?»

paras.en: She was in no humour for conversation with anyone but himself; and to him she had hardly courage to speak.
paras.uz: U o'zidan boshqa hech kim bilan suhbatlashish kayfiyatida emasdi; unga esa gapirishga zo'rg'a jur'ati yetardi.

paras.en: She inquired after his sister, but could do no more.
paras.uz: U uning singlisi haqida so'radi, lekin bundan ortiq hech narsa qila olmadi.

paras.en: “It is a long time, Mr. Bingley, since you went away,” said Mrs. Bennet.
paras.uz: «Ketganingizga ancha bo'ldi, janob Bingli», — dedi missis Bennet.

paras.en: He readily agreed to it.
paras.uz: U darhol bunga rozi bo'ldi.

paras.en: “I began to be afraid you would never come back again. People did say you meant to quit the place entirely at Michaelmas; but, however, I hope it is not true. A great many changes have happened in the neighbourhood, since you went away. Miss Lucas is married and settled. And one of my own daughters. I suppose you have heard of it; indeed, you must have seen it in the papers. It was in The Times and The Courier, I know; though it was not put in as it ought to be. It was only said, 'Lately, George Wickham, Esq. to Miss Lydia Bennet,' without there being a syllable said of her father, or the place where she lived, or anything. It was my brother Gardiner's drawing up too, and I wonder how he came to make such an awkward business of it. Did you see it?”
paras.uz: «Boshqa hech qachon qaytmaysiz deb qo'rqa boshlagan edim. Odamlar Mixaylov kunida joyni butunlay tark etmoqchisiz deyishgan edi; lekin baribir umid qilamanki, bu rost emas. Siz ketganingizdan beri mahallada juda ko'p o'zgarishlar bo'ldi. Miss Lukas turmushga chiqib, joylashib oldi. Mening qizlarimdan biri ham. O'ylaymanki, bu haqda eshitgansiz; haqiqatan ham, uni gazetalarda ko'rgan bo'lsangiz kerak. Bilaman, u "Taym" va "Kurer"da bor edi; garchi bo'lishi kerakdek qo'yilmagan bo'lsa ham. Faqat "Yaqinda, eskvayr Jorj Uikhem miss Lidiya Bennetga" deyilgan, uning otasi yoki yashagan joyi yoki boshqa narsa haqida bir bo'g'in ham aytilmagan. Buni ham ukam Gardiner tuzgan edi, hayronmanki, qanday qilib u bunchalik beso'naqay ish qilibdi. Uni ko'rdingizmi?»

paras.en: Bingley replied that he did, and made his congratulations. Elizabeth dared not lift up her eyes. How Mr. Darcy looked, therefore, she could not tell.
paras.uz: Bingli ko'rganini aytdi va tabriklarini bildirdi. Elizabet ko'zlarini ko'tarishga jur'at etmadi. Shuning uchun janob Darsi qanday ko'rinayotganini ayta olmadi.

paras.en: “It is a delightful thing, to be sure, to have a daughter well married,” continued her mother, “but at the same time, Mr. Bingley, it is very hard to have her taken such a way from me. They are gone down to Newcastle, a place quite northward, it seems, and there they are to stay I do not know how long. His regiment is there; for I suppose you have heard of his leaving the ----shire, and of his being gone into the regulars. Thank Heaven! he has some friends, though perhaps not so many as he deserves.”
paras.uz: «Albatta, qizni yaxshi turmushga berish ajoyib narsa, — davom etdi onasi, — lekin shu bilan birga, janob Bingli, uni mendan shunchalik uzoqqa olib ketishlari juda og'ir. Ular Nyukaslga ketishdi, aftidan, ancha shimoldagi joy, u yerda qancha qolishlarini bilmayman. Uning polki o'sha yerda; chunki o'ylaymanki, uning ----shir polkini tark etib, doimiy armiyaga o'tgani haqida eshitgansiz. Xudoga shukr! Uning ba'zi do'stlari bor, garchi, ehtimol, u loyiq bo'lgancha ko'p bo'lmasa ham».

paras.en: Elizabeth, who knew this to be levelled at Mr. Darcy, was in such misery of shame, that she could hardly keep her seat. It drew from her, however, the exertion of speaking, which nothing else had so effectually done before; and she asked Bingley whether he meant to make any stay in the country at present. A few weeks, he believed.
paras.uz: Bu janob Darsiga qaratilganini bilgan Elizabet shunday uyat azobida ediki, o'rnida zo'rg'a o'tira oldi. Biroq bu undan avval hech narsa bunchalik samarali qilmagan gapirish harakatini chiqarib oldi; va u Binglidan hozir bu yerlarda biroz qolmoqchimi, deb so'radi. U bir necha hafta, deb o'ylardi.

paras.en: “When you have killed all your own birds, Mr. Bingley,” said her mother, “I beg you will come here, and shoot as many as you please on Mr. Bennet's manor. I am sure he will be vastly happy to oblige you, and will save all the best of the covies for you.”
paras.uz: «O'z qushlaringizning hammasini otib bo'lgach, janob Bingli, — dedi onasi, — iltimos, bu yerga keling va janob Bennetning yerlarida xohlagancha oting. Ishonchim komilki, u sizga yoqish uchun nihoyatda baxtli bo'ladi va eng yaxshi qush to'dalarini siz uchun saqlab qo'yadi».

paras.en: Elizabeth's misery increased, at such unnecessary, such officious attention! Were the same fair prospect to arise at present as had flattered them a year ago, every thing, she was persuaded, would be hastening to the same vexatious conclusion. At that instant, she felt that years of happiness could not make Jane or herself amends for moments of such painful confusion.
paras.uz: Bunday keraksiz, bunday ortiqcha e'tibordan Elizabetning azobi ortdi! Agar bir yil oldin ularni ovutgan o'sha go'zal istiqbol hozir paydo bo'lsa, u ishonardiki, hamma narsa o'sha g'ashga tegadigan yakunga shoshilgan bo'lardi. O'sha lahzada u yillar davomidagi baxt Jeynga yoki o'ziga bunday og'riqli sarosima lahzalarining o'rnini to'ldira olmasligini his qildi.

paras.en: “The first wish of my heart,” said she to herself, “is never more to be in company with either of them. Their society can afford no pleasure that will atone for such wretchedness as this! Let me never see either one or the other again!”
paras.uz: «Qalbimning birinchi istagi, — dedi u o'ziga, — ularning hech biri bilan boshqa hech qachon bir davrada bo'lmaslik. Ularning davrasi bunday ayanchlikni yuvadigan hech qanday zavq bera olmaydi! Ularning birini ham, ikkinchisini ham boshqa hech qachon ko'rmay!»

paras.en: Yet the misery, for which years of happiness were to offer no compensation, received soon afterwards material relief, from observing how much the beauty of her sister re-kindled the admiration of her former lover. When first he came in, he had spoken to her but little; but every five minutes seemed to be giving her more of his attention. He found her as handsome as she had been last year; as good natured, and as unaffected, though not quite so chatty. Jane was anxious that no difference should be perceived in her at all, and was really persuaded that she talked as much as ever. But her mind was so busily engaged, that she did not always know when she was silent.
paras.uz: Shunga qaramay, yillar davomidagi baxt ham uning o'rnini to'ldira olmaydigan azob ko'p o'tmay opasining go'zalligi uning avvalgi sevgilisining hayratini qanchalik qayta alangalatganini kuzatishdan jiddiy yengillik oldi. U birinchi kirganda, u bilan kam gaplashgan edi; lekin har besh daqiqada unga ko'proq e'tibor berayotganga o'xshardi. U uni o'tgan yildagidek chiroyli, xuddi shunday xushfe'l va sodda deb topdi, garchi unchalik gapdon bo'lmasa ham. Jeyn unda hech qanday farq sezilmasligini juda istardi va haqiqatan ham har doimgidek ko'p gapirayotganiga ishonardi. Lekin uning ongi shunchalik band ediki, u qachon jim qolganini doim ham bilmasdi.

paras.en: When the gentlemen rose to go away, Mrs. Bennet was mindful of her intended civility, and they were invited and engaged to dine at Longbourn in a few days time.
paras.uz: Janoblar ketish uchun turishganda, missis Bennet niyat qilgan xushmuomalaligini esladi va ular bir necha kundan keyin Longbornda tushlik qilishga taklif qilindi va rozi bo'lishdi.

paras.en: “You are quite a visit in my debt, Mr. Bingley,” she added, “for when you went to town last winter, you promised to take a family dinner with us, as soon as you returned. I have not forgot, you see; and I assure you, I was very much disappointed that you did not come back and keep your engagement.”
paras.uz: «Siz menga bir tashrif qarzdorsiz, janob Bingli, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — chunki o'tgan qish Londonga ketayotganingizda, qaytishingiz bilanoq biz bilan oilaviy tushlik qilishga va'da bergan edingiz. Ko'ryapsizmi, unutmaganman; sizni ishontirib aytamanki, qaytib kelib va'dangizni bajarmaganingizdan hafsalam juda pir bo'lgan edi».

paras.en: Bingley looked a little silly at this reflection, and said something of his concern at having been prevented by business. They then went away.
paras.uz: Bingli bu mulohazadan biroz ahmoqona ko'rindi va ishlari to'sqinlik qilgani uchun afsusi haqida nimadir dedi. Keyin ular ketishdi.

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet had been strongly inclined to ask them to stay and dine there that day; but, though she always kept a very good table, she did not think anything less than two courses could be good enough for a man on whom she had such anxious designs, or satisfy the appetite and pride of one who had ten thousand a year.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet ularni qolib, o'sha kuni u yerda tushlik qilishga taklif qilishga qattiq moyil edi; lekin u doim juda yaxshi dasturxon tutsa ham, u shunchalik tashvishli rejalari bo'lgan erkak uchun yoki yiliga o'n ming daromadi bo'lgan odamning ishtahasi va g'ururini qondirish uchun ikki taomdan kam narsa yetarlicha yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin deb o'ylamadi.

gloss.ex: She sat intently at work, striving to be composed, and without daring to lift up her eyes, till anxious curiosity carried them to the face of her sister as the…
Bingley, she had likewise seen for an instant, and in that short period saw him looking both pleased and embarrassed.
He was not seated by her; perhaps that was the reason of his silence; but it had not been so in Derbyshire.
But the spiritless condition which this event threw her into was shortly relieved, and her mind opened again to the agitation of hope, by an article of news which then…
A great many changes have happened in the neighbourhood, since you went away.
“Some acquaintance or other, my dear, I suppose; I am sure I do not know.”
“It would be nothing; I could see him with perfect indifference, but I can hardly bear to hear it thus perpetually talked of.

quiz.q: Who returns to Netherfield?
quiz.why_uz: Missis Bennet yana umidga to'ladi.

quiz.q: How does Darcy behave at Longbourn?
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet uning his-tuyg'ularini tushuna olmaydi.

chapters.title: Dinner at Longbourn
chapters.recap_uz: Ziyofatda Bingley Jeyn yonida o'tiradi. Elizabet Darsi bilan gaplashmoqchi, lekin imkon bo'lmaydi. Jeyn Bingleyga endi faqat do'st sifatida qaraymiz, deydi — Elizabet kuladi.

paras.en: As soon as they were gone, Elizabeth walked out to recover her spirits; or in other words, to dwell without interruption on those subjects that must deaden them more. Mr. Darcy's behaviour astonished and vexed her.
paras.uz: Ular ketishlari bilanoq Elizabet kayfiyatini tiklash uchun tashqariga chiqdi; boshqacha aytganda, uni yanada so'ndirishi kerak bo'lgan mavzular ustida halaqitsiz to'xtalish uchun. Janob Darsining xatti-harakati uni hayratga soldi va g'ashini keltirdi.

paras.en: “Why, if he came only to be silent, grave, and indifferent,” said she, “did he come at all?”
paras.uz: «Agar u faqat jim, jiddiy va befarq bo'lish uchun kelgan bo'lsa, — dedi u, — umuman nega keldi?»

paras.en: She could settle it in no way that gave her pleasure.
paras.uz: U buni o'ziga zavq beradigan hech qanday yo'l bilan hal qila olmadi.

paras.en: “He could be still amiable, still pleasing, to my uncle and aunt, when he was in town; and why not to me? If he fears me, why come hither? If he no longer cares for me, why silent? Teasing, teasing, man! I will think no more about him.”
paras.uz: «U Londonda bo'lganida tog'am va xolamga hali ham yoqimli, hali ham maftunkor bo'la oldi; nega menga emas? Agar mendan qo'rqsa, nega bu yerga keladi? Agar menga endi ahamiyat bermasa, nega jim? Jonga tegadigan, jonga tegadigan odam! U haqida boshqa o'ylamayman».

paras.en: Her resolution was for a short time involuntarily kept by the approach of her sister, who joined her with a cheerful look, which showed her better satisfied with their visitors, than Elizabeth.
paras.uz: Uning qarori opasining yaqinlashishi bilan qisqa vaqt beixtiyor saqlandi, u quvnoq qiyofada unga qo'shildi, bu uning mehmonlardan Elizabetga qaraganda ko'proq qoniqqanini ko'rsatardi.

paras.en: “Now,” said she, “that this first meeting is over, I feel perfectly easy. I know my own strength, and I shall never be embarrassed again by his coming. I am glad he dines here on Tuesday. It will then be publicly seen that, on both sides, we meet only as common and indifferent acquaintance.”
paras.uz: «Endi, — dedi u, — bu birinchi uchrashuv o'tgach, o'zimni mutlaqo xotirjam his qilyapman. O'z kuchimni bilaman va uning kelishidan boshqa hech qachon xijolat bo'lmayman. Uning seshanba kuni bu yerda tushlik qilishidan xursandman. Shunda ikki tomondan ham faqat oddiy va befarq tanishlar sifatida uchrashishimiz hammaga ko'rinadi».

paras.en: “Yes, very indifferent indeed,” said Elizabeth, laughingly. “Oh, Jane, take care.”
paras.uz: «Ha, haqiqatan ham juda befarq, — dedi Elizabet kulib. — Oh, Jeyn, ehtiyot bo'l».

paras.en: “My dear Lizzy, you cannot think me so weak, as to be in danger now?”
paras.uz: «Azizim Lizzi, meni endi xavf ostida bo'ladigan darajada zaif deb o'ylay olmaysan-ku?»

paras.en: “I think you are in very great danger of making him as much in love with you as ever.”
paras.uz: «Menimcha, sen uni o'zingga har qachongidek oshiq qilib qo'yishning juda katta xavfi ostidasan».

paras.en: They did not see the gentlemen again till Tuesday; and Mrs. Bennet, in the meanwhile, was giving way to all the happy schemes, which the good humour and common politeness of Bingley, in half an hour's visit, had revived.
paras.uz: Ular janoblarni seshanbagacha yana ko'rishmadi; bu orada missis Bennet Binglining yarim soatlik tashrifdagi xushfe'lligi va oddiy xushmuomalaligi qayta jonlantirgan barcha baxtli rejalarga berildi.

paras.en: On Tuesday there was a large party assembled at Longbourn; and the two who were most anxiously expected, to the credit of their punctuality as sportsmen, were in very good time. When they repaired to the dining-room, Elizabeth eagerly watched to see whether Bingley would take the place, which, in all their former parties, had belonged to him, by her sister. Her prudent mother, occupied by the same ideas, forbore to invite him to sit by herself. On entering the room, he seemed to hesitate; but Jane happened to look round, and happened to smile: it was decided. He placed himself by her.
paras.uz: Seshanba kuni Longbornda katta davra yig'ildi; eng tashvish bilan kutilgan ikkisi ovchi sifatidagi aniqliklariga sharaf keltirib, juda vaqtida kelishdi. Ular ovqatxonaga o'tishganda, Elizabet Bingli avvalgi barcha yig'inlarida unga tegishli bo'lgan opasining yonidagi joyni egallaydimi, yo'qmi, ishtiyoq bilan kuzatdi. Xuddi shu fikrlar bilan band bo'lgan oqil onasi uni o'z yoniga o'tirishga taklif qilishdan o'zini tiydi. Xonaga kirganda u ikkilanganday ko'rindi; lekin Jeyn tasodifan atrofga qaradi va tasodifan jilmaydi: masala hal bo'ldi. U uning yoniga o'tirdi.

paras.en: Elizabeth, with a triumphant sensation, looked towards his friend. He bore it with noble indifference, and she would have imagined that Bingley had received his sanction to be happy, had she not seen his eyes likewise turned towards Mr. Darcy, with an expression of half-laughing alarm.
paras.uz: Elizabet g'olibona tuyg'u bilan uning do'sti tomon qaradi. U bunga olijanob befarqlik bilan chidadi va agar u Binglining ko'zlari ham yarim kulgili xavotir ifodasi bilan janob Darsiga qaratilganini ko'rmaganida, Bingli baxtli bo'lish uchun uning ruxsatini olgan deb tasavvur qilgan bo'lardi.

paras.en: His behaviour to her sister was such, during dinner time, as showed an admiration of her, which, though more guarded than formerly, persuaded Elizabeth, that if left wholly to himself, Jane's happiness, and his own, would be speedily secured. Though she dared not depend upon the consequence, she yet received pleasure from observing his behaviour. It gave her all the animation that her spirits could boast; for she was in no cheerful humour. Mr. Darcy was almost as far from her as the table could divide them. He was on one side of her mother. She knew how little such a situation would give pleasure to either, or make either appear to advantage. She was not near enough to hear any of their discourse, but she could see how seldom they spoke to each other, and how formal and cold was their manner whenever they did. Her mother's ungraciousness, made the sense of what they owed him more painful to Elizabeth's mind; and she would, at times, have given anything to be privileged to tell him that his kindness was neither unknown nor unfelt by the whole of the family.
paras.uz: Tushlik vaqtida uning opasiga nisbatan xatti-harakati shunday ediki, bu avvalgidan ehtiyotkorroq bo'lsa ham, unga hayratini ko'rsatardi va Elizabetni agar u butunlay o'z holiga qo'yilsa, Jeynning baxti va o'zining baxti tez orada ta'minlanishiga ishontirdi. Garchi u oqibatga tayanishga jur'at etmasa ham, uning xatti-harakatini kuzatishdan zavq oldi. Bu unga ruhi maqtana oladigan butun jonlilikni berdi; chunki u quvnoq kayfiyatda emasdi. Janob Darsi undan stol ajrata oladigan darajada deyarli uzoqda edi. U onasining bir tomonida edi. U bunday joylashuv ikkalasiga ham qanchalik kam zavq berishini yoki ikkalasini ham afzal ko'rsatishini bilardi. U ularning birorta gapini eshitish uchun yetarlicha yaqin emasdi, lekin ular bir-biri bilan qanchalik kam gaplashishini va gaplashganda muomalalari qanchalik rasmiy va sovuq ekanini ko'ra olardi. Onasining iltifotsizligi ular unga nimadan qarzdor ekanini anglashni Elizabetning ongida yanada og'riqliroq qildi; va u ba'zan uning mehribonligi butun oilaga noma'lum ham, sezilmagan ham emasligini unga aytish imtiyoziga ega bo'lish uchun hamma narsani bergan bo'lardi.

paras.en: She was in hopes that the evening would afford some opportunity of bringing them together; that the whole of the visit would not pass away without enabling them to enter into something more of conversation than the mere ceremonious salutation attending his entrance. Anxious and uneasy, the period which passed in the drawing-room, before the gentlemen came, was wearisome and dull to a degree that almost made her uncivil. She looked forward to their entrance as the point on which all her chance of pleasure for the evening must depend.
paras.uz: U oqshom ularni birga keltirish uchun biror imkoniyat berishiga umid qildi; butun tashrif uning kirishiga hamroh bo'lgan shunchaki rasmiy salomlashuvdan ko'ra ko'proq suhbatga kirishishga imkon bermasdan o'tib ketmasligiga. Tashvishli va bezovta holda, janoblar kelishidan oldin mehmonxonada o'tgan vaqt shunchalik charchatuvchi va zerikarli ediki, uni deyarli xushmuomalasiz qilib qo'ydi. U ularning kirishini oqshom uchun barcha zavq imkoniyatlari bog'liq bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan nuqta sifatida kutdi.

paras.en: “If he does not come to me, then,” said she, “I shall give him up for ever.”
paras.uz: «Agar u mening oldimga kelmasa, — dedi u, — undan abadiy voz kechaman».

paras.en: The gentlemen came; and she thought he looked as if he would have answered her hopes; but, alas! the ladies had crowded round the table, where Miss Bennet was making tea, and Elizabeth pouring out the coffee, in so close a confederacy that there was not a single vacancy near her which would admit of a chair. And on the gentlemen's approaching, one of the girls moved closer to her than ever, and said, in a whisper:
paras.uz: Janoblar kelishdi; va unga u uning umidlariga javob beradigandek ko'rindi; lekin, afsus! Xonimlar miss Bennet choy damlayotgan va Elizabet qahva quyayotgan stol atrofiga shunchalik zich ittifoqda to'planishgan ediki, uning yonida stul qo'yish uchun birorta ham bo'sh joy qolmagan edi. Janoblar yaqinlashganda esa qizlardan biri unga har qachongidan ham yaqinroq surildi va pichirlab dedi:

paras.en: “The men shan't come and part us, I am determined. We want none of them; do we?”
paras.uz: «Erkaklar kelib bizni ajratmaydi, qaror qildim. Bizga ularning hech biri kerak emas; shundaymi?»

paras.en: Darcy had walked away to another part of the room. She followed him with her eyes, envied everyone to whom he spoke, had scarcely patience enough to help anybody to coffee; and then was enraged against herself for being so silly!
paras.uz: Darsi xonaning boshqa qismiga ketib qoldi. U uni ko'zlari bilan kuzatdi, u gaplashgan har kimga hasad qildi, birovga qahva berish uchun zo'rg'a sabri yetdi; keyin bunchalik ahmoq bo'lgani uchun o'zidan g'azablandi!

paras.en: “A man who has once been refused! How could I ever be foolish enough to expect a renewal of his love? Is there one among the sex, who would not protest against such a weakness as a second proposal to the same woman? There is no indignity so abhorrent to their feelings!”
paras.uz: «Bir marta rad etilgan erkak! Qanday qilib uning muhabbati yangilanishini kutadigan darajada ahmoq bo'la olardim? Erkaklar orasida bitta ayolga ikkinchi marta taklif qilishdek zaiflikka qarshi chiqmaydigan birorta erkak bormi? Ularning tuyg'ulariga bundan jirkanchroq hech qanday tahqir yo'q!»

paras.en: She was a little revived, however, by his bringing back his coffee cup himself; and she seized the opportunity of saying:
paras.uz: Biroq u qahva finjonini o'zi qaytarib olib kelganda, u biroz jonlandi; va u imkoniyatdan foydalanib, dedi:

paras.en: “Is your sister at Pemberley still?”
paras.uz: «Singlingiz hali ham Pemberlidami?»

paras.en: “Yes, she will remain there till Christmas.”
paras.uz: «Ha, u Rojdestvogacha u yerda qoladi».

paras.en: “And quite alone? Have all her friends left her?”
paras.uz: «Butunlay yolg'izmi? Barcha dugonalari uni tark etishdimi?»

paras.en: “Mrs. Annesley is with her. The others have been gone on to Scarborough, these three weeks.”
paras.uz: «Missis Ennsli u bilan. Boshqalar uch haftadan beri Skarboroga ketishgan».

paras.en: She could think of nothing more to say; but if he wished to converse with her, he might have better success. He stood by her, however, for some minutes, in silence; and, at last, on the young lady's whispering to Elizabeth again, he walked away.
paras.uz: U boshqa aytadigan gap o'ylay olmadi; lekin agar u u bilan suhbatlashmoqchi bo'lsa, unda yaxshiroq muvaffaqiyat bo'lishi mumkin edi. Biroq u bir necha daqiqa jimgina uning yonida turdi; va nihoyat, yosh xonim Elizabetga yana pichirlaganda, u nari ketdi.

paras.en: When the tea-things were removed, and the card-tables placed, the ladies all rose, and Elizabeth was then hoping to be soon joined by him, when all her views were overthrown by seeing him fall a victim to her mother's rapacity for whist players, and in a few moments after seated with the rest of the party. She now lost every expectation of pleasure.
