They were confined for the evening at different tables, and she had nothing to hope, but that his eyes were so often turned towards her side of the room, as to make him play as unsuccessfully as herself.
paras.uz: Choy anjomlari olib ketilib, karta stollari qo'yilgach, xonimlar hammasi o'rnidan turdi va Elizabet tez orada u qo'shilishiga umid qilib turgan edi, shunda uning onasining vist o'yinchilariga bo'lgan ochko'zligi qurboni bo'lganini va bir necha lahzadan keyin davraning qolgan a'zolari bilan o'tirganini ko'rib, barcha rejalari ag'darildi. Endi u zavqning har qanday kutishini yo'qotdi. Ular oqshom davomida turli stollarga bog'lanib qolishdi va unga uning ko'zlari xonaning uning tomoniga shunchalik tez-tez qaratilganki, bu uni ham o'zi kabi omadsiz o'ynashga majbur qilishidan boshqa umid qiladigan narsa qolmadi.

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet had designed to keep the two Netherfield gentlemen to supper; but their carriage was unluckily ordered before any of the others, and she had no opportunity of detaining them.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet ikki Nezerfild janobini kechki ovqatga olib qolmoqchi edi; lekin afsuski, ularning aravasi boshqalarnikidan oldin buyurilgan edi va uning ularni ushlab qolish imkoniyati bo'lmadi.

paras.en: “Well girls,” said she, as soon as they were left to themselves, “What say you to the day? I think every thing has passed off uncommonly well, I assure you. The dinner was as well dressed as any I ever saw. The venison was roasted to a turn--and everybody said they never saw so fat a haunch. The soup was fifty times better than what we had at the Lucases' last week; and even Mr. Darcy acknowledged, that the partridges were remarkably well done; and I suppose he has two or three French cooks at least. And, my dear Jane, I never saw you look in greater beauty. Mrs. Long said so too, for I asked her whether you did not. And what do you think she said besides? 'Ah! Mrs. Bennet, we shall have her at Netherfield at last.' She did indeed. I do think Mrs. Long is as good a creature as ever lived--and her nieces are very pretty behaved girls, and not at all handsome: I like them prodigiously.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, qizlar, — dedi u, ular o'zlari qolishlari bilanoq, — kun haqida nima deysizlar? Menimcha, hamma narsa g'ayrioddiy darajada yaxshi o'tdi, sizni ishontirib aytaman. Tushlik men ko'rgan har qanday tushlik kabi yaxshi tayyorlangan edi. Kiyik go'shti aynan kerakli darajada qovurilgan edi — va hamma bunchalik semiz son go'shtini hech qachon ko'rmaganini aytdi. Sho'rva o'tgan hafta Lukaslarnikida ichganimizdan ellik barobar yaxshiroq edi; hatto janob Darsi ham kakliklar juda yaxshi pishirilganini tan oldi; menimcha, uning kamida ikki-uchta frantsuz oshpazi bor. Aziz Jeynim, seni hech qachon bundan go'zalroq ko'rmaganman. Missis Long ham shunday dedi, chunki undan shundaymi, deb so'radim. Bundan tashqari u nima dedi deb o'ylaysizlar? "Ah! Missis Bennet, nihoyat uni Nezerfildda ko'ramiz". Haqiqatan ham shunday dedi. Menimcha, missis Long hech qachon yashagan eng yaxshi mavjudot — uning jiyanlari esa juda odobli qizlar va umuman chiroyli emas: ularni nihoyatda yoqtiraman».

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet, in short, was in very great spirits; she had seen enough of Bingley's behaviour to Jane, to be convinced that she would get him at last; and her expectations of advantage to her family, when in a happy humour, were so far beyond reason, that she was quite disappointed at not seeing him there again the next day, to make his proposals.
paras.uz: Qisqasi, missis Bennet juda yaxshi kayfiyatda edi; u Binglining Jeynga nisbatan xatti-harakatidan nihoyat uni qo'lga kiritishiga ishonch hosil qilish uchun yetarlicha ko'rgan edi; uning oilasi uchun foyda kutishlari baxtli kayfiyatda bo'lganda aqldan shunchalik uzoqqa ketardiki, ertasi kuni uni taklif qilish uchun yana u yerda ko'rmaganidan hafsalasi butunlay pir bo'ldi.

paras.en: “It has been a very agreeable day,” said Miss Bennet to Elizabeth. “The party seemed so well selected, so suitable one with the other. I hope we may often meet again.”
paras.uz: «Bu juda yoqimli kun bo'ldi, — dedi miss Bennet Elizabetga. — Davra shunchalik yaxshi tanlangan, bir-biriga shunchalik mos edi. Umid qilamanki, tez-tez yana uchrashamiz».

paras.en: Elizabeth smiled.
paras.uz: Elizabet jilmaydi.

paras.en: “Lizzy, you must not do so. You must not suspect me. It mortifies me. I assure you that I have now learnt to enjoy his conversation as an agreeable and sensible young man, without having a wish beyond it. I am perfectly satisfied, from what his manners now are, that he never had any design of engaging my affection. It is only that he is blessed with greater sweetness of address, and a stronger desire of generally pleasing, than any other man.”
paras.uz: «Lizzi, bunday qilmasliging kerak. Menga shubha qilmasliging kerak. Bu meni xo'rlaydi. Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, endi men uning suhbatidan yoqimli va aqlli yosh yigit sifatida, bundan ortiq hech qanday istaksiz zavqlanishni o'rgandim. Uning hozirgi muomalasidan mutlaqo qanoat hosil qildimki, uning hech qachon mening mehrimni qozonish niyati bo'lmagan. Shunchaki u boshqa har qanday erkakdan ko'ra muomalada shirinroq va umuman yoqishga kuchliroq istak bilan siylangan».

paras.en: “You are very cruel,” said her sister, “you will not let me smile, and are provoking me to it every moment.”
paras.uz: «Sen juda shafqatsizsan, — dedi singlisi, — menga jilmayishga ruxsat bermaysan, lekin har lahza meni bunga undaysan».

paras.en: “How hard it is in some cases to be believed!”
paras.uz: «Ba'zi hollarda ishontirish qanchalik qiyin!»

paras.en: “And how impossible in others!”
paras.uz: «Boshqa hollarda esa qanchalik imkonsiz!»

paras.en: “But why should you wish to persuade me that I feel more than I acknowledge?”
paras.uz: «Lekin nega meni tan olganimdan ko'proq his qilayotganimga ishontirmoqchisan?»

paras.en: “That is a question which I hardly know how to answer. We all love to instruct, though we can teach only what is not worth knowing. Forgive me; and if you persist in indifference, do not make me your confidante.”
paras.uz: «Bu men qanday javob berishni zo'rg'a biladigan savol. Hammamiz o'rgatishni yaxshi ko'ramiz, garchi faqat bilishga arzimaydigan narsani o'rgata olsak ham. Meni kechir; agar befarqlikda davom etsang, meni sirdoshing qilma».

gloss.ex: “Why, if he came only to be silent, grave, and indifferent,”
Bennet, in short, was in very great spirits; she had seen enough of Bingley's behaviour to Jane, to be convinced that she would get him at last; and her expectations…
Darcy's behaviour astonished and vexed her.
His behaviour to her sister was such, during dinner time, as showed an admiration of her, which, though more guarded than formerly, persuaded Elizabeth, that if left wholly to himself,…
On entering the room, he seemed to hesitate; but Jane happened to look round, and happened to smile: it was decided.
It will then be publicly seen that, on both sides, we meet only as common and indifferent acquaintance.”
Darcy acknowledged, that the partridges were remarkably well done; and I suppose he has two or three French cooks at least.

quiz.q: What does Jane claim about Bingley?
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet bunga ishonmaydi.

quiz.q: Why is Elizabeth frustrated?
quiz.why_uz: U Darsi bilan yolg'iz gaplashishni juda istaydi.

chapters.title: Jane's Engagement
chapters.recap_uz: Bingley Jeynga turmush taklif qiladi va u rozi bo'ladi. Butun oila xursand. Jeyn: «Men eng baxtli odamman», deydi.

paras.en: A few days after this visit, Mr. Bingley called again, and alone. His friend had left him that morning for London, but was to return home in ten days time. He sat with them above an hour, and was in remarkably good spirits. Mrs. Bennet invited him to dine with them; but, with many expressions of concern, he confessed himself engaged elsewhere.
paras.uz: Bu tashrifdan bir necha kun o'tib, janob Bingli yana keldi, bu safar yolg'iz. Do'sti o'sha kuni ertalab uni tark etib, Londonga ketgan edi, lekin o'n kundan keyin qaytishi kerak edi. U ular bilan bir soatdan ortiq o'tirdi va nihoyatda yaxshi kayfiyatda edi. Missis Bennet uni ular bilan tushlik qilishga taklif qildi; lekin u ko'p afsus bildirib, boshqa joyda band ekanini tan oldi.

paras.en: “Next time you call,” said she, “I hope we shall be more lucky.”
paras.uz: «Keyingi safar kelganingizda, — dedi u, — umid qilamanki, omadimiz ko'proq keladi».

paras.en: He should be particularly happy at any time, etc. etc.; and if she would give him leave, would take an early opportunity of waiting on them.
paras.uz: U istalgan vaqtda ayniqsa baxtli bo'lardi va hokazo, va hokazo; va agar u ruxsat bersa, tez orada ularni ziyorat qilish imkoniyatidan foydalanadi.

paras.en: “Can you come to-morrow?”
paras.uz: «Ertaga kela olasizmi?»

paras.en: Yes, he had no engagement at all for to-morrow; and her invitation was accepted with alacrity.
paras.uz: Ha, ertaga uning umuman hech qanday bandligi yo'q edi; va uning taklifi tayyorlik bilan qabul qilindi.

paras.en: He came, and in such very good time that the ladies were none of them dressed. In ran Mrs. Bennet to her daughter's room, in her dressing gown, and with her hair half finished, crying out:
paras.uz: U keldi va shunchalik erta keldiki, xonimlarning hech biri kiyinmagan edi. Missis Bennet xalatda, sochini yarim tarab, qizining xonasiga yugurib kirib, qichqirdi:

paras.en: “My dear Jane, make haste and hurry down. He is come--Mr. Bingley is come. He is, indeed. Make haste, make haste. Here, Sarah, come to Miss Bennet this moment, and help her on with her gown. Never mind Miss Lizzy's hair.”
paras.uz: «Aziz Jeyn, shoshil, tezroq pastga tush. U keldi — janob Bingli keldi. Rostdan ham keldi. Shoshil, shoshil. Bu yoqqa, Sara, hozir miss Bennetning oldiga kel va unga ko'ylagini kiyishga yordam ber. Miss Lizzining sochiga qarama».

paras.en: “We will be down as soon as we can,” said Jane; “but I dare say Kitty is forwarder than either of us, for she went up stairs half an hour ago.”
paras.uz: «Iloji boricha tezroq tushamiz, — dedi Jeyn, — lekin ishonamanki, Ketti ikkalamizdan ham oldinda, chunki u yarim soat oldin yuqoriga chiqdi».

paras.en: “Oh! hang Kitty! what has she to do with it? Come be quick, be quick! Where is your sash, my dear?”
paras.uz: «Oh! Kettini qo'y! Uning bunga nima aloqasi bor? Qani, tez bo'l, tez bo'l! Belbog'ing qayerda, azizim?»

paras.en: But when her mother was gone, Jane would not be prevailed on to go down without one of her sisters.
paras.uz: Lekin onasi ketgach, Jeynni opa-singillaridan birisiz pastga tushishga ko'ndirib bo'lmadi.

paras.en: The same anxiety to get them by themselves was visible again in the evening. After tea, Mr. Bennet retired to the library, as was his custom, and Mary went up stairs to her instrument. Two obstacles of the five being thus removed, Mrs. Bennet sat looking and winking at Elizabeth and Catherine for a considerable time, without making any impression on them. Elizabeth would not observe her; and when at last Kitty did, she very innocently said, “What is the matter mamma? What do you keep winking at me for? What am I to do?”
paras.uz: Ularni yolg'iz qoldirishga bo'lgan xuddi shu intilish kechqurun yana ko'rindi. Choydan keyin janob Bennet odatiga ko'ra kutubxonaga chekindi, Meri esa cholg'usi oldiga yuqoriga chiqdi. Beshta to'siqdan ikkitasi shu tarzda olib tashlangach, missis Bennet ancha vaqt Elizabet va Ketringa qarab, ko'z qisib o'tirdi, lekin ularga hech qanday ta'sir qilmadi. Elizabet uni sezmaslikka harakat qildi; nihoyat Ketti sezganda, u juda beg'uborlik bilan dedi: «Nima bo'ldi, oyijon? Nega menga ko'z qisayapsiz? Men nima qilishim kerak?»

paras.en: “Nothing child, nothing. I did not wink at you.” She then sat still five minutes longer; but unable to waste such a precious occasion, she suddenly got up, and saying to Kitty, “Come here, my love, I want to speak to you,” took her out of the room. Jane instantly gave a look at Elizabeth which spoke her distress at such premeditation, and her entreaty that she would not give in to it. In a few minutes, Mrs. Bennet half-opened the door and called out:
paras.uz: «Hech narsa, bolam, hech narsa. Men senga ko'z qismadim». Keyin u yana besh daqiqa jim o'tirdi; lekin bunday qimmatli imkoniyatni boy berishga chiday olmay, to'satdan o'rnidan turdi va Kettiga «Bu yoqqa kel, azizim, sen bilan gaplashmoqchiman» deb, uni xonadan olib chiqdi. Jeyn darhol Elizabetga bunday oldindan rejalashtirishdan iztirobini va unga bo'ysunmaslikni iltimos qilishini bildiruvchi nigoh tashladi. Bir necha daqiqadan keyin missis Bennet eshikni yarim ochib, chaqirdi:

paras.en: “Lizzy, my dear, I want to speak with you.”
paras.uz: «Lizzi, azizim, sen bilan gaplashmoqchiman».

paras.en: Elizabeth was forced to go.
paras.uz: Elizabet borishga majbur bo'ldi.

paras.en: “We may as well leave them by themselves you know;” said her mother, as soon as she was in the hall. “Kitty and I are going up stairs to sit in my dressing-room.”
paras.uz: «Bilasanmi, ularni yolg'iz qoldirganimiz ma'qul, — dedi onasi, u zalga chiqishi bilanoq. — Ketti bilan men yuqoriga, kiyinish xonamga o'tiramiz».

paras.en: Elizabeth made no attempt to reason with her mother, but remained quietly in the hall, till she and Kitty were out of sight, then returned into the drawing-room.
paras.uz: Elizabet onasi bilan mantiqan gaplashishga urinmadi, lekin u va Ketti ko'zdan g'oyib bo'lguncha zalda jimgina qoldi, keyin mehmonxonaga qaytdi.

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet's schemes for this day were ineffectual. Bingley was every thing that was charming, except the professed lover of her daughter. His ease and cheerfulness rendered him a most agreeable addition to their evening party; and he bore with the ill-judged officiousness of the mother, and heard all her silly remarks with a forbearance and command of countenance particularly grateful to the daughter.
paras.uz: Missis Bennetning bu kungi rejalari samarasiz bo'ldi. Bingli qizining izhor qilgan oshig'i bo'lishdan tashqari hamma jihatdan maftunkor edi. Uning yengilligi va quvnoqligi uni oqshomgi davraga eng yoqimli qo'shimcha qilardi; u onaning noto'g'ri o'ylangan ortiqcha g'amxo'rligiga chidadi va uning barcha ahmoqona gaplarini qiziga ayniqsa yoqqan sabr va yuz ifodasini boshqarish bilan tingladi.

paras.en: He scarcely needed an invitation to stay supper; and before he went away, an engagement was formed, chiefly through his own and Mrs. Bennet's means, for his coming next morning to shoot with her husband.
paras.uz: Unga kechki ovqatga qolish uchun taklif zo'rg'a kerak bo'ldi; ketishidan oldin esa asosan uning va missis Bennetning sa'y-harakatlari bilan uning ertasi kuni ertalab uning eri bilan ov qilish uchun kelishi kelishildi.

paras.en: After this day, Jane said no more of her indifference. Not a word passed between the sisters concerning Bingley; but Elizabeth went to bed in the happy belief that all must speedily be concluded, unless Mr. Darcy returned within the stated time. Seriously, however, she felt tolerably persuaded that all this must have taken place with that gentleman's concurrence.
paras.uz: Shu kundan keyin Jeyn o'zining befarqligi haqida boshqa gapirmadi. Opa-singillar o'rtasida Bingli haqida bir og'iz ham gap bo'lmadi; lekin Elizabet, agar janob Darsi belgilangan vaqt ichida qaytmasa, hammasi tez orada tugashi kerak degan baxtli ishonch bilan uxlashga yotdi. Biroq jiddiy aytganda, u bularning hammasi o'sha janobning roziligi bilan sodir bo'lgan bo'lishi kerakligiga ancha ishonardi.

paras.en: Bingley was punctual to his appointment; and he and Mr. Bennet spent the morning together, as had been agreed on. The latter was much more agreeable than his companion expected. There was nothing of presumption or folly in Bingley that could provoke his ridicule, or disgust him into silence; and he was more communicative, and less eccentric, than the other had ever seen him. Bingley of course returned with him to dinner; and in the evening Mrs. Bennet's invention was again at work to get every body away from him and her daughter. Elizabeth, who had a letter to write, went into the breakfast room for that purpose soon after tea; for as the others were all going to sit down to cards, she could not be wanted to counteract her mother's schemes.
paras.uz: Bingli kelishuvga aniq keldi; u va janob Bennet kelishilganidek ertalabni birga o'tkazishdi. Ikkinchisi hamrohi kutganidan ancha yoqimliroq edi. Binglida uning masxarasini qo'zg'aydigan yoki uni jirkantirib jim qoldiradigan hech qanday takabburlik yoki ahmoqlik yo'q edi; u uni hech qachon ko'rmagan darajada gapdon va kamroq g'aroyib edi. Bingli, albatta, u bilan tushlikka qaytdi; kechqurun esa missis Bennetning ixtirochiligi yana hammani undan va qizidan uzoqlashtirish uchun ishga tushdi. Yozadigan xati bo'lgan Elizabet choydan ko'p o'tmay shu maqsadda nonushta xonasiga kirdi; chunki boshqalar hammasi karta o'ynashga o'tirmoqchi bo'lgani uchun, onasining rejalariga qarshi turish uchun u kerak bo'lmasdi.

paras.en: But on returning to the drawing-room, when her letter was finished, she saw, to her infinite surprise, there was reason to fear that her mother had been too ingenious for her. On opening the door, she perceived her sister and Bingley standing together over the hearth, as if engaged in earnest conversation; and had this led to no suspicion, the faces of both, as they hastily turned round and moved away from each other, would have told it all. Their situation was awkward enough; but hers she thought was still worse. Not a syllable was uttered by either; and Elizabeth was on the point of going away again, when Bingley, who as well as the other had sat down, suddenly rose, and whispering a few words to her sister, ran out of the room.
paras.uz: Lekin xati tugagach, mehmonxonaga qaytganida, u cheksiz hayrat bilan onasi uning uchun haddan tashqari ayyor bo'lganidan qo'rqish uchun asos borligini ko'rdi. Eshikni ochib, u opasi va Binglining go'yo jiddiy suhbat bilan band bo'lgandek kamin oldida birga turganini sezdi; agar bu hech qanday shubhaga olib kelmaganida ham, ular shoshilib o'girilib, bir-biridan uzoqlashganda ikkalasining yuzlari hammasini aytib bergan bo'lardi. Ularning ahvoli yetarlicha noqulay edi; lekin uning o'ylashicha, o'ziniki undan ham yomonroq edi. Hech biri bir bo'g'in ham aytmadi; Elizabet yana ketmoqchi bo'lib turganda, ikkinchisi kabi o'tirib olgan Bingli to'satdan o'rnidan turdi va opasiga bir necha so'z pichirlab, xonadan yugurib chiqdi.

paras.en: Jane could have no reserves from Elizabeth, where confidence would give pleasure; and instantly embracing her, acknowledged, with the liveliest emotion, that she was the happiest creature in the world.
paras.uz: Ishonch zavq bag'ishlaydigan joyda Jeyn Elizabetdan hech narsa yashira olmasdi; va darhol uni quchoqlab, eng jo'shqin hayajon bilan o'zi dunyodagi eng baxtli mavjudot ekanini tan oldi.

paras.en: “'Tis too much!” she added, “by far too much. I do not deserve it. Oh! why is not everybody as happy?”
paras.uz: «Bu haddan tashqari ko'p! — qo'shib qo'ydi u. — Juda ham haddan tashqari ko'p. Men bunga loyiq emasman. Oh! Nega hamma bunday baxtli emas?»

paras.en: Elizabeth's congratulations were given with a sincerity, a warmth, a delight, which words could but poorly express. Every sentence of kindness was a fresh source of happiness to Jane. But she would not allow herself to stay with her sister, or say half that remained to be said for the present.
paras.uz: Elizabetning tabriklari so'zlar zo'rg'a ifodalay oladigan samimiyat, iliqlik va zavq bilan aytildi. Har bir mehribon jumla Jeyn uchun yangi baxt manbai edi. Lekin u hozircha singlisi bilan qolishga yoki aytilishi kerak bo'lgan gaplarning yarmini aytishga o'ziga ruxsat bermadi.

paras.en: “I must go instantly to my mother;” she cried. “I would not on any account trifle with her affectionate solicitude; or allow her to hear it from anyone but myself. He is gone to my father already. Oh! Lizzy, to know that what I have to relate will give such pleasure to all my dear family! how shall I bear so much happiness!”
paras.uz: «Darhol onamning oldiga borishim kerak, — xitob qildi u. — Hech qanday holatda uning mehrli g'amxo'rligi bilan o'ynashni yoki buni mendan boshqa birovdan eshitishiga yo'l qo'ymayman. U allaqachon otamning oldiga ketdi. Oh! Lizzi, aytadiganlarim butun aziz oilamga shunchalik zavq berishini bilish! Bunchalik baxtga qanday chidayman!»

paras.en: She then hastened away to her mother, who had purposely broken up the card party, and was sitting up stairs with Kitty.
paras.uz: Keyin u ataylab karta o'yinini to'xtatib, yuqorida Ketti bilan o'tirgan onasining oldiga shoshildi.

paras.en: Elizabeth, who was left by herself, now smiled at the rapidity and ease with which an affair was finally settled, that had given them so many previous months of suspense and vexation.
paras.uz: Yolg'iz qolgan Elizabet endi ularga oldingi ko'p oylar davomida shuncha intizorlik va g'ashlik bergan ishning nihoyat qanday tez va oson hal bo'lganiga jilmaydi.

paras.en: “And this,” said she, “is the end of all his friend's anxious circumspection! of all his sister's falsehood and contrivance! the happiest, wisest, most reasonable end!”
paras.uz: «Mana, — dedi u, — uning do'stining butun tashvishli ehtiyotkorligining, singlisining butun yolg'on va hiylasining yakuni! Eng baxtli, eng oqilona, eng mantiqiy yakun!»

paras.en: In a few minutes she was joined by Bingley, whose conference with her father had been short and to the purpose.
paras.uz: Bir necha daqiqadan keyin unga otasi bilan suhbati qisqa va maqsadga muvofiq bo'lgan Bingli qo'shildi.

paras.en: “Where is your sister?” said he hastily, as he opened the door.
paras.uz: «Opangiz qayerda?» — dedi u shoshilib, eshikni ocharkan.

paras.en: “With my mother up stairs. She will be down in a moment, I dare say.”
paras.uz: «Yuqorida, onam bilan. Ishonamanki, u bir lahzada tushadi».

paras.en: He then shut the door, and, coming up to her, claimed the good wishes and affection of a sister. Elizabeth honestly and heartily expressed her delight in the prospect of their relationship. They shook hands with great cordiality; and then, till her sister came down, she had to listen to all he had to say of his own happiness, and of Jane's perfections; and in spite of his being a lover, Elizabeth really believed all his expectations of felicity to be rationally founded, because they had for basis the excellent understanding, and super-excellent disposition of Jane, and a general similarity of feeling and taste between her and himself.
paras.uz: Keyin u eshikni yopdi va uning oldiga kelib, singlining yaxshi tilaklari va mehrini talab qildi. Elizabet ularning qarindosh bo'lish istiqbolidan zavqini halol va chin dildan bildirdi. Ular katta samimiyat bilan qo'l berib ko'rishishdi; keyin, opasi tushguncha, u uning o'z baxti va Jeynning mukammalliklari haqida aytadigan hamma narsasini tinglashga majbur bo'ldi; va u oshiq bo'lishiga qaramay, Elizabet uning baxt haqidagi barcha kutishlari oqilona asoslangan ekaniga chin dildan ishondi, chunki ular Jeynning ajoyib aqli va o'ta ajoyib fe'li hamda u bilan o'zi o'rtasidagi tuyg'u va didlarning umumiy o'xshashligiga asoslangan edi.

paras.en: It was an evening of no common delight to them all; the satisfaction of Miss Bennet's mind gave a glow of such sweet animation to her face, as made her look handsomer than ever. Kitty simpered and smiled, and hoped her turn was coming soon. Mrs. Bennet could not give her consent or speak her approbation in terms warm enough to satisfy her feelings, though she talked to Bingley of nothing else for half an hour; and when Mr. Bennet joined them at supper, his voice and manner plainly showed how really happy he was.
paras.uz: Bu ularning hammasi uchun g'ayrioddiy zavqli oqshom edi; miss Bennet qalbining mamnuniyati uning yuziga shunday shirin jonlilik nurini berdiki, u har qachongidan ham go'zalroq ko'rindi. Ketti tirjayib jilmaydi va navbati tez orada kelishiga umid qildi. Missis Bennet yarim soat davomida Bingli bilan boshqa hech narsa haqida gaplashmasa ham, roziligini berish yoki ma'qullashini tuyg'ularini qondiradigan darajada qizg'in so'zlar bilan ifodalay olmadi; janob Bennet ularga kechki ovqatda qo'shilganda esa uning ovozi va muomalasi u qanchalik chinakam baxtli ekanini aniq ko'rsatdi.

paras.en: Not a word, however, passed his lips in allusion to it, till their visitor took his leave for the night; but as soon as he was gone, he turned to his daughter, and said:
paras.uz: Biroq mehmon tunga xayrlashguncha uning lablaridan bunga ishora qiluvchi bir og'iz ham so'z chiqmadi; lekin u ketishi bilanoq u qiziga o'girildi va dedi:

paras.en: “Jane, I congratulate you. You will be a very happy woman.”
paras.uz: «Jeyn, seni tabriklayman. Sen juda baxtli ayol bo'lasan».

paras.en: Jane went to him instantly, kissed him, and thanked him for his goodness.
paras.uz: Jeyn darhol uning oldiga borib, uni o'pdi va yaxshiligi uchun rahmat aytdi.

paras.en: “You are a good girl;” he replied, “and I have great pleasure in thinking you will be so happily settled. I have not a doubt of your doing very well together. Your tempers are by no means unlike. You are each of you so complying, that nothing will ever be resolved on; so easy, that every servant will cheat you; and so generous, that you will always exceed your income.”
paras.uz: «Sen yaxshi qizsan, — javob berdi u, — va sening bunchalik baxtli joylashishingni o'ylashdan katta zavq olaman. Birga juda yaxshi yashashingizga zarracha shubham yo'q. Fe'llaringiz umuman bir-biriga o'xshamaydigan emas. Ikkalangiz ham shunchalik ko'nuvchansizki, hech qachon hech narsa hal qilinmaydi; shunchalik yumshoqsizki, har bir xizmatkor sizni aldaydi; va shunchalik saxiysizki, doim daromadingizdan oshib ketasiz».

paras.en: “I hope not so. Imprudence or thoughtlessness in money matters would be unpardonable in me.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, bunday emas. Pul masalalarida ehtiyotsizlik yoki beparvolik menda kechirib bo'lmas bo'lardi».

paras.en: “Exceed their income! My dear Mr. Bennet,” cried his wife, “what are you talking of? Why, he has four or five thousand a year, and very likely more.” Then addressing her daughter, “Oh! my dear, dear Jane, I am so happy! I am sure I shan't get a wink of sleep all night. I knew how it would be. I always said it must be so, at last. I was sure you could not be so beautiful for nothing! I remember, as soon as ever I saw him, when he first came into Hertfordshire last year, I thought how likely it was that you should come together. Oh! he is the handsomest young man that ever was seen!”
paras.uz: «Daromadidan oshib ketishmi! Aziz janob Bennet, — xitob qildi xotini, — nima deyapsiz? Axir uning yiliga to'rt-besh ming, ehtimol undan ham ko'p daromadi bor». Keyin qiziga murojaat qilib: «Oh! Aziz, aziz Jeynim, shunchalik baxtliman! Ishonchim komilki, butun tun ko'z yummayman. Qanday bo'lishini bilgandim. Men doim oxir-oqibat shunday bo'lishi kerak, deganman. Bunchalik go'zalliging bekorga emasligiga amin edim! Esimda, o'tgan yili u Xertfordshirga birinchi kelganida, uni ko'rishim bilanoq sizlarning birga bo'lishingiz qanchalik ehtimolli ekanini o'ylagan edim. Oh! U hech qachon ko'rilgan eng chiroyli yosh yigit!»

paras.en: Wickham, Lydia, were all forgotten. Jane was beyond competition her favourite child. At that moment, she cared for no other. Her younger sisters soon began to make interest with her for objects of happiness which she might in future be able to dispense.
paras.uz: Uikhem, Lidiya — hammasi unutildi. Jeyn hech qanday raqobatsiz uning sevimli farzandi edi. O'sha lahzada u boshqa hech kimga ahamiyat bermasdi. Kichik opa-singillari tez orada u kelajakda tarqata oladigan baxt obyektlari uchun undan iltifot so'ray boshlashdi.

paras.en: Mary petitioned for the use of the library at Netherfield; and Kitty begged very hard for a few balls there every winter.
paras.uz: Meri Nezerfilddagi kutubxonadan foydalanishni so'radi; Ketti esa u yerda har qishda bir nechta bal o'tkazishni juda qattiq iltimos qildi.

paras.en: Bingley, from this time, was of course a daily visitor at Longbourn; coming frequently before breakfast, and always remaining till after supper; unless when some barbarous neighbour, who could not be enough detested, had given him an invitation to dinner which he thought himself obliged to accept.
paras.uz: Shu vaqtdan boshlab Bingli, albatta, Longbornning kundalik mehmoni bo'ldi; ko'pincha nonushtadan oldin kelar va doim kechki ovqatdan keyingacha qolardi; agar yetarlicha nafratlanib bo'lmaydigan biror vahshiy qo'shni unga qabul qilishga majbur deb hisoblagan tushlik taklifini bermagan bo'lsa.

paras.en: Elizabeth had now but little time for conversation with her sister; for while he was present, Jane had no attention to bestow on anyone else; but she found herself considerably useful to both of them in those hours of separation that must sometimes occur. In the absence of Jane, he always attached himself to Elizabeth, for the pleasure of talking of her; and when Bingley was gone, Jane constantly sought the same means of relief.
paras.uz: Endi Elizabetning opasi bilan suhbatlashishga vaqti kam edi; chunki u huzurida bo'lganda, Jeyn boshqa hech kimga e'tibor bera olmasdi; lekin u ba'zan bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan ajralish soatlarida ikkalasiga ham ancha foydali ekanini ko'rdi. Jeyn yo'qligida u doim u haqida gapirish zavqi uchun Elizabetga yopishardi; Bingli ketgach esa, Jeyn doimiy ravishda xuddi shunday yengillik vositasini izlardi.

paras.en: “He has made me so happy,” said she, one evening, “by telling me that he was totally ignorant of my being in town last spring! I had not believed it possible.”
paras.uz: «U meni shunchalik baxtli qildi, — dedi u bir kuni kechqurun, — o'tgan bahorda Londonda ekanimdan butunlay bexabar bo'lganini aytib! Bunga ishonish mumkin deb o'ylamagan edim».

paras.en: “I suspected as much,” replied Elizabeth. “But how did he account for it?”
paras.uz: «Men ham shundan gumon qilgandim, — javob berdi Elizabet. — Lekin u buni qanday tushuntirdi?»

paras.en: “It must have been his sister's doing. They were certainly no friends to his acquaintance with me, which I cannot wonder at, since he might have chosen so much more advantageously in many respects. But when they see, as I trust they will, that their brother is happy with me, they will learn to be contented, and we shall be on good terms again; though we can never be what we once were to each other.”
paras.uz: «Bu uning opa-singillarining ishi bo'lsa kerak. Ular, albatta, uning men bilan tanishligiga do'st emasdilar, bunga hayron bo'la olmayman, chunki u ko'p jihatdan ancha foydaliroq tanlov qilishi mumkin edi. Lekin ular, umid qilamanki, akalari men bilan baxtli ekanini ko'rganlarida, qanoatlanishni o'rganishadi va biz yana yaxshi munosabatda bo'lamiz; garchi biz bir-birimiz uchun hech qachon bir paytdagidek bo'la olmasak ham».

paras.en: “That is the most unforgiving speech,” said Elizabeth, “that I ever heard you utter. Good girl! It would vex me, indeed, to see you again the dupe of Miss Bingley's pretended regard.”
paras.uz: «Bu men sendan eshitgan eng kechirimsiz gap, — dedi Elizabet. — Yaxshi qiz! Seni yana miss Binglining soxta mehrining aldovchisi bo'lganingni ko'rish meni haqiqatan ham g'ashlantirardi».

paras.en: “Would you believe it, Lizzy, that when he went to town last November, he really loved me, and nothing but a persuasion of my being indifferent would have prevented his coming down again!”
paras.uz: «Ishonasanmi, Lizzi, o'tgan noyabrda Londonga ketganida u meni chindan ham sevgan va faqat mening befarqligimga ishonch uni yana kelishdan to'xtatgan!»

paras.en: “He made a little mistake to be sure; but it is to the credit of his modesty.”
paras.uz: «U, albatta, biroz xato qilgan; lekin bu uning kamtarligiga sharaf keltiradi».

paras.en: This naturally introduced a panegyric from Jane on his diffidence, and the little value he put on his own good qualities. Elizabeth was pleased to find that he had not betrayed the interference of his friend; for, though Jane had the most generous and forgiving heart in the world, she knew it was a circumstance which must prejudice her against him.
paras.uz: Bu tabiiy ravishda Jeyndan uning tortinchoqligi va o'zining yaxshi fazilatlariga qanchalik kam baho berishi haqida maqtovga sabab bo'ldi. Elizabet uning do'stining aralashuvini oshkor qilmaganidan xursand bo'ldi; chunki Jeynning qalbi dunyodagi eng olijanob va kechirimli qalb bo'lsa ham, u bu uni unga qarshi xurofotga solishi kerak bo'lgan holat ekanini bilardi.

paras.en: “I am certainly the most fortunate creature that ever existed!” cried Jane. “Oh! Lizzy, why am I thus singled from my family, and blessed above them all! If I could but see you as happy! If there were but such another man for you!”
paras.uz: «Men, albatta, hech qachon mavjud bo'lgan eng omadli mavjudotman! — xitob qildi Jeyn. — Oh! Lizzi, nega men oilamdan shunday ajratib olinib, ularning hammasidan ortiq baxtga muyassar bo'ldim! Seni ham shunday baxtli ko'ra olsam edi! Sen uchun ham shunday erkak bo'lsa edi!»

paras.en: “If you were to give me forty such men, I never could be so happy as you. Till I have your disposition, your goodness, I never can have your happiness. No, no, let me shift for myself; and, perhaps, if I have very good luck, I may meet with another Mr. Collins in time.”
paras.uz: «Agar menga shunday qirqta erkak bersang ham, hech qachon sen kabi baxtli bo'la olmasdim. Sening fe'ling, sening yaxshiligingga ega bo'lmagunimcha, sening baxtingga hech qachon ega bo'la olmayman. Yo'q, yo'q, menga o'zimga o'zim g'amxo'rlik qilishga ruxsat ber; ehtimol, agar juda omadim kelsa, vaqt o'tib yana bir janob Kollinzni uchratarman».

paras.en: The situation of affairs in the Longbourn family could not be long a secret. Mrs. Bennet was privileged to whisper it to Mrs. Phillips, and she ventured, without any permission, to do the same by all her neighbours in Meryton.
paras.uz: Longborn oilasidagi ishlarning holati uzoq sir bo'lib qola olmadi. Missis Bennet buni missis Fillipsga pichirlash imtiyoziga ega edi, u esa hech qanday ruxsatsiz Meritondagi barcha qo'shnilariga xuddi shunday qilishga jur'at etdi.

paras.en: The Bennets were speedily pronounced to be the luckiest family in the world, though only a few weeks before, when Lydia had first run away, they had been generally proved to be marked out for misfortune.
paras.uz: Bennetlar tez orada dunyodagi eng omadli oila deb e'lon qilindi, garchi atigi bir necha hafta oldin, Lidiya birinchi qochib ketganda, ular umuman baxtsizlikka mahkum ekani isbotlangan bo'lsa ham.

gloss.ex: Yes, he had no engagement at all for to-morrow; and her invitation was accepted with alacrity.
Every sentence of kindness was a fresh source of happiness to Jane.
Elizabeth's congratulations were given with a sincerity, a warmth, a delight, which words could but poorly express.

After this day, Jane said no more of her indifference.

chapters.title: Lady Catherine's Visit
chapters.recap_uz: Ledi Ketrin kutilmaganda kelib, Elizabetdan Darsiga turmushga chiqmasligiga va'da berishni talab qiladi. Elizabet qat'iyat bilan rad etadi.

paras.en: One morning, about a week after Bingley's engagement with Jane had been formed, as he and the females of the family were sitting together in the dining-room, their attention was suddenly drawn to the window, by the sound of a carriage; and they perceived a chaise and four driving up the lawn. It was too early in the morning for visitors, and besides, the equipage did not answer to that of any of their neighbours. The horses were post; and neither the carriage, nor the livery of the servant who preceded it, were familiar to them. As it was certain, however, that somebody was coming, Bingley instantly prevailed on Miss Bennet to avoid the confinement of such an intrusion, and walk away with him into the shrubbery. They both set off, and the conjectures of the remaining three continued, though with little satisfaction, till the door was thrown open and their visitor entered. It was Lady Catherine de Bourgh.
paras.uz: Bir kuni ertalab, Binglining Jeyn bilan unashtirilishidan taxminan bir hafta o'tib, u va oilaning ayollari ovqatxonada birga o'tirishganda, ularning e'tiborini to'satdan arava ovozi derazaga tortdi; va ular maysazor bo'ylab kelayotgan to'rt otli aravani ko'rishdi. Mehmonlar uchun ertalab haddan tashqari erta edi, bundan tashqari, ekipaj ularning qo'shnilaridan birortasinikiga mos kelmasdi. Otlar pochta otlari edi; na arava, na uning oldida kelayotgan xizmatkorning libosi ularga tanish emasdi. Biroq kimdir kelayotgani aniq bo'lgani uchun, Bingli darhol miss Bennetni bunday bostirib kelishning qamaliga tushmaslik va u bilan butazorga sayrga ketishga ko'ndirdi. Ikkalasi ham yo'lga chiqishdi va qolgan uchtasining taxminlari, garchi unchalik qoniqarsiz bo'lsa ham, eshik lang ochilib, mehmon kirguncha davom etdi. Bu ledi Ketrin de Burg edi.

paras.en: They were of course all intending to be surprised; but their astonishment was beyond their expectation; and on the part of Mrs. Bennet and Kitty, though she was perfectly unknown to them, even inferior to what Elizabeth felt.
paras.uz: Ular, albatta, hammasi hayratlanishga tayyor edilar; lekin ularning hayrati kutganlaridan ortiq edi; missis Bennet va Ketti tomonidan esa, u ularga mutlaqo notanish bo'lsa ham, Elizabet his qilganidan ham kamroq edi.

paras.en: She entered the room with an air more than usually ungracious, made no other reply to Elizabeth's salutation than a slight inclination of the head, and sat down without saying a word. Elizabeth had mentioned her name to her mother on her ladyship's entrance, though no request of introduction had been made.
paras.uz: U xonaga odatdagidan ham iltifotsizroq qiyofada kirdi, Elizabetning salomiga boshini biroz egishdan boshqa javob bermadi va bir og'iz ham gapirmay o'tirdi. Elizabet janoblari kirganda onasiga uning ismini aytgan edi, garchi tanishtirish so'ralmagan bo'lsa ham.

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet, all amazement, though flattered by having a guest of such high importance, received her with the utmost politeness. After sitting for a moment in silence, she said very stiffly to Elizabeth,
paras.uz: Butunlay hayratda bo'lgan, lekin bunchalik yuqori ahamiyatli mehmonga ega bo'lganidan mamnun missis Bennet uni eng katta xushmuomalalik bilan qabul qildi. Bir lahza jim o'tirgach, u Elizabetga juda qattiq ohangda dedi:

paras.en: “I hope you are well, Miss Bennet. That lady, I suppose, is your mother.”
paras.uz: «Umid qilamanki, yaxshisiz, miss Bennet. O'ylaymanki, o'sha xonim onangiz».

paras.en: Elizabeth replied very concisely that she was.
paras.uz: Elizabet juda qisqa qilib shunday ekanini aytdi.

paras.en: “And that I suppose is one of your sisters.”
paras.uz: «Bu esa, o'ylaymanki, opa-singillaringizdan biri».

paras.en: “Yes, madam,” said Mrs. Bennet, delighted to speak to Lady Catherine. “She is my youngest girl but one. My youngest of all is lately married, and my eldest is somewhere about the grounds, walking with a young man who, I believe, will soon become a part of the family.”
paras.uz: «Ha, xonim, — dedi ledi Ketrin bilan gaplashishdan xursand bo'lgan missis Bennet. — U mening eng kichigimdan oldingi qizim. Eng kichigim yaqinda turmushga chiqdi, to'ng'ichim esa hovli atrofida qayerdadir, menimcha, tez orada oilaning bir qismiga aylanadigan yosh yigit bilan sayr qilyapti».

paras.en: “You have a very small park here,” returned Lady Catherine after a short silence.
paras.uz: «Bu yerda juda kichik parkingiz bor ekan», — dedi ledi Ketrin qisqa sukutdan keyin.

paras.en: “It is nothing in comparison of Rosings, my lady, I dare say; but I assure you it is much larger than Sir William Lucas's.”
paras.uz: «Ishonamanki, u Rozings bilan solishtirganda hech narsa emas, janoblari; lekin sizni ishontirib aytamanki, u ser Uilyam Lukasnikidan ancha katta».

paras.en: “This must be a most inconvenient sitting room for the evening, in summer; the windows are full west.”
paras.uz: «Bu yozda kechqurun o'tirish uchun eng noqulay xona bo'lsa kerak; derazalar to'g'ri g'arbga qaragan».

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet assured her that they never sat there after dinner, and then added:
paras.uz: Missis Bennet uni tushlikdan keyin u yerda hech qachon o'tirmasliklariga ishontirdi va keyin qo'shib qo'ydi:

paras.en: “May I take the liberty of asking your ladyship whether you left Mr. and Mrs. Collins well.”
paras.uz: «Janoblaridan janob va missis Kollinzni sog'-salomat qoldirganmi, deb so'rashga jur'at qilsam bo'ladimi?»

paras.en: “Yes, very well. I saw them the night before last.”
paras.uz: «Ha, juda yaxshi. Ularni o'tgan kecha ko'rdim».

paras.en: Elizabeth now expected that she would produce a letter for her from Charlotte, as it seemed the only probable motive for her calling. But no letter appeared, and she was completely puzzled.
paras.uz: Endi Elizabet u Sharlottadan unga xat chiqaradi deb kutdi, chunki bu uning kelishining yagona ehtimoliy sababiga o'xshardi. Lekin hech qanday xat ko'rinmadi va u butunlay hayron bo'ldi.

paras.en: Mrs. Bennet, with great civility, begged her ladyship to take some refreshment; but Lady Catherine very resolutely, and not very politely, declined eating anything; and then, rising up, said to Elizabeth,
paras.uz: Missis Bennet katta xushmuomalalik bilan janoblaridan biror narsa yeyishni iltimos qildi; lekin ledi Ketrin juda qat'iy va unchalik xushmuomala bo'lmagan holda hech narsa yeyishdan bosh tortdi; keyin o'rnidan turib, Elizabetga dedi:

paras.en: “Miss Bennet, there seemed to be a prettyish kind of a little wilderness on one side of your lawn. I should be glad to take a turn in it, if you will favour me with your company.”
paras.uz: «Miss Bennet, maysazoringizning bir tomonida ancha chiroyli kichkina yovvoyi bog' borga o'xshaydi. Agar menga hamroh bo'lish iltifotini ko'rsatsangiz, unda aylanib chiqishdan xursand bo'lardim».

paras.en: “Go, my dear,” cried her mother, “and show her ladyship about the different walks. I think she will be pleased with the hermitage.”
paras.uz: «Bor, azizim, — xitob qildi onasi, — va janoblariga turli yo'laklarni ko'rsat. Menimcha, u zohid kulbasidan mamnun bo'ladi».

paras.en: Elizabeth obeyed, and running into her own room for her parasol, attended her noble guest downstairs. As they passed through the hall, Lady Catherine opened the doors into the dining-parlour and drawing-room, and pronouncing them, after a short survey, to be decent looking rooms, walked on.
paras.uz: Elizabet itoat qildi va soyaboni uchun o'z xonasiga yugurib kirib, oliyjanob mehmonini pastga kuzatib bordi. Ular zal orqali o'tishayotganda, ledi Ketrin ovqatxona va mehmonxona eshiklarini ochdi va qisqa ko'zdan kechirishdan keyin ularni tuzukkina ko'rinadigan xonalar deb e'lon qilib, yurishda davom etdi.

paras.en: Her carriage remained at the door, and Elizabeth saw that her waiting-woman was in it. They proceeded in silence along the gravel walk that led to the copse; Elizabeth was determined to make no effort for conversation with a woman who was now more than usually insolent and disagreeable.
paras.uz: Uning aravasi eshik oldida qoldi va Elizabet unda uning xizmatkor ayoli borligini ko'rdi. Ular daraxtzorga olib boradigan shag'alli yo'lak bo'ylab jimgina borishdi; Elizabet endi odatdagidan ham surbetroq va yoqimsizroq bo'lgan ayol bilan suhbatlashish uchun hech qanday harakat qilmaslikka qaror qilgan edi.

paras.en: “How could I ever think her like her nephew?” said she, as she looked in her face.
paras.uz: «Qanday qilib uni jiyaniga o'xshaydi deb o'ylay olardim?» — dedi u, uning yuziga qararkan.

paras.en: As soon as they entered the copse, Lady Catherine began in the following manner:--
paras.uz: Ular daraxtzorga kirishlari bilanoq ledi Ketrin quyidagicha boshladi:

paras.en: “You can be at no loss, Miss Bennet, to understand the reason of my journey hither. Your own heart, your own conscience, must tell you why I come.”
paras.uz: «Miss Bennet, bu yerga safarimning sababini tushunishda qiynalmasligingiz kerak. Nega kelganimni o'z qalbingiz, o'z vijdoningiz aytishi kerak».

paras.en: Elizabeth looked with unaffected astonishment.
paras.uz: Elizabet soxta bo'lmagan hayrat bilan qaradi.

paras.en: “Indeed, you are mistaken, Madam. I have not been at all able to account for the honour of seeing you here.”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham adashyapsiz, xonim. Sizni bu yerda ko'rish sharafini umuman tushuntira olmayapman».

paras.en: “Miss Bennet,” replied her ladyship, in an angry tone, “you ought to know, that I am not to be trifled with. But however insincere you may choose to be, you shall not find me so. My character has ever been celebrated for its sincerity and frankness, and in a cause of such moment as this, I shall certainly not depart from it. A report of a most alarming nature reached me two days ago. I was told that not only your sister was on the point of being most advantageously married, but that you, that Miss Elizabeth Bennet, would, in all likelihood, be soon afterwards united to my nephew, my own nephew, Mr. Darcy. Though I know it must be a scandalous falsehood, though I would not injure him so much as to suppose the truth of it possible, I instantly resolved on setting off for this place, that I might make my sentiments known to you.”
paras.uz: «Miss Bennet, — javob berdi janoblari g'azabli ohangda, — siz men bilan hazillashib bo'lmasligini bilishingiz kerak. Lekin siz qanchalik nosamimiy bo'lishni tanlamang, meni bunday topmaysiz. Mening xarakterim doim samimiyligi va ochiqligi bilan mashhur bo'lgan va bunchalik muhim ishda men, albatta, undan chekinmayman. Ikki kun oldin menga eng xavotirli tabiatdagi mish-mish yetib keldi. Menga nafaqat singlingiz eng foydali tarzda turmushga chiqish arafasida ekani, balki siz, miss Elizabet Bennet, ehtimol, tez orada jiyanim, o'z jiyanim janob Darsi bilan qo'shilishingiz aytildi. Garchi bu sharmandali yolg'on bo'lishi kerakligini bilsam ham, garchi uning haqiqat bo'lishi mumkinligini taxmin qilib, unga bunchalik zarar yetkazmasam ham, sizga tuyg'ularimni bildirish uchun darhol bu yerga yo'l olishga qaror qildim».

paras.en: “If you believed it impossible to be true,” said Elizabeth, colouring with astonishment and disdain, “I wonder you took the trouble of coming so far. What could your ladyship propose by it?”
paras.uz: «Agar siz uni haqiqat bo'lishi imkonsiz deb ishongan bo'lsangiz, — dedi Elizabet, hayrat va nafratdan qizarib, — bunchalik uzoqqa kelish zahmatini chekkaningizga hayronman. Janoblari bundan nimani ko'zlagan bo'lishi mumkin?»

paras.en: “At once to insist upon having such a report universally contradicted.”
paras.uz: «Darhol bunday mish-mish hamma joyda rad etilishini talab qilishni».

paras.en: “Your coming to Longbourn, to see me and my family,” said Elizabeth coolly, “will be rather a confirmation of it; if, indeed, such a report is in existence.”
paras.uz: «Sizning Longbornga meni va oilamni ko'rgani kelishingiz, — dedi Elizabet sovuqqonlik bilan, — aksincha uni tasdiqlaydi; agar haqiqatan ham bunday mish-mish mavjud bo'lsa».

paras.en: “If! Do you then pretend to be ignorant of it? Has it not been industriously circulated by yourselves? Do you not know that such a report is spread abroad?”
paras.uz: «Agar! Demak, siz undan bexabarman deb da'vo qilyapsizmi? U sizlar tomonidan tirishqoqlik bilan tarqatilmaganmi? Bunday mish-mish hamma joyga tarqalganini bilmaysizmi?»

paras.en: “I never heard that it was.”
paras.uz: «Hech qachon shunday ekanini eshitmaganman».

paras.en: “And can you likewise declare, that there is no foundation for it?”
paras.uz: «Va siz shuningdek buning hech qanday asosi yo'qligini e'lon qila olasizmi?»

paras.en: “I do not pretend to possess equal frankness with your ladyship. You may ask questions which I shall not choose to answer.”
paras.uz: «Men janoblari kabi ochiqlikka ega ekanimni da'vo qilmayman. Siz men javob berishni tanlamaydigan savollar berishingiz mumkin».

paras.en: “This is not to be borne. Miss Bennet, I insist on being satisfied. Has he, has my nephew, made you an offer of marriage?”
paras.uz: «Bunga chidab bo'lmaydi. Miss Bennet, qanoatlantirilishimni talab qilaman. U, jiyanim sizga nikoh taklif qildimi?»

paras.en: “Your ladyship has declared it to be impossible.”
paras.uz: «Janoblari buni imkonsiz deb e'lon qildi».

paras.en: “It ought to be so; it must be so, while he retains the use of his reason. But your arts and allurements may, in a moment of infatuation, have made him forget what he owes to himself and to all his family. You may have drawn him in.”
paras.uz: «Shunday bo'lishi kerak; u aqlini saqlar ekan, shunday bo'lishi shart. Lekin sizning hiylalaringiz va jozibalaringiz maftunlik lahzasida uni o'ziga va butun oilasiga nimadan qarzdor ekanini unutishga majbur qilgan bo'lishi mumkin. Siz uni tuzoqqa tortgan bo'lishingiz mumkin».

paras.en: “If I have, I shall be the last person to confess it.”
paras.uz: «Agar shunday qilgan bo'lsam, buni tan oladigan eng oxirgi odam men bo'laman».

paras.en: “Miss Bennet, do you know who I am? I have not been accustomed to such language as this. I am almost the nearest relation he has in the world, and am entitled to know all his dearest concerns.”
paras.uz: «Miss Bennet, men kim ekanimni bilasizmi? Men bunday tilga odatlanmaganman. Men dunyoda uning deyarli eng yaqin qarindoshiman va uning barcha eng aziz ishlarini bilishga haqqim bor».

paras.en: “But you are not entitled to know mine; nor will such behaviour as this, ever induce me to be explicit.”
paras.uz: «Lekin siz menikini bilishga haqli emassiz; bunday xatti-harakat ham meni hech qachon ochiq gapirishga undamaydi».

paras.en: “Let me be rightly understood. This match, to which you have the presumption to aspire, can never take place. No, never. Mr. Darcy is engaged to my daughter. Now what have you to say?”
paras.uz: «Meni to'g'ri tushuning. Siz intilishga jur'at etgan bu nikoh hech qachon amalga oshmaydi. Yo'q, hech qachon. Janob Darsi mening qizimga unashtirilgan. Xo'sh, endi nima deysiz?»

paras.en: “Only this; that if he is so, you can have no reason to suppose he will make an offer to me.”
paras.uz: «Faqat shuni: agar u shunday bo'lsa, uning menga taklif qilishini taxmin qilish uchun hech qanday sababingiz bo'lishi mumkin emas».

paras.en: Lady Catherine hesitated for a moment, and then replied:
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrin bir lahza ikkilandi, keyin javob berdi:

paras.en: “The engagement between them is of a peculiar kind. From their infancy, they have been intended for each other. It was the favourite wish of his mother, as well as of hers. While in their cradles, we planned the union: and now, at the moment when the wishes of both sisters would be accomplished in their marriage, to be prevented by a young woman of inferior birth, of no importance in the world, and wholly unallied to the family! Do you pay no regard to the wishes of his friends? To his tacit engagement with Miss de Bourgh? Are you lost to every feeling of propriety and delicacy? Have you not heard me say that from his earliest hours he was destined for his cousin?”
paras.uz: «Ular o'rtasidagi unashtiruv o'ziga xos turdagi. Go'dakligidanoq ular bir-biri uchun mo'ljallangan. Bu uning onasining ham, qizimning onasining ham eng sevimli orzusi edi. Ular beshikda yotganlarida biz bu ittifoqni rejalashtirgan edik; endi esa, ikkala opa-singilning istaklari ularning nikohida amalga oshishi kerak bo'lgan lahzada, past nasldan bo'lgan, dunyoda hech qanday ahamiyatga ega bo'lmagan va oilaga butunlay begona yosh ayol tomonidan to'sqinlik qilinishi! Siz uning do'stlarining istaklariga hech qanday e'tibor bermaysizmi? Uning miss de Burg bilan so'zsiz unashtiruviga-chi? Siz har qanday odob va nazokat tuyg'usini yo'qotganmisiz? Uning eng erta soatlaridanoq amakivachchasiga mo'ljallanganini aytganimni eshitmadingizmi?»

paras.en: “Yes, and I had heard it before. But what is that to me? If there is no other objection to my marrying your nephew, I shall certainly not be kept from it by knowing that his mother and aunt wished him to marry Miss de Bourgh. You both did as much as you could in planning the marriage. Its completion depended on others. If Mr. Darcy is neither by honour nor inclination confined to his cousin, why is not he to make another choice? And if I am that choice, why may not I accept him?”
paras.uz: «Ha, buni ilgari ham eshitganman. Lekin bu menga nima? Agar jiyaningizga turmushga chiqishimga boshqa hech qanday e'tiroz bo'lmasa, uning onasi va xolasi uning miss de Burgga uylanishini istaganini bilish meni bundan to'xtata olmaydi. Siz ikkalangiz nikohni rejalashtirishda qo'lingizdan kelganini qildingiz. Uning amalga oshishi boshqalarga bog'liq edi. Agar janob Darsi na sharaf, na moyillik bilan amakivachchasiga bog'langan bo'lmasa, nega u boshqa tanlov qilmasligi kerak? Va agar men o'sha tanlov bo'lsam, nega uni qabul qila olmayman?»

paras.en: “Because honour, decorum, prudence, nay, interest, forbid it. Yes, Miss Bennet, interest; for do not expect to be noticed by his family or friends, if you wilfully act against the inclinations of all. You will be censured, slighted, and despised, by everyone connected with him. Your alliance will be a disgrace; your name will never even be mentioned by any of us.”
paras.uz: «Chunki sharaf, odob, oqilonalik, yo'q, manfaat buni man etadi. Ha, miss Bennet, manfaat; chunki agar siz ataylab hammaning moyilliklariga qarshi harakat qilsangiz, uning oilasi yoki do'stlari tomonidan e'tibor topishni kutmang. Siz u bilan bog'liq har bir kishi tomonidan qoralanasiz, mensimaysiz va nafratlanasiz. Sizning ittifoqingiz sharmandalik bo'ladi; ismingizni hech birimiz hatto tilga ham olmaymiz».

paras.en: “These are heavy misfortunes,” replied Elizabeth. “But the wife of Mr. Darcy must have such extraordinary sources of happiness necessarily attached to her situation, that she could, upon the whole, have no cause to repine.”
paras.uz: «Bular og'ir baxtsizliklar, — javob berdi Elizabet. — Lekin janob Darsining xotini o'z mavqeiga muqarrar ravishda bog'liq bo'lgan shunday g'ayrioddiy baxt manbalariga ega bo'lishi kerakki, umuman olganda, u nolish uchun hech qanday sababga ega bo'lmasdi».

paras.en: “Obstinate, headstrong girl! I am ashamed of you! Is this your gratitude for my attentions to you last spring? Is nothing due to me on that score? Let us sit down. You are to understand, Miss Bennet, that I came here with the determined resolution of carrying my purpose; nor will I be dissuaded from it. I have not been used to submit to any person's whims. I have not been in the habit of brooking disappointment.”
paras.uz: «O'jar, qaysar qiz! Sizdan uyalaman! O'tgan bahorda sizga ko'rsatgan e'tiborlarim uchun minnatdorligingiz shumi? Bu borada menga hech narsa qarzdor emasmisiz? Keling, o'tiraylik. Tushunishingiz kerak, miss Bennet, men bu yerga maqsadimni amalga oshirish qat'iy qarori bilan keldim; undan meni qaytarib bo'lmaydi. Men hech kimning injiqliklariga bo'ysunishga odatlanmaganman. Hafsalam pir bo'lishiga chidashga odatlanmaganman».

paras.en: “That will make your ladyship's situation at present more pitiable; but it will have no effect on me.”
paras.uz: «Bu janoblarining hozirgi ahvolini yanada achinarli qiladi; lekin menga hech qanday ta'sir qilmaydi».

paras.en: “I will not be interrupted. Hear me in silence. My daughter and my nephew are formed for each other. They are descended, on the maternal side, from the same noble line; and, on the father's, from respectable, honourable, and ancient--though untitled--families. Their fortune on both sides is splendid. They are destined for each other by the voice of every member of their respective houses; and what is to divide them? The upstart pretensions of a young woman without family, connections, or fortune. Is this to be endured! But it must not, shall not be. If you were sensible of your own good, you would not wish to quit the sphere in which you have been brought up.”
paras.uz: «Gapimni bo'lmang. Meni jimgina tinglang. Qizim va jiyanim bir-biri uchun yaratilgan. Ular ona tomonidan bir xil oliyjanob nasldan; ota tomonidan esa unvonsiz bo'lsa ham, hurmatli, sharafli va qadimiy oilalardan. Ikkala tomonda ham ularning boyligi ajoyib. Ular o'z xonadonlarining har bir a'zosining ovozi bilan bir-biriga mo'ljallangan; ularni nima ajratishi kerak? Oilasi, aloqalari yoki boyligi bo'lmagan yosh ayolning yangi boyigan da'volari. Bunga chidash mumkinmi! Lekin bunday bo'lmasligi kerak, bo'lmaydi. Agar siz o'z manfaatingizni anglaganingizda, tarbiyalangan doirangizni tark etishni istamagan bo'lardingiz».

paras.en: “In marrying your nephew, I should not consider myself as quitting that sphere. He is a gentleman; I am a gentleman's daughter; so far we are equal.”
paras.uz: «Jiyaningizga turmushga chiqib, men o'zimni o'sha doirani tark etayotgan deb hisoblamagan bo'lardim. U janob; men janobning qiziman; shu jihatdan biz tengmiz».

paras.en: “True. You are a gentleman's daughter. But who was your mother? Who are your uncles and aunts? Do not imagine me ignorant of their condition.”
paras.uz: «To'g'ri. Siz janobning qizisiz. Lekin onangiz kim edi? Tog'alaringiz va xolalaringiz kim? Meni ularning ahvolidan bexabar deb tasavvur qilmang».

paras.en: “Whatever my connections may be,” said Elizabeth, “if your nephew does not object to them, they can be nothing to you.”
paras.uz: «Mening qarindoshlarim qanday bo'lmasin, — dedi Elizabet, — agar jiyaningiz ularga e'tiroz bildirmasa, ular siz uchun hech narsa bo'lishi mumkin emas».

paras.en: “Tell me once for all, are you engaged to him?”
paras.uz: «Menga bir marta va abadiy ayting, siz unga unashtirilganmisiz?»

paras.en: Though Elizabeth would not, for the mere purpose of obliging Lady Catherine, have answered this question, she could not but say, after a moment's deliberation:
paras.uz: Garchi Elizabet faqat ledi Ketrinni xursand qilish uchun bu savolga javob bermagan bo'lsa ham, bir lahza o'ylab, aytmay qololmadi:

paras.en: “I am not.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q».

paras.en: Lady Catherine seemed pleased.
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrin mamnun ko'rindi.

paras.en: “And will you promise me, never to enter into such an engagement?”
paras.uz: «Va menga hech qachon bunday unashtiruvga kirmaslikka va'da berasizmi?»

paras.en: “I will make no promise of the kind.”
paras.uz: «Men bunday va'da bermayman».

paras.en: “Miss Bennet I am shocked and astonished. I expected to find a more reasonable young woman. But do not deceive yourself into a belief that I will ever recede. I shall not go away till you have given me the assurance I require.”
paras.uz: «Miss Bennet, men hayratda va dahshatdaman. Men oqilonaroq yosh ayolni topishni kutgan edim. Lekin men qachondir chekinaman degan ishonch bilan o'zingizni aldamang. Siz men talab qilgan kafolatni bermaguningizcha ketmayman».

paras.en: “And I certainly never shall give it. I am not to be intimidated into anything so wholly unreasonable. Your ladyship wants Mr. Darcy to marry your daughter; but would my giving you the wished-for promise make their marriage at all more probable? Supposing him to be attached to me, would my refusing to accept his hand make him wish to bestow it on his cousin? Allow me to say, Lady Catherine, that the arguments with which you have supported this extraordinary application have been as frivolous as the application was ill-judged. You have widely mistaken my character, if you think I can be worked on by such persuasions as these. How far your nephew might approve of your interference in his affairs, I cannot tell; but you have certainly no right to concern yourself in mine. I must beg, therefore, to be importuned no farther on the subject.”
paras.uz: «Men esa uni, albatta, hech qachon bermayman. Meni bunchalik butunlay asossiz narsaga qo'rqitib bo'lmaydi. Janoblari janob Darsining qizingizga uylanishini istaydi; lekin men sizga istalgan va'dani berishim ularning nikohini umuman ehtimolroq qiladimi? Agar u menga bog'langan deb faraz qilsak, mening uning qo'lini qabul qilishdan bosh tortishim uni uni amakivachchasiga berishni istashga majbur qiladimi? Aytishga ruxsat bering, ledi Ketrin, siz bu g'ayrioddiy murojaatni qo'llab-quvvatlagan dalillar murojaatning o'zi qanchalik noto'g'ri o'ylangan bo'lsa, shunchalik arzimas bo'ldi. Agar meni bunday ko'ndirishlar bilan ta'sir qilish mumkin deb o'ylasangiz, xarakterimni juda noto'g'ri tushungansiz. Jiyaningiz sizning uning ishlariga aralashuvingizni qanchalik ma'qullashi mumkinligini ayta olmayman; lekin sizning menikiga aralashishga, albatta, hech qanday haqqingiz yo'q. Shuning uchun bu mavzuda boshqa bezovta qilinmasligimni iltimos qilishim kerak».

paras.en: “Not so hasty, if you please. I have by no means done. To all the objections I have already urged, I have still another to add. I am no stranger to the particulars of your youngest sister's infamous elopement. I know it all; that the young man's marrying her was a patched-up business, at the expence of your father and uncles. And is such a girl to be my nephew's sister? Is her husband, is the son of his late father's steward, to be his brother? Heaven and earth!--of what are you thinking? Are the shades of Pemberley to be thus polluted?”
paras.uz: «Shoshilmang, iltimos. Men umuman gapimni tugatmadim. Men allaqachon keltirgan barcha e'tirozlarga yana bittasini qo'shishim kerak. Men eng kichik singlingizning sharmandali qochishi tafsilotlariga begona emasman. Men hammasini bilaman; yosh yigitning unga uylanishi otangiz va tog'alaringiz hisobiga yamalgan ish bo'lganini. Va shunday qiz mening jiyanimning singlisi bo'lishi kerakmi? Uning eri, uning marhum otasining boshqaruvchisining o'g'li uning qarindoshi bo'lishi kerakmi? Yer-u osmon! — Nima haqida o'ylayapsiz? Pemberlining soyalari shunday bulg'anishi kerakmi?»

paras.en: “You can now have nothing further to say,” she resentfully answered. “You have insulted me in every possible method. I must beg to return to the house.”
paras.uz: «Endi boshqa aytadigan gapingiz bo'lishi mumkin emas, — ranjigan holda javob berdi u. — Siz meni har qanday mumkin bo'lgan usulda haqorat qildingiz. Uyga qaytishga ruxsat so'rashim kerak».

paras.en: And she rose as she spoke. Lady Catherine rose also, and they turned back. Her ladyship was highly incensed.
paras.uz: Va u gapirarkan o'rnidan turdi. Ledi Ketrin ham turdi va ular ortga burilishdi. Janoblari juda g'azablangan edi.

paras.en: “You have no regard, then, for the honour and credit of my nephew! Unfeeling, selfish girl! Do you not consider that a connection with you must disgrace him in the eyes of everybody?”
paras.uz: «Demak, siz jiyanimning sharafi va obro'siga hech qanday e'tibor bermaysiz! Bag'ritosh, xudbin qiz! Siz bilan qarindoshlik uni hammaning nazarida sharmanda qilishi kerakligini o'ylamaysizmi?»

paras.en: “Lady Catherine, I have nothing further to say. You know my sentiments.”
paras.uz: «Ledi Ketrin, boshqa aytadigan gapim yo'q. Siz mening tuyg'ularimni bilasiz».

paras.en: “You are then resolved to have him?”
paras.uz: «Demak, siz unga turmushga chiqishga qaror qilgansizmi?»

paras.en: “I have said no such thing. I am only resolved to act in that manner, which will, in my own opinion, constitute my happiness, without reference to you, or to any person so wholly unconnected with me.”
paras.uz: «Men bunday narsa demadim. Men faqat sizga yoki men bilan butunlay bog'liq bo'lmagan har qanday shaxsga murojaat qilmasdan, o'z fikrimcha baxtimni tashkil etadigan tarzda harakat qilishga qaror qilganman».

paras.en: “It is well. You refuse, then, to oblige me. You refuse to obey the claims of duty, honour, and gratitude. You are determined to ruin him in the opinion of all his friends, and make him the contempt of the world.”
paras.uz: «Yaxshi. Demak, siz meni xursand qilishdan bosh tortasiz. Burch, sharaf va minnatdorlik talablariga bo'ysunishdan bosh tortasiz. Siz uni barcha do'stlarining fikrida barbod qilishga va uni dunyoning nafrat obyektiga aylantirishga qaror qilgansiz».

paras.en: “Neither duty, nor honour, nor gratitude,” replied Elizabeth, “have any possible claim on me, in the present instance. No principle of either would be violated by my marriage with Mr. Darcy. And with regard to the resentment of his family, or the indignation of the world, if the former were excited by his marrying me, it would not give me one moment's concern--and the world in general would have too much sense to join in the scorn.”
paras.uz: «Na burch, na sharaf, na minnatdorlik, — javob berdi Elizabet, — hozirgi holatda menga hech qanday da'voga ega emas. Mening janob Darsiga turmushga chiqishim bilan ularning hech birining biror tamoyili buzilmaydi. Uning oilasining g'azabi yoki dunyoning noroziligiga kelsak, agar birinchisi uning menga uylanishi bilan qo'zg'alsa, bu meni bir lahza ham tashvishga solmasdi — dunyo esa umuman nafratga qo'shilish uchun haddan tashqari aqlli bo'lardi».

paras.en: “And this is your real opinion! This is your final resolve! Very well. I shall now know how to act. Do not imagine, Miss Bennet, that your ambition will ever be gratified. I came to try you. I hoped to find you reasonable; but, depend upon it, I will carry my point.”
paras.uz: «Demak, bu sizning haqiqiy fikringiz! Bu sizning yakuniy qaroringiz! Juda yaxshi. Endi qanday harakat qilishni bilaman. O'ylamang, miss Bennet, sizning shuhratparastligingiz qachondir qondiriladi. Men sizni sinash uchun keldim. Sizni oqilona topishga umid qildim; lekin ishonavering, men maqsadimga erishaman».

paras.en: In this manner Lady Catherine talked on, till they were at the door of the carriage, when, turning hastily round, she added, “I take no leave of you, Miss Bennet. I send no compliments to your mother. You deserve no such attention. I am most seriously displeased.”
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrin shu tarzda gapirishda davom etdi, toki ular arava eshigi oldiga yetib kelishdi, shunda u shoshilib o'girilib, qo'shib qo'ydi: «Siz bilan xayrlashmayman, miss Bennet. Onangizga salom yo'llamayman. Siz bunday e'tiborga loyiq emassiz. Men juda jiddiy norozi».

paras.en: Elizabeth made no answer; and without attempting to persuade her ladyship to return into the house, walked quietly into it herself. She heard the carriage drive away as she proceeded up stairs. Her mother impatiently met her at the door of the dressing-room, to ask why Lady Catherine would not come in again and rest herself.
paras.uz: Elizabet javob bermadi; va janoblarini uyga qaytishga ko'ndirishga urinmasdan, o'zi jimgina uyga kirdi. U yuqoriga chiqayotganda arava jo'nab ketganini eshitdi. Onasi uni kiyinish xonasining eshigida sabrsizlik bilan kutib olib, nega ledi Ketrin yana kirib, dam olmaganini so'radi.

paras.en: “She did not choose it,” said her daughter, “she would go.”
paras.uz: «U buni xohlamadi, — dedi qizi, — u ketishni istadi».

paras.en: “She is a very fine-looking woman! and her calling here was prodigiously civil! for she only came, I suppose, to tell us the Collinses were well. She is on her road somewhere, I dare say, and so, passing through Meryton, thought she might as well call on you. I suppose she had nothing particular to say to you, Lizzy?”
paras.uz: «U juda chiroyli ko'rinishli ayol! Uning bu yerga kelishi nihoyatda xushmuomala edi! Chunki u, menimcha, faqat bizga Kollinzlar sog'-salomat ekanini aytish uchun kelgan. Ishonamanki, u qayergadir yo'lda va Meriton orqali o'tayotib, senga kirib o'tishni ma'qul ko'rgan. O'ylaymanki, uning senga aytadigan alohida gapi yo'q edi, Lizzi?»

paras.en: Elizabeth was forced to give into a little falsehood here; for to acknowledge the substance of their conversation was impossible.
paras.uz: Bu yerda Elizabet ozgina yolg'onga berilishga majbur bo'ldi; chunki ularning suhbati mazmunini tan olish imkonsiz edi.
