chapters.title: Mr. Collins Warns
chapters.recap_uz: Janob Bennet Kollinzdan xat oladi: Elizabet Darsiga turmushga chiqishi mumkin, Ledi Ketrin bunga qarshi. Janob Bennet buni kulgili deb hisoblaydi, chunki u Darsi Elizabetni yoqtirmaydi deb o'ylaydi.

paras.en: The discomposure of spirits which this extraordinary visit threw Elizabeth into, could not be easily overcome; nor could she, for many hours, learn to think of it less than incessantly. Lady Catherine, it appeared, had actually taken the trouble of this journey from Rosings, for the sole purpose of breaking off her supposed engagement with Mr. Darcy. It was a rational scheme, to be sure! but from what the report of their engagement could originate, Elizabeth was at a loss to imagine; till she recollected that his being the intimate friend of Bingley, and her being the sister of Jane, was enough, at a time when the expectation of one wedding made everybody eager for another, to supply the idea. She had not herself forgotten to feel that the marriage of her sister must bring them more frequently together. And her neighbours at Lucas Lodge, therefore (for through their communication with the Collinses, the report, she concluded, had reached Lady Catherine), had only set that down as almost certain and immediate, which she had looked forward to as possible at some future time.
paras.uz: Bu g'ayrioddiy tashrif Elizabetni solgan ruhiy bezovtalikni osonlikcha yengib bo'lmasdi; u ko'p soatlar davomida bu haqda to'xtovsiz o'ylashdan kamroq o'ylashni o'rgana olmadi. Ma'lum bo'lishicha, ledi Ketrin haqiqatan ham faqat uning janob Darsi bilan taxminiy unashtiruvini buzish maqsadida Rozingsdan bu safar zahmatini chekkan edi. Bu, albatta, oqilona reja edi! Lekin ularning unashtiruvi haqidagi mish-mish qayerdan kelib chiqishi mumkinligini Elizabet tasavvur qila olmadi; toki uning Binglining yaqin do'sti, o'zining esa Jeynning singlisi ekani bir to'yni kutish hammani boshqasiga intiltirgan paytda bu fikrni berish uchun yetarli ekanini esladi. Uning o'zi ham opasining nikohi ularni tez-tez birga bo'lishga olib kelishini his qilishni unutmagan edi. Shuning uchun Lukas Lojdagi qo'shnilari (chunki u mish-mish ularning Kollinzlar bilan yozishmalari orqali ledi Ketringa yetib borgan, degan xulosaga keldi) u kelajakda qachondir mumkin deb kutgan narsani faqat deyarli aniq va darhol bo'ladigan narsa sifatida yozib qo'yishgan edi.

paras.en: In revolving Lady Catherine's expressions, however, she could not help feeling some uneasiness as to the possible consequence of her persisting in this interference. From what she had said of her resolution to prevent their marriage, it occurred to Elizabeth that she must meditate an application to her nephew; and how he might take a similar representation of the evils attached to a connection with her, she dared not pronounce. She knew not the exact degree of his affection for his aunt, or his dependence on her judgment, but it was natural to suppose that he thought much higher of her ladyship than she could do; and it was certain that, in enumerating the miseries of a marriage with one, whose immediate connections were so unequal to his own, his aunt would address him on his weakest side. With his notions of dignity, he would probably feel that the arguments, which to Elizabeth had appeared weak and ridiculous, contained much good sense and solid reasoning.
paras.uz: Biroq ledi Ketrinning iboralarini aylantirib o'ylarkan, u uning bu aralashuvni davom ettirishining mumkin bo'lgan oqibati haqida biroz bezovtalik his qilmay qololmadi. Uning ularning nikohini to'xtatish qarori haqida aytganlaridan Elizabetning xayoliga u jiyaniga murojaat qilishni o'ylayotgan bo'lsa kerak, degan fikr keldi; va u u bilan qarindoshlikka bog'liq yomonliklarning xuddi shunday tasvirini qanday qabul qilishi mumkinligini aytishga jur'at etmadi. U uning xolasiga bo'lgan mehrining aniq darajasini yoki uning mulohazasiga qanchalik tayanishini bilmasdi, lekin u janoblari haqida o'zidan ancha yuqori fikrda deb taxmin qilish tabiiy edi; va xolasi yaqin qarindoshlari uning o'zinikiga bunchalik teng bo'lmagan ayol bilan nikohning azoblarini sanab, unga eng zaif tomonidan murojaat qilishi aniq edi. Uning salobat haqidagi tushunchalari bilan u, ehtimol, Elizabetga zaif va kulgili ko'ringan dalillarda ko'p sog'lom aql va mustahkam mulohaza borligini his qilardi.

paras.en: If he had been wavering before as to what he should do, which had often seemed likely, the advice and entreaty of so near a relation might settle every doubt, and determine him at once to be as happy as dignity unblemished could make him. In that case he would return no more. Lady Catherine might see him in her way through town; and his engagement to Bingley of coming again to Netherfield must give way.
paras.uz: Agar u ilgari nima qilishi kerakligi haqida ikkilanayotgan bo'lsa — bu ko'pincha ehtimolli ko'ringan edi — bunchalik yaqin qarindoshning maslahati va iltimosi har qanday shubhani hal qilishi va uni darhol beg'ubor salobat qila oladigan darajada baxtli bo'lishga qaror qildirishi mumkin edi. U holda u boshqa qaytmasdi. Ledi Ketrin uni London orqali o'tayotib ko'rishi mumkin edi; uning Binglige Nezerfildga yana kelish haqidagi va'dasi esa bekor bo'lishi kerak edi.

paras.en: “If, therefore, an excuse for not keeping his promise should come to his friend within a few days,” she added, “I shall know how to understand it. I shall then give over every expectation, every wish of his constancy. If he is satisfied with only regretting me, when he might have obtained my affections and hand, I shall soon cease to regret him at all.”
paras.uz: «Shuning uchun agar bir necha kun ichida uning do'stiga va'dasini bajarmaslik uchun bahona kelsa, — qo'shib qo'ydi u, — buni qanday tushunishni bilaman. Shunda uning sodiqligi haqidagi har qanday kutishdan, har qanday istakdan voz kechaman. Agar u mening mehrim va qo'limni qo'lga kiritishi mumkin bo'lgan paytda men uchun faqat afsuslanish bilan qanoatlansa, men ham tez orada u uchun umuman afsuslanishni to'xtataman».

paras.en: The surprise of the rest of the family, on hearing who their visitor had been, was very great; but they obligingly satisfied it, with the same kind of supposition which had appeased Mrs. Bennet's curiosity; and Elizabeth was spared from much teasing on the subject.
paras.uz: Mehmon kim bo'lganini eshitib, oilaning qolgan a'zolarining hayrati juda katta edi; lekin ular uni missis Bennetning qiziqishini tinchitgan xuddi shu turdagi taxmin bilan iltifot qilib qondirishdi; Elizabet esa bu mavzuda ko'p bezovtalanishdan xalos bo'ldi.

paras.en: The next morning, as she was going downstairs, she was met by her father, who came out of his library with a letter in his hand.
paras.uz: Ertasi kuni ertalab u pastga tushayotganda, qo'lida xat bilan kutubxonasidan chiqqan otasi uni kutib oldi.

paras.en: “Lizzy,” said he, “I was going to look for you; come into my room.”
paras.uz: «Lizzi, — dedi u, — seni izlamoqchi edim; xonamga kir».

paras.en: She followed him thither; and her curiosity to know what he had to tell her was heightened by the supposition of its being in some manner connected with the letter he held. It suddenly struck her that it might be from Lady Catherine; and she anticipated with dismay all the consequent explanations.
paras.uz: U uning ortidan u yerga ergashdi; va unga nima aytishini bilishga qiziqishi bu uning qo'lidagi xat bilan qandaydir tarzda bog'liq degan taxmin bilan kuchaydi. Uning xayoliga to'satdan bu ledi Ketrindan bo'lishi mumkin degan fikr keldi; va u buning natijasidagi barcha tushuntirishlarni vahima bilan kutdi.

paras.en: She followed her father to the fire place, and they both sat down. He then said,
paras.uz: U otasining ortidan kamin oldiga bordi va ikkalasi ham o'tirishdi. Keyin u dedi:

paras.en: “I have received a letter this morning that has astonished me exceedingly. As it principally concerns yourself, you ought to know its contents. I did not know before, that I had two daughters on the brink of matrimony. Let me congratulate you on a very important conquest.”
paras.uz: «Bugun ertalab meni nihoyatda hayratga solgan xat oldim. U asosan senga tegishli bo'lgani uchun, sen uning mazmunini bilishing kerak. Nikoh bo'sag'asida ikki qizim borligini avval bilmagan ekanman. Seni juda muhim zabt bilan tabriklashga ruxsat ber».

paras.en: The colour now rushed into Elizabeth's cheeks in the instantaneous conviction of its being a letter from the nephew, instead of the aunt; and she was undetermined whether most to be pleased that he explained himself at all, or offended that his letter was not rather addressed to herself; when her father continued:
paras.uz: Endi bu xola emas, jiyan tomonidan yozilgan xat ekaniga bir lahzalik ishonch bilan Elizabetning yonoqlariga qon yugurdi; va u ko'proq uning umuman o'zini tushuntirganidan xursand bo'lishi kerakmi yoki xatning o'ziga yozilmaganidan ranjishi kerakmi, hal qila olmadi; shunda otasi davom etdi:

paras.en: “You look conscious. Young ladies have great penetration in such matters as these; but I think I may defy even your sagacity, to discover the name of your admirer. This letter is from Mr. Collins.”
paras.uz: «Sen buni bilgandek ko'rinasan. Yosh xonimlar bunday masalalarda katta ziyraklikka ega; lekin menimcha, hatto sening farosatingni ham muxlisingning ismini topishga chaqira olaman. Bu xat janob Kollinzdan».

paras.en: “From Mr. Collins! and what can he have to say?”
paras.uz: «Janob Kollinzdan! U nima deyishi mumkin?»

paras.en: “Something very much to the purpose of course. He begins with congratulations on the approaching nuptials of my eldest daughter, of which, it seems, he has been told by some of the good-natured, gossiping Lucases. I shall not sport with your impatience, by reading what he says on that point. What relates to yourself, is as follows: 'Having thus offered you the sincere congratulations of Mrs. Collins and myself on this happy event, let me now add a short hint on the subject of another; of which we have been advertised by the same authority. Your daughter Elizabeth, it is presumed, will not long bear the name of Bennet, after her elder sister has resigned it, and the chosen partner of her fate may be reasonably looked up to as one of the most illustrious personages in this land.'
paras.uz: «Albatta, juda maqsadga muvofiq narsa. U to'ng'ich qizimning yaqinlashib kelayotgan to'yi munosabati bilan tabriklardan boshlaydi, aftidan, bu haqda unga xushfe'l, g'iybatchi Lukaslardan kimdir aytgan. Bu borada uning aytganlarini o'qib, sabrsizligingni sinamayman. Senga tegishli qismi quyidagicha: "Shunday qilib, sizga missis Kollinz va mening bu baxtli voqea munosabati bilan samimiy tabriklarimizni bildirgach, endi xuddi shu manba orqali xabardor bo'lgan boshqa bir voqea mavzusida qisqa ishora qo'shishga ruxsat bering. Taxmin qilinishicha, qizingiz Elizabet opasi Bennet familiyasidan voz kechgandan keyin uni uzoq ko'tarmaydi va uning taqdirining tanlangan sherigi asosli ravishda bu yurtdagi eng mashhur shaxslardan biri sifatida qaralishi mumkin".

paras.en: “Can you possibly guess, Lizzy, who is meant by this? 'This young gentleman is blessed, in a peculiar way, with every thing the heart of mortal can most desire,--splendid property, noble kindred, and extensive patronage. Yet in spite of all these temptations, let me warn my cousin Elizabeth, and yourself, of what evils you may incur by a precipitate closure with this gentleman's proposals, which, of course, you will be inclined to take immediate advantage of.'
paras.uz: Lizzi, bu bilan kim nazarda tutilganini taxmin qila olasanmi? "Bu yosh janob o'ziga xos tarzda inson qalbi eng ko'p orzu qilishi mumkin bo'lgan hamma narsa — ajoyib mulk, oliyjanob qarindoshlar va keng homiylik imkoniyatlari bilan siylangan. Shunga qaramay, bu barcha vasvasalarga qaramay, amakivachcham Elizabetni va sizni bu janobning takliflarini shoshilib qabul qilish bilan qanday yomonliklarga duch kelishingiz mumkinligidan ogohlantirishga ruxsat bering, ulardan, albatta, siz darhol foydalanishga moyil bo'lasiz".

paras.en: “Have you any idea, Lizzy, who this gentleman is? But now it comes out:
paras.uz: Lizzi, bu janob kimligini tasavvur qila olasanmi? Lekin mana endi ochiladi:

paras.en: “'My motive for cautioning you is as follows. We have reason to imagine that his aunt, Lady Catherine de Bourgh, does not look on the match with a friendly eye.'
paras.uz: "Sizni ogohlantirish sababim quyidagicha. Uning xolasi ledi Ketrin de Burg bu nikohga do'stona ko'z bilan qaramaydi deb tasavvur qilish uchun asosimiz bor".

paras.en: “Mr. Darcy, you see, is the man! Now, Lizzy, I think I have surprised you. Could he, or the Lucases, have pitched on any man within the circle of our acquaintance, whose name would have given the lie more effectually to what they related? Mr. Darcy, who never looks at any woman but to see a blemish, and who probably never looked at you in his life! It is admirable!”
paras.uz: Ko'ryapsanmi, bu janob Darsi ekan! Xo'sh, Lizzi, menimcha, seni hayratga soldim. U yoki Lukaslar tanishlarimiz davrasidagi nomi ular aytganlarini bundan samaraliroq yolg'onga chiqaradigan biror erkakni tanlay olarmidi? Hech qachon biror ayolga faqat kamchilik topish uchun qaraydigan va, ehtimol, umrida senga hech qachon qaramagan janob Darsi! Bu ajoyib!»

paras.en: Elizabeth tried to join in her father's pleasantry, but could only force one most reluctant smile. Never had his wit been directed in a manner so little agreeable to her.
paras.uz: Elizabet otasining hazillariga qo'shilishga urindi, lekin faqat bitta eng istamay chiqarilgan tabassum bilan majburan jilmaya oldi. Uning zukkoligi hech qachon unga bunchalik yoqimsiz tarzda qaratilmagan edi.

paras.en: “Are you not diverted?”
paras.uz: «Ko'nglingni ochmayaptimi?»

paras.en: “Oh! yes. Pray read on.”
paras.uz: «Oh! Ha. Iltimos, o'qishda davom eting».

paras.en: “'After mentioning the likelihood of this marriage to her ladyship last night, she immediately, with her usual condescension, expressed what she felt on the occasion; when it became apparent, that on the score of some family objections on the part of my cousin, she would never give her consent to what she termed so disgraceful a match. I thought it my duty to give the speediest intelligence of this to my cousin, that she and her noble admirer may be aware of what they are about, and not run hastily into a marriage which has not been properly sanctioned.' Mr. Collins moreover adds, 'I am truly rejoiced that my cousin Lydia's sad business has been so well hushed up, and am only concerned that their living together before the marriage took place should be so generally known.
paras.uz: «"Kecha janoblariga bu nikohning ehtimoli haqida aytganimdan keyin, u darhol odatdagi iltifoti bilan bu munosabat bilan his qilganlarini bildirdi; shunda amakivachcham tomonidagi ba'zi oilaviy e'tirozlar tufayli u o'zi shunchalik sharmandali deb atagan nikohga hech qachon roziligini bermasligi ma'lum bo'ldi. Men buni amakivachchamga iloji boricha tezroq xabar qilishni o'z burchim deb hisobladim, toki u va uning oliyjanob muxlisi nima qilayotganlaridan xabardor bo'lishsin va munosib ravishda ruxsat berilmagan nikohga shoshilib kirmasinlar". Bundan tashqari janob Kollinz qo'shadi: "Amakivachcham Lidiyaning qayg'uli ishi bunchalik yaxshi bosdi-bosdi qilinganidan chin dildan xursandman va faqat ularning nikoh bo'lishidan oldin birga yashaganlari hammaga ma'lum bo'lganidan tashvishlanaman.

paras.en: I must not, however, neglect the duties of my station, or refrain from declaring my amazement at hearing that you received the young couple into your house as soon as they were married. It was an encouragement of vice; and had I been the rector of Longbourn, I should very strenuously have opposed it. You ought certainly to forgive them, as a Christian, but never to admit them in your sight, or allow their names to be mentioned in your hearing.' That is his notion of Christian forgiveness! The rest of his letter is only about his dear Charlotte's situation, and his expectation of a young olive-branch. But, Lizzy, you look as if you did not enjoy it. You are not going to be missish, I hope, and pretend to be affronted at an idle report.
paras.uz: Biroq men o'z mavqeimning burchlarini e'tiborsiz qoldirmasligim yoki yosh juftlikni turmush qurishlari bilanoq uyingizga qabul qilganingizni eshitgandagi hayratimni bildirishdan o'zimni tiymasligim kerak. Bu illatni rag'batlantirish edi; agar men Longbornning ruhoniysi bo'lganimda, bunga qattiq qarshi chiqqan bo'lardim. Siz ularni nasroniy sifatida, albatta, kechirishingiz kerak, lekin hech qachon ularni ko'zingizga ko'rsatmasligingiz yoki ismlarini eshitishingizda tilga olinishiga yo'l qo'ymasligingiz kerak". Mana uning nasroniycha kechirim haqidagi tushunchasi! Xatining qolgan qismi faqat aziz Sharlottasining ahvoli va yosh zaytun novdasini kutishi haqida. Lekin, Lizzi, sen bundan zavqlanmayotganga o'xshaysan. Umid qilamanki, injiqlik qilib, bekorchi mish-mishdan ranjiganday ko'rinmoqchi emassan.

paras.en: For what do we live, but to make sport for our neighbours, and laugh at them in our turn?”
paras.uz: Axir biz qo'shnilarimizga ermak bo'lish va navbatimizda ularning ustidan kulishdan boshqa nima uchun yashaymiz?»

paras.en: “Oh!” cried Elizabeth, “I am excessively diverted. But it is so strange!”
paras.uz: «Oh! — xitob qildi Elizabet. — Nihoyatda ko'nglim ochildi. Lekin bu shunchalik g'alati!»

paras.en: “Yes--that is what makes it amusing. Had they fixed on any other man it would have been nothing; but his perfect indifference, and your pointed dislike, make it so delightfully absurd! Much as I abominate writing, I would not give up Mr. Collins's correspondence for any consideration. Nay, when I read a letter of his, I cannot help giving him the preference even over Wickham, much as I value the impudence and hypocrisy of my son-in-law. And pray, Lizzy, what said Lady Catherine about this report? Did she call to refuse her consent?”
paras.uz: «Ha — aynan shu uni qiziqarli qiladi. Agar ular boshqa biror erkakni tanlaganlarida, bu hech narsa bo'lmasdi; lekin uning mutlaq befarqligi va sening aniq yoqtirmasliging buni shunchalik yoqimli bema'ni qiladi! Yozishni qanchalik yomon ko'rmayin, janob Kollinz bilan yozishmalardan hech qanday evaz uchun voz kechmasdim. Yo'q, uning xatini o'qiganimda, kuyovimning surbetligi va ikkiyuzlamachiligini qanchalik qadrlasam ham, uni hatto Uikhemdan ham afzal ko'rmasdan ilojim yo'q. Ayt-chi, Lizzi, ledi Ketrin bu mish-mish haqida nima dedi? U roziligini rad etish uchun keldimi?»

paras.en: To this question his daughter replied only with a laugh; and as it had been asked without the least suspicion, she was not distressed by his repeating it. Elizabeth had never been more at a loss to make her feelings appear what they were not. It was necessary to laugh, when she would rather have cried. Her father had most cruelly mortified her, by what he said of Mr. Darcy's indifference, and she could do nothing but wonder at such a want of penetration, or fear that perhaps, instead of his seeing too little, she might have fancied too much.
paras.uz: Bu savolga qizi faqat kulgi bilan javob berdi; u zarracha ham shubhasiz berilgani uchun, u uni takrorlaganda Elizabet bezovta bo'lmadi. Elizabet hech qachon tuyg'ularini ular bo'lmagan narsadek ko'rsatishda bunchalik qiynalmagan edi. U yig'lashni afzal ko'rgan paytda kulish kerak edi. Otasi janob Darsining befarqligi haqida aytganlari bilan uni eng shafqatsizlarcha xo'rlagan edi va u bunday ziyraklik yetishmasligiga hayron bo'lishdan yoki ehtimol, u juda kam ko'rgan o'rniga o'zi juda ko'p narsani tasavvur qilgan bo'lishi mumkinligidan qo'rqishdan boshqa hech narsa qila olmadi.

gloss.ex: And her neighbours at Lucas Lodge, therefore (for through their communication with the Collinses, the report, she concluded, had reached Lady Catherine), had only set that down as almost certain…

quiz.q: Why does Mr. Bennet laugh at the letter?
o: He thinks Darcy never looks at Elizabeth except to find fault
quiz.why_uz: Elizabet esa kulish o'rniga yig'lashga tayyor.

quiz.q: How does Elizabeth feel during this conversation?
quiz.why_uz: Otasi uning yuragidagi narsadan bexabar.

chapters.title: The Second Proposal
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet Darsiga Lidiya uchun minnatdorlik bildiradi. Darsi tuyg'ulari o'zgarmaganini aytadi va Elizabet bu safar rozi bo'ladi. Ular o'tmishdagi xatolarini tan olishadi.

paras.en: Instead of receiving any such letter of excuse from his friend, as Elizabeth half expected Mr. Bingley to do, he was able to bring Darcy with him to Longbourn before many days had passed after Lady Catherine's visit. The gentlemen arrived early; and, before Mrs. Bennet had time to tell him of their having seen his aunt, of which her daughter sat in momentary dread, Bingley, who wanted to be alone with Jane, proposed their all walking out. It was agreed to. Mrs. Bennet was not in the habit of walking; Mary could never spare time; but the remaining five set off together. Bingley and Jane, however, soon allowed the others to outstrip them. They lagged behind, while Elizabeth, Kitty, and Darcy were to entertain each other. Very little was said by either; Kitty was too much afraid of him to talk; Elizabeth was secretly forming a desperate resolution; and perhaps he might be doing the same.
paras.uz: Elizabet janob Binglidan kutganidek do'stidan uzr xati olish o'rniga, u ledi Ketrinning tashrifidan keyin ko'p kun o'tmay Darsini o'zi bilan Longbornga olib kela oldi. Janoblar erta kelishdi; va missis Bennet unga xolasini ko'rganlarini aytishga ulgurmasdanoq — qizi buning uchun bir lahza qo'rquvda o'tirdi — Jeyn bilan yolg'iz qolishni istagan Bingli hammasi sayrga chiqishni taklif qildi. Bunga kelishildi. Missis Bennet sayr qilishga odatlanmagan edi; Meri hech qachon vaqt ajrata olmasdi; lekin qolgan beshtasi birga yo'lga chiqishdi. Biroq Bingli va Jeyn tez orada boshqalarga ulardan o'zib ketishga imkon berishdi. Ular ortda qolishdi, Elizabet, Ketti va Darsi esa bir-birlarini ko'ngil ochishlari kerak edi. Ularning hech biri juda kam gapirdi; Ketti undan gapirish uchun haddan tashqari qo'rqardi; Elizabet yashirincha umidsiz qaror qabul qilayotgan edi; ehtimol, u ham xuddi shunday qilayotgandir.

paras.en: They walked towards the Lucases, because Kitty wished to call upon Maria; and as Elizabeth saw no occasion for making it a general concern, when Kitty left them she went boldly on with him alone. Now was the moment for her resolution to be executed, and, while her courage was high, she immediately said:
paras.uz: Ular Lukaslar tomon yurishdi, chunki Ketti Mariyaning oldiga kirmoqchi edi; Elizabet buni umumiy ish qilishga hech qanday sabab ko'rmagani uchun, Ketti ularni tark etganda, u u bilan yolg'iz dadil davom etdi. Endi uning qarorini amalga oshirish lahzasi keldi va jasorati baland bo'lgan paytda u darhol dedi:

paras.en: “Mr. Darcy, I am a very selfish creature; and, for the sake of giving relief to my own feelings, care not how much I may be wounding yours. I can no longer help thanking you for your unexampled kindness to my poor sister. Ever since I have known it, I have been most anxious to acknowledge to you how gratefully I feel it. Were it known to the rest of my family, I should not have merely my own gratitude to express.”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsi, men juda xudbin mavjudotman; va o'z tuyg'ularimga yengillik berish uchun sizning tuyg'ularingizni qanchalik yaralayotganimga ahamiyat bermayman. Bechora singlimga ko'rsatgan misli ko'rilmagan mehribonligingiz uchun sizga rahmat aytmasdan endi tura olmayman. Buni bilganimdan beri sizga buni qanchalik minnatdorlik bilan his qilayotganimni tan olishni juda istab kelaman. Agar bu oilamning qolgan a'zolariga ma'lum bo'lganida, men faqat o'z minnatdorligimni ifodalashim bilan cheklanmagan bo'lardim».

paras.en: “I am sorry, exceedingly sorry,” replied Darcy, in a tone of surprise and emotion, “that you have ever been informed of what may, in a mistaken light, have given you uneasiness. I did not think Mrs. Gardiner was so little to be trusted.”
paras.uz: «Afsusdaman, nihoyatda afsusdaman, — javob berdi Darsi hayrat va hayajon ohangida, — sizga noto'g'ri nurda bezovtalik bergan bo'lishi mumkin bo'lgan narsa haqida qachondir xabar berilganidan. Missis Gardinerga bunchalik kam ishonish mumkin deb o'ylamagan edim».

paras.en: “You must not blame my aunt. Lydia's thoughtlessness first betrayed to me that you had been concerned in the matter; and, of course, I could not rest till I knew the particulars. Let me thank you again and again, in the name of all my family, for that generous compassion which induced you to take so much trouble, and bear so many mortifications, for the sake of discovering them.”
paras.uz: «Xolamni ayblamasligingiz kerak. Lidiyaning beparvoligi birinchi bo'lib sizning bu ishda ishtirok etganingizni menga oshkor qildi; va, albatta, tafsilotlarni bilmaguncha tinchiy olmadim. Butun oilam nomidan sizni ularni topish uchun shunchalik ko'p tashvish chekishga va shunchalik ko'p xo'rlanishlarga chidashga undagan o'sha olijanob hamdardligingiz uchun sizga qayta-qayta rahmat aytishga ruxsat bering».

paras.en: “If you will thank me,” he replied, “let it be for yourself alone. That the wish of giving happiness to you might add force to the other inducements which led me on, I shall not attempt to deny. But your family owe me nothing. Much as I respect them, I believe I thought only of you.”
paras.uz: «Agar menga rahmat aytmoqchi bo'lsangiz, — javob berdi u, — faqat o'zingiz uchun bo'lsin. Sizga baxt berish istagi meni oldinga undagan boshqa sabablarga kuch qo'shgan bo'lishi mumkinligini inkor etishga urinmayman. Lekin oilangiz menga hech narsa qarzdor emas. Ularni qanchalik hurmat qilmayin, ishonamanki, men faqat siz haqingizda o'yladim».

paras.en: Elizabeth was too much embarrassed to say a word. After a short pause, her companion added, “You are too generous to trifle with me. If your feelings are still what they were last April, tell me so at once. My affections and wishes are unchanged, but one word from you will silence me on this subject for ever.”
paras.uz: Elizabet bir og'iz so'z aytish uchun haddan tashqari xijolatda edi. Qisqa sukutdan keyin hamrohi qo'shib qo'ydi: «Siz men bilan o'ynash uchun haddan tashqari olijanobsiz. Agar tuyg'ularingiz hali ham o'tgan apreldagidek bo'lsa, buni darhol menga ayting. Mening mehrim va istaklarim o'zgarmagan, lekin sizdan bir so'z meni bu mavzuda abadiy jim qiladi».

paras.en: Elizabeth, feeling all the more than common awkwardness and anxiety of his situation, now forced herself to speak; and immediately, though not very fluently, gave him to understand that her sentiments had undergone so material a change, since the period to which he alluded, as to make her receive with gratitude and pleasure his present assurances. The happiness which this reply produced, was such as he had probably never felt before; and he expressed himself on the occasion as sensibly and as warmly as a man violently in love can be supposed to do. Had Elizabeth been able to encounter his eye, she might have seen how well the expression of heartfelt delight, diffused over his face, became him; but, though she could not look, she could listen, and he told her of feelings, which, in proving of what importance she was to him, made his affection every moment more valuable.
paras.uz: Elizabet uning ahvolining odatdagidan ortiq noqulayligi va tashvishini to'liq his qilib, endi o'zini gapirishga majbur qildi; va darhol, unchalik ravon bo'lmasa ham, unga u ishora qilgan davrdan beri uning tuyg'ulari shunchalik jiddiy o'zgarganini tushuntirdiki, u uning hozirgi ishontirishlarini minnatdorlik va zavq bilan qabul qiladi. Bu javob keltirib chiqargan baxt u, ehtimol, ilgari hech qachon his qilmagan darajada edi; va u bu munosabat bilan qattiq oshiq erkak qila olishi taxmin qilinishi mumkin bo'lgan darajada oqilona va qizg'in ifoda etdi. Agar Elizabet uning ko'zlariga qaray olganida, uning yuziga yoyilgan chin dildan zavq ifodasi unga qanchalik yarashganini ko'rgan bo'lardi; lekin u qaray olmasa ham, tinglay olardi va u unga uning o'zi uchun qanchalik muhim ekanini isbotlab, uning mehrini har lahza qimmatliroq qiladigan tuyg'ular haqida gapirdi.

paras.en: They walked on, without knowing in what direction. There was too much to be thought, and felt, and said, for attention to any other objects. She soon learnt that they were indebted for their present good understanding to the efforts of his aunt, who did call on him in her return through London, and there relate her journey to Longbourn, its motive, and the substance of her conversation with Elizabeth; dwelling emphatically on every expression of the latter which, in her ladyship's apprehension, peculiarly denoted her perverseness and assurance; in the belief that such a relation must assist her endeavours to obtain that promise from her nephew which she had refused to give. But, unluckily for her ladyship, its effect had been exactly contrariwise.
paras.uz: Ular qaysi yo'nalishda ekanini bilmay yurishda davom etishdi. Boshqa narsalarga e'tibor berish uchun o'ylash, his qilish va aytish kerak bo'lgan narsa haddan tashqari ko'p edi. U tez orada ular hozirgi yaxshi tushunishlari uchun uning xolasining sa'y-harakatlaridan qarzdor ekanliklarini bildi, u qaytishda London orqali o'tayotib uning oldiga kirgan va u yerda Longbornga safari, uning sababi va Elizabet bilan suhbatining mazmunini aytib bergan edi; janoblari tushunchasiga ko'ra ayniqsa uning o'jarligi va surbetligini bildiradigan ikkinchisining har bir iborasiga urg'u bilan to'xtalib; bunday hikoya uning jiyanidan Elizabet berishdan bosh tortgan va'dani olish urinishlariga yordam berishi kerak deb ishongan holda. Lekin janoblari uchun afsuski, uning ta'siri aynan aksincha bo'ldi.

paras.en: “It taught me to hope,” said he, “as I had scarcely ever allowed myself to hope before. I knew enough of your disposition to be certain that, had you been absolutely, irrevocably decided against me, you would have acknowledged it to Lady Catherine, frankly and openly.”
paras.uz: «Bu menga umid qilishni o'rgatdi, — dedi u, — ilgari o'zimga deyarli hech qachon umid qilishga ruxsat bermaganimdek. Men sizning fe'lingizni yetarlicha bilardimki, agar siz mutlaqo, qaytib bo'lmas darajada menga qarshi qaror qilgan bo'lsangiz, buni ledi Ketringa ochiq va samimiy tan olgan bo'lardingiz».

paras.en: Elizabeth coloured and laughed as she replied, “Yes, you know enough of my frankness to believe me capable of that. After abusing you so abominably to your face, I could have no scruple in abusing you to all your relations.”
paras.uz: Elizabet qizarib, kulib javob berdi: «Ha, siz mening ochiqligimni buni qila olishimga ishonish uchun yetarlicha bilasiz. Sizni yuzingizga bunchalik jirkanch haqorat qilgandan keyin, barcha qarindoshlaringizga sizni haqorat qilishda hech qanday ikkilanishim bo'lishi mumkin emasdi».

paras.en: “What did you say of me, that I did not deserve? For, though your accusations were ill-founded, formed on mistaken premises, my behaviour to you at the time had merited the severest reproof. It was unpardonable. I cannot think of it without abhorrence.”
paras.uz: «Men loyiq bo'lmagan nimani aytdingiz? Chunki sizning ayblovlaringiz asossiz, noto'g'ri asoslarga qurilgan bo'lsa ham, o'sha paytdagi sizga nisbatan xatti-harakatim eng qattiq tanbehga loyiq edi. U kechirib bo'lmas edi. Uni nafratsiz o'ylay olmayman».

paras.en: “We will not quarrel for the greater share of blame annexed to that evening,” said Elizabeth. “The conduct of neither, if strictly examined, will be irreproachable; but since then, we have both, I hope, improved in civility.”
paras.uz: «O'sha oqshomga tegishli aybning kattaroq ulushi uchun janjallashmaymiz, — dedi Elizabet. — Qattiq tekshirilsa, hech birimizning xatti-harakati beayb bo'lmaydi; lekin o'shandan beri ikkalamiz ham, umid qilamanki, xushmuomalalikda yaxshilandik».

paras.en: “I cannot be so easily reconciled to myself. The recollection of what I then said, of my conduct, my manners, my expressions during the whole of it, is now, and has been many months, inexpressibly painful to me. Your reproof, so well applied, I shall never forget: 'had you behaved in a more gentlemanlike manner.' Those were your words. You know not, you can scarcely conceive, how they have tortured me;--though it was some time, I confess, before I was reasonable enough to allow their justice.”
paras.uz: «Men o'zim bilan bunchalik oson yarasha olmayman. O'shanda aytganlarim, butun suhbat davomidagi xatti-harakatim, muomalam, iboralarim haqidagi xotira hozir va ko'p oylardan beri men uchun ta'riflab bo'lmas darajada og'riqli. Shunchalik o'rinli qo'llangan tanbehingizni hech qachon unutmayman: "agar siz janoblarga xosroq tarzda o'zingizni tutganingizda". Bular sizning so'zlaringiz edi. Ular meni qanchalik qiynaganini bilmaysiz, zo'rg'a tasavvur qila olasiz; — garchi tan olaman, ularning adolatliligini tan olish uchun yetarlicha oqil bo'lishimga biroz vaqt kerak bo'lgan bo'lsa ham».

paras.en: “I was certainly very far from expecting them to make so strong an impression. I had not the smallest idea of their being ever felt in such a way.”
paras.uz: «Men, albatta, ular bunchalik kuchli taassurot qoldirishini kutishdan juda yiroq edim. Ular hech qachon shunday his qilinishi haqida zarracha ham tasavvurim yo'q edi».

paras.en: “I can easily believe it. You thought me then devoid of every proper feeling, I am sure you did. The turn of your countenance I shall never forget, as you said that I could not have addressed you in any possible way that would induce you to accept me.”
paras.uz: «Bunga osongina ishonaman. O'shanda siz meni har qanday munosib tuyg'udan mahrum deb o'ylagansiz, ishonchim komilki, shunday o'ylagansiz. Siz men sizga meni qabul qilishga undaydigan hech qanday mumkin bo'lgan tarzda murojaat qila olmasligimni aytganingizdagi yuzingiz ifodasini hech qachon unutmayman».

paras.en: “Oh! do not repeat what I then said. These recollections will not do at all. I assure you that I have long been most heartily ashamed of it.”
paras.uz: «Oh! O'shanda aytganlarimni takrorlamang. Bu xotiralar umuman to'g'ri kelmaydi. Sizni ishontirib aytamanki, men uzoq vaqtdan beri bundan chin dildan uyalib kelaman».

paras.en: Darcy mentioned his letter. “Did it,” said he, “did it soon make you think better of me? Did you, on reading it, give any credit to its contents?”
paras.uz: Darsi xatini tilga oldi. «U, — dedi u, — u sizni tez orada men haqimda yaxshiroq o'ylashga majbur qildimi? Uni o'qib, uning mazmuniga biroz ishondingizmi?»

paras.en: She explained what its effect on her had been, and how gradually all her former prejudices had been removed.
paras.uz: U uning o'ziga qanday ta'sir qilganini va avvalgi barcha xurofotlari qanday asta-sekin yo'qolganini tushuntirdi.

paras.en: “I knew,” said he, “that what I wrote must give you pain, but it was necessary. I hope you have destroyed the letter. There was one part especially, the opening of it, which I should dread your having the power of reading again. I can remember some expressions which might justly make you hate me.”
paras.uz: «Bilardim, — dedi u, — yozganlarim sizga og'riq berishi kerak, lekin bu zarur edi. Umid qilamanki, xatni yo'q qildingiz. Ayniqsa bir qismi, uning boshlanishi borki, uni yana o'qish imkoniyatingiz borligidan qo'rqardim. Sizni mendan nafratlanishga adolatli majbur qilishi mumkin bo'lgan ba'zi iboralarni eslay olaman».

paras.en: “The letter shall certainly be burnt, if you believe it essential to the preservation of my regard; but, though we have both reason to think my opinions not entirely unalterable, they are not, I hope, quite so easily changed as that implies.”
paras.uz: «Agar bu mening hurmatimni saqlash uchun zarur deb ishonsangiz, xat albatta yoqiladi; lekin garchi ikkalamizda ham fikrlarim butunlay o'zgarmas emas deb o'ylash uchun asos bo'lsa ham, umid qilamanki, ular bu nazarda tutgandek unchalik oson o'zgarmaydi».

paras.en: “When I wrote that letter,” replied Darcy, “I believed myself perfectly calm and cool, but I am since convinced that it was written in a dreadful bitterness of spirit.”
paras.uz: «O'sha xatni yozganimda, — javob berdi Darsi, — o'zimni mutlaqo xotirjam va sovuqqon deb ishongan edim, lekin o'shandan beri u dahshatli ruhiy achchiqlikda yozilganiga ishonch hosil qildim».

paras.en: “The letter, perhaps, began in bitterness, but it did not end so. The adieu is charity itself. But think no more of the letter. The feelings of the person who wrote, and the person who received it, are now so widely different from what they were then, that every unpleasant circumstance attending it ought to be forgotten. You must learn some of my philosophy. Think only of the past as its remembrance gives you pleasure.”
paras.uz: «Xat, ehtimol, achchiqlik bilan boshlangandir, lekin u shunday tugamagan. Xayrlashuv mehribonlikning o'zi. Lekin xat haqida boshqa o'ylamang. Uni yozgan va uni olgan odamning tuyg'ulari endi o'shanda bo'lganidan shunchalik farq qiladiki, unga hamroh bo'lgan har bir yoqimsiz holat unutilishi kerak. Siz mening falsafamdan biroz o'rganishingiz kerak. O'tmish haqida faqat uning xotirasi sizga zavq berganda o'ylang».

paras.en: “I cannot give you credit for any philosophy of the kind. Your retrospections must be so totally void of reproach, that the contentment arising from them is not of philosophy, but, what is much better, of innocence. But with me, it is not so. Painful recollections will intrude which cannot, which ought not, to be repelled. I have been a selfish being all my life, in practice, though not in principle. As a child I was taught what was right, but I was not taught to correct my temper. I was given good principles, but left to follow them in pride and conceit.
paras.uz: «Men sizni bunday falsafaga ega deb hisoblay olmayman. Sizning o'tmishga nazaringiz ta'nadan shunchalik butunlay xoli bo'lishi kerakki, ulardan kelib chiqadigan mamnuniyat falsafadan emas, balki undan ancha yaxshiroq narsa — beg'uborlikdan. Lekin men bilan bunday emas. Qaytarib bo'lmaydigan, qaytarilmasligi kerak bo'lgan og'riqli xotiralar bostirib keladi. Men butun umrim davomida amalda, garchi tamoyilda bo'lmasa ham, xudbin mavjudot bo'lganman. Bolaligimda menga nima to'g'ri ekanini o'rgatishgan, lekin fe'limni tuzatishni o'rgatishmagan. Menga yaxshi tamoyillar berishgan, lekin ularga g'urur va manmanlik bilan amal qilishga qoldirishgan.

paras.en: Unfortunately an only son (for many years an only child), I was spoilt by my parents, who, though good themselves (my father, particularly, all that was benevolent and amiable), allowed, encouraged, almost taught me to be selfish and overbearing; to care for none beyond my own family circle; to think meanly of all the rest of the world; to wish at least to think meanly of their sense and worth compared with my own. Such I was, from eight to eight and twenty; and such I might still have been but for you, dearest, loveliest Elizabeth! What do I not owe you! You taught me a lesson, hard indeed at first, but most advantageous. By you, I was properly humbled. I came to you without a doubt of my reception. You showed me how insufficient were all my pretensions to please a woman worthy of being pleased.”
paras.uz: Afsuski, yagona o'g'il (ko'p yillar davomida yagona farzand) bo'lganim uchun ota-onam meni erkalatib buzishgan, ular o'zlari yaxshi bo'lsalar ham (ayniqsa otam butunlay ezgu va yoqimli edi), menga xudbin va hukmron bo'lishga ruxsat berishgan, rag'batlantirishgan, deyarli o'rgatishgan; o'z oila davramdan tashqari hech kimga ahamiyat bermaslikka; dunyoning qolgan hammasi haqida past o'ylashga; hech bo'lmaganda ularning aqli va qadri haqida o'zimniki bilan solishtirganda past o'ylashni istashga. Men sakkiz yoshdan yigirma sakkiz yoshgacha shunday edim; va agar siz bo'lmaganingizda, eng aziz, eng go'zal Elizabet, hali ham shunday bo'lishim mumkin edi! Men sizga nimadan qarzdor emasman! Siz menga saboq berdingiz, avvaliga haqiqatan ham og'ir, lekin eng foydali. Siz tufayli men munosib ravishda kamsitildim. Men sizga qabul qilinishimga hech qanday shubhasiz keldim. Siz menga yoqishga loyiq ayolga yoqish uchun barcha da'volarim qanchalik yetarsiz ekanini ko'rsatdingiz».

paras.en: “Had you then persuaded yourself that I should?”
paras.uz: «Demak, siz o'shanda men qabul qilaman deb o'zingizni ishontirgan edingizmi?»

paras.en: “Indeed I had. What will you think of my vanity? I believed you to be wishing, expecting my addresses.”
paras.uz: «Haqiqatan ham shunday edi. Mening shuhratparastligim haqida nima deb o'ylaysiz? Men sizni murojaatlarimni istayapti, kutyapti deb ishongan edim».

paras.en: “My manners must have been in fault, but not intentionally, I assure you. I never meant to deceive you, but my spirits might often lead me wrong. How you must have hated me after that evening?”
paras.uz: «Mening muomalam aybdor bo'lgan bo'lsa kerak, lekin ataylab emas, sizni ishontirib aytaman. Men hech qachon sizni aldashni niyat qilmaganman, lekin mening jo'shqinligim ko'pincha meni noto'g'ri yo'lga olib borishi mumkin edi. O'sha oqshomdan keyin mendan qanchalik nafratlangan bo'lsangiz kerak?»

paras.en: “Hate you! I was angry perhaps at first, but my anger soon began to take a proper direction.”
paras.uz: «Sizdan nafratlanishmi! Avvaliga, ehtimol, g'azablangandirman, lekin g'azabim tez orada to'g'ri yo'nalish ola boshladi».

paras.en: “I am almost afraid of asking what you thought of me, when we met at Pemberley. You blamed me for coming?”
paras.uz: «Pemberlida uchrashganimizda men haqimda nima deb o'ylaganingizni so'rashdan deyarli qo'rqaman. Kelganim uchun meni aybladingizmi?»

paras.en: “No indeed; I felt nothing but surprise.”
paras.uz: «Yo'q, haqiqatan ham; hayratdan boshqa hech narsa his qilmadim».

paras.en: “Your surprise could not be greater than mine in being noticed by you. My conscience told me that I deserved no extraordinary politeness, and I confess that I did not expect to receive more than my due.”
paras.uz: «Sizning hayratingiz siz tomonidan e'tibor ko'rsatilganidagi mening hayratimdan katta bo'la olmasdi. Vijdonim menga hech qanday g'ayrioddiy xushmuomalalikka loyiq emasligimni aytardi va tan olaman, men loyiq bo'lganimdan ko'proq narsa olishni kutmagan edim».

paras.en: “My object then,” replied Darcy, “was to show you, by every civility in my power, that I was not so mean as to resent the past; and I hoped to obtain your forgiveness, to lessen your ill opinion, by letting you see that your reproofs had been attended to. How soon any other wishes introduced themselves I can hardly tell, but I believe in about half an hour after I had seen you.”
paras.uz: «O'shanda mening maqsadim, — javob berdi Darsi, — qo'limdan kelgan har qanday xushmuomalalik bilan sizga o'tmishdan ranjiydigan darajada past emasligimni ko'rsatish edi; va tanbehlaringizga e'tibor berilganini ko'rishingizga imkon berib, kechirimingizni olishga, yomon fikringizni kamaytirishga umid qilgandim. Boshqa istaklar qanchalik tez paydo bo'lganini zo'rg'a ayta olaman, lekin menimcha, sizni ko'rganimdan taxminan yarim soat o'tib».

paras.en: He then told her of Georgiana's delight in her acquaintance, and of her disappointment at its sudden interruption; which naturally leading to the cause of that interruption, she soon learnt that his resolution of following her from Derbyshire in quest of her sister had been formed before he quitted the inn, and that his gravity and thoughtfulness there had arisen from no other struggles than what such a purpose must comprehend.
paras.uz: Keyin u unga Jorjiananing u bilan tanishganidan zavqlangani va uning to'satdan uzilganidan hafsalasi pir bo'lgani haqida aytdi; bu tabiiy ravishda o'sha uzilishning sababiga olib kelgani uchun, u tez orada uning singlisini izlab Derbishirdan uning ortidan borish qarori mehmonxonadan chiqishidan oldin shakllanganini va u yerdagi jiddiyligi va o'ychanligi bunday maqsad o'z ichiga olishi kerak bo'lgan kurashlardan boshqa hech narsadan kelib chiqmaganini bildi.

paras.en: She expressed her gratitude again, but it was too painful a subject to each, to be dwelt on farther.
paras.uz: U yana minnatdorligini bildirdi, lekin bu har ikkisi uchun ham uzoqroq to'xtalish uchun haddan tashqari og'riqli mavzu edi.

paras.en: After walking several miles in a leisurely manner, and too busy to know anything about it, they found at last, on examining their watches, that it was time to be at home.
paras.uz: Bir necha mil shoshilmay yurib, bu haqda biror narsa bilish uchun haddan tashqari band bo'lgach, ular nihoyat soatlariga qarab, uyda bo'lish vaqti kelganini bilishdi.

paras.en: “What could become of Mr. Bingley and Jane!” was a wonder which introduced the discussion of their affairs. Darcy was delighted with their engagement; his friend had given him the earliest information of it.
paras.uz: «Janob Bingli va Jeyn nima bo'ldi ekan!» — degan hayronlik ularning ishlari muhokamasini boshladi. Darsi ularning unashtirilganidan xursand edi; do'sti bu haqda unga eng birinchi xabar bergan edi.

paras.en: “I must ask whether you were surprised?” said Elizabeth.
paras.uz: «Hayron bo'ldingizmi, deb so'rashim kerak», — dedi Elizabet.

paras.en: “Not at all. When I went away, I felt that it would soon happen.”
paras.uz: «Umuman yo'q. Ketayotganimda bu tez orada sodir bo'lishini his qilgandim».

paras.en: “That is to say, you had given your permission. I guessed as much.” And though he exclaimed at the term, she found that it had been pretty much the case.
paras.uz: «Ya'ni siz ruxsatingizni bergan edingiz. Men ham shunday taxmin qilgandim». Va u bu iboraga e'tiroz bildirgan bo'lsa ham, u bu ancha shunday bo'lganini bildi.

paras.en: “On the evening before my going to London,” said he, “I made a confession to him, which I believe I ought to have made long ago. I told him of all that had occurred to make my former interference in his affairs absurd and impertinent. His surprise was great. He had never had the slightest suspicion. I told him, moreover, that I believed myself mistaken in supposing, as I had done, that your sister was indifferent to him; and as I could easily perceive that his attachment to her was unabated, I felt no doubt of their happiness together.”
paras.uz: «Londonga ketishimdan oldingi kechqurun, — dedi u, — men unga ancha oldin qilishim kerak bo'lgan, ishonamanki, tan olish qildim. Men unga uning ishlariga avvalgi aralashuvimni bema'ni va surbet qilgan barcha voqealarni aytib berdim. Uning hayrati katta edi. Uning hech qachon zarracha ham shubhasi bo'lmagan. Bundan tashqari, men unga opangiz unga befarq deb taxmin qilganimda adashgan deb ishonishimni aytdim; va uning unga bo'lgan mehri susaymaganini osongina sezganim uchun, ularning birga baxtli bo'lishiga hech qanday shubha his qilmadim».

paras.en: Elizabeth could not help smiling at his easy manner of directing his friend.
paras.uz: Elizabet uning do'stini yo'naltirishdagi yengil uslubiga jilmaymay qololmadi.

paras.en: “Did you speak from your own observation,” said she, “when you told him that my sister loved him, or merely from my information last spring?”
paras.uz: «Siz unga opam uni sevishini aytganingizda, — dedi u, — o'z kuzatuvingizdan gapirdingizmi yoki shunchaki o'tgan bahordagi mening ma'lumotimdanmi?»

paras.en: “From the former. I had narrowly observed her during the two visits which I had lately made here; and I was convinced of her affection.”
paras.uz: «Birinchisidan. Yaqinda bu yerga qilgan ikki tashrifim davomida uni diqqat bilan kuzatdim va uning mehriga ishonch hosil qildim».

paras.en: “And your assurance of it, I suppose, carried immediate conviction to him.”
paras.uz: «Va sizning bunga ishontirishingiz, o'ylaymanki, unga darhol ishonch bag'ishladi».

paras.en: “It did. Bingley is most unaffectedly modest. His diffidence had prevented his depending on his own judgment in so anxious a case, but his reliance on mine made every thing easy. I was obliged to confess one thing, which for a time, and not unjustly, offended him. I could not allow myself to conceal that your sister had been in town three months last winter, that I had known it, and purposely kept it from him. He was angry. But his anger, I am persuaded, lasted no longer than he remained in any doubt of your sister's sentiments. He has heartily forgiven me now.”
paras.uz: «Shunday bo'ldi. Bingli eng soddadil kamtar. Uning tortinchoqligi unga bunchalik tashvishli ishda o'z mulohazasiga tayanishga to'sqinlik qilgan edi, lekin uning menikiga tayanishi hamma narsani osonlashtirdi. Men bir narsani tan olishga majbur bo'ldim, bu bir muddat va asossiz emas, uni ranjitdi. Opangiz o'tgan qish Londonda uch oy bo'lganini, men buni bilganimni va ataylab undan yashirganimni yashirishga o'zimga ruxsat bera olmadim. U g'azablandi. Lekin ishonamanki, uning g'azabi u opangizning tuyg'ulari haqida biror shubhada qolganidan uzoq davom etmadi. U endi meni chin dildan kechirdi».

paras.en: Elizabeth longed to observe that Mr. Bingley had been a most delightful friend; so easily guided that his worth was invaluable; but she checked herself. She remembered that he had yet to learn to be laughed at, and it was rather too early to begin. In anticipating the happiness of Bingley, which of course was to be inferior only to his own, he continued the conversation till they reached the house. In the hall they parted.
paras.uz: Elizabet janob Bingli eng yoqimli do'st bo'lgani, uni shunchalik oson yo'naltirish mumkinki, uning qadri bebaho ekani haqida aytishni juda istadi; lekin o'zini tiydi. U hali u masxara qilinishni o'rganishi kerakligini esladi va boshlash uchun ancha erta edi. Albatta, faqat o'zinikidan pastroq bo'lishi kerak bo'lgan Binglining baxtini oldindan tasavvur qilib, u uyga yetib kelgunlaricha suhbatni davom ettirdi. Zalda ular ajralishdi.

chapters.title: Telling the Family
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet Jeyn va otasiga unashtirilganini aytadi. Hamma hayron. Janob Bennet qizi Darsini chindan sevishiga ishonch hosil qilgach, rozi bo'ladi. Missis Bennet boylikdan hushini yo'qotadi.

paras.en: “My dear Lizzy, where can you have been walking to?” was a question which Elizabeth received from Jane as soon as she entered their room, and from all the others when they sat down to table. She had only to say in reply, that they had wandered about, till she was beyond her own knowledge. She coloured as she spoke; but neither that, nor anything else, awakened a suspicion of the truth.
paras.uz: «Azizim Lizzi, qayerga sayr qilib ketding?» — bu savolni Elizabet xonalariga kirishi bilanoq Jeyndan, dasturxonga o'tirishganda esa qolgan hammadan eshitdi. U javoban faqat ular o'zi bilmagan joylargacha kezib yurganlarini aytishi kerak edi. U gapirarkan qizardi; lekin na bu, na boshqa narsa haqiqatdan shubha uyg'otmadi.

paras.en: The evening passed quietly, unmarked by anything extraordinary. The acknowledged lovers talked and laughed, the unacknowledged were silent. Darcy was not of a disposition in which happiness overflows in mirth; and Elizabeth, agitated and confused, rather knew that she was happy than felt herself to be so; for, besides the immediate embarrassment, there were other evils before her. She anticipated what would be felt in the family when her situation became known; she was aware that no one liked him but Jane; and even feared that with the others it was a dislike which not all his fortune and consequence might do away.
paras.uz: Oqshom hech qanday g'ayrioddiy narsa bilan belgilanmay, sokin o'tdi. Tan olingan oshiqlar gaplashib, kulishdi, tan olinmaganlar esa jim o'tirishdi. Darsi baxti kulgida to'lib-toshadigan fe'lda emasdi; hayajonlangan va sarosimaga tushgan Elizabet esa o'zini baxtli his qilishdan ko'ra baxtli ekanini bilardi; chunki darhol xijolatdan tashqari, uning oldida boshqa yomonliklar ham bor edi. U ahvoli ma'lum bo'lganda oilada nimani his qilishlarini oldindan tasavvur qildi; Jeyndan boshqa hech kim uni yoqtirmasligini bilardi; va hatto boshqalarda bu uning butun boyligi va mavqei ham yo'qota olmaydigan yoqtirmaslik bo'lishidan qo'rqardi.

paras.en: At night she opened her heart to Jane. Though suspicion was very far from Miss Bennet's general habits, she was absolutely incredulous here.
paras.uz: Kechasi u Jeynga qalbini ochdi. Shubha miss Bennetning umumiy odatlaridan juda yiroq bo'lsa ham, bu yerda u mutlaqo ishonmadi.

paras.en: “You are joking, Lizzy. This cannot be!--engaged to Mr. Darcy! No, no, you shall not deceive me. I know it to be impossible.”
paras.uz: «Hazillashyapsan, Lizzi. Bunday bo'lishi mumkin emas! — janob Darsiga unashtirildingmi! Yo'q, yo'q, meni aldolmaysan. Bu imkonsiz ekanini bilaman».

paras.en: “This is a wretched beginning indeed! My sole dependence was on you; and I am sure nobody else will believe me, if you do not. Yet, indeed, I am in earnest. I speak nothing but the truth. He still loves me, and we are engaged.”
paras.uz: «Bu haqiqatan ham ayanchli boshlanish! Mening yagona tayanchim sen eding; ishonchim komilki, agar sen ishonmasang, boshqa hech kim menga ishonmaydi. Shunga qaramay, haqiqatan ham jiddiyman. Haqiqatdan boshqa hech narsa gapirmayapman. U meni hali ham sevadi va biz unashtirildik».

paras.en: Jane looked at her doubtingly. “Oh, Lizzy! it cannot be. I know how much you dislike him.”
paras.uz: Jeyn unga shubha bilan qaradi. «Oh, Lizzi! Bunday bo'lishi mumkin emas. Uni qanchalik yoqtirmasligingni bilaman».

paras.en: “You know nothing of the matter. That is all to be forgot. Perhaps I did not always love him so well as I do now. But in such cases as these, a good memory is unpardonable. This is the last time I shall ever remember it myself.”
paras.uz: «Sen bu masaladan hech narsa bilmaysan. Bularning hammasi unutilishi kerak. Ehtimol, men uni doim ham hozirgidek yaxshi ko'rmaganman. Lekin bunday hollarda yaxshi xotira kechirib bo'lmas. Bu men o'zim buni eslaydigan oxirgi marta».

paras.en: Miss Bennet still looked all amazement. Elizabeth again, and more seriously assured her of its truth.
paras.uz: Miss Bennet hali ham butunlay hayratda ko'rinardi. Elizabet yana, yanada jiddiyroq uni buning haqiqat ekaniga ishontirdi.

paras.en: “Good Heaven! can it be really so! Yet now I must believe you,” cried Jane. “My dear, dear Lizzy, I would--I do congratulate you--but are you certain? forgive the question--are you quite certain that you can be happy with him?”
paras.uz: «Yo xudo! Haqiqatan ham shundaymi! Lekin endi senga ishonishim kerak, — xitob qildi Jeyn. — Aziz, aziz Lizzim, men... seni tabriklayman — lekin aminmisan? Savol uchun kechir — u bilan baxtli bo'la olishingga butunlay aminmisan?»

paras.en: “There can be no doubt of that. It is settled between us already, that we are to be the happiest couple in the world. But are you pleased, Jane? Shall you like to have such a brother?”
paras.uz: «Bunga hech qanday shubha bo'lishi mumkin emas. Oramizda allaqachon kelishildiki, biz dunyodagi eng baxtli juftlik bo'lamiz. Lekin sen mamnunmisan, Jeyn? Bunday kuyovga ega bo'lishni yoqtirasanmi?»

paras.en: “Very, very much. Nothing could give either Bingley or myself more delight. But we considered it, we talked of it as impossible. And do you really love him quite well enough? Oh, Lizzy! do anything rather than marry without affection. Are you quite sure that you feel what you ought to do?”
paras.uz: «Juda, juda ham. Hech narsa Binglige ham, menga ham bundan ko'proq zavq bera olmasdi. Lekin biz buni o'ylab ko'rgan edik, bu haqda imkonsiz narsa sifatida gaplashgan edik. Sen uni chindan ham yetarlicha yaxshi ko'rasanmi? Oh, Lizzi! Mehrsiz turmushga chiqishdan ko'ra har narsa qil. His qilishing kerak bo'lgan narsani his qilayotganingga butunlay aminmisan?»

paras.en: “Oh, yes! You will only think I feel more than I ought to do, when I tell you all.”
paras.uz: «Oh, ha! Senga hammasini aytib berganimda, faqat his qilishim kerak bo'lganidan ko'proq his qilyapman deb o'ylaysan».

paras.en: “What do you mean?”
paras.uz: «Nima demoqchisan?»

paras.en: “Why, I must confess that I love him better than I do Bingley. I am afraid you will be angry.”
paras.uz: «Axir, tan olishim kerakki, men uni Binglidan ko'ra ko'proq sevaman. Qo'rqamanki, g'azablanasan».

paras.en: “My dearest sister, now be serious. I want to talk very seriously. Let me know every thing that I am to know, without delay. Will you tell me how long you have loved him?”
paras.uz: «Eng aziz singlim, endi jiddiy bo'l. Juda jiddiy gaplashmoqchiman. Bilishim kerak bo'lgan hamma narsani kechiktirmasdan menga bildir. Uni qancha vaqtdan beri sevishingni aytasanmi?»

paras.en: “It has been coming on so gradually, that I hardly know when it began. But I believe I must date it from my first seeing his beautiful grounds at Pemberley.”
paras.uz: «Bu shunchalik asta-sekin yaqinlashdiki, qachon boshlanganini zo'rg'a bilaman. Lekin menimcha, uni Pemberlidagi uning go'zal yerlarini birinchi ko'rganimdan boshlab hisoblashim kerak».

paras.en: Another entreaty that she would be serious, however, produced the desired effect; and she soon satisfied Jane by her solemn assurances of attachment. When convinced on that article, Miss Bennet had nothing further to wish.
paras.uz: Biroq jiddiy bo'lish haqidagi yana bir iltimos istalgan ta'sirni berdi; va u tez orada Jeynni mehri haqidagi tantanali ishontirishlari bilan qanoatlantirdi. Bu masalada ishonch hosil qilgach, miss Bennetning boshqa orzu qiladigan narsasi qolmadi.

paras.en: “Now I am quite happy,” said she, “for you will be as happy as myself. I always had a value for him. Were it for nothing but his love of you, I must always have esteemed him; but now, as Bingley's friend and your husband, there can be only Bingley and yourself more dear to me. But Lizzy, you have been very sly, very reserved with me. How little did you tell me of what passed at Pemberley and Lambton! I owe all that I know of it to another, not to you.”
paras.uz: «Endi men butunlay baxtliman, — dedi u, — chunki sen ham men kabi baxtli bo'lasan. Men uni doim qadrlardim. Agar faqat senga bo'lgan muhabbati uchun bo'lsa ham, uni doim hurmat qilishim kerak edi; lekin endi Binglining do'sti va sening ering sifatida menga faqat Bingli va sen undan azizroq bo'lishingiz mumkin. Lekin, Lizzi, sen men bilan juda ayyor, juda vazmin bo'lding. Pemberli va Lembtonda bo'lib o'tgan voqealar haqida menga qanchalik kam aytding! Bu haqda bilganlarimning hammasi uchun sendan emas, boshqa birovdan qarzdorman».

paras.en: Elizabeth told her the motives of her secrecy. She had been unwilling to mention Bingley; and the unsettled state of her own feelings had made her equally avoid the name of his friend. But now she would no longer conceal from her his share in Lydia's marriage. All was acknowledged, and half the night spent in conversation.
paras.uz: Elizabet unga sir saqlashining sabablarini aytdi. U Binglini tilga olishni istamagan edi; o'z tuyg'ularining beqaror holati esa uni do'stining nomidan ham xuddi shunday qochishga majbur qilgan edi. Lekin endi u undan uning Lidiyaning nikohidagi ulushini boshqa yashirmasdi. Hammasi tan olindi va tunning yarmi suhbatda o'tdi.

paras.en: “Good gracious!” cried Mrs. Bennet, as she stood at a window the next morning, “if that disagreeable Mr. Darcy is not coming here again with our dear Bingley! What can he mean by being so tiresome as to be always coming here? I had no notion but he would go a-shooting, or something or other, and not disturb us with his company. What shall we do with him? Lizzy, you must walk out with him again, that he may not be in Bingley's way.”
paras.uz: «Yo xudo! — xitob qildi missis Bennet ertasi kuni ertalab deraza oldida turarkan. — O'sha yoqimsiz janob Darsi yana aziz Binglimiz bilan bu yerga kelyapti-ya! Doim bu yerga kelib, bunchalik zeriktirib, u nima demoqchi? Men u ovga yoki boshqa biror narsaga ketadi va bizni davrasi bilan bezovta qilmaydi deb o'ylagan edim. U bilan nima qilamiz? Lizzi, sen u bilan yana sayrga chiqishing kerak, toki u Binglining yo'lida turmasin».

paras.en: Elizabeth could hardly help laughing at so convenient a proposal; yet was really vexed that her mother should be always giving him such an epithet.
paras.uz: Elizabet bunday qulay taklifga kulmaslikka zo'rg'a tutib turdi; shunga qaramay onasining unga doim shunday laqab berayotganidan haqiqatan ham g'ashi keldi.

paras.en: As soon as they entered, Bingley looked at her so expressively, and shook hands with such warmth, as left no doubt of his good information; and he soon afterwards said aloud, “Mrs. Bennet, have you no more lanes hereabouts in which Lizzy may lose her way again to-day?”
paras.uz: Ular kirishlari bilanoq Bingli unga shunchalik ma'noli qaradi va shunchalik iliqlik bilan qo'l berib ko'rishdiki, bu uning yaxshi xabardor ekaniga hech qanday shubha qoldirmadi; va u ko'p o'tmay baland ovozda dedi: «Missis Bennet, bu atrofda Lizzi bugun yana yo'ldan adashishi mumkin bo'lgan boshqa tor yo'llaringiz yo'qmi?»

paras.en: “I advise Mr. Darcy, and Lizzy, and Kitty,” said Mrs. Bennet, “to walk to Oakham Mount this morning. It is a nice long walk, and Mr. Darcy has never seen the view.”
paras.uz: «Janob Darsiga, Lizzi va Kettiga, — dedi missis Bennet, — bugun ertalab Oukem tepaligiga piyoda borishni maslahat beraman. Bu yaxshi uzoq sayr va janob Darsi u yerdan manzarani hech qachon ko'rmagan».

paras.en: “It may do very well for the others,” replied Mr. Bingley; “but I am sure it will be too much for Kitty. Won't it, Kitty?” Kitty owned that she had rather stay at home. Darcy professed a great curiosity to see the view from the Mount, and Elizabeth silently consented. As she went up stairs to get ready, Mrs. Bennet followed her, saying:
paras.uz: «Bu boshqalar uchun juda yaxshi bo'lishi mumkin, — javob berdi janob Bingli, — lekin ishonchim komilki, Ketti uchun bu haddan tashqari ko'p bo'ladi. Shunday emasmi, Ketti?» Ketti uyda qolishni afzal ko'rishini tan oldi. Darsi tepalikdan manzarani ko'rishga katta qiziqish bildirdi va Elizabet jimgina rozi bo'ldi. U tayyorlanish uchun yuqoriga chiqayotganda, missis Bennet uning ortidan kelib, dedi:

paras.en: “I am quite sorry, Lizzy, that you should be forced to have that disagreeable man all to yourself. But I hope you will not mind it: it is all for Jane's sake, you know; and there is no occasion for talking to him, except just now and then. So, do not put yourself to inconvenience.”
paras.uz: «Juda afsusdaman, Lizzi, sen o'sha yoqimsiz odamni butunlay o'zingga olishga majbur bo'lyapsan. Lekin umid qilamanki, bunga qarshi bo'lmaysan: bilasanmi, hammasi Jeyn uchun; u bilan gaplashishning hech qanday hojati yo'q, faqat vaqti-vaqti bilan. Shuning uchun o'zingni noqulay ahvolga solma».

paras.en: During their walk, it was resolved that Mr. Bennet's consent should be asked in the course of the evening. Elizabeth reserved to herself the application for her mother's. She could not determine how her mother would take it; sometimes doubting whether all his wealth and grandeur would be enough to overcome her abhorrence of the man. But whether she were violently set against the match, or violently delighted with it, it was certain that her manner would be equally ill adapted to do credit to her sense; and she could no more bear that Mr. Darcy should hear the first raptures of her joy, than the first vehemence of her disapprobation.
paras.uz: Sayr davomida kechqurun janob Bennetning roziligini so'rashga qaror qilindi. Elizabet onasining roziligini so'rashni o'z zimmasiga oldi. U onasi buni qanday qabul qilishini aniqlay olmadi; ba'zan uning butun boyligi va ulug'vorligi onasining bu odamdan nafratini yengish uchun yetarli bo'ladimi, deb shubhalanardi. Lekin u nikohga qattiq qarshi bo'ladimi yoki undan qattiq zavqlanadimi, uning muomalasi uning aqliga sharaf keltirish uchun bir xil darajada nomunosib bo'lishi aniq edi; va u janob Darsining uning quvonchining birinchi hayajonlarini eshitishiga uning noroziligining birinchi shiddatini eshitishidan ortiq chiday olmasdi.

paras.en: In the evening, soon after Mr. Bennet withdrew to the library, she saw Mr. Darcy rise also and follow him, and her agitation on seeing it was extreme. She did not fear her father's opposition, but he was going to be made unhappy; and that it should be through her means--that she, his favourite child, should be distressing him by her choice, should be filling him with fears and regrets in disposing of her--was a wretched reflection, and she sat in misery till Mr. Darcy appeared again, when, looking at him, she was a little relieved by his smile. In a few minutes he approached the table where she was sitting with Kitty; and, while pretending to admire her work said in a whisper, “Go to your father, he wants you in the library.” She was gone directly.
paras.uz: Kechqurun, janob Bennet kutubxonaga chekinganidan ko'p o'tmay, u janob Darsining ham o'rnidan turib, uning ortidan ketganini ko'rdi va buni ko'rib, hayajoni haddan oshdi. U otasining qarshiligidan qo'rqmasdi, lekin uni baxtsiz qilishmoqchi edi; va bu uning sharofati bilan bo'lishi — u, uning sevimli farzandi, tanlovi bilan uni qayg'uga solishi, uni turmushga berishda uni qo'rquv va afsuslarga to'ldirishi — ayanchli mulohaza edi va u janob Darsi yana paydo bo'lguncha azob ichida o'tirdi; unga qarab, uning tabassumidan biroz yengil tortdi. Bir necha daqiqadan keyin u u Ketti bilan o'tirgan stolga yaqinlashdi va uning tikuviga qoyil qolayotgandek ko'rinib, pichirlab dedi: «Otangizning oldiga boring, u sizni kutubxonada kutyapti». U darhol ketdi.

paras.en: Her father was walking about the room, looking grave and anxious. “Lizzy,” said he, “what are you doing? Are you out of your senses, to be accepting this man? Have not you always hated him?”
paras.uz: Otasi jiddiy va tashvishli ko'rinib, xona bo'ylab u yoqdan-bu yoqqa yurardi. «Lizzi, — dedi u, — nima qilyapsan? Bu odamni qabul qilib, aqldan ozdingmi? Sen doim undan nafratlanmaganmiding?»

paras.en: How earnestly did she then wish that her former opinions had been more reasonable, her expressions more moderate! It would have spared her from explanations and professions which it was exceedingly awkward to give; but they were now necessary, and she assured him, with some confusion, of her attachment to Mr. Darcy.
paras.uz: Shunda u avvalgi fikrlari oqilonaroq, iboralari mo''tadilroq bo'lganini qanchalik qizg'in istadi! Bu uni berish nihoyatda noqulay bo'lgan tushuntirishlar va izhorlardan qutqargan bo'lardi; lekin ular endi zarur edi va u biroz sarosimada uni janob Darsiga bo'lgan mehriga ishontirdi.

paras.en: “Or, in other words, you are determined to have him. He is rich, to be sure, and you may have more fine clothes and fine carriages than Jane. But will they make you happy?”
paras.uz: «Yoki boshqacha aytganda, sen unga turmushga chiqishga qaror qilgansan. U boy, albatta, va sening Jeyndan ko'proq chiroyli kiyimlaring va chiroyli aravalaring bo'lishi mumkin. Lekin ular seni baxtli qiladimi?»

paras.en: “Have you any other objection,” said Elizabeth, “than your belief of my indifference?”
paras.uz: «Mening befarqligimga ishonishingizdan boshqa biror e'tirozingiz bormi?» — dedi Elizabet.

paras.en: “None at all. We all know him to be a proud, unpleasant sort of man; but this would be nothing if you really liked him.”
paras.uz: «Umuman yo'q. Hammamiz uni mag'rur, yoqimsiz odam deb bilamiz; lekin agar uni chindan yoqtirsang, bu hech narsa bo'lmasdi».

paras.en: “I do, I do like him,” she replied, with tears in her eyes, “I love him. Indeed he has no improper pride. He is perfectly amiable. You do not know what he really is; then pray do not pain me by speaking of him in such terms.”
paras.uz: «Yoqtiraman, uni yoqtiraman, — javob berdi u, ko'zlarida yosh bilan. — Men uni sevaman. Haqiqatan ham unda nomunosib g'urur yo'q. U mutlaqo yoqimli. Siz uning aslida kimligini bilmaysiz; shuning uchun, iltimos, u haqida bunday so'zlar bilan gapirib, menga og'riq bermang».

paras.en: “Lizzy,” said her father, “I have given him my consent. He is the kind of man, indeed, to whom I should never dare refuse anything, which he condescended to ask. I now give it to you, if you are resolved on having him. But let me advise you to think better of it. I know your disposition, Lizzy. I know that you could be neither happy nor respectable, unless you truly esteemed your husband; unless you looked up to him as a superior. Your lively talents would place you in the greatest danger in an unequal marriage. You could scarcely escape discredit and misery. My child, let me not have the grief of seeing you unable to respect your partner in life. You know not what you are about.”
paras.uz: «Lizzi, — dedi otasi, — men unga roziligimni berdim. U haqiqatan ham shunday odamki, u so'rash iltifotini ko'rsatgan biror narsani unga rad etishga hech qachon jur'at etmagan bo'lardim. Agar unga turmushga chiqishga qaror qilgan bo'lsang, endi uni senga beraman. Lekin senga yaxshilab o'ylab ko'rishni maslahat beray. Men sening fe'lingni bilaman, Lizzi. Bilamanki, agar sen eringni chin dildan hurmat qilmasang, unga o'zingdan ustun deb qaramasang, na baxtli, na hurmatli bo'la olarding. Sening jo'shqin iste'dodlaring seni teng bo'lmagan nikohda eng katta xavf ostiga qo'yardi. Sen obro'sizlik va baxtsizlikdan zo'rg'a qochib qutula olarding. Bolam, hayotdagi hamrohingni hurmat qila olmasligingni ko'rish qayg'usini menga berma. Sen nima qilayotganingni bilmaysan».

paras.en: Elizabeth, still more affected, was earnest and solemn in her reply; and at length, by repeated assurances that Mr. Darcy was really the object of her choice, by explaining the gradual change which her estimation of him had undergone, relating her absolute certainty that his affection was not the work of a day, but had stood the test of many months' suspense, and enumerating with energy all his good qualities, she did conquer her father's incredulity, and reconcile him to the match.
paras.uz: Yanada ta'sirlangan Elizabet javobida jiddiy va tantanali edi; va nihoyat janob Darsi haqiqatan ham uning tanlovi ekani haqida qayta-qayta ishontirishlar, unga bo'lgan bahosi o'tgan asta-sekin o'zgarishni tushuntirish, uning mehri bir kunlik ish emas, balki ko'p oylik intizorlik sinovidan o'tganiga mutlaq ishonchini aytib berish va uning barcha yaxshi fazilatlarini g'ayrat bilan sanab o'tish orqali otasining ishonchsizligini yengdi va uni nikoh bilan murosaga keltirdi.

paras.en: “Well, my dear,” said he, when she ceased speaking, “I have no more to say. If this be the case, he deserves you. I could not have parted with you, my Lizzy, to anyone less worthy.”
paras.uz: «Xo'sh, azizim, — dedi u, u gapirishni to'xtatgach, — boshqa aytadigan gapim yo'q. Agar shunday bo'lsa, u senga loyiq. Men seni, Lizzim, undan kamroq loyiq hech kimga bera olmasdim».

paras.en: To complete the favourable impression, she then told him what Mr. Darcy had voluntarily done for Lydia. He heard her with astonishment.
paras.uz: Ijobiy taassurotni yakunlash uchun u keyin unga janob Darsi Lidiya uchun o'z ixtiyori bilan nima qilganini aytib berdi. U uni hayrat bilan tingladi.

paras.en: “This is an evening of wonders, indeed! And so, Darcy did every thing; made up the match, gave the money, paid the fellow's debts, and got him his commission! So much the better. It will save me a world of trouble and economy. Had it been your uncle's doing, I must and would have paid him; but these violent young lovers carry every thing their own way. I shall offer to pay him to-morrow; he will rant and storm about his love for you, and there will be an end of the matter.”
paras.uz: «Bu haqiqatan ham mo'jizalar oqshomi! Demak, Darsi hamma narsani qilgan; nikohni tashkil qilgan, pulni bergan, yigitning qarzlarini to'lagan va unga lavozimini olib bergan! Shunisi yaxshi. Bu meni dunyocha tashvish va tejamkorlikdan qutqaradi. Agar bu tog'angning ishi bo'lganida, men unga to'lashim kerak edi va to'lagan bo'lardim; lekin bu shiddatli yosh oshiqlar hamma narsani o'z bilganicha qilishadi. Ertaga unga to'lashni taklif qilaman; u senga bo'lgan muhabbati haqida baqirib-chaqiradi va masala shu bilan tugaydi».

paras.en: He then recollected her embarrassment a few days before, on his reading Mr. Collins's letter; and after laughing at her some time, allowed her at last to go--saying, as she quitted the room, “If any young men come for Mary or Kitty, send them in, for I am quite at leisure.”
paras.uz: Keyin u bir necha kun oldin janob Kollinzning xatini o'qiyotganda uning xijolat bo'lganini esladi; va biroz vaqt uning ustidan kulgach, nihoyat uni qo'yib yubordi — u xonadan chiqayotganda shunday dedi: «Agar Meri yoki Ketti uchun biror yosh yigit kelsa, ularni ichkariga yubor, chunki men butunlay bo'shman».

paras.en: Elizabeth's mind was now relieved from a very heavy weight; and, after half an hour's quiet reflection in her own room, she was able to join the others with tolerable composure. Every thing was too recent for gaiety, but the evening passed tranquilly away; there was no longer anything material to be dreaded, and the comfort of ease and familiarity would come in time.
paras.uz: Endi Elizabetning ongi juda og'ir yukdan xalos bo'ldi; va o'z xonasida yarim soatlik sokin mulohazadan keyin u boshqalarga ancha xotirjamlik bilan qo'shila oldi. Quvnoqlik uchun hamma narsa haddan tashqari yangi edi, lekin oqshom osoyishta o'tdi; endi qo'rqadigan jiddiy narsa qolmagan edi va yengillik hamda yaqinlik taskini vaqt o'tib keladi.

paras.en: When her mother went up to her dressing-room at night, she followed her, and made the important communication. Its effect was most extraordinary; for on first hearing it, Mrs. Bennet sat quite still, and unable to utter a syllable. Nor was it under many, many minutes that she could comprehend what she heard; though not in general backward to credit what was for the advantage of her family, or that came in the shape of a lover to any of them. She began at length to recover, to fidget about in her chair, get up, sit down again, wonder, and bless herself.
paras.uz: Kechasi onasi kiyinish xonasiga chiqqanda, u uning ortidan borib, muhim xabarni aytdi. Uning ta'siri eng g'ayrioddiy bo'ldi; chunki uni birinchi eshitganda missis Bennet butunlay qotib o'tirdi va bir bo'g'in ham aytolmadi. Garchi u odatda oilasi uchun foydali bo'lgan yoki ulardan birortasiga oshiq shaklida kelgan narsaga ishonishda sust bo'lmasa ham, eshitganini tushunishi uchun ko'p, ko'p daqiqalar kerak bo'ldi. Nihoyat u o'ziga kela boshladi, kursisida qimirlab, turib, yana o'tirib, hayron bo'lib, o'zini duolay boshladi.

paras.en: “Good gracious! Lord bless me! only think! dear me! Mr. Darcy! Who would have thought it! And is it really true? Oh! my sweetest Lizzy! how rich and how great you will be! What pin-money, what jewels, what carriages you will have! Jane's is nothing to it--nothing at all. I am so pleased--so happy. Such a charming man!--so handsome! so tall!--Oh, my dear Lizzy! pray apologise for my having disliked him so much before. I hope he will overlook it. Dear, dear Lizzy. A house in town! Every thing that is charming! Three daughters married! Ten thousand a year! Oh, Lord! What will become of me. I shall go distracted.”
paras.uz: «Yo xudo! Xudo saqlasin! O'ylab ko'ring-a! Voy-dod! Janob Darsi! Kim o'ylabdi! Bu haqiqatan ham rostmi? Oh! Eng shirin Lizzim! Qanchalik boy va qanchalik ulug' bo'lasan! Qanday cho'ntak puli, qanday javohirlar, qanday aravalaring bo'ladi! Jeynniki bunga nisbatan hech narsa — umuman hech narsa. Shunchalik mamnunman — shunchalik baxtliman. Shunday maftunkor erkak! — shunchalik chiroyli! shunchalik baland bo'yli! — Oh, aziz Lizzim! Iltimos, uni avval bunchalik yoqtirmaganim uchun mendan uzr so'rab qo'y. Umid qilamanki, u buni e'tiborsiz qoldiradi. Aziz, aziz Lizzi. Londonda uy! Hamma maftunkor narsalar! Uch qiz turmushga chiqdi! Yiliga o'n ming! Oh, Xudoyim! Menga nima bo'ladi? Aqldan ozaman».

paras.en: This was enough to prove that her approbation need not be doubted: and Elizabeth, rejoicing that such an effusion was heard only by herself, soon went away. But before she had been three minutes in her own room, her mother followed her.
paras.uz: Bu uning ma'qullashiga shubha qilmaslik kerakligini isbotlash uchun yetarli edi; Elizabet esa bunday to'lqinni faqat o'zi eshitganidan xursand bo'lib, tez orada ketdi. Lekin u o'z xonasida uch daqiqa ham bo'lmasdan, onasi uning ortidan keldi.

paras.en: “My dearest child,” she cried, “I can think of nothing else! Ten thousand a year, and very likely more! 'Tis as good as a Lord! And a special licence. You must and shall be married by a special licence. But my dearest love, tell me what dish Mr. Darcy is particularly fond of, that I may have it to-morrow.”
paras.uz: «Eng aziz bolam, — xitob qildi u, — boshqa hech narsa haqida o'ylay olmayman! Yiliga o'n ming, ehtimol undan ham ko'p! Bu lord kabi yaxshi! Va maxsus ruxsatnoma. Sen maxsus ruxsatnoma bilan turmushga chiqishing kerak va chiqasan. Lekin eng aziz jonim, menga ayt, janob Darsi qaysi taomni ayniqsa yaxshi ko'radi, ertaga uni tayyorlatay».

paras.en: This was a sad omen of what her mother's behaviour to the gentleman himself might be; and Elizabeth found that, though in the certain possession of his warmest affection, and secure of her relations' consent, there was still something to be wished for. But the morrow passed off much better than she expected; for Mrs. Bennet luckily stood in such awe of her intended son-in-law that she ventured not to speak to him, unless it was in her power to offer him any attention, or mark her deference for his opinion.
paras.uz: Bu onasining janobning o'ziga nisbatan xatti-harakati qanday bo'lishi mumkinligining qayg'uli belgisi edi; Elizabet uning eng qizg'in mehriga aniq ega bo'lsa va qarindoshlarining roziligiga ishonch hosil qilgan bo'lsa ham, hali ham orzu qilinadigan narsa borligini ko'rdi. Lekin ertasi kun u kutganidan ancha yaxshi o'tdi; chunki missis Bennet baxtiga bo'lajak kuyovidan shunchalik hayiqardiki, unga biror e'tibor ko'rsatish yoki uning fikriga hurmatini bildirish imkoni bo'lmasa, u bilan gaplashishga jur'at etmadi.

paras.en: Elizabeth had the satisfaction of seeing her father taking pains to get acquainted with him; and Mr. Bennet soon assured her that he was rising every hour in his esteem.
paras.uz: Elizabet otasining u bilan tanishish uchun harakat qilayotganini ko'rib mamnun bo'ldi; janob Bennet tez orada uni u har soat uning nazarida yuksalib borayotganiga ishontirdi.

paras.en: “I admire all my three sons-in-law highly,” said he. “Wickham, perhaps, is my favourite; but I think I shall like your husband quite as well as Jane's.”
paras.uz: «Men uchala kuyovimni ham juda qadrlayman, — dedi u. — Uikhem, ehtimol, mening sevimlim; lekin menimcha, sening eringni ham Jeynnikidek yoqtiraman».

quiz.q: What worries Mr. Bennet?
o: That Elizabeth might not truly respect and love Darcy
quiz.why_uz: U qizining baxtsiz nikohda bo'lishini istamaydi.
