chapters.title: How Did It Begin?
chapters.recap_uz: Elizabet Darsidan uni qachon sevib qolganini so'raydi. Darsi: «Bilmayman, men allaqachon yarim yo'lda edim», deydi. Elizabet Gardinerlarga, Darsi Ledi Ketringa xat yozadi.

paras.en: Elizabeth's spirits soon rising to playfulness again, she wanted Mr. Darcy to account for his having ever fallen in love with her. “How could you begin?” said she. “I can comprehend your going on charmingly, when you had once made a beginning; but what could set you off in the first place?”
paras.uz: Elizabetning kayfiyati tez orada yana o'ynoqilikka ko'tarilib, u janob Darsidan qachondir unga qanday oshiq bo'lib qolganini tushuntirib berishni istadi. «Qanday boshladingiz? — dedi u. — Bir marta boshlagach, maftunkor tarzda davom etganingizni tushuna olaman; lekin birinchi navbatda sizni nima harakatga keltirishi mumkin edi?»

paras.en: “I cannot fix on the hour, or the spot, or the look, or the words, which laid the foundation. It is too long ago. I was in the middle before I knew that I had begun.”
paras.uz: «Poydevor qo'ygan soatni, joyni, qarashni yoki so'zlarni aniqlay olmayman. Bu haddan tashqari uzoq vaqt oldin edi. Boshlaganimni bilmasdanoq o'rtasida edim».

paras.en: “My beauty you had early withstood, and as for my manners--my behaviour to you was at least always bordering on the uncivil, and I never spoke to you without rather wishing to give you pain than not. Now be sincere; did you admire me for my impertinence?”
paras.uz: «Mening go'zalligimga siz erta qarshi turdingiz, muomalamga kelsak — sizga nisbatan xatti-harakatim hech bo'lmaganda doim xushmuomalasizlik chegarasida edi va men siz bilan hech qachon og'riq bermaslikdan ko'ra og'riq berishni ko'proq istamasdan gaplashmaganman. Endi samimiy bo'ling; meni surbetligim uchun yoqtirdingizmi?»

paras.en: “For the liveliness of your mind, I did.”
paras.uz: «Aqlingizning jo'shqinligi uchun, ha».

paras.en: “You may as well call it impertinence at once. It was very little less. The fact is, that you were sick of civility, of deference, of officious attention. You were disgusted with the women who were always speaking, and looking, and thinking for your approbation alone. I roused, and interested you, because I was so unlike them. Had you not been really amiable, you would have hated me for it; but in spite of the pains you took to disguise yourself, your feelings were always noble and just; and in your heart, you thoroughly despised the persons who so assiduously courted you. There--I have saved you the trouble of accounting for it; and really, all things considered, I begin to think it perfectly reasonable. To be sure, you knew no actual good of me--but nobody thinks of that when they fall in love.”
paras.uz: «Buni darhol surbetlik deb ham atashingiz mumkin. U undan unchalik kam emasdi. Gap shundaki, siz xushmuomalalikdan, ehtiromdan, ortiqcha e'tibordan bezor bo'lgan edingiz. Siz doim faqat sizning ma'qullashingiz uchun gapiradigan, qaraydigan va o'ylaydigan ayollardan jirkangan edingiz. Men sizni uyg'otdim va qiziqtirdim, chunki ularga shunchalik o'xshamas edim. Agar siz chindan yoqimli bo'lmaganingizda, buning uchun mendan nafratlangan bo'lardingiz; lekin o'zingizni niqoblash uchun qilgan barcha harakatlaringizga qaramay, tuyg'ularingiz doim oliyjanob va adolatli edi; va qalbingizda sizga shunchalik tirishqoqlik bilan xushomad qilgan odamlarni butunlay mensimas edingiz. Mana — sizni buni tushuntirish zahmatidan qutqardim; va haqiqatan ham, hamma narsani hisobga olsam, buni mutlaqo oqilona deb o'ylay boshladim. Albatta, siz men haqimda hech qanday haqiqiy yaxshilikni bilmasdingiz — lekin oshiq bo'lganda hech kim bu haqda o'ylamaydi».

paras.en: “Was there no good in your affectionate behaviour to Jane while she was ill at Netherfield?”
paras.uz: «Jeyn Nezerfildda kasal bo'lganida unga nisbatan mehribon xatti-harakatingizda hech qanday yaxshilik yo'qmidi?»

paras.en: “Dearest Jane! who could have done less for her? But make a virtue of it by all means. My good qualities are under your protection, and you are to exaggerate them as much as possible; and, in return, it belongs to me to find occasions for teasing and quarrelling with you as often as may be; and I shall begin directly by asking you what made you so unwilling to come to the point at last. What made you so shy of me, when you first called, and afterwards dined here? Why, especially, when you called, did you look as if you did not care about me?”
paras.uz: «Eng aziz Jeyn! Uning uchun kim bundan kamroq qila olardi? Lekin albatta, buni fazilatga aylantiring. Mening yaxshi fazilatlarim sizning himoyangiz ostida va siz ularni iloji boricha bo'rttirishingiz kerak; evaziga esa, iloji boricha tez-tez siz bilan hazillashish va janjallashish uchun sabab topish menga tegishli; va men darhol sizdan oxirida asosiy masalaga kelishni nimaga bunchalik istamaganingizni so'rashdan boshlayman. Birinchi kelganingizda va keyin bu yerda tushlik qilganingizda sizni mendan nima bunchalik tortinchoq qildi? Ayniqsa kelganingizda nega menga ahamiyat bermayotgandek ko'rindingiz?»

paras.en: “Because you were grave and silent, and gave me no encouragement.”
paras.uz: «Chunki siz jiddiy va jim edingiz va menga hech qanday rag'bat bermadingiz».

paras.en: “But I was embarrassed.”
paras.uz: «Lekin men xijolat edim».

paras.en: “And so was I.”
paras.uz: «Men ham».

paras.en: “You might have talked to me more when you came to dinner.”
paras.uz: «Tushlikka kelganingizda men bilan ko'proq gaplashishingiz mumkin edi».

paras.en: “A man who had felt less, might.”
paras.uz: «Kamroq his qilgan erkak gaplashishi mumkin edi».

paras.en: “How unlucky that you should have a reasonable answer to give, and that I should be so reasonable as to admit it! But I wonder how long you would have gone on, if you had been left to yourself. I wonder when you would have spoken, if I had not asked you! My resolution of thanking you for your kindness to Lydia had certainly great effect. Too much, I am afraid; for what becomes of the moral, if our comfort springs from a breach of promise? for I ought not to have mentioned the subject. This will never do.”
paras.uz: «Qanday omadsizlik, sizda oqilona javob borligi va men uni tan oladigan darajada oqilona ekanim! Lekin hayronman, agar o'z holingizga qo'yilganingizda, qancha vaqt shunday davom etgan bo'lardingiz. Hayronman, agar men so'ramaganimda, qachon gapirgan bo'lardingiz! Lidiyaga ko'rsatgan mehribonligingiz uchun sizga rahmat aytish qarorim, albatta, katta ta'sir ko'rsatdi. Qo'rqamanki, haddan tashqari ko'p; chunki agar taskinimiz va'daning buzilishidan kelib chiqsa, axloqiy saboq nima bo'ladi? Chunki men bu mavzuni tilga olmasligim kerak edi. Bu to'g'ri kelmaydi».

paras.en: “You need not distress yourself. The moral will be perfectly fair. Lady Catherine's unjustifiable endeavours to separate us were the means of removing all my doubts. I am not indebted for my present happiness to your eager desire of expressing your gratitude. I was not in a humour to wait for any opening of yours. My aunt's intelligence had given me hope, and I was determined at once to know every thing.”
paras.uz: «Xavotirlanishingizga hojat yo'q. Axloqiy saboq mutlaqo to'g'ri bo'ladi. Ledi Ketrinning bizni ajratishga qaratilgan oqlab bo'lmaydigan urinishlari mening barcha shubhalarimni yo'qotish vositasi bo'ldi. Men hozirgi baxtim uchun sizning minnatdorligingizni ifodalash istagingizdan qarzdor emasman. Men sizdan biror imkoniyatni kutadigan kayfiyatda emasdim. Xolamning xabari menga umid berdi va men darhol hamma narsani bilishga qaror qildim».

paras.en: “Lady Catherine has been of infinite use, which ought to make her happy, for she loves to be of use. But tell me, what did you come down to Netherfield for? Was it merely to ride to Longbourn and be embarrassed? or had you intended any more serious consequence?”
paras.uz: «Ledi Ketrin cheksiz foyda keltirdi, bu uni baxtli qilishi kerak, chunki u foydali bo'lishni yaxshi ko'radi. Lekin ayting-chi, Nezerfildga nima uchun keldingiz? Faqat Longbornga otda kelib, xijolat bo'lish uchunmi? Yoki jiddiyroq oqibatni niyat qilganmidingiz?»

paras.en: “My real purpose was to see you, and to judge, if I could, whether I might ever hope to make you love me. My avowed one, or what I avowed to myself, was to see whether your sister were still partial to Bingley, and if she were, to make the confession to him which I have since made.”
paras.uz: «Mening haqiqiy maqsadim sizni ko'rish va iloji bo'lsa, qachondir sizni meni sevishga majbur qilishga umid qila olamanmi, yo'qmi, hukm chiqarish edi. Izhor qilgan maqsadim, yoki o'zimga izhor qilgan maqsadim, opangiz hali ham Binglige moyilmi, yo'qmi, ko'rish va agar moyil bo'lsa, o'shandan beri qilgan tan olishimni unga qilish edi».

paras.en: “Shall you ever have courage to announce to Lady Catherine what is to befall her?”
paras.uz: «Ledi Ketringa uning boshiga nima tushishini e'lon qilishga qachondir jur'atingiz yetadimi?»

paras.en: “I am more likely to want more time than courage, Elizabeth. But it ought to be done, and if you will give me a sheet of paper, it shall be done directly.”
paras.uz: «Menga jur'atdan ko'ra ko'proq vaqt yetishmasligi ehtimoli bor, Elizabet. Lekin buni qilish kerak va agar menga bir varaq qog'oz bersangiz, bu darhol qilinadi».

paras.en: “And if I had not a letter to write myself, I might sit by you and admire the evenness of your writing, as another young lady once did. But I have an aunt, too, who must not be longer neglected.”
paras.uz: «Agar o'zimning yozadigan xatim bo'lmaganida, bir paytlar boshqa bir yosh xonim qilganidek, yoningizda o'tirib, yozuvingizning tekisligiga qoyil qolishim mumkin edi. Lekin mening ham xolam bor, uni boshqa e'tiborsiz qoldirib bo'lmaydi».

paras.en: From an unwillingness to confess how much her intimacy with Mr. Darcy had been over-rated, Elizabeth had never yet answered Mrs. Gardiner's long letter; but now, having that to communicate which she knew would be most welcome, she was almost ashamed to find that her uncle and aunt had already lost three days of happiness, and immediately wrote as follows:
paras.uz: Janob Darsi bilan yaqinligi qanchalik ortiqcha baholanganini tan olishni istamagani uchun, Elizabet hali missis Gardinerning uzun xatiga javob bermagan edi; lekin endi eng xush kelishini bilgan xabari bo'lgani uchun, u tog'asi va xolasi allaqachon uch kunlik baxtni yo'qotganini bilib, deyarli uyaldi va darhol quyidagicha yozdi:

paras.en: “I would have thanked you before, my dear aunt, as I ought to have done, for your long, kind, satisfactory, detail of particulars; but to say the truth, I was too cross to write. You supposed more than really existed. But now suppose as much as you choose; give a loose rein to your fancy, indulge your imagination in every possible flight which the subject will afford, and unless you believe me actually married, you cannot greatly err. You must write again very soon, and praise him a great deal more than you did in your last. I thank you, again and again, for not going to the Lakes. How could I be so silly as to wish it! Your idea of the ponies is delightful. We will go round the Park every day. I am the happiest creature in the world. Perhaps other people have said so before, but not one with such justice. I am happier even than Jane; she only smiles, I laugh. Mr. Darcy sends you all the love in the world that he can spare from me. You are all to come to Pemberley at Christmas. Yours, etc.”
paras.uz: «Aziz xolajon, uzun, mehribon, qoniqarli tafsilotlaringiz uchun sizga avvalroq, qilishim kerak bo'lganidek, rahmat aytgan bo'lardim; lekin rostini aytsam, yozish uchun haddan tashqari jahlim chiqqan edi. Siz aslida mavjud bo'lganidan ko'proq narsani taxmin qilgan edingiz. Lekin endi xohlaganingizcha taxmin qiling; xayolingizga erk bering, tasavvuringizni mavzu imkon bergan har qanday parvozga qo'yib yuboring va agar meni haqiqatan ham turmush qurgan deb ishonmasangiz, unchalik adashmaysiz. Tez orada yana yozishingiz va uni oxirgi xatingizdagidan ancha ko'proq maqtashingiz kerak. Ko'llar o'lkasiga bormaganingiz uchun sizga qayta-qayta rahmat aytaman. Qanday qilib buni istaydigan darajada ahmoq bo'la oldim! Ponilar haqidagi fikringiz ajoyib. Biz har kuni parkni aylanib chiqamiz. Men dunyodagi eng baxtli mavjudotman. Ehtimol, boshqa odamlar ham ilgari shunday deyishgandir, lekin hech biri bunchalik haqli emas. Men hatto Jeyndan ham baxtliroqman; u faqat jilmayadi, men esa kulaman. Janob Darsi sizga mendan ajrata oladigan dunyodagi butun mehrini yo'llaydi. Rojdestvoda hammangiz Pemberliga kelishingiz kerak. Sizniki va hokazo».

paras.en: Mr. Darcy's letter to Lady Catherine was in a different style; and still different from either was what Mr. Bennet sent to Mr. Collins, in reply to his last.
paras.uz: Janob Darsining ledi Ketringa xati boshqacha uslubda edi; janob Bennetning janob Kollinzga uning oxirgi xatiga javoban yuborgan xati esa ikkalasidan ham farq qilardi.

paras.en: “DEAR SIR,
paras.uz: «AZIZ SER,

paras.en: “I must trouble you once more for congratulations. Elizabeth will soon be the wife of Mr. Darcy. Console Lady Catherine as well as you can. But, if I were you, I would stand by the nephew. He has more to give.
paras.uz: Sizni yana bir marta tabriklar uchun bezovta qilishim kerak. Elizabet tez orada janob Darsining xotini bo'ladi. Ledi Ketrinni iloji boricha yupating. Lekin agar sizning o'rningizda bo'lganimda, jiyan tomonida turardim. Uning beradigan narsasi ko'proq.

paras.en: “Yours sincerely, etc.”
paras.uz: Samimiy sizniki va hokazo».

paras.en: Miss Bingley's congratulations to her brother, on his approaching marriage, were all that was affectionate and insincere. She wrote even to Jane on the occasion, to express her delight, and repeat all her former professions of regard. Jane was not deceived, but she was affected; and though feeling no reliance on her, could not help writing her a much kinder answer than she knew was deserved.
paras.uz: Miss Binglining akasini yaqinlashib kelayotgan nikohi bilan tabriklashi butunlay mehrli va nosamimiy edi. U bu munosabat bilan hatto Jeynga ham xat yozib, quvonchini bildirdi va avvalgi barcha mehr izhorlarini takrorladi. Jeyn aldanmadi, lekin ta'sirlandi; garchi unga hech qanday ishonch his qilmasa ham, unga loyiq bo'lganidan ancha mehribonroq javob yozmay qololmadi.

paras.en: The joy which Miss Darcy expressed on receiving similar information, was as sincere as her brother's in sending it. Four sides of paper were insufficient to contain all her delight, and all her earnest desire of being loved by her sister.
paras.uz: Miss Darsining shunga o'xshash xabarni olgandagi quvonchi akasining uni yuborgandagi quvonchi kabi samimiy edi. To'rt sahifa qog'oz uning butun zavqini va kelinoyisi tomonidan sevilishga bo'lgan butun chin istagini sig'dirish uchun yetarli emasdi.

paras.en: Before any answer could arrive from Mr. Collins, or any congratulations to Elizabeth from his wife, the Longbourn family heard that the Collinses were come themselves to Lucas Lodge. The reason of this sudden removal was soon evident. Lady Catherine had been rendered so exceedingly angry by the contents of her nephew's letter, that Charlotte, really rejoicing in the match, was anxious to get away till the storm was blown over. At such a moment, the arrival of her friend was a sincere pleasure to Elizabeth, though in the course of their meetings she must sometimes think the pleasure dearly bought, when she saw Mr. Darcy exposed to all the parading and obsequious civility of her husband. He bore it, however, with admirable calmness. He could even listen to Sir William Lucas, when he complimented him on carrying away the brightest jewel of the country, and expressed his hopes of their all meeting frequently at St. James's, with very decent composure. If he did shrug his shoulders, it was not till Sir William was out of sight.
paras.uz: Janob Kollinzdan biror javob yoki uning xotinidan Elizabetga biror tabrik kelishidan oldin, Longborn oilasi Kollinzlarning o'zlari Lukas Lojga kelganini eshitishdi. Bu to'satdan ko'chishning sababi tez orada aniq bo'ldi. Ledi Ketrin jiyanining xati mazmunidan shunchalik qattiq g'azablangan ediki, nikohdan chin dildan xursand bo'lgan Sharlotta bo'ron tingunicha ketishga intildi. Bunday paytda dugonasining kelishi Elizabetga samimiy zavq bag'ishladi, garchi ularning uchrashuvlari davomida janob Darsining uning erining barcha dabdabali va yaltoq xushmuomalaligiga duchor bo'lganini ko'rganda, bu zavq qimmatga tushganini ba'zan o'ylashi kerak bo'lsa ham. Biroq u bunga ajoyib xotirjamlik bilan chidadi. U hatto ser Uilyam Lukas uni mamlakatning eng yorqin javohirini olib ketgani bilan maqtaganda va ularning hammasi Sent-Jeymsda tez-tez uchrashishiga umid bildirganda ham juda munosib xotirjamlik bilan tinglay oldi. Agar u yelkasini qisgan bo'lsa ham, buni ser Uilyam ko'zdan g'oyib bo'lgandan keyingina qildi.

paras.en: Mrs. Phillips's vulgarity was another, and perhaps a greater, tax on his forbearance; and though Mrs. Phillips, as well as her sister, stood in too much awe of him to speak with the familiarity which Bingley's good humour encouraged, yet, whenever she did speak, she must be vulgar. Nor was her respect for him, though it made her more quiet, at all likely to make her more elegant. Elizabeth did all she could to shield him from the frequent notice of either, and was ever anxious to keep him to herself, and to those of her family with whom he might converse without mortification; and though the uncomfortable feelings arising from all this took from the season of courtship much of its pleasure, it added to the hope of the future; and she looked forward with delight to the time when they should be removed from society so little pleasing to either, to all the comfort and elegance of their family party at Pemberley.
paras.uz: Missis Fillipsning qo'polligi uning sabriga yana bir, ehtimol kattaroq soliq edi; garchi missis Fillips ham, opasi kabi, Binglining xushfe'lligi rag'batlantiradigan bemalollik bilan gapirish uchun undan haddan tashqari hayiqsa ham, u har gapirganda qo'pol bo'lishi muqarrar edi. Uning unga bo'lgan hurmati uni jimroq qilgan bo'lsa ham, uni nafisroq qilishi umuman ehtimoldan yiroq edi. Elizabet uni ikkalasining tez-tez e'tiboridan himoya qilish uchun qo'lidan kelgan hamma narsani qildi va doim uni o'zida va u bilan xo'rlanishsiz suhbatlasha oladigan oila a'zolari yonida saqlashga intildi; garchi bularning hammasidan kelib chiqadigan noqulay tuyg'ular unashtiruv faslidan zavqining ko'p qismini tortib olgan bo'lsa ham, bu kelajakka umidni oshirdi; va u ular ikkalasiga ham bunchalik kam yoqimli bo'lgan jamiyatdan Pemberlidagi oila davrasining butun qulayligi va nafosatiga ko'chiriladigan vaqtni zavq bilan kutdi.

chapters.title: Ever After
chapters.recap_uz: Ikki to'y bo'ladi. Jeyn va Bingley Pemberli yaqiniga ko'chishadi, Ketti yaxshi tarbiya oladi. Lidiya va Uikhem pul so'rab turishadi. Ledi Ketrin oxiri yarashadi. Darsi va Elizabet Gardinerlarga doim minnatdor.

paras.en: Happy for all her maternal feelings was the day on which Mrs. Bennet got rid of her two most deserving daughters. With what delighted pride she afterwards visited Mrs. Bingley, and talked of Mrs. Darcy, may be guessed. I wish I could say, for the sake of her family, that the accomplishment of her earnest desire in the establishment of so many of her children produced so happy an effect as to make her a sensible, amiable, well-informed woman for the rest of her life; though perhaps it was lucky for her husband, who might not have relished domestic felicity in so unusual a form, that she still was occasionally nervous and invariably silly.
paras.uz: Missis Bennet eng munosib ikki qizidan qutulgan kun uning barcha onalik tuyg'ulari uchun baxtli kun bo'ldi. U keyinchalik missis Binglini qanday zavqli g'urur bilan ziyorat qilgani va missis Darsi haqida qanday gapirganini taxmin qilish mumkin. Oilasi xotiri uchun aytishni istardimki, shuncha farzandini joylashtirish haqidagi chin istagining amalga oshishi shunchalik baxtli ta'sir ko'rsatdiki, uni umrining qolgan qismida aqlli, yoqimli, bilimli ayolga aylantirdi; garchi, ehtimol, oilaviy baxtni bunday g'ayrioddiy shaklda yoqtirmasligi mumkin bo'lgan eri uchun u hali ham vaqti-vaqti bilan asabiy va o'zgarmas darajada ahmoq bo'lib qolgani omad bo'lgandir.

paras.en: Mr. Bennet missed his second daughter exceedingly; his affection for her drew him oftener from home than anything else could do. He delighted in going to Pemberley, especially when he was least expected.
paras.uz: Janob Bennet ikkinchi qizini nihoyatda sog'indi; unga bo'lgan mehri uni uydan boshqa har qanday narsadan ko'ra tez-tez olib chiqardi. U Pemberliga borishdan, ayniqsa eng kam kutilgan paytda borishdan zavqlanardi.

paras.en: Mr. Bingley and Jane remained at Netherfield only a twelvemonth. So near a vicinity to her mother and Meryton relations was not desirable even to his easy temper, or her affectionate heart. The darling wish of his sisters was then gratified; he bought an estate in a neighbouring county to Derbyshire, and Jane and Elizabeth, in addition to every other source of happiness, were within thirty miles of each other.
paras.uz: Janob Bingli va Jeyn Nezerfildda atigi bir yil qolishdi. Onasi va Meritondagi qarindoshlariga bunchalik yaqin qo'shnichilik hatto uning yengil fe'li yoki Jeynning mehribon qalbi uchun ham maqbul emasdi. Shunda uning opa-singillarining aziz orzusi amalga oshdi; u Derbishirga qo'shni graflikda mulk sotib oldi va Jeyn bilan Elizabet boshqa barcha baxt manbalariga qo'shimcha ravishda bir-biridan o'ttiz mil masofada bo'lishdi.

paras.en: Kitty, to her very material advantage, spent the chief of her time with her two elder sisters. In society so superior to what she had generally known, her improvement was great. She was not of so ungovernable a temper as Lydia; and, removed from the influence of Lydia's example, she became, by proper attention and management, less irritable, less ignorant, and less insipid. From the further disadvantage of Lydia's society she was of course carefully kept, and though Mrs. Wickham frequently invited her to come and stay with her, with the promise of balls and young men, her father would never consent to her going.
paras.uz: Ketti o'zi uchun juda katta foyda bilan vaqtining asosiy qismini ikki katta opasi bilan o'tkazdi. Odatda bilganidan ancha yuqori jamiyatda uning rivojlanishi katta bo'ldi. U Lidiya kabi boshqarib bo'lmas fe'lli emasdi; va Lidiyaning namunasi ta'siridan uzoqlashtirilgach, munosib e'tibor va boshqaruv bilan kamroq jizzaki, kamroq johil va kamroq zerikarli bo'lib qoldi. Lidiyaning davrasining keyingi zararidan u, albatta, ehtiyotkorlik bilan saqlandi; garchi missis Uikhem uni ballar va yosh yigitlar va'dasi bilan tez-tez o'zinikiga kelib qolishga taklif qilsa ham, otasi hech qachon uning borishiga rozi bo'lmadi.

paras.en: Mary was the only daughter who remained at home; and she was necessarily drawn from the pursuit of accomplishments by Mrs. Bennet's being quite unable to sit alone. Mary was obliged to mix more with the world, but she could still moralize over every morning visit; and as she was no longer mortified by comparisons between her sisters' beauty and her own, it was suspected by her father that she submitted to the change without much reluctance.
paras.uz: Meri uyda qolgan yagona qiz edi; missis Bennet yolg'iz o'tira olmagani uchun u muqarrar ravishda hunarlarni egallashdan chalg'itildi. Meri dunyo bilan ko'proq aralashishga majbur bo'ldi, lekin u hali ham har bir ertalabgi tashrif haqida axloqiy mulohaza yurita olardi; va endi opa-singillarining go'zalligi bilan o'zinikini taqqoslashdan xo'rlanmagani uchun, otasi u bu o'zgarishga unchalik qarshiliksiz bo'ysungan deb gumon qilardi.

paras.en: As for Wickham and Lydia, their characters suffered no revolution from the marriage of her sisters. He bore with philosophy the conviction that Elizabeth must now become acquainted with whatever of his ingratitude and falsehood had before been unknown to her; and in spite of every thing, was not wholly without hope that Darcy might yet be prevailed on to make his fortune. The congratulatory letter which Elizabeth received from Lydia on her marriage, explained to her that, by his wife at least, if not by himself, such a hope was cherished. The letter was to this effect:
paras.uz: Uikhem va Lidiyaga kelsak, ularning xarakterlari opa-singillarining nikohidan hech qanday inqilobga uchramadi. U endi Elizabet uning avval unga noma'lum bo'lgan har qanday noshukrligi va yolg'onlari bilan tanishishi kerakligiga bo'lgan ishonchni falsafiy tarzda ko'tardi; va hamma narsaga qaramay, Darsini hali ham uning boyligini tuzishga ko'ndirish mumkinligiga butunlay umidsiz emasdi. Elizabet turmushga chiqishi munosabati bilan Lidiyadan olgan tabrik xati unga hech bo'lmaganda uning xotini, agar o'zi bo'lmasa ham, bunday umidni qadrlaganini tushuntirdi. Xat quyidagi mazmunda edi:

paras.en: “MY DEAR LIZZY,
paras.uz: «AZIZ LIZZI,

paras.en: “I wish you joy. If you love Mr. Darcy half as well as I do my dear Wickham, you must be very happy. It is a great comfort to have you so rich, and when you have nothing else to do, I hope you will think of us. I am sure Wickham would like a place at court very much, and I do not think we shall have quite money enough to live upon without some help. Any place would do, of about three or four hundred a year; but however, do not speak to Mr. Darcy about it, if you had rather not.
paras.uz: Senga baxt tilayman. Agar sen janob Darsini men aziz Uikhemimni sevganimning yarmicha sevsang, juda baxtli bo'lishing kerak. Seni bunchalik boy ko'rish katta taskin va qiladigan boshqa ishing bo'lmaganda, umid qilamanki, biz haqimizda o'ylaysan. Ishonchim komilki, Uikhem saroydagi lavozimni juda yoqtirardi va menimcha, biroz yordamsiz yashash uchun pulimiz yetarli bo'lmaydi. Yiliga uch-to'rt yuzlik har qanday lavozim bo'laveradi; lekin baribir, agar istamasang, bu haqda janob Darsi bilan gaplashma.

paras.en: “Yours, etc.”
paras.uz: Seniki va hokazo».

paras.en: As it happened that Elizabeth had much rather not, she endeavoured in her answer to put an end to every entreaty and expectation of the kind. Such relief, however, as it was in her power to afford, by the practice of what might be called economy in her own private expences, she frequently sent them. It had always been evident to her that such an income as theirs, under the direction of two persons so extravagant in their wants, and heedless of the future, must be very insufficient to their support; and whenever they changed their quarters, either Jane or herself were sure of being applied to for some little assistance towards discharging their bills. Their manner of living, even when the restoration of peace dismissed them to a home, was unsettled in the extreme. They were always moving from place to place in quest of a cheap situation, and always spending more than they ought. His affection for her soon sunk into indifference; hers lasted a little longer; and in spite of her youth and her manners, she retained all the claims to reputation which her marriage had given her.
paras.uz: Elizabet aynan istamagani uchun, u javobida bunday har qanday iltimos va kutishga barham berishga harakat qildi. Biroq o'zining shaxsiy xarajatlarida tejamkorlik deb atash mumkin bo'lgan narsani qo'llash orqali bera oladigan yordamni u ularga tez-tez yuborib turdi. Uning uchun ehtiyojlarida shunchalik isrofgar va kelajakka beparvo bo'lgan ikki kishining boshqaruvidagi ularnikidek daromad ularni ta'minlash uchun juda yetarsiz bo'lishi kerakligi doim aniq edi; va ular har safar turar joyini o'zgartirganda, Jeyn yoki undan hisoblarini to'lash uchun biroz yordam so'rab murojaat qilishlari aniq edi. Ularning turmush tarzi, hatto tinchlikning tiklanishi ularni uyga qaytarganda ham, nihoyatda beqaror edi. Ular doim arzon joy izlab bir joydan boshqasiga ko'chib yurishardi va doim kerak bo'lganidan ko'proq sarflashardi. Uning unga bo'lgan mehri tez orada befarqlikka cho'kdi; uniki biroz uzoqroq davom etdi; va yoshligi va muomalasiga qaramay, u nikohi bergan obro'ga bo'lgan barcha da'volarini saqlab qoldi.

paras.en: Though Darcy could never receive him at Pemberley, yet, for Elizabeth's sake, he assisted him further in his profession. Lydia was occasionally a visitor there, when her husband was gone to enjoy himself in London or Bath; and with the Bingleys they both of them frequently staid so long, that even Bingley's good humour was overcome, and he proceeded so far as to talk of giving them a hint to be gone.
paras.uz: Darsi uni hech qachon Pemberlida qabul qila olmasa ham, Elizabet xotiri uchun unga kasbida qo'shimcha yordam berdi. Lidiya vaqti-vaqti bilan, eri Londonga yoki Batga ko'ngil ochishga ketganda, u yerga mehmon bo'lardi; Binglilarnikida esa ular ikkalasi ham tez-tez shunchalik uzoq qolishardiki, hatto Binglining xushfe'lligi ham yengilib, u ularga ketish haqida ishora qilish haqida gapirish darajasiga yetdi.

paras.en: Miss Bingley was very deeply mortified by Darcy's marriage; but as she thought it advisable to retain the right of visiting at Pemberley, she dropt all her resentment; was fonder than ever of Georgiana, almost as attentive to Darcy as heretofore, and paid off every arrear of civility to Elizabeth.
paras.uz: Miss Bingli Darsining nikohidan juda chuqur xo'rlandi; lekin u Pemberliga tashrif buyurish huquqini saqlab qolishni maqsadga muvofiq deb hisoblagani uchun, barcha ranjishidan voz kechdi; Jorjianani har qachongidan ham ko'proq yaxshi ko'rdi, Darsiga deyarli avvalgidek e'tiborli bo'ldi va Elizabetga barcha xushmuomalalik qarzlarini to'ladi.

paras.en: Pemberley was now Georgiana's home; and the attachment of the sisters was exactly what Darcy had hoped to see. They were able to love each other even as well as they intended. Georgiana had the highest opinion in the world of Elizabeth; though at first she often listened with an astonishment bordering on alarm at her lively, sportive, manner of talking to her brother. He, who had always inspired in herself a respect which almost overcame her affection, she now saw the object of open pleasantry. Her mind received knowledge which had never before fallen in her way. By Elizabeth's instructions, she began to comprehend that a woman may take liberties with her husband which a brother will not always allow in a sister more than ten years younger than himself.
paras.uz: Pemberli endi Jorjiananing uyi edi; opa-singillarning mehri aynan Darsi ko'rishga umid qilgandek edi. Ular bir-birini hatto niyat qilganlaridek yaxshi sevishga qodir edilar. Jorjiana Elizabet haqida dunyodagi eng yuqori fikrda edi; garchi avvaliga u uning akasi bilan jo'shqin, o'ynoqi gaplashish uslubini ko'pincha qo'rquvga yaqin hayrat bilan tinglagan bo'lsa ham. O'zida doim mehrini deyarli yengib ketadigan hurmat uyg'otgan akasini u endi ochiq hazil obyekti sifatida ko'rardi. Uning ongi ilgari hech qachon yo'liga tushmagan bilimni oldi. Elizabetning ko'rsatmalari bilan u ayol eri bilan aka o'zidan o'n yoshdan ortiq kichik singlisiga har doim ham ruxsat bermaydigan erkinliklarni qila olishini tushuna boshladi.

paras.en: Lady Catherine was extremely indignant on the marriage of her nephew; and as she gave way to all the genuine frankness of her character in her reply to the letter which announced its arrangement, she sent him language so very abusive, especially of Elizabeth, that for some time all intercourse was at an end. But at length, by Elizabeth's persuasion, he was prevailed on to overlook the offence, and seek a reconciliation; and, after a little further resistance on the part of his aunt, her resentment gave way, either to her affection for him, or her curiosity to see how his wife conducted herself; and she condescended to wait on them at Pemberley, in spite of that pollution which its woods had received, not merely from the presence of such a mistress, but the visits of her uncle and aunt from the city.
paras.uz: Ledi Ketrin jiyanining nikohidan nihoyatda g'azablandi; va u uning tashkil etilishini e'lon qilgan xatga javobida xarakterining butun chinakam ochiqligiga erk bergani uchun, unga, ayniqsa Elizabet haqida shunchalik haqoratli so'zlar yubordiki, bir muddat barcha munosabatlar to'xtadi. Lekin nihoyat Elizabetning ko'ndirishi bilan u haqoratni e'tiborsiz qoldirishga va yarashishni izlashga ko'ndirildi; va xolasi tomonidan yana biroz qarshilikdan keyin, uning ranjishi unga bo'lgan mehri yoki uning xotini o'zini qanday tutishini ko'rishga bo'lgan qiziqishi oldida chekindi; va u o'rmonlari nafaqat bunday bekaning bo'lishi, balki uning shahardan kelgan tog'asi va xolasining tashriflari bilan ham olgan bulg'anishga qaramay, Pemberlida ularni ziyorat qilish iltifotini ko'rsatdi.

paras.en: With the Gardiners, they were always on the most intimate terms. Darcy, as well as Elizabeth, really loved them; and they were both ever sensible of the warmest gratitude towards the persons who, by bringing her into Derbyshire, had been the means of uniting them.
paras.uz: Gardinerlar bilan ular doim eng yaqin munosabatda bo'lishdi. Darsi ham, Elizabet ham ularni chin dildan sevardi; va ular ikkalasi ham uni Derbishirga olib kelib, ularni birlashtirish vositasi bo'lgan insonlarga nisbatan doim eng qizg'in minnatdorlikni his qilishardi.
